API_KEY=swat-dev-key

# NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY was deliberately DELETED, not renamed (checklist S6-3).
# It put the shared operator control-plane key into the browser bundle -- Next.js
# inlines every NEXT_PUBLIC_* variable at build time, so it was published to every
# visitor rather than configured. The frontend now authenticates with the session
# cookie the API issues at POST /v1/auth/login, plus the double-submit CSRF token;
# see apps/web/lib/api.ts, which has no way to send an API key at all.
# API_KEY above is now internal service-to-API only. Never mirror it into a
# NEXT_PUBLIC_* name.
#
# NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is a URL, not a secret, and stays public config. The rule
# being enforced is "no secrets in the bundle", not "no config in the bundle".

# â”€â”€ Admin bootstrap â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# âœ… REQUIRED once, before anyone can use the dashboard.
#
# The operator console (/workspace, /wallets, /signals, /logs, /setup,
# /performance, /clusters) is admin-only: the API refuses every route outside
# /v1/auth/ and /v1/me/ to a non-admin, and the web middleware redirects rather
# than render a shell whose requests will all 403.
#
# Signing up through the app creates a plain `user`, never an admin -- so without
# this seed there is no way into the console at all. Set both, then run once:
#
#     pnpm --filter @swat/db seed:admin
#
# Idempotent: it never rewrites an existing admin's password, so re-running after
# you rotate it cannot restore the bootstrap value. Refuses a password under 12
# characters. Change the password after first login.

# Resend API key, from resend.com â†’ API Keys. âš ï¸ Secret â€” it carries send

EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS=10000

# â”€â”€ Execution Bot â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€

# Native balance retained instead of being offered as trade value.

# â”€â”€ Jupiter Swap API (Paper-Trade Simulation) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Used by: apps/trade-executor (paper-trade quote simulation)
# Get your free key at: https://developers.jup.ag/portal
# When set, paper trades fetch a real Jupiter swap quote to get accurate
# output amounts, price impact, and routing â€” instead of a naive spot-price
# division.  The system works without this key, but paper trades won't have
# AMM-routed accuracy.  No SOL or wallet required â€” quotes are read-only.
JUPITER_API_KEY=
JUPITER_QUOTE_TIMEOUT_MS=8000

# Which Solana executor carries a live trade: 'trojan' (default) or 'jupiter-jito'.
#
# Jupiter+Jito is built and unit-tested but NOT certified â€” checklist S3-9 requires
# a capped live canary recorded under docs/certification/solana.md first. Leaving
# this unset keeps the incumbent certified path. A typo throws at startup rather
# than falling back, so a misrouted execution variable cannot fail silently.
#
# Setting this alone is not sufficient: a signer (SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY) and a block
# engine (JITO_BLOCK_ENGINE_URL) must also be configured, and LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS
# plus an active chain_certifications row still gate live mode on top.
SOLANA_EXECUTOR=

# â”€â”€â”€ Solana live execution: Jupiter + Jito (DG-1) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Replaces the Trojan webhook path. Both remain wired until the new path is
# certified (checklist S3-6); `resolveChainMode` accepts either being ready and
# clamps Solana to paper when neither is.
#
# Base58-encoded 64-byte secret key. Absent = Solana cannot execute live, which
# is the correct default: a paper-mode box must not hold a signing key.
SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY=
# Defaults to the Helius endpoint derived from HELIUS_API_KEY when unset.
SOLANA_RPC_URL=
# Comma-separated list of fallback Solana RPC endpoints for automatic circuit-breaker failover.
# SOLANA_RPC_URLS=https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=...,https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com
# Jito block-engine base URL, e.g. https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf
# Deliberately has NO default: a wrong URL fails every bundle at submit time,
# and guessing one turns a config omission into a runtime mystery.
JITO_BLOCK_ENGINE_URL=
# Optional block-engine auth key (x-jito-auth).
JITO_AUTH_KEY=
# Hard ceiling on the tip, in lamports. Not advisory â€” without it a congestion
# spike or a malformed tip-floor response could spend an unbounded amount of SOL
# per trade, and the tip counts against position P&L. Default 5000000 (0.005 SOL).
JITO_MAX_TIP_LAMPORTS=5000000
# Used when the block engine's tip floor is unreadable. Default 100000.
JITO_FALLBACK_TIP_LAMPORTS=100000
# Tip floor percentile to target: p50 | p75 | p95. Higher lands more reliably
# and costs more. Default p75.
JITO_TIP_PERCENTILE=p75
# How long a submitted bundle stays pending before the sweep calls it ambiguous.
# Minimum 60000. Default 600000.
JITO_PENDING_TTL_MS=600000
JITO_TIMEOUT_MS=10000

# â”€â”€â”€ Pre-trade simulation on Solana (checklist S4-M15) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# The built Jupiter swap is run through the RPC simulator before a tip is fetched
# or anything is signed, so a broken route is discovered without paying for it.
#
# Opt-out, not opt-in: an unsimulated submit is the unsafe default. Set to false
# only to deliberately disable the gate. Simulation needs SOLANA_RPC_URL (or
# HELIUS_API_KEY); with neither, no gate is built and the swap submits unsimulated.
SOLANA_SIMULATION_ENABLED=true
# What to do when the simulator itself cannot answer (RPC down, timeout, malformed
# response) â€” as opposed to a simulation that actually reverted, which is ALWAYS a
# skip. 'skip' (default) fails closed: one missed copy trade, visibly reported with
# the distinct reason code solana-simulator-unreachable. 'submit' trades that
# safety for availability and must be chosen deliberately. A typo throws at
# startup rather than defaulting, so a misspelling cannot silently disable the gate.
SOLANA_SIMULATION_ON_UNAVAILABLE=skip
# Simulator deadline in milliseconds. Sits between the Jupiter swap-build timeout
# (8000) and the Jito submit timeout (10000): a slower simulation has spent more of
# the quote's life than the check is worth. Default 5000.
SOLANA_SIMULATION_TIMEOUT_MS=5000
# Optional hard cap on simulated compute units. UNSET BY DEFAULT AND DELIBERATELY
# SO â€” nothing in this repo configures a compute-unit limit today (the swap is
# built with no ComputeBudgetProgram instruction and no compute unit price), so any
# default here would be invented. Left unset the consumed units are reported for
# observability and never refuse a trade. Set it only from measured route data.
SOLANA_SIMULATION_MAX_COMPUTE_UNITS=

# â”€â”€ Trading Configuration â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Used by: apps/trade-executor, apps/api (/v1/trading/status)

# Exact, case-sensitive modes: off, paper, live, live+shadow.
# Precedence is database execution_config, chain-specific value, global value,
# then paper. Keep per-chain overrides commented to inherit TRADING_MODE.
TRADING_MODE=paper
# TRADING_MODE_SOLANA=paper
# TRADING_MODE_POLYGON=paper
# TRADING_MODE_ROBINHOOD_CHAIN=paper

# Comma-separated operator allowlist. A live/live+shadow request remains paper
# unless the chain is listed here AND has an active reviewed certification row.
LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS=

# Abort a Trojan request after this many milliseconds. Retried jobs reuse the
# signal ID as their idempotency key.
TROJAN_TIMEOUT_MS=15000

# Master switch for automatic trade execution.
# âš ï¸ Keep false until signal quality is validated over 2+ weeks.
# Used by: apps/trade-executor
AUTO_EXECUTE=false

# Minimum signal score (0â€“100) to trigger an automatic trade.
# Manual execution via /v1/signals/:id/execute ignores this threshold.
# Used by: apps/trade-executor
AUTO_EXECUTE_MIN_SCORE=85

# Base trade size in SOL before tier Ã— score multipliers are applied.
# Final size = BASE_POSITION_SOL Ã— tier_multiplier Ã— score_multiplier
#   eliteÃ—scoreâ‰¥90  â†’ 1.0 Ã— 1.0 Ã— base = full base
#   promisingÃ—scoreâ‰¥80 â†’ 0.5 Ã— 0.75 Ã— base = 37.5% of base
# Used by: apps/trade-executor, apps/alert-service (suggested execution display)
BASE_POSITION_SOL=0.5
MAX_POSITION_SOL=5

# Paper sizing inputs. PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT is intentionally omitted by
# default: Solana falls back to 5%, while EVM chains use their risk percentage.
PAPER_BANKROLL_USD=10000
# PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT=5

# Current executor-wide daily cap. Risk-policy consolidation remains tracked in
# the audit checklist; do not treat this as a per-chain certified risk policy.
DAILY_EXPOSURE_CAP_USD=50000

# â”€â”€ Copy Eligibility â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Enforced at the canonical claim boundary, before a signal is claimed for
# execution. Re-checks source selection at execution time, because the nightly
# scorer sweep can pause a wallet after the signal-engine emitted its signal.
# A stop-loss carries no source trade and is never gated here â€” an exit must
# stay possible after its source wallet has been dropped.
# Used by: apps/trade-executor
#
# Tolerance for an indexer clock running ahead of ours.
COPY_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS=30000
# Confirmed USD the source wallet must have traded in the lookback window.
# 0 disables the floor: notional is strategy-dependent, so it is opt-in.
COPY_MIN_SOURCE_ACTIVITY_USD=0
# Lifetime recorded trades the source wallet must have. Below this, any score it
# carries is an artifact of a tiny sample.
COPY_MIN_SOURCE_TRADES=3
# Window over which COPY_MIN_SOURCE_ACTIVITY_USD is measured (default 30 days).
COPY_ACTIVITY_LOOKBACK_MS=2592000000

# â”€â”€ Mirrorable Activity (S4-M5) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Minimum USD notional a tracked wallet's own trade must carry before it is
# mirrored. Excludes dust: a $2 remainder costs more in fees and slippage than
# the position is worth. 0 disables the floor and is the default, because a
# useful notional is strategy-dependent.
#
# NOT the same knob as COPY_MIN_SOURCE_ACTIVITY_USD above. That one is a track
# record floor â€” total confirmed USD the wallet traded over
# COPY_ACTIVITY_LOOKBACK_MS â€” and a wallet can clear it comfortably while still
# making a $2 trade. This one is per-event.
#
# Set it above 0 only knowing what it does on unpriced chains: source events
# carry no amount_usd on robinhood-chain at all, nor on any Solana route without
# a USDC/USDT leg. Those are reported as `source-notional-unknown` and skipped,
# since an amount nobody recorded cannot be shown to clear a floor.
# Used by: apps/signal-engine
SOURCE_COPY_MIN_NOTIONAL_USD=0

# â”€â”€ Copy signal shelf life (S4-M33) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# How old a tracked wallet's event may be and still be copied. Read by BOTH
# signal-engine (emit time) and trade-executor (submission time), each with its
# own 10-minute default.
#
# They must hold the SAME value, and the reason is not symmetry for its own sake:
# if the executor's window were tighter than the engine's, a signal would be fresh
# enough to create, alert on and queue, then stale enough to refuse at the venue --
# a skip for every copy with no failure anywhere to point at. One root .env makes
# that automatic; setting one of them only is what breaks it.
#
# Lower is not strictly safer. A shorter window refuses more late signals, but a
# refused copy of a buy leaves the user with no position while the master holds
# one, and there is no retry: the event ages out.
SOURCE_COPY_MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS=600000

# How old the master's position evidence may be when a SELL is sized. A copied
# sell is proportional to what the master exited, so it needs their position as it
# was at the time -- `computeCopySellProportion` throws rather than defaulting to
# sell-everything when the evidence is missing or too old, which is why this knob
# is a refusal boundary and not a hint. Same dual-reader rule as above.
SOURCE_COPY_POSITION_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_MS=600000

# â”€â”€ Signal Quality â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Signals with score below this threshold are logged to DB but NOT alerted.
# (Telegram alert is suppressed, trade queue is not touched)
# Used by: apps/signal-engine
MIN_SIGNAL_SCORE=70

# Shared external-request timeouts.
PRICE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=8000

# â”€â”€ Service Startup Flags â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Set to 'true' on the scorer and/or discovery service to run the batch
# immediately on startup instead of waiting for the 02:00/02:30 UTC cron.
# Useful for: first-run seeding, manual batch triggers.
# Used by: apps/scorer, apps/discovery
RUN_ON_STARTUP=false

# â”€â”€ Wallet Seeding â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Optional: comma-separated wallets to ingest on indexer start. Bare entries
# default to Solana; EVM entries must use polygon: or robinhood-chain: prefixes.
# Alternatively use the API: POST /v1/discovery/from-token or POST /v1/wallets
# Used by: apps/indexer/src/index.ts
WALLET_ADDRESSES=

# Optional starter-pack ingestion defaults. Entries may also be objects with
# their own `chain`, or strings prefixed with `solana:`, `polygon:`, or
# `robinhood-chain:`. Invalid/mismatched addresses fail before any DB write.
WALLET_CHAIN=solana
STARTER_PACK_PATH=wallet-starter-pack.json

# Bounded Helius history used by discover-starter-pack.ts. The discoverer skips
# launch/funder claims when it cannot reach the account origin within the cap.
DEX_CHAIN_ID=solana
STARTER_LAUNCH_WINDOW_TXS=50
STARTER_LAUNCH_SIGNATURE_CAP=20000
STARTER_WALLET_SIGNATURE_LIMIT=30
STARTER_FUNDER_SIGNATURE_CAP=5000
STARTER_FUNDER_TX_SCAN_LIMIT=50

# Parameters for token-based wallet discovery. Controls how far back to look
# when determining early and large buyers.
TOKEN_DISCOVERY_WINDOW=5000
TOKEN_DISCOVERY_MAX_TOTAL_SIGNATURES=20000
EARLY_BUYER_SLOTS=40
BIG_BUYER_SLOTS=10

# â”€â”€ EVM & Multi-Chain Configuration â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# RPC URLs. These explicit values match the runtime fallbacks; do not leave them
# blank because URL consumers distinguish an empty string from an unset value.
POLYGON_RPC_URL=https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com
ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL=https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com

# Multi-Provider RPC Failover pools (comma-separated fallback endpoints)
# POLYGON_RPC_URLS=https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com,https://polygon.llamarpc.com
# ROBINHOOD_RPC_URLS=https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com

# â”€â”€ Robinhood Chain (4663) execution â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Enforced by `pnpm check:env` -- every ROBINHOOD_* the code reads must appear
# here. That gate exists because this block previously documented THREE of the
# twenty-six, one of which (ROBINHOOD_QUOTER_V2) nothing read while the variable
# the code wants (ROBINHOOD_QUOTER) was absent -- so the documented value could
# never take effect, and its value was an ETHEREUM MAINNET address on a chain
# where that is not a quoter. See checklist S4-M39.
#
# âš ï¸ ADDRESSES BELOW MARKED "unknown" ARE NOT PLACEHOLDERS TO GUESS AT.
# A wrong address is worse than a blank one: it reads as configuration rather
# than as a gap. Live boot refuses any configured address with no deployed
# bytecode on the chain (robinhood-startup.ts), so a guess fails at startup
# rather than at the first trade -- but only in live mode. Leave them blank.
#
# VERIFIED on chain 4663 by RPC, 2026-08-31 -- safe to rely on:
#   Permit2         0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3  (42 chars, ends 78BA3)
#   L2 WETH         0x0Bd7D308f8E1639FAb988df18A8011f41EAcAD73  (symbol WETH, 18 dp)
#   USDG            0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168  (symbol USDG, 6 dp)
#   QuoterV2        0x33e885ed0ec9bf04ecfb19341582aadcb4c8a9e7  (answers factory(); its WETH9() == our WETH)
#   Uniswap V3 factory 0x1f7d7550b1b028f7571e69a784071f0205fd2efa  (read from the quoter, not assumed)
#   Rialto registry 0x71a120CbBf3Ce7cD910a3c50fF77aFc62735687E
#
# âš ï¸ USDG HAS 6 DECIMALS, NOT 18. Verified by decimals(). Every amount that
# crosses this token must be scaled by 1e6. Assuming 18 understates a balance by
# a factor of a trillion, which reads as "no funds" rather than as a bug.

# Chain id. Must match what ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL reports or live boot refuses.
ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID=4663

# Swap router.
# âš ï¸ Under S4-M13/S4-M40 this variable is expected to be REPLACED by a runtime
# lookup against the Rialto Router Registry (getFeature(featureId) -> the live
# router), so a router address is never pinned in config at all. That survives a
# Rialto router migration without a redeploy. Until that lands, this is required
# and its value is unknown -- there is no verified Uniswap SwapRouter on 4663.
ROBINHOOD_SWAP_ROUTER=

# Uniswap V3 QuoterV2, for pre-trade price discovery.
# Renamed from ROBINHOOD_QUOTER_V2, which nothing read; the old value was
# Ethereum mainnet's and is not a quoter on this chain.
# Verified 2026-08-31: 16,548 chars of code, factory() answers, and its WETH9()
# returns our L2 WETH exactly -- which is what distinguishes a real Uniswap
# quoter from an unrelated contract that happens to have code at the address.
ROBINHOOD_QUOTER=0x33e885ed0ec9bf04ecfb19341582aadcb4c8a9e7

# Wrapped ETH on the L2. Verified against docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts.
ROBINHOOD_WETH9=0x0Bd7D308f8E1639FAb988df18A8011f41EAcAD73

# What we spend on a buy and receive on a sell.
#   native-weth -> must EQUAL ROBINHOOD_WETH9. Simpler, but every position is
#                  ETH-denominated, so ETH's own price movement enters P&L on a
#                  trade that went nowhere.
#   erc20       -> a stablecoin (USDG). Cost basis is stable, which is what the
#                  S4-M35 USD cost-basis work assumes. Only worth it if USDG has
#                  real liquidity here; a stablecoin base with no pools is worse
#                  than WETH.
ROBINHOOD_BASE_ASSET_MODE=native-weth
ROBINHOOD_BASE_ASSET=0x0Bd7D308f8E1639FAb988df18A8011f41EAcAD73

# A second token, distinct from the base asset, used ONLY at startup: live boot
# quotes base -> this token across the configured fee tiers and refuses to start
# if no tier returns a route. It is a liveness probe for the quoter and the pool
# set, so it must be the most dependable liquidity on the chain.
# USDG/WETH is that pair -- verified pool reserves below.
ROBINHOOD_SANITY_TOKEN=0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168

# Uniswap V3 fee tiers to try, in order. Comma-separated, each below 1000000.
# NOT a guess -- measured on the WETH/USDG pools 2026-08-31 by reading each
# pool's token balances directly:
#     fee   100   1,357 WETH   5,178,280 USDG   <- deepest
#     fee   500     352 WETH   2,056,819 USDG
#     fee  3000      78 WETH   1,583,606 USDG
#     fee 10000    0.01 WETH          27 USDG   <- dust, deliberately EXCLUDED
# Ordered deepest first so the first tier that returns a route is also the one
# with the least price impact. 10000 is omitted on purpose: a pool that exists
# but holds nothing still returns a quote, at a price that would be a large
# realised loss -- "a pool exists" and "a pool can fill this" are different
# facts, and only the second one matters here.
ROBINHOOD_FEE_TIERS=100,500,3000

# ABI variants. Only these exact strings are accepted; anything else throws.
ROBINHOOD_ROUTER_ABI_VERSION=uniswap-v3-swap-router-01
ROBINHOOD_QUOTER_ABI_VERSION=uniswap-v3-quoter-v2

# Gas ceilings, in units. maxApprovalGas leaves the budget entirely once S4-M13
# lands, because Permit2 removes the on-chain approve from the steady-state path.
ROBINHOOD_MAX_SWAP_GAS=400000
ROBINHOOD_MAX_APPROVAL_GAS=80000

# Refuse to submit above this gas price rather than paying any price to land.
ROBINHOOD_MAX_FEE_PER_GAS_GWEI=10

# Slippage ceiling in basis points. A loss limit, not MEV protection -- ADR-0006
# is explicit that a single sequencer monopolises reordering rather than removing
# it, and this bound is all that caps the loss.
ROBINHOOD_MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS=100

# Reject a token whose transfer takes a fee above this (basis points). A
# fee-on-transfer token breaks the quantity maths silently.
ROBINHOOD_MAX_TRANSFER_FEE_BPS=0

# How long to wait for a receipt before treating a submission as unresolved.
ROBINHOOD_RECEIPT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000

# â”€â”€ Robinhood Chain ingestion (indexer) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
# Router addresses whose logs count as swaps. Comma-separated; falls back to
# ROBINHOOD_SWAP_ROUTER when unset. Plural because ingestion should keep
# recognising an old router through a migration window, which is exactly what the
# Rialto registry's prev() dwell window describes.
ROBINHOOD_INGESTION_ROUTERS=

# Pools the indexer will attribute swaps from, as JSON:
#   [{"address":"0x...","token0":"0x...","token1":"0x..."}]
# An explicit allowlist by design -- an unreviewed pool is ignored rather than
# trusted, so a fake pool cannot inject a fabricated trade. Required and
# non-empty; without it the indexer sees no Robinhood Chain swaps at all.
# Verified 2026-08-31 via factory.getPool(WETH, USDG, fee) and each pool's own
# token0()/token1() -- read from the chain, never hand-assembled, because a
# token0/token1 the wrong way round silently inverts every price this produces.
# token0 is WETH and token1 is USDG on all three, which is address order, not a
# choice. The 10000 tier's pool is real but holds dust and is excluded for the
# same reason it is excluded from ROBINHOOD_FEE_TIERS.
ROBINHOOD_REVIEWED_POOLS_JSON=[{"address":"0x52e65b17fb6e5ba00ed806f37afcd2daa50271ca","token0":"0x0bd7d308f8e1639fab988df18a8011f41eacad73","token1":"0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168"},{"address":"0x69bfaf19c9f377bb306a89aed9f6b07e2c1a8d9a","token0":"0x0bd7d308f8e1639fab988df18a8011f41eacad73","token1":"0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168"},{"address":"0xa9188730fe85be88ad499d7d52b099e800fb0334","token0":"0x0bd7d308f8e1639fab988df18a8011f41eacad73","token1":"0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168"}]

# Private Key for live trading on EVM chains (Polymarket CLOB & Robinhood Uniswap V3)
# Keep empty to run in paper trading mode or simulated EVM execution
EVM_PRIVATE_KEY=

# Polymarket CLOB V2 identity. EOA uses the signer as funder; proxy, Safe, and

POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE=EOA

==> .woodpecker.yaml <==
when:
  - event: [push, pull_request, manual]

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: swat_integration
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: swat
    ports:
      - 5432

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - 6379

steps:
  - name: prepare
    image: node:22-slim
    commands:
      - corepack enable
      - corepack prepare pnpm@10.2.0 --activate
      - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - cp .env.example .env
      - sed -i "s|localhost:5432|postgres:5432|g" .env
      - sed -i "s|127.0.0.1:5432|postgres:5432|g" .env
      - sed -i "s|localhost:6379|redis:6379|g" .env
      - sed -i "s|127.0.0.1:6379|redis:6379|g" .env
      - sed -i "s|:5432/swat|:5432/swat_integration|g" .env
      - sed -i "s|POSTGRES_DB=swat|POSTGRES_DB=swat_integration|g" .env
      - echo "INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://swat:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration" >> .env
      - pnpm check:secrets
      - pnpm check:env

  - name: verify
    image: node:22-slim
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://swat:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration
      INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://swat:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration
      ADMIN_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
    commands:
      - corepack enable
      - corepack prepare pnpm@10.2.0 --activate
      - pnpm db:init:ci
      - pnpm db:migrate
      - pnpm typecheck

  - name: test
    image: node:22-slim
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://swat:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration
      INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://swat:swat@postgres:5432/swat_integration
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
      TRADING_MODE: paper
      AUTO_EXECUTE: "false"
      API_KEY: swat-ci-key
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY: swat-ci-key
    commands:
      - corepack enable
      - corepack prepare pnpm@10.2.0 --activate
      - pnpm test
      - pnpm build
      - pnpm test:integration

## Phase 4 completion map

### Current position

The branch has most of the pure decision logic and several production wirings, but the remaining work falls into three different classes:

- **Near-term code path:** finish lot-aware accounting and lifecycle exits, then prove multi-user paper fan-out end to end.
- **Production hardening:** wire and verify the remaining venue, capacity, observability, and monitoring controls.
- **External launch gates:** legal approval, custody/delegation infrastructure, provider decisions, real-chain configuration, and withdrawal controls. These cannot be closed by more TypeScript alone.

The migration/profile boundary is now in place. Core work must continue against clean `*_integration` databases with `SWAT_DB_PROFILE=core`; LP remains opt-in through `SWAT_DB_PROFILE=lp` and stays out of the core implementation.

## Batch 1: Finish S4-M3 lot-aware lifecycle

**Goal:** make every open tenant position attributable to a master lot and closeable through every exit path.

1. **Lot-scoped P&L and stop-loss snapshots**
   - Refactor `packages/db/src/pnl-queries.ts` to derive open snapshots from `copy_position_master_lots` / reductions, preserving the operator aggregate path for legacy rows.
   - Emit one snapshot per open `(user, master, signal, token)` lot scope with `positionKey`; preserve signal-level P&L rollup by summing disjoint lot results.
   - Keep unknown, oversold, mixed-token, and missing-price states fail-closed.
   - Thread `positionKey` into scorer claims, job IDs, and releases while retaining the exact legacy operator behavior.
   - Add tests for two masters on one signal, two lots for one master, FIFO reductions, winding-down users, and independent stop-loss claims.

2. **Manual exit and redemption allocation**
   - Extend the existing Polymarket three-entrant race in `packages/db/src/polymarket-exit-queries.ts` / `apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-exit-race.ts` to carry lot identity and exact quantity.
   - Allocate manual sells and mirrored sells through the master-lot allocator; redemption must preserve outcome-token identity and allocate proceeds to the matching open lots.
   - Add a chain-generic position-exit claim if manual Solana/Robinhood exits still lack a durable single-shot claim; do not reuse stop-loss claims because their schema is stop-loss-specific.
   - Verify the race remains one winner for mirrored sell, resolution redemption, and manual exit, including concurrent/replay cases.

3. **Close-all consumer and subscription transitions**
   - Add a consumer for `close_all_requested_at` that enumerates exact open lots, enqueues exact-quantity sells, and records idempotent exit claims.
   - Transition `winding_down -> ended` only after no open lots remain; do not end merely because enqueue succeeded.
   - Redirect the API unsubscribe route from hard delete to `beginWindDown` or direct `ended` only when no open positions exist.
   - Change `pauseUnsubscribedWallets` to use `state <> 'ended'` and retain sell eligibility for winding-down rows.
   - Add integration coverage for unsubscribe, close-all replay, final close, and re-subscribe/member-slot behavior.

**Batch gate:** clean core migration replay, lifecycle integration, lot allocator tests, P&L/stop-loss tests, exit-race tests, and explicit integration typecheck all pass.

## Batch 2: Prove the paper fan-out path end to end

**Goal:** turn the existing pure fan-out work into a durable multi-user execution path.

1. **Wire source-signal fan-out fully**
   - Confirm `processSourceTradeSignals` calls candidate enumeration, `planFanout`, capacity resolution, and `enqueueFanoutTradeJobs` exactly once per source signal.
   - Ensure enumeration failure falls back only to the legacy operator job and never accidentally admits users.
   - Ensure `source_dispatched_at` is marked only after all required enqueue work succeeds, with stable per-user job IDs and durable tenant uniqueness guards.

2. **Complete per-user sizing and risk threading**
   - Pass the user principal through sizing, risk policy lookup, breaker keys, rolling exposure, daily exposure, paper bankroll, slippage, and execution settings.
   - Fix the known `FanoutVerdict.downgraded` / requested-mode propagation gap so platform clamping is observable and cannot re-widen downstream.
   - Decide and implement the per-user paper bankroll representation rather than silently sharing the operator bankroll.
   - Keep `RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT='operator'` separate from risk-policy account keys.

3. **Capacity and ledger verification**
   - Run migration `053` on a clean database and exercise one admitted cohort plus one rejected cohort.
   - Verify the capacity ledger writer is idempotent under evidence replay and that Polygon uses the real Redis book feed while AMM chains use their declared approximate liquidity basis.
   - Confirm capacity skips are uniform and expose only the generic user message; retain detailed internal reason codes.

4. **End-to-end tenant isolation test**
   - Drive two paper users through the same source signal and token.
   - Assert separate `trades`, `copy_executions`, `copy_positions`, lots, P&L, stop-loss claims, job IDs, exposure, and breaker state.
   - Assert legacy operator rows still use null user identity and old job/release compatibility.

**Batch gate:** a clean Docker Postgres/Redis run demonstrates two users copying one signal with disjoint quantities/cost basis, stable retry idempotency, and no cross-user claim or cap interference.

## Batch 3: Close the remaining immediate venue-path gaps

Run these as focused slices after Batch 2, keeping each behind its own test seam:

- **Polymarket FAK mirror bound wiring:** add a real `handleJob` execution-lifecycle fixture that reaches the Polymarket branch and proves master-fill price bounds are used.
- **Polymarket exit escalation:** wire the existing rung ladder into the guarded reconciliation path; never create a second timer or bypass the exit claim.
- **Jupiter V2 migration:** replace undocumented V1 construction with `/swap/v2/build`, assemble instructions safely, set `forJitoBundle: true`, preserve tip accounting, and resolve the live API host/key behavior with one real request.
- **Permit2/Rialto settlement:** record the already-decided split, resolve the Router Registry at runtime, decode and policy-check any aggregator calldata before signing, then wire the chosen settlement path with no guessed router address.
- **Augmented neg-risk guard:** fetch the required event-level fields and reject unnamed/placeholder outcomes with actionable skip reasons.
- **Solana LP/liquid-staking probe:** implement the decided routability probe with asymmetric caching and fail-open-on-probe-error semantics, scoped to Solana only.

**Batch gate:** executor integration tests cover happy path, stale/invalid market, unavailable feed, off-tick/minimum-size, escalation failure, and policy rejection. No live path signs opaque or uninspected calldata.

## Batch 4: Operational and observability controls

- **S4-M23 tracking difference:** thread master fill and follower fill through the executor ledger, persist the typed unknown/computed result, expose it through the API, and add the UI surface without turning unknown into zero.
- **S4-M25 integration typecheck:** formalize the integration `tsconfig`, include Fastify augmentation correctly, and run it in CI.
- **S4-M26 detector coverage:** extract detector queries from the interval-starting signal-engine composition root, then add query/parse tests.
- **S4-M10/M11 independence:** add explorer label lookup/cache, distinguish independent/unassessed/hub, refuse confirmed exchange hubs, and provide advisory funding/behavior cluster warnings.
- **S4-M42 pUSD monitor:** add the polling/alert job for native-USDC pool depth, pause state, simulated unwrap, and partial/unknown outcomes.
- **S4-M21 ingestion decision:** either obtain a Helius tier that supports `transactionSubscribe` or record the current-plan limitation and select the next acceptable ingestion mode; do not claim the item complete without the required feed.
- **S4-M17/M24:** standardize actionable skip reasons and alerting across all new exit/venue failure paths.

**Batch gate:** CI runs unit, package typecheck, integration typecheck, and clean-database integration suites; operational monitors produce explicit unknown/impaired states rather than false healthy results.

## Batch 5: Custody, authority, and withdrawal launch gates

These are Phase 4 work but not prerequisites for proving paper fan-out. Track them separately so they do not contaminate the core loop:

1. **Authority and EVM:** pin EntryPoint, finish on-chain argument-scoped enforcement, verify the 4663 account/delegate path against a real bundler, and close the remaining Permit2/router configuration.
2. **Solana delegation:** evaluate or implement the audited destination-constrained delegation program; this is the long pole and should not be hidden behind application abstractions.
3. **Polymarket authority:** implement the selected fork-b signer/grant flow, seal credentials, and ensure signing material never leaves trade-executor.
4. **Grant lifecycle:** persist expiry/revocation, warn before expiry, surface lapsed grants as a distinct skip reason, and add re-consent.
5. **Paymaster/relay:** finish the Rialto gasless pricing/quotas decision first; only then build per-user and global sponsored-operation caps if self-paymaster remains selected.
6. **Per-user SOL reserve:** enforce the live USD 10 equivalent gate before each Solana trade with explicit funded/underfunded/price-unknown outcomes.
7. **Withdrawal anti-theft core:** verified email, linked-wallet verification and cooling-off, Resend delivery semantics, signed transfer only to an eligible wallet, daily cap, and adversarial tests.
8. **Legal and geo controls:** counsel/ToS/risk disclosures, Cloudflare geo-block, consent-time Polymarket eligibility with staleness enforcement. These remain external launch gates even after code is complete.

**Batch gate:** no custody launch until the checklist's paper fan-out, withdrawal adversarial suite, key/log/API scan, Vault Transit staging migration, and legal/geo approvals are all green.

## Recommended execution order

1. Batch 1: lot-aware P&L, exits, close-all, unsubscribe.
2. Batch 2: clean-database two-user paper fan-out and capacity verification.
3. Batch 3: Polymarket/Jupiter/Permit2/LP venue gaps in parallel slices.
4. Batch 4: observability, detector coverage, monitors, and CI integration typecheck.
5. Batch 5: custody, withdrawal, provider, and legal gates.

This order preserves the existing safety decisions: no destructive LP cleanup, no fabricated liquidity/prices, no bypass of the three-way Polymarket exit race, no widening of user settings through platform defaults, and no live custody claim before the external controls exist.

## Status legend

- `[x]` â€” implemented, focused tests pass, evidence in the repo.
- `[ ]` â€” not started or partial; the **Done when** line is the acceptance test.
- `[!]` â€” **blocker or correction.** Do these before the stage they sit in.
- `(ext)` â€” **cannot be closed by code.** Needs credentials, funded wallets, a canary, a human
  reviewer, **a fact we do not have, or a decision only the operator can make.** The last two were
  added 2026-08-22: an item blocked on "which labels feed do we use" is as unclosable by
  engineering as one blocked on a funded wallet, and hiding it among ordinary open work meant it
  was picked up, half-built, and put down again. Every such item is listed in
  **Â§0 Information needed** with what would close it.
- `[=]` â€” **standing constraint.** A rule every other item must honour, not a task. It has no done
  state; it is listed so nobody re-opens it as a gap or builds against it by accident.
- `[â†’]` â€” **pointer.** Not separate work. Closes when the item it names closes.

**Classification added 2026-08-22, nothing deleted.** One unchecked box had been doing four
different jobs â€” buildable work, work blocked on a human, a rule that can never be "done", and a
cross-reference â€” which made the open count useless as a measure of remaining work. The items are
unchanged; only their kind is now visible.

## How to test what has been built â€” added 2026-09-13

**Asked by the operator: "at what stage can we test our build so far in case we have issues?"** The
honest answer has three stages, because this branch has been built with **no database and no Redis**,
and that determines exactly which faults are already impossible and which are still completely
unobserved.

### Stage A â€” runs today, needs nothing (and already passes)

No infrastructure, no keys, no network. This is what has been run after every change:

```bash
pnpm --filter @swat/<pkg> typecheck     # per package; all 11 clean
pnpm --filter @swat/<pkg> exec vitest run
pnpm check:secrets                      # no browser-exposed secrets
pnpm check:env                           # every governed env var documented
```

**2,567 tests pass across nine packages.** Do NOT run `pnpm build`, `pnpm dev` or
`docker-compose up` â€” the operator's machine crashes on them. Per-package commands only.

**What Stage A can prove:** every *decision* â€” who is eligible, what the cap admits, whether a book
is stale, whether a figure is unknown rather than zero. These are pure functions with injected
ports, and they are mutation-tested rather than merely green.

**What Stage A structurally CANNOT prove, and this is the important half:** that any SQL runs, that
any migration applies, that Redis round-trips, that a venue's field names still match, or that two
processes agree on a wire format. Every one of those is mocked. A unit test cannot fail when
Polymarket renames a field.

### Stage B â€” needs Redis + outbound network (~5 minutes to set up)

The first stage that exercises real I/O. One command, and it is the highest-value test available
right now because it closes the single largest unknown on the branch:

```bash
pnpm acceptance:polymarket-book
```

Needs **Redis only** â€” deliberately *not* Postgres, so it can run before any migration has ever been
applied. It discovers live markets from Polymarket's public Gamma API (nothing hardcoded, so it
cannot rot), then checks six things in order: Redis reachable â†’ `POST /books` returns rows â†’ the rows
carry a ladder â†’ the live WebSocket delivers a snapshot â†’ **the entry written by `indexer` comes back
out of Redis decodable by `signal-engine`'s reader** â†’ the depth model produces a *priced* verdict
rather than a plausible unknown. It writes only its own book keys and deletes them on the way out;
there is no order path in the file, so it cannot trade.

That fifth step is the one that matters: it is the only place the bytes leave the process, and it is
what 115 unit tests structurally cannot cover.

Also runnable at this stage, against a throwaway database:

```bash
pnpm db:migrate                    # needs Postgres; applies all 57 migrations
pnpm test:integration              # refuses to run unless the DB name ends _integration/_test
pnpm acceptance:g0-d11
pnpm acceptance:polymarket-context
```

**Expect failures here, and that is the point.** Nothing in `packages/db/sql/` has ever executed.
The migrations are idempotent *by inspection*, which is not the same as verified.

### Stage C â€” needs funded wallets and a reviewed certification

Live execution stays gated behind `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` **and** an active `chain_certifications` row.
`TRADING_MODE=paper` and `AUTO_EXECUTE=false` stay set until that review happens. Everything in Â§0
that is marked `(ext)` blocks this stage, not the two above it.

### The recommendation

**Set up Redis and run `pnpm acceptance:polymarket-book` before building anything further on top of
the book feed.** It is five minutes of setup against a whole subsystem that has never touched a real
socket, and a venue-shape surprise found now is cheap â€” found after the per-user sizing and billing
work stacks on top of it, it is not.

**Engine is complete and green.** Audit batches Aâ€“F all landed: build fix, CI, artifact cleanup, account-keyed circuit breaker, DB-resolved risk policy, stop-loss enforcement, reconciliation coordinator, copy-eligibility policy, read/write pool split, BRIN index, `pg_stat_statements`, chaos fixtures, per-chain pipeline fixtures, and the four Polymarket partials. Ingestion, scoring, clustering, signal detection, alerting, and paper execution work end to end on all three chains.

**Stage 0 blockers cleared; Stages 1 and 2 complete; Stage 3 codeable half in progress** (2026-08-05). Identity, sessions, SIWE/SIWS wallet linking, tiers/roles, the `forUser()` tenancy layer, the audit log, per-user subscriptions with transactional quotas, admin-gated global routes, and two mutation-tested isolation/safety suites are all in place. Stage 3 has the Jito bundle client, Jupiter swap build, CLOB V2 auth, and the Jupiter+Jito runtime â€” see Â§6.0.

**Still absent (Stages 4â€“7):** `user_execution_grants`, `user_balances`, `user_execution_settings`, `subscriptions`, `payments`, `chains`; no `packages/authority`; no `wake-vault` Anchor program; no `user_id` on `trades`/`copy_executions` yet; no Stripe, wagmi, or email provider dependency; the frontend is unrebuilt (`/workspace` still unauthenticated, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` still shipped â€” both S6).

**The groundwork that keeps Stage 4 cheap:** Standing Rule 2 is honoured across the risk surface. `account: string` is threaded through `resolveRiskPolicy`, `circuit-breaker` (`breaker:${account}:${chain}`), `stop-loss`, and `copy-eligibility`. Every caller passes the literal `'operator'`, so per-user risk is *mostly* a value-substitution exercise rather than a signature rewrite.

**Three exceptions, verified in source 2026-08-07 â€” do not assume the substitution is uniform:**
- **`runStopLossSweep` needs a signature change, not a substituted value.** It resolves **one** account before the loop (`apps/scorer/src/stop-loss.ts:85`) and then claims every position under it. With `signal_stop_losses` keyed `PRIMARY KEY (account, signal_id)` (`034_stop_loss_triggers.sql:18`), under fan-out the **first user to breach claims the signal and every other holder is never sold** â€” the position stays open past its stop. The account must become per-position, sequenced *after* migration `050`.
- **`RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT` must stay `'operator'`.** It is an escalation label, not a tenancy key â€” the C1 code carries a comment saying exactly that, because `copy_executions.target_account` holds a wallet address and filtering it by an account value claims zero rows. Mechanically substituting a user id here fragments one alert stream into N while scoping nothing. `S4-P2` therefore introduced a **separate** `RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT` constant in the executor: that one *does* become the user id, and keeping the two literals apart is what stops a later find-and-replace from breaking reconciliation.
- **The risk policy was not reaching live sizing at all** â€” see `S4-P2`. Substituting a user id into `resolveRiskPolicy` would have had no effect on a live trade before that fix, because the call sat inside a paper-only branch.

Four of these are defects **in the planning documents**, found by reading them against the code. Building on them as written would put a wrong tenancy key into a table that later holds real money.

- [x] **S0-B1 â€” `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` is not empty.** *(Closed 2026-08-04.)* `.env:66` read `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS=solana,robinhood-chain`, contradicting both `audit-history.md` and `G2-R13`. Nothing was live â€” `TRADING_MODE=paper`, `AUTO_EXECUTE=false`, and `chain_certifications` had **0 rows** (verified) â€” but one of two independent controls was off, and `G2-R13` forbids `robinhood-chain` appearing here before its certification doc is reviewed.
  **Fixed:** set to empty with a comment stating both gates required to re-add a chain.

- [x] **S0-B2 â€” build artifacts tracked again.** *(Closed 2026-08-04.)* 30 `.turbo/cache/*` files, reintroduced by commit `71624e1` after task A3 removed them.

- [x] **S0-B3 â€” `bullmq` / `ioredis` declared but not installed.** *(Closed 2026-08-04.)* Root `devDependencies` listed both; neither was in `node_modules`, so `chaos.integration.test.ts` failed to load.

- [x] **S0-B4 â€” stale integration schema produced a misleading failure cascade.** *(Closed 2026-08-04. Root cause differs from the original diagnosis â€” recorded because the wrong one is easy to re-reach.)*
  **What was seen:** `pnpm test:integration` failed 20/20, loudest error a *cleanup* failure, and an orphaned `trades` row (`copy_execution_id` set, `signal_id`/`source_trade_id` NULL) was blocking migration `030`.
  **What it looked like:** a third instance of the E2 fixture-teardown selector gap.
  **What it actually was:** `swat_integration` was stranded at migration `029`. On a migrated database that orphan shape **cannot exist** â€” `030` adds both `chk_trades_copy_execution_identity_complete` (rejects the shape on insert) and `fk_trades_copy_execution_identity ... ON DELETE RESTRICT` (a `copy_executions` delete fails loudly rather than orphaning). The teardown logic was never at fault; an extra delete statement for that shape would have been unreachable dead code.
  **Fixed:** `tests/integration/helpers/schema-guard.ts` + `tests/integration/global-setup.ts` assert the schema is current **once, before any test file**, failing with a single actionable message naming the missing objects, the newest migration on disk, and the command to run. It checks for late-migration tables/columns rather than counting applied files, because `migrate.ts` deliberately keeps no applied-migrations table (D16) â€” the schema is the only record. `trades` was also added to the teardown's leftover-verification count, so a stray trade can never again let cleanup report success.
  **Verified:** suite green 28/28 against a current schema; a deliberately stale scratch database produces exactly one error naming `signal_stop_losses`, `copy_eligibility_rejections`, and `trades.venue_settlement_status`.

- [x] **S1-B5 â€” `target_account` does not hold a user id.** *(Resolved 2026-08-04 â€” `docs/adr/0001-tenancy-key.md`.)* `saas-conversion-plan.md` Â§Phase 3 claimed "`target_account` already exists in 028 and maps to user id." It does not: `apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts:904` fills it from `resolveLiveCopyTargetAccount(chain)` / `resolvePaperCopyTargetAccount(chain)` â€” a **chain-prefixed wallet address**. Both fan-out uniqueness constraints were therefore keyed on a wallet, not a tenant.
  **Decided:** explicit `user_id UUID` FK is the tenancy key; `target_account` keeps its real meaning (settlement wallet). Reusing the address was rejected for two reasons found while writing the ADR: paper mode has a synthetic per-chain address, so **every paper user on a chain would collide onto one key** and the unique constraint would admit exactly one user's paper execution per source trade â€” breaking the default path for every free-tier user; and a custodial key rotation (`user_trading_wallets.key_version` exists precisely because rotation is expected) would fork a user's execution history, silently resetting their P&L, exposure cap, and breaker.
  **Consequence:** no signature changes needed â€” the `account: string` parameter already threaded through the risk surface (Standing Rule 2) becomes the user id at Stage 4. `saas-conversion-plan.md` corrected.

- [x] **S1-B6 â€” migration numbering in the SaaS plan was stale.** *(Closed 2026-08-05.)* The plan said "new migrations `029+`"; `029`â€“`038` were already consumed by audit work. Stage 1 took **`039`â€“`043`**, and Â§11 now reserves a range per stage so the next collision cannot happen silently.

That file is now a 509-line marketing landing page whose `enterWorkspace()` is a bare `router.push('/workspace')` â€” there is no login at all, fake or otherwise, and no route protection. ## 4. Stage 1 â€” Auth & tenancy *(SaaS Phase 1)*

*May start in parallel with Stage 0 infra once CI is green â€” it touches no execution code.*

### 4.1 Decide first
- [x] **S1-1** `DG-5` resolved (`docs/adr/0001-tenancy-key.md`) and `DG-6` numbering corrected. Construction spec written: **`docs/plans/stage-1-design.md`** â€” DDL, session/credential parameters, SIWE/SIWS flow, route contracts, `forUser()` layer, test plan.

### 4.2 Schema â€” migrations `039`â€“`043` *(applied 2026-08-04; replayed twice clean on both databases; 43/43)*
- [x] **S1-2** `039_users.sql` â€” `CITEXT` email (case-insensitive uniqueness is a column property, so no call site can bypass it), argon2id `password_hash` as `TEXT` (encoded hashes change length when parameters are tuned), CHECKs on role/tier/status, partial index on `tier_expires_at`. `tier_expires_at IS NULL` means **lifetime**, not expired.
- [x] **S1-3** `040_user_sessions.sql` â€” SHA-256 `token_hash` only, never the raw token, so a database dump cannot be replayed as a login. Fast hash is correct here (256-bit CSPRNG token has no low-entropy secret to protect); argon2 is for passwords. `revoked_at` set rather than row deleted, so logout-everywhere leaves a trail.
- [x] **S1-4** `041_user_auth_wallets.sql` â€” `UNIQUE (chain_kind, address)` **globally, not per user**: one wallet proves one identity, otherwise Stage 4's withdraw-to-linked-wallet-only control has no single answer to whose address it is. `chain_kind` not `chain`, because an EVM signature proves control on every EVM chain at once.
- [x] **S1-5** `042_user_api_keys.sql` â€” indexed `UNIQUE key_prefix` so verification is one indexed equality plus one constant-time compare; the scan-all-and-compare alternative degrades linearly and is a timing oracle.
- [x] **S1-6** `043_audit_log.sql` â€” **no FK on `actor_id`, deliberately**: the log must outlive the user it describes, and a failed login for a nonexistent email has no user to reference â€” precisely the row worth keeping during credential stuffing. `actor_type = 'anonymous'` covers pre-auth events.

  **Verified by direct SQL probe, not assumed** â€” each design claim exercised in a rolled-back transaction: `Alice@Example.com` then `alice@example.com` rejected by `users_email_key`; `tier='platinum'` and `role='superuser'` rejected; a second user claiming a linked address rejected by `uq_auth_wallet` while the same address under a different `chain_kind` is allowed; `chain_kind='bitcoin'` rejected; deleting a user cascades its sessions to zero; `audit_log` accepts both an anonymous actor and an `actor_id` for a nonexistent user, and rejects `actor_type='robot'`.
- [x] **S1-7** Admin seed. **Split from `039` deliberately:** a migration that seeds a credential would put a password hash in a file that replays on every deploy (D16), and would make the schema undeployable without also choosing an admin password. `packages/db/src/seed-admin.ts` + `pnpm seed:admin` instead. **Never rewrites an existing admin's password**, so re-running after the operator rotates it cannot restore the bootstrap value; refuses a password under 12 chars (the one account that reaches every admin route is the worst place for an exception); tolerates losing a race with a concurrent seed. Existing operator `trades`/`copy_executions` keep `user_id NULL` per ADR-0001 and are never backfilled â€” attributing historical single-operator activity to an account would corrupt its P&L, expectancy, and exposure caps with trades it never made.
  **Verified:** no-env â†’ no-action Â· weak password â†’ refused Â· proper â†’ created Â· re-run with a *different* password â†’ no-action.

- [x] **S1-16** Cross-tenant CI suite + browser-secret lint. *(Both land before Stage 2's `/v1/me/*` routes exist, not after â€” that ordering is the point.)*
  `tests/integration/cross-tenant.integration.test.ts` â€” 8 cases against the **real** auth plugin and routes, mounted on a minimal Fastify app rather than importing `apps/api/src/index.ts` (which opens Redis and BullMQ at module scope; importing it would start a second API against the test database â€” the same constraint the pipeline suite documents for `signal-engine`). It includes a stand-in `/v1/me/wallets` route so the scoping path is exercised now and inherited by real routes later. Covers: wallet isolation between tenants, no-credential 401, **tenant-less legacy service key refused on a per-user route**, normal user â†’ admin route 403, one tenant's CSRF token paired with another's session 403, logout revoking only the logging-out tenant, cross-tenant wallet link 409, and own-wallet re-link idempotent.
  **Mutation-tested, so the suite is known to have teeth:** deleting the `WHERE user_id = $1` filter from `listAuthWallets` â€” the classic tenancy bug â€” turned it red immediately (2 failures). A green isolation suite that cannot fail is worse than none, because it licenses the assumption it never checked.
  `scripts/check-public-secrets.mjs` + `pnpm check:secrets`, wired into CI **before** typecheck so it fails fast. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined into the client bundle and shipped to every visitor, so a secret there is *published*, not configured. The existing `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` is grandfathered with a pointer to S6-3; the script's job is that no **new** one can appear while that work is pending. **Verified both directions:** passes on the tree as-is (197 files, 1 grandfathered), and rejects a planted `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` with exit 1.

**Exit gate:** âœ… **met 2026-08-05.** signup â†’ login â†’ wallet-link â†’ `/v1/auth/me` end to end; cross-tenant suite green in CI; browser holds no *new* shared secret (the pre-existing one is tracked by S6-3 and blocked from growing).
Full gate: typecheck 13/13 Â· test 13/13 Â· build 11/11 Â· **integration 36/36 across 6 files** Â· migrations 43/43.

### 4.3 API â€” `apps/api/src/auth/` *(built 2026-08-05)*
- [x] **S1-8** `POST /v1/auth/signup`, `/login`, `/logout`; `GET /v1/auth/me`. Login returns a byte-identical 401 for unknown-email and wrong-password, backed by the matching argon2 burn in `authenticateUser` so timing agrees with the body.
- [x] **S1-9** `POST /v1/auth/wallet/nonce` and `/verify` â€” SIWE (EIP-4361 via `viem`) and SIWS (ed25519 via `tweetnacl`/`bs58`). Serves both linking (session present) and wallet-only login (no session). A proven signature for an *unlinked* wallet is **not** an account â€” creating one there would let anyone with a keypair mint accounts without an email.
  Nonces are consumed with Redis **`GETDEL`**: a `GET`-then-`DEL` pair lets two concurrent requests both observe the same nonce, which is precisely the replay the nonce exists to stop. The nonce is also bound to the address it was issued for, so one minted for wallet A cannot be spent proving control of wallet B.
- [x] **S1-10** Layered auth plugin replacing the global `onRequest` key hook: session cookie â†’ per-user API key (reserved) â†’ legacy `X-Api-Key` as a **tenant-less service principal**. `requireUser` rejects the service principal outright rather than trusting each route to remember.
- [x] **S1-11** `requireTier` / `requireRole`. An expired paid tier degrades to `free`; `tier_expires_at IS NULL` means lifetime and is never read as expired.
- [x] **S1-12** `@fastify/rate-limit` â€” 300/min globally, plus a scoped 10/15-min bucket on credential routes keyed on **IP + email**, so one attacker cannot lock out a whole NAT and one account cannot be sprayed from a single address. Double-submit CSRF on every state-changing cookie request; `SameSite=Lax` is deliberate (see design doc) and CSRF covers what it does not.
- [x] **S1-13** SSE tickets preserved and hardened â€” see the regression below.
- [x] **S1-14** Legacy `API_KEY` is now service/admin-only and carries no tenant.

  **Verified against a live server, not just types.** Three defects surfaced that unit tests would not have caught:
  1. **SSE was briefly left unauthenticated.** Moving the hook dropped the ticket check, and `GET /v1/logs/stream` performs *no validation of its own* â€” the old hook was the only gate. Ticket consumption is now injected into the plugin (`consumeSseTicket`) with a comment recording that the route cannot be trusted to check.
  2. **Auth routes were registered before the hook.** Fastify applies a parent's hooks only to children registered *after* `addHook`, so `request.principal` was never populated for them â€” an authenticated wallet-link request was silently treated as an anonymous wallet-only login and returned 401. Registration order is now explicit and commented.
  3. **Public paths returned before resolving the session.** `POST /v1/auth/wallet/verify` is public (wallet-only login needs it) but must still see a session when one exists, or linking can never work. The hook now resolves opportunistically on public paths, still enforces CSRF when a session is present, and lets a *stale* cookie through so an expired user can log in again without manually clearing cookies.

  **Live probe results:** health 200 Â· no-creds 401 Â· wrong-key 401 Â· legacy-key 200 Â· bearer 401 Â· SSE-no-ticket 401 Â· signup 201 Â· me-with-session 200 Â· me-without 401 Â· duplicate-signup 409 Â· wrong-password and unknown-email both `401 {"error":"Invalid credentials"}` Â· short-password 400 Â· POST-without-CSRF 403 Â· POST-with-CSRF 200 Â· forged-CSRF rejected Â· logout revokes session Â· wallet link 200 Â· **nonce replay 410** Â· wallet-only login 200 Â· unlinked-wallet login 401.
- [x] **S1-20** `packages/db/src/auth-wallets.ts` â€” re-linking a wallet the same user already owns is an idempotent success; claiming one owned by **another** user is a 409, never a silent re-link, because quietly moving a verified wallet between accounts would hand over its role as a Stage 4 withdrawal destination.
- [x] **S1-21** `packages/db/src/audit-log.ts` â€” `recordAuditEvent` is best-effort and never throws (an audit failure must not turn a successful login into a 500); `recordAuditEventStrict` throws, for custody/withdrawal/tier events where an unlogged action is worse than a failed one.
- [x] **S1-22** `apps/api/src/auth/wallet-signature.test.ts` â€” 12 cases with real keypairs, including the **cross-domain replay**: a signature harvested by `evil.test` is rejected here even though it is cryptographically valid. Domain/URI binding is the check most often omitted, and signature validity alone never proves the signer meant to authenticate *here*.

### 4.4 Tenancy discipline (D12) â€” establish before any per-user route exists
- [x] **S1-15** `packages/db/src/tenancy.ts` â€” `forUser(userId)` is the only constructor for a `UserScope`. Made a **branded nominal type**, not `{userId: string}`: a signature of `(userId: string, â€¦)` accepts `request.body.userId` exactly as happily as the session's id and the mistake is invisible in review, whereas `(scope: UserScope, â€¦)` will not compile against a raw string. The type is the control, not the convention. `crossTenantScope(reason)` is the deliberately verbose, greppable escape hatch for admin and background-job paths.

### 4.5 Credential layer *(built 2026-08-05)*
- [x] **S1-17** `packages/db/src/credentials.ts` â€” argon2id for passwords, SHA-256 + `timingSafeEqual` for session tokens and API keys. **Two strategies on purpose:** passwords are low-entropy so they need a slow memory-hard hash; tokens are 256-bit CSPRNG output where a slow hash buys nothing and would put ~110 ms on *every authenticated request*.
  **Parameters measured, not assumed:** the first draft specified m=65536/t=3, which costs **450 ms** on this 2-core box. Every login *and every failed login* pays that, making it a self-inflicted DoS lever under exactly the credential stuffing the rate limit exists to blunt. Switched to **m=47104/t=1/p=1 (110 ms)** â€” a configuration OWASP treats as equivalent in strength. Raising parallelism was not an option: 2 cores.
- [x] **S1-18** `packages/db/src/users.ts` â€” user and session queries. `authenticateUser` burns an equivalent argon2 verify against a module-scoped dummy hash when the email is unknown, so response *timing* cannot enumerate users; the identical 401 body is otherwise cosmetic. `changePassword` revokes all sessions **in the same transaction** â€” separable, it fails to evict whoever the user is changing the password because of. `resolveSession` applies both expiry rules inside the `UPDATE â€¦ RETURNING` CTE so touching and validating are one atomic step; select-then-update would leave a window where a concurrently revoked session still resolves.
- [x] **S1-19** `packages/db/src/credentials.test.ts` â€” 14 cases. **Found and fixed a real bug:** `parseApiKeyPrefix` split on `_` and required exactly 3 parts, but the base64url secret alphabet *includes* `_`, so roughly half of all generated keys were rejected as malformed. Now parsed by position with a hex prefix that cannot contain the delimiter; the regression is pinned by a 40-iteration round-trip test.

## 5. Stage 2 â€” Per-user tracking, backfill, feeds *(SaaS Phase 2)*

**Model:** global dedup, per-user subscription. `wallets`, `transactions`, clusters, and scoring stay **global** â€” one wallet indexed once serves every subscriber (D9).

### 5.1 Schema â€” migrations `044`â€“`045` *(applied 2026-08-05; replayed twice clean on both databases; 45/45)*
- [x] **S2-1** `044_user_wallet_subscriptions.sql` â€” `PRIMARY KEY (user_id, wallet_address)` rather than a surrogate id, because the pair **is** the fact. Reverse index on `wallet_address` so the nightly "does this wallet have subscribers?" sweep is not a sequential scan. `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both sides is safe *here* â€” a subscription is a preference, not a financial record â€” and is deliberately not used on `trades`/`copy_executions`.
- [x] **S2-2** `045_user_token_watches.sql` â€” surrogate PK (lifecycle state outlives identity), `UNIQUE (user_id, chain, token_mint)` so re-requesting a backfill is idempotent rather than burning quota, and a `(user_id, created_at DESC)` index serving the rolling-24h count directly.

### 5.2 Tiers and quotas
- [x] **S2-3** `packages/shared/src/tiers.ts` â€” capability matrix, **capability only, never price**, so a Stage 5 price change never touches quota logic. `unlimited` is `null`, not `Infinity`: `Infinity` does not survive `JSON.stringify` or a numeric column, and invites `if (!limit)` checks that treat it as `0`. 17 unit tests including the matrix invariants (a higher tier can never have a smaller quota; higher tiers get a *lower* BullMQ priority number, an inversion that would otherwise silently starve paying users behind free ones).
- [x] **S2-4** Quotas enforced in `packages/db`, not in route handlers â€” a quota checked in a handler is one the next handler forgets. Over-quota returns **402, not 403**: 403 means "never", 402 means "upgrade and you may", and the frontend needs that distinction to show an upgrade prompt rather than an error.
- [x] **S2-5** `pauseUnsubscribedWallets` (D9) â€” pauses zero-subscriber wallets with no platform interest, so growth cannot multiply webhook volume indefinitely. Never pauses a wallet holding an open position (its P&L is still being marked to market) or one in a cluster (dropping it would corrupt cluster membership).
- [x] **S2-6** Tier-based BullMQ backfill priority wired into `POST /v1/me/wallets`.

  **The pause conflict, found by reading the sweep against tenancy.** `pauseUnderperformingWallets` was written for a single operator: it paused any wallet scoring below 40. Under tenancy that silently stops data for a wallet a user *explicitly chose and may be paying to track*, with no event and no way to diagnose it. Resolved by making `wallets.status` answer exactly one question â€” "is the platform indexing this?" â€” with subscriber count as the dominant input: a subscriber pins a wallet `active` regardless of score. Underperformance is *surfaced* (score and tier are already on the row), never acted on for the user. Per-user status was rejected: it multiplies rows by user count for a genuinely global fact and would make the indexer's poll query per-user.

### 5.3 Routes â€” `/v1/me/*` *(built 2026-08-05)*
- [x] **S2-7** â€¦ **S2-10** `apps/api/src/routes/me.ts` â€” wallets CRUD, history/holdings, token backfill, signals, feed. Backfill is enqueued **only when the call created the global wallet**; enqueuing on every subscribe would re-backfill each time another user tracks it, which is the exact cost the dedup model exists to avoid. Not-subscribed on history/holdings returns **404, not 403** â€” whether another user tracks a wallet is not this user's business, and 403 would confirm the wallet exists.
- [x] **S2-11** Global routes are admin-only via `registerAdminOnlyGlobals`. Implemented as an **allowlist** (`/v1/auth/*`, `/v1/me/*`, `/v1/health`), not a blocklist, so a global route added later is admin-gated *by default* â€” a blocklist would leave every new operator route open until someone remembered it.
- [x] **S2-12** *(deferred to Stage 6)* SSE `/v1/me/stream` â€” the polling it replaces lives in the frontend, which Stage 6 rebuilds. Noted so it is not lost.

  **Verified against a live server:** free-tier quota blocks at exactly 3/3 with `402 QUOTA 3/3` Â· second subscriber to the same wallet returns `backfillQueued=false` (dedup proven) Â· isolation holds (alice 3, bob 1) Â· unsubscribe leaves the other subscriber *and* the global wallet intact Â· free tier `delayedSeconds=900` Â· token backfill 402s at 1/day and a re-request of the same token returns 200 without burning quota Â· free-tier polygon â†’ 402 `chain-not-in-tier` Â· legacy service key â†’ 401 on `/v1/me/*` Â· normal user â†’ **403 on all six global routes** while the service key still gets 200 (internal calls unbroken).

  **A real TOCTOU bug the tests caught.** The first implementation counted inside `withTransaction` and my own comment claimed that made the quota safe. It did not: `withTransaction` runs at **READ COMMITTED**, so N concurrent `COUNT(*)` reads all observe the pre-commit state â€” five concurrent subscribes against the 3-wallet free tier granted **all five**. Fixed with `SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` before the count, serialising one user's quota writes without contending with any other user. Chosen over `SERIALIZABLE` (needs a retry loop) and an advisory lock (the row exists; the transaction releases it). Both quota paths now hold the lock. The design doc's incorrect claim was corrected rather than left to mislead.

  **A pre-existing bug found while probing:** the API error handler discarded `err.statusCode`, so Fastify's own 4xx client errors (malformed JSON, empty body, payload too large) were reported as **500**. That hides real 500s in the logs and tells clients to retry something that cannot work. Now mapped through.

**Exit gate:** âœ… **met 2026-08-05.** Two users track different wallets and see disjoint feeds; quotas enforced under concurrency; cross-tenant tests green; global routes admin-only.
Gate numbers for this stage live in Â§1 only. They were duplicated here and drifted; Â§1 is the single current baseline and a stage section is not a place to read one from.

### 6.1 Solana â€” retarget to Jupiter + Jito (`DG-1` resolved 2026-07-27)
- [x] **S3-1** Jupiter `/swap` transaction-build step â€” `packages/shared/src/jupiter-swap.ts`. The signer is a **parameter** (`signTransaction`), not a module-level key, so Stage 4 substitutes a per-user custodial signer with no call-site change. `apps/trade-executor/src/solana-signer.ts` is the operator implementation; the private key is loaded once into a closure and never returned, logged, or placed on a reachable object.
- [x] **S3-2** Jito `sendBundle` with an appended tip â€” `packages/shared/src/jito.ts`. Never broadcasts over public RPC.
- [x] **S3-3** Dynamic tip sizing from the block engine's tip-floor percentiles, capped by `JITO_MAX_TIP_LAMPORTS`. The cap is enforced, not advisory: without it a congestion spike or a malformed floor response spends unbounded SOL per trade. A zero/absent floor reads as *no data* and falls back, never as "free" â€” a zero tip never lands, which would look identical to a dead executor.
- [x] **S3-4** Confirmation and reconciliation â€” `jupiter-jito-runtime.ts` `reconcile`/`sweep`, wired into the **existing** guarded `reconcilePending` loop (no second timer, per C1). A miss is declared **only** once the block height passes `lastValidBlockHeight`, which is the only point the transaction provably cannot land â€” and is why a retry needs a fresh quote and build rather than a blind resubmit. An unobservable bundle resolves to `null`, deliberately distinct from `failed`.
- [x] **S3-5** Fallback policy â€” a Jito failure is reported honestly (`submission_unknown` when retryable, `rejected` when definitive) and never downgraded to a public RPC broadcast.
- [ ] **S3-6** Retire Trojan: delete `TROJAN_WEBHOOK_URL` / `TROJAN_API_KEY` and the client path once the new path is certified; `TROJAN_WALLET_ADDRESS` balance reads become the parameterized operator signing wallet. `H4` is superseded with the path. **Blocked on `S3-9` certification** â€” both paths run side by side until then, and `clampExecutionModeForStartup` accepts either being ready.
  **Pulled forward by ADR-0005 Â§7.1 (2026-08-19), ordering unchanged.** The operator has decided Solana executes via Jupiter+Jito. Under single-master mirroring the user is waiting on a specific trade, and that trade is currently placed by a third-party Telegram bot on a 60-second timeout (`MAX_TROJAN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `trojan.ts:2`) with no control over route, slippage, tip, or priority fee â€” so this stops being cleanup and becomes product work. **The sequence is still certify â†’ flip â†’ delete, and must not be compressed:** flipping `SOLANA_EXECUTOR` before `S3-9` would put an uncertified path on the money path, which inverts the audit's own ordering. Raising the priority of this item does not license skipping its gate.
- [ ] **S3-7** `F-SOL2` / `F-SOL3` (retargeted) â€” **dispatch adapter built and now WIRED, behind a flag.** `apps/trade-executor/src/solana-dispatch.ts` (15 tests) owns the two things the runtime does not: turning a trade intent into a Jupiter quote, and flattening the submission union into the shape `persistTrade` expects.
  **A BUY is `ExactIn` on SOL; a SELL is `ExactIn` on the token** â€” the proportional exit gives an exact base-unit quantity to dispose of, not a target SOL amount, and `ExactOut` would name a SOL figure we do not have while letting the venue take more tokens than the position holds. A sell quantity beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is rejected rather than rounded.
  **A bundle id is not a transaction signature.** It exists only once the bundle lands, so `trades.signature` stays null at submit and the reconciliation sweep fills it in; persisting the bundle id there would put a value in the column that no explorer can resolve.
  **Cutover is flag-gated, not unconditional** â€” `apps/trade-executor/src/solana-executor-selection.ts` (9 tests). Jupiter+Jito is unit-tested but **uncertified**, and `S3-9` requires the canary to run *before* the path carries real trades. So `handleJob` routes to it only when `SOLANA_EXECUTOR=jupiter-jito` **and** a signer plus block engine are configured; neither control implies the other. Default stays Trojan. A typo in `SOLANA_EXECUTOR` throws at startup rather than falling back, because a misrouted execution variable must not fail silently. `trades.executor` is `varchar(20)` with no CHECK constraint, so the new `'jupiter-jito'` value needed no migration â€” verified against the live schema.
  **Mutation-verified:** flipping the default to the uncertified path fails 2 tests; dropping the readiness requirement fails 1.
  **Remaining:** the fixture matrix (entry, partial exit, full exit, failure, duplicate webhook, timeout-after-submit), then `S3-9`'s canary â€” after which the flag becomes the default and `S3-6` retires Trojan.
- [ ] **S3-8** `G1-S1` â€” measure webhookâ†’signalâ†’alertâ†’execution over a real review window; hold Solana median signal-to-alert under 60s.
- [ ] **S3-9 (ext)** Capped live canary recorded under `docs/certification/solana.md`.

  **Wired 2026-08-05:** `jupiter-jito-config.ts` provides `createJupiterJitoRuntimeFromEnvironment` + `getJupiterJitoLiveReadiness`, mirroring the Trojan pattern. Startup configures it alongside Trojan; a configuration error is caught and recorded as a readiness reason rather than thrown, because taking down execution for *every* chain when one chain's optional live path is misconfigured is the wrong failure mode. `JITO_BLOCK_ENGINE_URL` has no default on purpose. Two exit cases added in `robinhood-runtime.test.ts` (11 â†’ 13).
