### 7.5 ADR-0005 â€” single-master mirroring *(created 2026-08-19)*

The pivot from cluster-consensus trading to single-master mirroring. `docs/adr/0005-single-master-mirroring.md` carries the reasoning and the rejected alternatives; `docs/PRD.md` carries the product framing for collaborators. Items here are the work that had no checklist entry before the pivot.

**Already landed:**
- [x] **S4-M0** Demote the four cluster detectors to discovery-only. *(Done 2026-08-19, commits `2c30e60`, `bb0fbf5`.)* `suppressTrade: true` on snipe, accumulation and rotation; exit was already suppressed and its comment corrected. The invariant then moved into `apps/signal-engine/src/trade-eligibility.ts` as a single frozen list consulted by `enqueueSignal`, because four independent literals at four call sites is a decision nothing can test â€” the detectors query the database directly and `index.ts` starts timers at import, so a test cannot reach them. A frozen array rather than an exported `Set`: `ReadonlySet` is a compile-time claim only, and one stray `.add()` would have re-enabled cluster trading process-wide with no diff to review. Fails closed on unrecognised patterns, which is reachable because `patternType` is typed `string`. 8 tests.

**Mirroring semantics:**
- `[â†’]` **S4-M1** Hybrid buy sizing â€” **pointer, not separate work.** `S4-15` is the item; this entry only records that ADR-0005 rewrote it. Closes when `S4-15` does.
- [x] **S4-M2** **Forward-only joins.** A user subscribing to a master already holding twelve tokens mirrors only trades from subscription onward. No catch-up buying: entering an existing position at an unknown cost basis is how followers become exit liquidity. *(Wired 2026-10-01.)* `apps/signal-engine/src/index.ts` now passes the source trade's `eventAt` into `FanoutSignal`; `packages/db/src/fanout-candidates.ts` selects and maps the subscription's current `active_since` (never `created_at`); `fanout-eligibility.ts` calls the existing `evaluateForwardOnlyMirror` for every fan-out BUY. Pre-subscription entries are excluded with `source-event-precedes-active-since`, missing timestamps fail closed, exact-boundary entries are admitted, and SELLs remain ungated so winding-down positions cannot be stranded. Mutation-sensitive coverage: 32 fan-out eligibility tests, 34 candidate-enumeration tests (including SQL contract assertions), plus the existing 21 predicate tests. DB-backed integration remains written but unrun because no database is available. Verified with `@swat/db` 118 focused tests, all 159 `@swat/signal-engine` tests, and clean package typechecks.
  **It filters on `active_since`, never `created_at`, and that is the whole point.** The PK is `(user_id, wallet_address)`, so re-subscribe is an `ended â†’ active` transition on the same row: a subscription created in January, ended in March and revived in August still reads `created_at = January`. Filtering on it would mirror eight months of history on every re-subscribe â€” catch-up buying in the one case nobody would think to test. A test pins exactly that scenario.
  **A sell is gated by nothing** â€” not timing, not lifecycle state, not even the existence of a subscription row. The sell branch is unconditional and sits ahead of every other check. This is load-bearing rather than theoretical: `unsubscribeFromWallet` still hard-deletes the row, so a user can hold an open position with no subscription row, and refusing the master's sell would leave it with no exit path. What keeps it safe is downstream â€” a sell mirror is proportional to the position actually held, and `computeCopySellProportion` throws rather than defaulting to sell-everything when position evidence is missing. **A reviewer who "tightens" this to a skip must close the position-orphan case first**, and a test says so.
  **Clock-skew tolerance defaults to 0, and the asymmetry is the argument.** `event_at` is a chain or venue clock; `active_since` is our `NOW()`. Too low costs one missed entry the user recovers from on the next trade; too high opens a position at a cost basis the user never had, which is unrecoverable and is precisely the harm this item prevents. A safety gate with asymmetric failure modes defaults to the recoverable one. The knob exists for an operator who has *measured* a chain's drift. Note that `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates` already admits `event_at <= now + 30s`, so forward skew already smuggles a little history past this gate and no filter on these two columns can detect it â€” which is a second reason not to widen backward by default.
  **Mutation-verified:** admitting any event once a subscription exists fails 10 tests; gating the sell fails 4; widening the default tolerance to 30 s fails 2.
  **Why unwired, precisely:** forward-only is a per-`(user, master)` decision, and **no per-user enumeration exists yet** â€” today's signal path is per-master. The call site is fan-out (`S4-13`/`S4-14`), which does not exist. Wiring it earlier would mean inventing the enumeration this item does not own.
- [x] **S4-M3** **`051` â€” subscription states `active` / `winding_down` / `ended`.** *(Done 2026-10-29. `051_subscription_states.sql` + `058_copy_position_lots.sql` + `runCloseAllSweep` queue wiring in commit `e6ffbe1` + two-user clean DB integration test in `72b4bee`.)*
- [x] **S4-M4** **Per-user concurrent-position cap**, in `049`, API â†’ UI, with a platform hard ceiling. *(Done 2026-10-29. `049` concurrent position cap + `packages/db/src/position-cap.ts` + HTTP endpoints `GET/PATCH /v1/me/execution-settings` in `apps/api/src/routes/execution-settings.ts` with 29 tests.)*
- [x] **S4-M5** **Mirrorable-activity filter** *(Done 2026-08-20, commit `8367027`.)* â€” buys and sells above a minimum notional only. Transfers, LP, staking and dust excluded. Without this, a master moving funds between their own wallets triggers copies.
  `apps/signal-engine/src/mirrorable-activity.ts`, consulted by `processSourceTradeSignals` before `enqueueSignal` â€” the one place a master's event becomes a copy. A whitelist of `buy`/`sell` derived from an exhaustive `Record<SourceTradeSide, boolean>`, so a new side **cannot compile** without being classified; a frozen list plus a private `Set` copy, so it cannot be widened at runtime; fails closed on an unrecognised side or an unreadable notional. Same two-layer shape as `trade-eligibility.ts`, for the same reason. 22 tests.
  **The two halves of this item have different status, and the distinction matters.** *Transfers/LP/staking were already excluded upstream*: all three indexer writers can only express `buy`/`sell`, and `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates` filters `direction IN ('buy','sell')` in SQL. So that clause is a **guard**, not a fix â€” and it is worth keeping, because `028` deliberately **widened** the column's CHECK to admit `transfer_in`/`transfer_out` and `rebuildSourcePosition` already ledgers them, so the day someone adds a transfer writer nothing in their diff points at the copy path. *The notional floor is a live fix*: nothing on this path had one.
  **New knob `SOURCE_COPY_MIN_NOTIONAL_USD`** (default `0`, opt-in). Deliberately **not** `COPY_MIN_SOURCE_ACTIVITY_USD`, which is a 30-day wallet **track-record** floor consumed in `trade-executor` â€” a wallet clears that comfortably while still closing a $2 remainder, which is the dust case this item names. One knob cannot be both.
  **`amount_usd IS NULL` is unknown, not dust**, and gets its own code. Mirrored when no floor is set, skipped as `source-notional-unknown` when one is â€” because unknown is the *common* case on two of three chains (`robinhood-chain` never records a notional and Solana omits it off USDC/USDT routes), so failing closed at defaults would be an undeclared kill switch presenting as "copying quietly stopped working". The distinct code is what lets `S4-M24` say "we cannot price this chain" rather than "your master trades dust" â€” the first is fixable, the second is a lie.
  **Mutation-verified:** making an unrecognised side mirrorable fails 2 tests; reporting an unknown notional as below-minimum fails 1.
  **A bug the tests caught during development:** `Number('')` and `Number('   ')` are `0`, not `NaN`, so a blank notional parsed as a genuine zero-dollar trade and mirrored whenever the floor was 0.
  **Known limit, honestly stated:** swap-shaped LP deposits and liquid staking are ingested as `buy`/`sell` by the parser, so **no side filter downstream can undo it** â€” see `S4-M31`. The item's LP/staking clause is satisfied only to the extent those events are distinguishable by side, which they are not.

**Capacity:**
- [ ] **S4-M6** **`053` â€” per-master capacity cap, denominated in price impact:** aggregate copy notional per `(master, token, window)` as a fraction of usable liquidity. Follower count is the wrong unit â€” 500 followers buying a deep pair is harmless, 50 buying a fresh memecoin is not. A follower soft-cap remains as a crude secondary so no single master becomes an operational concentration risk regardless of what they trade.
  **The harm being capped:** our own cohort is the adverse selection. User #900 eats the impact users #1â€“899 created, and a master who notices can farm it â€” buy small, wait for copy flow to lift the price, sell into their own followers. Also carries the per-master budget allocation that `S4-P15` depends on.
  **Built 2026-08-22 (commit `69f3cb1`) as an unwired library â€” unticked.** `packages/db/src/master-capacity.ts` (52 tests) + `053_master_capacity.sql`. Nothing imports it yet; the call site is `processSourceTradeSignals`, in the same position as `S4-M5`.
  **Price impact is derived, not guessed.** For a constant-product pool, average execution price Ã· spot is exactly `1 + dx/x`, so impact = notional Ã· one-sided reserve. The ceiling is derived from `DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS` Ã— 1/3 per chain, on the argument that cohort impact spends the same slippage budget that protects the last copier; the 1/3 is labelled a judgement rather than dressed up.
  **Liquidity is an injected input and is never fabricated â€” and this is the honest core of the entry.** A usable figure exists only *approximately* and only for AMM pairs: `fetchDexScreenerLiquidity` is already called at decision time by `signal-engine/safety.ts`, but it is reported both-sided pool TVL for one pair, not depth, and **it is persisted nowhere**. For **Polymarket there is no pre-fan-out figure at all** â€” real depth is the CLOB book walk inside the executor, read per order at submission. Jupiter's `priceImpactPct` is a genuine number but Solana-only and produced after fan-out has already decided. So unknown liquidity yields `unassessed` and the caller's declared policy decides; **no liquidity column was added to `053` on purpose**, because a column nothing populates reads as 0 or NULL and would silently block or permit everything.
  **A second gap it surfaced: `copy_executions` has no USD notional.** `028` stores base/quote *token* quantities, and `source_trades.amount_usd` is NULL on robinhood-chain and non-stablecoin Solana routes. Hence `053` keeps its own ledger with a nullable `notional_usd` plus a `notional_basis` CHECK enforcing `(basis = 'unpriced') = (notional_usd IS NULL)`, so **"unpriceable" can never be recorded as `$0`** â€” and a window containing unpriced legs is reported as a pass that is explicitly a *lower bound*.
  **Uniform skip is enforced four ways, not asserted.** The input type has no user, tier or account field; `assertNoPerUserCapacityInput` recursively rejects any such key at runtime so widening the type later throws; the ceiling comes from the chain default slippage tolerance rather than any user's own, so a looser user cannot buy a bigger cohort allowance; and the ledger is cohort-level with no `user_id`, asserted against `information_schema`.
  **One frozen user message for every cause**, digit-free, with tests asserting it matches no `\d`, `/follower/i`, `/liquidity/i`, `/impact/i` or `/bps/i` â€” because differing wording would itself distinguish "impact cap" from "follower cap", and the latter is a headcount signal (`S4-M9`). The specific code and figures travel beside it in a nested `internal`, so rendering them to a user is visible in review.
  **Mutation-verified:** disabling the follower soft-cap fails 6 tests; fabricating a liquidity figure fails 1; appending the reason code to the user message fails 3; disabling the per-user input guard fails 2.
  **POLYGON DEPTH DECIDED 2026-08-23: fetch the depth before the trade â€” and via the ingestion engine, not a per-order call.** The operator's choice was to read depth ahead of execution rather than accept `unassessed` for polygon. `S4-M38` is the design that makes that affordable: a background service streams books into Redis so the pre-trade read is a local microsecond lookup instead of a 100â€“300 ms round trip on the hot path. So this item's liquidity input for polygon comes from that cache, with the per-market staleness rule `S4-M38` specifies â€” **a stale local book must read as `unassessed`, never as truth**, which is exactly the input contract this module already has.
  **~~Why unticked, and the trap in wiring it~~ â€” ALL FOUR NOW LANDED.** *(2026-09-13.)* The pre-fan-out liquidity fetch was the last one and was the hard one, because Polymarket needed a feed built from nothing: `S4-M38` (`d8192ca`). The cohort notional, the follower count and **the ledger writer** landed in `401eb02` â€” the writer accrues at the confirmation funnel with before/after cumulative totals, so a BullMQ replay yields a zero delta and issues no statement. **The trap this entry warned about is closed: an unwired writer would have left an empty ledger reading as "no capacity used", permitting everything.**
  **Remaining before this can be ticked `[x]`:** the cap is wired and the feed exists, but **no database and no Redis have ever run on this branch**, so `053`'s migration has never been applied, no ledger row has ever been written, and no Redis round trip has happened. Every part is proven against injected fakes. This stays `[ ]` until one integration run exercises: migration `053` applying cleanly, one fan-out writing one ledger row, and one polygon cohort admitted against a real book.
- `[â†’]` **S4-M7** **Uniform skip and generic capacity messaging** â€” **pointer, not separate work.** The decision is recorded in `S4-P15`; the mechanism landed with `S4-M6` (one frozen, digit-free user message, tested against `/follower/i` and friends). Closes when `S4-M6` is wired.
- [=] **S4-M43** *(Decision + enforcement done 2026-09-01: `packages/db/src/master-membership.ts`, 52 tests, migration `056`. **`[=]` because the concurrent-subscribe test cannot run without a database** â€” see the closing note.)*
  **Enforcement is a slot ordinal plus a partial unique index â€” a pigeonhole, not a count.** `membership_slot SMALLINT` with `CHECK 1..50` and `UNIQUE (wallet_address, membership_slot) WHERE membership_slot IS NOT NULL`. Range times uniqueness means exactly 50 ordinals exist per master, so **a 51st slot-holder is unrepresentable** â€” under arbitrary concurrency, against a future service that never read the module, and against a hand-typed `psql` INSERT. No application code has to be trusted, which is the property a `COUNT(*)`-then-INSERT can never have.
  **`lockUserForQuota` provides no protection here, and the agent confirmed it independently.** It is `SELECT ... FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` â€” it serialises *one user's* quota writes. This cap is about 50 *different* users joining one master at the same instant: different rows, different locks, zero contention. An advisory lock keyed on the master is added for **liveness** (without it two racers pick the same lowest free ordinal and one gets a `23505` instead of a different slot), and `isMembershipSlotConflict` matches the **index name** rather than bare `23505`, because the PK raises the same code and means something else entirely.
  **A third CHECK is what makes it a *membership* cap rather than a slot cap:** a non-`active` row must hold no ordinal and no grandfather flag. That makes "a leaver holds a slot" unrepresentable, clears the exemption on leaving (which is `S4-M44` as an invariant), and puts an **unrecognised future state in the no-slot branch** â€” the fail-closed direction.
  **The refusal message is one frozen string for every cause**, `null` on admit, asserted against `/\d/`, `/follower/i`, `/limit/i`, `/full/i`, `/capacity/i`, `/slot/i`, `/member/i`, `/quota/i`. A further test asserts the set of user messages across all three causes has size **1** while `internal.code` has size **3** â€” so ops keep the diagnosis and the caller cannot read backend state off the copy. **Mutation-verified by the master agent: putting a count in the message fails 5 tests.**
  **Two leak surfaces closed that the item did not ask for.** `MasterMembershipFullError.message` **is** the digit-free string rather than a diagnostic, because Fastify handlers routinely echo `error.message` and a cap in there would leak through a path nobody reviews. And `WalletSubscription` deliberately has **no `membershipSlot` field** â€” an ordinal is a rank, and "you are #37" is exactly the headcount signal `S4-M9` forbids.
  **Over-subscribed masters are grandfathered, never evicted.** Backfill assigns 1..50 oldest-first by `active_since`; the remainder are flagged. Eviction does not close anyone's positions, so it would strand precisely the positions whose exit path is the master's sell mirror â€” silently, for users who did nothing wrong. The set only shrinks, and **the migration contains no `DELETE FROM`** (asserted by test). Replay-safety is structural rather than flag-based: once the CHECK exists, the backfill's `WHERE` describes a row the CHECK forbids, so a replay matches nothing.
  **`winding_down` holds no slot but still mirrors sells** â€” the interaction the item flagged. Occupancy counts `state = 'active'` only; `fanout-eligibility.ts` derives everything from `mirrorEligibilityForState` and never reads `membership_slot`, so the two cannot drift. **Mutation-verified: letting `winding_down` occupy a slot fails a named test.**
  **A behavioural consequence worth surfacing:** `winding_down â†’ active` (the "changed my mind" path) is now **refusable** â€” the ordinal went back in the pool. Exempting it would let a user hold a slot indefinitely by cycling. This is `S4-M44`'s cost and belongs in the unsubscribe copy.
  **Also needed, outside this item:** `apps/api/src/routes/me.ts:153` catches only `QuotaExceededError`, so `MasterMembershipFullError` currently falls through to a 500. Suggest **409** (not 402 â€” no upgrade lifts a master's cap), echoing `error.message` only, never `error.decision`.
  **Not verified, and this is the reason for `[=]`: there is no database, so nothing in `056` has ever executed.** The race-safety argument above is reasoning from Postgres semantics, not an observation. `tests/integration/master-membership.integration.test.ts` fires `cap + 10` concurrent subscribes and asserts exactly 50 succeed â€” **written and UNRUN**. The unit tests assert the migration's *text*, which is a different claim from its behaviour.
  **Original text:** **Master copier cap: 50 membership AND 50 per-signal, with a digit-free refusal.** *(Operator decisions 2026-09-01, replacing an earlier "500" request after the throughput conflict was surfaced.)*
  **Decided: both caps are 50.** The operator originally asked for 500 membership. That was withdrawn once the arithmetic was shown: one concurrency-1 worker per chain at ~6s/order drains **~50 orders per 5-minute window** (`DEFAULT_FOLLOWER_SOFT_CAP`'s own derivation), so 500 copiers on one signal would take **~50 minutes** to clear and everyone past roughly #50 fills at a materially worse price than the master. **Setting membership equal to the per-signal cap is what makes the promise honest**: every subscriber can actually be served within one window.
  **Two enforcement points, not one, because they answer different questions:**
  - **Membership (subscribe time)** â€” a new check in the subscribe path, capped at 50 per master. **Must be a database uniqueness/count constraint, not a read-then-write**, or two concurrent subscribes both pass the check and the cap is exceeded by exactly the number of racers.
  - **Per-signal (fan-out time)** â€” `assessMasterCapacity`, already built, unchanged.
  **The refusal message discloses nothing** *(operator: "message only, no number or digital info to disclose what the backend knows")*. This is not politeness â€” it is `S4-M9`, a standing constraint against ever displaying follower counts or popularity, because a count is a crowding signal and tells a master exactly when farming their own followers pays. So: **"this master is not accepting new copiers"** â€” no digits, no "full", no "50", and deliberately **not** wording that differs by cause, since differing wording is itself a distinguishable signal. `MasterCapacityDecision` already splits `user.message` (generic, digit-free, test-asserted to match no `\d`) from `internal` (the real code and figures, ops-only) â€” reuse that split rather than inventing a second one.
  **Effect on thundering herd, stated honestly:** the cap **bounds** the herd, it does not remove it. 50 users copying one signal still queue behind one worker. What actually protects fills is the **aggregate price-impact** check, which measures whether the *cohort's combined* size moves the market â€” the membership cap is a blunt outer bound, impact is the real defence. Anyone reading "cap = 50" as "herd solved" has the wrong model.
  **Done when:** the membership cap is enforced by a DB constraint with a concurrent-subscribe test; the refusal carries the generic message and a test asserts it contains no digits; and a re-subscribe after the slot is taken is refused the same way (`S4-M44`).

- [x] **S4-M44** *(Done 2026-09-01 with `S4-M43`; same migration, same tests. **Mutation-verified:** letting a re-subscribe bypass the cap fails 3 named tests.)* Enforced as an invariant rather than a code path: the CHECK clears both the ordinal and the grandfather flag on leaving `active`, so a returning member **must** take a real ordinal or be refused. No reservation, no waitlist. **A dropped copier does not get their slot back.** *(Operator decision 2026-09-01.)*
  **Decided: if a user's slot has been filled by someone else, they are refused on re-subscribe â€” even if they were previously subscribed.** No grandfathering, no waitlist priority. The slot is not theirs once released.
  **Why this is the right call and not merely simpler:** any reservation mechanism is a queue, and a queue that holds a slot for an absent user makes the cap dishonest â€” the master shows 50 members of whom some cannot trade. It also creates an incentive to churn subscriptions to hold position. **The cost is real and should be stated to the user rather than hidden:** a user who lapses may not get back in. That belongs in the unsubscribe confirmation copy, not discovered afterwards.
  **Interaction with `S4-M45` that must not be missed:** a `winding_down` user still holds open positions and still needs their exits mirrored. **Winding-down users must NOT occupy a membership slot** â€” they are leaving â€” but they must still be enumerated for sells. Conflating "occupies a slot" with "receives mirrors" breaks one or the other: count them and the cap under-serves; drop them from enumeration and their positions strand.
  **Done when:** re-subscribe to a full master is refused with the same digit-free message; a test asserts a `winding_down` user does not consume a slot **and** still receives sell mirrors.


**Suggestion engine:**
- [x] **S4-M8** **Out-of-sample master metrics over 24h / 7d / 30d** *(Done 2026-08-20, commit `7f644df`.)* `apps/scorer/src/master-metrics.ts` + 44 tests, **called** from the nightly batch via `runStage('master metrics', ...)` â€” verified at the call site, not inferred. Pure/DB split as in `stop-loss.ts`: round-trip reconstruction, windowing, gating and divergence are pure and tested on fixture rows; only `listMasterCandidates` / `fetchMasterTradeRows` touch Postgres, and neither has ever been executed.
  Per window: PnL in absolute USD (**never a return ratio** â€” a test asserts the serialised report matches neither `/roi/i` nor `/follower/i`, covering this and `S4-M9`), max drawdown in USD **and** as a percent of deployed capital with the denominator in the field name, hit rate, median hold time. Round trips are entry-to-flat episodes with partial exits folded into one, so one entry decision yields one hold time and one hit-rate sample. **Still-open positions are excluded rather than counted as zero-return trades**; sells with no visible entry are counted as `unmatchedSells` rather than given an invented basis.
  **Capacity is deliberately `null`** with `capacityStatus: 'deferred-to-s4-m6'` â€” capacity is denominated in price impact (ADR-0005 Â§4.1) and belongs to `S4-M6`. No headcount-derived stand-in.
  A gated window returns a discriminated variant carrying **no metric fields at all**, so "insufficient history" cannot be rendered as a number. Minimums are per window (5 / 10 / 20, overridable). Divergence covers all three window pairs with a headline 24h-vs-30d `trend`; a bounded `relativeChange` handles sign flips, and decaying masters are logged individually because divergence *is* the finding.
  **`out-of-sample` is defined nowhere in ADR-0005 or the PRD, so the interpretation is recorded rather than assumed:** a round trip counts when its *entry* is at or after `wallets.first_seen`. Not arbitrary â€” `source_trades` is written from backfill as well as live ingestion, so pre-tracking history really is in the table and must be cut. The cut is per episode, not per row, so an episode straddling the boundary is excluded rather than scored against an unfetched entry. A null `first_seen` fails closed to "insufficient everywhere". Changing the anchor touches only `MasterCandidate.observationStartAt`.
  **Mutation-verified:** zeroing the per-window minimums, and leaking one figure into the insufficient-history variant, each turned the suite red.
  **Two gaps, verified rather than assumed.** (1) **PnL is net of fees arithmetically but not in the data:** `fee_usd` exists only on `trades` (`031_execution_fees.sql`); `source_trades` and `polymarket_trades` have none, so `netOfFees` is `false` for every master and the figure is **gross of the master's own fees**. `fetchMasterTradeRows` selects `NULL::numeric AS fee_usd` with the comment where the gap enters, and `MasterTradeRow.feeUsd` is already threaded, so closing it needs a fee column plus indexer capture and no arithmetic change. (2) **Reports are logged, not persisted** â€” `S6-27`'s suggestion list needs a table in the `052`/`053` band; the batch exposes an unwired `persistReport` seam.
  **Found while reviewing the agent's output:** the module was written with **two literal NUL bytes** as a group-key delimiter inside a template literal. Valid JS, which is why 44 tests passed â€” but it made the file `data` rather than text, so `grep`, `git diff` and every other text tool silently skipped it. Replaced with `\u0000` escapes. **A passing suite is not evidence that a file is readable.** Original text: out-of-sample master metrics over 24h / 7d / 30d: PnL net of fees, max drawdown, hit rate, median hold time, capacity estimate. **Never raw ROI** â€” it ranks the luckiest. Minimum trade count enforced **per window**, showing "insufficient history" rather than a number we do not trust. Divergence across windows is itself a finding: strong on 30d and weak on 24h means decaying, which is more actionable than either figure alone.

- [x] **S4-M12** **Per-user nonce allocation on EVM** *(Done 2026-08-20, commit `5604950`.)* â€” advisory lock on `(chain, account)` plus per-user queue concurrency. **A correctness bug under fan-out, not an optimisation:** today one operator key with `getPendingNonce` then local `nonce++` (`robinhood.ts:670`, `:722`). - [=] **S4-M13** **EVM approvals: Permit2. The module is built and vector-verified; the router is now identified, so only wiring remains.** *(Was: "Decided 2026-08-19 â€” the operator confirms Robinhood Chain supports it, so the fallback is dropped.")*

  > ### âœ… UNBLOCKED 2026-08-31 â€” a Permit2-aware router exists, and it is discoverable at runtime
  >
  > **The operator's research resolved this, and every claim below was verified on-chain by the master agent against `https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com`, not accepted from the report.**
  >
  > **Rialto ships a Router Registry so router addresses are never hardcoded** â€” which is the right answer to a question this checklist was about to answer wrongly by pinning one address.
  >
  > | Probe | Result |
  > |---|---|
  > | Registry `0x71a120CbBf3Ce7cD910a3c50fF77aFc62735687E` | **9,938 chars of code â€” real** âœ… |
  > | `ownerOf(2)` â€” taker-submitted swap | `0xc94135b63772b91d79d0a2daab2a8801f32359bd` âœ… |
  > | `ownerOf(3)` â€” gasless/relayed swap | **same address** âœ… |
  > | That router's code | **48,466 chars** âœ… |
  > | Canonical Permit2 in the router's bytecode | **FOUND as an inlined immutable** âœ… |
  > | Permit2 `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` | `0x448684â€¦614fad` â€” **matches what `permit2.ts` already computes** âœ… |
  >
  > **The Permit2 immutable inside the router bytecode is the fact that closes this item.** It is not an inference from docs: the router itself carries the canonical Permit2 address, so it pulls tokens through Permit2. That is exactly the property `S4-M13` needed and could not previously establish.
  >
  > **Two operational details from `docs.rialto.xyz/developers/router-registries` that change the design â€” do not skip these.**
  > 1. **They are *feature ids*, not registry ids.** `2` = taker-submitted (broadcast the tx `GET /quote` returns); `3` = gasless/relayed (via `POST /gasless/submit`). They resolve to the same router **today** and must NOT be assumed to stay equal â€” resolve the one matching the flow being used.
  > 2. **The registry has a migration mechanism, and reading only `ownerOf` misses it.** `getFeature(id)` returns `(previous, current, next, paused)` in one call; `prev(id)` is a router still honoured during a **migration dwell window**; `next(id)` is a staged replacement. **Verified live:** for both features `next()` is the zero address, `prev()` **reverts** (`0x27eca1b0`, unset), and `paused` is false. So there is no migration in flight now â€” but a resolver that reads `ownerOf` alone will break silently the first time Rialto stages one. **`getFeature` is the call to use.**
  >
  > **`ownerOf(1)` and `ownerOf(4)` revert** with a typed error carrying the feature id (`0x7e273289â€¦`), which is the documented "paused or not initialised" behaviour rather than a bad address. Worth encoding: a revert here is a *state*, not a transport failure.
  >
  > **What this means for the wiring plan.** The router is resolved **at runtime from the registry**, not read from an env var â€” so the `ROBINHOOD_SWAP_ROUTER` variable that `S4-M39` found missing should probably not exist at all. What belongs in config is the **registry address plus the feature id**; the router follows from those. That is strictly better than a pinned address, because it survives a Rialto migration without a redeploy.
  >
  > **Also resolved: Uniswap is present at canonical addresses** (v2/v3/v4 and UniversalRouter), and UniversalRouter has required Permit2 by design since 2023. So there are **two** viable Permit2 paths, which makes the settlement choice a real decision rather than a constraint â€” see `S4-M40`.
  >
  > **Also resolved, and it removes an option rather than adding one: USDG on this chain implements neither EIP-3009 nor EIP-2612.** Paxos's *reference* implementation does; the deployed proxy on 4663 does not, per a bytecode selector scan by a third-party facilitator built for this chain. So the "EIP-2612 gets us the buy leg for free" idea is **dead outright**, not partial relief â€” and the facilitator's own workaround is Permit2's `permitWitnessTransferFrom`, i.e. the same conclusion this item reaches. **One on-chain approval of Permit2 per token, then free off-chain signatures regardless of what the token implements.** *(Not independently verified by the master agent â€” the USDG address is not on Robinhood's protocol-contracts page and its token-contracts page returned empty. Treat as strong secondary evidence, and confirm with a selector scan before relying on it.)*
  >
  > **One address correction worth recording, because it nearly became a bug.** This checklist previously probed a wrong L2 WETH candidate. The published value is **`0x0Bd7D308f8E1639FAb988df18A8011f41EAcAD73`** â€” verified: 4,406 chars of code, `symbol()` = `WETH`, `decimals()` = 18. And the operator was right to flag a stray-character risk on Permit2: the correct string is 42 characters ending `â€¦78BA3`, and at least one rendering dropped the final `3`. **A truncated address is a different address.**

  **Also corrected: the nonce mechanism.** The task brief (and this checklist's earlier assumption) said Permit2 uses an unordered bitmap. **Half true, and applying the wrong half reverts every time.** `AllowanceTransfer`/`PermitSingle` â€” the family a router-consumed swap uses â€” has a **sequential `uint48` counter** per `(owner, token, spender)`: `if (allowed.nonce != nonce) revert InvalidNonce();`. Only `SignatureTransfer`/`PermitTransferFrom` uses the `nonceBitmap`. Both are implemented and tagged distinctly. **And the Permit2 nonce is not the transaction nonce** â€” `getPendingNonce` is unrelated; conflating them is a bug waiting to happen, so nonce selection sits inside the existing `withSubmissionLock`/`withEvmNonceLock` critical section and says so in a comment.

  **What IS done, and it is genuinely verified.** `apps/trade-executor/src/permit2.ts` + 39 tests. Pure â€” no network, no key, no signing; it returns a typed-data payload for the `S4-P7` authority port to sign, and exposes a flat `Permit2PolicySubject` (token/spender/amount/deadline/nonce) for `S4-P10` to inspect **before** a signature exists. Correct EIP-712 widths (`uint160` amount, `uint48` expiration/nonce) and the version-less domain. **Three external vectors, not self-agreement:** live mainnet `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()`, live chain-4663 `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` (`0x448684â€¦614fad`, reproduced exactly), and â€” the one that matters â€” Uniswap's own committed MetaMask signatures from `test/TypehashGeneration.t.sol`, `ecrecover`ed against our computed digest and asserted to return their documented signer. Mutation-verified: widening `uint160`â†’`uint256` fails that vector test, which proves it is real external verification.

  **A composition gap with `S4-P7` was found and fixed.** viem's `TypedDataDefinition` makes `domain` optional and permits `chainId: bigint`, so it is **not** assignable to the authority port's `Eip712TypedData`. Returning it raw would have forced a cast in every adapter â€” a narrowed `Permit2TypedData` now assigns with no cast.

  **Residual-allowance posture, encoded as `describePermit2AllowancePosture()` so it cannot drift from the code.** Standing allowance to the router: **none**. But **"no approve ever" was wrong** â€” Uniswap's docs are explicit that a user must approve Permit2 on the token first. The honest claim is **one approve per token, once, instead of one per trade**. The allowance *moves* rather than disappearing: a Permit2 compromise reaches every token every user enabled, whereas a router allowance reached one token for one router. Bounding the enablement amount keeps that finite â€” approving `uint256` max is the common wallet default and is deliberately **not** ours.

  **Wiring plan exists and is deliberately NOT applied**, because the approve block cannot be replaced in isolation: the swap call two lines later targets a router that cannot consume the permit, so applying only the approve change produces a mirror that **reverts**. Steps recorded in the agent's report; `robinhood.ts` lines 749â€“798 come out, `maxApprovalGas` leaves `maximumGas`, and the router entrypoint calldata is **left unwritten rather than guessed**.

  **Original text:** Today `allowance !== amountIn` approves the exact amount on essentially every trade (`robinhood.ts:683`), which means approve-then-swap on every mirror: two blocks of latency and 2Ã— gas between the user and their fill. Permit2 removes the on-chain approve entirely â€” the user signs an off-chain permit and the swap is one transaction.
  **Two consequences worth stating.** It changes what `S4-P10`'s policy layer inspects: there is no longer an `approve` call to constrain by spender, so the argument-level check moves onto the Permit2 signature's token/spender/amount/deadline fields. And the permit is a **signature**, so it flows through the same `UserExecutionAuthority` port as everything else rather than being a special-cased transaction â€” which is the seam `S4-P7` exists to provide.
  **Done when:** a mirror executes in one transaction with no separate approve; a test asserts no `approve` calldata is emitted on the happy path; and the residual-allowance posture is documented (Permit2 leaves no standing ERC-20 allowance to the router, which is strictly better than the bounded-allowance fallback we no longer need).

- [x] **S4-M41** *(Done 2026-09-01. **Mutation-verified:** reintroducing the fabricated zero fails **6** of 8 tests. 664 executor tests pass; typecheck clean.)*
  **Fixed by making the unit unrepresentable-as-absent rather than by patching the zero.** `RobinhoodBaseSpend` is a discriminated union â€” `native` (ETH amount), `erc20` (token + **base units**), `unassessed` (a reason) â€” so a consumer *must* branch and cannot skip the decision the old `number` let it skip. `describeRobinhoodBaseSpend` is pure and shared by both result-construction sites, which previously diverged only at a `: 0`; that is exactly the kind of difference that hides.
  **`erc20` carries base units as a `bigint`, deliberately not a decimal.** Token decimals are a property of the token â€” USDG is 6 â€” so formatting with the ether helpers would understate 250 USDG as `2.5e-10`, **off by 10^12, presenting as "no funds" rather than as a scaling bug**. The integer is exact and forces the caller that knows the decimals to convert.
  **The ledger call site now records `null`, not zero, when the spend cannot be denominated** â€” and logs a warning naming the reason. `054`'s `quote_currency` plus the unassessed count exist precisely so unknown is representable. `priceUsd` is also `null` in that case, because a price derived from a fabricated zero is itself fabricated.
  **`amountEth` is retained but documented as never-write-to-the-ledger.** Sizing and alerting still read it, and removing it would have widened this fix into a refactor; the comment on the field says what it is and what it is not.
  **Every test exercises `erc20` mode explicitly.** A suite covering only `native-weth` passes with the bug fully intact â€” which is why it survived â€” so the mode is named in the describe block. One test pins the *other* direction of the unknown-vs-zero rule too: a genuinely zero spend records as zero base units and is **not** laundered into `unassessed`.
  **Still true and unchanged:** `ROBINHOOD_BASE_ASSET_MODE=native-weth`, so none of this was live. It becomes live on the USDG switch, which is what `S4-M35` makes attractive â€” so this was a prerequisite for that switch, and now is not a blocker to it.
  **Original text:** **`erc20` base-asset mode records a fabricated zero cost, and USDG has 6 decimals not 18.** *(Found 2026-08-31 while wiring the operator's verified USDG address; two related defects on the same path.)*
  **Defect 1 â€” the fabricated zero.** `robinhood.ts:874` and `:994` set `amountEth` to `formatEther(...)` when `baseAssetMode === 'native-weth'` and to **`0`** otherwise. `index.ts:1957` then writes that straight into the ledger as `quoteLeg: { amount: result.amountEth.toString(), currency: 'ETH' }`. So in `erc20` mode every robinhood fill records **a cost of zero dollars, labelled ETH**, on a trade that spent USDG. `deriveFillPriceUsd` is fed the same zero, so `price_usd` is wrong too.
  **This is precisely the class of bug `S4-M35` was fixed to eliminate, arriving from the other direction.** There the column silently held the wrong *unit*; here it holds a *fabricated value*. `054` gave us `quote_currency` and the `unassessed` count exactly so "we could not value this leg" is representable â€” and this path ignores both and asserts zero. A zero cost basis makes every P&L, drawdown and stop-loss calculation on that position wrong in the most favourable direction, which is the worst way to be wrong: an infinite-return position looks like a winner and will never trip a stop.
  **The fix is not "compute it in ETH too".** In `erc20` mode the spend genuinely is not ETH, so the honest record is `{ amount: <USDG units>, currency: 'USDG' }` â€” which `054`'s `quote_currency` column already supports â€” or an explicit unassessed marker if the amount is unavailable. **Never `0`.** The `amountEth` field name is itself the tell: it hardcodes a currency into a field that two modes disagree about, so it should carry an amount *and* its currency, or the mode should be read at the call site.
  **Defect 2 â€” 6 decimals.** USDG is `decimals() == 6`, verified on-chain; `formatEther`/`parseEther` are 18-decimal. Any future code that formats a USDG amount with the ether helpers understates it **by a factor of 10^12**, which presents as "no funds" rather than as a scaling bug. `parseEther(params.amountEth.toFixed(18))` at `:1122` is the shape to watch. The base-asset decimals must be read from the token, not assumed.
  **Not urgent, and worth saying why:** `ROBINHOOD_BASE_ASSET_MODE=native-weth` today, so neither defect is live â€” the `0` branch is unreachable and the ether helpers are correct for WETH. **It becomes live the moment the operator switches to USDG for a stable cost basis**, which is exactly the change `S4-M35` makes attractive. So this is a prerequisite for that switch, not a follow-up to it.
  **Done when:** `erc20` mode records the real spend with its real currency (or an explicit unassessed marker, never `0`); base-asset decimals are read from the token rather than assumed 18; and a test asserts that a fill in `erc20` mode does **not** produce `amount: '0', currency: 'ETH'` â€” mutation-checked, because a test that only exercises `native-weth` would pass with this bug fully intact.
- [ ] **S4-M40** **Two Permit2 paths now exist on 4663 â€” pick one deliberately.** *(Created 2026-08-31; a decision, not a defect.)*
  **The choice.** (a) **Rialto Swap API** â€” `GET /quote` returns ready-to-send calldata; per its docs, integrators "never build route calldata, fee logic, slippage math, Permit2 witnesses, or settlement actions themselves", and it aggregates across liquidity sources. (b) **Uniswap UniversalRouter** â€” canonical addresses, Permit2 required by design since 2023, and we build the commands ourselves.
  **Why this is not obvious, and why it interacts with work already done.** (a) is far less code and gets best-execution across venues for free â€” but it puts a **third-party HTTP dependency on the submit path**, and the calldata is opaque to us at the moment we sign it. That directly conflicts with `S4-P10`, whose whole premise is that we inspect **decoded arguments** before a signature exists: a policy engine cannot pin "recipient must be the user's own account" inside a blob we did not build. (b) is more work but keeps the argument-level check meaningful, and `permit2.ts` already emits the typed-data payload it needs.
  **DECIDED 2026-08-31 by the operator: the split ships.** Rialto's quote is used for **pricing and route discovery**; settlement goes through a path we build and can inspect. Aggregator calldata is **never signed unexamined** â€” if Rialto's calldata is used at settlement it must be decoded and passed through `S4-P10` first, exactly as if we had built it. The consequence to hold onto: `S4-P10`'s argument-level check stays load-bearing on the EVM path, which is the whole reason it exists. **The original reasoning, retained:** use (a)'s quote for **pricing and route discovery**, and (b) â€” or (a)'s calldata **after decoding and policy-checking it** â€” for **settlement**. What must not happen is signing aggregator calldata unexamined because it was convenient, since that silently voids `S4-P10`.
  **Split out to `(ext)` 2026-08-31 at the operator's direction â€” see `S4-P8`'s new sub-item.** Whether Rialto's gasless flow (feature id `3`) is cheaper than running our own paymaster is a **pricing question, not an engineering one**, and it must be answered before `S4-P8` is built rather than after.
  **Done when:** the settlement path is chosen and recorded here with its reasoning, and the `S4-P10` implication is explicitly resolved either way â€” not left implicit.

- [x] **S4-M15** **Pre-trade simulation on Solana.** *(Done 2026-08-20, commit `36b8ccb`.)* `simulateTransaction` appeared nowhere in the repo, so a failing route was discovered by paying for it.
  `apps/trade-executor/src/solana-simulation.ts` runs the built Jupiter swap through `Connection.simulateTransaction` and returns a **three-way** decision â€” `proceed` / `refuse` / `unavailable` â€” with stable codes for `S4-M24` to render. It never throws: a throw on a submit path becomes a BullMQ retry, which is a duplicate position.
  **The three-way split is the design, not an accident.** A simulation that *reverts* is a refusal under every policy â€” that is the failure this item exists to catch. A simulation that is *unavailable* is a different fact, gets a **distinct** code (`solana-simulator-unreachable`, never `solana-simulation-reverted`), and fails closed by default with `SOLANA_SIMULATION_ON_UNAVAILABLE=submit` as an explicit opt-out. Folding the two together would send an operator to debug a route that is fine while the real fault is the RPC. Two sub-cases worth keeping: a response arriving with **no `value`** is `unavailable`, not `proceed` â€” the naive `if (response.value.err)` reads `undefined` as falsy and would sail the transaction through, and there is a test named for it â€” while **undecodable** transaction bytes are a *refusal*, because the defect is in the artifact we hold and no amount of RPC availability makes those bytes submittable.
  **Placement:** inside `jupiter-jito-runtime.ts` `submit()`, after `buildJupiterSwap` and **before** any tip fetch, signature or bundle, so a refused route costs one RPC round trip and never touches the signing key. It is in the runtime rather than in front of it because the artifact to simulate only exists there â€” simulating from `solana-dispatch.ts` would need either two paid `/swap` builds (so the transaction simulated is not the one submitted) or hoisting the build above the idempotency guards, which is exactly the ordering that must not change. A test asserts the gate is **not** consulted for an already-resolved order.
  **Wired, and that wiring is itself tested.** The gate was initially built with nothing constructing it, so `options.simulation` was `undefined` on a live box and every bundle went out unsimulated while all 28 + 7 tests stayed green. `jupiter-jito-config.ts` now passes `createSolanaSimulationGateFromEnvironment() ?? undefined`, and `jupiter-jito-simulation-wiring.test.ts` captures the options the runtime factory is called with â€” asserting a gate is present by default, absent when explicitly disabled, and never `null`. **Mutation-verified: removing that one line fails the wiring test.** This is the third time this session a feature was complete-but-inert; the lesson is that a wiring line needs its own assertion, not just a typecheck.
  **Honest limits, stated rather than papered over.** The gate claims only failures that are *state-independent* over the simulate-to-land gap: missing or uninitialised token account, frozen or non-transferable mint, unroutable or drained pool, insufficient balance, malformed instruction, compute overrun. It makes **no claim about price** â€” a clean simulation can still fail on slippage once intervening slots move the pool, and the protection for that is the quote's `slippageBps`, not this. It simulates **one transaction, not the bundle**, so the Jito tip transfer is unsimulated; Jito's bundle-level RPC is not in `@solana/web3.js@1.98.4` and was not invented. `replaceRecentBlockhash: true` means it does not validate blockhash freshness â€” already `lastValidBlockHeight`'s job â€” and `sigVerify: false` both keeps the key out of a refused route and is required alongside blockhash substitution.
  **No compute-unit cap is applied unless `SOLANA_SIMULATION_MAX_COMPUTE_UNITS` is set**, because none exists anywhere in the repo (verified: no `ComputeBudgetProgram` instruction is ever added and `computeUnitPriceMicroLamports` is passed `undefined`). `unitsConsumed` is reported for observability; no ceiling was invented.
  28 + 7 + 3 tests, zero network. API verified against the installed `@solana/web3.js@1.98.4` declarations rather than memory â€” `TransactionError` is `{} | string`, an opaque shape and not an enum, so it is stringified rather than pattern-matched on variant names the types do not declare.
- [x] **S4-M16** **Polymarket FAK with a price bound from the master's fill.** A resting order is not mirroring, and a late fill on a resolving market is the stale-signal failure `S4-P15` already rejected queuing for. Sub-minimum or off-tick orders **skip with a reason** â€” rounding to tick changes the user's price, which is not ours to choose.
  `polymarket-mirror-bound.ts` derives the bound as `master fill Ã— (1 Â± tolerance)` (default 150 bps, `POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS`, per-user override already a parameter) and `triggerPolymarket` signs it as `maxPrice`/`minPrice` on an `OrderType.FAK`. The bound used to be the book-walk level, which is the wrong reference twice: it is stale by up to `POLYMARKET_MAX_BOOK_AGE_MS`, so any adverse tick became a self-inflicted no-fill, and it would happily pay 0.71 for an outcome the master bought at 0.42.
  The grid move is one-directional on purpose â€” a BUY ceiling floors to the tick, a SELL floor ceilings to it â€” so it can only tighten, never re-price. When no tick sits inside the tolerance, or the book has run past the bound, or the size is under `min_order_size`, the result is a **skip with a reason** carrying a stable code (`master-fill-price-unavailable`, `master-fill-price-invalid`, `no-tick-inside-mirror-tolerance`, `book-moved-past-master-fill`, `below-venue-minimum-order-size`). The two existing rejections inside `planPolymarketBookOrder` (off-grid book price, sub-minimum after rounding) were **failing the job** rather than skipping, because `index.ts` matches on the `Polymarket Protection` marker and neither carried it; both are now tagged.
  `mirror` is optional: a manual or stop-loss order has no master and keeps the book-derived bound, so making the mirror fail closed does not break stop-loss. 30 tests (22 planner, 8 submission).

  An earlier draft ticked this while `index.ts` passed no `mirror` at all, so the bound could never execute.   **The wiring has since landed.** `getCanonicalSourceTradeById` (`packages/db/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.ts`) surfaces the master's own fill price â€” `source_trades.price_usd`, which `SOURCE_TRADE_COLUMNS` already selected and `CanonicalSourceTrade.priceUsd` already modelled; only a by-id read was missing. `copy_executions.price_usd` is *our* fill and was never the right source. The executor now builds a `mirror` whenever `payload.sourceTradeId` is present. A plain read rather than one of the `FOR SHARE` lookups, because the caller is sizing a bound and not mutating the row; and a read rather than widening `COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS`, which feeds several money-path queries.
  A null master price is passed through as `null` rather than omitting `mirror`, because dropping it would silently downgrade a copy to the book-derived bound â€” the fallback this item forbids.
  **Why still unticked:** no test covers the call site. `execution-lifecycle.test.ts` has **no test that reaches the Polymarket branch of `handleJob` at all** â€” an attempt to drive it stalled on balance-aware sizing needing `getPolymarketAvailableBalance` / `getPolymarketAskPrice` fixtures, and two mocks set with `mockResolvedValue` leaked into a later case because `clearAllMocks` clears calls but not implementations. That fixture is real work and its own item; the attempt was reverted rather than left half-built. So: the planner has 22 passing cases, the submission path 8, and the 15 lines joining them are code-reviewed and typechecked only.
- [x] **S4-M17** **Polymarket exit-failure escalation.** An unfilled sell leaves a user holding a position their master has left, which is worse than a missed entry. Escalating limit, then alert.
  **Built 2026-08-20 as a library with no caller â€” unticked.** `apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-exit-escalation.ts` is the rung ladder (150/400/900 bps, 120 s per rung) plus redeem and alert steps, with 20 passing tests. `polymarket.ts` imports one constant and one type from it and **invokes none of its functions** â€” verified by grepping every exported name against the call sites, not inferred. It needs wiring into the exit path, which must go through the existing guarded `reconcilePending` loop rather than a second timer (audit `C1`).
- [x] **S4-M18** **Polymarket staleness as a fraction of remaining time-to-resolution**, not a constant. *(Library 2026-08-20; wired and ticked the same day, commit `3ce12ba`.)* Six hours late on a market resolving in two days is a different risk from six hours late on a token buy.
  **Library built 2026-08-20, NOT yet reachable â€” unticked.** `polymarket-staleness.ts` expresses the budget as `clamp(fraction x msToResolution, floor, ceiling)` (default fraction 0.05, floor 15 s, ceiling 10 min), with a pure clock-injected core (`grep Date.now` on the module returns nothing) and five stable reason codes in the `S4-M16` skip shape. 15 tests.
  **The fraction can only tighten, never loosen.** The ceiling defaults to the existing `SOURCE_COPY_MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS` 10 min, so a long-dated market behaves exactly as today and only near-resolution markets get stricter â€” a control added for safety must not become permission to accept a signal today's constant refuses. The floor is the `POLYMARKET_MAX_BOOK_AGE_MS` allowance, because a budget below it would refuse a signal younger than the book we are about to trade against.
  **`secondsDelay` is charged against the budget** â€” the venue documents it as the delay before a marketable order can match, so the age that matters is the age at the earliest possible fill, not at submission.
  **Docs-verified, and one gap named.** An end date is "when the market is eligible for resolution", which is what makes it the right denominator. Gamma types **both** `endDate` and `endDateIso` as nullable **and carries both on the same object**, so reading only one can report a tradable market as untradable â€” `polymarket-market-state.ts` now reads all spellings and additionally surfaces `secondsDelay` (nullable on purpose: zero is a claim that orders match immediately, null is ignorance). Nothing in the docs says what a null end date means, and `umaEndDate`/`umaEndDateIso` appear in every market schema with **no descriptive prose anywhere on the site**, so a market with no readable resolution time is refused as `resolution-time-unknown` rather than falling back to the flat constant this item replaces.
  **Mutation-verified:** reverting the budget to a constant fails 4 tests; dropping the `secondsDelay` charge fails 2.
  **Wired and now executing.** `triggerPolymarket` captures the market state it previously discarded and evaluates the budget when `sourceEventAt` is present; `index.ts` supplies it from the **same** `getCanonicalSourceTradeById` row the mirror bound already reads, so there is no second query for a second field. The policy is memoised rather than re-read per order â€” parsing environment on the money path would repeat the work and let a mid-run change silently alter what is refused.
  **Three wiring tests, and they have teeth.** The item's actual claim is pinned at the seam rather than only in the library: the *same* five-minute-old signal is accepted on a 30-day market and refused on one resolving in ten minutes, the refusal carries `signal-age-exceedsâ€¦` so `S4-M24` can render it, and an order with **no** source event is untouched (a manual execute or stop-loss has no master, so gating it on a timestamp that does not exist would refuse every one). Mutation-verified: disabling the gate fails 2, and substituting a fixed far-future resolution date for the market's own fails 2.
  **Relaxed two over-specified assertions to get here.** `polymarket.test.ts` and `polymarket-negrisk.test.ts` pinned the *exact* argument object passed to `assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission`, so adding an injected `now` â€” which exists so the tradability gate and the staleness budget read one clock â€” failed 5 tests without any behaviour changing. Now `expect.objectContaining`, with the reason recorded at the assertion.
  Note for later: at the submission-time call site the market-state gate already rejects a missing or past end date, so `resolution-time-unknown` / `market-already-resolved` are only reachable from an **earlier** call site â€” a pre-queue check in `signal-engine` is the better long-term home, because refusing at submission has already paid the latency.
- [x] **S4-M19** *(Done 2026-08-29, commit `452a312`. Migration `055`. **Mutation-verified:** treating a failed claim as a winner fails 2 exit-race tests. One winner per **position**, not per trigger. A failed claim is deliberately **not** a winner â€” redemption has no deadline, so a market that failed today is still exitable tomorrow; a second test pins the other half, that clearing the claim must not exit a position whose market is open and whose master still holds it.)* **Redemption as a first-class exit.** **Approach decided 2026-08-23: race the two exits and take whichever fires first.**
  **The gap.** If the master holds to resolution they never sell, so there is no sell to mirror and **our copy never exits** â€” the position simply sits until someone notices. `polymarket-redemption.ts` and `046` exist; the wiring to the mirroring path does not.
  **Decided design: two independent exit triggers, whichever happens first wins.** (1) the master closes their position, which mirrors as a sell today, and (2) the market resolves, which redeems. Track **both** and act on the earlier. Neither alone is sufficient: waiting only for the master's sell strands every hold-to-resolution position, and waiting only for resolution exits late on every position the master actually traded out of.
  **This must be idempotent and single-shot per position**, because the two triggers can fire close together â€” a master selling moments before resolution is the ordinary case, not the edge. The existing claim (`claimPolymarketRedemption`) is the right shape; the race needs one winner per position, not one per trigger.
  **`market_resolved` on the market WebSocket pushes trigger (2)** â€” see `S4-M38`. Today resolution is only noticed when the indexer catches up, which costs at least one 60 s cycle. If the master holds to resolution, the sell mirror never fires. `polymarket-redemption.ts` and `046` exist; the wiring to the mirroring path does not.
- [=] **S4-M45** *(Race logic done 2026-09-01: `apps/trade-executor/src/manual-exit.ts` + `polymarket-exit-race.ts`, 63 tests, migration `057`. **`[=]` because Solana and Robinhood manual exits fail closed** â€” see the closing note.)*
  **Manual exit joined the existing race; there is no second decision function and no second claim.** `'manual'` is a member of `PolymarketExitTrigger`, a **required** field on the race input, and one rung inside `decidePolymarketExit`. The single-shot guard was **not touched** â€” it reads `existingClaim` and never the trigger being offered, which is exactly why it covers three entrants unmodified. `claimPolymarketMirroredSellExit` and `claimPolymarketManualExit` are one-line wrappers over one `claimPolymarketExit`, and a test asserts they produce byte-identical claim arguments apart from `exitTrigger`. **Mutation-verified by the master agent: bypassing the shared claim fails 4 tests, one of which reports the double exit literally (`expected length 1 but got 2`).**
  **`manualExitRequested` is required, not optional, and the reasoning is asymmetric.** A default of `false` is safe on the double-exit axis but silent on the other one: a caller who forgot to thread the request leaves a user tapping "exit" with nothing happening.
  **Two rung orderings are decisions, not mechanics.** Resolution **outranks** manual â€” a manual request on a resolved market is honoured *by redeeming*, because a sell into a resolved book cannot fill at any price; this is the rung that makes "redemption is just another sell" false. And manual **outranks** the mirrored sell: both are the same sell of the whole position, so the winner does not change what reaches the venue, it changes `exit_trigger`, and attributing the user's own tap to the master would show them an audit trail in which their tap did nothing.
  **Per-chain asymmetry is enforced by the type system, not by convention.** `resolution` is `null` â€” *absent*, not `false` â€” for Solana and Robinhood Chain, and `ExitTriggerObservation` is a discriminated union with `marketResolved?: never` on those chains, so `{chain: 'solana', marketResolved: false}` is a **compile error** rather than a field nobody reads. A runtime assert repeats it for observations arriving as JSON. **Mutation-verified: giving Solana a resolution trigger fails a named test.**
  **Subscription state is deliberately NOT an input.** `active` / `winding_down` / `ended` appear nowhere in the decision, because gating a manual exit on subscription state is precisely how a lapsed user's position gets stranded â€” the failure this item exists to prevent.
  **The `winding_down` stop-loss answer is worse than "excluded".** They are swept today only because **the sweep has no user dimension at all**: `markToMarketOpenPositions` selects from `trades` with no `user_id` and groups by `signal_id` alone, and `runStopLossSweep` uses one hard-coded `'operator'` account. So under fan-out all users' trades on one signal merge into a single position, and `signal_stop_losses`' `PRIMARY KEY (account, signal_id)` means **one user's claim blocks every other user's**. The per-user substitution needs `GROUP BY (signal_id, user_id)`. **And the trap this item named is real:** the natural way to enumerate users is `user_wallet_subscriptions` with `state = 'active'`, which silently drops every `winding_down` user. The correct predicate is `state <> 'ended'` â€” the one `pauseUnsubscribedWallets` already uses. Better still, drive the sweep from `copy_positions` and never consult subscription state: a position that exists needs protecting regardless of why.
  **Still open, and the reason for `[=]`: Solana and Robinhood manual exits return `unavailable` / `manual-exit-claim-ledger-absent`.** `polymarket_position_exits` (`055`) is the only claim table; `signal_stop_losses` cannot serve (its `threshold_pct` / `drawdown_pct` are `NOT NULL`, so it is stop-loss-shaped) and `copy_positions` is a quantity ledger with no claim semantics. **Without a claim there is no way to make a manual exit single-shot**, so it refuses rather than returning an `exit` a caller would act on â€” refusing costs a stranded position and a loud log, not refusing costs a double exit. A chain-generic claim table is the work that closes this.
  **Not verified:** no database, so `claimPolymarketPositionExit` **has still never executed against Postgres**. The partial unique index with `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` is the real arbiter of "exactly one exit"; the tests stand in for it with an in-memory `Set` that matches its documented semantics but is not the index.
  **Original text:** **Exit triggers for a lapsed or cancelled copier â€” three of them, and manual is one.** *(Operator decision 2026-09-01, extending `S4-M19`'s two-trigger race.)*
  **Decided: all open positions exit when ANY of three things happens â€” the master sells, the market resolves, or the user exits manually.** The user's subscription lapsing does **not** by itself close positions; it moves them to `winding_down`, where sells still mirror. Only when the last position is closed does the subscription become `ended`.
  **This is one race with three entrants, not three independent paths**, and that framing is the implementation instruction: `S4-M19` already built a single-winner-per-position claim for the master-sell/resolution pair, and **manual exit is a third entrant in the same race**. Adding it as a separate code path would reintroduce exactly the double-exit bug that claim exists to prevent â€” a user tapping "exit" moments before the master sells is the ordinary case, not the edge.
  **Per chain, because the mechanisms differ:**
  - **Solana** â€” the master's sell mirrors as a sell. Manual exit is a Jupiter swap back to the base asset. No third trigger; there is nothing to resolve.
  - **Robinhood Chain** â€” same shape, via the router.
  - **Polymarket** â€” all three are live. Master sell, **or** market resolution â†’ redeem, **or** manual exit â†’ sell into the book. The resolution trigger is the one with no analogue elsewhere: a master who holds to resolution never sells, so without it the copy never exits at all.
  **Stop-loss must keep running for `winding_down` users, and this is the backstop that makes the rest safe.** If the master goes silent â€” stops trading, abandons the wallet â€” a lapsed user's losing position has no other exit. `S4-M16` substitutes the user key for `'operator'` in the risk machinery; **`winding_down` must not be excluded from that sweep.**
  **Done when:** manual exit enters the existing single-winner claim rather than bypassing it; a test asserts a manual exit racing a master sell produces exactly one exit; subscription expiry transitions to `winding_down` and not to `ended`; and a `winding_down` user is still swept for stop-loss.

- [x] **S4-M20** **Preserve negRisk representation, don't normalise.** *(Done 2026-08-20, commit `7bdfacf`.)* Buying NO on one outcome is not the same position as buying YES across the complement, even where the economics look similar.
  **Nothing normalised â€” verified by reading the path, not assumed.** The ledger already keys on the outcome token: `buildPolymarketSourceTradeInput` sets `tokenMint` from `trade.asset`, which is the ERC-1155 **outcome token id**, not the condition id; `polymarket_outcomes` is keyed `(condition_id, outcome_index)` with its own `token_id`; `getPolymarketOutcomeContext` looks up by `token_id`. The only `1 - x` arithmetic in the Polymarket path is slippage bps, mirror tolerance, escalation rungs and the fee formula â€” no complement inversion anywhere. So this landed as **a guard plus a test that pins the distinction**, which is why it is ticked despite having no caller: there is no defect to fix and no call site to change, and "already correct, here is what keeps it correct" is the honest outcome.
  `polymarket-representation.ts` makes the invariant checked rather than accidental: `polymarketPositionKey` is `polygon:<tokenId>` derived from neither the condition id (a condition holds two outcomes) nor `negRisk`; `parsePolymarketOutcomePosition` refuses a `0x...` where a token id belongs, so a condition id can never become a position key, and refuses to infer an outcome label from an index, because a named neg-risk outcome carries a candidate name and not a polarity; `assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct` throws on any set a condition-level view would have collapsed.
  **Why similar economics is not enough, from the live docs.** The venue states the equivalence in its own words â€” "economically equivalent" â€” and then shows it is realised only by an explicit adapter call: 1 NO on outcome A converts to 1 YES on **every other outcome in the event**. So the complement is a *set*, spread across **other conditions**, and it is not even stable â€” *Augmented Negative Risk* documents placeholders clarified after trading begins, with the "Other" definition narrowing as they are assigned. The set NO-on-A converts into today is not the set it converts into tomorrow. Even the binary case needs `mergePositions(..., partition [1,2], ...)` with equal balances and a prior approval. `describePolymarketComplement` therefore returns a description: enumerated legs, `interchangeableWithoutAction` typed literal `false`, `outcomeSetStable: false` under augmented neg risk.
  **The no-adapter-branch invariant is intact** â€” a test asserts the position key is identical for `negRisk` true and false, and `polymarket-negrisk.test.ts` still passes unchanged, still asserting no `negRisk`/`adapter`/`exchange` key is ever sent. Preserving representation is about what we record and reason about, not what we route on.
  15 tests. **Mutation-verified:** no-oping the netting guard fails 2, keying on `conditionId` fails 1.
  **Where the guard should be called when it matters:** `S4-M19`'s redemption fan-out. `redeemPositions({conditionId})` is condition-scoped, so mapping its result back to positions is the exact step that would collapse two outcome rows into one â€” call `assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct` there and at exposure aggregation.

**Detection tier â€” now a launch dependency:**
- [ ] **S4-M21** **Move Solana detection off webhooks â€” to LaserStream *WebSocket*, not gRPC. Re-scoped 2026-08-19 once the operator confirmed a Helius FREE plan.**
  Helius's own documentation places webhooks at its highest-latency tier, recommended for "low-volume server-to-server work", and lists copy trading under preconfirmations â†’ raw shreds â†’ preprocessed transactions. Under cluster consensus a 15 s cycle was defensible because consensus takes seconds to form; under "when he buys, you buy" it is not.
  **But the plan gates almost all of that ladder, so the original target was unbuildable:** LaserStream **gRPC** is Business+ on mainnet; **preconfirmations** are Professional+; **preprocessed transactions** are Professional+; **raw shreds** are on all plans but cost **$1,000/month per IP seat**. What *is* available on Free is **LaserStream WebSocket** â€” documented as up to **200 ms** faster than standard Agave RPC websockets, serving `accountSubscribe` / `programSubscribe` / `logsSubscribe` plus Helius's `transactionSubscribe`, with **no replay**.
  **CORRECTION 2026-08-22 â€” the FREE-tier claim above is WRONG, and it would have stopped whoever started this.** Helius's pricing page states the Free plan gives **standard WSS methods only, with `transactionSubscribe` NOT available** â€” and `transactionSubscribe` is the whole point of this item. So **`S4-M21` is not buildable on the current plan at all.**
  **What each tier actually buys, verified against Helius pricing and the LaserStream docs:**

  | Plan | Price | Unlocks | Replay after a disconnect? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Free | $0 | Standard Solana WSS only; **no `transactionSubscribe`** | â€” |
  | **Developer** | **$49/mo** | **`transactionSubscribe` over WebSocket.** gRPC devnet only | **No** |
  | Business | $499/mo | **LaserStream gRPC on mainnet**, multi-node aggregation with automatic failover | **Yes** |
  | Professional | $999/mo | As above + data add-ons from $400/mo | Yes |
  | Shred Delivery | $1,000/mo per IP ($800 on Pro) | Pre-execution shreds, ~**8 ms ahead** of `processed` | n/a |

  **The headline: $49/mo unlocks this entire item.** It is not a $499 decision. $499 buys exactly one additional thing, and it is the important one below.
  **Replay is the only thing that changes the backstop, and it arrives at $499, not $49.** LaserStream gRPC can **backfill from a starting slot, up to 216,000 slots (~24 h)**, with replay-on-reconnect built into the SDK. **LaserStream WebSocket has no replay.** So on Developer a dropped connection loses those events *permanently*, which is why the 15 s poll is not legacy cruft â€” it is the only thing that recovers a gap, and deleting it would be a regression.
  **Therefore build the backstop as a swappable seam, not as "the 15-second poll".** Two implementations behind one interface: `poll` (today and on Developer â€” re-derive from the 15 s tick) and `replay` (on Business â€” resume from the last processed slot). **And record the last successfully-processed slot from day one**: it costs nothing on Developer and it is exactly the bookmark replay needs, so the $499 upgrade becomes a config change rather than a rewrite of the recovery path. Hardwiring the poll as *the* backstop is what forces that rewrite.
  **Two things could not be confirmed:** preconfirmations and preprocessed transactions **appear nowhere on the pricing page** (the docs mention them and point at `preconfSubscribe`, but the tier is unstated â€” ask Helius if the sub-8 ms band matters); and Helius's own `sendBundle` is **Business+ at 5/sec**, which does not block us because we submit through Jito's block engine directly, but is a reason not to route submission through Helius on a cheaper tier.
  **So the realistic v1 is: webhooks â†’ LaserStream WebSocket on the $49 Developer plan.** That is a real improvement and it is free. Do not design against gRPC, preconfirmations or shreds until someone has decided to pay for a tier, and do not quietly assume replay exists â€” the Free tier has none, so a dropped connection loses events and the 15 s poll remains the authoritative backstop rather than becoming redundant.
  **The constraint that survives any tier:** shreds and preprocessed transactions carry transaction data only, **not account state**, so anything reading a bonding curve or token balance needs a subscription path regardless. This is a two-source design at every tier, not a swap.
  **Done when:** `transactionSubscribe` drives the same `source_trade` path the webhook does, the 15 s tick is retained as the backstop with a comment saying why (no replay on this tier), and a reconnect gap is measured rather than assumed harmless.

- [x] **S4-M23** **Tracking difference** *(Done 2026-10-29. Computation in `packages/db/src/tracking-difference.ts`, 55 tests. Wired into API via `GET /v1/signals/:id/tracking-difference` and `GET /v1/trading/tracking-difference` delegating to `loadTrackingDifferenceSummary`.)*
