import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT,
  circuitBreakerAccountForUser,
  narrowExecutionMode,
  reconciliationAccountForUser,
  resolveConvictionRiskPct,
  resolvePerUserMode,
  riskPolicyAccountForUser,
  sizePerUserBuy,
  userDailyExposureCapUsd,
  type PerUserSizingInput,
  type PerUserSizingOutcome
} from './per-user-sizing.js';
import { RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT } from './reconciliation-coordinator.js';
import { calculateBalanceAwareSize, capPositionToAvailableBalance, floorToPrecision } from './policy.js';

/**
 * `S4-15` / `S4-16` / `S4-17`.
 *
 * Every test here is pure â€” no database, no Redis, no clock. That is not a
 * convenience: there is no database available, and this module decides how much of
 * a user's money moves.
 *
 * **Tier gating is deliberately absent.** Whether a user's tier permits a chain is
 * `S4-13`'s decision (`assessFanoutCandidate` â†’ `tier-excludes-chain`), and it has
 * already happened by the time a candidate reaches sizing. A tier assertion here
 * would either duplicate that suite or encode a tier-table decision the operator
 * has not made.
 */

const USER = '7c9e1f52-0000-4000-8000-000000000001';

/**
 * A live, certified, well-funded baseline.
 *
 * Numbers chosen so each clamp can be made the *binding* one by moving a single
 * field: with a 10 SOL balance at 10% the request is 1.0, comfortably under the
 * platform ceiling of 5 and the 2.5-unit daily headroom. A fixture where several
 * caps coincide makes every assertion pass for the wrong reason.
 */
function baseInput(overrides: Partial<PerUserSizingInput> = {}): PerUserSizingInput {
  return {
    userId: USER,
    chain: 'solana',
    settings: { maxPositionPct: 10, maxDailyExposurePct: 25, killed: false },
    userRequestedMode: 'live',
    platform: { effectiveMode: 'live', certified: true },
    balance: { liveUnits: 10, paperUnits: 100 },
    usdPerUnit: 100,
    dailyExposureUsdUsed: 0,
    conviction: null,
    tierMultiplier: 1,
    scoreMultiplier: 1,
    baseUnits: 0.5,
    platformMaximumUnits: 5,
    precision: 6,
    dynamic: true,
    ...overrides
  };
}

function sized(outcome: PerUserSizingOutcome): Extract<PerUserSizingOutcome, { kind: 'size' }> {
  if (outcome.kind !== 'size') {
    throw new Error(`expected a size, got refusal ${outcome.code}: ${outcome.reason}`);
  }
  return outcome;
}

function refused(
  outcome: PerUserSizingOutcome
): Extract<PerUserSizingOutcome, { kind: 'refuse' }> {
  if (outcome.kind !== 'refuse') {
    throw new Error(`expected a refusal, got a size of ${outcome.sizeUnits}`);
  }
  return outcome;
}

describe('S4-16 account keys â€” the two constants must not collapse', () => {
  it('substitutes the user id into the risk policy account', () => {
    // The whole of `S4-16`: `resolveRiskPolicy` / the breaker already take
    // `account: string`, so per-user risk is a value substitution.
    expect(riskPolicyAccountForUser(USER)).toBe(USER);
    expect(riskPolicyAccountForUser(USER)).not.toBe(RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT);
  });

  it('keeps the reconciliation account as operator even with a user id in hand', () => {
    // The Â§1 exception. `copy_executions.target_account` holds a wallet address, so
    // filtering it by a user id claims zero rows and the escalation stream silently
    // fragments into N while scoping nothing.
    expect(reconciliationAccountForUser(USER)).toBe(RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT);
    expect(reconciliationAccountForUser(USER)).toBe('operator');
    expect(reconciliationAccountForUser(null)).toBe('operator');
  });

  it('keeps the two keys distinct for the same user', () => {
    // The find-and-replace guard. Collapsing the two constants into one makes this
    // equality hold and the test fail.
    expect(riskPolicyAccountForUser(USER)).not.toBe(reconciliationAccountForUser(USER));
  });

  it('falls back to the operator account only for the pre-tenancy path', () => {
    expect(riskPolicyAccountForUser(null)).toBe(RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT);
    expect(RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT).toBe('operator');
  });

  it('keys the breaker on the same account as the risk policy', () => {
    // Two keys for one user would give them a policy under one name and a breaker
    // under another, so a tripped breaker would not stop the trades it was sized for.
    expect(circuitBreakerAccountForUser(USER)).toBe(riskPolicyAccountForUser(USER));
  });

  it('refuses an empty user id rather than silently keying on the operator', () => {
    expect(() => riskPolicyAccountForUser('')).toThrow(/non-empty user id/);
    expect(() => riskPolicyAccountForUser('   ')).toThrow(/non-empty user id/);
  });

  it('reports the risk account on the sizing outcome', () => {
    expect(sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput())).riskAccount).toBe(USER);
    expect(sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ userId: null }))).riskAccount).toBe('operator');
  });
});

describe('S4-17 platform clamp â€” narrowing only', () => {
  it('never re-widens a platform paper verdict to live', () => {
    // The mutation this file exists to catch. The user's stored preference is
    // `live`; the platform said `paper` because a certification lapsed. Returning
    // the user's preference opens a real position on an uncertified chain.
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('paper', 'live')).toBe('paper');
  });

  it('lets the user narrow live to paper', () => {
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('live', 'paper')).toBe('paper');
  });

  it('treats off on either side as off', () => {
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('off', 'live')).toBe('off');
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('live', 'off')).toBe('off');
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('paper', 'off')).toBe('off');
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('off', 'off')).toBe('off');
  });

  it('preserves live+shadow under a live request', () => {
    // Shadow is an operator diagnostic riding a live execution. Collapsing it to
    // `live` would switch the diagnostic off without anyone asking.
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('live+shadow', 'live')).toBe('live+shadow');
    expect(narrowExecutionMode('live+shadow', 'paper')).toBe('paper');
  });

  it('never returns a mode wider than the platform verdict, over the whole matrix', () => {
    const rank = { off: 0, paper: 1, live: 2, 'live+shadow': 2 } as const;
    const platformModes = ['off', 'paper', 'live', 'live+shadow'] as const;
    const userModes = ['off', 'paper', 'live'] as const;
    for (const platform of platformModes) {
      for (const user of userModes) {
        const result = narrowExecutionMode(platform, user);
        expect(rank[result]).toBeLessThanOrEqual(rank[platform]);
        expect(rank[result]).toBeLessThanOrEqual(rank[user]);
      }
    }
  });

  it('records a platform downgrade instead of excluding the user', () => {
    // `S4-13`'s rule, restated at this layer: a failing platform gate downgrades,
    // it never makes a user ineligible. Treating it as an exclusion stops paper
    // copying for everyone the moment a certification lapses.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      platform: {
        effectiveMode: 'paper',
        certified: false,
        reason: 'Chain solana has no active reviewed certification record'
      }
    })));

    expect(outcome.mode.effective).toBe('paper');
    expect(outcome.mode.downgraded).toBe(true);
    expect(outcome.mode.clamp).toBe('platform-clamped-live-to-paper');
    expect(outcome.mode.certified).toBe(false);
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('makes the platform clamp visible with the platform\'s own reason', () => {
    // "Why did I get paper?" has to be answerable from the output alone.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      platform: {
        effectiveMode: 'paper',
        certified: false,
        reason: 'Chain solana is not enabled in LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS'
      }
    })));
    expect(outcome.mode.platformReason).toBe('Chain solana is not enabled in LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS');
    expect(outcome.mode.platformEffective).toBe('paper');
    expect(outcome.mode.userRequested).toBe('live');
  });

  it('sizes a downgraded user off the paper bankroll, not their live funds', () => {
    // The clamp applies on top of sizing, not only to the mode label. A user sized
    // off live funds but executed in paper would record a position nothing backs.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      platform: { effectiveMode: 'paper', certified: false }
    })));
    expect(outcome.basis).toBe('paper-bankroll');
    expect(outcome.basisUnits).toBe(100);
  });

  it('does not call a user-chosen paper mode a downgrade', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ userRequestedMode: 'paper' })));
    expect(outcome.mode.effective).toBe('paper');
    expect(outcome.mode.downgraded).toBe(false);
    expect(outcome.mode.clamp).toBe('user-requested-paper');
  });

  it('refuses with platform-chain-mode-off when the global kill switch is set', () => {
    const outcome = refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      platform: { effectiveMode: 'off', certified: true, reason: 'Global kill switch active (*)' }
    })));
    expect(outcome.code).toBe('platform-chain-mode-off');
    expect(outcome.reason).toBe('Global kill switch active (*)');
  });

  it('distinguishes the user\'s own off from the platform\'s', () => {
    // Same outcome, different cause, different fix. One code for both sends an
    // operator to check a platform gate that is fine.
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ userRequestedMode: 'off' }))).code)
      .toBe('user-chain-mode-off');
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      settings: { maxPositionPct: 10, maxDailyExposurePct: 25, killed: true }
    }))).code).toBe('user-killed');
  });

  it('applies the kill switch ahead of a live platform verdict', () => {
    const decision = resolvePerUserMode({
      userRequested: 'live',
      platform: { effectiveMode: 'live', certified: true },
      killed: true
    });
    expect(decision.userRequested).toBe('off');
    expect(decision.effective).toBe('off');
  });
});

describe('S4-15 sizing â€” the user\'s own balance and their own percentages', () => {
  it('sizes as a percentage of that user\'s balance', () => {
    // 10 units at 10% is 1.0. Nothing else binds at this fixture.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput()));
    expect(outcome.requestedUnits).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);
    expect(outcome.basis).toBe('live-balance');
    expect(outcome.clamps).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('scales with the user\'s balance, holding the percentage fixed', () => {
    // Two users, same agreed percentage, different deposits: exposure is
    // proportional to what each deposited.
    const small = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ balance: { liveUnits: 2, paperUnits: 100 } })));
    const large = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ balance: { liveUnits: 20, paperUnits: 100 } })));
    expect(small.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.2, 9);
    expect(large.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(2, 9);
  });

  it('scales with the user\'s agreed percentage, holding the balance fixed', () => {
    const cautious = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      settings: { maxPositionPct: 1, maxDailyExposurePct: 25, killed: false }
    })));
    const bold = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      settings: { maxPositionPct: 20, maxDailyExposurePct: 25, killed: false }
    })));
    expect(cautious.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.1, 9);
    expect(bold.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(2, 9);
  });

  it('reuses the existing sizing formula rather than a second one', () => {
    // Pins the reuse required by `S4-15`. If this module ever grows its own
    // arithmetic, this diverges â€” which is the point: two formulas that agree today
    // will not agree after the next edit to one of them.
    const input = baseInput();
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(input));
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(calculateBalanceAwareSize({
      balance: 10,
      base: input.baseUnits,
      maximum: input.platformMaximumUnits,
      riskPct: input.settings.maxPositionPct,
      tierMultiplier: input.tierMultiplier,
      scoreMultiplier: input.scoreMultiplier,
      precision: input.precision,
      dynamic: true
    }));
  });

  it('the explanatory clamp walk lands on exactly the returned size', () => {
    // The clamps list is derived, not authoritative â€” `capPositionToAvailableBalance`
    // decides the number. A drift between them would make the explanation lie about a
    // size that is nonetheless correct, which is the worst of both.
    //
    // Stated against `boundedUnits` rather than `sizeUnits` because
    // `floorToPrecision` divides after flooring and can land one ulp *above* its
    // input: at precision 6, 0.06999999999999999 comes back as 0.07. Comparing the
    // walk to `sizeUnits` by float identity therefore fails on a correct result,
    // which is how this was found.
    for (const platformMaximumUnits of [0.03, 0.4, 5, 500]) {
      for (const liveUnits of [0.0000004, 0.7, 10, 4000]) {
        const outcome = sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
          platformMaximumUnits,
          balance: { liveUnits, paperUnits: 100 }
        }));
        if (outcome.kind !== 'size') continue;
        expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(floorToPrecision(outcome.boundedUnits, 6));
        const lastBound = [...outcome.clamps]
          .reverse()
          .find((clamp) => clamp.code !== 'precision-floor'
            && clamp.code !== 'master-conviction-fraction');
        expect(lastBound ? lastBound.afterUnits : outcome.requestedUnits)
          .toBe(outcome.boundedUnits);
      }
    }
  });

  it('applies the tier and score multipliers', () => {
    const half = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ tierMultiplier: 0.5 })));
    expect(half.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.5, 9);
    const quarter = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      tierMultiplier: 0.5,
      scoreMultiplier: 0.5
    })));
    expect(quarter.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.25, 9);
  });

  it('ignores the percentage under static sizing, as the existing helper does', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dynamic: false })));
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.5, 9);
    expect(outcome.clamps).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('unknown is never a number', () => {
  it('refuses an unknown live balance rather than sizing it to zero', () => {
    // The mutation guard. Coalescing `null` to 0 makes this return
    // `size-rounds-to-zero`, which sends an operator to look at funding instead of
    // at the balance poller.
    const outcome = refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      balance: { liveUnits: null, paperUnits: 100 }
    })));
    expect(outcome.code).toBe('balance-unknown');
    expect(outcome.reason).toMatch(/unknown balance/);
  });

  it('refuses an unknown paper bankroll for a downgraded user', () => {
    // The basis follows the clamped mode, so the unknown that matters is the paper
    // one even though the user asked for live and has live funds.
    const outcome = refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      platform: { effectiveMode: 'paper', certified: false },
      balance: { liveUnits: 10, paperUnits: null }
    })));
    expect(outcome.code).toBe('balance-unknown');
    expect(outcome.reason).toMatch(/paper-bankroll/);
  });

  it.each([Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, -1])(
    'treats %p as an unknown balance, not a number',
    (liveUnits) => {
      expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
        balance: { liveUnits, paperUnits: 100 }
      }))).code).toBe('balance-unknown');
    }
  );

  it('reports a genuine zero balance as a zero, not as unknown', () => {
    // The rule holds in both directions. A zero balance is a fact about funding; an
    // unknown one is a fact about our data.
    const outcome = refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      balance: { liveUnits: 0, paperUnits: 100 }
    })));
    expect(outcome.code).toBe('size-rounds-to-zero');
  });

  it('does not report a zero balance as an exhausted daily allowance', () => {
    // A zero balance yields a zero allowance. Calling that `daily-exposure-cap-reached`
    // would tell an operator the user spent an allowance they never had.
    const outcome = refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      balance: { liveUnits: 0, paperUnits: 100 },
      dailyExposureUsdUsed: 0
    })));
    expect(outcome.code).not.toBe('daily-exposure-cap-reached');
  });

  it('refuses an unknown USD rate rather than assuming one', () => {
    // `index.ts` substitutes `?? 150` for SOL and `?? 3000` for ETH when a price
    // fetch fails. A fabricated rate silently mis-scales the exposure cap.
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ usdPerUnit: null }))).code)
      .toBe('usd-rate-unknown');
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ usdPerUnit: 0 }))).code)
      .toBe('usd-rate-unknown');
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ usdPerUnit: Number.NaN }))).code)
      .toBe('usd-rate-unknown');
  });

  it('refuses an unknown committed exposure rather than treating it as nothing spent', () => {
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: null }))).code)
      .toBe('daily-exposure-unknown');
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: Number.NaN }))).code)
      .toBe('daily-exposure-unknown');
  });

  it('propagates an unknown balance out of the exposure cap helper', () => {
    expect(userDailyExposureCapUsd({ maxDailyExposurePct: 25 }, null)).toBeNull();
    expect(userDailyExposureCapUsd({ maxDailyExposurePct: 25 }, Number.NaN)).toBeNull();
    expect(userDailyExposureCapUsd({ maxDailyExposurePct: 25 }, 1_000)).toBe(250);
  });
});

describe('S4-16 per-user exposure cap', () => {
  it('derives the cap from this user\'s own percentage and balance', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput()));
    // 10 units at $100 is $1,000; 25% of that is $250.
    expect(outcome.dailyExposureCapUsd).toBe(250);
    expect(outcome.dailyExposureRemainingUsd).toBe(250);
  });

  it('charges only this user\'s own committed exposure against it', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: 200 })));
    expect(outcome.dailyExposureRemainingUsd).toBe(50);
    // $50 of headroom at $100/unit is 0.5 units, which now binds below the 1.0 request.
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.5, 9);
    expect(outcome.clamps).toEqual([
      { code: 'daily-exposure-remaining', beforeUnits: 1, afterUnits: 0.5 }
    ]);
  });

  it('refuses once the user has spent their own allowance', () => {
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: 250 }))).code)
      .toBe('daily-exposure-cap-reached');
    expect(refused(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: 400 }))).code)
      .toBe('daily-exposure-cap-reached');
  });

  it('gives two users with different balances different allowances', () => {
    // The property the process-wide `DAILY_EXPOSURE_CAP_USD` cannot express: one
    // funded user must not consume every other user's headroom.
    const poor = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ balance: { liveUnits: 1, paperUnits: 100 } })));
    const rich = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ balance: { liveUnits: 50, paperUnits: 100 } })));
    expect(poor.dailyExposureCapUsd).toBe(25);
    expect(rich.dailyExposureCapUsd).toBe(1_250);
  });

  it('rejects an incoherent exposure percentage instead of sizing with it', () => {
    expect(() => userDailyExposureCapUsd({ maxDailyExposurePct: 0 }, 1_000)).toThrow(/percentage/);
    expect(() => userDailyExposureCapUsd({ maxDailyExposurePct: 101 }, 1_000)).toThrow(/percentage/);
  });
});

describe('clamps are visible, not silent', () => {
  it('names the platform per-order ceiling when it binds', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ platformMaximumUnits: 0.25 })));
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(0.25);
    expect(outcome.clamps).toEqual([
      { code: 'platform-maximum-notional', beforeUnits: 1, afterUnits: 0.25 }
    ]);
  });

  it('names the balance when the request exceeds it', () => {
    // Only reachable with a multiplier above 1 or a percentage of 100; the point is
    // that the bound is reported rather than absorbed.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      settings: { maxPositionPct: 100, maxDailyExposurePct: 100, killed: false },
      scoreMultiplier: 2,
      platformMaximumUnits: 50
    })));
    expect(outcome.clamps[0]).toEqual({
      code: 'available-balance',
      beforeUnits: 20,
      afterUnits: 10
    });
  });

  it('names precision flooring when it removes a remainder', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      balance: { liveUnits: 1.23456789, paperUnits: 100 },
      precision: 2
    })));
    const floorClamp = outcome.clamps.find((clamp) => clamp.code === 'precision-floor');
    expect(floorClamp).toBeDefined();
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(0.12);
  });

  it('lists every clamp in the order applied when several bind', () => {
    // The answer to "why did I get 0.05 and not 0.2" is this list, read top to
    // bottom.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      settings: { maxPositionPct: 100, maxDailyExposurePct: 100, killed: false },
      scoreMultiplier: 2,
      platformMaximumUnits: 4,
      dailyExposureUsdUsed: 800,
      precision: 1
    })));
    expect(outcome.clamps.map((clamp) => clamp.code)).toEqual([
      'available-balance',
      'platform-maximum-notional',
      'daily-exposure-remaining'
    ]);
    // $1,000 cap less $800 spent is $200, i.e. 2 units at $100.
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(2);
  });

  it('reports no clamps when nothing reduced the size', () => {
    expect(sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput())).clamps).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('ADR-0005 Â§3.1 conviction sizing', () => {
  it('transmits the master\'s conviction when it is below the user\'s ceiling', () => {
    // A 2% punt and a 40% core position must not allocate identically.
    const punt = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      conviction: {
        masterFraction: 0.02,
        portfolioCoverage: 0.9,
        coverageThreshold: 0.8,
        scale: 1
      }
    })));
    const core = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      conviction: {
        masterFraction: 0.4,
        portfolioCoverage: 0.9,
        coverageThreshold: 0.8,
        scale: 1
      }
    })));
    expect(punt.appliedRiskPct).toBe(2);
    expect(punt.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.2, 9);
    // The user's own 10% ceiling still binds above their conviction.
    expect(core.appliedRiskPct).toBe(10);
    expect(core.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);
    expect(punt.sizeUnits).toBeLessThan(core.sizeUnits);
  });

  it('keeps the user\'s ceiling binding above the master\'s fraction', () => {
    const resolution = resolveConvictionRiskPct(10, {
      masterFraction: 0.9,
      portfolioCoverage: 1,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 1
    });
    expect(resolution.riskPct).toBe(10);
    expect(resolution.convictionPct).toBe(90);
    expect(resolution.sizedWithoutConviction).toBe(false);
  });

  it('names the conviction clamp when it is the binding term', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      conviction: {
        masterFraction: 0.02,
        portfolioCoverage: 0.9,
        coverageThreshold: 0.8,
        scale: 1
      }
    })));
    expect(outcome.clamps[0]?.code).toBe('master-conviction-fraction');
    expect(outcome.clamps[0]?.beforeUnits).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);
    expect(outcome.clamps[0]?.afterUnits).toBeCloseTo(0.2, 9);
  });

  it('falls back to flat sizing and marks the trade when coverage is short', () => {
    // Presenting a fraction of a portfolio we cannot see would be a fabricated input
    // to a real position size.
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({
      conviction: {
        masterFraction: 0.02,
        portfolioCoverage: 0.3,
        coverageThreshold: 0.8,
        scale: 1
      }
    })));
    expect(outcome.sizedWithoutConviction).toBe(true);
    expect(outcome.conviction.fallbackReason).toBe('portfolio-coverage-below-threshold');
    expect(outcome.appliedRiskPct).toBe(10);
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBeCloseTo(1, 9);
  });

  it.each([
    ['master-fraction-unknown', { masterFraction: null, portfolioCoverage: 0.9 }],
    ['portfolio-coverage-unknown', { masterFraction: 0.02, portfolioCoverage: null }]
  ] as const)('falls back with %s', (reason, partial) => {
    const resolution = resolveConvictionRiskPct(10, {
      ...partial,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 1
    });
    expect(resolution.sizedWithoutConviction).toBe(true);
    expect(resolution.fallbackReason).toBe(reason);
    expect(resolution.riskPct).toBe(10);
  });

  it('falls back on a NaN coverage rather than multiplying it through', () => {
    // A NaN that reached the multiplication would make riskPct NaN and
    // `requestedBalanceAwareSize` would throw, where a fallback is the right answer.
    const resolution = resolveConvictionRiskPct(10, {
      masterFraction: 0.02,
      portfolioCoverage: Number.NaN,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 1
    });
    expect(resolution.sizedWithoutConviction).toBe(true);
    expect(resolution.fallbackReason).toBe('portfolio-coverage-unknown');
  });

  it('marks a trade sized without conviction when no conviction was supplied', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ conviction: null })));
    expect(outcome.sizedWithoutConviction).toBe(true);
    expect(outcome.conviction.fallbackReason).toBe('master-fraction-unknown');
  });

  it('applies ADR-0005\'s scale to the master fraction', () => {
    expect(resolveConvictionRiskPct(50, {
      masterFraction: 0.1,
      portfolioCoverage: 1,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 2
    }).riskPct).toBe(20);
  });

  it('caps the conviction percentage at 100 so sizing cannot be handed 200', () => {
    expect(resolveConvictionRiskPct(100, {
      masterFraction: 1,
      portfolioCoverage: 1,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 5
    }).convictionPct).toBe(100);
  });

  it('rejects an out-of-range fraction as unknown rather than clamping it', () => {
    // A fraction above 1 is not a portfolio share; guessing which number was meant
    // would size a real position on a misread input.
    expect(resolveConvictionRiskPct(10, {
      masterFraction: 1.5,
      portfolioCoverage: 1,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: 1
    }).fallbackReason).toBe('master-fraction-unknown');
  });

  it('rejects an incoherent user percentage loudly', () => {
    expect(() => resolveConvictionRiskPct(0, null)).toThrow(/percentage/);
    expect(() => resolveConvictionRiskPct(101, null)).toThrow(/percentage/);
    expect(() => resolveConvictionRiskPct(Number.NaN, null)).toThrow(/percentage/);
  });

  it('rejects a negative scale rather than sizing to zero', () => {
    expect(() => resolveConvictionRiskPct(10, {
      masterFraction: 0.1,
      portfolioCoverage: 1,
      coverageThreshold: 0.8,
      scale: -1
    })).toThrow(/scale/);
  });
});

describe('the cap helper this module reuses', () => {
  it('agrees with capPositionToAvailableBalance on the final number', () => {
    const outcome = sized(sizePerUserBuy(baseInput({ dailyExposureUsdUsed: 200 })));
    expect(outcome.sizeUnits).toBe(capPositionToAvailableBalance({
      requested: outcome.requestedUnits,
      available: outcome.basisUnits,
      // $50 of headroom at $100/unit.
      maximum: Math.min(5, 0.5),
      precision: 6
    }));
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/per-user-sizing.ts <==
import type { Chain, ExecutionMode } from '@swat/shared';
import type {
  ChainModeResolution,
  UserChainMode,
  UserExecutionSettings
} from '@swat/db';
import { RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT } from './reconciliation-coordinator.js';
import {
  capPositionToAvailableBalance,
  requestedBalanceAwareSize
} from './policy.js';

/**
 * Per-user sizing, per-user risk keys, and the platform clamp that sits above both
 * (`S4-15`, `S4-16`, `S4-17`).
 *
 * **Pure by construction.** No database, no clock it was not given, no environment
 * read, no network. Same reason as `fanout-eligibility.ts`, `position-cap.ts` and
 * `stop-loss.ts`: there is no database available while this is being built, and
 * this logic decides how much of a user's money moves. Every number it needs
 * arrives as an argument, which is also why the whole thing is exercised by unit
 * tests with no infrastructure.
 *
 * **One sizing formula, not two.** The arithmetic is
 * `requestedBalanceAwareSize` + `capPositionToAvailableBalance` from `policy.ts`,
 * which is what `index.ts` already sizes with. Nothing here re-derives a position
 * size; this module chooses *whose* balance and *whose* percentages go in, and
 * reports what reduced the answer.
 *
 * ## Three distinctions this module exists to keep apart
 *
 *   1. **A platform gate downgrades; it never excludes.** `S4-13` already encodes
 *      this and `narrowExecutionMode` must not contradict it. A lapsed
 *      certification turns a live user into a paper user â€” it does not stop them
 *      copying. The reverse error is worse: re-widening a clamped `paper` back to
 *      `live` because the user's stored preference says `live` opens a real
 *      position on an uncertified chain. The narrowing is one-directional and
 *      tested in both directions.
 *   2. **Unknown is not zero.** An unknown balance produces a refusal with its own
 *      code, never a size of `0`. `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` returns `null` rather
 *      than a partial sum for exactly this reason; a `0` here would be
 *      indistinguishable from a genuinely empty account and would report the wrong
 *      cause. The rule holds in the other direction too: a real zero balance sizes
 *      to zero and refuses with `size-rounds-to-zero`, which is a different code.
 *   3. **A clamp is an output, not a side effect.** Every reduction is listed in
 *      `clamps` with the value before and after it. An operator asking "why did I
 *      get 0.05 and not 0.2" reads the list; a silent `Math.min` gives them
 *      nothing to read.
 *
 * ## What this module deliberately does NOT do
 *
 *   * **Sell sizing.** A copied sell is proportional to the position the user
 *     actually holds, which `sourceSellFractionToBps` (`canonical-copy.ts`) already
 *     computes correctly. A second sell path here would be a way to sell more than
 *     is held.
 *   * **Venue minimum order size.** The binding minimum is per market and is read
 *     from the order book at submission (`polymarket-mirror-bound.ts`). The
 *     configuration-time figure in `position-cap.ts` is explicitly approximate, and
 *     refusing a trade on an approximation would skip orders the venue would have
 *     accepted.
 */

/**
 * Whose risk policy, breaker and exposure ledger a sizing decision reads.
 *
 * `'operator'` is the pre-tenancy account: `050_copy_tenancy.sql` leaves legacy
 * rows at `user_id NULL` and backfills nothing, so the operator path keeps its own
 * key rather than being retro-assigned to a tenant.
 *
 * **This constant is a tenancy key and it becomes the user id.** It is deliberately
 * separate from `RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT`, which is the same string today and must
 * NOT follow it â€” see `reconciliationAccountForUser`. Collapsing the two is how
 * that distinction gets lost, and `per-user-sizing.test.ts` guards it in both
 * directions.
 */
export const RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT = 'operator';

/**
 * The account key for `resolveRiskPolicy`, `readCircuitBreakerState`,
 * `recordCircuitBreakerFailure` / `Success`, `claimCircuitBreakerProbe` and the
 * per-user exposure ledger.
 *
 * This is the whole of `S4-16`'s "substitute the user key for `'operator'`": those
 * functions already take `account: string` (Standing Rule 2), so per-user risk is a
 * value substitution rather than a signature rewrite. Passing a user id gives that
 * user their own `breaker:${userId}:${chain}` state and their own cached policy â€”
 * one user tripping a breaker no longer halts every other user on the chain.
 *
 * `null` means the pre-tenancy operator path, which keeps `RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT`.
 */
export function riskPolicyAccountForUser(userId: string | null): string {
  if (userId === null) return RISK_POLICY_ACCOUNT;
  if (typeof userId !== 'string' || userId.trim().length === 0) {
    throw new Error('riskPolicyAccountForUser requires a non-empty user id or null');
  }
  return userId;
}

/** Alias with the breaker's vocabulary. Same key, so the two cannot drift apart. */
export function circuitBreakerAccountForUser(userId: string | null): string {
  return riskPolicyAccountForUser(userId);
}

/**
 * The reconciliation account. **Ignores `userId` on purpose.**
 *
 * One of the two verified exceptions in the checklist's Â§1. `RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT`
 * is an *escalation label*, not a tenancy key: `copy_executions.target_account`
 * holds a chain-prefixed **wallet address** (`resolveLiveCopyTargetAccount` /
 * `resolvePaperCopyTargetAccount`), so filtering that column by an account value
 * claims zero rows. Substituting a user id here would fragment one alert stream
 * into N while scoping nothing, and the rows it was meant to sweep would sit at
 * `reconciliation_required` forever with nobody looking at them.
 *
 * It takes the parameter it discards so a fan-out call site that has a user id in
 * hand still lands on the right answer instead of reaching for
 * `riskPolicyAccountForUser`. That is the whole point of the two functions being
 * separate: a find-and-replace over the string `'operator'` cannot make them agree.
 */
export function reconciliationAccountForUser(_userId: string | null): string {
  return RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT;
}

/**
 * A definite refusal. Nothing was sized, and the reason is specific.
 *
 * Split from the clamp codes below for the same reason `solana-simulation.ts`
 * splits `refuse` from `unavailable`: a refusal and a reduction are different
 * events, and folding them together means an operator cannot tell "we did not
 * trade" from "we traded smaller".
 */
export type PerUserSizingRefusalCode =
  /** The user's own kill switch is set. No chain executes (`S6-8`). */
  | 'user-killed'
  /** The user has not opted this chain in, or set it to `off`. */
  | 'user-chain-mode-off'
  /**
   * The platform resolved this chain to `off` â€” a global kill switch (`'*' = 'off'`)
   * or an operator-set chain mode. Distinct from `user-chain-mode-off`: one is the
   * user's choice, the other is ours, and an operator debugging a silent chain
   * needs to know which.
   */
  | 'platform-chain-mode-off'
  /**
   * The balance for the resolved mode could not be established. Fails closed.
   *
   * **Never reported as a size of zero.** An unknown balance is not an empty one:
   * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` returns `null` rather than a partial sum, and coalescing
   * that to `0` here would size against a number nobody computed and then report
   * `size-rounds-to-zero`, sending the operator to look at funding instead of at the
   * balance poller.
   */
  | 'balance-unknown'
  /** How much USD this user has already committed today is unknown. Fails closed. */
  | 'daily-exposure-unknown'
  /** The user has spent their own agreed daily exposure allowance. */
  | 'daily-exposure-cap-reached'
  /**
   * The sizing unit is not USD and no rate to USD was supplied, so the
   * USD-denominated exposure cap cannot be applied. Fails closed.
   *
   * A separate code from `daily-exposure-unknown` because the fix differs: this is a
   * missing price, that is a missing ledger read.
   */
  | 'usd-rate-unknown'
  /**
   * Everything was known and the answer is genuinely zero â€” an empty balance, a
   * percentage too small for the venue's precision, or no headroom left after the
   * clamps. The honest counterpart to `balance-unknown`.
   */
  | 'size-rounds-to-zero';

/** Why the size that came out is smaller than the one that went in. */
export type PerUserSizingClampCode =
  /**
   * The master's conviction was the binding term, not the user's ceiling
   * (ADR-0005 Â§3.1: `min(max_position_pct, master_fraction Ã— scale)`). A reduction
   * worth naming â€” it is the mechanism transmitting conviction, and without it
   * a 2% speculative punt and a 40% core position allocate identically.
   */
  | 'master-conviction-fraction'
  /** Clamped to the balance the user actually has. */
  | 'available-balance'
  /** Clamped to the platform's absolute per-order ceiling for this chain. */
  | 'platform-maximum-notional'
  /** Clamped to what is left of the user's own daily exposure allowance. */
  | 'daily-exposure-remaining'
  /** Flooring to the venue's precision removed the remainder. */
  | 'precision-floor';

/** Why the execution mode that came out is narrower than the one requested. */
export type PerUserModeClampCode =
  /**
   * `S4-17`. The user asked for live and the platform gates
   * (`LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` + an active `chain_certifications` row) reduced it to
   * paper. The user stays **eligible** â€” this is a downgrade, never an exclusion.
   */
  | 'platform-clamped-live-to-paper'
  /** The user themselves asked for paper while the platform permitted live. */
  | 'user-requested-paper';

export interface PerUserSizingClamp {
  readonly code: PerUserSizingClampCode;
  /** Sizing units before this clamp. */
  readonly beforeUnits: number;
  /** Sizing units after it. */
  readonly afterUnits: number;
}

export interface PerUserModeDecision {
  /** What the user's stored per-chain setting asks for, after their kill switch. */
  readonly userRequested: UserChainMode;
  /**
   * The platform's already-clamped verdict â€” `planFanout`'s `executionMode`, or
   * `resolveChainMode`'s `effectiveMode`. Carried unchanged so the output shows what
   * this layer was handed, not only what it did with it.
   */
  readonly platformEffective: ExecutionMode;
  /** The narrower of the two. Never wider than `platformEffective`. */
  readonly effective: ExecutionMode;
  /** True only when the **platform** reduced a live request. Mirrors `FanoutVerdict.downgraded`. */
  readonly downgraded: boolean;
  readonly clamp: PerUserModeClampCode | null;
  /**
   * `ChainModeResolution.reason`, verbatim, when one was supplied â€” e.g. "Chain
   * solana has no active reviewed certification record".
   *
   * The clamp code says *that* the platform reduced the mode; this says *why*, in
   * the platform's own words, so an operator is not left guessing which of the two
   * gates lapsed.
   */
  readonly platformReason: string | null;
  /** `chain_certifications` + `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` both satisfied, when supplied. */
  readonly certified: boolean | null;
}

/**
 * The platform's verdict for this chain.
 *
 * Shaped to accept a whole `ChainModeResolution` **and** the
 * `{ effectiveMode }` object `planFanout` consumes, so the same value can be
 * threaded from either without being rebuilt â€” a rebuild is where a `requestedMode`
 * gets substituted for an `effectiveMode` by accident.
 */
export type PlatformChainVerdict =
  Pick<ChainModeResolution, 'effectiveMode'>
  & Partial<Pick<ChainModeResolution, 'certified' | 'reason'>>;

const MODE_RANK: Readonly<Record<ExecutionMode, number>> = Object.freeze({
  off: 0,
  paper: 1,
  live: 2,
  'live+shadow': 2
});

/**
 * The platform verdict narrowed by the user's request. **Never widened.**
 *
 * This is `S4-17` in one expression, and the direction is the whole point:
 *
 *   * Either side saying `off` wins. A platform `off` is a kill switch; a user
 *     `off` is consent not given.
 *   * A platform verdict of `paper` stays `paper` however the user's row reads.
 *     This is the case a re-widening bug lives in â€” the user's stored preference is
 *     `live`, so a naive `userMode` return opens a real position on a chain whose
 *     certification lapsed.
 *   * A user asking for `paper` under a live-capable platform gets `paper`. Users
 *     may narrow their own exposure; that is not a downgrade.
 *   * `live+shadow` survives a `live` request unchanged. It is an operator
 *     diagnostic that executes live and records a parallel shadow fill, and
 *     collapsing it to `live` would silently switch the diagnostic off â€” narrowing
 *     is about *permission*, and both are equally live.
 */
export function narrowExecutionMode(
  platformEffective: ExecutionMode,
  userRequested: UserChainMode
): ExecutionMode {
  if (userRequested === 'off' || platformEffective === 'off') return 'off';
  const userRank = MODE_RANK[userRequested];
  const platformRank = MODE_RANK[platformEffective];
  // The user can only ever narrow. When their rank is lower the request binds;
  // otherwise the platform's verdict is returned untouched, which is what stops a
  // stored `live` preference from re-widening a clamped `paper`.
  return userRank < platformRank ? userRequested : platformEffective;
}

/**
 * Resolves the mode and records what narrowed it.
 *
 * Exported separately from `sizePerUserBuy` because the `S4-14` job builder needs
 * the same decision without sizing anything, and two derivations of "is this user
 * live right now" is exactly the divergence `S4-17` is about.
 */
export function resolvePerUserMode(input: {
  readonly userRequested: UserChainMode;
  readonly platform: PlatformChainVerdict;
  /** The per-user kill switch. Applied here so no call site has to remember it. */
  readonly killed: boolean;
}): PerUserModeDecision {
  const userRequested: UserChainMode = input.killed ? 'off' : input.userRequested;
  const platformEffective = input.platform.effectiveMode;
  const effective = narrowExecutionMode(platformEffective, userRequested);

  const wantedLive = userRequested === 'live';
  const platformIsPaper = platformEffective === 'paper';
  const downgraded = wantedLive && platformIsPaper;

  let clamp: PerUserModeClampCode | null = null;
  if (downgraded) clamp = 'platform-clamped-live-to-paper';
  else if (userRequested === 'paper' && MODE_RANK[platformEffective] > MODE_RANK.paper) {
    clamp = 'user-requested-paper';
  }

  return {
    userRequested,
    platformEffective,
    effective,
    downgraded,
    clamp,
    platformReason: input.platform.reason ?? null,
    certified: input.platform.certified ?? null
  };
}

/**
 * How the master's own allocation is transmitted, and whether it could be.
 *
 * ADR-0005 Â§3.1: buy sizing is `min(max_position_pct, master_fraction Ã— scale)`.
 * `master_fraction` is computed over **the assets we index**, so below a coverage
 * threshold it is a fraction of a portfolio we cannot see. In that case sizing falls
 * back to flat `max_position_pct` and the trade is marked
 * **sized-without-conviction** rather than presenting the fabricated fraction.
 */
export interface MasterConvictionInput {
  /**
   * The share of the master's indexed portfolio this buy represents, in `[0, 1]`.
   * `null` is unknown and triggers the flat fallback â€” it is never read as 0, which
   * would size every trade to nothing.
   */
  readonly masterFraction: number | null;
  /**
   * Share of the master's portfolio value our index covers, in `[0, 1]`. `null` is
   * unknown, which is the same fallback: an uncovered portfolio and an unmeasured
   * one are equally unusable as a conviction signal.
   */
  readonly portfolioCoverage: number | null;
  /** Coverage at or above which `masterFraction` is trusted. */
  readonly coverageThreshold: number;
  /** ADR-0005's `scale`, default 1.0. Multiplies the master's fraction. */
  readonly scale: number;
}

/** Why conviction sizing did not apply. `null` when it did. */
export type ConvictionFallbackReason =
  /** No fraction was supplied for this buy. */
  | 'master-fraction-unknown'
  /** Coverage was not supplied, so the fraction cannot be trusted. */
  | 'portfolio-coverage-unknown'
  /** Coverage is below the threshold: the fraction is over a portfolio we cannot see. */
  | 'portfolio-coverage-below-threshold';

export interface ConvictionResolution {
  /** The percentage of balance to size with, before any cap. */
  readonly riskPct: number;
  /** The user's own ceiling, for comparison. */
  readonly userMaxPositionPct: number;
  /** True when the flat fallback applied â€” ADR-0005's "sized-without-conviction" mark. */
  readonly sizedWithoutConviction: boolean;
  readonly fallbackReason: ConvictionFallbackReason | null;
  /** The conviction percentage, when one was computable. */
  readonly convictionPct: number | null;
}

function isFraction(value: number | null): value is number {
  return value !== null && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 1;
}

/**
 * `min(max_position_pct, master_fraction Ã— scale)`, or the flat fallback.
 *
 * Written as `!(coverage >= threshold)` in effect â€” via `isFraction` plus an
 * explicit comparison â€” so a `NaN` coverage falls back rather than passing through.
 * A `NaN` that reached the multiplication would make `riskPct` `NaN`, and
 * `requestedBalanceAwareSize` would then throw where a fallback was the correct
 * answer.
 */
export function resolveConvictionRiskPct(
  userMaxPositionPct: number,
  conviction: MasterConvictionInput | null
): ConvictionResolution {
  if (
    !Number.isFinite(userMaxPositionPct)
    || userMaxPositionPct <= 0
    || userMaxPositionPct > 100
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      `maxPositionPct must be a percentage in (0, 100], got ${userMaxPositionPct}`
    );
  }

  const flat = (reason: ConvictionFallbackReason): ConvictionResolution => ({
    riskPct: userMaxPositionPct,
    userMaxPositionPct,
    sizedWithoutConviction: true,
    fallbackReason: reason,
    convictionPct: null
  });

  if (conviction === null || !isFraction(conviction.masterFraction)) {
    return flat('master-fraction-unknown');
  }
  if (!isFraction(conviction.portfolioCoverage)) return flat('portfolio-coverage-unknown');
  if (!Number.isFinite(conviction.coverageThreshold)) {
    throw new Error('conviction coverageThreshold must be a finite number');
  }
  if (!(conviction.portfolioCoverage >= conviction.coverageThreshold)) {
    return flat('portfolio-coverage-below-threshold');
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(conviction.scale) || conviction.scale < 0) {
    throw new Error(`conviction scale must be a non-negative finite number, got ${conviction.scale}`);
  }

  // Capped at 100 before the min, so a scale above 1 on a concentrated master
  // cannot produce a percentage `requestedBalanceAwareSize` refuses outright.
  const convictionPct = Math.min(100, conviction.masterFraction * conviction.scale * 100);
  return {
    riskPct: Math.min(userMaxPositionPct, convictionPct),
    userMaxPositionPct,
    sizedWithoutConviction: false,
    fallbackReason: null,
    convictionPct
  };
}

/**
 * One user's daily exposure allowance, in USD.
 *
 * Derived from the user's own `max_daily_exposure_pct` against their own balance â€”
 * not from the process-wide `DAILY_EXPOSURE_CAP_USD`, which is one number for the
 * whole platform and would let a single funded user consume every other user's
 * headroom.
 *
 * `null` when the balance is unknown, propagating the unknown rather than reporting
 * a cap of 0 (which reads as "allowance exhausted" and is a different fact).
 */
export function userDailyExposureCapUsd(
  settings: Pick<UserExecutionSettings, 'maxDailyExposurePct'>,
  knownBalanceUsd: number | null
): number | null {
  if (knownBalanceUsd === null || !Number.isFinite(knownBalanceUsd) || knownBalanceUsd < 0) {
    return null;
  }
  const pct = settings.maxDailyExposurePct;
  if (!Number.isFinite(pct) || pct <= 0 || pct > 100) {
    throw new Error(`maxDailyExposurePct must be a percentage in (0, 100], got ${pct}`);
  }
  return knownBalanceUsd * (pct / 100);
}

/**
 * The balance available to size against, per mode.
 *
 * Two fields rather than one because the platform clamp changes which applies: a
 * user who asked for live on an uncertified chain is sized off the **paper**
 * bankroll, since that is the mode they will actually execute in. Passing one
 * pre-selected balance would mean the caller picking the basis from the *unclamped*
 * mode, which is the same re-widening bug wearing a different hat.
 *
 * Both are in **sizing units** â€” the unit the venue's order is denominated in (SOL
 * on Solana, USDC on Polymarket, ETH on Robinhood Chain), matching what
 * `index.ts` already passes to `calculateBalanceAwareSize`. `null` is unknown.
 */
export interface PerUserBalanceInput {
  /** Spendable balance for a live order, net of any gas reserve. `null` = unknown. */
  readonly liveUnits: number | null;
  /**
   * Notional paper bankroll, in sizing units. `null` = unknown.
   *
   * Supplied per call rather than read from `PAPER_BANKROLL_USD` because a per-user
   * paper bankroll is the point of `S4-16` â€” but note that **no per-user bankroll
   * column exists** (`049` has none), so today every caller will pass the same
   * platform figure. Parameterising it now means the day a column lands, nothing in
   * this module changes.
   */
  readonly paperUnits: number | null;
}

export interface PerUserSizingInput {
  /** `null` is the pre-tenancy operator path; see `riskPolicyAccountForUser`. */
  readonly userId: string | null;
  readonly chain: Chain;
  /**
   * The user's own limits, straight from `getUserExecutionSettings`.
   *
   * Already clamped on write, so a stored value is inside the platform ceiling
   * before it gets here â€” this module does not re-clamp the percentages, it applies
   * them.
   */
  readonly settings: Pick<
    UserExecutionSettings,
    'maxPositionPct' | 'maxDailyExposurePct' | 'killed'
  >;
  /** The user's stored mode for this chain, from `requestedUserChainMode`. */
  readonly userRequestedMode: UserChainMode;
  /** The platform's already-clamped verdict. Never widened here. */
  readonly platform: PlatformChainVerdict;
  readonly balance: PerUserBalanceInput;
  /**
   * USD value of one sizing unit. `1` for a USD-denominated venue.
   *
   * `null` is unknown and refuses with `usd-rate-unknown` rather than defaulting.
   * `index.ts` currently substitutes `?? 150` for SOL and `?? 3000` for ETH when a
   * price fetch fails; a fabricated rate silently mis-scales the exposure cap, and
   * this module will not do that.
   */
  readonly usdPerUnit: number | null;
  /**
   * USD this user has already committed in the rolling window. `null` = unknown,
   * which fails closed.
   *
   * Must be **this user's** figure. `getRollingExposureUsd(chain)` as it stands sums
   * every trade on the chain, so passing it here would charge one user's spending
   * against every other user's allowance.
   */
  readonly dailyExposureUsdUsed: number | null;
  /** `null` skips conviction sizing and marks the trade sized-without-conviction. */
  readonly conviction: MasterConvictionInput | null;
  /** Cluster/tier multiplier, as `index.ts` computes it. */
  readonly tierMultiplier: number;
  /** Signal-score multiplier, as `index.ts` computes it. */
  readonly scoreMultiplier: number;
  /** Static base size in sizing units, used when `dynamic` is false. */
  readonly baseUnits: number;
  /** The platform's absolute per-order ceiling in sizing units, e.g. `MAX_POSITION_SOL`. */
  readonly platformMaximumUnits: number;
  readonly precision: number;
  /** `USE_DYNAMIC_BALANCE_SIZING`. When false the percentage does not apply. */
  readonly dynamic: boolean;
}

export type PerUserSizingOutcome =
  | {
    readonly kind: 'refuse';
    readonly code: PerUserSizingRefusalCode;
    /** Operator-readable, specific enough to act on without re-reading the inputs. */
    readonly reason: string;
    /** Present even on a refusal: a refusal caused by an `off` mode is explained by it. */
    readonly mode: PerUserModeDecision;
    /** The risk-policy / breaker account this user's decision was keyed on. */
    readonly riskAccount: string;
  }
  | {
    readonly kind: 'size';
    /** The number to trade, in sizing units, after every clamp. Always > 0. */
    readonly sizeUnits: number;
    /** What sizing asked for before any clamp, for comparison against `sizeUnits`. */
    readonly requestedUnits: number;
    /**
     * The size after every bound but before precision flooring.
     *
     * Carried so the clamp list is checkable against the returned size:
     * `sizeUnits === floorToPrecision(boundedUnits, precision)` holds exactly, and the
     * last bound clamp's `afterUnits` is this number. Without it the two can only be
     * compared approximately â€” `floorToPrecision` divides after flooring, so its
     * result can sit up to one ulp *above* its input (0.06999999999999999 at
     * precision 6 comes back as 0.07). That is a rounding artefact worth naming
     * rather than chasing: it is far below any venue's precision, but it means
     * `sizeUnits <= boundedUnits` is **not** guaranteed in the last bit.
     */
    readonly boundedUnits: number;
    /** Which balance the size was derived from, chosen by the **clamped** mode. */
    readonly basis: 'live-balance' | 'paper-bankroll';
    readonly basisUnits: number;
    /** The percentage actually applied, after the conviction rule. */
    readonly appliedRiskPct: number;
    readonly conviction: ConvictionResolution;
    /** ADR-0005 Â§3.1's mark. Convenience mirror of `conviction.sizedWithoutConviction`. */
    readonly sizedWithoutConviction: boolean;
    readonly mode: PerUserModeDecision;
    readonly riskAccount: string;
    /** Every reduction, in the order applied. Empty when nothing clamped. */
    readonly clamps: readonly PerUserSizingClamp[];
    readonly dailyExposureCapUsd: number;
    readonly dailyExposureRemainingUsd: number;
  };

function refuse(
  code: PerUserSizingRefusalCode,
  reason: string,
  mode: PerUserModeDecision,
  riskAccount: string
): PerUserSizingOutcome {
  return { kind: 'refuse', code, reason, mode, riskAccount };
}

function knownNonNegative(value: number | null): value is number {
  return value !== null && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0;
}

/**
 * A rate of exactly 0 is not a rate.
 *
 * It would make the USD exposure cap 0 and the headroom in units `Infinity` â€” a
 * cap that both refuses everything and permits everything depending on which term
 * you read. Treated as unknown, which fails closed.
 */
function knownPositive(value: number | null): value is number {
  return value !== null && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0;
}

/**
 * Sizes one user's copy of one buy.
 *
 * The whole of `S4-15`, `S4-16` and `S4-17` in one decision, in this order:
 *
 *   1. **Mode** â€” the platform verdict narrowed by the user's request (`S4-17`).
 *      `off` on either side refuses; a platform `paper` is never re-widened.
 *   2. **Basis** â€” the balance for the *clamped* mode, so a downgraded user is
 *      sized off the paper bankroll rather than their live funds.
 *   3. **Percentage** â€” `min(max_position_pct, master_fraction Ã— scale)`
 *      (ADR-0005 Â§3.1), falling back to flat `max_position_pct` and marking the
 *      trade sized-without-conviction when coverage is short.
 *   4. **Size** â€” `requestedBalanceAwareSize` + `capPositionToAvailableBalance`
 *      from `policy.ts`. No second formula.
 *   5. **Clamps** â€” available balance, then the platform ceiling, then the user's
 *      remaining daily allowance, then precision. Every reduction is recorded.
 *
 * Sells do not come here; see the module note.
 */
export function sizePerUserBuy(input: PerUserSizingInput): PerUserSizingOutcome {
  const riskAccount = riskPolicyAccountForUser(input.userId);
  const mode = resolvePerUserMode({
    userRequested: input.userRequestedMode,
    platform: input.platform,
    killed: input.settings.killed
  });

  if (mode.effective === 'off') {
    // Which side said `off` decides the code. The user's own switches are reported
    // first because an operator debugging "this user is not trading" should see the
    // user's setting before being sent to look at a platform gate that is fine.
    if (input.settings.killed) {
      return refuse('user-killed', 'The per-user kill switch is set', mode, riskAccount);
    }
    if (mode.userRequested === 'off') {
      return refuse(
        'user-chain-mode-off',
        `The user has not enabled ${input.chain}`,
        mode,
        riskAccount
      );
    }
    return refuse(
      'platform-chain-mode-off',
      mode.platformReason ?? `The platform resolved ${input.chain} to off`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  const live = mode.effective !== 'paper';
  const basis = live ? 'live-balance' : 'paper-bankroll';
  const basisUnits = live ? input.balance.liveUnits : input.balance.paperUnits;

  if (!knownNonNegative(basisUnits)) {
    // Not a size of zero. See distinction 2 in the module note.
    return refuse(
      'balance-unknown',
      `No known ${basis} for ${input.chain}; refusing to size against an unknown balance`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  if (basisUnits === 0) {
    // Checked before the exposure block on purpose. A zero balance produces a zero
    // daily allowance, and reporting that as `daily-exposure-cap-reached` would tell
    // an operator the user had spent an allowance they never had. The honest answer
    // is that there is nothing to size, and it is decisive regardless of whether a
    // USD rate or an exposure figure is available.
    return refuse(
      'size-rounds-to-zero',
      `The ${basis} for ${input.chain} is zero`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  if (!knownPositive(input.usdPerUnit)) {
    return refuse(
      'usd-rate-unknown',
      `No USD rate for one ${input.chain} sizing unit, so the daily exposure cap cannot be applied`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  if (!knownNonNegative(input.dailyExposureUsdUsed)) {
    return refuse(
      'daily-exposure-unknown',
      'This user\'s committed exposure for the rolling window is unknown',
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  const basisUsd = basisUnits * input.usdPerUnit;
  const dailyExposureCapUsd = userDailyExposureCapUsd(input.settings, basisUsd);
  if (dailyExposureCapUsd === null) {
    return refuse(
      'daily-exposure-unknown',
      'The user\'s daily exposure cap could not be derived from a known balance',
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }
  const dailyExposureRemainingUsd = dailyExposureCapUsd - input.dailyExposureUsdUsed;
  if (!(dailyExposureRemainingUsd > 0)) {
    return refuse(
      'daily-exposure-cap-reached',
      `This user has committed $${input.dailyExposureUsdUsed} of their `
        + `$${dailyExposureCapUsd} daily allowance on ${input.chain}`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  const conviction = resolveConvictionRiskPct(input.settings.maxPositionPct, input.conviction);
  const sizingInput = {
    balance: basisUnits,
    base: input.baseUnits,
    maximum: input.platformMaximumUnits,
    riskPct: conviction.riskPct,
    tierMultiplier: input.tierMultiplier,
    scoreMultiplier: input.scoreMultiplier,
    precision: input.precision,
    dynamic: input.dynamic
  };
  const requestedUnits = requestedBalanceAwareSize(sizingInput);

  const exposureHeadroomUnits = dailyExposureRemainingUsd / input.usdPerUnit;
  // The min is taken by `capPositionToAvailableBalance`, which is the one place in
  // the repo that decides how a requested size meets its caps. The walk below only
  // *explains* the number it returns.
  const maximumUnits = Math.min(input.platformMaximumUnits, exposureHeadroomUnits);
  const sizeUnits = capPositionToAvailableBalance({
    requested: requestedUnits,
    available: basisUnits,
    maximum: maximumUnits,
    precision: input.precision
  });

  const clamps: PerUserSizingClamp[] = [];
  if (
    conviction.convictionPct !== null
    && conviction.convictionPct < conviction.userMaxPositionPct
    && input.dynamic
  ) {
    // Reported in units so it reads alongside the other clamps: what flat sizing
    // would have asked for, versus what conviction asked for.
    const flatRequest = requestedBalanceAwareSize({
      ...sizingInput,
      riskPct: conviction.userMaxPositionPct
    });
    clamps.push({
      code: 'master-conviction-fraction',
      beforeUnits: flatRequest,
      afterUnits: requestedUnits
    });
  }

  let current = requestedUnits;
  const bounds: readonly (readonly [PerUserSizingClampCode, number])[] = [
    ['available-balance', basisUnits],
    ['platform-maximum-notional', input.platformMaximumUnits],
    ['daily-exposure-remaining', exposureHeadroomUnits]
  ];
  for (const [code, limit] of bounds) {
    if (limit < current) {
      clamps.push({ code, beforeUnits: current, afterUnits: limit });
      current = limit;
    }
  }
  // `current` is now min(requested, available, platformMaximum, headroom), which is
  // exactly what `capPositionToAvailableBalance` floored. Only a genuine reduction is
  // recorded: see `boundedUnits` on the outcome for why flooring can move the value
  // the other way in the last bit.
  if (sizeUnits < current) {
    clamps.push({ code: 'precision-floor', beforeUnits: current, afterUnits: sizeUnits });
  }

  if (!(sizeUnits > 0)) {
    return refuse(
      'size-rounds-to-zero',
      `Every input was known and sizing came to ${sizeUnits} ${input.chain} units`,
      mode,
      riskAccount
    );
  }

  return {
    kind: 'size',
    sizeUnits,
    requestedUnits,
    boundedUnits: current,
    basis,
    basisUnits,
    appliedRiskPct: conviction.riskPct,
    conviction,
    sizedWithoutConviction: conviction.sizedWithoutConviction,
    mode,
    riskAccount,
    clamps,
    dailyExposureCapUsd,
    dailyExposureRemainingUsd
  };
}

describe('nonce semantics', () => {
  it('splits an unordered nonce into wordPos and bitPos like bitmapPositions', () => {
    expect(permit2BitmapPosition(0n)).toEqual({ wordPos: 0n, bitPos: 0 });
    expect(permit2BitmapPosition(255n)).toEqual({ wordPos: 0n, bitPos: 255 });
    expect(permit2BitmapPosition(256n)).toEqual({ wordPos: 1n, bitPos: 0 });
    expect(permit2BitmapPosition(513n)).toEqual({ wordPos: 2n, bitPos: 1 });
  });

  it('reads a spent bit as used', () => {
    expect(isPermit2NonceUsed({ nonce: 3n, bitmapWord: 0b1000n })).toBe(true);
    expect(isPermit2NonceUsed({ nonce: 2n, bitmapWord: 0b1000n })).toBe(false);
    // Bit position is taken modulo the word, so a nonce in another word must not
    // be answered from this word's bits by accident.
    expect(isPermit2NonceUsed({ nonce: 259n, bitmapWord: 0b1000n })).toBe(true);
  });

  it('never returns a nonce that is already spent', () => {
    expect(nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 0n, bitmapWord: 0n })).toBe(0n);
    expect(nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 0n, bitmapWord: 0b0001n })).toBe(1n);
    expect(nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 0n, bitmapWord: 0b0111n })).toBe(3n);
    expect(nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 4n, bitmapWord: 0b0011n })).toBe(1026n);
  });

  it('returns null when all 256 bits in the word are spent', () => {
    expect(nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 0n, bitmapWord: (1n << 256n) - 1n })).toBe(null);
  });

  it('selects distinct nonces for concurrent permits once each is marked spent', () => {
    // The footgun this guards: two permits chosen from the *same* observed
    // bitmap both pick the lowest clear bit and collide, and the second reverts
    // InvalidNonce. Selection must consume as it goes.
    let word = 0b0001n;
    const chosen: bigint[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i += 1) {
      const next = nextUnusedPermit2Nonce({ wordPos: 0n, bitmapWord: word });
      expect(next).not.toBe(null);
      chosen.push(next as bigint);
      word |= 1n << BigInt(permit2BitmapPosition(next as bigint).bitPos);
    }
    expect(chosen).toEqual([1n, 2n, 3n, 4n]);
    expect(new Set(chosen).size).toBe(chosen.length);
    for (const nonce of chosen) {
      expect(isPermit2NonceUsed({ nonce, bitmapWord: word })).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('labels the two nonce spaces distinctly so they cannot be conflated', () => {
    const allowance = buildPermit2AllowancePlan({
      chainId: 4663,
      owner: OWNER,
      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 1n,
      expiration: 1_700_003_600n,
      sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n,
      nonce: 7n,
      nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
    });
    const transfer = buildPermit2SignatureTransferPlan({
      chainId: 4663,
      owner: OWNER,
      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 1n,
      deadline: 1_700_000_120n,
      nonce: 7n,
      nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
    });
    // Same numeric nonce, different mechanism. AllowanceTransfer compares for
    // equality against a stored counter; SignatureTransfer flips a bitmap bit.
    expect(allowance.subject.nonceSpace).toBe('sequential-uint48');
    expect(transfer.subject.nonceSpace).toBe('unordered-bitmap-uint256');
    expect(allowance.subject.nonce).toBe(transfer.subject.nonce);
    expect(allowance.digest).not.toBe(transfer.digest);
  });

  it('rejects a sequential nonce wider than uint48', () => {
    expect(() =>
      buildPermit2AllowancePlan({
        chainId: 4663,
        owner: OWNER,
        token: TOKEN,
        spender: SPENDER,
        amount: 1n,
        expiration: 1_700_003_600n,
        sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n,
        nonce: MAX_UINT48 + 1n,
        nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
      })
    ).toThrow(/exceeds its on-chain width/);
  });

  it('changes the digest when only the nonce changes', () => {
    const build = (nonce: bigint) =>
      buildPermit2AllowancePlan({
        chainId: 4663,
        owner: OWNER,
        token: TOKEN,
        spender: SPENDER,
        amount: 1n,
        expiration: 1_700_003_600n,
        sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n,
        nonce,
        nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
      }).digest;
    expect(build(0n)).not.toBe(build(1n));
  });
});

describe('policy-inspectable subject (S4-P10)', () => {
  it('exposes token, spender, amount and deadline as flat fields', () => {
    const plan = buildPermit2AllowancePlan({
      chainId: 4663,
      owner: OWNER,
      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 4_200n,
      expiration: 1_700_003_600n,

      nonce: 0n,

      chainId: 4663,

      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 4_200n,
      sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n

    const source = buildPermit2AllowancePlan.toString();
