describe('width and argument guards', () => {
  const base = {
    chainId: 4663,
    owner: OWNER,
    token: TOKEN,
    spender: SPENDER,
    expiration: 1_700_003_600n,
    sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n,
    nonce: 0n,
    nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
  } as const;

  it('rejects an allowance amount wider than uint160', () => {
    expect(() =>
      buildPermit2AllowancePlan({ ...base, amount: MAX_PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_AMOUNT + 1n })
    ).toThrow(/exceeds its on-chain width/);
    expect(() =>
      buildPermit2AllowancePlan({ ...base, amount: MAX_PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_AMOUNT })
    ).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('rejects a negative amount', () => {
    expect(() => buildPermit2AllowancePlan({ ...base, amount: -1n })).toThrow(/non-negative/);
  });

  it('rejects a requestedAmount above the permitted ceiling', () => {
    expect(() =>
      buildPermit2SignatureTransferPlan({
        chainId: 4663,
        owner: OWNER,
        token: TOKEN,
        spender: SPENDER,
        amount: 10n,
        requestedAmount: 11n,
        deadline: 1_700_000_120n,
        nonce: 0n,
        nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
      })
    ).toThrow(/exceeds permitted/);
  });

  it('rejects a non-positive chainId', () => {
    expect(() => permit2Domain({ chainId: 0 })).toThrow(/positive integer chainId/);
  });

  it('requires a signature before it will encode a call', () => {
    expect(() =>
      buildPermit2AllowancePlan({ ...base, amount: 1n, emitPermitCall: true })
    ).toThrow(/requires the signature/);
  });

  it('rejects a zero enablement amount', () => {
    expect(() => buildPermit2EnablementCall({ token: TOKEN, amount: 0n })).toThrow(/must be positive/);
  });

  it('keeps the declared EIP-712 widths pinned to the on-chain struct', () => {
    // These widths are load-bearing: widening amount to uint256 silently changes
    // every struct hash, and the only symptom is InvalidSigner.
    expect(PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_TRANSFER_TYPES.PermitDetails).toEqual([
      { name: 'token', type: 'address' },
      { name: 'amount', type: 'uint160' },
      { name: 'expiration', type: 'uint48' },
      { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint48' }
    ]);
  });
});

describe('composes with the authority port (S4-P7)', () => {
  /**
   * A local mirror of `execution-authority.ts`'s `Eip712TypedData`.
   *
   * Mirrored rather than imported because that port is being refactored
   * concurrently, and a type-only import would make this suite fail for reasons
   * that have nothing to do with Permit2. The trade-off is that this copy can go
   * stale â€” so it is written to the same shape deliberately, and the master agent
   * should replace it with the real import once `S4-P7` settles.
   *
   * The check is real: viem's own `TypedDataDefinition` does **not** satisfy this
   * (it makes `domain` optional and allows `chainId: bigint`), which is why
   * `Permit2TypedData` exists.
   */
  type PortEip712TypedData = {
    readonly domain: {
      readonly name?: string;
      readonly version?: string;
      readonly chainId?: number;
      readonly verifyingContract?: string;
      readonly salt?: string;
    };
    readonly types: Readonly<
      Record<string, readonly { readonly name: string; readonly type: string }[]>
    >;
    readonly primaryType: string;
    readonly message: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  };

  it('hands the authority port a payload it can sign as-is', () => {
    const plan = buildPermit2AllowancePlan({
      chainId: 4663,
      owner: OWNER,
      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 1n,
      expiration: 1_700_003_600n,
      sigDeadline: 1_700_000_120n,
      nonce: 0n,
      nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
    });
    // Compile-time: no cast. If Permit2TypedData ever widens, this stops building.
    const payload: PortEip712TypedData = plan.typedData;
    const request: { kind: 'eip712-typed-data'; typedData: PortEip712TypedData } = {
      kind: 'eip712-typed-data',
      typedData: plan.typedData
    };
    expect(payload.primaryType).toBe('PermitSingle');
    expect(payload.domain.chainId).toBe(4663);
    expect(request.kind).toBe('eip712-typed-data');
  });

  it('hands the port a signature-transfer payload too', () => {
    const plan = buildPermit2SignatureTransferPlan({
      chainId: 4663,
      owner: OWNER,
      token: TOKEN,
      spender: SPENDER,
      amount: 1n,
      deadline: 1_700_000_120n,
      nonce: 0n,
      nowSeconds: 1_700_000_000n
    });
    const payload: PortEip712TypedData = plan.typedData;
    expect(payload.primaryType).toBe('PermitTransferFrom');
  });
});

describe('residual allowance posture', () => {
  it('documents that the allowance moves to Permit2 rather than disappearing', () => {
    const posture = describePermit2AllowancePosture();
    expect(posture.standingAllowanceToRouter).toBe('none');
    expect(posture.approvalsPerTrade).toBe(0);
    expect(posture.approvalsPerTokenLifetime).toBe(1);
    expect(posture.notes.join(' ')).toMatch(/moves/);
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/permit2.ts <==
import {
  encodeFunctionData,
  erc20Abi,
  getAddress,
  hashDomain,
  hashTypedData,
  parseAbi,
  type Hex,
  type TypedDataDefinition
} from 'viem';

/**
 * Permit2 payload construction (`S4-M13`).
 *
 * **Read the Phase 1 caveat before wiring this.** This module is *unwired*. It
 * builds correct Permit2 payloads and correct `Permit2`-contract calldata, both
 * verified against Uniswap's own published source and against live on-chain
 * domain separators (see `permit2.test.ts`). What it deliberately does **not**
 * do is emit swap-router calldata, because the router this repo currently calls
 * cannot consume a Permit2 signature at all:
 *
 * - `robinhood.ts` calls a Uniswap **V3 SwapRouter01/02** (`ROBINHOOD_SWAP_ROUTER`,
 *   ABI chosen by `ROBINHOOD_ROUTER_ABI_VERSION`). Neither router knows about
 *   Permit2. `SwapRouter02`'s inheritance list is
 *   `ISwapRouter02, V2SwapRouter, V3SwapRouter, ApproveAndCall, MulticallExtended, SelfPermit`
 *   â€” and `SelfPermit` is **EIP-2612 token-level permit**, a different mechanism
 *   that requires the *token* to implement `permit`. Permit2 integration lives in
 *   the Universal Router, not in either SwapRouter.
 * - Permit2 itself *is* deployed on Robinhood Chain (4663) at the canonical
 *   address, confirmed both by Robinhood's own protocol-contracts page and by
 *   `eth_getCode` (9152 bytes) plus a live `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` read.
 *
 * So the missing fact is the router, not Permit2. Until a Permit2-aware router
 * address on 4663 is confirmed, assembling `execute(bytes,bytes[])` command
 * calldata would be building against an interface nobody has verified is
 * reachable, which is worse than leaving the seam open.
 *
 * **No signing here, by design (`S4-P7`).** Every builder returns a
 * `TypedDataDefinition` for something else to sign. This module never accepts a
 * private key and never produces a signature: the permit is a signature like any
 * other, so it flows through the `UserExecutionAuthority` port rather than being
 * a special-cased transaction.
 *
 * **Policy inspection is structural (`S4-P10`).** Every plan carries a flat
 * {@link Permit2PolicySubject} exposing token / spender / amount / deadline as
 * plain fields *before* anything is signed. A policy engine must never have to
 * decode a blob to find out what it is about to authorise â€” that is the
 * `approve`-spender hole reappearing in a new costume.
 */

/**
 * The canonical, deterministic Permit2 deployment address.
 *
 * The same on every chain that has one, because Permit2 is deployed via a
 * deterministic deployer. Verified present on Robinhood Chain (4663) â€” listed in
 * `docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts` under "Misc (L2)" for both
 * mainnet and testnet, and confirmed by `eth_getCode` returning 9152 bytes.
 *
 * Kept as a checksummed literal rather than an env var **on purpose**: a
 * mistyped Permit2 address does not fail loudly, it silently produces a domain
 * separator nobody will ever counter-sign, and the failure surfaces as an
 * unexplained `InvalidSigner` revert. Callers that genuinely need to override it
 * (a fork, a test chain) pass `permit2` explicitly and eat the risk visibly.
 */
export const CANONICAL_PERMIT2_ADDRESS = '0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3' as const;

/** ERC-20 `approve(address,uint256)` selector, used to *prove absence*. */
export const ERC20_APPROVE_SELECTOR = '0x095ea7b3' as const;

/** `uint160` ceiling â€” the width of `PermitDetails.amount`. */
export const MAX_PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_AMOUNT = (1n << 160n) - 1n;
/** `uint48` ceiling â€” the width of `PermitDetails.expiration` and `.nonce`. */
export const MAX_UINT48 = (1n << 48n) - 1n;
/** `uint256` ceiling â€” the width of a SignatureTransfer unordered nonce. */
export const MAX_UINT256 = (1n << 256n) - 1n;

/**
 * Which of Permit2's two halves a payload targets.
 *
 * Permit2 is documented as "a unification of 2 contracts, `SignatureTransfer`
 * and `AllowanceTransfer`". They are not interchangeable and â€” the part that
 * bites â€” **they do not share nonce semantics**. See {@link Permit2NonceSpace}.
 */
export type Permit2Kind = 'allowance-transfer' | 'signature-transfer';

/**
 * How a nonce is validated on-chain. The two are genuinely different mechanisms.
 *
 * - `sequential-uint48` â€” `AllowanceTransfer` / `PermitSingle`. A plain
 *   incrementing counter stored per `(owner, token, spender)` inside
 *   `PackedAllowance`. `_updateApproval` does `if (allowed.nonce != nonce)
 *   revert InvalidNonce();` then stores `nonce + 1`. The signed nonce must equal
 *   the currently stored one **exactly**; permits for one triple are therefore
 *   consumed strictly in order.
 * - `unordered-bitmap-uint256` â€” `SignatureTransfer` / `PermitTransferFrom`. A
 *   `uint256` split into `wordPos = nonce >> 8` and `bitPos = uint8(nonce)`,
 *   indexing `nonceBitmap[owner][wordPos]`. `_useUnorderedNonce` XORs the bit in
 *   and reverts `InvalidNonce` if it was already set. Any unused bit is valid,
 *   in any order.
 *
 * Note the asymmetry that a lot of integration code gets wrong: only the
 * *unordered* half is a bitmap. It is common to read "Permit2 uses unordered
 * nonces" and apply that to `PermitSingle`, which then reverts `InvalidNonce`
 * the moment the value is anything other than the stored counter.
 */
export type Permit2NonceSpace = 'sequential-uint48' | 'unordered-bitmap-uint256';

/**
 * Everything a policy engine needs, flat and pre-signature (`S4-P10`).
 *
 * This is the whole point of the module's shape. `S4-M13` deletes the `approve`
 * call that `S4-P10` was going to constrain by spender, so the argument-level
 * check has to move onto these fields instead. If they were only reachable by
 * decoding `typedData`, every policy implementation would have to re-derive
 * Permit2's ABI, and the ones that got it subtly wrong would fail *open*.
 */
export type Permit2PolicySubject = {
  kind: Permit2Kind;
  chainId: number;
  /** The Permit2 instance that will verify the signature. */
  permit2: `0x${string}`;
  /** The account whose tokens move. The signer must be this address. */
  owner: `0x${string}`;
  /** The ERC-20 being permitted. */
  token: `0x${string}`;
  /**
   * The address authorised to pull the tokens.
   *
   * For `signature-transfer` this address is **not** present in the on-chain
   * struct â€” Permit2 substitutes `msg.sender` when it rebuilds the digest. It is
   * still signed over, so it must equal whoever will call `permitTransferFrom`,
   * and a policy engine must be able to see it. Hence it lives here.
   */
  spender: `0x${string}`;
  /** Maximum spendable: `uint160` for allowance-transfer, `uint256` otherwise. */
  amount: bigint;
  /** Unix seconds past which Permit2 reverts `SignatureExpired`. */
  sigDeadline: bigint;
  /**
   * Unix seconds at which the *allowance* lapses; `null` for signature-transfer,
   * which grants no standing allowance at all.
   */
  expiration: bigint | null;
  nonce: bigint;
  nonceSpace: Permit2NonceSpace;
};

/**
 * The signable payload, shaped to satisfy the `S4-P7` authority port.
 *
 * **Deliberately not viem's `TypedDataDefinition`.** That type declares `domain`
 * as optional and `domain.chainId` as `number | bigint`, so it is *not*
 * assignable to `ExecutionAuthority`'s `Eip712TypedData`, which requires a
 * present `domain` and a `number` chain id. Returning viem's type directly would
 * push a cast onto every call site in the authority adapters â€” and a cast at the
 * boundary is exactly where a genuinely malformed payload would slip through.
 *
 * So this narrows to what is actually always true here: the domain is always
 * built, `chainId` is always a `number`, and the primary type is one of two known
 * strings. The literals are still checked against viem's own type internally via
 * `satisfies`, so the field/type/message consistency viem enforces is not lost.
 *
 * Declared structurally rather than imported from `execution-authority.ts` so
 * this module does not depend on a port that is being refactored concurrently;
 * `permit2.test.ts` pins the shape so drift is caught.
 */
export type Permit2TypedData = {
  readonly domain: {
    readonly name: 'Permit2';
    readonly chainId: number;
    readonly verifyingContract: `0x${string}`;
  };
  readonly types: Readonly<
    Record<string, readonly { readonly name: string; readonly type: string }[]>
  >;
  readonly primaryType: 'PermitSingle' | 'PermitTransferFrom';
  readonly message: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
};

/** A transaction call to submit once the signature exists. */
export type Permit2Call = {
  to: `0x${string}`;
  data: Hex;
  value: bigint;
  /** Why this call exists, so callers can log and assert without decoding. */
  purpose: 'permit2-enablement-approve' | 'permit2-permit' | 'permit2-transfer-from';
};

/**
 * A signable payload plus the calls it unlocks.
 *
 * `calls` is empty for the plans that only need a signature handed onward to a
 * router; it is populated when the caller intends to drive Permit2 directly.
 */
export type Permit2Plan = {
  subject: Permit2PolicySubject;
  typedData: Permit2TypedData;
  /** The EIP-712 digest that will be signed. Exposed for logging and tests. */
  digest: Hex;
  calls: Permit2Call[];
};

/**
 * The Permit2 EIP-712 domain.
 *
 * **There is no `version` field, and that is not an omission.** Permit2's
 * `EIP712.sol` hashes the preimage
 * `"EIP712Domain(string name,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)"` â€” four
 * members, no `version`, no `salt`. Adding `version: '1'` (the reflex, since
 * almost every other EIP-712 domain has one) changes the domain separator and
 * every resulting signature verifies as a *different signer*, so it surfaces as
 * `InvalidSigner` rather than as anything that points at the domain.
 *
 * Verified against two live deployments in `permit2.test.ts`.
 */
export function permit2Domain(input: {
  chainId: number;
  permit2?: `0x${string}`;
}): { name: 'Permit2'; chainId: number; verifyingContract: `0x${string}` } {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(input.chainId) || input.chainId <= 0) {
    throw new Error('permit2Domain requires a positive integer chainId');
  }
  return {
    name: 'Permit2',
    chainId: input.chainId,
    verifyingContract: getAddress(input.permit2 ?? CANONICAL_PERMIT2_ADDRESS)
  };
}

/**
 * The EIP-712 domain type, spelled out.
 *
 * viem infers this from the domain's keys when hashing typed data, but the
 * inference is exactly the thing worth pinning: if `permit2Domain` ever gained a
 * `version` key the inferred type would silently follow it, and every signature
 * would start verifying as a different signer with no test failing. Declaring it
 * explicitly means the separator is computed from a fixed type regardless.
 */
export const PERMIT2_EIP712_DOMAIN_TYPE = [
  { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
  { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' },
  { name: 'verifyingContract', type: 'address' }
] as const;

/**
 * The `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` Permit2 would return on `chainId`.
 *
 * Pure, so it can be checked against a live `eth_call` without this module ever
 * making one. `permit2.test.ts` pins it against two real deployments.
 */
export function permit2DomainSeparator(input: {
  chainId: number;
  permit2?: `0x${string}`;
}): Hex {
  const domain = permit2Domain(input);
  return hashDomain({
    // `chainId` is `uint256` in the domain type, so it is widened to `bigint`
    // here. `permit2Domain` keeps it a `number` because that is what viem's
    // `signTypedData` domain expects, and the signer is the primary consumer.
    domain: { ...domain, chainId: BigInt(domain.chainId) },
    types: { EIP712Domain: [...PERMIT2_EIP712_DOMAIN_TYPE] }
  });
}

/**
 * EIP-712 types for `AllowanceTransfer`.
 *
 * Field order and widths mirror `IAllowanceTransfer.sol` exactly. The widths are
 * load-bearing: `amount` is `uint160` (not `uint256`) and `expiration`/`nonce`
 * are `uint48`, because all three pack into one storage slot. Widening any of
 * them here changes the struct hash.
 */
export const PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_TRANSFER_TYPES = {
  PermitDetails: [
    { name: 'token', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint160' },
    { name: 'expiration', type: 'uint48' },
    { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint48' }
  ],
  PermitSingle: [
    { name: 'details', type: 'PermitDetails' },
    { name: 'spender', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'sigDeadline', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
} as const;

/**
 * EIP-712 types for `SignatureTransfer`.
 *
 * `PermitTransferFrom` carries `spender` in the *signed* type even though the
 * on-chain struct does not â€” Permit2 hashes `msg.sender` into that position. The
 * signed type and the ABI struct therefore differ by one field, deliberately.
 */
export const PERMIT2_SIGNATURE_TRANSFER_TYPES = {
  TokenPermissions: [
    { name: 'token', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint256' }
  ],
  PermitTransferFrom: [
    { name: 'permitted', type: 'TokenPermissions' },
    { name: 'spender', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint256' },
    { name: 'deadline', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
} as const;

/** Permit2 ABI fragments. Transcribed from the published interfaces. */
export const PERMIT2_ABI = parseAbi([
  'struct PermitDetails { address token; uint160 amount; uint48 expiration; uint48 nonce; }',
  'struct PermitSingle { PermitDetails details; address spender; uint256 sigDeadline; }',
  'struct TokenPermissions { address token; uint256 amount; }',
  'struct PermitTransferFrom { TokenPermissions permitted; uint256 nonce; uint256 deadline; }',
  'struct SignatureTransferDetails { address to; uint256 requestedAmount; }',
  'function permit(address owner, PermitSingle permitSingle, bytes signature) external',
  'function permitTransferFrom(PermitTransferFrom permit, SignatureTransferDetails transferDetails, address owner, bytes signature) external',
  'function allowance(address owner, address token, address spender) external view returns (uint160 amount, uint48 expiration, uint48 nonce)',
  'function nonceBitmap(address owner, uint256 wordPos) external view returns (uint256)',
  'function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32)'
]);

function requireUnsigned(value: bigint, max: bigint, label: string): void {
  if (value < 0n) throw new Error(`${label} must be non-negative`);
  if (value > max) throw new Error(`${label} exceeds its on-chain width`);
}

/**
 * Rejects a `sigDeadline` that is already past at `nowSeconds`.
 *
 * Permit2's check is `if (block.timestamp > sigDeadline) revert
 * SignatureExpired(sigDeadline)`, so equality is still valid â€” the permit is
 * live *through* its deadline second, not up to it. Mirrored exactly here rather
 * than approximated with `>=`, because an off-by-one in the safe direction still
 * means we reject payloads the chain would have accepted, and an off-by-one the
 * other way means we ask a user to sign something guaranteed to revert.
 */
export function assertPermit2DeadlineUnexpired(input: {
  sigDeadline: bigint;
  nowSeconds: bigint;
}): void {
  requireUnsigned(input.sigDeadline, MAX_UINT256, 'sigDeadline');
  if (input.nowSeconds > input.sigDeadline) {
    throw new Error(
      `Permit2 sigDeadline ${input.sigDeadline} is already expired at ${input.nowSeconds}`
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Splits a SignatureTransfer nonce into its bitmap coordinates.
 *
 * Mirrors Permit2's private `bitmapPositions`: the high 248 bits select the word
 * in `nonceBitmap[owner]`, the low 8 bits select the bit inside it. One word
 * therefore tracks 256 nonces.
 */
export function permit2BitmapPosition(nonce: bigint): { wordPos: bigint; bitPos: number } {
  requireUnsigned(nonce, MAX_UINT256, 'nonce');
  return { wordPos: nonce >> 8n, bitPos: Number(nonce & 0xffn) };
}

/**
 * Whether `nonce` has already been spent, given the on-chain bitmap word.
 *
 * `bitmapWord` must be `nonceBitmap[owner][wordPos]` for the *matching*
 * `wordPos` â€” passing the wrong word answers a different question and answers it
 * confidently, so callers should derive both from {@link permit2BitmapPosition}.
 */
export function isPermit2NonceUsed(input: { nonce: bigint; bitmapWord: bigint }): boolean {
  requireUnsigned(input.bitmapWord, MAX_UINT256, 'bitmapWord');
  const { bitPos } = permit2BitmapPosition(input.nonce);
  return ((input.bitmapWord >> BigInt(bitPos)) & 1n) === 1n;
}

/**
 * Lowest unspent nonce in one bitmap word, or `null` if all 256 are spent.
 *
 * **This is not the EVM transaction nonce and must never be derived from it.**
 * The transaction nonce is per-account, strictly sequential, and consumed by the
 * node when a transaction lands; this one is per-`(owner, wordPos)`, unordered,
 * and consumed by the Permit2 contract when a *signature* is redeemed. They
 * advance independently: a permit signed but never submitted burns no
 * transaction nonce, and a failed transaction burns a transaction nonce while
 * leaving the Permit2 bit clear. `packages/db/src/evm-nonce.ts`
 * (`withEvmNonceLock`) and `withSubmissionLock` in `robinhood.ts` serialise the
 * *transaction* nonce; neither one protects this.
 *
 * Which matters here because the exclusion those locks provide is per-account,
 * and it happens to be sufficient â€” while one process holds the account's lock,
 * no other process is choosing a Permit2 nonce for that account either. Two
 * concurrent permits under the same lock would both read the same bitmap word
 * and both pick the same bit; the second reverts `InvalidNonce`. So Permit2
 * nonce selection has to sit *inside* the existing lock, not beside it. Reusing
 * the lock is correct; reusing the *number* is not.
 */
export function nextUnusedPermit2Nonce(input: {
  wordPos: bigint;
  bitmapWord: bigint;
}): bigint | null {
  requireUnsigned(input.wordPos, MAX_UINT256 >> 8n, 'wordPos');
  requireUnsigned(input.bitmapWord, MAX_UINT256, 'bitmapWord');
  for (let bit = 0n; bit < 256n; bit += 1n) {
    if (((input.bitmapWord >> bit) & 1n) === 0n) return (input.wordPos << 8n) | bit;
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Builds the `PermitSingle` payload for `AllowanceTransfer`.
 *
 * `nonce` must be the value currently stored at
 * `Permit2.allowance(owner, token, spender).nonce` â€” not "the next one", not the
 * transaction nonce. Permit2 compares for equality and increments itself.
 */
export function buildPermit2AllowancePlan(input: {
  chainId: number;
  owner: `0x${string}`;
  token: `0x${string}`;
  spender: `0x${string}`;
  amount: bigint;
  /** Unix seconds at which the allowance lapses. */
  expiration: bigint;
  /** Unix seconds after which the signature is dead. */
  sigDeadline: bigint;
  /** Current on-chain allowance nonce for `(owner, token, spender)`. */
  nonce: bigint;
  /** For the deadline sanity check. Injected, so this stays pure. */
  nowSeconds: bigint;
  permit2?: `0x${string}`;
  /**
   * Emit the `Permit2.permit(...)` call as well as the payload.
   *
   * Off by default: a Permit2-aware router consumes the signature inline (the
   * Universal Router's `PERMIT2_PERMIT` command), so a separate `permit`
   * transaction would defeat the single-transaction goal that `S4-M13` exists to
   * achieve. Turn it on only when driving Permit2 directly.
   */
  emitPermitCall?: boolean;
  /**
   * Placeholder signature used purely to shape the `permit` calldata.
   *
   * Required when `emitPermitCall` is set. This module never signs, so the
   * caller supplies the signature it obtained from the authority port.
   */
  signature?: Hex;
  /**
   * Permit `expiration: 0`, which Permit2 reads as a sentinel.
   *
   * `Allowance.updateAll` stores `expiration == 0 ? uint48(block.timestamp)`, so
   * a zero expiration does not mean "never expires" â€” it means the allowance
   * lives for exactly one block. Almost always a bug, so it must be opted into.
   */
  allowBlockScopedExpiration?: boolean;
}): Permit2Plan {
  const domain = permit2Domain({ chainId: input.chainId, permit2: input.permit2 });
  const owner = getAddress(input.owner);
  const token = getAddress(input.token);
  const spender = getAddress(input.spender);

  requireUnsigned(input.amount, MAX_PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_AMOUNT, 'amount');
  requireUnsigned(input.expiration, MAX_UINT48, 'expiration');
  requireUnsigned(input.nonce, MAX_UINT48, 'nonce');
  if (input.expiration === 0n && input.allowBlockScopedExpiration !== true) {
    throw new Error(
      'expiration 0 makes the allowance last a single block; pass allowBlockScopedExpiration to accept that'
    );
  }
  assertPermit2DeadlineUnexpired({ sigDeadline: input.sigDeadline, nowSeconds: input.nowSeconds });
  if (input.expiration !== 0n && input.expiration < input.nowSeconds) {
    throw new Error(`allowance expiration ${input.expiration} is already past at ${input.nowSeconds}`);
  }

  // `expiration` and `nonce` are `uint48` on-chain, and viem models any uint
  // narrower than 53 bits as `number`. Narrowing here is lossless â€” `uint48` max
  // is 281474976710655, comfortably inside `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` â€” and both
  // widths were already bounded above. The public API keeps `bigint` throughout
  // so callers never have to think about where the boundary is.
  const message = {
    details: {
      token,
      amount: input.amount,
      expiration: Number(input.expiration),
      nonce: Number(input.nonce)
    },
    spender,
    sigDeadline: input.sigDeadline
  };
  const typedData = {
    domain,
    types: PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_TRANSFER_TYPES,
    primaryType: 'PermitSingle',
    message
  } as const satisfies TypedDataDefinition;

  const calls: Permit2Call[] = [];
  if (input.emitPermitCall === true) {
    if (!input.signature) {
      throw new Error('emitPermitCall requires the signature produced by the authority port');
    }
    calls.push({
      to: domain.verifyingContract,
      data: encodeFunctionData({
        abi: PERMIT2_ABI,
        functionName: 'permit',
        args: [owner, message, input.signature]
      }),
      value: 0n,
      purpose: 'permit2-permit'
    });
  }

  return {
    subject: {
      kind: 'allowance-transfer',
      chainId: input.chainId,
      permit2: domain.verifyingContract,
      owner,
      token,
      spender,
      amount: input.amount,
      sigDeadline: input.sigDeadline,
      expiration: input.expiration,
      nonce: input.nonce,
      nonceSpace: 'sequential-uint48'
    },
    typedData,
    digest: hashTypedData(typedData),
    calls
  };
}

/**
 * Builds the `PermitTransferFrom` payload for `SignatureTransfer`.
 *
 * The signed message includes `spender`, but the ABI struct does not: Permit2
 * rebuilds the digest using `msg.sender`. So the address that submits
 * `permitTransferFrom` must be exactly `spender`, or verification fails with
 * `InvalidSigner` and gives no hint that the mismatch was the caller's identity.
 */
export function buildPermit2SignatureTransferPlan(input: {
  chainId: number;
  owner: `0x${string}`;
  token: `0x${string}`;
  /** The address that will call `permitTransferFrom`. Signed over. */
  spender: `0x${string}`;
  /** Ceiling authorised by the signature. */
  amount: bigint;
  /** Unix seconds after which the signature is dead. */
  deadline: bigint;
  /** An unspent unordered nonce â€” see {@link nextUnusedPermit2Nonce}. */
  nonce: bigint;
  nowSeconds: bigint;
  permit2?: `0x${string}`;
  /** Where the pulled tokens land. Defaults to `spender`. */
  transferTo?: `0x${string}`;
  /** Amount actually pulled; must be `<= amount`. Defaults to `amount`. */
  requestedAmount?: bigint;
  emitTransferCall?: boolean;
  signature?: Hex;
}): Permit2Plan {
  const domain = permit2Domain({ chainId: input.chainId, permit2: input.permit2 });
  const owner = getAddress(input.owner);
  const token = getAddress(input.token);
  const spender = getAddress(input.spender);
  const transferTo = getAddress(input.transferTo ?? input.spender);

  requireUnsigned(input.amount, MAX_UINT256, 'amount');
  requireUnsigned(input.nonce, MAX_UINT256, 'nonce');
  assertPermit2DeadlineUnexpired({ sigDeadline: input.deadline, nowSeconds: input.nowSeconds });

  const requestedAmount = input.requestedAmount ?? input.amount;
  requireUnsigned(requestedAmount, MAX_UINT256, 'requestedAmount');
  if (requestedAmount > input.amount) {
    // Permit2 reverts InvalidAmount; catching it here keeps a doomed payload
    // from ever reaching a signer, which is the cheaper place to fail.
    throw new Error(`requestedAmount ${requestedAmount} exceeds permitted ${input.amount}`);
  }

  const typedData = {
    domain,
    types: PERMIT2_SIGNATURE_TRANSFER_TYPES,
    primaryType: 'PermitTransferFrom',
    message: {
      permitted: { token, amount: input.amount },
      spender,
      nonce: input.nonce,
      deadline: input.deadline
    }
  } as const satisfies TypedDataDefinition;

  const calls: Permit2Call[] = [];
  if (input.emitTransferCall === true) {
    if (!input.signature) {
      throw new Error('emitTransferCall requires the signature produced by the authority port');
    }
    calls.push({
      to: domain.verifyingContract,
      data: encodeFunctionData({
        abi: PERMIT2_ABI,
        functionName: 'permitTransferFrom',
        args: [
          // Note the absent `spender`: it is signed but not transmitted.
          { permitted: { token, amount: input.amount }, nonce: input.nonce, deadline: input.deadline },
          { to: transferTo, requestedAmount },
          owner,
          input.signature
        ]
      }),
      value: 0n,
      purpose: 'permit2-transfer-from'
    });
  }

  return {
    subject: {
      kind: 'signature-transfer',
      chainId: input.chainId,
      permit2: domain.verifyingContract,
      owner,
      token,
      spender,
      amount: input.amount,
      sigDeadline: input.deadline,
      expiration: null,
      nonce: input.nonce,
      nonceSpace: 'unordered-bitmap-uint256'
    },
    typedData,
    digest: hashTypedData(typedData),
    calls
  };
}

/**
 * Whether the one-time `token.approve(permit2, â€¦)` is still outstanding.
 *
 * **Permit2 does not abolish the ERC-20 approval; it relocates it.** Uniswap's
 * own documentation is explicit: "users must first approve the Permit2 contract
 * on the token itself before an integrating contract can pull their tokens". So
 * the honest claim for `S4-M13` is *one approve, once, per token* rather than
 * one approve per trade â€” not "no approve ever".
 *
 * What genuinely improves is the residual-allowance surface. See
 * {@link describePermit2AllowancePosture}.
 */
export function permit2EnablementRequired(input: {
  currentAllowanceToPermit2: bigint;
  amount: bigint;
}): boolean {
  requireUnsigned(input.currentAllowanceToPermit2, MAX_UINT256, 'currentAllowanceToPermit2');
  requireUnsigned(input.amount, MAX_UINT256, 'amount');
  return input.currentAllowanceToPermit2 < input.amount;
}

/**
 * The one-time enablement call: `token.approve(permit2, amount)`.
 *
 * Deliberately a *separate* function rather than something the plan builders
 * splice in, so the happy path provably emits no `approve` calldata and a test
 * can assert exactly that. Folding it in conditionally would make the absence
 * untestable without reproducing the condition.
 *
 * `amount` is not defaulted to `uint256` max. Unlimited is what Uniswap suggests
 * for general wallets, but this repo's posture is bounded approvals, and an
 * infinite standing allowance to Permit2 is precisely the risk this module is
 * supposed to be honest about.
 */
export function buildPermit2EnablementCall(input: {
  token: `0x${string}`;
  amount: bigint;
  permit2?: `0x${string}`;
}): Permit2Call {
  requireUnsigned(input.amount, MAX_UINT256, 'amount');
  if (input.amount === 0n) throw new Error('enablement amount must be positive');
  return {
    to: getAddress(input.token),
    data: encodeFunctionData({
      abi: erc20Abi,
      functionName: 'approve',
      args: [getAddress(input.permit2 ?? CANONICAL_PERMIT2_ADDRESS), input.amount]
    }),
    value: 0n,
    purpose: 'permit2-enablement-approve'
  };
}

/** True when `call` is an ERC-20 `approve`. Used to assert its absence. */
export function isErc20ApproveCall(call: Pick<Permit2Call, 'data'>): boolean {
  return call.data.slice(0, 10).toLowerCase() === ERC20_APPROVE_SELECTOR;
}

/**
 * The residual-allowance posture, as required by `S4-M13`'s "done when".
 *
 * Written as data rather than prose in a markdown file so it cannot drift away
 * from the code it describes.
 */
export function describePermit2AllowancePosture(): {
  standingAllowanceToRouter: 'none';
  standingAllowanceToPermit2: 'bounded-or-unlimited-one-time';
  approvalsPerTrade: 0;
  approvalsPerTokenLifetime: 1;
  notes: string[];
} {
  return {
    standingAllowanceToRouter: 'none',
    standingAllowanceToPermit2: 'bounded-or-unlimited-one-time',
    approvalsPerTrade: 0,
    approvalsPerTokenLifetime: 1,
    notes: [
      'Permit2 leaves no standing ERC-20 allowance to the swap router: the router is authorised per-signature, with an amount and a deadline, and AllowanceTransfer allowances additionally carry their own expiration.',
      'That is strictly better than the rolling bounded-allowance fallback this replaces, which left a live router allowance between trades.',
      'The standing allowance does not disappear, it moves: the user must approve Permit2 itself once per token. Permit2 is audited and very widely used, but it is a different risk surface, not an absent one â€” a Permit2 compromise would reach every token every user has enabled, whereas a router allowance reached one token for one router.',
      'Bounding the enablement amount keeps that blast radius finite. Approving uint256 max is the common wallet default and is explicitly not this module default.'
    ]
  };
}

==> apps/trade-executor/src/policy.ts <==
export type TradingMode = 'paper' | 'live';

function parseNumericValue(value: unknown, label: string): number {
  if (typeof value === 'number') return value;
  if (typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0 && value.trim() === value) {
    return Number(value);
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} must be numeric`);
}

export function parseTradingMode(value: string | undefined): TradingMode {
  if (value === undefined) return 'paper';
  if (value === 'paper' || value === 'live') return value;
  throw new Error(`TRADING_MODE must be exactly "paper" or "live"; received ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
}

export function parseScore(value: unknown, label: string): number {
  const score = parseNumericValue(value, label);
  if (!Number.isFinite(score) || score < 0 || score > 100) {
    throw new Error(`${label} must be a finite number between 0 and 100`);
  }
  return score;
}

export function parsePositiveNumber(value: string | undefined, fallback: number, label: string): number {
  const parsed = value === undefined ? fallback : parseNumericValue(value, label);
  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed <= 0) {
    throw new Error(`${label} must be a positive finite number`);
  }
  return parsed;
}

export function parseNonNegativeNumber(value: string | undefined, fallback: number, label: string): number {
  const parsed = value === undefined ? fallback : parseNumericValue(value, label);
  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed < 0) {
    throw new Error(`${label} must be a non-negative finite number`);
  }
  return parsed;
}

export function floorToPrecision(value: number, precision: number): number {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new Error('Value must be a finite, non-negative number');
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(precision) || precision < 0 || precision > 12) {
    throw new Error('Precision must be an integer between 0 and 12');
  }

  const factor = 10 ** precision;
  return Math.floor(value * factor) / factor;
}

export function capPositionToAvailableBalance(opts: {
  requested: number;
  available: number;
  maximum: number;
  precision: number;
}): number {
  const values = [opts.requested, opts.available, opts.maximum];
  if (values.some((value) => !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0)) {
    throw new Error('Balance cap inputs must be finite, non-negative numbers');
  }

  return floorToPrecision(Math.min(opts.requested, opts.available, opts.maximum), opts.precision);
}

export interface BalanceAwareSizingInput {
  balance: number;
  base: number;
  maximum: number;
  riskPct: number;
  tierMultiplier: number;
  scoreMultiplier: number;
  precision: number;
  dynamic: boolean;
}

/**
 * The size this configuration *asks for*, before any cap is applied.
 *
 * Extracted from `calculateBalanceAwareSize` rather than reimplemented, and it is
 * the only statement of the formula in this repo. `per-user-sizing.ts` needs the
 * pre-clamp figure so it can report *which* bound reduced a user's size â€” an
 * operator asking "why did I get 0.05 and not 0.2" cannot be answered from a
 * single already-clamped number. Deriving the request a second time there would
 * have put two copies of the sizing formula in the tree, and the copy that drifted
 * would misattribute the clamp while still returning a plausible size.
 *
 * Validation lives here, so both this and `calculateBalanceAwareSize` refuse the
 * same inputs.
 */
export function requestedBalanceAwareSize(opts: BalanceAwareSizingInput): number {
  const values = [
    opts.balance,
    opts.base,
    opts.maximum,
    opts.riskPct,
    opts.tierMultiplier,
    opts.scoreMultiplier
  ];
  if (values.some((value) => !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0)) {
    throw new Error('Balance-aware sizing inputs must be finite, non-negative numbers');
  }
  if (opts.riskPct > 100) {
    throw new Error('Risk percentage cannot exceed 100');
  }

  return opts.dynamic
    ? opts.balance * (opts.riskPct / 100) * opts.tierMultiplier * opts.scoreMultiplier
    : opts.base * opts.tierMultiplier * opts.scoreMultiplier;
}

export function calculateBalanceAwareSize(opts: BalanceAwareSizingInput): number {
  return capPositionToAvailableBalance({
    requested: requestedBalanceAwareSize(opts),
    available: opts.balance,
    maximum: opts.maximum,
    precision: opts.precision
  });
}

export function calculateRiskBasedSize(opts: {
  balance: number;
  riskPct: number;
  tierMultiplier: number;
  scoreMultiplier: number;
  maximum: number;
  precision: number;
}): number {
  const values = [
    opts.balance,
    opts.riskPct,
    opts.tierMultiplier,
    opts.scoreMultiplier,
    opts.maximum
  ];
  if (values.some((value) => !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0)) {
    throw new Error('Risk sizing inputs must be finite, non-negative numbers');
  }
  if (opts.riskPct > 100) {
    throw new Error('Risk percentage cannot exceed 100');
  }

  const computed =
    opts.balance *
    (opts.riskPct / 100) *
    opts.tierMultiplier *
    opts.scoreMultiplier;
  return capPositionToAvailableBalance({
    requested: computed,
    available: opts.balance,
    maximum: opts.maximum,
    precision: opts.precision
  });
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness,
  interpretPolymarketCancellation,
  planPolymarketRungRetirement,
  polymarketCancellationError
} from './polymarket-cancellation.js';

/**
 * Tests for the one shared reading of Polymarket's cancellation contract
 * (`S4-M36`).
 *
 * The fixtures below are the documented response bodies, copied from
 * `/trading/manage-orders` â†’ *Cancellation Results* and
 * `/api-reference/trade/cancel-single-order`, not invented. That matters here
 * more than usual: the bug being fixed was a *misread of the contract*, so a test
 * written against a made-up shape would re-encode the same mistake.
 */

describe('interpretPolymarketCancellation', () => {
  it('confirms an order the venue listed in canceled', () => {
    expect(interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: ['ORDER_ID_1'], not_canceled: {} },
      'ORDER_ID_1'
    )).toEqual({ kind: 'confirmed' });
  });

  it('reads a not_canceled refusal as terminal, with NO exception thrown', () => {
    // This is the exact documented example. The old code awaited cancelOrder in
    // a try/catch and only acted in the catch, so this 200 response â€” the one
    // failure path the cancel existed to cover â€” was silently read as success.
    const reading = interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: ['ORDER_ID_1'], not_canceled: { ORDER_ID_2: 'order already matched' } },
      'ORDER_ID_2'
    );
    expect(reading).toEqual({ kind: 'already-terminal', reason: 'order already matched' });
  });

  it('reads the camelCase notCanceled spelling the TypeScript SDK returns', () => {
    // The REST reference documents `not_canceled`; the @polymarket/client type is
    // `notCanceled`. A parser that reads only one silently never matches.
    expect(interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: [], notCanceled: { 'stale-1': 'order already matched' } },
      'stale-1'
    )).toEqual({ kind: 'already-terminal', reason: 'order already matched' });
  });

  it('does not treat another order id being canceled as this order being canceled', () => {
    const reading = interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: ['someone-elses-order'], not_canceled: {} },
      'my-order'
    );
    expect(reading.kind).toBe('unreported');
  });

  it('reads an unrecognised refusal as refused, never as confirmed', () => {
    const reading = interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: [], not_canceled: { 'rung-1': 'internal error 500' } },
      'rung-1'
    );
    expect(reading).toEqual({ kind: 'refused', reason: 'internal error 500' });
  });

  it('recognises a delay-window refusal as its own state', () => {
    const reading = interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: [], not_canceled: { 'rung-1': 'order is in a pending delay window' } },
      'rung-1'
    );
    expect(reading.kind).toBe('delay-window');
  });

  it('never throws on a malformed body â€” it reports learning nothing', () => {
    for (const body of [null, undefined, 'nope', 42, {}, { canceled: 'not-an-array' }]) {
      expect(interpretPolymarketCancellation(body, 'rung-1').kind).toBe('unreported');
    }
  });

  it('coerces non-string order ids, because the venue types them as OrderId', () => {
    expect(interpretPolymarketCancellation(
      { canceled: [12345] },
      '12345'
    )).toEqual({ kind: 'confirmed' });
  });

  it('wraps a thrown call as error, which says nothing about the order', () => {
    expect(polymarketCancellationError(new Error('ECONNRESET')))
      .toEqual({ kind: 'error', reason: 'ECONNRESET' });
  });
});

describe('classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness', () => {
  it('classifies the documented statuses', () => {
    // /concepts/order-lifecycle â†’ Order Statuses: live, matched, delayed,
    // unmatched. fetchOrder returns them upper-cased.
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('LIVE').kind).toBe('resting');
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('MATCHED').kind).toBe('terminal');
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('DELAYED').kind).toBe('delayed');
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('UNMATCHED').kind).toBe('resting');
  });

  it('treats UNMATCHED as resting, not finished', () => {
    // The docs define it as "placed on the book after the delay expired without a
    // match" â€” i.e. it IS on the book. Reading it as terminal would be the same
    // class of mistake this item fixes.
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('unmatched')).toEqual({
      kind: 'resting',
      status: 'UNMATCHED'
    });
  });

  it('treats cancelled and expired as terminal', () => {
    for (const status of ['CANCELLED', 'CANCELED', 'EXPIRED', 'FAILED', 'REJECTED']) {
      expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness(status).kind).toBe('terminal');
    }
  });

  it('reports an undocumented status as unknown rather than guessing', () => {
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('SOMETHING_NEW')).toEqual({
      kind: 'unknown',
      status: 'SOMETHING_NEW'
    });
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness(undefined).kind).toBe('unknown');
  });

  it('strips the ORDER_STATUS_ prefix the venue sometimes carries', () => {
    expect(classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness('ORDER_STATUS_LIVE').kind).toBe('resting');
  });
});

describe('planPolymarketRungRetirement', () => {
  const base = { orderId: 'rung-1', attempt: 1, maxAttempts: 3 } as const;

  it('retires an order the venue reports terminal', () => {
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'already-terminal', reason: 'order already matched' },
      liveness: { kind: 'terminal', status: 'MATCHED' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('retired');
  });

  it('does NOT retire on a confirmed cancel while the order still reads LIVE', () => {
    // The fetched order wins over the cancellation response. This is requirement
    // (1) of the item: the order must be terminal, not merely "we asked nicely".
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'confirmed' },
      liveness: { kind: 'resting', status: 'LIVE' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('retry-cancel');
  });

  it('retries the cancel while a resting order still has attempts left', () => {
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'refused', reason: 'internal error' },
      liveness: { kind: 'resting', status: 'LIVE' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('retry-cancel');
  });

  it('BLOCKS the next rung when a resting order survives every attempt', () => {
    // The whole point. Placing the next rung on top of a live one gives two live
    // sell orders whose combined size can exceed the position.
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      attempt: 3,
      cancellation: { kind: 'refused', reason: 'internal error' },
      liveness: { kind: 'resting', status: 'LIVE' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('blocked');
    expect(plan.reason).toContain('two live sell orders');
  });

  it('treats a delay-window refusal as WAIT, not as failure', () => {
    // /concepts/order-lifecycle documents cancels as blocked in the delay window,
    // so the refusal is the venue behaving as specified.
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'delay-window', reason: 'pending delay window' },
      liveness: { kind: 'resting', status: 'LIVE' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('wait');
  });

  it('treats a DELAYED order status as wait even when the cancel merely errored', () => {
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'error', reason: 'ECONNRESET' },
      liveness: { kind: 'delayed', status: 'DELAYED' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('wait');
  });

  it('blocks rather than waits forever when the delay window outlasts the attempts', () => {
    const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      attempt: 3,
      cancellation: { kind: 'delay-window', reason: 'pending delay window' },
      liveness: { kind: 'delayed', status: 'DELAYED' }
    });
    expect(plan.kind).toBe('blocked');
  });

  it('never retires an order whose status it cannot recognise', () => {
    const attemptsLeft = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      cancellation: { kind: 'confirmed' },
      liveness: { kind: 'unknown', status: 'WAT' }
    });
    expect(attemptsLeft.kind).toBe('retry-cancel');

    const exhausted = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
      ...base,
      attempt: 3,
      cancellation: { kind: 'confirmed' },
      liveness: { kind: 'unknown', status: 'WAT' }
    });
    expect(exhausted.kind).toBe('blocked');
  });

  it('never returns retired for any non-terminal liveness, across every cancellation reading', () => {
    // Exhaustive rather than illustrative: 'retired' is the branch that unlocks
    // the next rung, so the invariant worth pinning is that ONLY a terminal
    // fetched order can produce it.
    const readings = [
      { kind: 'confirmed' },
      { kind: 'already-terminal', reason: 'r' },
      { kind: 'delay-window', reason: 'r' },
      { kind: 'refused', reason: 'r' },
      { kind: 'unreported', reason: 'r' },
      { kind: 'error', reason: 'r' }
    ] as const;
    const livenesses = [
      { kind: 'resting', status: 'LIVE' },
      { kind: 'delayed', status: 'DELAYED' },
      { kind: 'unknown', status: 'WAT' }
    ] as const;

    for (const cancellation of readings) {
      for (const liveness of livenesses) {
        for (const attempt of [1, 3]) {
          const plan = planPolymarketRungRetirement({
            orderId: 'rung-1',
            attempt,
            maxAttempts: 3,
            cancellation,
            liveness
          });
          expect(plan.kind, `${cancellation.kind}/${liveness.kind}/${attempt}`)
            .not.toBe('retired');
        }
      }
    }
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-cancellation.ts <==
/**
 * One reading of Polymarket's cancellation contract, shared by every call site
 * (checklist `S4-M36`).
 *
 * **Why this module exists rather than two inline reads.** The repo had two
 * disagreeing interpretations of the same API. `reconcilePendingPolymarketTrade`
 * checked `cancellation.canceled.some(...)`; `createPolymarketExitRungSubmitter`
 * wrapped the call in a try/catch and assumed a failure would throw. Only one of
 * those can be right, and the wrong one was silently a no-op on exactly the
 * failure path it was written to cover. Two readings of one contract is the
 * defect, so there is now one reading.
 *
 * **What the venue actually returns** (verified against the live docs, not
 * memory):
 *
 *   * `/trading/manage-orders` â†’ *Cancellation Results*: "A cancellation can
 *     succeed for only some of the requested orders. Reconcile the result before
 *     retrying." The TypeScript SDK's type is
 *     `{ canceled: OrderId[]; notCanceled: Record<OrderId, string> }`; the Python
 *     SDK and the raw REST body spell the second field `not_canceled`. Both
 *     spellings are accepted below because the SDK's camelCase is what
 *     `@polymarket/client` hands us while the API reference documents snake_case,
 *     and a reader of only one page would write a parser that silently never
 *     matches.
 *   * `/api-reference/trade/cancel-single-order`: `DELETE /order` answers **200**
 *     with that same body. A stale order therefore lands in `not_canceled` with
 *     **no exception** â€” the documented example is
 *     `{"canceled": ["ORDER_ID_1"], "not_canceled": {"ORDER_ID_2": "order already matched"}}`.
 *   * `/concepts/order-lifecycle` â†’ *Cancellation*: "You can cancel orders at any
 *     time before they're matched via the CLOB API, **except while a marketable
 *     order is in a pending delay window**." And *Match or Rest*: "During either
 *     delay, the order is pending and cannot be canceled." So a cancel refused
 *     inside that window is the venue behaving as documented â€” a reason to wait,
 *     not a failure.
 *   * `/concepts/order-lifecycle` â†’ *Order Statuses*: `live` (resting on the
 *     book), `matched`, `delayed` (accepted into the asynchronous delay window on
 *     a `secondsDelay` market), `unmatched` (placed on the book after the delay
 *     expired without a match). `/trading/manage-orders` shows `fetchOrder`
 *     returning `status: "LIVE"`, i.e. upper-case over the wire.
 *   * `/concepts/order-lifecycle` â†’ *Cancellation*: "Partial fills cannot be
 *     cancelled: only the unfilled portion of an order can be cancelled." This is
 *     why a non-zero `sizeMatched` is **not** evidence the order is finished: a
 *     partially filled order rests on the book for its remainder.
 *
 * **What the docs do not say, and how that is handled.** The docs give one
 * example `not_canceled` message ("order already matched") and never enumerate
 * the set, so the exact prose for a delay-window refusal is unknown. The
 * authoritative wait signal is therefore the *order status* (`delayed`), which is
 * documented, and reason-text matching is only ever an additional hint. Anything
 * unrecognised is reported as `refused`, which fails closed.
 *
 * Pure: no clock, no client, no environment. Every function here is a total
 * function of the venue's response shape.
 */

/** How a cancellation response reads for one specific order id. */
export type PolymarketCancellationReading =
  /** The venue listed the order in `canceled`. It is gone. */
  | { readonly kind: 'confirmed' }
  /**
   * The venue refused because the order was already finished â€” matched, filled,
   * expired or unknown to it. Not a cancellation, but not something resting
   * either.
   */
  | { readonly kind: 'already-terminal'; readonly reason: string }
  /**
   * The venue refused because the order is inside a matching-delay window. The
   * docs say cancels are blocked there, so this is expected and means wait.
   */
  | { readonly kind: 'delay-window'; readonly reason: string }
  /** Refused for a reason we do not recognise. Not proof of anything. */
  | { readonly kind: 'refused'; readonly reason: string }
  /** The order appeared in neither list, so the response says nothing about it. */
  | { readonly kind: 'unreported'; readonly reason: string }
  /** The call itself failed (transport, auth, 5xx). Says nothing about the order. */
  | { readonly kind: 'error'; readonly reason: string };

function asRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
    ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
    : null;
}

function canceledIds(response: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
  const raw = response.canceled;
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
  return raw.map((id) => String(id));
}

/**
 * The refusal map, under either spelling.
 *
 * `notCanceled` is the `@polymarket/client` TypeScript type; `not_canceled` is
 * what the REST reference and the Python SDK document. Reading only one is how a
 * parser ends up never matching a refusal.
 */
function notCanceledEntries(response: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, string> {
  const candidate = asRecord(response.notCanceled) ?? asRecord(response.not_canceled);
  if (!candidate) return {};
  const entries: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [orderId, reason] of Object.entries(candidate)) {
    entries[String(orderId)] = typeof reason === 'string' ? reason : String(reason);
  }
  return entries;
}

/**
 * Reasons that mean the order is already finished.
 *
 * Only "order already matched" is documented, as the example refusal on
 * `/trading/manage-orders`. The rest are conservative synonyms of the same fact.
 * Being wrong in this direction is the dangerous one, so the list is short and
 * anything outside it reads as `refused`.
 */
const TERMINAL_REFUSAL_PATTERNS: readonly RegExp[] = [
  /already\s+matched/i,
  /already\s+filled/i,
  /already\s+cancell?ed/i,
  /already\s+expired/i,
  /not\s+found/i,
  /does\s+not\s+exist/i,
  /unknown\s+order/i
];

/**
 * Reasons that hint at the documented delay window.
 *
 * A hint only. The docs never state the refusal text for this case, so the
 * decision to wait is driven by the order's own `delayed` status in
 * `planPolymarketRungRetirement`; this exists so a recognisable message is not
 * thrown away.
 */
const DELAY_REFUSAL_PATTERNS: readonly RegExp[] = [
  /delay/i,
  /pending\s+match/i,
  /not\s+cancellable\s+yet/i
];

/**
 * Read a cancellation response for one order id.
 *
 * Never throws: a malformed response is `unreported`, which is treated as "we
 * learned nothing" rather than as success. The alternative â€” assuming a 200 with
 * an unreadable body means the order is gone â€” is the assumption this whole
 * module exists to remove.
 */
export function interpretPolymarketCancellation(
  response: unknown,
  orderId: string
): PolymarketCancellationReading {
  const body = asRecord(response);
  if (!body) {
    return {
      kind: 'unreported',
      reason: `Polymarket cancellation returned no readable body for order ${orderId}`
    };
  }

  if (canceledIds(body).includes(orderId)) {
    return { kind: 'confirmed' };
  }

  const refusal = notCanceledEntries(body)[orderId];
  if (refusal !== undefined) {
    if (TERMINAL_REFUSAL_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(refusal))) {
      return { kind: 'already-terminal', reason: refusal };
    }
    if (DELAY_REFUSAL_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(refusal))) {
      return { kind: 'delay-window', reason: refusal };
    }
    return { kind: 'refused', reason: refusal };
  }

  return {
    kind: 'unreported',
    reason:
      `Polymarket cancellation listed order ${orderId} in neither canceled nor not_canceled`
  };
}

/** Wrap a thrown cancellation call so the planner sees one input shape. */
export function polymarketCancellationError(error: unknown): PolymarketCancellationReading {
  return {
    kind: 'error',
    reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
  };
}

/**
 * Whether an order the venue just described is still capable of filling.
 *
 * This is the reading the rung submitter was missing. It already called
 * `fetchOrder` and read `sizeMatched` from it, then threw the status away â€” so it
 * knew how much had filled and never asked whether anything was still live.
 */
export type PolymarketOrderLiveness =
  /** Provably dead: it cannot fill again. */
  | { readonly kind: 'terminal'; readonly status: string }
  /** Resting on the book, remainder still fillable. */
  | { readonly kind: 'resting'; readonly status: string }
  /** Inside the venue's matching-delay window; cancels are blocked there. */
  | { readonly kind: 'delayed'; readonly status: string }
  /** A status outside the documented set. Not evidence of anything. */
  | { readonly kind: 'unknown'; readonly status: string };

function normalizeStatus(value: unknown): string {
  return String(value ?? '').trim().toUpperCase().replace(/^ORDER_STATUS_/, '');
}

/**
 * Classify an order status into "can this still fill?".
 *
 * The documented statuses are `live`, `matched`, `delayed` and `unmatched`.
 * `unmatched` is explicitly "placed on the book after the delay expired without a
 * match", so it is *resting*, not finished â€” reading it as terminal would be the
 * same class of mistake this item fixes. The extra spellings mirror
 * `classifyOrderState` in `polymarket.ts`, which has to tolerate the venue's
 * upper-case and legacy variants.
 */
export function classifyPolymarketOrderLiveness(status: unknown): PolymarketOrderLiveness {
  const normalized = normalizeStatus(status);
  switch (normalized) {
    case 'LIVE':
    case 'OPEN':
    case 'UNMATCHED':
      return { kind: 'resting', status: normalized };
    case 'DELAYED':
    case 'PENDING':
      return { kind: 'delayed', status: normalized };
    case 'MATCHED':
    case 'FILLED':
    case 'COMPLETED':
    case 'CANCELLED':
    case 'CANCELED':
    case 'EXPIRED':
    case 'FAILED':
    case 'REJECTED':
    case 'INVALID':
      return { kind: 'terminal', status: normalized };
    default:
      return { kind: 'unknown', status: normalized };
  }
}

/**
 * What to do with an escalation rung once its resting window has elapsed.
 *
 * The whole point is the `blocked` branch. An exit ladder places the next rung
 * for whatever the previous rung did not fill, so if the previous rung is still
 * resting we would have **two live sell orders whose combined size exceeds the
 * position** â€” selling a user's shares twice. Refusing to continue costs a slower
 * exit and an alert; continuing costs an oversell. That asymmetry is why this
 * fails closed, and it is deliberately the opposite of `S4-M31`, where failing
 * closed would have halted all copying to avoid one odd trade.
 */
export type PolymarketRungRetirement =
  /** Provably dead. Safe to read its fill and move to the next rung. */
  | { readonly kind: 'retired'; readonly reason: string }
  /** Expected transient state (delay window). Wait, then re-check. */
  | { readonly kind: 'wait'; readonly reason: string }
  /** Still resting or unproven, and attempts remain. Cancel again. */
  | { readonly kind: 'retry-cancel'; readonly reason: string }
  /** Not provably dead and out of attempts. Do not place another rung. */
  | { readonly kind: 'blocked'; readonly reason: string };

export interface PolymarketRungRetirementInput {
  readonly orderId: string;
  readonly cancellation: PolymarketCancellationReading;
  readonly liveness: PolymarketOrderLiveness;
  /** 1-based count of cancel attempts already made. */
  readonly attempt: number;
  readonly maxAttempts: number;
}

/**
 * Decide whether a rung is retired, worth another cancel, or must stop the
 * ladder.
 *
 * The fetched order state wins over the cancellation response wherever the two
 * disagree, because it describes the order rather than describing one request
 * about the order. A cancel the venue confirmed while the order still reads
 * `LIVE` is therefore *not* accepted as retired â€” the ordering is what makes
 * requirement (1) of the item ("require the order to be terminal, not merely
 * partially matched") actually bind.
 */
export function planPolymarketRungRetirement(
  input: PolymarketRungRetirementInput
): PolymarketRungRetirement {
  const attemptsRemain = input.attempt < input.maxAttempts;
  const suffix =
    `after ${input.attempt} of ${input.maxAttempts} cancel attempts`;

  if (input.liveness.kind === 'terminal') {
    return {
      kind: 'retired',
      reason:
        `order ${input.orderId} is terminal (${input.liveness.status}), so nothing is resting`
    };
  }

  if (input.liveness.kind === 'delayed' || input.cancellation.kind === 'delay-window') {
    const detail = input.cancellation.kind === 'delay-window'
      ? input.cancellation.reason
      : `status ${input.liveness.status}`;
    return attemptsRemain
      ? {
        kind: 'wait',
        reason:
          `order ${input.orderId} is inside the venue's matching-delay window (${detail}); `
          + 'the docs block cancels there, so this is expected'
      }
      : {
        kind: 'blocked',
        reason:
          `order ${input.orderId} is still inside the venue's matching-delay window (${detail}) `
          + `${suffix}; refusing to place the next rung against an order that can still match`
      };
  }

  if (input.liveness.kind === 'resting') {
    return attemptsRemain
      ? {
        kind: 'retry-cancel',
        reason:
          `order ${input.orderId} is still resting on the book (${input.liveness.status}) `
          + `despite cancellation reading '${input.cancellation.kind}'`
      }
      : {
        kind: 'blocked',
        reason:
          `order ${input.orderId} is still resting on the book (${input.liveness.status}) `
          + `${suffix}; placing the next rung would leave two live sell orders whose `
          + 'combined size can exceed the position'
      };
  }

  // Unknown status. An unreadable order is not a dead order, and the cost of
  // guessing wrong here is an oversell, so it is never treated as retired.
  return attemptsRemain
    ? {
      kind: 'retry-cancel',
      reason:
        `order ${input.orderId} returned an unrecognised status '${input.liveness.status}', `
        + 'which is not proof it stopped resting'
    }
    : {
      kind: 'blocked',
      reason:
        `order ${input.orderId} returned an unrecognised status '${input.liveness.status}' `
        + `${suffix}; it cannot be shown to be dead, so the ladder stops here`
    };
}

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness,
  POLYMARKET_CONTRACTS,
  type PolymarketCollateralGateway
} from './polymarket-collateral.js';

function createGateway(
  overrides: Partial<PolymarketCollateralGateway> = {}
): PolymarketCollateralGateway {
  return {
    getPusdDecimals: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(6),
    getUsdcEDecimals: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(6),
    getPusdBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(10_000_000n),
    getUsdcEBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n),
    getUsdcEAllowance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n),
    approveUsdcE: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('0x-usdce-approve'),
    wrapUsdcE: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('0x-wrap'),
    getPusdAllowance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(10_000_000n),
    approvePusd: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('0x-pusd-approve'),
    isConditionalTokenApproved: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true),
    approveConditionalTokenOperator: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('0x-conditional-approve'),
    ...overrides
  };
}

const baseOptions = {
  funderAddress: '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
  signerAddress: '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
  accountWalletType: 'EOA' as const,
  directWalletWritesAllowed: true,
  minimumPusdUnits: 1_000_000n,
  allowanceCapUnits: 10_000_000n,
  autoOnramp: false,
  autoApprove: false
};

describe('Polymarket collateral readiness', () => {
  it('accepts the exact minimum balance, exact exchange caps, and sell approvals', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(baseOptions.minimumPusdUnits)
    });

    const result = await ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, baseOptions);

    expect(result.pUsdBalanceUnits).toBe(baseOptions.minimumPusdUnits);
    expect(result.allowanceCapUnits).toBe(baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits);
    expect(result.actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(gateway.getPusdAllowance).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(gateway.isConditionalTokenApproved).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(gateway.approvePusd).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('onramps only the exact deficit and installs bounded EOA approvals', async () => {
    let pUsdBalance = 0n;
    let usdcEAllowance = 0n;
    const pUsdAllowances = new Map<string, bigint>();
    const conditionalApprovals = new Set<string>();
    const approveUsdcE = vi.fn(async (_spender: string, amount: bigint) => {
      usdcEAllowance = amount;
      return `0x-usdce-${amount}`;
    });
    const approvePusd = vi.fn(async (spender: string, amount: bigint) => {
      pUsdAllowances.set(spender, amount);
      return `0x-pusd-${spender.slice(-4)}-${amount}`;
    });
    const approveConditionalTokenOperator = vi.fn(async (operator: string) => {
      conditionalApprovals.add(operator);
      return `0x-ctf-${operator.slice(-4)}`;
    });
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdBalance: vi.fn(async () => pUsdBalance),
      getUsdcEBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(5_000_000n),
      getUsdcEAllowance: vi.fn(async () => usdcEAllowance),
      approveUsdcE,
      wrapUsdcE: vi.fn(async (_to, amount) => {
        pUsdBalance += amount;
        usdcEAllowance -= amount;
        return '0x-wrap';
      }),
      getPusdAllowance: vi.fn(async (_account, spender) => pUsdAllowances.get(spender) ?? 0n),
      approvePusd,
      isConditionalTokenApproved: vi.fn(
        async (_account, operator) => conditionalApprovals.has(operator)
      ),
      approveConditionalTokenOperator
    });

    const result = await ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      autoOnramp: true,
      autoApprove: true
    });

    expect(approveUsdcE).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      POLYMARKET_CONTRACTS.collateralOnramp,
      1_000_000n
    );
    expect(gateway.wrapUsdcE).toHaveBeenCalledWith(baseOptions.funderAddress, 1_000_000n);
    expect(approvePusd).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(approvePusd.mock.calls.map((call) => call[1])).toEqual([
      baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits,
      baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits
    ]);
    expect(approveConditionalTokenOperator).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result.pUsdBalanceUnits).toBe(1_000_000n);
    expect(result.actions).toHaveLength(6);
  });

  it('reduces unlimited existing allowances to the exact configured cap', async () => {
    const allowances = new Map<string, bigint>([
      [POLYMARKET_CONTRACTS.ctfExchange, ethersMaxUint256()],
      [POLYMARKET_CONTRACTS.negRiskCtfExchange, ethersMaxUint256()]
    ]);
    const approvePusd = vi.fn(async (spender: string, amount: bigint) => {
      allowances.set(spender, amount);
      return `0x-${amount}`;
    });
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdAllowance: vi.fn(async (_account, spender) => allowances.get(spender) ?? 0n),
      approvePusd
    });

    const result = await ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      autoApprove: true
    });

    expect(approvePusd.mock.calls.map((call) => call[1])).toEqual([
      0n,
      baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits,
      0n,
      baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits
    ]);
    expect(approvePusd.mock.calls.flat().includes(ethersMaxUint256())).toBe(false);
    expect(result.actions.map((action) => action.type)).toEqual([
      'approve-pusd-exchange-reset',
      'approve-pusd-exchange',
      'approve-pusd-exchange-reset',
      'approve-pusd-exchange'
    ]);
  });

  it('fails closed on over-cap allowance when automatic approval is not opted in', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdAllowance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits + 1n)
    });

    );

  });

  it('fails if an approval transaction does not confirm the exact allowance', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdAllowance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n)
    });

    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      autoApprove: true
    })).rejects.toThrow('did not confirm at the configured exact cap');
  });

  it('rejects wrong collateral decimals before reading balances', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdDecimals: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(18)
    });

    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, baseOptions)).rejects.toThrow(
      'pUSD decimals mismatch'
    );
    expect(gateway.getPusdBalance).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('fails closed below the balance minimum and at an uncovered onramp deficit', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway({
      getPusdBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(baseOptions.minimumPusdUnits - 1n)
    });
    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, baseOptions)).rejects.toThrow(
      'explicitly enable POLYMARKET_AUTO_ONRAMP=true'
    );

    const insufficientUsdc = createGateway({
      getPusdBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n),
      getUsdcEBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(baseOptions.minimumPusdUnits - 1n)
    });
    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(insufficientUsdc, {
      ...baseOptions,
      autoOnramp: true
    })).rejects.toThrow('cannot cover the exact pUSD onramp amount');
    expect(insufficientUsdc.approveUsdcE).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('rejects an automatic proxy setup before any wallet call', async () => {
    const gateway = createGateway();

    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(gateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      funderAddress: '0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222',
      accountWalletType: 'POLY_PROXY',
      directWalletWritesAllowed: false,
      autoApprove: true
    })).rejects.toThrow('automatic setup is EOA-only');
    expect(gateway.getPusdBalance).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(gateway.approvePusd).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('reports actionable Safe and deposit-wallet manual readiness', async () => {
    const safeGateway = createGateway({
      getPusdAllowance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n)
    });
    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(safeGateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      funderAddress: '0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222',
      accountWalletType: 'POLY_GNOSIS_SAFE',
      directWalletWritesAllowed: false
    })).rejects.toThrow('complete it through that account wallet rather than signer');
    expect(safeGateway.approvePusd).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    const depositWalletGateway = createGateway({
      getPusdBalance: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(0n)
    });
    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(depositWalletGateway, {
      ...baseOptions,
      funderAddress: '0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333',
      accountWalletType: 'POLY_1271',
      directWalletWritesAllowed: false
    })).rejects.toThrow('manual pUSD funding');
    expect(depositWalletGateway.wrapUsdcE).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('rejects unbounded minimum configuration', async () => {
    await expect(ensurePolymarketCollateralReadiness(createGateway(), {
      ...baseOptions,
      minimumPusdUnits: baseOptions.allowanceCapUnits + 1n
    })).rejects.toThrow('cannot exceed the bounded allowanceCapUnits');
  });
});

function ethersMaxUint256(): bigint {
  return (1n << 256n) - 1n;
}

import { ethers } from 'ethers';

export const POLYMARKET_CONTRACTS = Object.freeze({
  ctfExchange: '0xE111180000d2663C0091e4f400237545B87B996B',
  negRiskCtfExchange: '0xe2222d279d744050d28e00520010520000310F59',
  conditionalTokens: '0x4D97DCd97eC945f40cF65F87097ACe5EA0476045',
  pUsd: '0xC011a7E12a19f7B1f670d46F03B03f3342E82DFB',
  pUsdImplementation: '0x6bBCef9f7ef3B6C592c99e0f206a0DE94Ad0925f',
