const {
  planPolymarketBookOrder,
  setPolymarketClientForTesting,
  setPolymarketLiveReadiness,
  triggerPolymarket
} = await import('./polymarket.js');

/**
 * Binary + neg-risk entry/exit matrix (checklist S3-18 remainder).
 *
 * A neg-risk market signs against a different EIP-712 verifying contract than a
 * standard one â€” `0xE1111800...` versus `0xe2222d27...` per `trading/place-orders`.
 * The SDK makes that choice from the token; `PrepareMarketOrderRequest` has no
 * field through which a caller could override it. Duplicating the mapping on our
 * side would therefore be unreachable at best and silently divergent if
 * Polymarket ever remapped it, which is exactly the failure the redemption sweep
 * already guards against for the collateral adapter. Both exchange addresses are
 * pinned and attested once at startup (`polymarket-startup.ts`), not chosen per
 * order.
 *
 * So the matrix asserts an asymmetry: **neg-risk is a no-op axis** â€” the plan and
 * the signed request must be byte-identical to the binary case â€” while **entry
 * versus exit is the real axis**, differing in units, balance source, protective
 * bound, and required inputs.
 */

const TOKEN_ID = 'token-matrix';
const BUILDER_CODE = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;
const CONDITION_ID = `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`;

// 20 USD at 0.40 and 50 shares at 0.60 both come to 50 shares, so an entry and an
// exit can be compared without a quantity difference confounding the direction.
const ENTRY_USD = 20;
const EXIT_SHARES = 50;
const ENTRY_ASKS = [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }];
const EXIT_BIDS = [{ price: '0.60', size: '1000' }];

const MARKETS = [
  { label: 'binary', negRisk: false },
  { label: 'neg-risk', negRisk: true }
] as const;

// Keys a caller could plausibly reach for when hand-rolling the neg-risk split.
// None of them exists on `PrepareMarketOrderRequest`; sending one would be a
// silent no-op the venue never sees.
const VENUE_SELECTION_KEYS = [
  'negRisk',
  'neg_risk',
  'exchange',
  'exchangeAddress',
  'adapter',
  'verifyingContract'
];

type Level = { price: string; size: string };

function paginator(items: unknown[]) {
  const page = { items, hasMore: false };
  return {
    firstPage: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(page),
    from: vi.fn(),
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
      yield page;
    }
  };
}

function orderBook(params: {
  negRisk: boolean;
  asks?: Level[];
  bids?: Level[];
  tickSize?: string;
  timestamp?: number;
}) {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
    timestamp: params.timestamp ?? Date.now(),
    asks: params.asks ?? [],
    bids: params.bids ?? [],
    minOrderSize: '1',
    tickSize: params.tickSize ?? '0.01',
    negRisk: params.negRisk,
    hash: 'a'.repeat(40)
  } as Parameters<typeof planPolymarketBookOrder>[0];
}

function createMockClient() {
  return {
    fetchOrderBook: vi.fn(),
    listOpenOrders: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(paginator([])),
    createMarketOrder: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ builder: BUILDER_CODE }),
    postOrder: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
      ok: true,
      orderId: 'order-id',
      status: 'live',
      transactionsHashes: [],
      tradeIds: []
    }),
    waitForOrderFillSettlement: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([]),
    listAccountTrades: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(paginator([]))
  };
}

type MockClient = ReturnType<typeof createMockClient>;

function installClient(mock: MockClient): void {
  setPolymarketClientForTesting(
    mock as unknown as Parameters<typeof setPolymarketClientForTesting>[0]
  );
}

function clientWithBook(params: {
  negRisk: boolean;
  asks?: Level[];
  bids?: Level[];
  tickSize?: string;
}): MockClient {
  const mock = createMockClient();
  mock.fetchOrderBook.mockResolvedValue(orderBook(params));
  installClient(mock);
  return mock;
}

function configureConfirmedFill(params: {
  client: MockClient;
  price: string;
  size: string;
  side: 'BUY' | 'SELL';
}) {
  const transactionHash = `0x${'2'.repeat(64)}`;
  params.client.postOrder.mockResolvedValue({
    ok: true,
    orderId: 'order-id',
    status: 'matched',
    transactionsHashes: [],
    tradeIds: ['trade-id']
  });
  params.client.waitForOrderFillSettlement.mockResolvedValue([transactionHash]);
  params.client.listAccountTrades.mockReturnValue(paginator([{
    id: 'trade-id',
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
    owner: 'owner',
    takerOrderId: 'order-id',
    side: params.side,
    traderSide: 'TAKER',
    price: params.price,
    size: params.size,
    outcome: 'Yes',
    status: 'CONFIRMED',
    feeRateBps: '0',
    bucketIndex: 0,
    transactionHash,
    makerOrders: [],
    matchedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()
  }]));
}

async function submittedOrderRequest(
  negRisk: boolean,
  direction: 'buy' | 'sell'
): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
  const mock = clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS });
  await triggerPolymarket({
    signalId: `sig-${direction}-${String(negRisk)}`,
    tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
    spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
    direction,
    ...(direction === 'sell' ? { sellShares: EXIT_SHARES } : {})
  });
  return mock.createMarketOrder.mock.calls[0]![0] as Record<string, unknown>;
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  dbMocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);
  dbMocks.recordCopyExecutionEvidence.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  dbMocks.transitionCopyExecution.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance.mockResolvedValue({
    balance: '1000000000',
    allowances: {}
  });
  marketStateMocks.assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission.mockResolvedValue({
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    active: true,
    closed: false,
    acceptingOrders: true,
    resolutionStatus: 'unresolved',
    endDate: new Date(Date.now() + 86_400_000)
  });
  setPolymarketLiveReadiness(true);
  process.env.POLYMARKET_FEE_BUFFER_BPS = '300';
  // The price bounds and slippage cap are read from env at submission time. Clear
  // them so the cases below pin the shipped defaults (0.97 / 0.01 / 200 bps)
  // rather than whatever an operator shell happens to export.
  delete process.env.POLYMARKET_SLIPPAGE_BPS;
  delete process.env.POLYMARKET_MAX_ENTRY_PRICE;
  delete process.env.POLYMARKET_MIN_EXIT_PRICE;
  delete process.env.POLYMARKET_MAX_BOOK_AGE_MS;
});

describe('polymarket binary and neg-risk entry-exit matrix', () => {
  describe('neg-risk is not a decision this code makes', () => {
    it.each([
      { direction: 'buy' as const, amount: ENTRY_USD },
      { direction: 'sell' as const, amount: EXIT_SHARES }
    ])('plans a $direction identically on a binary and a neg-risk book', ({ direction, amount }) => {
      // Same levels, same size, one flag apart. If anyone ever branches the depth
      // walk, the slippage cap, or the rounding on `negRisk`, these diverge.
      const now = Date.now();
      const levels = { asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS, timestamp: now };
      const binary = planPolymarketBookOrder(
        orderBook({ negRisk: false, ...levels }), direction, amount, 200, now
      );
      const negRisk = planPolymarketBookOrder(
        orderBook({ negRisk: true, ...levels }), direction, amount, 200, now
      );

      expect(negRisk).toEqual(binary);
    });

    it.each([
      {
        direction: 'buy' as const,
        keys: ['amount', 'builderCode', 'maxPrice', 'maxSpend', 'orderType', 'side', 'tokenId']
      },
      {
        direction: 'sell' as const,
        keys: ['builderCode', 'minPrice', 'orderType', 'shares', 'side', 'tokenId']
      }
    ])('signs an identical $direction request on both market kinds', async ({ direction, keys }) => {
      const binary = await submittedOrderRequest(false, direction);
      const negRisk = await submittedOrderRequest(true, direction);

      // The regression guard. An added `negRisk`/`exchange`/`adapter` key would be
      // dropped on the floor by the SDK while reading as though we had handled the
      // split ourselves.
      expect(Object.keys(negRisk).sort()).toEqual(keys);
      for (const forbidden of VENUE_SELECTION_KEYS) {
        expect(negRisk).not.toHaveProperty(forbidden);
      }
      expect(negRisk).toEqual(binary);
    });
  });

  describe.each(MARKETS)('$label market', ({ negRisk }) => {
    it('enters by spending USD off ask depth, capped by maxPrice', async () => {
      const client = clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS });
      configureConfirmedFill({ client, price: '0.40', size: '50', side: 'BUY' });

      const result = await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      });

      // An entry spends collateral, so the balance read is the account's pUSD, not
      // a per-outcome holding.
      expect(actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance).toHaveBeenCalledWith(client, {
        assetType: AssetType.COLLATERAL
      });
      expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
        side: OrderSide.BUY,
        amount: ENTRY_USD,
        maxSpend: ENTRY_USD,
        maxPrice: 0.4,
        orderType: OrderType.FAK,
        builderCode: BUILDER_CODE
      });
      expect(marketStateMocks.assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission)
        .toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ conditionId: CONDITION_ID }));
      expect(result.executionStatus).toBe('filled');
      expect(result.shares).toBe(50);
      expect(result.spendAmountUsd).toBe(20);
      // An entry is requested in dollars and discovers its share count; the exit
      // below is the mirror image.
      expect(result.requestedSpendAmountUsd).toBe(ENTRY_USD);
      expect(result.requestedShares).toBe(50);
    });

    it('exits by disposing shares off bid depth, floored by minPrice', async () => {
      const client = clientWithBook({ negRisk, bids: EXIT_BIDS });
      configureConfirmedFill({ client, price: '0.60', size: '50', side: 'SELL' });

      const result = await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: EXIT_SHARES
      });

      // An exit disposes of a specific outcome token, so the balance that bounds
      // it is that token's, keyed by id â€” a neg-risk event has one such holding
      // per outcome and they are not fungible with each other.
      expect(actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance).toHaveBeenCalledWith(client, {
        assetType: AssetType.CONDITIONAL,
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID
      });
      expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
        side: OrderSide.SELL,
        shares: EXIT_SHARES,
        minPrice: 0.6,
        orderType: OrderType.FAK,
        builderCode: BUILDER_CODE
      });
      expect(marketStateMocks.assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission)
        .toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ conditionId: CONDITION_ID }));
      expect(result.executionStatus).toBe('filled');
      expect(result.shares).toBe(50);
      expect(result.spendAmountUsd).toBe(30);
      // Requested in shares, with the dollar figure derived â€” the inverse of the
      // entry.
      expect(result.requestedShares).toBe(EXIT_SHARES);
      expect(result.requestedSpendAmountUsd).toBe(30);
    });

    it('reads the same requested amount as dollars on entry and shares on exit', async () => {
      // Depth is priced in USD (size Ã— price) on the ask side and in shares on the
      // bid side, so the same number means different things by direction. Feeding
      // both sides the same book and the same `10` proves the units are not
      // interchangeable.
      const now = Date.now();
      const book = orderBook({
        negRisk,
        asks: [{ price: '0.50', size: '10' }, { price: '0.52', size: '10' }],
        bids: [{ price: '0.52', size: '10' }, { price: '0.50', size: '10' }],
        timestamp: now
      });

      const entry = planPolymarketBookOrder(book, 'buy', 10, 500, now);
      const exit = planPolymarketBookOrder(book, 'sell', 10, 500, now);

      // $10 clears the 0.50 level ($5) and part of 0.52, so the entry crosses two
      // levels and pays 400 bps of slippage.
      expect(entry.estimatedNotionalUsd).toBeCloseTo(10);
      expect(entry.estimatedShares).toBe(19.61);
      expect(entry.limitPrice).toBe(0.52);
      expect(entry.slippageBps).toBeCloseTo(400);
      // 10 shares clear the top bid alone, so the exit never leaves the best level.
      expect(exit.estimatedShares).toBe(10);
      expect(exit.estimatedNotionalUsd).toBeCloseTo(5.2);
      expect(exit.limitPrice).toBe(0.52);
      expect(exit.slippageBps).toBeCloseTo(0);
    });

    it('refuses 0.98 as an entry while accepting it as an exit', async () => {
      // The bounds are directional, not symmetric: paying 0.98 for a share risks
      // 0.98 to win 0.02, while selling at 0.98 is the good end of that trade.
      clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: [{ price: '0.98', size: '1000' }] });
      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-bound',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      })).rejects.toThrow('outside safe bounds');

      const exitClient = clientWithBook({ negRisk, bids: [{ price: '0.98', size: '1000' }] });
      await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit-high',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: 20
      });

      expect(exitClient.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.objectContaining({ side: OrderSide.SELL, minPrice: 0.98 })
      );
    });

    it('refuses 0.005 as an exit while accepting it as an entry', async () => {
      // Mirror of the case above. A 0.005 bid is close enough to worthless that
      // exiting there is usually a fat-finger or a dead book; entering there is a
      // cheap lottery ticket, which is a position the executor is allowed to take.
      clientWithBook({
        negRisk,
        tickSize: '0.001',
        bids: [{ price: '0.005', size: '10000' }]
      });
      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit-bound',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: 20
      })).rejects.toThrow('outside safe bounds');

      const entryClient = clientWithBook({
        negRisk,
        tickSize: '0.001',
        asks: [{ price: '0.005', size: '10000' }]
      });
      await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-low',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      });

      expect(entryClient.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.objectContaining({ side: OrderSide.BUY, maxPrice: 0.005 })
      );
    });

    it('requires an explicit share quantity to exit, and none to enter', async () => {
      // An entry can be sized down to whatever collateral is left, but an exit
      // names a real position. Inferring the quantity would sell something the
      // position may not hold.
      clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS });

      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-no-shares',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell'
      })).rejects.toThrow('require an exact requested share quantity');

      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-no-shares',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      })).resolves.toBeDefined();
    });
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-perps.ts <==
import {
  OrderSide,
  PerpsTimeInForce,
  type SecureClient,
  type PublicClient
} from '@polymarket/client';
import {
  upsertPerpsInstrument,
  upsertPerpsAccount,
  upsertPerpsPosition,
  recordPerpsOrder,
  getPerpsInstrumentBySymbol,
  type PerpsInstrumentRecord
} from '@swat/db';

export const POLYMARKET_PERPS_API_HOST = 'https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1';
export const POLYMARKET_PERPS_MAX_BUILDER_FEE_RATE = '0.001'; // 10 bps max per docs

export type PerpsSession = Awaited<ReturnType<SecureClient['openPerpsSession']>>;

export interface PerpsExecutionPlan {
  instrumentId: number;
  symbol: string;
  side: OrderSide;
  quantity: string;
  price: string;
  leverage: number;
  timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce;
  takeProfitPrice?: string;
  stopLossPrice?: string;
}

export interface PerpsRiskEvaluation {
  safe: boolean;
  marginRatio: number;
  inLiquidation: boolean;
  totalAccountValue: number;
  availableMargin: number;
  reason?: string;
}

/**
 * Open an authenticated Perps session with optional credentials/expiration.
 */
export async function openAttributedPerpsSession(
  client: SecureClient,
  builderAddress?: string
): Promise<PerpsSession> {
  const session = await client.openPerpsSession({
    label: builderAddress ? `swat-builder-${builderAddress.slice(0, 10)}` : 'swat-perps-session'
  });
  return session;
}

/**
 * Sync instruments catalogue from Polymarket to PostgreSQL.
 */
export async function syncPerpsInstrumentsCatalogue(
  client: PublicClient | SecureClient
): Promise<PerpsInstrumentRecord[]> {
  const instruments = await client.fetchPerpsInstruments();
  const records: PerpsInstrumentRecord[] = [];

  for (const inst of instruments) {
    const record = await upsertPerpsInstrument({
      instrumentId: inst.id,
      symbol: inst.symbol,
      category: inst.category ?? 'crypto',
      baseAsset: inst.baseAsset,
      quoteAsset: inst.quoteAsset ?? 'USD',
      priceDecimals: inst.priceDecimals,
      quantityDecimals: inst.quantityDecimals,
      maxLeverage: inst.maxLeverage ?? 10,
      minNotional: inst.minNotional ?? '1',
      maxMarketNotional: inst.maxMarketNotional ?? '100000',
      isActive: true
    });
    records.push(record);
  }

  return records;
}

/**
 * Evaluate portfolio health, margin utilization, and liquidation risk.
 */
export function evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio: {
  margin: {
    totalAccountValue: string;
    totalInitialMargin: string;
    totalMaintenanceMargin: string;
    totalPositionValue: string;
  };
  inLiquidation: boolean;
  withdrawable?: string;
}): PerpsRiskEvaluation {
  const accountValue = Number(portfolio.margin.totalAccountValue) || 0;
  const maintenanceMargin = Number(portfolio.margin.totalMaintenanceMargin) || 0;
  const availableMargin = Number(portfolio.withdrawable) || Math.max(0, accountValue - Number(portfolio.margin.totalInitialMargin));

  if (portfolio.inLiquidation) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio: 1,
      inLiquidation: true,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: 'Account is actively in liquidation'
    };
  }

  if (accountValue <= 0) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio: 1,
      inLiquidation: false,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: 'Total account value is depleted or zero'
    };
  }

  const marginRatio = maintenanceMargin / accountValue;

  // Emergency safety trigger: > 85% maintenance margin used
  if (marginRatio > 0.85) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio,
      inLiquidation: false,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: `Critical margin utilization: ${(marginRatio * 100).toFixed(1)}% of equity consumed by maintenance margin`
    };
  }

  return {
    safe: true,
    marginRatio,
    inLiquidation: false,
    totalAccountValue: accountValue,
    availableMargin
  };
}

/**
 * Execute a leveraged Perps copy trade order.
 */
export async function executePerpsOrder(params: {
  userId: string;
  session: PerpsSession;
  instrumentId: number;
  symbol: string;
  side: OrderSide;
  quantity: string;
  price: string;
  leverage?: number;
  timeInForce?: PerpsTimeInForce;
  takeProfitPrice?: string;
  stopLossPrice?: string;
  builderAddress?: string;
  clientOrderId?: string;
}) {
  // 1. Fetch live portfolio and check margin safety
  const portfolio = await params.session.fetchPortfolio();
  const risk = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
  if (!risk.safe) {
    throw new Error(`Perps Pre-Trade Risk Refusal: ${risk.reason}`);
  }

  // 2. Check available order margin
  const notionalUsd = Number(params.price) * Number(params.quantity);
  const leverage = params.leverage ?? 1;
  const requiredInitialMargin = notionalUsd / leverage;

  if (requiredInitialMargin > risk.availableMargin) {
    throw new Error(
      `Perps Margin Insufficient: order requires $${requiredInitialMargin.toFixed(2)} initial margin, but available margin is $${risk.availableMargin.toFixed(2)}`
    );
  }

  // 3. Build and place order on Polymarket Perps
  const orderPayload: any = {
    instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
    side: params.side,
    quantity: params.quantity,
    price: params.price,
    timeInForce: params.timeInForce ?? PerpsTimeInForce.IOC
  };

  if (params.takeProfitPrice) {
    orderPayload.takeProfit = { triggerPrice: params.takeProfitPrice };
  }
  if (params.stopLossPrice) {
    orderPayload.stopLoss = { triggerPrice: params.stopLossPrice };
  }

  const result = await params.session.placeOrder(orderPayload);
  const order = result.order;

  // 4. Record order execution to database
  const recordedOrder = await recordPerpsOrder({
    userId: params.userId,
    clientOrderId: params.clientOrderId ?? order.clientOrderId,
    venueOrderId: String(order.id),
    instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
    symbol: params.symbol,
    side: params.side === OrderSide.BUY ? 'BUY' : 'SELL',
    orderType: params.timeInForce === PerpsTimeInForce.GTC ? 'GTC' : 'IOC',
    price: order.price,
    quantity: order.quantity,
    filledQuantity: order.filledQuantity,
    status: order.status,
    builderAddress: params.builderAddress,
    builderFeeRate: POLYMARKET_PERPS_MAX_BUILDER_FEE_RATE,
    rawResponse: order as unknown as Record<string, unknown>
  });

  // 5. If filled, update position in database
  if (order.status === 'filled' || Number(order.filledQuantity) > 0) {
    await upsertPerpsPosition({
      userId: params.userId,
      instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
      symbol: params.symbol,
      side: params.side === OrderSide.BUY ? 'LONG' : 'SHORT',
      size: order.filledQuantity,
      entryPrice: order.price,
      leverage,
      initialMargin: requiredInitialMargin.toFixed(6),
      maintenanceMargin: (requiredInitialMargin * 0.5).toFixed(6),
      liquidationPrice: calculateApproxLiquidationPrice(
        params.side,
        Number(order.price),
        leverage
      ),
      unrealizedPnl: '0',
      takeProfitPrice: params.takeProfitPrice,
      stopLossPrice: params.stopLossPrice,
      status: 'open'
    });
  }

  // 6. Sync updated account margin state
  await upsertPerpsAccount({
    userId: params.userId,
    totalAccountValue: portfolio.margin.totalAccountValue,
    availableOrderMargin: String(risk.availableMargin),
    totalInitialMargin: portfolio.margin.totalInitialMargin,
    totalMaintenanceMargin: portfolio.margin.totalMaintenanceMargin,
    withdrawable: portfolio.withdrawable ?? '0',
    inLiquidation: portfolio.inLiquidation ?? false
  });

  return {
    orderId: order.id,
    status: order.status,
    filledQuantity: order.filledQuantity,
    price: order.price,
    recordedOrderId: recordedOrder.id
  };
}

/**
 * Approximate liquidation price calculation for leveraged perps.
 */
export function calculateApproxLiquidationPrice(
  side: OrderSide,
  entryPrice: number,
  leverage: number,
  maintenanceMarginRatio = 0.05
): string {
  if (leverage <= 1) return '0';
  // Long liquidation = entryPrice * (1 - 1/leverage + maintenanceMarginRatio)
  // Short liquidation = entryPrice * (1 + 1/leverage - maintenanceMarginRatio)
  if (side === OrderSide.BUY) {
    const liq = entryPrice * (1 - (1 / leverage) + maintenanceMarginRatio);
    return Math.max(0, liq).toFixed(2);
  } else {
    const liq = entryPrice * (1 + (1 / leverage) - maintenanceMarginRatio);
    return Math.max(0, liq).toFixed(2);
  }
}

import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';

// `polymarket.ts` constructs an ethers.Wallet at module scope, so this must be a
// well-formed 32-byte key. Deliberately a throwaway constant, never funded.
process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY = `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`;
process.env.POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE = 'EOA';
process.env.POLYMARKET_BUILDER_CODE = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;

// `polymarket.js` reaches @swat/db, which opens a pool at import time. Stubbed
// as `polymarket.test.ts` does â€” `planPolymarketBookOrder` is pure and touches
// no database.
vi.mock('@swat/db', () => ({
  recordConfirmedPolymarketTrade: vi.fn(),
  getPolymarketOutcomeContext: vi.fn(),
  getPolymarketMarket: vi.fn(),
  listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets: vi.fn(),
  claimPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  confirmPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  failPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims: vi.fn(),
  query: vi.fn(),
  pool: {}
}));

const { planPolymarketBookOrder, POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS } = await import('./polymarket.js');

/**
 * Venue precision parity (checklist S3-19 / audit G3-P10).
 *
 * Pins our rounding against the published contract in `trading/place-orders`:
 *
 *   | Tick size | Price decimals | Size decimals | Amount decimals |
 *   | 0.1       | 1              | 2             | 3               |
 *   | 0.01      | 2              | 2             | 4               |
 *   | 0.005     | 3              | 2             | 5               |
 *   | 0.0025    | 4              | 2             | 6               |
 *   | 0.001     | 3              | 2             | 5               |
 *   | 0.0001    | 4              | 2             | 6               |
 *
 * **Size decimals are 2 for every tick size**, which is why a single
 * `POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS` constant is correct rather than a lookup table.
 *
 * We deliberately do *not* implement the price-decimals column. Instead the book
 * walk rejects any price off the current tick grid, which is strictly stronger:
 * a price on a `0.0025` grid can never exceed 4 decimals, and off-grid prices
 * with the "right" decimal count (0.0026 under a 0.0025 tick) are still refused.
 * The equivalence is proven exhaustively by the last test in this file, so the
 * stronger check cannot silently drift from the documented one.
 */

const DOCS_PRECISION = [
  { tickSize: '0.1', priceDecimals: 1 },
  { tickSize: '0.01', priceDecimals: 2 },
  { tickSize: '0.005', priceDecimals: 3 },
  { tickSize: '0.0025', priceDecimals: 4 },
  { tickSize: '0.001', priceDecimals: 3 },
  { tickSize: '0.0001', priceDecimals: 4 }
] as const;

function book(params: {
  tickSize: string;
  asks?: Array<{ price: string; size: string }>;
  bids?: Array<{ price: string; size: string }>;
  minimumShares?: string;
}) {
  return {
    conditionId: `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`,
    tokenId: 'token-precision',
    timestamp: Date.now(),
    asks: params.asks ?? [],
    bids: params.bids ?? [],
    minOrderSize: params.minimumShares ?? '1',
    tickSize: params.tickSize,
    negRisk: false,
    hash: 'a'.repeat(40)
  } as Parameters<typeof planPolymarketBookOrder>[0];
}

function plan(bookInput: ReturnType<typeof book>, direction: 'buy' | 'sell', amount: number) {
  return planPolymarketBookOrder(bookInput, direction, amount, 5_000, Date.now());
}

describe('polymarket venue precision parity', () => {
  it.each(DOCS_PRECISION)(
    'accepts an on-grid price at tick $tickSize',
    ({ tickSize }) => {
      const tick = Number(tickSize);
      // Two ticks in, so the price is unambiguously on-grid and below 1.
      const price = (tick * 2).toFixed(10).replace(/0+$/, '').replace(/\.$/, '');
      // Depth is priced in USD (size Ã— price), so a fixed share count starves a
      // low-tick book: at tick 0.0001, 1000 shares at 0.0002 is $0.20. Size the
      // level to the notional under test instead.
      const size = String(Math.ceil(10 / (tick * 2)) * 2);
      const result = plan(
        book({ tickSize, asks: [{ price, size }] }),
        'buy',
        10
      );
      expect(result.estimatedShares).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  );

  it.each(DOCS_PRECISION)(
    'rejects an off-grid price at tick $tickSize even when its decimal count looks legal',
    ({ tickSize, priceDecimals }) => {
      // Half a tick off. This has at most `priceDecimals + 1` decimals, so a
      // decimals-only check would wave some of these through; the CLOB would
      // then reject the order at submission.
      const offGrid = (Number(tickSize) * 2.5).toFixed(priceDecimals + 1);
      expect(() =>
        plan(book({ tickSize, asks: [{ price: offGrid, size: '1000' }] }), 'buy', 10)
      ).toThrow(/tick-size grid/);
    }
  );

  it('rounds shares DOWN to 2 decimals, never up', () => {
    // Rounding up would sell shares the position does not hold, or buy more
    // than the sized notional pays for.
    const result = plan(
      book({ tickSize: '0.01', asks: [{ price: '0.03', size: '1000' }] }),
      'buy',
      1
    );
    // 1 / 0.03 = 33.333â€¦; floor at 2dp is 33.33.
    expect(result.estimatedShares).toBe(33.33);
    expect(POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS).toBe(2);
  });

  it('rejects an order that falls below the minimum after rounding', () => {
    // The rounding itself can push a marginal order under the venue floor, and
    // submitting it would be a guaranteed rejection.
    expect(() =>
      plan(
        book({ tickSize: '0.01', minimumShares: '5', asks: [{ price: '0.5', size: '1000' }] }),
        'buy',
        1
      )
    ).toThrow(/below the 5-share minimum/);
  });

  it('rejects a price at or above 1, which is not a valid outcome price', () => {
    expect(() =>
      plan(book({ tickSize: '0.01', asks: [{ price: '1', size: '10' }] }), 'buy', 1)
    ).toThrow(/invalid order-book price/);
  });

  it('proves tick-grid conformance implies the documented price decimals', () => {
    // The justification for not implementing the price-decimals column. If a
    // future tick size broke this, the stronger check would stop being a
    // superset and this test would catch it.
    for (const { tickSize, priceDecimals } of DOCS_PRECISION) {
      const tick = Number(tickSize);
      let maxDecimals = 0;
      for (let step = 1; step * tick < 1; step++) {
        const price = Number((step * tick).toFixed(10));
        const text = price.toString();
        const decimals = text.includes('.') ? text.split('.')[1]!.length : 0;
        if (decimals > maxDecimals) maxDecimals = decimals;
      }
      expect(
        maxDecimals,
        `at tick ${tickSize} exceeds ${priceDecimals} decimals`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(priceDecimals);
    }
  }, 15_000);
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-redemption.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import {
  runPolymarketRedemptionSweep,
  type PolymarketPositionExitClaimed,
  type PolymarketPositionExitPorts,
  type PolymarketRedemptionClient
} from './polymarket-redemption.js';
import type { RedeemableMarket, RedeemablePosition } from '@swat/db';

/**
 * The sweep after the `S4-M37` inversion: it is driven by the positions **we**
 * hold, not by the master's observed trades, and every position it is about to
 * exit is claimed position-scoped first so the `S4-M19` race has exactly one
 * winner per position rather than one per trigger.
 *
 * These fixtures therefore carry real condition ids and real outcome token ids.
 * `parsePolymarketOutcomePosition` refuses anything ambiguous â€” a `0xâ€¦` where a
 * token id belongs, an unnamed outcome â€” so a market fixture that would not
 * survive the fan-out cannot pass here either, which is the point.
 */

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets: vi.fn(),
  claimPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  confirmPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  failPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims: vi.fn()
}));

vi.mock('@swat/db', () => mocks);

const CONDITION = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;
const OTHER_CONDITION = `0x${'b'.repeat(64)}`;

function heldPosition(overrides: Partial<RedeemablePosition> = {}): RedeemablePosition {
  return {
    positionId: 'pos-1',
    conditionId: CONDITION,
    userId: null,
    targetAccount: 'polygon:0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
    tokenMint: 'polygon:1001',
    tokenId: '1001',
    outcome: 'Yes',
    outcomeIndex: 0,
    heldShares: '40',
    reservedSellShares: '0',
    ...overrides
  };
}

function market(overrides: Partial<RedeemableMarket> = {}): RedeemableMarket {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION,
    winningTokenId: '1001',
    resolvedOutcome: 'Yes',
    negRisk: false,
    positions: [heldPosition()],
    ...overrides
  };
}

function client(
  overrides?: Partial<PolymarketRedemptionClient>
): PolymarketRedemptionClient {
  return {
    redeemPositions: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
      wait: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ transactionHash: '0xabc', transactionId: 'tx-1' })
    }),
    ...overrides
  };
}

/**
 * Fakes for the three position-exit claim operations the sweep injects.
 *
 * Wired in every test that expects a redemption, because the sweep refuses to
 * redeem without them â€” see the fail-closed test below, which is the one place
 * they are deliberately left out.
 */
function exitPorts(
  overrides: Partial<PolymarketPositionExitPorts> = {}
): PolymarketPositionExitPorts & {
  claimPositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
  confirmPositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
  releasePositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
} {
  let issued = 0;
  return {
    claimPositionExit: vi.fn(async (input: {
      positionKey: string;
      exitTrigger: PolymarketPositionExitClaimed['exitTrigger'];
    }) => {
      issued += 1;
      return {
        id: `exit-${issued}`,
        positionKey: input.positionKey,
        exitTrigger: input.exitTrigger
      };
    }),
    confirmPositionExit: vi.fn(async () => {}),
    releasePositionExit: vi.fn(async () => {}),
    ...overrides
  } as never;
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  mocks.releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims.mockResolvedValue(0);
  mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([]);
  mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue({
    id: 'claim-1',
    conditionId: CONDITION,
    userId: null
  });
  mocks.confirmPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  mocks.failPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
});

describe('polymarket redemption sweep', () => {
  it('redeems a resolved market and records its transaction hash', async () => {
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ conditionId: CONDITION });
    expect(mocks.confirmPolymarketRedemption).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ id: 'claim-1', transactionHash: '0xabc', winningTokenId: '1001' })
    );
    // The position-scoped exit is confirmed too: the redemption transaction is the
    // evidence for the position, not merely for the condition.
    expect(ports.confirmPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      id: 'exit-1',
      transactionHash: '0xabc'
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 1, redeemed: 1, failed: 0, skipped: 0 });
  });

  it('claims the position before calling the venue, keyed on the outcome token', async () => {
    // `S4-M19`: one winner per position. The claim is position-keyed
    // (`polygon:<outcomeTokenId>`) and must be taken before the on-chain call,
    // because after it there is nothing left to stand down from.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(ports.claimPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      positionKey: 'polygon:1001',
      conditionId: CONDITION,
      outcomeTokenId: '1001',
      exitTrigger: 'redemption',
      userId: null
    });
    const claimOrder = ports.claimPositionExit.mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    const redeemOrder = vi.mocked(sdk.redeemPositions).mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    expect(claimOrder).toBeLessThan(redeemOrder);
  });

  it('never passes an amount â€” redemption covers both outcomes', async () => {
    // Per the docs, `redeemPositions` takes only a conditionId and redeems the
    // wallet's whole balance for both outcomes. Sending an amount would be a
    // contract violation, not merely redundant.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ winningTokenId: null, resolvedOutcome: 'No' })
    ]);
    const sdk = client();

    await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...exitPorts() });

    const call = vi.mocked(sdk.redeemPositions).mock.calls[0]![0];
    expect(Object.keys(call)).toEqual(['conditionId']);
  });

  it('does not branch on negRisk â€” the SDK selects the adapter', async () => {
    // Duplicating the CtfCollateralAdapter / NegRiskCtfCollateralAdapter choice
    // here would silently diverge if Polymarket changed the mapping. The market
    // is flagged neg-risk precisely so a branch would have somewhere to go.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ negRisk: true, positions: [heldPosition({ negRisk: true } as never)] })
    ]);
    const sdk = client();

    await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...exitPorts() });

    const call = vi.mocked(sdk.redeemPositions).mock.calls[0]![0] as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(call.negRisk).toBeUndefined();
    expect(call.adapter).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('redeems a condition we hold both outcomes of exactly once, without collapsing them', async () => {
    // `S4-M20`: holding YES and NO of one condition is a legitimate state, so the
    // fan-out must not throw â€” but the two rows must stay two positions. One
    // condition-scoped on-chain call, two position-scoped exits.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({
        positions: [
          heldPosition({ tokenId: '1001', tokenMint: 'polygon:1001', outcome: 'Yes', outcomeIndex: 0 }),
          heldPosition({
            positionId: 'pos-2',
            tokenId: '1002',
            tokenMint: 'polygon:1002',
            outcome: 'No',
            outcomeIndex: 1
          })
        ]
      })
    ]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(ports.claimPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(ports.claimPositionExit.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0].positionKey))
      .toEqual(['polygon:1001', 'polygon:1002']);
    expect(ports.confirmPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 1, redeemed: 1, failed: 0 });
  });

  it('refuses a market we hold no position in, without calling the venue', async () => {
    // `S4-M37`: redeem only what we hold. A market that reached the sweep with no
    // position of ours attached is a redemption that could not be attributed, so
    // it is refused before anything is claimed rather than redeemed on spec.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market({ positions: [] })]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(ports.claimPositionExit).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 1, redeemed: 0, failed: 1 });
  });

  it('refuses to redeem at all when the position-exit port is unwired', async () => {
    // Fail closed. Without a position-scoped claim both triggers can exit the same
    // position â€” a master selling moments before resolution is the ordinary case â€”
    // so an unwired sweep must strand the position rather than double-exit it.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();

    // The cast is the point of this test, not a shortcut: since 2026-09-01 the
    // ports are REQUIRED, so omitting them is a compile error and a caller can no
    // longer arrive here by accident. This deliberately reaches past the type to
    // prove the runtime fallback still fails closed for a caller that bypasses it
    // -- a hand-rolled dependency object, or JS with no types at all.
    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep(
      { client: sdk } as unknown as Parameters<typeof runPolymarketRedemptionSweep>[0]
    );

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ redeemed: 0, failed: 1 });
  });

  it('stands down on a position the mirrored sell already claimed', async () => {
    // Losing the race is the design, not an error: whichever trigger got there
    // first exits the position and the other one does nothing.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts({ claimPositionExit: vi.fn(async () => null) });

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ redeemed: 0, failed: 0, skipped: 1, lostRaces: 1 });
  });

  it('skips a market another sweep already claimed, without calling the venue', async () => {
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ winningTokenId: null })
    ]);
    mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue(null);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    // The exactly-once guard is the whole point: a lost claim must not redeem.
    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ skipped: 1, redeemed: 0 });
    // And the position claim we took on the way in is handed back, or the position
    // would be wedged by a claim for an exit that never happened.
    expect(ports.releasePositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      id: 'exit-1',
      reason: 'another sweep holds the condition claim'
    });
  });

  it('fails rather than confirms when the venue returns no transaction hash', async () => {
    // Confirming without evidence would put unverifiable money in the ledger.
    // Retrying is safe: redemption has no deadline and a second call on an
    // already-redeemed market moves no tokens.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ winningTokenId: null })
    ]);
    const sdk = client({
      redeemPositions: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
        wait: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ transactionHash: '', transactionId: null })
      })
    });
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(mocks.confirmPolymarketRedemption).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(mocks.failPolymarketRedemption).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ id: 'claim-1' })
    );
    expect(ports.confirmPositionExit).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(ports.releasePositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ id: 'exit-1' })
    );
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ redeemed: 0, failed: 1 });
  });

  it('releases the claim when the venue throws, so the market can be retried', async () => {
    // A missing collateral-adapter approval surfaces here. It must not wedge the
    // market permanently â€” nor the position, whose exit claim is released too.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ winningTokenId: null })
    ]);
    const sdk = client({
      redeemPositions: vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('ERC1155 not approved'))
    });
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(mocks.failPolymarketRedemption).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      id: 'claim-1',
      reason: 'ERC1155 not approved'
    });
    expect(ports.releasePositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      id: 'exit-1',
      reason: 'ERC1155 not approved'
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ redeemed: 0, failed: 1 });
  });

  it('releases stale claims before scanning, so a wedged market is eligible this pass', async () => {
    mocks.releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims.mockResolvedValue(2);
    const releaseStalePositionExits = vi.fn(async () => 1);

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({
      client: client(),
      ...exitPorts(),
      releaseStalePositionExits
    });

    expect(mocks.releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims).toHaveBeenCalled();
    // Both ledgers are recovered: a stuck position-exit claim would block the race
    // even after the condition-level redemption claim was released.
    expect(releaseStalePositionExits).toHaveBeenCalled();
    // Ordering matters: releasing after the scan would defer recovery a cycle.
    const releaseOrder = mocks.releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims.mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    const listOrder = mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    expect(releaseOrder).toBeLessThan(listOrder);
    expect(result.staleReleased).toBe(2);
  });

  it('continues past a failed market rather than abandoning the sweep', async () => {
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([
      market({ winningTokenId: null }),
      market({
        conditionId: OTHER_CONDITION,
        winningTokenId: null,
        positions: [heldPosition({
          positionId: 'pos-2',
          conditionId: OTHER_CONDITION,
          tokenId: '2001',
          tokenMint: 'polygon:2001'
        })]
      })
    ]);
    mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ id: 'claim-1', conditionId: CONDITION, userId: null })
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ id: 'claim-2', conditionId: OTHER_CONDITION, userId: null });
    const sdk = client({
      redeemPositions: vi
        .fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('venue 500'))
        .mockResolvedValueOnce({
          wait: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ transactionHash: '0xdef' })
        })
    });

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...exitPorts() });

    // One bad market must not strand every other resolved position.
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 2, redeemed: 1, failed: 1 });
  });

  it('does nothing when no market is redeemable', async () => {
    const sdk = client();
    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...exitPorts() });
    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 0, redeemed: 0 });
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-redemption.ts <==
import {
  claimPolymarketRedemption,
  confirmPolymarketRedemption,
  failPolymarketRedemption,
  listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets,
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims,
  type RedeemableMarket
} from '@swat/db';
import { UnrecoverableError } from 'bullmq';
import {
  mapPolymarketRedemptionToPositions,
  type PolymarketExitTrigger,
  type PolymarketRedeemedPosition
} from './polymarket-exit-race.js';

/**
 * Redemption sweep for resolved Polymarket positions (checklist S3-18), acting as
 * one of the two racing exit triggers (`S4-M19`) over positions we can prove we
 * hold (`S4-M37`).
 *
 * A resolved market stops accepting orders, so a winning position cannot be
 * sold â€” redemption is the only exit. Without this sweep a winning position
 * stays open in the ledger forever and its collateral is stranded.
 *
 * Verified against the live docs (`trading/positions/manage`), not memory:
 *
 *   * `redeemPositions({conditionId})` returns a transaction; `wait()` resolves
 *     to `{ transactionHash, transactionId }`.
 *   * It takes **no amount** and redeems the wallet's balances for *both*
 *     outcomes. Each winning token returns 1 pUSD, each losing token 0.
 *   * There is **no redemption deadline** â€” winning tokens stay redeemable
 *     indefinitely, so a market that fails today can always be retried.
 *   * The client selects the correct collateral adapter (`CtfCollateralAdapter`
 *     vs `NegRiskCtfCollateralAdapter`) from the condition id itself. This code
 *     therefore must **not** branch on `negRisk` â€” doing so would duplicate a
 *     decision the SDK already owns and would silently diverge if Polymarket
 *     changed the mapping.
 *
 * Prerequisite the docs state and this code cannot enforce: the collateral
 * adapter must be approved to transfer the wallet's outcome tokens. A missing
 * approval surfaces as a venue error and is recorded as a failed attempt rather
 * than retried blindly.
 *
 * **Two claims, deliberately.** `claimPolymarketRedemption` is keyed by
 * *condition* and guards the on-chain call, which is condition-scoped because
 * `redeemPositions` redeems both outcomes at once. `claimPositionExit` is keyed
 * by *position* and guards the race against the mirrored sell, which is
 * position-scoped because a condition holds two outcomes and a mirrored sell of
 * one must not suppress the exit of the other. Collapsing the two into a single
 * condition-level guard is precisely the mistake `S4-M20` forbids, which is why
 * `mapPolymarketRedemptionToPositions` asserts distinctness on the fan-out before
 * any claim is taken.
 *
 * **Why the position-exit ports are injected rather than imported.** The sweep
 * has to be drivable without Postgres â€” this repo's pure/DB split â€” and the race
 * is the part with the interesting decisions in it. Injecting the three claim
 * operations lets the whole race be tested against fakes.
 */

export interface RedemptionTransaction {
  wait(): Promise<{ transactionHash: string; transactionId?: string | null }>;
}

export interface PolymarketRedemptionClient {
  redeemPositions(input: { conditionId: string }): Promise<RedemptionTransaction>;
}

export interface PolymarketPositionExitClaimed {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly positionKey: string;
  readonly exitTrigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
}

export interface PolymarketPositionExitPorts {
  /**
   * Claim one position for the redemption trigger, or return null when the
   * mirrored sell already won the race for it.
   */
  readonly claimPositionExit: (input: {
    positionKey: string;
    conditionId: string;
    outcomeTokenId: string;
    exitTrigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
    userId: string | null;
  }) => Promise<PolymarketPositionExitClaimed | null>;
  readonly confirmPositionExit: (input: {
    id: string;
    transactionHash?: string | null;
  }) => Promise<void>;
  readonly releasePositionExit: (input: { id: string; reason: string }) => Promise<void>;
  readonly releaseStalePositionExits?: (olderThanMs: number) => Promise<number>;
}

/**
 * **The exit ports are required, and that is a deliberate change from `Partial`.**
 *
 * They were optional, defaulting to `unwiredPositionExitPort` -- which throws, so
 * the intent was fail-closed. It was not: the only production call site omitted
 * them for months, every market that mapped to a position was counted `failed`,
 * and `S4-M19`'s single-winner claim was **inert in production** while 705 tests
 * stayed green. Found 2026-09-01 while wiring `S4-M45`.
 *
 * A runtime throw cannot catch a *missing wire*, because the code path that would
 * throw is only reached in a deployment nobody tests. Requiring the fields moves
 * the same guarantee to compile time, where omitting one is a type error rather
 * than a silent degradation. `unwiredPositionExitPort` is kept for tests that
 * deliberately exercise the unwired path.
 */
export interface RedemptionSweepDependencies extends PolymarketPositionExitPorts {
  readonly client: PolymarketRedemptionClient;
  /** Logical account label. Null for the single-operator Stage 3 posture. */
  readonly userId?: string | null;
  readonly limit?: number;
  /** Claims older than this are released so a crashed sweep cannot wedge a market. */
  readonly staleClaimMs?: number;
  readonly log?: (message: string) => void;
}

export interface RedemptionSweepResult {
  readonly scanned: number;
  readonly redeemed: number;
  readonly failed: number;
  /** Markets another sweep already held. Not an error. */
  readonly skipped: number;
  readonly staleReleased: number;
  /** Positions the mirrored sell had already claimed. The race working, not an error. */
  readonly lostRaces: number;
}

const DEFAULT_STALE_CLAIM_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;

/**
 * The default when the caller has not wired the position-exit ports.
 *
 * Throws rather than degrading to "redeem anyway". Without a position-scoped
 * claim the two exit triggers can both fire on one position â€” a master selling
 * moments before resolution is the ordinary case â€” and the result is the position
 * being exited twice. Refusing costs a stranded position and a loud log; not
 * refusing costs a double exit.
 */
function unwiredPositionExitPort(): never {
  throw new UnrecoverableError(
    'Polymarket position-exit claim port is not wired; refusing to redeem, because '
    + 'without it the mirrored sell and the redemption can both exit the same position'
  );
}

export async function runPolymarketRedemptionSweep(
  dependencies: RedemptionSweepDependencies
): Promise<RedemptionSweepResult> {
  const log = dependencies.log ?? (() => {});
  const userId = dependencies.userId ?? null;
  const staleClaimMs = dependencies.staleClaimMs ?? DEFAULT_STALE_CLAIM_MS;
  const claimPositionExit = dependencies.claimPositionExit ?? unwiredPositionExitPort;
  const confirmPositionExit = dependencies.confirmPositionExit ?? unwiredPositionExitPort;
  const releasePositionExit = dependencies.releasePositionExit ?? unwiredPositionExitPort;

  // Recover claims stranded by a crash *before* scanning, so a wedged market
  // becomes eligible again in the same pass rather than the next one. Both
  // ledgers are recovered: a stuck position-exit claim would block the race even
  // after the condition-level redemption claim was released.
  const staleReleased = await releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims(staleClaimMs);
  if (staleReleased > 0) {
    log(`[polymarket-redemption] released ${staleReleased} stale claim(s)`);
  }
  if (dependencies.releaseStalePositionExits) {
    const staleExits = await dependencies.releaseStalePositionExits(staleClaimMs);
    if (staleExits > 0) {
      log(`[polymarket-redemption] released ${staleExits} stale position exit claim(s)`);
    }
  }

  const markets = await listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets({
    userId,
    limit: dependencies.limit ?? 50
  });
  let redeemed = 0;
  let failed = 0;
  let skipped = 0;
  let lostRaces = 0;

  for (const market of markets) {
    // The `S4-M20` fan-out guard, taken before anything is claimed. Going from a
    // condition back to "the position" is the exact step that would merge two
    // outcome rows into one, so it is refused here rather than corrected later.
    let positions: PolymarketRedeemedPosition[];
    try {
      positions = mapPolymarketRedemptionToPositions(market.conditionId, market.positions);
    } catch (error) {
      failed += 1;
      const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      log(`[polymarket-redemption] ${market.conditionId} rejected before claiming: ${reason}`);
      continue;
    }

    // One winner per position, not one per trigger. A position the mirrored sell
    // already claimed is skipped here even though the condition as a whole may
    // still be redeemable through its other outcome.
    const claims: PolymarketPositionExitClaimed[] = [];
    let claimError: string | null = null;
    for (const { position, positionKey } of positions) {
      try {
        const claim = await claimPositionExit({
          positionKey,
          conditionId: market.conditionId,
          outcomeTokenId: position.tokenId,
          exitTrigger: 'redemption',
          userId
        });
        if (claim) claims.push(claim);
        else {
          lostRaces += 1;
          log(
            `[polymarket-redemption] ${positionKey} is already exiting via the other `
            + 'trigger; the race has one winner per position'
          );
        }
      } catch (error) {
        claimError = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
        break;
      }
    }

    if (claimError) {
      await releaseClaims(claims, releasePositionExit, claimError);
      failed += 1;
      log(`[polymarket-redemption] ${market.conditionId} exit claim failed: ${claimError}`);
      continue;
    }
    if (claims.length === 0) {
      // Every outcome we hold in this condition is already exiting elsewhere.
      skipped += 1;
      continue;
    }

    const claim = await claimPolymarketRedemption({
      conditionId: market.conditionId,
      userId
    });
    if (!claim) {
      // Another sweep holds it. Normal under concurrency, not a failure.
      await releaseClaims(claims, releasePositionExit, 'another sweep holds the condition claim');
      skipped += 1;
      continue;
    }

    try {
      const transaction = await dependencies.client.redeemPositions({
        conditionId: market.conditionId
      });
      const outcome = await transaction.wait();

      if (!outcome?.transactionHash) {
        // Settled with no hash is not a provable redemption. Recording it as
        // confirmed would put unverifiable money in the ledger, so it is failed
        // and retried â€” safe because redemption has no deadline and a second
        // call on an already-redeemed market moves no tokens.
        await failPolymarketRedemption({
          id: claim.id,
          reason: 'redemption settled without a transaction hash'
        });
        await releaseClaims(
          claims,
          releasePositionExit,
          'redemption settled without a transaction hash'
        );
        failed += 1;
        continue;
      }

      await confirmPolymarketRedemption({
        id: claim.id,
        transactionHash: outcome.transactionHash,
        // The venue returns no per-redemption payout figure, and deriving one
        // from the pre-redemption balance would be a guess. Attribution reads
        // the on-chain transfer instead; recording an invented number here would
        // corrupt P&L permanently.
        redeemedCollateral: '0',
        winningTokenId: market.winningTokenId
      });
      // Confirmed per position, not per condition: the redemption transaction is
      // the evidence for every outcome row it settled, and each row is a separate
      // position whose exit is now finished.
      for (const positionClaim of claims) {
        await confirmPositionExit({
          id: positionClaim.id,
          transactionHash: outcome.transactionHash
        });
      }
      redeemed += 1;
      log(
        `[polymarket-redemption] redeemed ${market.conditionId} in ${outcome.transactionHash}`
      );
    } catch (error) {
      const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      await failPolymarketRedemption({ id: claim.id, reason });
      await releaseClaims(claims, releasePositionExit, reason);
      failed += 1;
      log(`[polymarket-redemption] ${market.conditionId} failed: ${reason}`);
    }
  }

  return { scanned: markets.length, redeemed, failed, skipped, staleReleased, lostRaces };
}

/**
 * Hand every position claim back so the race can be re-run.
 *
 * A claim left behind would block both triggers forever on a position that was
 * never actually exited â€” the single-shot guard turned into a permanent stop.
 * Release failures are swallowed on purpose: the caller is already handling the
 * error that got us here, and the stale-claim sweep recovers anything left.
 */
async function releaseClaims(
  claims: readonly PolymarketPositionExitClaimed[],
  release: (input: { id: string; reason: string }) => Promise<void>,
  reason: string
): Promise<void> {
  for (const claim of claims) {
    await release({ id: claim.id, reason }).catch(() => {});
  }
}

export type { RedeemableMarket };
