    throw new Error(`Polymarket order ${order.id} returned inconsistent matched quantities`);
  }
  return { originalSize, matchedSize };
}

async function fetchAssociatedTradeEvidence(
  client: PolymarketSecureClient,
  order: OpenOrder
): Promise<AssociatedTradeEvidence> {
  const evidence: AssociatedTradeEvidence = {
    confirmed: [],
    failedIds: [],
    pendingIds: [],
    pendingByState: new Map(),
    unknownIds: [],
    missingIds: []
  };
  const tradeIds = [...new Set(order.associateTrades.filter((id) => id.trim() !== ''))];
  for (const tradeId of tradeIds) {
    const page = await client.listAccountTrades({ id: tradeId }).firstPage();
    const trade = page.items.find((item) => item.id === tradeId);
    if (!trade) {
      evidence.missingIds.push(tradeId);
      continue;
    }
    const state = classifySettlementState(trade.status);
    if (state === 'confirmed') {
      evidence.confirmed.push(trade);
    } else if (state === 'failed') {
      evidence.failedIds.push(tradeId);
    } else if (state === null) {
      evidence.unknownIds.push(tradeId);
    } else {
      evidence.pendingIds.push(tradeId);
      const grouped = evidence.pendingByState.get(state) ?? [];
      grouped.push(tradeId);
      evidence.pendingByState.set(state, grouped);
    }
  }
  return evidence;
}

function summarizeConfirmedFills(order: OpenOrder, fills: ClobTrade[]): ConfirmedFillSummary {
  let shares = 0;
  let amountUsd = 0;
  let feesUsd = 0;
  let allFeesAvailable = true;
  let occurredAt = new Date(0);
  const venueTradeIds: string[] = [];
  const settlementTransactionHashes = new Set<string>();

  for (const fill of fills) {
    if (String(fill.tokenId) !== String(order.tokenId)) {
      throw new Error(`Polymarket fill ${fill.id} has a different token from order ${order.id}`);
    }

    const legs = fill.takerOrderId === order.id
      ? [{
          size: String(fill.size),
          price: String(fill.price),
          feeRateBps: fill.feeRateBps
        }]
      : fill.makerOrders
          .filter((makerOrder) => makerOrder.orderId === order.id)
          .map((makerOrder) => ({
            size: String(makerOrder.matchedAmount),
            price: String(makerOrder.price),
            feeRateBps: makerOrder.feeRateBps
          }));
    if (legs.length === 0) {
      throw new Error(`Polymarket fill ${fill.id} is not attributable to order ${order.id}`);
    }

    for (const leg of legs) {
      const legShares = nonNegativeDecimal(leg.size, `fill ${fill.id} size`);
      const price = nonNegativeDecimal(leg.price, `fill ${fill.id} price`);
      if (legShares <= 0 || price <= 0 || price >= 1) {
        throw new Error(`Polymarket fill ${fill.id} returned invalid execution quantities`);
      }
      shares += legShares;
      amountUsd += legShares * price;

      if (leg.feeRateBps === null || leg.feeRateBps === undefined || leg.feeRateBps === '') {
        allFeesAvailable = false;
      } else {
        const feeRateBps = nonNegativeDecimal(String(leg.feeRateBps), `fill ${fill.id} fee rate`);
        feesUsd += legShares * (feeRateBps / 10_000) * price * (1 - price);
      }
    }

    const transactionHash = fill.transactionHash.trim();
    if (!transactionHash) {
      throw new Error(`Polymarket confirmed fill ${fill.id} omitted its settlement transaction hash`);
    }
    venueTradeIds.push(fill.id);
    settlementTransactionHashes.add(transactionHash);

    const matchedAt = new Date(fill.matchedAt);
    if (Number.isNaN(matchedAt.getTime())) {
      throw new Error(`Polymarket fill ${fill.id} returned an invalid match timestamp`);
    }
    if (matchedAt > occurredAt) occurredAt = matchedAt;
  }

  if (shares <= 0 || amountUsd <= 0 || settlementTransactionHashes.size === 0) {
    throw new Error(`Polymarket order ${order.id} has incomplete confirmed fill evidence`);
  }
  return {
    shares,
    amountUsd,
    averagePrice: amountUsd / shares,
    feesUsd: allFeesAvailable ? feesUsd : null,
    venueTradeIds,
    settlementTransactionHashes: [...settlementTransactionHashes],
    occurredAt
  };
}

async function setPendingReconciliationState(
  row: PendingPolymarketTrade,
  venueStatus: string,
  reason: string | null,
  settlementStatus: SettlementState | null = null
): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `UPDATE trades
        SET venue_status = $2,
            error_message = $3,
            venue_settlement_status = $4
      WHERE id = $1
        AND status = 'pending_confirmation'`,
    [row.id, venueStatus, reason, settlementStatus]
  );
}

async function markAmbiguous(
  row: PendingPolymarketTrade,
  reason: string
): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome> {
  if (row.copy_execution_id) {
    await transitionCopyExecution({
      executionId: row.copy_execution_id,
      nextState: 'reconciliation_required',
      reason,
      nextReconciliationAt: new Date(Date.now() + 30_000)
    });
  }
  await setPendingReconciliationState(row, 'ambiguous', reason);
  return {
    tradeId: row.id,
    orderId: row.venue_order_id,
    status: 'ambiguous',
    reason
  };
}

async function finishWithoutFill(
  row: PendingPolymarketTrade,
  status: 'cancelled' | 'failed',
  venueStatus: string,
  reason: string
): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome> {
  if (row.copy_execution_id) {
    await transitionCopyExecution({
      executionId: row.copy_execution_id,
      nextState: status,
      reason
    });
  }
  await query<{ id: string }>(
    `WITH reconciled AS (
       UPDATE trades
          SET status = $2,
              venue_status = $3,
              venue_trade_ids = '[]'::jsonb,
              settlement_transaction_hashes = '[]'::jsonb,
              error_message = $4
        WHERE id = $1
          AND status = 'pending_confirmation'
      RETURNING id, signal_id
     ), released_signal AS (
       UPDATE signals
          SET status = 'pending'
        WHERE id IN (SELECT signal_id FROM reconciled WHERE signal_id IS NOT NULL)
          AND status = 'executing'
      RETURNING id
     )
     SELECT id FROM reconciled`,
    [row.id, status, venueStatus, reason]
  );
  return {
    tradeId: row.id,
    orderId: row.venue_order_id,
    status,
    reason
  };
}

async function finishConfirmedFill(
  row: PendingPolymarketTrade,
  order: OpenOrder,
  status: 'partial' | 'filled',
  summary: ConfirmedFillSummary
): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome> {
  if (row.copy_execution_id) {
    await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
      executionId: row.copy_execution_id,
      evidenceType: 'venue_fill',
      evidenceId: `order:${order.id}`,
      baseQuantity: summary.shares.toString(),
      quoteLeg: { amount: summary.amountUsd.toString(), currency: 'USD' },
      priceUsd: summary.averagePrice.toString(),
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      completesExecution: true,
      occurredAt: summary.occurredAt
    });
  }
  await query<{ id: string }>(
    `WITH reconciled AS (
       UPDATE trades
          SET status = $2,
              amount_sol = $3,
              amount_usd = $3,
              token_amount = $4,
              price_usd = $5,
              fee_usd = $6,
              signature = COALESCE($7, signature),
              venue_status = $8,
              venue_trade_ids = $9::jsonb,
              settlement_transaction_hashes = $10::jsonb,
              error_message = NULL,
              confirmed_at = COALESCE(confirmed_at, NOW())
        WHERE id = $1
          AND status = 'pending_confirmation'
      RETURNING id, signal_id
     ), executed_signal AS (
       UPDATE signals
          SET status = 'executed',
              executed_at = COALESCE(executed_at, NOW())
        WHERE id IN (SELECT signal_id FROM reconciled WHERE signal_id IS NOT NULL)
      RETURNING id
     )
     SELECT id FROM reconciled`,
    [
      row.id,
      status,
      summary.amountUsd,
      summary.shares,
      summary.averagePrice,
      summary.feesUsd,
      summary.settlementTransactionHashes[0] ?? null,
      order.status,
      JSON.stringify(summary.venueTradeIds),
      JSON.stringify(summary.settlementTransactionHashes)
    ]
  );
  return {
    tradeId: row.id,
    orderId: row.venue_order_id,
    status,
    shares: summary.shares,
    amountUsd: summary.amountUsd,
    averagePrice: summary.averagePrice,
    feesUsd: summary.feesUsd,
    venueTradeIds: summary.venueTradeIds,
    settlementTransactionHashes: summary.settlementTransactionHashes
  };
}

async function reconcilePendingPolymarketTrade(
  client: PolymarketSecureClient,
  row: PendingPolymarketTrade,
  now: number
): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome> {
  let order: OpenOrder;
  try {
    order = await client.fetchOrder({ orderId: row.venue_order_id });
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket order fetch is unresolved: ${message}`);
  }

  let quantities: { originalSize: number; matchedSize: number };
  try {
    quantities = validateFetchedOrder(row, order);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    return markAmbiguous(row, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
  }

  let orderState = classifyOrderState(order.status);
  if (orderState === 'ambiguous') {
    return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket order ${order.id} returned unknown status ${order.status}`);
  }

  let evidence: AssociatedTradeEvidence;
  try {
    evidence = await fetchAssociatedTradeEvidence(client, order);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket trade evidence lookup is unresolved: ${message}`);
  }

  if (evidence.unknownIds.length > 0) {
    // An undocumented settlement status is not evidence of anything. Treating
    // it as pending would leave the position parked indefinitely.
    return markAmbiguous(
      row,
      `Polymarket associated trades returned an unrecognised settlement status: ${evidence.unknownIds.join(', ')}`
    );
  }
  if (evidence.missingIds.length > 0) {
    const reason = `Polymarket associated trades are not yet readable: ${evidence.missingIds.join(', ')}`;
    if (orderState === 'pending') {
      await setPendingReconciliationState(row, order.status, reason);
      return { tradeId: row.id, orderId: order.id, status: 'pending_confirmation', reason };
    }
    return markAmbiguous(row, reason);
  }
  if (evidence.pendingIds.length > 0) {
    const settlement = weakestPendingSettlement(evidence);
    const reason =
      `Polymarket associated trades are not confirmed (settlement ${settlement ?? 'unknown'}): `
      + evidence.pendingIds.join(', ');
    await setPendingReconciliationState(row, order.status, reason, settlement);
    return { tradeId: row.id, orderId: order.id, status: 'pending_confirmation', reason };
  }

  let summary: ConfirmedFillSummary | null = null;
  if (evidence.confirmed.length > 0) {
    try {
      summary = summarizeConfirmedFills(order, evidence.confirmed);
    } catch (error: unknown) {
      return markAmbiguous(row, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
    }
    if (!quantitiesMatch(summary.shares, quantities.matchedSize)) {
      return markAmbiguous(
        row,
        `Polymarket order ${order.id} matched size does not equal its confirmed trade evidence`
      );
    }
  } else if (quantities.matchedSize > 0) {
    if (evidence.failedIds.length > 0 && orderState !== 'cancelled') {
      return finishWithoutFill(
        row,
        'failed',
        order.status,
        `Polymarket order ${order.id} has only failed settlement trades`
      );
    }
    return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket order ${order.id} reports fills without confirmed trades`);
  }

  if (orderState === 'pending') {
    const createdAt = Date.parse(order.createdAt);
    if (!Number.isFinite(createdAt)) {
      return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket order ${order.id} returned an invalid creation timestamp`);
    }
    if (!summary && now - createdAt > POLYMARKET_ORDER_TIMEOUT_MS) {
      try {
        const cancellation = interpretPolymarketCancellation(
          await client.cancelOrder({ orderId: order.id }),
          order.id
        );
        // One reading of the contract, shared with the exit-rung submitter
        // (`S4-M36`). Only an explicit listing in `canceled` retires the order;
        // a `not_canceled` entry â€” including "order already matched" â€” is not a
        // cancellation and must not be recorded as one.
        if (cancellation.kind === 'confirmed') {
          console.log(`[trade-executor] Cancelled timed out Polymarket order: ${order.id}`);
          return finishWithoutFill(
            row,
            'cancelled',
            'cancelled',
            'Polymarket order timed out without a confirmed fill'
          );
        }
        const detail = 'reason' in cancellation ? `: ${cancellation.reason}` : '';
        return markAmbiguous(
          row,
          `Polymarket did not confirm cancellation of timed out order ${order.id} `
          + `(${cancellation.kind})${detail}`
        );
      } catch (error: unknown) {
        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
        return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket cancellation is unresolved: ${message}`);
      }
    }
    const reason = summary
      ? `Polymarket order ${order.id} has confirmed fills but is not terminal`
      : `Polymarket order ${order.id} remains ${order.status}`;
    await setPendingReconciliationState(row, order.status, reason);
    return { tradeId: row.id, orderId: order.id, status: 'pending_confirmation', reason };
  }

  if (summary) {
    const status = quantitiesMatch(summary.shares, quantities.originalSize) ? 'filled' : 'partial';
    return finishConfirmedFill(row, order, status, summary);
  }
  if (orderState === 'cancelled') {
    return finishWithoutFill(
      row,
      'cancelled',
      order.status,
      `Polymarket order ${order.id} was cancelled without a confirmed fill`
    );
  }
  if (orderState === 'failed' || evidence.failedIds.length > 0) {
    return finishWithoutFill(
      row,
      'failed',
      order.status,
      `Polymarket order ${order.id} failed without a confirmed fill`
    );
  }
  return markAmbiguous(row, `Polymarket matched order ${order.id} has no confirmed fill evidence`);
}

/**
 * Reconcile the one pending trade belonging to a canonical execution.
 *
 * `pollPolymarketOrders` sweeps by `status = 'pending_confirmation'`, so an
 * execution whose trade row has already left that status is invisible to it.
 * The reconciliation coordinator claims from `copy_executions` instead and needs
 * to drive a single execution, so it comes through here.
 *
 * Returns null when there is nothing to reconcile â€” either live readiness is
 * absent or no matching pending trade row exists.
 */
export async function reconcilePolymarketExecution(
  executionId: string,
  now: number = Date.now()
): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome | null> {
  if (!liveReadiness.ready) return null;
  const client = requireSecureClobClient();
  const [row] = await query<PendingPolymarketTrade>(
    `SELECT id, signal_id, copy_execution_id, token_mint, direction,
            venue_order_id, submitted_at
       FROM trades
      WHERE copy_execution_id = $1
        AND chain = 'polygon'
        AND executor = 'polymarket-clob'
        AND venue_order_id IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY COALESCE(submitted_at, executed_at) DESC, id DESC
      LIMIT 1`,
    [executionId]
  );
  if (!row) return null;
  return reconcilePendingPolymarketTrade(client, row, now);
}

export async function pollPolymarketOrders(): Promise<PolymarketReconciliationOutcome[]> {
  if (!liveReadiness.ready) return [];
  const outcomes: PolymarketReconciliationOutcome[] = [];
  try {
    const client = requireSecureClobClient();
    const pending = await query<PendingPolymarketTrade>(
      `SELECT id, signal_id, copy_execution_id, token_mint, direction,
              venue_order_id, submitted_at
         FROM trades
        WHERE chain = 'polygon'
          AND execution_mode = 'live'
          AND executor = 'polymarket-clob'
          AND status = 'pending_confirmation'
          AND venue_order_id IS NOT NULL
        ORDER BY COALESCE(submitted_at, executed_at), id
        LIMIT 100`
    );
    const now = Date.now();
    for (const row of pending) {
      try {
        outcomes.push(await reconcilePendingPolymarketTrade(client, row, now));
      } catch (error: unknown) {
        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
        console.error(
          `[trade-executor] Polymarket order ${row.venue_order_id} reconciliation failed: ${message}`
        );
        outcomes.push({
          tradeId: row.id,
          orderId: row.venue_order_id,
          status: 'ambiguous',
          reason: message
        });
      }
    }
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    console.error(`[trade-executor] Polymarket order polling failed: ${message}`);
  }
  return outcomes;
}

/**
 * Drive the exit-escalation ladder for exits that reconciliation has already
 * declared unfilled (`S4-M17`).
 *
 * `pollPolymarketOrders` is where an exit *becomes* known-unfilled: a sell whose
 * FAK reconciled to `cancelled`, `failed`, or `partial` is a position the master
 * has left and the user still holds. Until this sweep existed the ladder in
 * `polymarket-exit-escalation.ts` had no caller, so that state was terminal â€”
 * the trade row said "cancelled" and nobody sold the shares.
 *
 * **Where it runs.** Inside the single guarded `reconcilePending` pass in
 * `index.ts`, at the tail, after the per-venue sweeps and the canonical
 * coordinator. Not on its own timer (audit finding `C1`): a second timer could
 * overlap this ladder with the reconciliation that classifies its own rungs. At
 * the tail because a ladder occupies the pass for as long as its rungs rest, and
 * the fast sweeps must not queue behind it.
 *
 * **What it deliberately does not do.** It does not resume a partly-walked
 * ladder. `escalatePolymarketExit` holds the rung index in a local, so one call
 * walks the whole ladder or terminates; there is no column to persist a rung in
 * and this module does not invent one. The consequences are stated on
 * `POLYMARKET_EXIT_ESCALATION_SWEEP_LIMIT` and
 * `resolvePolymarketExitReferencePrice`.
 */

/**
 * How many exits one pass will escalate.
 *
 * One by default, and low on purpose. A ladder rests each rung for its full
 * effective lifetime inside this call, so N candidates occupy the guarded
 * reconciliation pass for N ladders' worth of wall clock. Raising this trades
 * reconciliation latency for exit throughput, and the honest fix is not a bigger
 * number â€” it is persisted rung state so each pass can advance one rung and
 * return.
 */
export const POLYMARKET_EXIT_ESCALATION_SWEEP_LIMIT = 1;

/**
 * How far back a failed exit stays escalatable.
 *
 * An exit that failed an hour ago is not the same trade any more: the market has
 * moved, and re-offering a ladder measured from that reference is the staleness
 * `S4-M18` refuses on the entry path. Bounded rather than unbounded so a backlog
 * of historical failures cannot be replayed by a restart.
 */
export const POLYMARKET_EXIT_ESCALATION_MAX_AGE_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;

/**
 * Reconciliation outcomes that mean "the exit did not complete".
 *
 * `partial` is the case this sweep can actually act on. `cancelled` and `failed`
 * are listed because reconciliation does produce them, but per
 * `/resources/error-codes` a FAK that matches nothing is *rejected* at post time
 * ("no orders found to match with FAK order") rather than resting and being
 * cancelled â€” so a zero-fill exit often has no `venue_order_id` and never enters
 * this query at all, and when it does it has no persisted reference price. Both
 * are the same missing column; see `resolvePolymarketExitReferencePrice`.
 */
const POLYMARKET_UNFILLED_EXIT_STATUSES: readonly string[] = ['partial', 'cancelled', 'failed'];

export interface PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly copy_execution_id: string | null;
  readonly signal_id: string | null;
  readonly token_mint: string;
  readonly status: string;
  readonly venue_order_id: string;
  /** Average price of the confirmed portion, or null when nothing filled. */
  readonly price_usd: string | number | null;
  readonly token_amount: string | number | null;
  readonly target_amount_usd: string | number | null;
}

export type PolymarketExitReferenceResolution =
  | { readonly kind: 'reference'; readonly referencePrice: number }
  | { readonly kind: 'unavailable'; readonly reason: string };

/**
 * Find the price the failed attempt was bounded at, or say why it cannot be found.
 *
 * The ladder measures rungs down from the price the attempt that just failed
 * offered â€” see `polymarket-exit-escalation.ts` on why the master's raw fill is
 * the wrong reference. `triggerPolymarket` computes exactly that number
 * (`boundPrice`, returned as `mirrorBoundPrice`) and then drops it: `TradeInsert`
 * has no column for a signed protective bound, so it is not persisted.
 *
 * What survives is `price_usd`, which `finishConfirmedFill` sets to the average
 * price of the *confirmed* portion. For a sell that is a price the venue actually
 * paid us, so it is at or above the bound we signed â€” a valid, slightly
 * conservative reference. A sell that filled nothing has `price_usd = NULL`
 * (`insertTrade` only writes a price when there is a confirmed fill), and there
 * is nothing else on the row that means "the price we offered":
 * `target_amount_usd` is a requested notional and `token_amount` is null too, so
 * dividing them would invent a price rather than recover one.
 *
 * So this returns `unavailable` for the zero-fill case rather than guessing. That
 * is the honest half of `S4-M17`: the ladder runs for exits that partially
 * filled, and a zero-fill exit is reported as needing the missing column.
 */
export function resolvePolymarketExitReferencePrice(
  row: Pick<PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate, 'id' | 'status' | 'price_usd'>
): PolymarketExitReferenceResolution {
  if (row.price_usd === null || row.price_usd === undefined || row.price_usd === '') {
    return {
      kind: 'unavailable',
      reason:
        `trade ${row.id} reconciled to ${row.status} with no confirmed fill, so no price it `
        + 'offered was persisted; the escalation reference needs the signed mirror bound stored '
        + 'on the trade row'
    };
  }
  const referencePrice = Number(row.price_usd);
  if (!Number.isFinite(referencePrice) || referencePrice <= 0 || referencePrice >= 1) {
    return {
      kind: 'unavailable',
      reason: `trade ${row.id} persisted price ${row.price_usd} is not a valid outcome price`
    };
  }
  return { kind: 'reference', referencePrice };
}

/**
 * Exits this process has already walked a ladder for.
 *
 * Process-local, and that is a stated gap rather than a design: the terminal
 * alert exists so a human decides the next lever, and without a durable marker
 * the next pass sixty seconds later would start the same ladder from rung zero
 * and alert again. A restart forgets, and a second executor instance never knew.
 * The durable form is a claim on the trade row, which does not exist yet.
 */
const escalatedExitTradeIds = new Set<string>();

/** Test seam; also the reset an operator would want after fixing a market by hand. */
export function resetPolymarketExitEscalationMemoryForTesting(): void {
  escalatedExitTradeIds.clear();
}

export interface PolymarketExitEscalationSweepPorts {
  /** Publish the ladder's terminal alert. */
  readonly emitAlert: (
    alert: PolymarketExitAlert,
    candidate: PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate
  ) => Promise<void>;
  readonly loadCandidates?: () => Promise<PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate[]>;
  readonly fetchBook?: (tokenID: string) => Promise<OrderBook>;
  readonly fetchSellableShares?: (tokenID: string) => Promise<number>;
  readonly fetchMarketState?: (conditionId: string) => Promise<PolymarketMarketState>;
  readonly submitRungFor?: (
    tokenID: string
  ) => (rung: PolymarketExitLimitRung) => Promise<{ filledShares: number }>;
  readonly requestRedemption?: (
    redeem: PolymarketExitRedeem,
    candidate: PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate
  ) => Promise<void>;
  readonly escalate?: typeof escalatePolymarketExit;
  readonly limit?: number;
  readonly now?: () => number;
  readonly log?: (message: string) => void;
}

export interface PolymarketExitEscalationSweepResult {
  readonly scanned: number;
  readonly escalated: number;
  readonly completed: number;
  readonly alerted: number;
  readonly redeemed: number;
  readonly failed: number;
  readonly skipped: number;
  readonly skips: readonly { readonly tradeId: string; readonly reason: string }[];
  readonly outcomes: readonly {
    readonly tradeId: string;
    readonly outcome: PolymarketExitEscalationOutcome;
  }[];
}

/**
 * Highest bid on the book, or null when there is no usable bid.
 *
 * Computed as a maximum rather than read from `bids[0]` on purpose. The docs
 * contradict themselves on ordering: `/api-reference/market-data/get-order-book`
 * says bids are "sorted by price descending" (best first) while
 * `/market-data/prices-order-books` says "bids are ordered by ascending price...
 * so the best bid and ask are the last entries". A maximum is correct under
 * either, and indexing would silently price a rung against the *worst* bid under
 * one of them. Do not simplify this.
 */
function bestBidFromBook(book: OrderBook): number | null {
  const bids = book.bids ?? [];
  let best: number | null = null;
  for (const level of bids) {
    const price = Number(level.price);
    if (!Number.isFinite(price) || price <= 0 || price >= 1) continue;
    const size = Number(level.size);
    if (!Number.isFinite(size) || size <= 0) continue;
    if (best === null || price > best) best = price;
  }
  return best;
}

function resolvePolymarketMinimumExitPrice(): number {
  const value = Number(process.env.POLYMARKET_MIN_EXIT_PRICE ?? '0.01');
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0 || value >= 1) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError('POLYMARKET_MIN_EXIT_PRICE must be between 0 and 1 exclusive');
  }
  return value;
}

async function loadUnfilledPolymarketExits(
  now: number,
  limit: number
): Promise<PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate[]> {
  return query<PolymarketExitEscalationCandidate>(
    `SELECT id, copy_execution_id, signal_id, token_mint, status,
            venue_order_id, price_usd, token_amount, target_amount_usd
       FROM trades
      WHERE chain = 'polygon'
        AND executor = 'polymarket-clob'
        AND execution_mode = 'live'
        AND direction = 'sell'
        AND status = ANY($1::text[])
        AND venue_order_id IS NOT NULL
        AND COALESCE(confirmed_at, submitted_at, executed_at) > $2::timestamptz
      ORDER BY COALESCE(confirmed_at, submitted_at, executed_at) DESC, id DESC
      LIMIT $3`,
    [
      POLYMARKET_UNFILLED_EXIT_STATUSES,
      new Date(now - POLYMARKET_EXIT_ESCALATION_MAX_AGE_MS).toISOString(),
      Math.max(1, limit) * 10
    ]
  );
}

export async function runPolymarketExitEscalationSweep(
  ports: PolymarketExitEscalationSweepPorts
): Promise<PolymarketExitEscalationSweepResult> {
  const log = ports.log ?? (() => {});
  const now = ports.now ?? Date.now;
  const limit = ports.limit ?? POLYMARKET_EXIT_ESCALATION_SWEEP_LIMIT;
  const escalate = ports.escalate ?? escalatePolymarketExit;
  const skips: { tradeId: string; reason: string }[] = [];
  const outcomes: { tradeId: string; outcome: PolymarketExitEscalationOutcome }[] = [];
  let escalated = 0;
  let completed = 0;
  let alerted = 0;
  let redeemed = 0;
  let failed = 0;

  // Escalating means signing and posting a real sell. There is nothing to
  // escalate in paper mode, and the live-readiness gate is the same one
  // `runPolymarketRedemptionSweep` sits behind.
  if (!liveReadiness.ready) {
    return {
      scanned: 0, escalated: 0, completed: 0, alerted: 0, redeemed: 0, failed: 0,
      skipped: 0, skips: [], outcomes: []
    };
  }

  const minimumExitPrice = resolvePolymarketMinimumExitPrice();
  const loadCandidates = ports.loadCandidates
    ?? (() => loadUnfilledPolymarketExits(now(), limit));
  const candidates = await loadCandidates();

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (escalated + alerted + redeemed + completed >= limit) break;
    if (escalatedExitTradeIds.has(candidate.id)) {
      skips.push({
        tradeId: candidate.id,
        reason: 'this process has already walked a ladder for this exit'
      });
      continue;
    }
    const reference = resolvePolymarketExitReferencePrice(candidate);
    if (reference.kind === 'unavailable') {
      skips.push({ tradeId: candidate.id, reason: reference.reason });
      log(`[polymarket-exit] skipping ${candidate.id}: ${reference.reason}`);
      continue;
    }

    const tokenID = unprefixedPolygonToken(candidate.token_mint);
    const fetchBook = ports.fetchBook
      ?? ((id: string) => requireSecureClobClient().fetchOrderBook({ tokenId: id }));
    const fetchSellableShares = ports.fetchSellableShares
      ?? ((id: string) => getPolymarketAvailableBalance(id, 'sell'));
    const fetchMarketState = ports.fetchMarketState
      ?? ((conditionId: string) => fetchPolymarketMarketState(conditionId));

    // The ladder's own `observe` port. Every value it needs is readable from the
    // venue, which is why no schema is required to know *what is left*: the
    // conditional-token balance is the remaining position, and the book carries
    // the tick grid and the venue minimum. Only the reference price is not.
    const observe = async () => {
      const book = await fetchBook(tokenID);
      const [remainingShares, market] = await Promise.all([
        fetchSellableShares(tokenID),
        fetchMarketState(String(book.conditionId))
      ]);
      return {
        remainingShares,
        bestBid: bestBidFromBook(book),
        // Passed through as a share count, matching `planPolymarketBookOrder`.
        // The docs disagree with themselves about the unit â€”
        // `/trading/place-orders` calls `min_order_size` "the minimum number of
        // shares the CLOB accepts" while `/market-data/market-details` calls the
        // same field a "minimum USDC notional" â€” so this deliberately keeps the
        // interpretation the rest of this module already uses rather than
        // introducing a second one.
        minimumShares: Number(book.minOrderSize),
        tickSize: Number(book.tickSize),
        market
      };
    };

    // Claimed before the first rung, not after the ladder: a throw partway
    // through has already sold shares, and re-running from rung zero would sell
    // them twice.
    escalatedExitTradeIds.add(candidate.id);
    try {
      const observed = await observe();
      const outcome = await escalate(
        {
          ...observed,
          referencePrice: reference.referencePrice,
          minimumExitPrice
        },
        {
          submitRung: ports.submitRungFor
            ? ports.submitRungFor(tokenID)
            : createPolymarketExitRungSubmitter({ tokenID, log }),
          observe,
          emitAlert: (alert) => ports.emitAlert(alert, candidate),
          requestRedemption: async (redeem) => {
            // No queue and no table: `runPolymarketRedemptionSweep` scans for
            // resolved positions on this same guarded pass, so the correct
            // action is to stop escalating and let it find this one. Inventing a
            // redemption request row would duplicate the sweep's own source of
            // truth.
            if (ports.requestRedemption) await ports.requestRedemption(redeem, candidate);
            else log(`[polymarket-exit] ${candidate.id} defers to the redemption sweep: ${redeem.reason}`);
          },
          now,
          log
        }
      );
      outcomes.push({ tradeId: candidate.id, outcome });
      escalated += outcome.rungsSubmitted > 0 ? 1 : 0;
      if (outcome.terminal === 'alert') alerted += 1;
      else if (outcome.terminal === 'redeem') redeemed += 1;
      else completed += 1;
      log(
        `[polymarket-exit] trade ${candidate.id} ladder ended ${outcome.terminal} after `
        + `${outcome.rungsSubmitted} rungs, filled ${outcome.filledShares}, `
        + `remaining ${outcome.remainingShares}`
      );
    } catch (error: unknown) {
      failed += 1;
      const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      log(`[polymarket-exit] trade ${candidate.id} escalation failed: ${message}`);
    }
  }

  return {
    scanned: candidates.length,
    escalated,
    completed,
    alerted,
    redeemed,
    failed,
    skipped: skips.length,
    skips,
    outcomes
  };
}

    submissionType: 'transaction',
    submissionId: 'sig-1',
    nextReconciliationAt: null,
    reconciliationClaimId: 'claim-1',
    reconciliationAttempts: 1,
    maxReconciliationAttempts: 5,
    sourcePositionBeforeQuantity: null,
    sourceSellFraction: null,
    ...overrides
  } as CopyExecutionRecord;
}

function deps(
  overrides: Partial<ReconciliationCoordinatorDependencies> = {}
): ReconciliationCoordinatorDependencies {
  return {
    claim: vi.fn(async () => []),
    release: vi.fn(async () => true),
    reconcilers: {},
    escalate: vi.fn(async () => undefined),
    now: () => NOW,
    ...overrides
  };
}

describe('runReconciliationCoordinator', () => {
  it('claims a default batch size', async () => {
    const claim = vi.fn(async () => []);
    await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({ claim }));
    expect(claim).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ limit: 20 });
  });

  it('releases with no retry when the venue resolves the execution', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    const reconcile: VenueReconciler = vi.fn(async () => ({ status: 'resolved' as const }));
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution()],
      release,
      reconcilers: { solana: reconcile }
    }));

    expect(result.resolved).toBe(1);
    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      executionId: 'exec-1',
      claimId: 'claim-1',
      retryAt: null
    });
  });

  it('reschedules a pending execution using the venue retry time', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    const retryAt = new Date('2026-08-01T12:05:00.000Z');
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution()],
      release,
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'pending', retryAt }) }
    }));

    expect(result.pending).toBe(1);
    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      executionId: 'exec-1',
      claimId: 'claim-1',
      retryAt
    });
  });

  it('falls back to the configured backoff when the venue gives no retry time', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution()],
      release,
      retryDelayMs: 30_000,
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'pending' }) }
    }));

    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      executionId: 'exec-1',
      claimId: 'claim-1',
      retryAt: new Date('2026-08-01T12:00:30.000Z')
    });
  });

  // The whole point of the coordinator is to unstick executions, so it must
  // never be the thing that leaves a claim held.
  it('releases the claim when the venue handler throws', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution()],
      release,
      reconcilers: {
        solana: async () => {
          throw new Error('rpc timeout');
        }
      }
    }));

    expect(result.unresolved).toBe(1);
    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('does not throw when releasing the claim itself fails', async () => {
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution()],
      release: async () => {
        throw new Error('db down');
      },
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'resolved' }) }
    }));

    expect(result.resolved).toBe(1);
  });

  // A chain whose runtime is absent must be handed back untouched, not resolved
  // by a process that has no way to observe the venue.
  it('reschedules a chain with no handler instead of resolving it', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    const escalate = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution({ chain: 'polygon' })],
      release,
      escalate,
      retryDelayMs: 60_000,
      reconcilers: {}
    }));

    expect(result.unsupported).toBe(1);
    expect(result.resolved).toBe(0);
    expect(escalate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      executionId: 'exec-1',
      claimId: 'claim-1',
      retryAt: new Date('2026-08-01T12:01:00.000Z')
    });
  });

  it('escalates once an unresolved execution has burned its last attempt', async () => {
    const escalate = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution({
        reconciliationAttempts: 5,
        maxReconciliationAttempts: 5
      })],
      escalate,
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'unresolved', reason: 'no evidence' }) }
    }));

    expect(result.exhausted).toBe(1);
    expect(escalate).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ id: 'exec-1' }),
      '[operator] no evidence'
    );
  });

  it('does not escalate while attempts remain', async () => {
    const escalate = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution({ reconciliationAttempts: 2, maxReconciliationAttempts: 5 })],
      escalate,
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'unresolved', reason: 'no evidence' }) }
    }));

    expect(result.unresolved).toBe(1);
    expect(result.exhausted).toBe(0);
    expect(escalate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('still releases the claim when escalation fails', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution({
        reconciliationAttempts: 5,
        maxReconciliationAttempts: 5
      })],
      release,
      escalate: async () => {
        throw new Error('redis down');
      },
      reconcilers: { solana: async () => ({ status: 'unresolved', reason: 'no evidence' }) }
    }));

    expect(release).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  // Without a claim id this process cannot prove it owns the row, so acting on
  // it risks a concurrent executor reconciling the same execution.
  it('skips a claimed row that carries no claim id', async () => {
    const release = vi.fn(async () => true);
    const reconcile = vi.fn(async () => ({ status: 'resolved' as const }));
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [execution({ reconciliationClaimId: null })],
      release,
      reconcilers: { solana: reconcile }
    }));

    expect(result.unresolved).toBe(1);
    expect(reconcile).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(release).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('routes each claimed execution to the handler for its own chain', async () => {
    const seen: Chain[] = [];
    const handler = (chain: Chain): VenueReconciler => async () => {
      seen.push(chain);
      return { status: 'resolved' };
    };
    const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({
      claim: async () => [
        execution({ id: 'a', chain: 'solana' }),
        execution({ id: 'b', chain: 'polygon' }),
        execution({ id: 'c', chain: 'robinhood-chain' })
      ],
      reconcilers: {
        solana: handler('solana'),
        polygon: handler('polygon'),
        'robinhood-chain': handler('robinhood-chain')
      }
    }));

    expect(result.claimed).toBe(3);
    expect(result.resolved).toBe(3);
    expect(seen).toEqual(['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain']);
  });

  it('passes an explicit batch size through to the DB claim', async () => {
    const claim = vi.fn(async () => []);
    await runReconciliationCoordinator(deps({ claim, limit: 5 }));
    expect(claim).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ limit: 5 });
  });
});

describe('createEvmReceiptReconciler', () => {
  it('fails the execution when the transaction reverted', async () => {
    const fail = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const reconcile = createEvmReceiptReconciler({
      probe: async () => ({ status: 'reverted' }),
      fail
    });

    const outcome = await reconcile(execution({ chain: 'robinhood-chain', submissionId: '0xdead' }));

    expect(outcome).toEqual({ status: 'resolved' });
    expect(fail).toHaveBeenCalledWith('exec-1', expect.stringContaining('0xdead'));
  });

  it('stays pending while the receipt is unavailable', async () => {
    const fail = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const reconcile = createEvmReceiptReconciler({ probe: async () => null, fail });

    expect(await reconcile(execution({ chain: 'robinhood-chain' }))).toEqual({ status: 'pending' });
    expect(fail).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  // Booking a fill needs the submitted amounts, which live in the pending store
  // that is by definition gone here. Guessing would corrupt the ledger.
  it('reports unresolved for a success it cannot quantify', async () => {
    const fail = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const reconcile = createEvmReceiptReconciler({
      probe: async () => ({ status: 'success' }),
      fail
    });

    const outcome = await reconcile(execution({ chain: 'robinhood-chain' }));

    expect(outcome.status).toBe('unresolved');
    expect(fail).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('never fails an execution whose submission identity is unknown', async () => {
    const probe = vi.fn(async () => null);
    const fail = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
    const reconcile = createEvmReceiptReconciler({ probe, fail });

    const outcome = await reconcile(execution({ chain: 'robinhood-chain', submissionId: null }));

    expect(outcome.status).toBe('unresolved');
    expect(probe).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(fail).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/reconciliation-coordinator.ts <==
import type { CopyExecutionRecord } from '@swat/db';
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';

/**
 * Canonical reconciliation coordinator.
 *
 * Each venue already sweeps its own pending store (Trojan and Robinhood in
 * Redis, Polymarket from the `trades` table). Those sweeps are the fast path
 * and stay authoritative. This coordinator is the backstop for the case they
 * structurally cannot cover: a `copy_executions` row that is still ambiguous
 * while its venue-side pending entry is gone â€” expired from Redis, dropped by a
 * flush, or written by a process that died before the store was updated. Such a
 * row is invisible to every venue sweeper and would otherwise stay
 * `reconciliation_required` forever.
 *
 * It claims work through `claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation`, which is a
 * `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim, so several executor processes can run this
 * concurrently without double-reconciling a row.
 *
 * Every dependency is injected so the coordinator can be tested without
 * Postgres, Redis, or a venue client.
 */

export const RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT = 'operator';

/** What a venue handler concluded about one canonical execution. */
export type VenueReconciliationOutcome =
  /** Terminal: the handler resolved the execution and already persisted it. */
  | { status: 'resolved' }
  /** Not terminal yet â€” still genuinely in flight. Retry after `retryAt`. */
  | { status: 'pending'; retryAt?: Date }
  /**
   * The handler could not reach a conclusion (venue unreachable, evidence
   * missing). Distinct from 'pending': this is a failure to observe, not an
   * observation of incompleteness.
   */
  | { status: 'unresolved'; reason: string };

export type VenueReconciler = (
  execution: CopyExecutionRecord
) => Promise<VenueReconciliationOutcome>;

export type ReconciliationCoordinatorDependencies = {
  claim: (input: { limit: number }) => Promise<CopyExecutionRecord[]>;
  release: (input: {
    executionId: string;
    claimId: string;
    retryAt?: Date | null;
  }) => Promise<boolean>;
  /** Venue handler per chain. A chain with no handler is left claimed-and-released. */
  reconcilers: Partial<Record<Chain, VenueReconciler>>;
  /** Escalation for an execution that has burned every reconciliation attempt. */
  escalate: (execution: CopyExecutionRecord, reason: string) => Promise<unknown>;
  /**
   * Operator account this sweep runs on behalf of (Standing Rule 2). It is a
   * logical label, not a filter: `copy_executions.target_account` holds a
   * chain-prefixed wallet address, so matching it against `'operator'` would
   * claim nothing. Executions are scoped by chain instead, via the handler set.
   */
  account?: string;
  limit?: number;
  /** Backoff before the next sweep may retry an unresolved execution. */
  retryDelayMs?: number;
  now?: () => Date;
};

export type ReconciliationCoordinatorResult = {
  claimed: number;
  resolved: number;
  pending: number;
  unresolved: number;
  exhausted: number;
  unsupported: number;
};

/**
 * Claim a batch of ambiguous canonical executions and route each to its venue.
 *
 * The claim must always be released, whatever the handler does â€” a claim left
 * held blocks that execution until `staleClaimBefore` expires it, which is the
 * exact stuck state this coordinator exists to prevent. So every path below
 * releases, and release failures are logged rather than thrown.
 */
export async function runReconciliationCoordinator(
  dependencies: ReconciliationCoordinatorDependencies
): Promise<ReconciliationCoordinatorResult> {
  const account = dependencies.account ?? RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT;
  const limit = dependencies.limit ?? 20;
  const retryDelayMs = dependencies.retryDelayMs ?? 60_000;
  const now = dependencies.now ?? (() => new Date());

  const result: ReconciliationCoordinatorResult = {
    claimed: 0,
    resolved: 0,
    pending: 0,
    unresolved: 0,
    exhausted: 0,
    unsupported: 0
  };

  const claimed = await dependencies.claim({ limit });
  result.claimed = claimed.length;

  for (const execution of claimed) {
    const claimId = execution.reconciliationClaimId;
    if (!claimId) {
      // The claim returned a row without its own claim id, so this process
      // cannot prove ownership and must not act on it.
      console.error(
        `[trade-executor] reconciliation claim for ${execution.id} has no claim id`
      );
      result.unresolved++;
      continue;
    }

    const reconcile = dependencies.reconcilers[execution.chain];
    if (!reconcile) {
      result.unsupported++;
      await releaseClaim(dependencies, execution, claimId, new Date(now().getTime() + retryDelayMs));
      continue;
    }

    let outcome: VenueReconciliationOutcome;
    try {
      outcome = await reconcile(execution);
    } catch (error) {
      const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
      console.error(
        `[trade-executor] ${execution.chain} reconciliation threw for ${execution.id}`,
        error
      );
      outcome = { status: 'unresolved', reason };
    }

    if (outcome.status === 'resolved') {
      result.resolved++;
      // A resolved execution is terminal, so no retry is scheduled. The DB
      // helper nulls next_reconciliation_at for terminal states anyway.
      await releaseClaim(dependencies, execution, claimId, null);
      continue;
    }

    const retryAt = outcome.status === 'pending' && outcome.retryAt
      ? outcome.retryAt
      : new Date(now().getTime() + retryDelayMs);

    if (outcome.status === 'pending') {
      result.pending++;
      await releaseClaim(dependencies, execution, claimId, retryAt);
      continue;
    }

    result.unresolved++;

    // The claim already incremented reconciliation_attempts, so this row has
    // now consumed its last attempt and no future claim will pick it up. It
    // needs a human before it is silently abandoned.
    if (execution.reconciliationAttempts >= execution.maxReconciliationAttempts) {
      result.exhausted++;
      await dependencies
        .escalate(execution, `[${account}] ${outcome.reason}`)
        .catch((error) => {
          console.error(
            `[trade-executor] reconciliation escalation failed for ${execution.id}`,
            error
          );
        });
    }

    await releaseClaim(dependencies, execution, claimId, retryAt);
  }

  return result;
}

async function releaseClaim(
  dependencies: ReconciliationCoordinatorDependencies,
  execution: CopyExecutionRecord,
  claimId: string,
  retryAt: Date | null
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await dependencies.release({ executionId: execution.id, claimId, retryAt });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(
      `[trade-executor] failed to release reconciliation claim for ${execution.id}`,
      error
    );
  }
}

==> apps/trade-executor/src/reconciliation-venues.ts <==
import { transitionCopyExecution, type CopyExecutionRecord } from '@swat/db';
import type { VenueReconciler, VenueReconciliationOutcome } from './reconciliation-coordinator.js';
import type { PolymarketReconciliationStatus } from './polymarket.js';

/**
 * Venue handlers for the canonical reconciliation coordinator.
 *
 * These are deliberately narrower than the per-venue sweeps. A sweep reads its
 * own pending store, which carries the submission metadata needed to decode a
 * fill (account, token, submitted amounts). The coordinator claims from
 * `copy_executions` precisely because that store entry is *gone*, so a handler
 * here cannot reconstruct fill quantities.
 *
 * What it can do is settle the cases that need no quantities:
 *   - the venue says the submission failed  -> terminate as `failed`, with evidence
 *   - the venue says it is still in flight  -> `pending`, retry later
 *   - the venue says it succeeded           -> `unresolved`, because booking a
 *     fill without quantities would corrupt the position ledger
 *
 * `unresolved` is not a dead end: the coordinator escalates once an execution
 * exhausts its reconciliation attempts, which turns a silently stuck row into a
 * human-visible one. Never guess a quantity to avoid an escalation.
 */

type FailExecution = (executionId: string, reason: string) => Promise<unknown>;

const failExecution: FailExecution = (executionId, reason) =>
  transitionCopyExecution({ executionId, nextState: 'failed', reason });

function requireSubmissionId(execution: CopyExecutionRecord): string | null {
  return execution.submissionId && execution.submissionId.trim().length > 0
    ? execution.submissionId
    : null;
}

/**
 * A claimed execution with no submission identity cannot be probed at all.
 *
 * This is not the same as "nothing was submitted": the row may have been written
 * by a process that died between the network call and the identity write, so the
 * order could well be live at the venue. Marking it failed would be a guess, so
 * it is reported unresolved and left for escalation.
 */
function missingSubmissionIdentity(execution: CopyExecutionRecord): VenueReconciliationOutcome {
  return {
    status: 'unresolved',
    reason:
      `${execution.chain} execution ${execution.id} has no submission identity, `
      + 'so the venue cannot be probed'
  };
}

export type EvmReceiptProbe = (
  transactionHash: string
) => Promise<{ status: 'success' | 'reverted' } | null>;

/**
 * Robinhood Chain and any other EVM venue: probe the transaction receipt.
 *
 * A null receipt means the node has not seen the transaction yet, which is
 * indistinguishable from "dropped from the mempool" without the original
 * blockhash window â€” so it stays `pending` and the attempt counter is what
 * eventually forces a human look.
 */
export function createEvmReceiptReconciler(input: {
  probe: EvmReceiptProbe;
  fail?: FailExecution;
}): VenueReconciler {
  const fail = input.fail ?? failExecution;
  return async (execution) => {
    const hash = requireSubmissionId(execution);
    if (!hash) return missingSubmissionIdentity(execution);

    const receipt = await input.probe(hash);
    if (!receipt) {
      return { status: 'pending' };
    }
    if (receipt.status === 'reverted') {
      await fail(execution.id, `transaction ${hash} reverted on ${execution.chain}`);
      return { status: 'resolved' };
    }
    return {
      status: 'unresolved',
      reason:
        `transaction ${hash} succeeded but its pending record is gone, `
        + 'so the filled quantities cannot be decoded'
    };
  };
}

export type SolanaConfirmationProbe = (
  transactionIdentity: string
) => Promise<{ status: 'confirmed' | 'failed' | 'not-found' }>;

/** Solana via Trojan: probe the signature's confirmation status. */
export function createSolanaConfirmationReconciler(input: {
  probe: SolanaConfirmationProbe;
  fail?: FailExecution;
}): VenueReconciler {
  const fail = input.fail ?? failExecution;
  return async (execution) => {
    const signature = requireSubmissionId(execution);
    if (!signature) return missingSubmissionIdentity(execution);

    const confirmation = await input.probe(signature);
    if (confirmation.status === 'failed') {
      await fail(execution.id, `Solana transaction ${signature} failed on chain`);
      return { status: 'resolved' };
    }
    if (confirmation.status === 'not-found') {
      return { status: 'pending' };
    }
    return {
      status: 'unresolved',
      reason:
        `Solana transaction ${signature} confirmed but its pending record is gone, `
        + 'so the swapped quantities cannot be decoded'
    };
  };
}

export type PolymarketExecutionProbe = (
  executionId: string
) => Promise<{ status: PolymarketReconciliationStatus; reason?: string } | null>;

/**
 * Polygon via Polymarket, the one venue that needs no store entry.
 *
 * Its pending state lives in the `trades` table alongside `copy_execution_id`,
 * and its reconcile path persists canonical state itself â€” so unlike the other
 * venues it can settle a fill outright, and this handler only has to translate
 * the outcome.
 */
export function createPolymarketReconciler(input: {
  probe: PolymarketExecutionProbe;
}): VenueReconciler {
  return async (execution) => {
    const outcome = await input.probe(execution.id);
    if (!outcome) {
      return {
        status: 'unresolved',
        reason: `no Polymarket order row is joined to execution ${execution.id}`
      };
    }
    switch (outcome.status) {
      case 'filled':
      case 'partial':
      case 'cancelled':
      case 'failed':
        return { status: 'resolved' };
      case 'pending_confirmation':
        return { status: 'pending' };
      default:
        return {
          status: 'unresolved',
          reason: outcome.reason ?? `Polymarket reported ${outcome.status}`
        };
    }
  };
}

==> apps/trade-executor/src/robinhood-base-spend.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { describeRobinhoodBaseSpend } from './robinhood.js';

const WETH = '0x0bd7d308f8e1639fab988df18a8011f41eacad73' as const;
const USDG = '0x5fc5360d0400a0fd4f2af552add042d716f1d168' as const;

/**
 * S4-M41 â€” the base-asset spend must carry its unit.
 *
 * The defect these pin: `amountEth` is a `number` whose name hardcodes a currency
 * only one of the two base-asset modes uses. In `erc20` mode it was `0`, and the
 * ledger wrote that zero as a real ETH cost â€” a fabricated value on a trade that
 * spent a stablecoin. A zero cost basis makes an ordinary position look like an
 * infinite-return winner, and one that can never trip a stop-loss.
 *
 * Every case here exercises `erc20` mode explicitly. A suite that only covered
 * `native-weth` would pass with the bug fully intact, which is why it survived.
 */
describe('describeRobinhoodBaseSpend (S4-M41)', () => {
  describe('native-weth mode', () => {
    it('reports the ETH amount that went in on a buy', () => {
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'native-weth',
        baseAsset: WETH,
        direction: 'buy',
        actualAmountIn: 100000000000000000n, // 0.1 ETH
        actualAmountOut: 4900n
      });
      expect(spend).toEqual({ kind: 'native', currency: 'ETH', amount: 0.1 });
    });

    it('reports the ETH amount that came out on a sell', () => {
      // The base asset is what we spend on a buy and what we receive on a sell,
      // so the leg flips with direction. Reading the wrong one silently reports a
      // token quantity as an ETH amount.
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'native-weth',
        baseAsset: WETH,
        direction: 'sell',
        actualAmountIn: 4900n,
        actualAmountOut: 250000000000000000n // 0.25 ETH
      });
      expect(spend).toEqual({ kind: 'native', currency: 'ETH', amount: 0.25 });
    });
  });

  describe('erc20 mode â€” where the fabricated zero used to be', () => {
    it('never reports ETH, and never reports zero, for a USDG spend', () => {
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'erc20',
        baseAsset: USDG,
        direction: 'buy',
        actualAmountIn: 250_000_000n, // 250 USDG at 6 decimals
        actualAmountOut: 4900n
      });
      expect(spend).toEqual({ kind: 'erc20', token: USDG, baseUnits: 250_000_000n });
      // The two assertions that are the whole point of the item.
      expect(spend).not.toMatchObject({ currency: 'ETH' });
      expect(spend).not.toMatchObject({ amount: 0 });
    });

    it('carries base units rather than a decimal, because USDG has 6 decimals not 18', () => {
      // 250 USDG is 250_000_000 base units. Formatting it with the ether helpers
      // would yield 2.5e-10 â€” understated by 10^12, which presents as "no funds"
      // rather than as a scaling bug. Keeping the integer makes the amount exact
      // and forces the caller that knows the decimals to do the conversion.
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'erc20',
        baseAsset: USDG,
        direction: 'buy',
        actualAmountIn: 250_000_000n,
        actualAmountOut: 1n
      });
      expect(spend.kind).toBe('erc20');
      if (spend.kind !== 'erc20') throw new Error('unreachable');
      expect(spend.baseUnits).toBe(250_000_000n);
      expect(typeof spend.baseUnits).toBe('bigint');
    });

    it('flips to the output leg on a sell, same as native mode', () => {
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'erc20',
        baseAsset: USDG,
        direction: 'sell',
        actualAmountIn: 4900n,
        actualAmountOut: 310_500_000n
      });
      expect(spend).toEqual({ kind: 'erc20', token: USDG, baseUnits: 310_500_000n });
    });

    it('reports the configured base asset, not a hardcoded one', () => {
      // A caller could reasonably assume erc20 mode means USDG. It means whatever
      // ROBINHOOD_BASE_ASSET is set to, and the ledger needs to know which token
      // the number is denominated in to ever convert it.
      const other = '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111' as const;
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'erc20',
        baseAsset: other,
        direction: 'buy',
        actualAmountIn: 1n,
        actualAmountOut: 1n
      });
      expect(spend).toMatchObject({ kind: 'erc20', token: other });
    });

    it('reports a genuinely zero spend as zero base units, not as unassessed', () => {
      // Distinguishing the two directions of the unknown-vs-zero rule: a real zero
      // is representable and must not be laundered into "unknown" either.
      const spend = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
        baseAssetMode: 'erc20',
        baseAsset: USDG,
        direction: 'buy',
        actualAmountIn: 0n,
        actualAmountOut: 0n
      });
      expect(spend).toEqual({ kind: 'erc20', token: USDG, baseUnits: 0n });
    });
  });

  it('the two modes never produce the same shape, so a consumer must branch', () => {
    // Structural point: `kind` is what forces the ledger call site to decide what
    // to record. The old `number` let it skip that decision and write a zero.
    const native = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
      baseAssetMode: 'native-weth', baseAsset: WETH, direction: 'buy',
      actualAmountIn: 1n, actualAmountOut: 1n
    });
    const erc20 = describeRobinhoodBaseSpend({
      baseAssetMode: 'erc20', baseAsset: USDG, direction: 'buy',
      actualAmountIn: 1n, actualAmountOut: 1n
    });
    expect(native.kind).not.toBe(erc20.kind);
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/robinhood-nonce.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  NonceContentionError,
  executeRobinhoodOrder,
  type EvmNonceLock,
  type RobinhoodExecutionAdapter,
  type RobinhoodExecutionConfig,
  type RobinhoodPendingStore
} from './robinhood.js';

/**
 * S4-M12 â€” nonce serialisation.
 *
 * These cases deliberately use an order that fails validation immediately (an
 * empty `clientOrderId`), so the adapter and pending store are never reached.
 * What is under test is the *locking* around the order, not the order itself â€”
 * which has 28 cases of its own in `robinhood.test.ts`. Keeping the body trivial
 * means a failure here can only be the lock.
 */
function minimalOrder(account: `0x${string}`, nonceLock: EvmNonceLock) {
  return {
    order: {
      clientOrderId: '', // rejected before any adapter or store call
      token: '0x5000000000000000000000000000000000000005' as `0x${string}`,
      direction: 'buy' as const,
      amountInBaseUnits: 1n,
      slippageBps: 100
    },
    config: { maxSlippageBps: 500 } as unknown as RobinhoodExecutionConfig,
    account,
    adapter: {} as unknown as RobinhoodExecutionAdapter,
    pendingStore: {} as unknown as RobinhoodPendingStore,
    safetyAssessment: vi.fn(),
    requireReadiness: false as const,
    nonceLock
  };
}

const ACCOUNT_A = '0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' as const;
const ACCOUNT_B = '0xbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb' as const;

/** A lock whose critical section blocks until the returned latch is released. */
function latchedLock() {
  const entered: string[] = [];
  const released: string[] = [];
  const gates = new Map<string, () => void>();
  const lock: EvmNonceLock = async (account, run) => {
    entered.push(account);
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => gates.set(account, resolve));
    const result = await run();
    released.push(account);
    return { acquired: true, result };
  };
  return {
    lock,
    entered,
    released,
    open: (account: string) => gates.get(account)?.()
  };
}

describe('cross-process nonce lock (S4-M12)', () => {
  it('refuses to run the order when the lock is held elsewhere', async () => {
    // The whole point of the item: a second process must not read the same
    // pending nonce. Running the body anyway is the bug.
    const run = vi.fn();
    const contended: EvmNonceLock = async () => {
      run();
      return { acquired: false };
    };

    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, contended)))
      .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NonceContentionError);
  });

  it('names the account in the contention error', async () => {
    const contended: EvmNonceLock = async () => ({ acquired: false });
    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, contended)))
      .rejects.toThrow(new RegExp(ACCOUNT_A));
  });

  it('is NOT an UnrecoverableError, so the queue retries rather than burying the job', async () => {
    // An UnrecoverableError would drop the mirror permanently for a millisecond
    // overlap. BullMQ must be free to retry once the holder has submitted.
    const contended: EvmNonceLock = async () => ({ acquired: false });
    const error = await executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, contended)).catch((e) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(NonceContentionError);
    expect(error.constructor.name).toBe('NonceContentionError');
  });

  it('runs the order inside the lock, not around it', async () => {
    const calls: string[] = [];
    const lock: EvmNonceLock = async (account, run) => {
      calls.push('lock-acquired');
      const result = await run();
      calls.push('lock-released');
      return { acquired: true, result };
    };

    await executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, lock));
    expect(calls).toEqual(['lock-acquired', 'lock-released']);
  });

  it('passes the signing account through as the lock key', async () => {
    const seen: string[] = [];
    const lock: EvmNonceLock = async (account, run) => {
      seen.push(account);
      return { acquired: true, result: await run() };
    };
    await executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_B, lock));
    expect(seen).toEqual([ACCOUNT_B]);
  });
});

describe('in-process submission chain is per account (S4-M12)', () => {
  it('lets two different accounts hold their locks concurrently', async () => {
    // Before S4-M12 this chain was global: user B's mirror waited on user A's,
    // on a venue where being late is the entire risk. Both must be in flight.
    const { lock, entered, open } = latchedLock();

    const a = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, lock));
    const b = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_B, lock));
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(entered).toHaveLength(2));

    expect(entered).toEqual([ACCOUNT_A, ACCOUNT_B]);
    open(ACCOUNT_A);
    open(ACCOUNT_B);
    await Promise.all([a, b]);
  });

  it('serialises two orders for the SAME account', async () => {
    // This is the ordering nonce allocation actually requires: one account's
    // second order must not read the pending nonce until the first has submitted.
    const { lock, entered, open } = latchedLock();

    const first = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, lock));
    const second = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, lock));
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(entered).toHaveLength(1));

    // The second call has not entered the lock at all while the first is inside.
    expect(entered).toEqual([ACCOUNT_A]);

    open(ACCOUNT_A);
    await first;
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(entered).toHaveLength(2));
    open(ACCOUNT_A);
    await second;
  });

  it('releases the chain when an order throws, so one failure cannot wedge an account', async () => {
    const boom: EvmNonceLock = async () => { throw new Error('lock backend down'); };
    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, boom)))
      .rejects.toThrow('lock backend down');

    // A wedged chain would hang here instead of resolving.
    const ok: EvmNonceLock = async (_a, run) => ({ acquired: true, result: await run() });
    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, ok)))
      .resolves.toMatchObject({ status: 'skipped' });
  });

  it('releases the chain after a contention throw too', async () => {
    const contended: EvmNonceLock = async () => ({ acquired: false });
    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, contended)))
      .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NonceContentionError);

    const ok: EvmNonceLock = async (_a, run) => ({ acquired: true, result: await run() });
    await expect(executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, ok)))
      .resolves.toMatchObject({ status: 'skipped' });
  });

  it('treats differently-cased forms of one account as one chain', async () => {
    // viem returns checksummed addresses; other paths lowercase them. Two
    // spellings must not both proceed for the same account.
    const { lock, entered, open } = latchedLock();
    const upper = ACCOUNT_A.toUpperCase().replace('0X', '0x') as `0x${string}`;

    const first = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(ACCOUNT_A, lock));
    const second = executeRobinhoodOrder(minimalOrder(upper, lock));
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(entered).toHaveLength(1));
    expect(entered).toHaveLength(1);

    open(ACCOUNT_A);
    await first;
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(entered).toHaveLength(2));
    open(upper);
    await second;
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/robinhood-runtime.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  createRedisRobinhoodPendingStore,
  createRobinhoodSafetyAssessment
} from './robinhood-runtime.js';
import { evaluateRobinhoodSafety, type PendingRobinhoodSubmission } from './robinhood.js';
import { encodeRuntimeValue } from './runtime-codec.js';

function redisHash() {
  const values = new Map<string, Map<string, string>>();
  return {
    async hget(key: string, field: string) {
      return values.get(key)?.get(field) ?? null;
    },
    async hgetall(key: string) {
      return Object.fromEntries(values.get(key) ?? []);
    },
    async hset(key: string, field: string, value: string) {
      const hash = values.get(key) ?? new Map<string, string>();
      hash.set(field, value);
      values.set(key, hash);
      return 1;
    }
  };
}

const pending: PendingRobinhoodSubmission = {
  clientOrderId: 'signal-rh-1',
  stage: 'swap',
  hash: '0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa',
  submittedAt: new Date('2026-07-26T10:00:00.000Z'),
  expiresAt: new Date('2026-07-26T10:10:00.000Z'),
  direction: 'buy',
  account: '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
  token: '0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222',
  baseAsset: '0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333',
  amountIn: '100000000000000000',
  quotedAmountOut: '5000',
  feeTier: 3000,
  slippageBps: 300
};

describe('Redis Robinhood pending store', () => {
  it('restores unresolved submissions and terminal receipt truth after a process restart', async () => {
    const redis = redisHash();
    const firstProcess = createRedisRobinhoodPendingStore(redis);
    await firstProcess.save(pending);

    const restartedProcess = createRedisRobinhoodPendingStore(redis);
    await expect(restartedProcess.findUnresolved('signal-rh-1')).resolves.toEqual(pending);

    await restartedProcess.resolve('signal-rh-1', {
      status: 'filled',
      clientOrderId: 'signal-rh-1',
      signature: pending.hash!,
      transactionHash: pending.hash!,
      amountEth: 0.1,
      // native-weth mode, so baseSpend mirrors amountEth (S4-M41).
      baseSpend: { kind: 'native' as const, currency: 'ETH' as const, amount: 0.1 },
      actualAmountIn: 100000000000000000n,
      actualAmountOut: 4900n,
      quotedAmountOut: 5000n,
      feeTier: 3000,
      gasUsed: 100000n,
      latencyMs: 1200
    });

    await expect(firstProcess.findUnresolved('signal-rh-1')).resolves.toBeNull();
    await expect(firstProcess.findResolution('signal-rh-1')).resolves.toMatchObject({
      status: 'filled',
      actualAmountOut: 4900n
    });
  });

  it('decodes legacy v1 records with an unknown fee tier as null', async () => {
    const redis = redisHash();
    const key = 'test:pending:robinhood:v1';
    const legacyPending = {
      clientOrderId: pending.clientOrderId,
      stage: pending.stage,
      hash: pending.hash,
      submittedAt: pending.submittedAt,
      expiresAt: pending.expiresAt,
      direction: pending.direction,
      account: pending.account,
      token: pending.token,
      baseAsset: pending.baseAsset,
      amountIn: pending.amountIn,
      quotedAmountOut: pending.quotedAmountOut,
      slippageBps: pending.slippageBps
    };
    await redis.hset(key, pending.clientOrderId, encodeRuntimeValue({
      state: 'pending',
      pending: legacyPending
    }));
    await redis.hset(key, 'legacy-resolution', encodeRuntimeValue({
      state: 'resolved',
      resolution: {
        status: 'filled',
        clientOrderId: 'legacy-resolution',
        signature: pending.hash,
        transactionHash: pending.hash,
        amountEth: 0.1,
        actualAmountIn: 100000000000000000n,
        actualAmountOut: 4900n,
        quotedAmountOut: 5000n,
        gasUsed: 100000n,
        latencyMs: 1200
      }
    }));

    const store = createRedisRobinhoodPendingStore(redis, key);
    await expect(store.findUnresolved(pending.clientOrderId)).resolves.toEqual({
      ...pending,
      feeTier: null
    });
    await expect(store.listUnresolved()).resolves.toEqual([{ ...pending, feeTier: null }]);
    await expect(store.findResolution('legacy-resolution')).resolves.toMatchObject({
      status: 'filled',
      feeTier: null
    });
  });
});

describe('Robinhood runtime safety assessment', () => {
  it('uses a real reverse quote and fails closed when liquidity evidence is unavailable', async () => {
    const quote = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(90n);
    const assess = createRobinhoodSafetyAssessment({
