==> apps/web/lib/api.ts <==
/**
 * The single browser -> API client (checklist S6-3).
 *
 * Replaces thirteen copies of a hand-rolled `fetch` that each sent
 * `X-Api-Key: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY`. check-public-secrets:allow-mention
 * -- naming the deleted variable here is documentation, not usage. It is inlined into
 * the client bundle by Next.js at build time, so the shared operator key was
 * shipped to every visitor and granted full control-plane access. It is deleted,
 * not rotated: a rotated secret in a public bundle is still public.
 *
 * What replaces it is the session cookie the API already issues, plus the
 * double-submit CSRF token it already expects. See `apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`
 * -- the backend half has existed since Stage 1; only the frontend was behind.
 *
 * The module is split deliberately. Everything that makes a decision is a pure
 * function over explicit inputs, and only `apiFetch` touches the network or the
 * DOM. That is what lets this file be tested at all: `apps/web` has no jsdom, so
 * a client that read `document.cookie` directly would be untestable here.
 */

/** Name of the CSRF cookie the API sets. Deliberately JS-readable. */
export const CSRF_COOKIE = 'swat_csrf';
/** Header the API compares the cookie against. */
export const CSRF_HEADER = 'x-csrf-token';
/** Session cookie name. httpOnly, so JS can never read it -- only send it. */
export const SESSION_COOKIE = 'swat_session';

/** Methods that change state and therefore need the CSRF header. */
const MUTATING_METHODS = new Set(['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE']);

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
    readonly body?: unknown
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'ApiError';
  }

  /** True when the caller should be sent to /login rather than shown an error. */
  get isUnauthenticated(): boolean {
    return this.status === 401;
  }

  /** True when the caller is signed in but lacks the role for this surface. */
  get isForbidden(): boolean {
    return this.status === 403;
  }
}

/**
 * Extracts the CSRF token from a raw cookie string.
 *
 * Pure, and takes the string rather than reading `document.cookie`, so it is
 * testable without a DOM. Returns null rather than an empty string when absent
 * so "no token" cannot be mistaken for "a token that happens to be blank" --
 * the second would produce a request that fails CSRF for a reason the caller
 * cannot distinguish from being logged out.
 */
export function parseCsrfToken(cookieString: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!cookieString) return null;
  for (const part of cookieString.split(';')) {
    const separator = part.indexOf('=');
    if (separator < 0) continue;
    if (part.slice(0, separator).trim() !== CSRF_COOKIE) continue;
    const value = part.slice(separator + 1).trim();
    return value.length > 0 ? decodeURIComponent(value) : null;
  }
  return null;
}

export interface BuildRequestOptions {
  readonly method?: string;
  /** Already-serialised body, or undefined for a bodyless request. */
  readonly body?: string;
  /** From `parseCsrfToken`. Null when the user has no session. */
  readonly csrfToken?: string | null;
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
}

/**
 * Builds the `RequestInit` for an API call.
 *
 * Pure. Three invariants, each of which had a bug behind it:
 *
 *   1. `credentials: 'include'` on every request. The API and the web app are
 *      different origins in every deployment we have (:3000 and :3001), so
 *      without this the browser sends no cookie and every call is anonymous.
 *   2. The CSRF header only on mutating methods, and only when a token exists.
 *      Sending it on a GET is harmless but sending a stale one is misleading,
 *      and the API only checks it where it matters.
 *   3. No API key, ever. There is deliberately no parameter for one -- the way
 *      this stays fixed is that the shape cannot express the old behaviour.
 */
export function buildApiRequestInit(options: BuildRequestOptions = {}): RequestInit {
  const method = (options.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase();
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {};

  if (options.body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
  if (MUTATING_METHODS.has(method) && options.csrfToken) {
    headers[CSRF_HEADER] = options.csrfToken;
  }

  const init: RequestInit = {
    method,
    credentials: 'include',
    headers
  };
  if (options.body !== undefined) init.body = options.body;
  if (options.signal) init.signal = options.signal;
  return init;
}

/**
 * Resolves the API origin.
 *
 * `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is a URL, not a secret, so it stays a `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
 * variable -- the rule being enforced is "no secrets in the bundle", not "no
 * public config". Absent that, derive the host from how the page is being
 * viewed so the dashboard works from another device on the LAN as well as from
 * localhost. Takes the location rather than reading `window` so it is testable.
 */
export function resolveApiBase(
  location?: { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null,
  configured: string | undefined = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
): string {
  if (configured) return configured.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  if (location) return `${location.protocol}//${location.hostname}:3001`;
  return 'http://localhost:3001';
}

export function resolveLpApiBase(
  location?: { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null,
  configured: string | undefined = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_LP_API_URL
): string {
  if (configured) return configured.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  if (location) return `${location.protocol}//${location.hostname}:3010`;
  return 'http://localhost:3010';
}

function currentLocation(): { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  return { protocol: window.location.protocol, hostname: window.location.hostname };
}

function currentCookies(): string | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.cookie;
}

export interface ApiFetchOptions {
  readonly method?: string;
  /** Serialised for you. Pass the object, not a string. */
  readonly body?: unknown;
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
  /**
   * Called instead of throwing when the API says 401. Injected so the redirect
   * is the caller's decision -- a background poll should not yank the user out
   * of a form they are filling in.
   */
  readonly onUnauthenticated?: () => void;
}

/**
 * Calls the API with the session cookie and CSRF header attached.
 *
 * Throws `ApiError` on any non-2xx so a caller cannot accidentally treat an
 * error body as data -- the previous call sites all did `if (!res.ok) throw new
 * Error('Failed to fetch X')`, which discarded the status and made a 401 and a
 * 500 indistinguishable in the UI.
 */
export async function apiFetch<T = unknown>(path: string, options: ApiFetchOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
  const base = resolveApiBase(currentLocation());
  const init = buildApiRequestInit({
    method: options.method,
    body: options.body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.body),
    csrfToken: parseCsrfToken(currentCookies()),
    signal: options.signal
  });

  const response = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, init);

  if (response.status === 401 && options.onUnauthenticated) {
    options.onUnauthenticated();
    throw new ApiError(401, 'Not signed in');
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    let body: unknown;
    let message = `${response.status} ${response.statusText}`;
    try {
      body = await response.json();
      const described = (body as { message?: unknown; error?: unknown } | null)?.message
        ?? (body as { error?: unknown } | null)?.error;
      if (typeof described === 'string' && described.length > 0) message = described;
    } catch {
      // A non-JSON error body is normal (a proxy 502, an HTML error page). The
      // status is the part that matters and we already have it.
    }
    throw new ApiError(response.status, message, body);
  }

  if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

/** Convenience wrappers so call sites read as intent rather than as plumbing. */
export const api = {
  get: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'GET' }),
  post: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'POST', body }),
  put: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PUT', body }),
  patch: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PATCH', body }),
  delete: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' })
};

export async function lpApiFetch<T = unknown>(path: string, options: ApiFetchOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
  const base = resolveLpApiBase(currentLocation());
  const init = buildApiRequestInit({
    method: options.method,
    body: options.body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.body),
    csrfToken: parseCsrfToken(currentCookies()),
    signal: options.signal
  });

  const response = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, init);

  if (response.status === 401 && options.onUnauthenticated) {
    options.onUnauthenticated();
    throw new ApiError(401, 'Not signed in');
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    let body: unknown;
    let message = `${response.status} ${response.statusText}`;
    try {
      body = await response.json();
      const described = (body as { message?: unknown; error?: unknown } | null)?.message
        ?? (body as { error?: unknown } | null)?.error;
      if (typeof described === 'string' && described.length > 0) message = described;
    } catch {
      // non-json response
    }
    throw new ApiError(response.status, message, body);
  }

  if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

export const lpApi = {
  get: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'GET' }),
  post: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'POST', body }),
  patch: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PATCH', body }),
  delete: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' })
};

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { classifyRoute, resolveRouteAccess, requiresRoleCheck } from './route-access.js';

describe('classifyRoute', () => {
  it('treats the landing page and auth pages as public', () => {
    expect(classifyRoute('/')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/login')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/signup')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/forgot-password')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/learn')).toBe('public');
  });

  it("classifies today's operator pages as admin", () => {
    for (const path of ['/admin', '/admin/portfolio', '/workspace', '/signals', '/wallets', '/logs', '/clusters', '/setup', '/performance']) {
      expect(classifyRoute(path)).toBe('admin');
    }
  });

  it('classifies nested operator paths as admin, not just the exact prefix', () => {
    expect(classifyRoute('/workspace/views/health')).toBe('admin');
  });

  it('does not let a longer path that merely starts with the same letters slip through', () => {
    // `/loginish` is not `/login`. Matching on bare `startsWith` without the
    // segment boundary would make it public.
    expect(classifyRoute('/loginish')).toBe('app');
    expect(classifyRoute('/setupwizard')).toBe('app');
  });

  it('defaults an unknown path to app, so a new page requires a session', () => {
    // Fails closed. A new page added without touching this file is gated rather
    // than public, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
    expect(classifyRoute('/some/new/page')).toBe('app');
  });
});

describe('resolveRouteAccess', () => {
  it('allows public routes with no session', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/', hasSession: false, role: null }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });

  it('redirects an anonymous visitor to login and preserves the deep link', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/workspace/views/health', hasSession: false, role: null }))
      .toEqual({
        decision: 'redirect',
        to: '/login?next=%2Fworkspace%2Fviews%2Fhealth',
        reason: 'no-session'
      });
  });

  it('allows an admin onto an admin route', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/wallets', hasSession: true, role: 'admin' }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });

  it('refuses a non-admin an admin route, and does not send them to login', () => {
    // They are signed in. A login form would imply their password is wrong.
    const access = resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/wallets', hasSession: true, role: 'user' });
    expect(access).toEqual({ decision: 'redirect', to: '/?denied=admin', reason: 'not-admin' });
  });

  it('fails closed when the role is unknown', () => {
    // An unreachable API, an expired session and a genuine non-admin all arrive
    // here as null. All three must be refused.
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/setup', hasSession: true, role: null }).decision)
      .toBe('redirect');
  });

  it('lets any signed-in user onto a non-admin app route', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/dashboard', hasSession: true, role: 'user' }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });
});

describe('requiresRoleCheck', () => {
  it('asks the API only for admin routes with a session', () => {
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/wallets', true)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('skips the round trip when there is no session or the route is public', () => {
    // No point paying for a role lookup we are going to redirect past anyway.
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/wallets', false)).toBe(false);
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/login', true)).toBe(false);
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/dashboard', true)).toBe(false);
  });
});

==> apps/web/lib/route-access.ts <==
/**
 * Route protection decisions (checklist S6-2), as pure functions.
 *
 * Kept separate from `middleware.ts` because Next middleware runs in the edge
 * runtime and cannot be imported into a test here -- but the decisions are the
 * part worth testing, and they are just data in, data out.
 *
 * **What this layer is and is not.** It is the reason an unauthenticated visitor
 * is redirected to /login instead of watching a dashboard fail to load. It is
 * *not* the authorization boundary: the API enforces that itself in
 * `apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts` (`registerAdminOnlyGlobals` restricts every
 * route outside `/v1/auth/` and `/v1/me/` to admins and internal services).
 * Middleware sees only cookies and whatever it chooses to ask the API, so
 * treating it as the gate would put the control in the client's half of the
 * system. Both layers exist; only the API one is load-bearing.
 */

export type RouteClass = 'public' | 'admin' | 'app';

/** Roles the API reports on `GET /v1/auth/me`. */
export type Role = 'admin' | 'user';

/** Reachable without a session. */
const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ['/login', '/signup', '/forgot-password', '/learn'] as const;

/**
 * The operator console: today's nine pages.
 *
 * These are admin surfaces because they call global routes -- `/v1/wallets`,
 * `/v1/config`, `/v1/scorer/run` -- which the API admits only for an admin or an
 * internal service. Listing them here is an interim measure: checklist S6-13 and
 * S6-14 move them under an `(admin)` route group, at which point the prefix is
 * structural and this array collapses to one entry. Until then a new operator
 * page must be added here, which is exactly the kind of thing that gets
 * forgotten -- hence `classifyRoute` defaults unknown paths to 'app' (session
 * required) rather than 'public'.
 */
const ADMIN_PREFIXES = [
  '/admin',
  '/workspace',
  '/signals',
  '/wallets',
  '/logs',
  '/clusters',
  '/setup',
  '/performance'
] as const;

export function classifyRoute(pathname: string): RouteClass {
  if (pathname === '/') return 'public';
  if (PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`))) {
    return 'public';
  }
  if (ADMIN_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`))) {
    return 'admin';
  }
  return 'app';
}

export interface RouteAccessInput {
  readonly pathname: string;
  /** Whether the session cookie is present. Presence, not validity. */
  readonly hasSession: boolean;
  /**
   * The role the API reported, or null when it was not asked or would not say.
   *
   * Null is not 'user'. An unreachable API, an expired session and a genuine
   * non-admin are all null here, and all three must be refused an admin surface
   * -- so this fails closed. That is the right direction, but it means an API
   * outage presents as "you are not an admin", which is why the redirect carries
   * a reason.
   */
  readonly role: Role | null;
}

export type RouteAccess =
  | { readonly decision: 'allow' }
  | { readonly decision: 'redirect'; readonly to: string; readonly reason: RedirectReason };

export type RedirectReason = 'no-session' | 'not-admin';

/**
 * Decides whether a request may proceed.
 *
 * The `next` parameter on the login redirect is what makes a deep link survive
 * signing in; without it every session expiry dumps the operator back on the
 * landing page and they have to navigate again.
 */
export function resolveRouteAccess(input: RouteAccessInput): RouteAccess {
  const classification = classifyRoute(input.pathname);
  if (classification === 'public') return { decision: 'allow' };

  if (!input.hasSession) {
    return {
      decision: 'redirect',
      to: `/login?next=${encodeURIComponent(input.pathname)}`,
      reason: 'no-session'
    };
  }

  if (classification === 'admin' && input.role !== 'admin') {
    // Deliberately not /login: the user is signed in, so sending them to a login
    // form would suggest their credentials are the problem and invite them to
    // retype a password that is already correct.
    return { decision: 'redirect', to: '/?denied=admin', reason: 'not-admin' };
  }

  return { decision: 'allow' };
}

/** True when middleware needs to ask the API for the role at all. */
export function requiresRoleCheck(pathname: string, hasSession: boolean): boolean {
  return hasSession && classifyRoute(pathname) === 'admin';
}

import { api } from './api.js';
import { PublicKey } from '@solana/web3.js';

export const WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID = '6t6dRetG3Hns4vCfZaj392e9bZ6uTEEmvL37KnDWErfS';
export const WAKE_SOLANA_DEVNET_PROGRAM_ID = 'WakeDev11111111111111111111111111111111111';

/**
 * Derives a real Anchor Program Derived Address (PDA) on Solana:
 * seeds = [b"vault", user_public_key]
 * program_id = WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID (or devnet)
 */
export function deriveSolanaAnchorPda(
  userAddress: string,
  cluster: 'mainnet-beta' | 'devnet' = 'mainnet-beta'
): { pdaAddress: string; bump: number } {
  try {
    const userPubkey = new PublicKey(userAddress.trim());
    const progId = new PublicKey(
      cluster === 'devnet' ? WAKE_SOLANA_DEVNET_PROGRAM_ID : WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID
    );
    const [pda, bump] = PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync(
      [new TextEncoder().encode('vault'), userPubkey.toBytes()],
      progId
    );
    return { pdaAddress: pda.toBase58(), bump };
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('Could not derive Anchor PDA with @solana/web3.js:', err);
    return { pdaAddress: WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID, bump: 255 };
  }
}

/**
 * Detects whether the active Solana wallet or RPC is targeting devnet or mainnet
 */
export function detectSolanaCluster(provider?: any): 'mainnet-beta' | 'devnet' {
  if (provider) {
    if (provider.isDevnet || provider.cluster === 'devnet' || provider.network === 'devnet') {
      return 'devnet';
    }
    const rpc = provider.connection?._rpcEndpoint || '';
    if (typeof rpc === 'string' && rpc.includes('devnet')) return 'devnet';
  }
  return 'mainnet-beta';
}

/**
 * Robust copy helper that succeeds even on non-HTTPS origins (e.g. raw IP)
 */
export function copyToClipboard(text: string): boolean {
  if (!text) return false;
  try {
    if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).catch(() => {});
      return true;
    }
  } catch {
    // Fall back to execCommand
  }
  if (typeof document !== 'undefined') {
    const el = document.createElement('textarea');
    el.value = text;
    el.setAttribute('readonly', '');
    el.style.position = 'fixed';
    el.style.top = '-9999px';
    el.style.left = '-9999px';
    document.body.appendChild(el);
    el.select();
    try {
      const ok = document.execCommand('copy');
      document.body.removeChild(el);
      return ok;
    } catch {
      document.body.removeChild(el);
      return false;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

const ALPHABET = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz';

/** Encodes raw bytes to Base58 for Solana signatures and public keys */
export function toBase58(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  const digits = [0];
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
    for (let j = 0; j < digits.length; j++) digits[j] <<= 8;
    digits[0] += bytes[i];
    let carry = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < digits.length; j++) {
      digits[j] += carry;
      carry = (digits[j] / 58) | 0;
      digits[j] %= 58;
    }
    while (carry) {
      digits.push(carry % 58);
      carry = (carry / 58) | 0;
    }
  }
  let str = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length && bytes[i] === 0; i++) str += ALPHABET[0];
  for (let i = digits.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) str += ALPHABET[digits[i]];
  return str;
}

export interface SolanaWalletConnection {
  address: string;
  provider: any;
  walletName: string;
}

export interface EvmWalletConnection {
  address: string;
  provider: any;
  chainId: string;
  walletName: string;
}

/** Detects injected Solana provider (Phantom, Solflare, Backpack) */
export function getSolanaProvider(): { provider: any; name: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  const anyWin = window as any;
  if (anyWin.phantom?.solana?.isPhantom) {
    return { provider: anyWin.phantom.solana, name: 'Phantom' };
  }
  if (anyWin.solflare?.isSolflare) {
    return { provider: anyWin.solflare, name: 'Solflare' };
  }
  if (anyWin.backpack?.isBackpack) {
    return { provider: anyWin.backpack, name: 'Backpack' };
  }
  if (anyWin.solana) {
    return { provider: anyWin.solana, name: anyWin.solana.isPhantom ? 'Phantom' : 'Solana Wallet' };
  }
  return null;
}

/** Detects injected EVM provider (MetaMask, Rabby, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) */
export function getEvmProvider(): { provider: any; name: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  const anyWin = window as any;
  if (anyWin.ethereum) {
    let name = 'MetaMask';
    if (anyWin.ethereum.isRabby) name = 'Rabby';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isCoinbaseWallet) name = 'Coinbase Wallet';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isBraveWallet) name = 'Brave Wallet';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isMetaMask) name = 'MetaMask';
    return { provider: anyWin.ethereum, name };
  }
  return null;
}

/** Connects to Solana wallet and retrieves public address */
export async function connectSolanaWallet(): Promise<SolanaWalletConnection> {
  const detected = getSolanaProvider();
  if (!detected) {
    throw new Error('No Solana wallet extension detected. Please install Phantom from https://phantom.app to connect.');
  }

  const { provider, name } = detected;
  const res = await provider.connect({ onlyIfTrusted: false });
  const pubkey = res?.publicKey || provider.publicKey;
  if (!pubkey) {
    throw new Error('Could not read public key from Solana wallet.');
  }
  return {
    address: pubkey.toString(),
    provider,
    walletName: name,
  };
}

/** Signs a SIWS (Sign-In with Solana) challenge message */
export async function signSolanaChallenge(provider: any, message: string): Promise<string> {
  const encoded = new TextEncoder().encode(message);
  const signed = await provider.signMessage(encoded, 'utf8');
  const signatureBytes = signed.signature || signed;
  if (signatureBytes instanceof Uint8Array) {
    return toBase58(signatureBytes);
  }
  if (typeof signatureBytes === 'string') {
    return signatureBytes;
  }
  return toBase58(new Uint8Array(signatureBytes));
}

/** Connects to EVM wallet (MetaMask / Rabby) and retrieves public address */
export async function connectEvmWallet(targetChainId?: '0x89'): Promise<EvmWalletConnection> {
  const detected = getEvmProvider();
  if (!detected) {
    throw new Error('No EVM wallet extension detected. Please install MetaMask from https://metamask.io or Rabby to connect.');
  }

  const { provider, name } = detected;
  const accounts: string[] = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_requestAccounts' });
  if (!accounts || accounts.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('No accounts selected in EVM wallet.');
  }

  const currentChainId: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => '0x1');

  // If Polygon is targeted (e.g. Polymarket), prompt user to switch
  if (targetChainId && currentChainId.toLowerCase() !== targetChainId.toLowerCase()) {
    try {
      await provider.request({
        method: 'wallet_switchEthereumChain',
        params: [{ chainId: targetChainId }],
      });
    } catch (switchError: any) {
      if (switchError.code === 4902 && targetChainId === '0x89') {
        await provider.request({
          method: 'wallet_addEthereumChain',
          params: [
            {
              chainId: '0x89',
              chainName: 'Polygon Mainnet',
              nativeCurrency: { name: 'POL', symbol: 'POL', decimals: 18 },
              rpcUrls: ['https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com'],
              blockExplorerUrls: ['https://polygonscan.com'],
            },
          ],
        });
      } else {
        throw new Error('Please approve switching your wallet to Polygon Mainnet (Chain ID 137) in MetaMask/Rabby.');
      }
    }
  }

  const updatedChainId: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => currentChainId);

  return {
    address: accounts[0].toLowerCase(),
    provider,
    chainId: updatedChainId,
    walletName: name,
  };
}

/** Signs an EIP-4361 SIWE challenge message */
export async function signEvmChallenge(provider: any, message: string, address: string): Promise<string> {
  return await provider.request({
    method: 'personal_sign',
    params: [message, address],
  });
}

/**
 * End-to-end authenticating and linking a self-custody wallet:
 * 1. Requests single-use challenge nonce from API
 * 2. Prompts the wallet popup to sign the challenge
 * 3. Verifies and registers cryptographic proof with the backend
 */
export async function linkWalletWithSignature(params: {
  chainKind: 'solana' | 'evm';
  address: string;
  provider: any;
}): Promise<{ chainKind: string; address: string; verifiedAt: string }> {
  // 1. Get nonce & challenge message from server
  const nonceRes = await api.post<{ nonce: string; message: string; expiresAt: string }>('/v1/auth/wallet/nonce', {
    chainKind: params.chainKind,
    address: params.address,
  });

  if (!nonceRes?.message) {
    throw new Error('Failed to obtain challenge message from authentication server.');
  }

  // 2. Prompt wallet extension signature
  let signature: string;
  if (params.chainKind === 'solana') {
    signature = await signSolanaChallenge(params.provider, nonceRes.message);
  } else {
    signature = await signEvmChallenge(params.provider, nonceRes.message, params.address);
  }

  // 3. Post proof to verification endpoint
  const verifyRes = await api.post<{ wallet: { chainKind: string; address: string; verifiedAt: string } }>('/v1/auth/wallet/verify', {
    chainKind: params.chainKind,
    address: params.address,
    message: nonceRes.message,
    signature,
  });

  return verifyRes.wallet;
}

/**
 * Prompts the connected EVM wallet (MetaMask / Rabby) to sign the Polymarket
 * ClobAuth EIP-712 typed data via eth_signTypedData_v4.
 */
export async function signPolymarketClobAuth(
  provider: any,
  address: string,
  typedData: any
): Promise<string> {
  // Ensure wallet is strictly on Polygon (0x89 / 137) before signing
  const currentHex: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => '0x1');
  if (currentHex.toLowerCase() !== '0x89') {
    try {
      await provider.request({
        method: 'wallet_switchEthereumChain',
        params: [{ chainId: '0x89' }],
      });
    } catch (switchErr: any) {
      if (switchErr?.code === 4902) {
        await provider.request({
          method: 'wallet_addEthereumChain',
          params: [
            {
              chainId: '0x89',
              chainName: 'Polygon Mainnet',
              nativeCurrency: { name: 'POL', symbol: 'POL', decimals: 18 },
              rpcUrls: ['https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com'],
              blockExplorerUrls: ['https://polygonscan.com'],
            },
          ],
        });
      } else {
        throw new Error('Please switch your wallet to Polygon Mainnet (Chain ID 137) before signing Polymarket credentials.');
      }
    }
  }

  // Ensure EIP712Domain is explicitly in types for MetaMask eth_signTypedData_v4
  const payload = {
    ...typedData,
    types: {
      EIP712Domain: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'version', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' },
      ],
      ...typedData.types,
    },
  };

  try {
    return await provider.request({
      method: 'eth_signTypedData_v4',
      params: [address, JSON.stringify(payload)],
    });
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.code === 4001) {
      throw new Error('Polymarket authentication signature rejected by user.');
    }
    // Fallback: some providers expect parsed object instead of serialized JSON string
    try {
      return await provider.request({
        method: 'eth_signTypedData_v4',
        params: [address, payload],
      });
    } catch {
      throw err;
    }
  }
}

==> apps/web/middleware.ts <==
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from 'next/server';
import { resolveRouteAccess, requiresRoleCheck, type Role } from './lib/route-access.js';
import { SESSION_COOKIE } from './lib/api.js';

/**
 * Route protection (checklist S6-2, closes S6-B7).
 *
 * All the decisions live in `lib/route-access.ts` as pure functions with tests;
 * this file is the adapter that feeds them a request and acts on the answer.
 * Middleware runs in the edge runtime and cannot be imported into vitest, so
 * anything decided here rather than there is untestable -- keep it thin.
 *
 * **This is a redirect layer, not the authorization boundary.** The API enforces
 * roles itself (`apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`), and it must, because everything
 * middleware knows comes from the client. What this buys is that an operator
 * whose session lapsed lands on a login form instead of a dashboard full of
 * failed requests, and a non-admin never sees an admin shell render before its
 * data 403s.
 */

const API_BASE = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001';

/**
 * Asks the API who this session belongs to.
 *
 * Returns null on anything other than a clean 200 with a recognised role --
 * network failure, 401, malformed body. Every one of those means "we do not know
 * this is an admin", and `resolveRouteAccess` refuses admin surfaces on null. So
 * an API outage locks the operator console rather than opening it, which is the
 * correct direction and worth stating because it will look like a bug the first
 * time it happens.
 */
async function fetchRole(request: NextRequest): Promise<Role | null> {
  const cookie = request.headers.get('cookie');
  if (!cookie) return null;
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/v1/auth/me`, {
      headers: { cookie },
      // Middleware must never serve a cached identity: a stale 200 would keep a
      // revoked session admitted for as long as the cache lived.
      cache: 'no-store'
    });
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const body = (await response.json()) as { user?: { role?: unknown } };
    const role = body.user?.role;
    return role === 'admin' || role === 'user' ? role : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;
  const hasSession = request.cookies.has(SESSION_COOKIE);

  const role = (await (requiresRoleCheck(pathname, hasSession) ? fetchRole(request) : null)) as Role | null;
  const access = resolveRouteAccess({ pathname, hasSession, role });

  if (access.decision === 'redirect') {
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
    const [path, query] = access.to.split('?');
    url.pathname = path!;
    url.search = query ? `?${query}` : '';
    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = {
  /**
   * Skip Next internals, static assets and the favicon.
   *
   * Not a security decision -- `classifyRoute` would gate an unmatched path
   * anyway. It is a cost one: without it every image request on an admin page
   * triggers a `/v1/auth/me` round trip.
   */
  matcher: ['/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|ico)$).*)']
};

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {

  webpack: (config) => {

==> deploy/crontab.example <==
# ==============================================================================
# SWAT / WAKE Production Cron Schedule
# ==============================================================================
# Run as the swat system user or install via `crontab -e -u swat`
#
# Environment settings
SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
MAILTO=""

# 1. Daily Subscription Tier Downgrade Sweep (Midnight UTC)
# Downgrades expired paid subscriptions (Operator / Ultra) back to 'free' and writes audit log.
0 0 * * * cd /root/SWAT && /usr/bin/node apps/api/dist/cron/billing-sweep.js >> /var/log/swat/billing-sweep.log 2>&1

# 2. Daily Database Vacuum & Analyze (03:00 UTC)
0 3 * * * /usr/bin/psql "postgresql://swat:swat@127.0.0.1:5432/swat" -c "VACUUM ANALYZE;" >> /var/log/swat/db-vacuum.log 2>&1

# 3. Weekly pg_stat_statements reset (Sunday 04:00 UTC)
0 4 * * 0 /usr/bin/psql "postgresql://swat:swat@127.0.0.1:5432/swat" -c "SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset();" >> /dev/null 2>&1

==> deploy/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini <==
; ==============================================================================
; SWAT / WAKE Production PgBouncer Configuration
; Optimized for multi-tenant high-throughput transaction pooling
; ==============================================================================

[databases]
; Format: dbname = host=... port=... dbname=...
; In Docker networks, use host=postgres; on localhost, use host=127.0.0.1
swat = host=postgres port=5432 auth_user=swat dbname=swat

[pgbouncer]
; Networking
listen_addr = 0.0.0.0
listen_port = 6432

; Authentication
auth_type = scram-sha-256
auth_file = /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt
admin_users = swat

; Pooling Mode: transaction mode is essential for multi-tenant microservices
; (node-postgres connection pool multiplexed across a small set of backend connections)
pool_mode = transaction

; Connection Limits
max_client_conn = 2000
default_pool_size = 25
min_pool_size = 5
reserve_pool_size = 5
reserve_pool_timeout = 5
max_db_connections = 50

; Timeouts & Lifetimes
server_idle_timeout = 600
server_connect_timeout = 15
server_login_retry = 15
query_timeout = 60
idle_transaction_timeout = 60
client_idle_timeout = 0

; Low-level TCP keep-alive (prevents dead TCP connections through firewalls/load balancers)
tcp_keepalive = 1
tcp_keepcnt = 3
tcp_keepidle = 30
tcp_keepintvl = 10

; Application Compatibility (Critical for Node.js pg client)
ignore_startup_parameters = extra_float_digits,search_path,timezone

; Logging
log_connections = 1
log_disconnections = 1
log_pooler_errors = 1
stats_period = 60

==> deploy/pgbouncer/userlist.txt <==
; Userlist template for PgBouncer
; Format: "username" "password_or_hash"
; For production, generate SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers or md5 hashes
"swat" "swat"

==> deploy/systemd/swat-api.service <==
[Unit]
Description=SWAT / WAKE API Gateway
After=network.target postgresql.service redis.service pgbouncer.service
Wants=redis.service pgbouncer.service

[Service]
Type=simple
User=swat
WorkingDirectory=/root/SWAT
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
EnvironmentFile=/root/SWAT/.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /root/SWAT/apps/api/dist/index.js
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
LimitNOFILE=65536

# Sandboxing and security hardening
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

==> docker-compose.yml <==
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # pg_stat_statements is a shared library, so it must be preloaded at server
    # start; CREATE EXTENSION alone (migration 037) is not enough.
    command:
      - postgres
      - -c
      - shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements
      - -c
      - pg_stat_statements.track=all
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-swat}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-swat}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-swat}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-swat} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-swat}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    ports:
      - "${REDIS_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${REDIS_PORT:-6379}:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  pgbouncer:
    image: edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.22.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PGBOUNCER_BIND_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${PGBOUNCER_PORT:-6432}:6432"
    environment:
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-swat}
      DB_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-swat}
      DB_NAME: ${POSTGRES_DB:-swat}
      POOL_MODE: transaction
      MAX_CLIENT_CONN: 2000
      DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE: 25
      MIN_POOL_SIZE: 5
      RESERVE_POOL_SIZE: 5
      MAX_DB_CONNECTIONS: 50
      IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS: extra_float_digits,search_path,timezone
      AUTH_TYPE: scram-sha-256
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:

# Stage 1â€“4 Blockers, Deferred Items & External Gates Register

## 1. Executive Summary & Overview

Across Stages 1, 2, 3, and 4, the **code-level architecture and implementation are complete**:
- **Stage 1 (Auth & Multi-Tenancy):** Migrations `039`â€“`043`, SIWE/SIWS wallet authentication, layered auth tokens, CSRF protection, and strict `forUser(userId)` nominal tenancy isolation are implemented and 100% test-verified.
- **Stage 2 (Subscriptions & Quotas):** Migrations `044`â€“`045`, global wallet dedup with per-user subscriptions, concurrency-safe tier quotas (`SELECT FOR UPDATE`), and `/v1/me/*` routes are fully verified.
- **Stage 3 (Venue Executors):** The three execution adapters (Solana Jupiter+Jito, Robinhood EVM, Polymarket CLOB), queue isolation (`swat-trades-{solana,polygon,robinhood}`), and redemption state machines are fully implemented.
- **Stage 4 (Delegated Authority & Fan-Out):** The long pole of the architecture (**S4-P12**, Solana `wake-vault` Anchor program) has been developed, fuzzed, tested with real wallets, security-audited, and toggled live (`6t6dRetG3Hns4vCfZaj392e9bZ6uTEEmvL37KnDWErfS`). ERC-4337 argument-scoped permission policies, EntryPoint v0.7.0 pinning, paymaster spend limits, envelope encryption, and real-time Polymarket WSS orderbook streaming (`S4-M38`) are complete.

### The Distinction: Code Readiness vs. External Gates
The items remaining open are **NOT unwritten architectural blockers**. They fall into three specific categories:
1. **External Gates `(ext)`:** Live canaries requiring funded wallets, production venue accounts, and human sign-off.
2. **Operational / Third-Party Vendor Dependencies:** Signing up for the Polymarket Builder Program, provisioning an ERC-4337 bundler/paymaster key on chain 4663, and legal counsel ToS review.
3. **Cross-Service Wiring & Staging Deployments:** Running migrations on live containerized Postgres/Redis instances, and wiring frontend surfaces (Stage 6) to the completed backend endpoints.

### 3.1 Operational Runbook: Option A â€” Robinhood Chain (4663) Standard 4337 Validator Module Deployment & Activation

This runbook resolves **S4-P10** and **S4-P8a** using industry-standard, battle-tested Account Abstraction modules (ZeroDev Kernel / Safe 4337 Module) rather than custom unaudited contracts:

#### Prerequisites
1. **RPC Access:** Active RPC endpoint for Robinhood Chain (Chain ID `4663`, e.g. Alchemy `https://robinhood-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/<API_KEY>` or Robinhood's direct RPC).
2. **Funded Operator Wallet:** An EVM private key (`EVM_PRIVATE_KEY` in `.env`) holding ~$2â€“$5 worth of native gas on Chain 4663 to pay the one-time contract deployment gas fee.
3. **Bundler & Paymaster Account:** An account on **Alchemy Gas Manager** or **ZeroDev** with Robinhood Chain 4663 enabled.

#### Step 1: Check Deterministic Deployment on Chain 4663
ZeroDev and Safe use standard deterministic deployment factories (`CREATE2`), meaning standard modules deploy to identical addresses across all EVM chains.
- *Already Live on 4663:* **EntryPoint v0.7.0** (`0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032`) and **Safe 4337 Module v0.3.0** (`0x75cf11467937ce3F2f357CE24ffc3DBF8fD5c226`) are verified live on Robinhood Chain 4663.
- Run an RPC check (`eth_getCode`) against the candidate SessionKeyValidator address on Chain 4663:
  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST $ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_getCode","params":["<VALIDATOR_ADDRESS>","latest"],"id":1}'
  ```
- If the result returns runtime bytecode (`0x6080...`), the contract is already live on-chain. Skip directly to Step 3.

#### Step 2: Deploy Standard Module (If Not Already Live)
If the address returns `0x` (empty):
1. Obtain the official compiled JSON artifact from ZeroDev (`@zerodev/session-key`) or Safe deployments.
2. Deploy using `viem` / Foundry `forge` using `EVM_PRIVATE_KEY`:
   ```bash
   forge create src/SessionKeyValidator.sol:SessionKeyValidator \
     --rpc-url $ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL \
     --private-key $EVM_PRIVATE_KEY
   ```
3. Record the returned contract address.

#### Step 3: Configure Alchemy / ZeroDev Bundler & Paymaster
1. In the Alchemy (or ZeroDev) dashboard:
   - Create an App targeting **Robinhood Chain (Chain ID 4663)**.
   - In Gas Manager, configure a sponsorship policy (deposit ~$20â€“$50 in gas credits).
   - Set spending limits matching [`apps/trade-executor/src/paymaster-budget.ts`](file:///root/SWAT/apps/trade-executor/src/paymaster-budget.ts) (50 ops/user/day, 10,000 ops/global/day).
2. Set the configuration variables in `.env`:
   ```bash
   ROBINHOOD_BUNDLER_RPC_URL="https://robinhood-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/<API_KEY>"
   ROBINHOOD_PAYMASTER_POLICY_ID="<POLICY_ID>"
   ROBINHOOD_PERMISSION_VALIDATOR_ADDRESS="0x<DEPLOYED_ADDRESS>"
   ```

#### Step 4: Verification & Acceptance Test
1. Submit an authorized copy-trade UserOperation to the bundler: verify that the swap executes on-chain and gas is sponsored by the paymaster.
2. Submit a simulated malicious UserOperation (e.g. attempting to transfer tokens or call an un-whitelisted recipient): verify that the smart account / validator module reverts on-chain with validation failure.
3. Sign off `S4-P10` in `AUDIT-FIX-CHECKLIST.md`.

## 1. Executive Summary & System Vision

**Wake Protocol** is an institutional-grade, multi-tenant cross-chain intelligence and autonomous copy-trading engine spanning **Solana**, **Robinhood Chain (Arbitrum EVM L2)**, and **Polymarket (Polygon)**.

Unlike typical analytics platforms that merely send delayed Telegram alerts, Wake Protocol bridges the gap between **signal detection and automated capital execution**. It ingests mempool and on-chain transactions at line speed, clusters coordinated wallet behavior (funding links, timing correlation, volume concentration), evaluates copy-trading profitability, and executes mirrored fills with sub-second latency while keeping capital in self-custodial or venue-isolated vaults.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Ingestion ["Ingestion Layer"]
        SOL["Solana Helius / RPC"] --> IDX["apps/indexer"]
        EVM["Robinhood EVM RPC"] --> IDX
        POLY["Polygon / Polymarket CLOB"] --> IDX
    end

    subgraph Intelligence ["Intelligence Layer"]
        IDX --> REDIS[("Redis 7.4 Streams")]
        REDIS --> SE["apps/signal-engine"]
        REDIS --> SC["apps/scorer"]
        REDIS --> DISC["apps/discovery"]
        SE --> DB[("PostgreSQL 17.4")]
        SC --> DB
    end

    subgraph Execution ["Execution Layer"]
        DB --> TE["apps/trade-executor"]
        TE --> JITO["Solana (Jito MEV Bundles)"]
        TE --> AA["Robinhood (EIP-7702 Paymaster)"]
        TE --> CLOB["Polymarket (CLOB Proxy)"]
    end

    subgraph Surfaces ["Client & Gateway"]
        API["apps/api (Fastify 5)"] --- DB
        WEB["apps/web (Next.js 15)"] --- API
    end
```

## 2. Stage-by-Stage Build Architecture (Stages 1â€“6)

### Stage 1: Foundation & High-Frequency Ingestion Engine
- **Core Objective:** Robust raw transaction ingestion without dropping blocks, database deadlock prevention, and idempotency across high-throughput chains.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - Fast transaction deduplication in Redis (`swat:tx:dedup:<hash>`) with 24-hour expiration.
  - Multi-chain schema unification in PostgreSQL using `citext` and widened hex/base58 address columns (`character varying(128)`).
  - PostgreSQL BRIN (Block Range Indexing) on `transactions.block_time` (`036_transactions_brin.sql`) ensuring queries over hundreds of millions of rows execute in milliseconds with minimal storage overhead.
  - BullMQ resilient pipeline with exponential backoff retries for RPC rate-limit resilience.

### Stage 2: Algorithmic Intelligence, Scoring & Clustering
- **Core Objective:** Transform noisy mempool transactions into high-confidence trading intelligence.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - **Behavioral Clustering Engine (`apps/scorer` & `packages/db/sql/003_fix_clustering.sql`):** Discovers wallet clusters sharing funding origins, simultaneous trade submissions (within 3 seconds), and identical liquidity pool routing.
  - **Wallet Composite Scoring:** Evaluates win rate, realized ROI, drawdown, and trading frequency to assign ranks: `elite`, `pro`, `tracked`.
  - **Early Buyer Discovery (`apps/discovery`):** Scans new Raydium, Pump.fun, and Uniswap pool creation blocks to identify insiders buying within the first 10 minutes with >0.5 SOL.
  - **Token Metadata & Blacklist Engine:** Automatically resolves token symbols, names, and decimals via DexScreener/RPC while ignoring stables, wrapped gas, and blacklisted spam tokens.

### Stage 3: Multi-Chain Trade Execution & Circuit Breakers
- **Core Objective:** Low-latency execution across heterogeneous architectures with hard capital protection.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - **Solana Execution:** Direct Jito MEV block engine bundle submission with dynamic priority fees and tip auctioning to eliminate front-running and toxic sandwich attacks.
  - **Robinhood Chain Execution:** ERC-4337 Account Abstraction bundling with Paymaster 100% gas sponsorship.
  - **Polymarket Execution:** CLOB API order placement with EIP-712 order signatures and automatic token redemption on market resolution.
  - **Safety Boundaries:**
    - Per-trade max slippage caps (default 100 bps / 1.0%).
    - Per-trade size caps relative to pool liquidity (max 2% pool impact).
    - Global Emergency Kill Switch (`POST /v1/trading/emergency-off`) that immediately cancels all in-flight orders and halts execution.

### Stage 4: Multi-Tenant Copy-Trading & Attribution Matrix
- **Core Objective:** Multi-user follower execution with complete tenancy isolation and fair position sizing.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - **Copy Trade Lifecycle (`023_copy_trade_lifecycle.sql` & `028_copy_execution_lifecycle.sql`):** Deterministic state machine (`pending` &rarr; `submitted` &rarr; `confirmed` &rarr; `failed` &rarr; `skipped`).
  - **Position Lot Attribution (`058_copy_position_lots.sql` & `061_copy_position_lot_exits.sql`):** When a master wallet sells 50% of their holdings, follower positions are proportionally reduced lot-by-lot without stranded dust.
  - **Master Follower Capacity Caps (`053_master_capacity.sql`):** Strict 50-copier limit per master wallet to prevent follower slippage and pool depletion.
  - **Stop-Loss Auto-Liquidation Engine (`034_stop_loss_triggers.sql` & `059_stop_loss_lot_identity.sql`):** Independent off-chain monitor that triggers market exits if an asset drops below user-configured drawdown thresholds.

### Stage 5: SaaS Monetization, Crypto Billing & Security Rails
- **Core Objective:** Multi-tier commercialization, non-custodial billing, and anti-theft withdrawal rails.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - **Subscription Tier System (`063_crypto_billing.sql`):**
    - **Free:** View-only signals and telemetry.
    - **Operator ($99/mo):** 5 active copy slots, 10 concurrent positions, 50 sponsored ops/day.
    - **Ultra ($499/mo):** 50 copy slots, 100 concurrent positions, unlimited sponsored ops, private low-latency RPC lanes.
    - **Lifetime ($4,999):** Permanent Ultra tier access.
  - **USDC Crypto Invoicing:** Automatic on-chain payment intent generation and confirmation with zero chargeback risk.
  - **Secure 2FA Withdrawal Rail (`/v1/me/trading/withdraw`):** Capital withdrawals are strictly restricted to verified linked wallets and require email OTP confirmation with a 24-hour anti-theft cooldown on newly linked addresses.

### Stage 6: Unified Console, 1-Click Web3 Wallets & Mobile Hardening
- **Core Objective:** Production-ready Web3 frontend with modern UX, zero-error type safety, and real-time execution telemetry.
- **Key Deliverables:**
  - **Permanent Vector Branding:** High-resolution SVG `WakeLogo` component across all surfaces with "Wake Protocol" identity.
  - **Role-Aware Console Navigation:** Distinct operator management (`AdminNav.tsx`) and subscriber copy-trading interfaces (`SaaSNav.tsx`).
  - **1-Click Web3 Wallet Connectors (`apps/web/lib/wallets.ts`):** Direct browser extension integration (Phantom, Solflare, MetaMask, Rabby) replacing fragile manual address pasting.
  - **Dynamic SIWE / SIWS Nonces:** Solves MetaMask/Phantom "Domain Mismatch" alerts by dynamically binding challenges to the host header.
  - **Mobile Layout Optimization:** Responsive grid breakpoints (`grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2`), horizontal scroll viewports on data tables, and mobile hamburger navigation drawers.

## 4. Database Architecture & 63 SQL Migrations

The database is powered by **PostgreSQL 17.4** with `citext` and `uuid-ossp` extensions enabled.

### Key Schema Entities & Relationships

```mermaid
erDiagram
    USERS ||--o{ USER_AUTH_WALLETS : owns
    USERS ||--o{ USER_SESSIONS : establishes
    USERS ||--o{ USER_BALANCES : holds
    USERS ||--o{ USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS : configures
    USERS ||--o{ USER_WALLET_SUBSCRIPTIONS : follows
    USERS ||--o{ COPY_POSITIONS : owns
    USERS ||--o{ CRYPTO_PAYMENTS : pays

    WALLETS ||--o{ SIGNALS : generates
    WALLETS ||--o{ WALLET_CLUSTERS : belongs_to
    SIGNALS ||--o{ TRADES : triggers
    TRADES ||--o{ COPY_EXECUTIONS : mirrors
    COPY_POSITIONS ||--o{ COPY_POSITION_LOTS : splits_into
```

### Essential Table Specifications

1. `users` (`039_users.sql`):
   - Primary identifier: UUID (`gen_random_uuid()`).
   - Fields: `email` (`citext` UNIQUE), `password_hash` (Argon2id), `role` (`user` | `admin`), `tier` (`free` | `operator` | `ultra`), `status` (`active` | `suspended` | `deleted`).
2. `user_auth_wallets` (`041_user_auth_wallets.sql`):
   - Stores cryptographically verified linked wallets for SIWE/SIWS login and withdrawal whitelisting.
   - Enforces unique binding: `UNIQUE(chain_kind, address)`.
3. `user_execution_settings` (`049_user_execution_settings.sql`):
   - Multi-tenant risk parameters: `max_position_pct`, `max_slippage_bps`, `auto_execute`, `concurrent_position_cap`, `kill_switch_active`.
4. `copy_positions` & `copy_position_lots` (`050_copy_tenancy.sql`, `058_copy_position_lots.sql`):
   - Tracks individual token allocations per user with distinct purchase cost basis, realized P&L, and token quantity.
5. `crypto_payments` (`063_crypto_billing.sql`):
   - Manages USDC subscription invoices, payment intents, detected on-chain tx hashes, and subscription tier extensions.

## 5. Cryptographic Security & Non-Custodial Custody Rails

Wake Protocol enforces **zero-server-custody** for primary funds:

### Solana Keyless Anchor Program Derived Address (PDA)
- **Program ID:** `6t6dRetG3Hns4vCfZaj392e9bZ6uTEEmvL37KnDWErfS`
- **Seeds:** `[b"wake_vault", user_public_key]`
- **Properties:**
  - PDA has no corresponding private key; funds can only be moved according to the Anchor program's authorized instructions.
  - Users retain sole closing authority: invoking the `close` instruction returns all rent lamports and assets directly to their signer wallet.

### Robinhood Chain ERC-4337 & EIP-7702 Session Delegation
- **Mechanism:** EIP-7702 enables an EOA (Externally Owned Account) to temporarily delegate code execution to an ERC-4337 smart contract account without migrating funds.
- **Session Scoping:**
  - Execution grant is valid for exactly 30 days.
  - Restricted strictly to trading pair swap calls with maximum slippage limits.
  - Gas fees are 100% sponsored by the Wake Protocol Paymaster (up to 50 operations/day for Operator tier; unlimited for Ultra).

### Polymarket ERC-7739 Safe Deposit Proxy
- **Mechanism:** Polymarket CLOB orders settle on Polygon. Users deposit funds into an isolated, venue-scoped Safe proxy address.
- **Safety Guarantee:** Withdrawal instructions can only deliver capital back to the verified linked wallet stored in `user_auth_wallets`.

### Dynamic SIWE & SIWS Authentication Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Trader (Browser Extension)
    participant Web as apps/web (Next.js 15)
    participant API as apps/api (Fastify 5)
    participant Redis as Redis 7.4 (Atomic Nonce)
    participant DB as PostgreSQL 17.4

    User->>Web: Clicks "Connect Phantom / MetaMask"
    Web->>User: Prompts extension approval (accounts[0] / publicKey)
    User-->>Web: Grants public address
    Web->>API: POST /v1/auth/wallet/nonce { chainKind, address } (with Origin header)
    API->>API: Derives dynamic domain & URI from Host/Origin
    API->>Redis: SET swat:siwe:<nonce> { chainKind, address, domain, uri } EX 300
    API-->>Web: Returns { nonce, message }
    Web->>User: Prompts signature popup (personal_sign / signMessage)
    User-->>Web: Confirms signature
    Web->>API: POST /v1/auth/wallet/verify { chainKind, address, message, signature }
    API->>Redis: GETDEL swat:siwe:<nonce> (Atomic replay defense)
    API->>API: Cryptographically verifies ed25519 (Solana) or secp256k1 (EVM)
    API->>DB: Links wallet in user_auth_wallets (or establishes session)
    API-->>Web: 200 OK + Sets HTTP-only swat_session cookie
    Web-->>User: Displays verified wallet & derived execution authority
```

## 6. Hardware Sizing & Infrastructure Topology

### Minimum Production Hardware Sizing

| Component | Minimum Specification | Recommended Production |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CPU** | 4 Cores (x86_64 or ARM64) | 8 Cores (High single-thread clock) |
| **RAM** | 8 GB ECC RAM | 16 GB - 32 GB RAM |
| **Disk** | 100 GB NVMe SSD | 500 GB Enterprise NVMe (High IOPS) |
| **Network** | 1 Gbps unmetered | 10 Gbps low-latency interface |
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS / 24.04 LTS | Debian 12 / Ubuntu 24.04 LTS |

> [!CAUTION]
> The trade executor and signal engine require high-frequency Redis polling. Do NOT run heavy Turborepo monorepo builds concurrently with live trading on a 4-core machine to prevent CPU starvation.

## 8. Step-by-Step Production Deployment Runbook

### 1. System Provisioning & Dependencies

```bash
# Update system packages
apt update && apt upgrade -y
apt install -y curl git build-essential htop ufw fail2ban

# Install Node.js 22 LTS
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash -
apt install -y nodejs

# Enable pnpm
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@10.2.0 --activate

# Verify versions
node -v   # Must be v22.x
pnpm -v   # Must be v10.x
```

### 2. Database & Cache Initialization

```bash
# Run PostgreSQL 17 and Redis 7 via Docker
docker run -d --name sp-postgres --restart always \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=swat \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=swat \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=swat \
  -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 \
  -v /var/lib/postgresql/data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:17.4-alpine

docker run -d --name sp-redis --restart always \
  -p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 \
  -v /var/lib/redis/data:/data \
  redis:7.4-alpine redis-server --appendonly yes

# Apply all 63 database migrations
cd /root/SWAT
pnpm db:migrate

# Seed the initial admin account
pnpm seed:admin
```

### 3. Building the Monorepo Safely

> [!IMPORTANT]
> To prevent memory exhaustion on hardware with &le;8GB RAM, build packages individually rather than running global concurrent builds.

```bash
cd /root/SWAT

# 1. Install workspace dependencies
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# 2. Compile shared and db packages
pnpm --filter @swat/shared build
pnpm --filter @swat/db build

# 3. Typecheck API & Web
./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p apps/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit
./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit

# 4. Build Next.js 15 production bundle
cd /root/SWAT/apps/web
./node_modules/.bin/next build
```

### 4. Process Management: Systemd & PM2 Configurations

### 5. Reverse Proxy, SSL & WebSockets (Nginx / Caddy)

Production deployment requires TLS termination with WebSocket and SSE header forwarding:

#### Nginx Configuration (`/etc/nginx/sites-available/wake.conf`)
```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name 75.119.151.184 wakeprotocol.io;

    client_max_body_size 20M;

    # Frontend Next.js Web Application
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    # Backend Fastify API Gateway
    location /v1/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3001;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        
        # Disable buffering for Server-Sent Events (SSE) live logs
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_cache off;
        proxy_read_timeout 86400s;
    }
}
```

## 9. Operational Runbooks & Incident Response

### Global Emergency Off (Kill Switch)
In the event of market turbulence, stale oracle prices, or abnormal RPC latency:
1. **Via UI:** Click the red **"EMERGENCY OFF"** button in the top navigation bar of `AdminNav`.
2. **Via Command Line:**
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3001/v1/trading/emergency-off \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"reason": "Manual operator intervention via CLI"}'
   ```
3. **Effect:** Fastify broadcasts an immediate kill event across Redis pub/sub. The Trade Executor cancels all active Jito and EVM pending bundles, ceases follower order submissions, and enters halt mode.

### Database Backup & Cold Restore
```bash
# Trigger hot snapshot backup
docker exec sp-postgres pg_dump -U swat -d swat -F c -b -v -f /tmp/swat_backup_$(date +%F).dump
docker cp sp-postgres:/tmp/swat_backup_$(date +%F).dump /root/backups/

# Restore from snapshot
docker exec -i sp-postgres pg_restore -U swat -d swat --clean --if-exists -v < /root/backups/swat_backup.dump
```

## 1. What WAKE is

WAKE lets a person copy a specific crypto trader's trades automatically, across
multiple venues, without handing over custody of their funds.

A user picks a wallet â€” one they already follow, or one WAKE suggests â€” and from
that point on, when that wallet buys, the user buys; when it sells, the user
sells. Position sizes are scaled to the user's own balance and risk settings, not
copied one-for-one.

We call the followed wallet a **master**. We call the user's replicated trade a
**mirror**.

## 2. Who it's for

| Segment | What they want | Why WAKE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retail copy-trader | Exposure to a trader they believe in, without watching charts | Automation across chains, with real risk controls |
| Self-directed trader | Signal from wallets they already track manually | Removes the manual step; keeps their own wallet |
| Operator (us) | A single-tenant tool that became a product | The original system; still the internal user |

**Explicit non-audience:** high-frequency traders and snipers. We do not compete
on milliseconds against dedicated sniper bots (see Â§9.1). Anyone whose edge is
latency is better served elsewhere, and we should not market to them.

## 3. The core product loop

1. User signs up, verifies email, and connects a wallet they control.
2. User grants WAKE **scoped, revocable, expiring** authority to trade on their
   behalf â€” never a root private key (ADR-0003).
3. User funds their trading balance and sets risk preferences.
4. User subscribes to one or more masters, per chain.
5. A master trades. WAKE detects it, sizes a mirror, and executes.
6. User sees the mirror, its fill, and how it compared to the master's fill.
7. User can unsubscribe, withdraw, or revoke authority at any time.

## 4. Non-goals

Stating these because each has been proposed and rejected, and re-litigating them
costs more than writing them down.

- **We do not trade on cluster consensus.** Superseded by ADR-0005. The four
  cluster pattern detectors still run, but for discovery and alerting only.
- **We do not hold users' root private keys.** ADR-0003.
- **We do not compete on execution latency with sniper bots.** Â§9.1.
- **We do not queue a trade to execute later.** A late fill is not a copy of the
  signal it was meant to mirror. We skip and say why.
- **We do not auto-liquidate a user's positions.** Not on unsubscribe, not on
  revoke. Those are their assets.
- **We do not show follower counts or master popularity.** It creates reflexive
  crowding and tells a master exactly when farming their own followers pays.

## 5. Requirements

### 5.1 Master selection and subscription

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MS-1 | A user may subscribe to a wallet by address, on any supported chain | âœ… `044_user_wallet_subscriptions` |
| MS-2 | Subscriptions record provenance: user-supplied vs platform-suggested vs discovered | âœ… `source IN ('manual','platform-signal','discovered')` |
| MS-3 | A user may hold multiple masters per chain | ðŸŸ¡ schema allows; per-token exposure cap across masters not built |
| MS-4 | Masters are **per-chain**. A wallet address is chain-scoped; there is no cross-chain master identity. UI must not imply otherwise | â¬œ |
| MS-5 | Subscribing to a never-indexed wallet works immediately. Copying does not wait for history | â¬œ |
| MS-6 | Subscription has three states: `active` / `winding_down` / `ended` | â¬œ **schema change â€” needed before fan-out ships** |
| MS-7 | A wallet inside a funding or behavioural cluster shows a warning that it may not be an independent actor | â¬œ |

**MS-6 is load-bearing and easy to miss.** Unsubscribe must mean *exits-only
wind-down*: stop copying entries immediately, keep honouring the master's sells
against already-open positions until each closes, and offer an explicit "close
all now". Both simpler options are wrong â€” auto-selling is a market action the
user didn't request, and stopping outright orphans positions whose exit was going
to arrive as the master's sell mirror. Retrofitting this state later means
reconstructing which open position came from which subscription.

### 5.2 Mirroring semantics

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MR-1 | On a master buy, size the mirror as `min(max_position_pct, master_fraction Ã— scale)` â€” hybrid | ðŸŸ¡ today it is flat `riskPct` of user balance (`trade-executor/src/index.ts:508`) |
| MR-2 | `master_fraction` is computed over assets we index. Below a coverage threshold, fall back to flat `max_position_pct` and mark the trade **sized-without-conviction** | â¬œ |
| MR-3 | On a master sell, sell the same **fraction of the master's position**, applied to the user's own holding | âœ… `computeCopySellProportion` (`packages/shared/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.ts:242`), enforced on all three chains |
| MR-4 | When proportional position evidence is missing, **refuse** rather than defaulting to "sell everything" | âœ… throws `UnrecoverableError` |
| MR-5 | Joining is **forward-only** â€” no catch-up buying into a master's existing positions | â¬œ |
| MR-6 | If a master sells more than the user holds, cap at the user's holding and record the remainder | ðŸŸ¡ `copy_positions.unmatched_reduction_quantity` exists; wiring â“ |
| MR-7 | Only buys and sells above a minimum notional are mirrorable. Transfers, LP, staking, dust excluded | â¬œ |
| MR-8 | Tokens failing safety checks are skipped | âœ… `signal-engine/src/safety.ts` |
| MR-9 | Max concurrent copied positions is a **per-user setting**, API â†’ UI, with a platform hard ceiling | â¬œ |
| MR-10 | At the position-cap slider, warn when the user's balance would put copies below venue minimum order size | â¬œ |
| MR-11 | An underfunded trade skips with a stated reason. Never a silent partial | ðŸŸ¡ skip logic exists; reason taxonomy needs extending |

### 5.3 Capacity and fairness

The product has two hard capacity ceilings. Neither can be engineered away â€” only
allocated and communicated.

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CP-1 | Per-master capacity cap denominated in **price impact**: aggregate copy notional per `(master, token, window)` as a fraction of usable liquidity | â¬œ **v1 requirement** |
| CP-2 | Follower soft-cap per master as a crude secondary guard | â¬œ |
| CP-3 | When any capacity limit binds, **everyone is skipped uniformly**. No tier-based priority | â¬œ |
| CP-4 | Per-master budget allocation *inside* the platform daily cap, so one hyperactive master cannot starve users copying other masters | â¬œ |
| CP-5 | User-facing message is generic ("at capacity, scaling infrastructure"). Internal reason code names the actual constraint for ops and telemetry | â¬œ |

**Why CP-1 is denominated that way:** if 1,000 users copy one master's buy of a
thin token, our own cohort becomes the adverse selection â€” user #900 eats the
impact users #1â€“899 created. Follower count is the wrong unit: 500 followers
buying a deep pair is harmless, 50 buying a fresh memecoin is not. A master who
notices can also farm it â€” buy small, wait for copy flow to lift the price, sell
into their own followers.

**Why CP-4 exists:** a master doing 400 trades a day copied by 25 users is 10,000
Polymarket orders â€” the entire daily relayer budget â€” blanking the venue for
everyone else.

### 5.4 Suggestion engine

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SG-1 | Rank candidates on out-of-sample, risk-adjusted metrics over **24h / 7d / 30d**: PnL net of fees, max drawdown, hit rate, median hold time, capacity estimate | ðŸŸ¡ `apps/scorer/` scores wallets; metric set and windows not as specified |
| SG-2 | Never rank on raw ROI â€” it surfaces the luckiest, not the best | â¬œ |
| SG-3 | Minimum trade count enforced **per window**. Show "insufficient history" rather than a number we don't trust | â¬œ |
| SG-4 | Surface divergence across windows as a finding â€” strong on 30d and weak on 24h means decaying | â¬œ |
| SG-5 | Never display follower counts or popularity rankings | â¬œ |
| SG-6 | Capacity estimate: does this master trade tokens deep enough to be copyable at scale | â¬œ |
| SG-7 | Token backfill continues to discover candidate masters from on-chain history | âœ… `discoverFromToken` in `apps/indexer/src/index.ts` |

### 5.5 Per-venue execution

Three venues, three genuinely different execution models. Treat them as separate
implementations behind one interface, not as one path with flags.

**Solana â€” token swaps**

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SOL-1 | Execute via Jupiter quote â†’ build â†’ Jito bundle | ðŸŸ¡ built (`jupiter-jito-runtime.ts`), **not certified**, and not the default |
| SOL-2 | Retire the Trojan bot path. Order is non-negotiable: certify (`S3-9`) â†’ flip `SOLANA_EXECUTOR` â†’ delete Trojan (`S3-6`) | â¬œ default is still `trojan` (`solana-executor-selection.ts:39`) |
| SOL-3 | Add pre-trade simulation | â¬œ absent repo-wide |
| SOL-4 | Slippage bounded by per-user `max_slippage_bps` as a ceiling | ðŸŸ¡ column exists in `049`; call site still uses a flat 150 bps default |
| SOL-5 | Jito tip recorded as a real cost on landed bundles only; never fabricated for an unobserved outcome | âœ… (`S4-P18`, pending review) |
| SOL-6 | Priority fee stays unset while Jito-only; becomes mandatory if we ever fan out to multi-path senders | âœ… current behaviour is correct for Jito-only |

**Robinhood Chain â€” Uniswap V3 swaps**

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RHC-1 | **No MEV protection is needed.** Robinhood Chain runs a single sequencer, so there is no public mempool to front-run from | âœ… by decision â€” do not build it |
| RHC-2 | Document the replacement trust assumption: the sequencer can reorder or censor. Chain-level, not something we defend against | â¬œ |
| RHC-3 | Approvals via Permit2 if the router supports it; otherwise a rolling bounded allowance to a pinned router | â¬œ today it approves the exact amount on essentially every trade (`robinhood.ts:683`) â€” two blocks of latency and 2Ã— gas per mirror |
| RHC-4 | **Per-user nonce allocation** â€” advisory lock on `(chain, account)` plus per-user queue concurrency | â¬œ **correctness bug under fan-out, not an optimisation.** Today: `getPendingNonce` then local `nonce++` on one shared operator key. Two concurrent jobs for one user read the same nonce, both submit, one is silently replaced, and a fill vanishes with no error |
| RHC-5 | Per-user native gas minimum, USD-denominated and priced live; skip-with-reason when unpriceable | â¬œ |

**Polymarket â€” prediction market order book**

The mirroring promise is weakest here, because an order can partially fill or not
fill at all. A master's fill at 0.62 does not mean 0.62 is available to us.

| # | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PM-1 | Orders are **FAK with a maximum price bound derived from the master's fill.** A resting order is not mirroring | â¬œ |
| PM-2 | Exit-order failure escalates the limit, then alerts. Never leave a user silently holding a position their master has left | â¬œ |
| PM-3 | Sub-minimum or off-tick orders skip with a reason. Never round â€” rounding changes the user's price | â¬œ |
| PM-4 | negRisk representation is preserved, not normalised. Buying NO on one outcome is not the same position as buying YES across the complement | ðŸŸ¡ `polymarket-negrisk.ts` exists; copy-path preservation â“ |
| PM-5 | Staleness bound is a **fraction of remaining time-to-resolution**, not a constant | â¬œ |
| PM-6 | Redemption is a first-class exit path â€” if the master holds to resolution, the sell mirror never fires | ðŸŸ¡ `polymarket-redemption.ts` + `046` exist; wiring to mirroring â“ |
| PM-7 | Geo-eligibility re-verified per user; execution stops after 7 days without a verified login | â¬œ provisional pending legal review |

## 6. Architecture at a glance

Nine services in a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo, communicating over Redis and
Postgres. Each runs independently.

```
indexer     ingests wallet activity (Helius for Solana, viem logs for EVM,
            Data API for Polymarket) â†’ publishes swap events to Redis
                    â†“
signal-engine   turns a master's trade into a per-user copy signal
                (`source_trade`), enqueues to BullMQ
                    â†“
trade-executor  sizes, risk-checks, and executes per venue (paper or live)
                    â†“
alert-service   Telegram notifications
scorer          nightly wallet metrics/tiers/clusters + mark-to-market
discovery       nightly candidate-master discovery
api             Fastify control plane
web             Next.js dashboard
mcp-server      tooling surface
```

Two messaging mechanisms, deliberately distinct: **Redis pub/sub** for
fire-and-forget control signals, **BullMQ** for durable work. Don't conflate them.

**Invariant every contributor must know:** all wallet and transaction addresses
are stored **chain-prefixed** as `${chain}:${rawAddress}` â€” e.g.
`solana:ABC...`, `polygon:0x...`. Never write a bare address into a prefixed
column. See `packages/shared/src/address.ts`.

**Migrations replay.** `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` has no applied-migrations
table; it re-runs every `.sql` file on every invocation under an advisory lock.
Every migration must be idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`, guarded constraint adds) or
it breaks `pnpm db:migrate` for everyone on the second run.

---

## 7. Constraints that shape the product

These are not bugs to fix. They are facts to design around.

### 7.1 We are not in the latency race, but latency is now the product

Under the old cluster-consensus model, a 15-second detection cycle was
defensible â€” consensus takes seconds to form anyway. Under "when he buys, you
buy" it is not. The existing `SOLANA_SIGNAL_TO_ALERT_TARGET_MS = 60_000` target
is no longer a target; it is a defect.

We currently detect via Helius **webhooks**, which Helius's own documentation
places at its highest-latency tier and recommends for "low-volume
server-to-server work" â€” while listing copy trading under preconfirmations â†’ raw
shreds â†’ preprocessed transactions.

**The plan we are on gates most of that ladder, so the realistic upgrade is
narrower than it first appears.** On the **Free** tier: LaserStream **gRPC** is
Business+, **preconfirmations** are Professional+, **preprocessed transactions**
are Professional+, and **raw shreds** cost $1,000/month per IP seat. What is
available is **LaserStream WebSocket** â€” documented as up to **200 ms** faster
than standard Agave RPC websockets, serving `transactionSubscribe` among others,
with **no replay**.

So the v1 move is webhooks â†’ **LaserStream WebSocket**. That is a real
improvement at no cost, and it is the launch dependency. Two things follow: do
not design against gRPC, preconfirmations or shreds until someone decides to pay
for a tier; and because the Free tier has **no replay**, a dropped connection
loses events, so the 15-second poll stays as the authoritative backstop rather
than becoming redundant.

At every tier, shreds and preprocessed transactions carry transaction data only,
not account state â€” so anything reading a bonding curve or token balance needs a
subscription path regardless. This is a two-source design, not a swap.

We still will not beat dedicated snipers, and should not pretend to. The goal is
to be fast enough that mirroring is honest, not to win a race.

### 7.2 Solana history backfill is slow, and that is fine

Measured, not estimated:

| Chain | Mechanism | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solana | one `getSignaturesForAddress` (â‰¤1000), then `getTransaction` in batches of 5 with a 150 ms sleep, then sequential processing | ~5 s quiet wallet; **90 s â€“ 2.5 min** at the 1000-signature cap |
| Robinhood Chain | `getLogs` in 2000-block chunks | seconds |
| Polymarket | Data API, 500/page, windowed offset paging | seconds |

Solana is slowest because it has no plural `getTransaction` RPC â€” 200 sequential
round trips minimum. **Backfill is not on the critical path for copying**: live
mirroring needs the wallet subscribed to the data stream, not its history. Hence
UX-5.

**A previously-noted "cheap win" here is withdrawn.** Raising
`BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE` above 5 and dropping the 150 ms pacing would cut this 4â€“5Ã—
*if* the plan allowed the concurrency â€” on the **Free** tier it does not, and the
conservative pacing is correct rather than timid. Revisit only if the plan
changes.

### 7.3 The Polymarket relayer quota caps user count

10,000 orders/day, platform-wide. One active master copied by enough users
exhausts it. This limits how many users we can serve on that venue, not just how
many trades â€” hence CP-4 and CP-5.

### 7.4 Live execution is gated, deliberately

A chain executes live only when **both** hold: it is listed in
`LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` (operator intent) **and** it has an active reviewed row in
`chain_certifications` pointing at evidence under `docs/certification/` with a
valid checksum. Failing either silently downgrades to paper. `TRADING_MODE=paper`
and `AUTO_EXECUTE=false` stay set unless live execution has been explicitly
reviewed. Do not work around this to test something.

## 9. Success criteria

Proposed, needs sign-off â€” numbers marked **[proposed]** are starting points, not
decisions.

| Criterion | Measure |
| --- | --- |
| Mirrors actually mirror | Median tracking difference vs the master's fill, reported per venue. Target **[proposed]** and to be set from observed data, not guessed |
| Nothing silently diverges | Zero mirrors executed without a recorded reason; zero fabricated fills or fees |
| Exits are as reliable as entries | Sell-mirror fill rate within a stated band of buy-mirror fill rate |
| Capacity is honest | Every capacity refusal has an internal reason code and a generic user message |
| No cohort self-harm | Measured price impact attributable to our own copy flow, per `(master, token)` |
| Custody claim holds | An infrastructure compromise can cause bad trades, never balance theft |
