# Domain Docs

How the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.

This repo is **single-context**: one `CONTEXT.md` and one `docs/adr/` at the root. SWAT is a pnpm monorepo, but its services share a single domain vocabulary (wallets, clusters, signals, chains), so the glossary is not split per package.

## Before exploring, read these

- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root.
- **`docs/adr/`** â€” read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in.

If any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.

## File structure

```
/
â”œâ”€â”€ CONTEXT.md
â”œâ”€â”€ docs/adr/
â”‚   â”œâ”€â”€ 0001-chain-prefixed-addresses.md
â”‚   â””â”€â”€ 0002-redis-pubsub-vs-bullmq.md
â”œâ”€â”€ apps/
â””â”€â”€ packages/
```

## Use the glossary's vocabulary

When your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids.

If the concept you need isn't in the glossary yet, that's a signal â€” either you're inventing language the project doesn't use (reconsider) or there's a real gap (note it for `/domain-modeling`).

## Flag ADR conflicts

If your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:

> _Contradicts ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders) â€” but worth reopening becauseâ€¦_

==> docs/agents/issue-tracker.md <==
# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and PRDs for this repo live as GitHub issues on [`xamie01/SWAT`](https://github.com/xamie01/SWAT). Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

> **Prerequisite:** the `gh` CLI is not yet installed on this machine. Install it (`sudo apt install gh` or see [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com)) and run `gh auth login` before any skill can read or write issues.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v` â€” `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either â€” resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies** â€” the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/xamie01/SWAT/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/xamie01/SWAT/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only â€” the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me` â€” the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

# Polygon / Polymarket Certification

Status: **NOT CERTIFIED**

This file is an evidence checklist for the Polymarket CLOB V2 executor on Polygon. It must not be used to enable `polygon` in `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` until every runtime and manual gate below has concrete, redacted evidence and an independent reviewer has signed off.

## Verification Checklist

1. **Authentication (F-PM3, G3-P3)**
   - [ ] Pin the current official production CLOB V2 SDK and Polygon chain ID 137.
   - [ ] Record the explicit signer, account wallet/funder, and resolved signature type without recording signer material.
   - [ ] Derive or load authenticated L2 credentials without logging them.
   - [ ] Record a successful authenticated account/order round trip.
   - [ ] Attach the registered `bytes32` builder code before signing every order and verify matched attribution.

2. **Collateral & Sizing (F-PM4)**
   - [ ] Verify pUSD (`0xC011a7E12a19f7B1f670d46F03B03f3342E82DFB`) balance using 6-decimal units.
   - [ ] Where needed, record a confirmed USDC.e-to-pUSD wrap through the official CollateralOnramp.
   - [ ] Record bounded, least-privilege allowances for the onramp and both current V2 exchange contracts; never record or grant an unlimited ERC-20 allowance.
   - [ ] Prove BUY sizing includes platform/builder fees and SELL sizing cannot exceed confirmed outcome shares.

3. **Execution Rules (F-PM5, F-PM6)**
   - [ ] Attest the current CTF Exchange V2, Neg Risk Exchange V2, pUSD, onramp, CTF, and wallet contracts against official sources and deployed bytecode.
   - [ ] Re-read the correct outcome-token book immediately before submission and enforce market-state, staleness, depth, deviation, and near-certainty gates.
   - [ ] Prove tick-size/minimum-size rounding for standard and neg-risk markets.
   - [ ] Prove proportional SELL execution for the exact outcome token.

4. **Safety & Reconciliation (G3-P7, G3-P8, G3-P9)**
   - [ ] Prove stable client-order idempotency and duplicate retry rejection.
   - [ ] Record a tiny filled BUY with the CLOB order ID, trade IDs, actual matched size, average price, fees, and settlement transaction hash from the venue.
   - [ ] Record an unfillable order that cancels cleanly and a partial fill whose remainder is cancelled.
   - [ ] Prove restart reconciliation for unresolved submitted/matched/mined states without resubmission.
   - [ ] Keep the CLOB order ID separate from settlement transaction hashes.

5. **Context and Operator Review (G3-P1, G3-P2, G3-P5)**
   - [ ] Attach the existing non-empty, 100%-coverage market-context acceptance evidence.
   - [ ] Confirm the operator account, jurisdiction, venue terms, and funding source are eligible.
   - [ ] Reconcile the final pUSD and outcome-token balances against every recorded fill.

## Evidence

- Live BUY order ID: pending
- Venue trade IDs: pending
- Settlement transaction hash: pending
- Cancelled order ID: pending
- Duplicate client-order rejection: pending
- Restart-reconciled order ID: pending
- Reviewer: pending
- Review date: pending

## Conclusion

`polygon` remains clamped to paper. Unit and fixture tests can validate implementation contracts, but they cannot substitute for authenticated canaries, balance reconciliation, operator eligibility, or reviewer sign-off.

==> docs/dg-8/wake-execution-decisions-report.md <==
# WAKE â€” Execution Authority Design Decisions
**Companion to ADR-0003 (Delegated Execution Authority) and AUDIT-FIX-CHECKLIST.md Â§7.1**
Date: 2026-08-11 Â· Status: Decided (pending implementation) unless marked Open

This report closes out the open decision points flagged in ADR-0003 and the
S4-P10/P12/P15/P16 checklist items, plus the Jito tip-handling gaps identified
during design review. Each item below states the decision, the reasoning
behind it, and what's still open.

---

## 1. DG-9 â€” Polymarket custody while a user is offline

**Decision: Fork (b) â€” hold the key, scoped and disclosed.**

WAKE will hold an encrypted copy of each user's Polymarket signer key, scoped
*only* to their Polymarket wallet â€” never their Solana or EVM funds. This is
custodial for that one venue, by necessity: Polymarket requires a signature
from the user's own key for every order, and there is no restricted or
delegated version of that key available. The alternative (fork a, defer live
execution) was rejected in favor of keeping copy-trading functional on this
venue.

**Required before this ships:** an explicit consent/disclosure step at
Polymarket-wallet setup, stating plainly that WAKE holds this key and what
that means if WAKE is compromised. This is a UX/legal deliverable, not an
engineering one â€” copy should be reviewed alongside DG-2.

**Open:** DG-2's underlying legal question (money-transmitter exposure from
holding user funds, even venue-scoped) has not been reviewed by counsel. This
decision assumes that review clears it; if it doesn't, DG-9 needs revisiting.

---

## 2. DG-3 / S4-P10 â€” EVM session-key permission policy

**Decision: Use a vendor for wallet infrastructure; build the permission
check ourselves regardless of what the vendor claims to support.**

Vendors (Privy, Alchemy, ZeroDev) will be evaluated and used for wallet
creation, UX, and bundler/paymaster infrastructure. But the assumption going
in is that none of them restrict `approve` calls by *spender address* â€” only
by function name â€” which is the actual security-critical check (a session
key scoped to "may call `approve`" can still approve an attacker's address
directly, bypassing any router-level restriction). WAKE will build and own
this argument-level check as a policy layer sitting in front of signing,
independent of vendor answers.

**Open:** which vendor, and the exact schema for the policy layer (target
contract + function selector + allowed argument values per delegation). This
is the natural fit for the planned `047_user_execution_grants` migration's
`scope_policy` column â€” not yet designed in detail.

---

## 3. S4-P12 â€” Solana delegated execution (non-custodial vault)

**Decision: Build a custom Anchor program**, using a program-owned vault
account (Program Derived Address) per user rather than any form of held key
or session key. Key properties, as designed:

- **No private key exists for the vault** â€” it's a PDA, mathematically
  keyless. There's nothing to steal or store.
- **`execute_swap`** is signed by WAKE's operator key, but that key only
  authenticates the request. The instruction independently checks that the
  swap's source and destination token accounts both belong to the vault
  itself, and that the CPI target is the verified Jupiter program ID â€” so a
  compromised operator key can trigger swaps but cannot redirect funds
  anywhere else.
- **`withdraw`** requires the *original depositor's own signature* â€”
  never the operator's. This is the actual kill switch: even a fully
  compromised WAKE backend cannot move funds out arbitrarily.
- **`revoke_executor`** is an immediate, user-signed, on-chain kill switch â€”
  not a database flag WAKE promises to honor.
- **Vault `owner` is set once, at `initialize_vault`, and is permanent.**
  Decision confirmed: no recovery path if a user loses access to their
  wallet â€” same trade-off as any self-custody product. This was deliberate,
  not an oversight: an editable owner field would reintroduce the exact
  attack surface (redirect withdrawals) the design exists to remove.

A design skeleton (`wake-vault-skeleton.rs`) was produced covering the vault,
config, and swap-forwarding logic. It is a scaffold, not deployable code â€”
Jupiter's program ID and CPI account shape still need verification against
current docs before any devnet work begins.

**Open / next steps, in order:**
1. Quick sanity check on whether Squads V4 already covers this (low-cost,
   worth doing before committing engineering time, even though it isn't
   blocking anything today).
2. Formalize the spec above into an ADR-0004-style document before writing
   real Rust.
3. Budget audit lead time (multiple weeks, real cost) the same way Polymarket
   Verified status is budgeted â€” not something scheduled after the build is
   "basically done."

---

## 4. S4-P16 â€” Geo-eligibility staleness

**Decision: 7-day staleness window.**

A user's location is checked at signup and re-verified whenever they log in.
If more than 7 days pass without a fresh, verified login, WAKE stops
automated Polymarket execution for that account until they return and
re-verify. This closes the gap where the compliance check was reading WAKE's
server location instead of the user's.

**Open:** this is implemented as a policy default, not yet reviewed by
counsel as part of DG-2. Treat 7 days as provisional until that review
happens.

---

## 5. S4-P15 â€” Polymarket relayer capacity

**Decision: alert and skip, no queuing.**

When the platform is at or near the daily relayer cap, trades that can't be
placed are **skipped with a logged reason** and the operator is alerted â€”
they are not deferred to the next day. This was a deliberate change from an
earlier "queue for tomorrow" answer: a queued trade executing a day later is
no longer actually copying the signal it was meant to copy â€” the tracked
wallet's position may have already changed, so a late fill risks acting on a
stale signal rather than the one it was supposed to mirror. Skip-and-alert
avoids that failure mode entirely.

**Decision: file for Verified relayer status once the platform hits the
100/day Unverified cap with sustained contention for 2 consecutive weeks.**
This will be tracked as a metric (consecutive days at cap with skipped
trades), not as an actual trade queue â€” purely to build a concrete usage
record to present to Polymarket's Builder team when applying.

**Open:** the specific metric/dashboard for "days at cap" doesn't exist yet
and needs to be built alongside the skip-and-alert logic â€” it's the trigger
for the 2-week filing decision, so it needs to exist before that clock can
start.

---

## 6. Jito tip handling (Solana, per-user execution)

Five separate issues, each addressed:

**Tip-as-attack-surface (paying tips means sending SOL to an address).**
Bounded by design: `pay_jito_tip` in the vault program enforces both a
per-call cap (`max_tip_lamports`) and an allowlist (`tip_accounts`), both
read from the shared `WakeConfig` account. Worst case on a compromised
operator key: tip-sized drains to Jito's own validators, capped per call â€”
vandalism, not theft, but still worth the cap.

**Hardcoded allowlist as a liveness risk.**
Resolved structurally: the allowlist lives in `WakeConfig`, a single
admin-updatable account, not baked into each user's vault grant. Rotating
Jito's tip addresses becomes one config update instead of a
re-consent flow for every user. **This same fix should be applied today,
independent of the Solana vault timeline** â€” `JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS` in
`packages/shared/src/jito.ts` is currently a hardcoded constant and has the
identical liveness problem right now, for the single-operator path.

**Per-user SOL minimum: calculated per user**, based on their position size
and expected trade frequency â€” not a flat platform-wide number, and not left
to the user to self-determine. Checked at onboarding and before each trade,
with a clear "add SOL" error rather than a generic execution failure.

**Open:** the actual formula (how position size and trade frequency map to a
SOL minimum) hasn't been specified yet â€” this needs a first pass before it
can be implemented.

**Tip fairness: hybrid â€” platform sets a floor, users can add more on top.**
This avoids the worst version of pay-to-win (nobody can buy their way below
the floor), but it's worth being direct about the trade-off: users who choose
to add more than the floor will still get systematically better inclusion
odds than users who don't, on the same signal, inside the same product. The
original recommendation was a strict uniform tip specifically to avoid this.
The hybrid is a reasonable middle ground, but it's a deliberate reopening of
a smaller version of the same fairness question â€” worth revisiting if it
becomes a visible complaint once real users are on Solana.

**Tips must enter P&L.** Not a preference decision â€” a fix. `tipLamports` is
already computed in `jupiter-jito-runtime.ts` but discarded; `persistTrade()`
already has an unused `feeUsd` parameter for exactly this. The fix is to
thread the lamport amount through `JupiterJitoResolution`, convert it to USD,
and pass it into the existing parameter â€” only when a bundle actually lands,
since atomic bundles mean a missed trade is never charged a tip.

---

## Summary table

| ID | Item | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| DG-9 | Polymarket custody | Hold key, scoped + disclosed |
| DG-3 / S4-P10 | EVM permission policy | Vendor for infra, build spender-check ourselves |
| S4-P12 | Solana delegation | Custom Anchor vault, immutable owner, no recovery path |
| S4-P16 | Geo staleness | 7-day window since last verified login |
| S4-P15 | Relayer cap behavior | Alert + skip, no queuing |
| S4-P15 | Verified filing trigger | 100/day cap + 2 weeks sustained contention |
| Jito #1 | Tip attack surface | Capped + allowlisted in vault program |
| Jito #2 | Allowlist liveness | Central config, not baked into grants (fix now in `jito.ts` too) |
| Jito #3 | Per-user SOL minimum | Calculated per user (formula: open) |
| Jito #4 | Tip fairness | Hybrid floor + optional user boost (residual pay-to-win noted) |
| Jito #5 | Tip P&L accounting | Thread into existing `feeUsd` param, only on landed bundles |

## Open items carried forward

- DG-2 legal review (money-transmitter exposure, staleness-window sign-off) â€” not yet done, gates DG-9 and S4-P16.
- Squads V4 evaluation for S4-P12 â€” not yet done, do before committing to custom-program build.
- Vendor selection for DG-3 (Privy vs Alchemy vs ZeroDev).
- `047_user_execution_grants.scope_policy` schema design.
- Per-user SOL minimum formula.
- "Days at cap" metric/dashboard build for the Verified filing trigger.
- Audit vendor + timeline for the Solana vault program.

==> docs/dg-8/wake-vault-skeleton.rs <==
// programs/wake-vault/src/lib.rs
//
// WAKE non-custodial execution vault (S4-P12, ADR-0003 Â§3).
//
// DESIGN SKELETON, NOT A DEPLOYABLE PROGRAM. Missing: Anchor.toml/Cargo.toml
// boilerplate, associated-token-account creation helpers, the full set of
// #[derive(Accounts)] structs (two are shown; the rest follow the same
// pattern), and â€” critically â€” the Jupiter program id below MUST be verified
// against Jupiter's current docs before this touches mainnet. Jupiter has
// changed this across versions; a stale id here is a silent security hole,
// not a compile error, because `invoke_signed` will happily CPI into
// whatever address is configured.
//
// The property this buys: even a fully compromised WAKE operator key can
// only trigger swaps *inside* a user's own vault. It cannot move funds to
// any other address. Only the original depositor's own signature can do
// that, via `withdraw`. That is the whole design.

use anchor_lang::prelude::*;
use anchor_lang::solana_program::instruction::{AccountMeta, Instruction};
use anchor_lang::solana_program::program::invoke_signed;
use anchor_spl::token::{Token, TokenAccount};
use std::str::FromStr;

declare_id!("Vau1t1111111111111111111111111111111111111"); // placeholder â€” real id assigned at first deploy

pub mod jupiter {
    // Jupiter Aggregator program id. VERIFY at https://station.jup.ag before
    // any mainnet deploy â€” do not trust this constant as-is.
    pub const PROGRAM_ID: &str = "JUP6LkbZbjS1jKKwapdHNy74zcZ3tLUZoi5QNyVTaV";
}

#[program]
pub mod wake_vault {
    use super::*;

    /// One-time setup. Called by the USER's own wallet â€” WAKE never signs
    /// this. Creates the vault PDA and records who may withdraw from it
    /// (owner) and who may trigger swaps in it (executor_authority, read
    /// from the shared config so it can be rotated without touching every
    /// vault â€” same reasoning as moving JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS out of a hardcoded
    /// constant).
    pub fn initialize_vault(ctx: Context<InitializeVault>) -> Result<()> {
        let vault = &mut ctx.accounts.vault;
        vault.owner = ctx.accounts.user.key();
        vault.executor_authority = ctx.accounts.config.executor;
        vault.bump = ctx.bumps.vault;
        vault.revoked = false;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Immediate, on-chain kill switch. User-signed only. This is what makes
    /// S4-P9's "expiry is a liveness dependency" concern moot for Solana:
    /// revocation isn't a database flag WAKE promises to honor, it's enforced
    /// by every subsequent execute_swap call failing the revoked check below.
    pub fn revoke_executor(ctx: Context<RevokeExecutor>) -> Result<()> {
        ctx.accounts.vault.revoked = true;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn restore_executor(ctx: Context<RevokeExecutor>) -> Result<()> {
        ctx.accounts.vault.revoked = false;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Executes a swap sourced from and settled back into the SAME vault.
    ///
    /// Signed by WAKE's operator key â€” but that key only proves "this
    /// request came from WAKE's backend". It grants no authority beyond what
    /// the constraints below check. `jupiter_ix_data` is the raw instruction
    /// Jupiter's Swap API already returns today (same call
    /// `buildJupiterSwap` in jupiter-jito-runtime.ts makes) â€” this program
    /// does not reimplement Jupiter's routing, it validates the instruction's
    /// shape and forwards it via CPI with the vault's own signer seeds.
    pub fn execute_swap<'info>(
        ctx: Context<'_, '_, '_, 'info, ExecuteSwap<'info>>,
        jupiter_ix_data: Vec<u8>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let vault = &ctx.accounts.vault;
        require!(!vault.revoked, VaultError::ExecutorRevoked);
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.executor.key(),
            vault.executor_authority,
            VaultError::UnauthorizedExecutor
        );

        // The two checks that actually matter. Jupiter's instruction names
        // its own source/destination token accounts explicitly â€” if either
        // one isn't owned by this vault, this is an attempted redirect and
        // the whole point of the program is defeated. Neither check is
        // optional and neither is inferred from caller-supplied intent.
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.jupiter_program.key(),
            Pubkey::from_str(jupiter::PROGRAM_ID).unwrap(),
            VaultError::UnknownCpiTarget
        );
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.source_token_account.owner,
            vault.key(),
            VaultError::SourceNotVault
        );
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.destination_token_account.owner,
            vault.key(),
            VaultError::DestinationNotVault
        );

        let owner_key = vault.owner;
        let bump = vault.bump;
        let seeds: &[&[u8]] = &[b"vault", owner_key.as_ref(), &[bump]];

        // Route accounts vary per swap (that's why they're remaining_accounts
        // rather than a fixed list) â€” but every account in a Jupiter route
        // instruction is either the program itself, a pool/market account, or
        // one of the two token accounts already checked above. Nothing here
        // grants the instruction data any authority the checks above didn't.
        let ix = Instruction {
            program_id: ctx.accounts.jupiter_program.key(),
            accounts: ctx
                .remaining_accounts
                .iter()
                .map(|a| AccountMeta {
                    pubkey: a.key(),
                    is_signer: a.is_signer,
                    is_writable: a.is_writable,
                })
                .collect(),
            data: jupiter_ix_data,
        };
        invoke_signed(&ix, ctx.remaining_accounts, &[seeds])?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Pays a Jito tip from the vault â€” bounded and allowlisted, both read
    /// from WakeConfig rather than hardcoded, so rotating Jito's tip
    /// addresses is one config update, not a re-consent flow for every user.
    pub fn pay_jito_tip(ctx: Context<PayJitoTip>, lamports: u64) -> Result<()> {
        let vault = &ctx.accounts.vault;
        require!(!vault.revoked, VaultError::ExecutorRevoked);
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.executor.key(),
            vault.executor_authority,
            VaultError::UnauthorizedExecutor
        );
        require!(
            lamports <= ctx.accounts.config.max_tip_lamports,
            VaultError::TipExceedsCap
        );
        require!(
            ctx.accounts.config.tip_accounts.contains(&ctx.accounts.tip_account.key()),
            VaultError::TipAccountNotAllowlisted
        );
        // system_program::transfer from the vault PDA to tip_account, signed
        // with the same seeds pattern as execute_swap. Worst case on a
        // stolen operator key: tip-sized drains to Jito's own validators â€”
        // vandalism, not theft, and bounded by max_tip_lamports per call.
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The ONLY path funds leave to an address other than the vault's own
    /// swaps. Requires the ORIGINAL DEPOSITOR's signature â€” never the
    /// operator's. This is what makes revoke_executor meaningful: even a
    /// fully compromised WAKE backend cannot call this successfully.
    pub fn withdraw(ctx: Context<Withdraw>, amount: u64) -> Result<()> {
        require_keys_eq!(
            ctx.accounts.owner.key(),
            ctx.accounts.vault.owner,
            VaultError::NotOwner
        );
        // token::transfer from the vault's token account to the owner's own
        // associated token account, signed with the vault's PDA seeds.
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[account]
pub struct Vault {
    pub owner: Pubkey,              // original depositor â€” the ONLY withdraw target
    pub executor_authority: Pubkey, // WAKE's current operator key, set at init from WakeConfig
    pub revoked: bool,
    pub bump: u8,
}

#[account]
pub struct WakeConfig {
    pub executor: Pubkey,          // rotate WAKE's operator key here, not per-vault
    pub tip_accounts: Vec<Pubkey>, // the Jito allowlist â€” one place to update, not baked per-grant
    pub max_tip_lamports: u64,
    pub admin: Pubkey,             // ideally a multisig, not a single key
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct InitializeVault<'info> {
    #[account(mut)]
    pub user: Signer<'info>, // the depositor, signing their own account creation
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = user,
        space = 8 + 32 + 32 + 1 + 1,
        seeds = [b"vault", user.key().as_ref()],
        bump
    )]
    pub vault: Account<'info, Vault>,
    pub config: Account<'info, WakeConfig>,
    pub system_program: Program<'info, System>,
}

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct ExecuteSwap<'info> {
    #[account(seeds = [b"vault", vault.owner.as_ref()], bump = vault.bump)]
    pub vault: Account<'info, Vault>,
    pub executor: Signer<'info>, // WAKE's operator key â€” proves the request's origin only
    /// CHECK: identity checked against jupiter::PROGRAM_ID above, not trusted from caller
    pub jupiter_program: UncheckedAccount<'info>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub source_token_account: Account<'info, TokenAccount>,
    #[account(mut)]
    pub destination_token_account: Account<'info, TokenAccount>,
    pub token_program: Program<'info, Token>,
}

#[error_code]
pub enum VaultError {
    #[msg("executor authority has been revoked for this vault")]
    ExecutorRevoked,
    #[msg("signer is not this vault's authorized executor")]
    UnauthorizedExecutor,
    #[msg("CPI target is not the configured Jupiter program")]
    UnknownCpiTarget,
    #[msg("swap source account is not owned by this vault")]
    SourceNotVault,
    #[msg("swap destination account is not owned by this vault")]
    DestinationNotVault,
    #[msg("tip exceeds the configured per-transaction cap")]
    TipExceedsCap,
    #[msg("tip account is not on the configured allowlist")]
    TipAccountNotAllowlisted,
    #[msg("only the original depositor may withdraw")]
    NotOwner,
}

==> docs/plans/BUILDER-GUIDE.md <==
# SWAT Unified Builder Guide

**The single build order for taking SWAT from its current state to the final product.** This guide merges three sources into one sequence and resolves their conflicts:

1. `AUDIT-FIX-CHECKLIST.md` â€” current codebase status: ~120 supported completion marks, ~114 open items after the 2026-07-24 validation review.
2. `docs/plans/saas-conversion-plan.md` â€” the destination: multi-tenant SaaS (auth, per-user tracking, custody, billing, dynamic chains, frontend).
3. `docs/plans/production-decisions.md` â€” the 18 decided infrastructure/scaling/security/database decisions (D1â€“D18).

Where this guide and an older doc disagree, **this guide wins** (it exists to supersede their sequencing). Where this guide is silent on a detail, the source doc is authoritative. Audit item IDs (F-CORE1, G5-R3, â€¦) and decision IDs (D1â€“D18) are kept for traceability.

---

## 1. Destination

A SaaS platform where users sign up (email/password + linked EVM/Solana wallets), track any wallet or token contract with backfilled history, receive signal feeds scoped to what they track, and opt into autonomous execution from a **platform-managed custodial trading wallet**, sized proportionally to the balance and risk % they agreed to. Tiers: Free / Operator / Ultra (billed via Stripe **and** USDC). Ultra unlocks dynamic any-EVM-chain tracking (Chainlist metadata, DeFi Llama top-5 DEXes, CoinGecko pricing). Runs on one hardened US VPS with staging, CI-gated deploys, and the D1â€“D18 posture.

## 2. Where the codebase is today

- **Solid (verified closed):** all of audit Phase 0 (data-corruption, ingestion, safety, API/web/alert repairs), ingestion health end-to-end, execution-mode matrix parsing/gating (G1-M1â€“M4, M6, M7), Polymarket canonical market data (F-PM1/PM2, G3-P1/P2), balance-capped sizing (H1), timestamp/chain-resolution correctness (L14/L15), shadow schema (G4-S1/S4).
- **Open â€” engine gaps:** canonical copy-trade lifecycle has schema but no runtime callers (F-CORE1â€“7); risk enforcement is env-based, not DB-policy-based (G5); mode dispatch incomplete (G1-M5/M8/M9); **`pnpm test` fails, no CI exists, a literal test key sits in the worktree** (G7 area).
- **Open â€” venue executors:** Robinhood live (F-RH, G2-R) and Polymarket live (F-PM3â€“8, G3-P3â€“12) are unbuilt/uncertified; Solana live is Trojan-based and uncertified (F-SOL).
- **Absent entirely:** users, sessions, tenancy, custody, billing, dynamic chains â€” the whole SaaS layer.

## 3. Standing rules (apply to every stage)

These never expire; several come from the audit's Working Rules and carry forward:

1. **Green gate:** `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` pass at every stage exit. No stage is "done" with a red suite. (After Stage 0, CI enforces this.)
2. **Account-parameterization rule:** any execution/risk code touched from now on takes an account/scope parameter with `'operator'` as today's only value. Migration 028's schema already supports this (`target_account`, UNIQUE `(source_trade_id, target_account, execution_mode)` and `(chain, target_account, client_order_id)`). Concretely:
   - Idempotency/client order IDs keyed `(signalId, target_account)` â€” never `signalId` alone (affects F-CORE5, G3-P6, G3-P7).
   - Risk policy resolver signature `resolveRiskPolicy({account, chain})` (G5-R1/R2); exposure caps and daily-cap alerts keyed the same way.
   - Circuit breaker state keyed `(account, chain)` (G5-R3).
   - Mode dispatch resolves `(account, chain)` (G1-M5).
   - Balance readers take a wallet address argument; env wallets become the operator default (`balances.ts`).
   - Executors accept a signer/credentials parameter; `EVM_PRIVATE_KEY` is passed in at the call site, not read deep inside (`robinhood.ts`, `polymarket.ts`, F-PM3/G3-P3).
3. **Idempotency:** source events and executions are idempotent; never infer or fabricate a fill. Deterministic BullMQ job IDs everywhere.
4. **Migrations:** idempotent files, replay model kept (D16); dedicated deploy step, CI double-replay + staging-copy replay; expand-and-contract for breaking changes; destructive statements never ship in the same release as dependent code.
5. **Tenancy (once Stage 2 lands):** `user_id` comes from the session, never the request payload; all per-user SQL goes through the `forUser(userId)` helper layer (D12).
6. **Money safety:** live modes stay clamped by `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` + `chain_certifications`; staging never holds a custody master key or certifications (D2); least-privilege bounded token approvals, never infinite allowances.
7. **Secrets:** SOPS-encrypted env files, never git; nothing secret in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` (D10/D12).

## 4. The build order

Seven stages. Each lists what it pulls from the audit checklist, the SaaS plan, and the production decisions, plus its exit gate. Stages 1â€“2 and 6 can overlap with their predecessors; everything else is sequential.

### Stage 0 â€” Engine hardening + infra baseline
*The shared substrate. Everything else stands on this.*

**Audit items (close these):**
- Canonical lifecycle: F-CORE1â€“F-CORE7, G1-C1, G1-C2 â€” immutable source events with runtime callers, transactional position updates, full execution state machine (requestedâ†’â€¦â†’confirmed/failed/cancelled/reconciliation_required), startup + periodic reconciliation. Built account-parameterized per Standing Rule 2. This goes from important to existential once one signal fans out to N users' funds.
- Mode matrix completion: G1-M5 (off/paper/live/live+shadow dispatch), G1-M8 (real API-backed dashboard controls â€” the workspace toggles are currently hard-coded local state), G1-M9 (mode tests).
- Risk enforcement: G5-R1, G5-R2, G5-R3, G5-R5, G5-R6, G5-R7, L17 â€” one DB-resolved validated risk policy enforced **before claim** in every mode; persisted per-`(account, chain)` breaker; atomic kill switch honored within one cache TTL; gas reserves sized down not floored up. Migrate existing operator config explicitly, don't overwrite.
- Test/CI hygiene: green `pnpm test`; G7-T3 (`pnpm test:integration` + CI with Postgres/Redis services); G7-T4 unit tests (execution config, risk math, breaker state, reconciliation idempotency); remove generated artifacts and the literal test private key from the worktree (Final Repository Gate items); L16 (Jupiter decimal/threshold correctness â€” paper quotes depend on it).

**Production decisions activated:** D1 (provision the box), D2 (staging, paper-clamped), D3 (CI/CD pipeline â€” same CI as G7-T3), D7+D10 (Caddy + Cloudflare + full hardening bundle), D15 (backups + nightly staging restore), D17-now items (`pg_stat_statements`, BRIN on transaction timestamps, `readPool`/`writePool` split in `packages/db`).

**Exit gate:** audit Phase 1 lifecycle exit gate met; risk policy DB-resolved and pre-claim-enforced; CI green on every merge; staging receiving auto-deploys; backups restoring nightly.

### Stage 1 â€” Auth & tenancy (SaaS Phase 1)
*Orthogonal to Stage 0 â€” may start in parallel once CI is green.*

- Migrations 029+: `users`, `user_sessions`, `user_auth_wallets`, `user_api_keys` (argon2id, opaque session tokens, SIWE/SIWS wallet linking).
- `apps/api/src/auth/` module: signup/login/logout/me, wallet nonce+verify; layered auth plugin attaching `request.user` (session cookie or per-user API key); `requireTier()`/`requireRole()` guards; rate limits on auth routes.
- The global `API_KEY` becomes internal serviceâ†’API only and is rotated; `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` is deleted (D12).
- **Audit-log table** for auth/custody/billing/admin events â€” built now per D10/D13 (cheap early, impossible to retrofit); alerts ride the existing Telegram alert-service.

**Exit gate:** signupâ†’loginâ†’wallet-linkâ†’`/v1/auth/me` works end-to-end; cross-tenant test suite scaffolded; browser holds no shared secrets.

### Stage 2 â€” Per-user tracking, backfill, feeds (SaaS Phase 2)

- `user_wallet_subscriptions`, `user_token_watches`; global-dedup model preserved (wallet indexed once, many subscribers); zero-subscriber wallets paused via scorer lifecycle (D9).
- Tier matrix in `packages/shared/src/tiers.ts` â€” single source of truth for quotas/features; API-enforced quotas (free 3 / operator 25 / ultra unlimited wallets; token backfills/day).
- `/v1/me/*` routes (wallets, tokens/backfill, signals, feed) via the `forUser()` helper layer; existing global routes become admin-only.
- Backfill scaling: BullMQ tier priority, 429-aware concurrency within the Helius plan budget (D9).
- Real-time: generalize SSE+ticket to `/v1/me/stream` fed by existing Redis channels, filtered per subscription; retire dashboard polling (D8).
- **Attribution (parallel, non-blocking):** G6-A2â€“A10 â€” outcomes keyed by (signal, mode), all latency stamps written at their real transitions, expectancy persisted and dashboard-exposed. Feeds the per-user dashboards and justifies platform-curated signals.

**Exit gate:** two users track different wallets and see disjoint feeds; quotas enforced; cross-tenant attack tests pass in CI; SSE feed live.

### Stage 3 â€” Venue executors & certification (audit Phases 2â€“3, on demand)
*Pull-based: certify a venue when (and only when) you want live money on it. Paper mode ships everywhere without this stage.*

- **Solana path (DG-1 â€” RESOLVED 2026-07-27): direct Jupiter signing with Jito bundle submission.** The Trojan webhook path is retired; F-SOL2/F-SOL3 are retargeted to certify the new path. Executor spec:
  - **Build:** Jupiter Swap API â€” the quote client already exists (`packages/shared/src/jupiter.ts`); add the `/swap` transaction-build step. Sign locally with the operator wallet now, per-user custodial keys in Stage 4 (the signer is a parameter per Standing Rule 2).
  - **Submit:** Jito block engine `sendBundle` with a tip instruction appended â€” **never broadcast via public RPC**, that's the front-running protection. Bundles are atomic (all-or-nothing), so there is no partial-execution state to reconcile.
  - **Tip sizing:** dynamic from the Jito tip-floor percentile endpoints, bounded by a `JITO_MAX_TIP_LAMPORTS` cap; tip counts against the user's position cost in sizing/P&L.
  - **Confirmation:** poll bundle status + on-chain signature status; on timeout mark `pending_confirmation` and hand to the reconciliation sweeper (same pattern as G2-R9). Resubmission is safe only under the `(signalId, target_account)` idempotency key with the same blockhash-expiry semantics â€” an expired blockhash means a fresh quote+build, never a blind retry.
  - **Fallback policy:** if the Jito block engine is unavailable, fail the job honestly (breaker counts it) rather than silently downgrading to public RPC broadcast â€” a silent downgrade would reintroduce the exact exposure the decision removed. A config flag may later allow explicit RPC fallback per account.
  - **Retirements:** `TROJAN_WEBHOOK_URL`/`TROJAN_API_KEY` env and the Trojan client path are deleted once the new path is certified; `TROJAN_WALLET_ADDRESS` balance reads become the operator signing wallet passed into the parameterized `balances.ts`. The already-closed H4 (Trojan timeout/idempotency) work is superseded with the path.
  - **Certification (retargeted F-SOL2/F-SOL3):** stable idempotency key, returned bundle/signature identity, chain-confirmed fill amounts from the transaction meta, truthful failure/timeout states, then a deliberately capped live canary recorded under `docs/certification/solana.md`. F-SOL1 (canonical event parity) and G1-S1 (latency measurement) are unchanged.
- **Robinhood:** F-RH1â€“F-RH6, G2-R1â€“G2-R13 as specified in the checklist (configured chain tuple, receipt decoding, golden calldata vectors, restart reconciliation, tiny canary, certification doc review) â€” with the signer passed as a parameter (Standing Rule 2).
- **Polymarket:** F-PM3â€“F-PM8, G3-P3â€“G3-P12 â€” credential derivation implemented as a *function of an EVM signer* (per-user-ready), client order ID = `(signalId, target_account)`, book-walking/rounding/fill-polling/reconciliation as specified, canaries + certification doc review.
- Per-chain queue split lands here or at first paying cohort, whichever first: `swat-trades-{solana,polygon,robinhood}`, concurrency 1 each (D6, satisfies F-ACC2 isolation).

**Exit gate (per venue):** the checklist's own certification gate â€” `docs/certification/<chain>.md` reviewed, canary evidence recorded, then and only then the chain enters `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS`.

### Stage 4 â€” Custody & per-user autonomous execution (SaaS Phase 3)
*Hard prerequisites: Stage 0 complete, Stage 2 complete, DG-1 decided, and the legal gate below.*

- **Decision gate (DG-2, non-negotiable):** legal counsel opinion on custodial funds + autonomous trading in the operating jurisdiction; ToS/risk disclosures; Cloudflare geo-blocks live; Polymarket per-user geo-gate (D13). Custody does not launch without this.
- `packages/custody`: per-user Solana + EVM keypairs, envelope encryption (per-key AES-256-GCM data keys, master key only in trade-executor env on the hardened host), `KeyWrapper` interface for the later KMS swap (D11). API can request keygen, never decryption.
- `user_trading_wallets`, `user_balances` (poller reuses parameterized `balances.ts`), `user_execution_settings` (per-chain mode, auto-execute, min score, max position %, daily exposure %, stop loss â€” defaults from `DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG`, live execution tier-gated).
- Deposit (address + QR) and withdraw (**only to SIWE/SIWS-verified linked wallets**, email confirm, daily cap â€” D11's anti-theft core).
- **Fan-out:** on a trade-eligible signal, enumerate eligible users (subscribed âˆ© auto-execute âˆ© chain enabled âˆ© tier âˆ© balance) â†’ one job per `(signal, user)` on the per-chain queue, idempotent via the Stage-0 `(signalId, target_account)` keys; `trades.user_id` added; per-user breaker/exposure/paper-bankroll ride the account-parameterized Stage-0 machinery unchanged.
- Executor network isolation: no inbound connections to the trade-executor container; consider the dedicated custody host split (D5 step 2) at this point.
- Platform-wide gates (`chain_certifications` + `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS`) still clamp on top of user settings.

**Exit gate:** paper-mode fan-out proven for multiple users on one signal with disjoint sizing; withdraw controls tested adversarially; custody keys never observed outside trade-executor (log/API scan); KMS migration path demonstrated on staging.

### Stage 5 â€” Billing (SaaS Phase 4)
*Can overlap Stage 4.*

- `subscriptions` + `payments`; Stripe Checkout + signature-verified webhook; USDC treasury watcher (Solana + Polygon) reusing indexer infra, reference/memo-matched; lifetime tier = `tier_expires_at NULL`; nightly downgrade job with 3-day grace.
- Tier changes write the audit log; billing events alert via Telegram.

**Exit gate:** end-to-end tier grant from both rails on staging (Stripe test mode; USDC on a devnet/testnet or small mainnet canary); downgrade path proven.

### Stage 6 â€” Frontend rebuild (SaaS Phase 6)
*Runs progressively from Stage 1 onward; each backend stage gets its UI as it lands.*

- Foundation first: build-time Tailwind (drop the CDN script), shared `lib/api.ts` (cookie auth, no API key), `middleware.ts` route protection, react-query.
- Stage-1 UI: real signup/login replacing the fake `admin@wake.com` modal; wallet linking via wagmi + RainbowKit + `@solana/wallet-adapter`.
- Stage-2 UI: My Wallets / My Signals / activity feed on the SSE stream; existing `HealthView` + `SignalsView` safety drawer carry over user-scoped.
- Stage-4 UI: trading wallet page (deposit QR, balances, withdraw), risk settings (`RiskExecutionView` rebuilt per-user: their exposure vs agreed risk %, personal kill switch), G1-M8's real API-backed admin mode matrix.
- Stage-5 UI: billing page (Stripe portal + USDC pay). Stage-7 UI: Ultra chain manager.
- Admin area: current global pages behind `role=admin` + IP allowlist.

**Exit gate per slice:** the corresponding backend stage's flows are drivable end-to-end in the browser with no shared secrets and no hard-coded data (this also retires the workspace's remaining mocked copy).

### Stage 7 â€” Ultra dynamic chains (SaaS Phase 5)
*Strictly last: the chain-registry refactor touches audit-hardened code everywhere, and the audit's "no new chains" scope rule expires only when the checklist's engine work is closed. The green suite from Stage 0 is the safety net.*

- `chains` registry table (seed the 3 built-ins); `Chain` union â†’ registry-validated string across the ~15 hard-coded sites (`types.ts`, `address.ts`, `validation.ts`, `execution.ts`, `prices.ts`, `db/wallets.ts` SQL, `trading-control.ts`, SQL CHECKs â†’ FK). Full regression suite is the gate.
- Ultra onboarding: `POST /v1/me/chains` â†’ Chainlist metadata + RPC liveness probe â†’ DeFi Llama top-5 DEXes â†’ CoinGecko platform mapping.
- Custom chains: tracking via parameterized `evm.ts`; **paper-only by default** â€” live requires a supported router config + platform certification, same `chain_certifications` gate as everything else.

**Exit gate:** an Ultra user adds an uncatalogued EVM chain, backfills a wallet on it, and receives feed events â€” with all built-in-chain regression tests green.

## 7. Verification cadence

- **Every merge:** CI â€” typecheck, unit tests, migration double-replay on scratch Postgres, cross-tenant attack suite (from Stage 2), lint for `NEXT_PUBLIC_` secrets.
- **Every stage exit:** integration suite against staging; the stage's exit gate demonstrated (not inferred); diff review for secrets/artifacts/unrelated changes (audit Working Rules, kept verbatim).
- **Before any live-money change:** venue certification evidence under `docs/certification/`, reviewed; canary with capped size; reconciliation-after-restart demonstrated.
- **Continuously:** nightly staging restore proves backups (D15); ingestion-health alerts prove the pipeline (already shipped, G0-H).

==> docs/plans/addition_plan.md <==
WAKE LP Dashboard â€” Coding Build Plan (for GLM 5.3 Flash)
A step-by-step, function-level task list grouped into build tracks. Each task should be built, tested, and confirmed working before moving to the next â€” don't batch multiple tasks into one pass.
How to use this doc
Work through tracks roughly in this order: A first (shared models, nothing else depends-free of it), then B and C (can run in parallel), then D, then E (depends on A + C), then F (depends on E), then G (depends on A + E + F), then H last (depends on everything). Within a track, tasks are already ordered â€” don't skip ahead. Each task should end with a passing test before the next one starts; that's the main lever for keeping a flash-tier model's output reliable across a build this size.
MCP tools worth connecting before starting
â€¢ A GitHub MCP server â€” lets the agent create a branch and commit per finished task instead of one giant diff at the end. With a "one function at a time" approach, a commit boundary per task is the natural checkpoint, and makes a bad step easy to isolate and revert.
â€¢ A Postgres MCP server (or whichever database WAKE runs on) â€” Track A defines new tables/types for positions, pools, and risk scores. Letting the agent inspect and migrate the schema directly avoids it guessing column names that drift from what the rest of WAKE already uses.
â€¢ A Solana RPC MCP server â€” Tracks B, D, E, and F all have a Solana/Meteora path. Live devnet queries while building beat hand-written fixtures, especially for bin-math edge cases.
â€¢ An EVM RPC MCP server pointed at Robinhood Chain â€” same reasoning as above for the Uniswap v3/v4 path (Tracks B, D, E, F).
â€¢ A web-search or docs-fetch MCP tool â€” Meteora's Zap SDK and Uniswap v4's hooks are both young and still moving; having the agent pull current docs mid-task instead of relying on training data saves real debugging time, specifically on Tracks E and F.
Track A â€” Shared data models
1. Position model â€” fields: id, user id, chain, pool address, strategy type (spot/curve/bidask), range bounds, per-rung allocation array, deposit amount + token, status enum (building â†’ active â†’ near_edge â†’ out_of_range â†’ rebalancing â†’ closed), opened-at/closed-at timestamps.
2. Pool model â€” fields: chain, pool address, pair, TVL, active TVL, 24h volume, fee tier, realized fee APR, risk score, last-scanned timestamp.
3. Risk guardrail config model â€” per-user settings: max % of deployed capital per pool (default 50%), profit-bank % on realized gains (default 50%), reserve sub-vault reference.
4. Net LP Result calculator â€” pure function: (feesEarned, impermanentLoss, gasCost, rebalanceCost, inventoryChange) â†’ netResult. No chain calls, no side effects â€” this gets reused by Tracks D, E, and F, so get the signature right here before building anything that depends on it.
Track B â€” Pool scanner
1. Solana/Meteora pool-list fetcher â€” calls Meteora's pool endpoint, returns raw pool list for a given pair or "all pairs."
2. Robinhood Chain pool-list fetcher â€” same for Uniswap v3/v4 pools (subgraph query or direct RPC enumeration, whichever Robinhood Chain tooling supports better right now).
3. Active-TVL calculator â€” per chain: for Meteora, sum liquidity in bins near the active bin; for Uniswap v3/v4, sum liquidity in ticks near the current tick. Two implementations behind one interface.
4. Realized fee APR calculator â€” shared pure function: trailing 24h/7d fees Ã· TVL, taking normalized pool data from either fetcher.
5. Volume/active-liquidity ranking function â€” sorts a pool list by volume-to-active-liquidity ratio; shared across chains since it only needs the normalized Pool model from Track A.
6. Scan job â€” wires 1â€“5 into a single scheduled job that writes results into the Pool model table, tagged by chain.
Track C â€” Token/wallet risk filter
1. Holder-concentration checker â€” top-10 holder percentage, using chain-specific token account queries.
2. Bundled/connected-wallet volume detector â€” heuristic pass: flag wallets funded from a common source within a short time window around launch.
3. Liquidity-lock verifier â€” checks whether LP tokens sit in a locked contract or burn address versus a freely-movable wallet.
4. Mint-authority/permission checker â€” can the deployer mint more supply, pause trading, or blacklist addresses.
5. Risk score combiner â€” folds 1â€“4 into a single score plus a pass/fail gate against the thresholds from the Track A guardrail config.
6. Wire into scanner â€” attach the risk score to every pool the Track B scan job writes, so nothing reaches the Discover feed without one.
Track D â€” LP wallet indexer
1. Solana LP-position reader â€” reads a given wallet's DLMM position accounts.
2. Robinhood Chain LP-position reader â€” reads a given wallet's Uniswap v3/v4 position NFTs.
3. PnL calculator per tracked wallet â€” reuses the Track A Net LP Result function against indexed position history.
4. Tracked-wallet storage layer â€” which wallets are being watched, polling cadence, last-indexed timestamp.
5. Leaderboard query â€” sorts tracked wallets by realized PnL, win rate, and dominant strategy type for the LP Wallets screen.
Track E â€” Ladder / position builder
1. Meteora zap-in wrapper â€” single-token deposit â†’ auto-split via the Zap SDK â†’ opens a position.
2. Meteora ladder builder â€” given a range, rung count, and Spot/Curve/Bid-Ask distribution, computes per-rung bin allocations and calls the zap-in wrapper per rung (check whether the SDK supports batching before assuming one call per rung).
3. Uniswap v3/v4 zap-in wrapper (Robinhood Chain) â€” single-token deposit â†’ swap/split â†’ mints a position.
4. Uniswap v3/v4 ladder builder â€” same per-rung logic as E2, using tick ranges instead of bins.
5. Strategy-template resolver â€” maps a named preset (tight-Spot scalp, deep Bid-Ask accumulation, wide-range dump-capture, passive majors auto-compound) to concrete ladder parameters for either chain.
6. Build-position entrypoint â€” single function taking {chain, pool, template-or-custom-params, deposit}, returning a signed-and-ready transaction bundle. This is what the "Deploy Ladder" button in the UI actually calls.
Track F â€” Position monitor + rebalancer
1. Active-bin/active-tick poller â€” per chain, checks current price position against each open position's range on a schedule.
2. Range-state classifier â€” labels a position active / near_edge / out_of_range based on the poll result.
3. Rebalance economic-check function â€” pure function: expected extra fees vs. (IL + gas + repositioning cost). Build and test this against mock data before wiring it to anything live.
4. Meteora rebalance executor â€” wraps rebalanceDlmmPosition from the Zap SDK.
5. Uniswap v3/v4 rebalance executor â€” close position, swap if needed, remint around the new range.
6. Scheduled wiring â€” runs 1â€“2 on a cadence per open position, calls 3 when a position is near_edge or out_of_range, fires 4 or 5 only when 3 returns a positive result.
Track G â€” Risk guardrail enforcement
1. Pool-exposure-cap check â€” runs before Track E's build-position entrypoint commits; blocks or caps size if it would exceed the per-pool % limit from the Track A config.
2. Profit-banking sweep â€” triggered on position close or fee harvest; moves the configured % of realized gain to the user's reserve sub-vault.
3. Reserve sub-vault model â€” a separate PDA on Solana, a separate address on Robinhood Chain, reusing WAKE's existing non-custodial vault pattern rather than inventing a new custody path.
4. State machine wiring â€” folds 1â€“3 into the same order lifecycle state machine already used for trade execution, rather than running a parallel one.
Track H â€” API / dashboard wiring
1. Discover feed endpoint â€” paginated, sortable, serves Track B+C output.
2. LP Wallets leaderboard endpoint â€” serves Track D output.
3. Position manager endpoint â€” open positions, live PnL, rebalance-recommendation flag, serves Track F output.
4. Strategy template list endpoint â€” serves the Track E5 resolver's available presets.
5. Deploy-ladder action endpoint â€” calls Track E6, gated by Track G1.
Revision â€” self-directed, not auto-managed
LP positions are user-built and user-managed through WAKE's own tools, the same way someone would use Meteora's DLMM interface directly â€” not an algorithm picking pool and range and executing on the user's behalf. Strategy templates and LP-wallet copying stay, but as starting points the user reviews and confirms, not auto-pilot actions. This changes a few pieces of the plan above and adds one new track.
What's unchanged
Tracks A through D, Track E's ladder-building mechanics (E1â€“E4, E6), Track H's endpoints, and the MCP tool list all stay exactly as written â€” none of that logic cares whether a human or an algorithm supplied the final range and distribution parameters.
What changes
â€¢ E5 (strategy-template resolver) no longer feeds E6 directly. It now pre-fills an editable builder state the user can adjust before confirming â€” add a small validation function that checks a user-edited (possibly template-seeded) set of parameters before the confirm action is allowed to call E6.
â€¢ F6 (scheduled wiring) no longer auto-fires the rebalance executor by default. F3's positive result now just flags a recommendation on the position record for the UI to surface. The rebalance executors (F4/F5) only run on an explicit user action, or when a position has the auto-rebalance opt-in flag set (see I4 below).
â€¢ Track G's guardrails are worth revisiting as confirmations rather than hard blocks in a self-directed product â€” flag this as an open decision rather than assuming either way.
New: Track I â€” Manual position builder
1. Live bin/tick-ladder fetch â€” given a selected pool, returns current price plus nearby bin/tick structure and liquidity depth, formatted for a visual range editor.
2. Range/distribution live-preview calculator â€” pure, read-only: given a user-set range, rung count, and Spot/Curve/Bid-Ask choice, computes the resulting per-rung allocation and the range-specific expected fee-capture zone, nothing submitted on-chain. Called on every drag/edit in the UI, so it needs to be fast.
3. Manual-build confirm handler â€” takes the user's final parameters (template-seeded or fully custom) and calls the existing E6 entrypoint. No new on-chain logic, just wiring from the new builder UI.
4. Auto-rebalance opt-in field â€” a per-position boolean added to the Position model from A1. Track F's scheduled wiring checks this flag before auto-firing; otherwise it only flags the recommendation.
5. Manual rebalance trigger endpoint â€” exposes F4/F5 as a user-callable action for a "Rebalance now" button, separate from any auto-path.
Revision 2 â€” reintroducing automation, suggested master wallets, and demo mode
The platform now ships four modes side by side: manual self-directed building (Track I, unchanged), LP-wallet copying (Track D, unchanged), a new fully-autonomous strategy mode for advanced users, and a demo/paper-trading mode scoped specifically to that autonomous mode â€” manual and copy modes don't need simulation since the user directly sees and controls what they're doing.
New: Track J â€” Ingestion layer upgrade (latency-sensitive paths)
Both the wallet-copy and automated-strategy modes need faster-than-polling data. Build this once, shared by both.
1. Solana Geyser stream listener â€” gRPC stream (Triton/Helius-class provider) against the Meteora DLMM program, filtering for addLiquidity / removeLiquidity / claimFee instructions. Replaces polling for any latency-sensitive path; Track D's indexer can still poll for the leaderboard/history views where latency doesn't matter.
2. EVM WebSocket event listener â€” subscribes to Mint / Burn / Collect events on Uniswap v3/v4 pool contracts via a WebSocket RPC connection (Alchemy/QuickNode-class provider), for Robinhood Chain.
3. Unified event schema â€” normalizes both listeners' output into one JSON shape (chain, masterWallet, action, poolAddress, token0/token1, positionId, strategyType, range bounds, raw amounts). Both Track D (copying) and the new Track K (automation) consume this schema rather than chain-specific payloads.
4. Proportional-sizing calculator â€” given a master wallet's absolute position size and a follower's allocated budget, computes the ratio and scales token inputs to match price bounds exactly at a different size. This is the actual math behind "copy," now made precise â€” feeds the existing Mirror flow (Screen 2) instead of leaving it as a vague scaling step.
New: Track K â€” Automated strategy engine (advanced/opt-in mode)
This is a second execution path, separate from Track I's manual builder â€” it runs without a per-action confirm step once a user has opted a position into it.
1. Strategy rule schema â€” a structured, storable definition of an automated strategy: trigger condition, pool-selection rule, liquidity-structuring rule (asset split, bound offsets from current price), monitoring cadence, exit-condition rule. Evil Panda becomes the first entry in this schema, not special-cased code.
2. Trigger evaluator â€” watches for a strategy's entry condition (e.g. volume/TVL ratio crossing a threshold, price pump over a set % in a set window) using Track J's normalized event stream.
3. Pool-selection resolver â€” given a trigger firing, queries Track B's scanner output for the matching pool per the strategy's rule (e.g. "highest fee tier available for this pair").
4. Autonomous ladder builder â€” computes bounds and asset split per the strategy rule and calls Track E's ladder-building primitives directly â€” no user confirm step, this is what distinguishes Track K from Track I.
5. Monitoring loop â€” runs on a short interval (not Track F's economic-gated cadence â€” this mode is meant to watch closely once committed) checking the exit-condition rule against live indicators (e.g. RSI(2), Bollinger Band position) sourced from a price-feed/indicator service.
6. Autonomous exit executor â€” when the exit condition fires, calls remove-liquidity and swap-back as one atomic action, converting back to the base asset. Reuses Track E/F's underlying transaction primitives; the difference from Track F is that this fires without a human approving the specific trade.
7. Strategy library storage â€” persists strategy rule definitions (Track K1) so they can be listed, selected, and (for advanced users) cloned/edited â€” feeds both the Strategy Templates screen and a new "Automated Strategies" surface.
New: Track L â€” Suggested master wallets
1. Wallet-quality scoring function â€” beyond Track D's raw PnL/win-rate, scores tracked wallets on consistency (PnL variance over time, not just total), track record length, and strategy-type diversity â€” feeds a "suggested for new users" subset rather than just the top of the raw leaderboard.
2. New-user onboarding query â€” serves a short curated list from L1's output specifically for users with no tracked wallets yet, surfaced during onboarding rather than requiring the user to find the leaderboard first.
New: Track M â€” Demo mode (scoped to automated strategies only)
Manual building and wallet-copying are not simulated â€” a user directly sees and controls those, so a demo layer adds little. Demo mode exists specifically so a user can trust an automated strategy before opting real capital into it.
1. Virtual balance ledger â€” a per-user demo balance, separate from any real vault, with its own deposit/reset actions (no real token transfer involved).
2. Simulated execution adapter â€” intercepts Track K's autonomous ladder builder (K4) and exit executor (K6) calls when a strategy is running in demo mode: computes the same fills, fees, and bound math against live real-time price/liquidity data, but writes results only to the virtual ledger â€” no transaction is ever built or signed.
3. Demo position state â€” reuses the Position model (A1) and the order lifecycle state machine, tagged isDemo: true, so demo positions appear in the same Position Manager views without polluting real PnL totals or triggering Track G's real-capital guardrails.
4. Demo-to-live promotion flow â€” a function that takes a demo strategy configuration a user is satisfied with and hands it to Track K's real executor path with the user's actual deposit â€” the strategy definition carries over unchanged; only the execution adapter and capital source change.
MCP tools â€” additions for this revision
â€¢ A price/indicator feed MCP tool (or wrapping an existing one like TAAPI or a DEX-data aggregator) â€” Track K5's exit-condition monitoring needs RSI/Bollinger Band-class indicators on short intervals; building that math from raw price ticks in-house is avoidable work.
â€¢ GoPlus Security / RugCheck API access (EVM / Solana respectively) â€” slot into Track C's risk filter as the actual token-safety check (mint-function detection, honeypot flags) rather than building equivalent heuristics from scratch; faster to ship, and this is exactly what Track K3's pool-selection resolver should gate on before an automated strategy ever deploys into a new pool.

### Batch B - Risk controls, account-keyed

All three touch risk sizing. Do B1 first: B2 and B3 read breaker state.

#### B1. Re-key the circuit breaker to `(account, chain)` - DONE 2026-07-31

**Problem:** State is keyed `breaker:${chain}` (`packages/db/src/circuit-breaker.ts:33`). Standing Rule 2 requires `(account, chain)`. One user's failures would trip every user's breaker.

**Fix:**

2. Add `account: string` as the first parameter of `readCircuitBreakerState`, `recordCircuitBreakerFailure`, `recordCircuitBreakerSuccess`, `claimCircuitBreakerProbe`.
3. Update callers in `apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts` (imports at L14, L27, L29, L30; `executeJobWithCircuitBreaker` at L680). Pass `'operator'`.
4. Add `packages/db/sql/033_breaker_account_key.sql`: copy each `breaker:<chain>` config row to `breaker:operator:<chain>`. Idempotent (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). **Keep the old rows** - expand-and-contract, per Standing Rule 4. Delete them in a later release.

**Done when:** breaker tests pass with the account parameter; migration replays twice; old keys still present.
**Closes:** `G5-R3` (reopened under Standing Rule 2)

#### B2. Resolve risk policy from the database - DONE 2026-08-01

**Problem:** `resolveRiskPolicy` does not exist. The DB value `trading.max_position_pct` is read only by `apps/api/src/attribution-routes.ts:43`, for reporting. The executor sizes from environment variables instead (`apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts:341-370`: `PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT`, `USDC_BALANCE_RISK_PCT`, `BASE_POSITION_*`). Changing the DB value has no effect on trading.

**Fix:**
1. Add `resolveRiskPolicy({account, chain})` to `packages/db` (new file, next to `execution-config.ts`). Return one validated object: max position pct, daily exposure pct, stop loss pct, breaker threshold.
2. Precedence, matching `execution-config.ts`: DB `config` row, then env, then `DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG` from `packages/shared/src/constants.ts`.
3. Cache like `getExecutionConfigSnapshot` (30s TTL) so a kill-switch-style change lands within one TTL.
4. Call it in `apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts` **before the claim**, in every mode - not just live.
5. Migrate existing operator config explicitly; never overwrite it (per `H15`).

**Done when:** changing `trading.max_position_pct` in the DB changes position size within 30s, in paper mode, without a restart.
**Closes:** `G5-R1`

#### B3. Enforce stop-loss - DONE 2026-08-01

**Problem:** `stopLossPct: 20` exists in `DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG` (`packages/shared/src/constants.ts:25`) and `config.risk.stop_loss_pct` (migration `001`). The API and dashboard read it. **Nothing enforces it.** No code closes a position on drawdown.

**Fix:**
1. Add `stopLossPct` to the B2 policy object so there is one source.
2. Define the contract: evaluated against which price, on what schedule, emitting which order. The scorer already runs mark-to-market every 5 minutes (`apps/scorer/src/index.ts:171`) - reuse it rather than adding a loop.
3. Enforce it. Emit a sell through the normal canonical path so it inherits idempotency and reconciliation.
4. Alert on trigger through the existing alert queue.

**Done when:** a paper position past the threshold produces exactly one sell, and a test proves it.
**Closes:** `L17` (the only `NOT BUILT` row in Phase 5)

**As built:**
- `packages/db/src/stop-loss.ts` - pure threshold math (`positionDrawdownPct`, `isStopLossBreached`) plus the exactly-once claim (`claimStopLossTrigger` / `releaseStopLossTrigger`).
- `packages/db/sql/034_stop_loss_triggers.sql` - `signal_stop_losses`, primary key `(account, signal_id)`. This row **is** the claim: the entry signal is already `status = 'executed'` by the time a stop-loss fires, so `claimSignalForExecution` can never grant it.
- `packages/db/src/pnl-queries.ts` - `markToMarketOpenPositions` now also returns the positions it priced, so the sweep reuses that pass's prices instead of adding a second polling loop or refetching quotes.
- `apps/scorer/src/stop-loss.ts` - `runStopLossSweep`, fully dependency-injected. Queues one full-position sell on `swat-trades` per breach and publishes `STOP_LOSS_TRIGGERED`. Releases the claim if the enqueue fails so the next sweep retries; an alert failure never undoes a queued exit.
- `apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts` - a `stopLoss` job skips the pending claim, is exempt from `AUTO_EXECUTE` (it only reduces exposure; gating it would leave every position opened while `AUTO_EXECUTE` was off permanently unprotected), and sells `sellTokenAmount` exactly rather than a bankroll-derived size. The chain execution-mode gate, including the `'*' = 'off'` kill switch, still applies.
