import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS,
  InvalidPositionCapError,
  MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS,
  PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS,
  VENUE_MINIMUM_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD,
  assessPositionCap,
  clampConcurrentPositionCap,
  perPositionNotionalUsd
} from './position-cap.js';

describe('clampConcurrentPositionCap (S4-M4 platform ceiling)', () => {
  it('passes an in-range request through untouched', () => {
    expect(clampConcurrentPositionCap(10)).toEqual({
      cap: 10,
      clampedByCeiling: false,
      clampedByFloor: false,
      ceiling: PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS
    });
  });

  it('clamps to the platform ceiling and says the ceiling did it', () => {
    // The UI has to be able to tell the user their number was overridden. A bare
    // clamped value would display a different number than they typed with no
    // explanation.
    const result = clampConcurrentPositionCap(PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS + 450);
    expect(result.cap).toBe(PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
    expect(result.clampedByCeiling).toBe(true);
    expect(result.clampedByFloor).toBe(false);
  });

  it('clamps to the floor rather than allowing a cap of zero', () => {
    // A cap of 0 means "never open a position", which is a halt, not a risk
    // setting. Storing it here would make a paused account look configured.
    const result = clampConcurrentPositionCap(0);
    expect(result.cap).toBe(MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
    expect(result.clampedByFloor).toBe(true);
  });

  it('clamps a negative request to the floor too', () => {
    expect(clampConcurrentPositionCap(-5).cap).toBe(MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
  });

  it('throws rather than clamping a non-integer, which is not a wish about counts', () => {
    // 500 is a coherent wish the platform declines; 2.5 is not a wish about
    // position counts at all, and rounding it would be guessing.
    expect(() => clampConcurrentPositionCap(2.5)).toThrow(InvalidPositionCapError);
    expect(() => clampConcurrentPositionCap(Number.NaN)).toThrow(InvalidPositionCapError);
    expect(() => clampConcurrentPositionCap(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)).toThrow(InvalidPositionCapError);
  });

  it('rejects a nonsensical ceiling instead of trusting the caller', () => {
    expect(() => clampConcurrentPositionCap(5, 0)).toThrow(InvalidPositionCapError);
    expect(() => clampConcurrentPositionCap(5, 1.5)).toThrow(InvalidPositionCapError);
  });

  it('honours a lower per-caller ceiling', () => {
    const result = clampConcurrentPositionCap(20, 8);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ cap: 8, clampedByCeiling: true, ceiling: 8 });
  });

  it('keeps the default inside the platform range', () => {
    expect(DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
    expect(DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS).toBeLessThanOrEqual(PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
  });
});

describe('perPositionNotionalUsd', () => {
  it('takes the tighter of the percentage cap and the balance split', () => {
    // 1000 balance, cap 10 -> 100 per position by division; 5% -> 50. The
    // percentage binds.
    expect(perPositionNotionalUsd(1_000, 10, 5)).toBe(50);
    // cap 100 -> 10 by division, which is now tighter than 5% (50).
    expect(perPositionNotionalUsd(1_000, 100, 5)).toBe(10);
  });

  it('shrinks as the cap rises, which is what makes the warning necessary', () => {
    const atFive = perPositionNotionalUsd(100, 5, 100);
    const atFifty = perPositionNotionalUsd(100, 50, 100);
    expect(atFifty).toBeLessThan(atFive);
  });
});

describe('assessPositionCap (S4-M4 derived warning)', () => {
  const polygonMin = VENUE_MINIMUM_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD.polygon.minOrderNotionalUsd;

  it('warns when the cap spreads the balance below the venue minimum', () => {
    // $20 across 50 positions is $0.40 a copy against a $5 minimum: every trade
    // would be skipped. Better said at the slider than discovered in a skip reason.
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 50,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 20 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    const warning = assessment.warnings.find((w) => w.chain === 'polygon');
    expect(warning?.code).toBe('cap-spreads-balance-below-venue-minimum');
    expect(warning?.minOrderNotionalUsd).toBe(polygonMin);
    // The actionable part: the highest cap that still clears the minimum.
    expect(warning?.maxCapClearingMinimum).toBe(Math.floor(20 / polygonMin));
  });

  it('does not warn when every copy clears the minimum', () => {
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 2,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 1_000 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    expect(assessment.warnings.filter((w) => w.chain === 'polygon')).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('distinguishes a percentage that is too low from a cap that is too high', () => {
    // A 0.1% slice of $1,000 is $1 at ANY cap, so lowering the cap fixes nothing.
    // Same symptom, different fix, therefore a different code.
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 1,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 1_000 },
      maxPositionPct: 0.1
    });
    expect(assessment.warnings.find((w) => w.chain === 'polygon')?.code)
      .toBe('position-pct-below-venue-minimum');
  });

  it('reports an unknown balance as unassessed, never as a passing check', () => {
    // The balance poller can be behind. "We have not priced your balance yet" is
    // not "your copies will be skipped", and an empty warnings array must not be
    // readable as "checked everywhere and fine".
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 50,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: null },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    expect(assessment.warnings).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(assessment.unassessed).toContainEqual({ chain: 'polygon', reason: 'balance-unknown' });
  });

  it('treats an absent chain as unknown rather than zero', () => {
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 50,
      balancesUsd: {},
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    expect(assessment.unassessed.some((u) => u.chain === 'polygon' && u.reason === 'balance-unknown'))
      .toBe(true);
  });

  it('lists the two venues with no minimum as unassessed, not as passing', () => {
    // Solana and Robinhood are AMMs that quote any size. There is nothing to
    // check, and inventing a threshold would be fabricating a venue rule.
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 50,
      balancesUsd: { solana: 1, 'robinhood-chain': 1, polygon: 1_000 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    for (const chain of ['solana', 'robinhood-chain'] as const) {
      expect(assessment.unassessed).toContainEqual({ chain, reason: 'no-venue-minimum' });
      expect(assessment.warnings.some((w) => w.chain === chain)).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  it('flags the Polymarket minimum as approximate, because it is per market', () => {
    // The binding value is read from the order book at submission. A caller that
    // renders this as the venue's truth is misleading the user.
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 50,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 20 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    const warning = assessment.warnings.find((w) => w.chain === 'polygon');
    expect(warning?.approximate).toBe(true);
    expect(warning?.message.toLowerCase()).toMatch(/approx|typical|per market|may be/);
  });

  it('reports the clamped cap it actually assessed, not the raw request', () => {
    // Assessing the requested 500 rather than the stored 50 would warn about a
    // cap that can never exist.
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 500,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 1_000 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    expect(assessment.requestedCap).toBe(500);
    expect(assessment.effectiveCap).toBe(PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS);
    expect(assessment.clampedByCeiling).toBe(true);
  });

  it('says no cap works when the balance cannot fund even one order', () => {
    const assessment = assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap: 5,
      balancesUsd: { polygon: 1 },
      maxPositionPct: 100
    });
    expect(assessment.warnings.find((w) => w.chain === 'polygon')?.maxCapClearingMinimum).toBe(0);
  });

  it('covers exactly the supported chains in the minimum table', () => {
    // Typed Record<Chain, ...> so a new chain cannot compile without a decision;
    // this pins the runtime shape too, since a silent undefined reads as
    // "no minimum" and quietly stops warning.
    expect(Object.keys(VENUE_MINIMUM_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD).sort())
      .toEqual(['base', 'bsc', 'ethereum', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'solana']);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/position-cap.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';

/**
 * Per-user concurrent-position cap (`S4-M4`, migration `049`), and the derived
 * below-minimum warning that belongs at the slider rather than in a skip reason.
 *
 * Everything in this module is **pure**: no database, no clock, no network. The
 * cap itself is a column on `user_execution_settings` (see
 * `user-execution-settings.ts`); what lives here is the arithmetic the API and the
 * UI both need to answer *"is the number you just typed going to work?"* before it
 * is stored.
 *
 * Two separate jobs, deliberately not merged:
 *
 *   * `clampConcurrentPositionCap` applies the **platform hard ceiling**. That is a
 *     platform decision, not a user preference, so it is enforced here and mirrored
 *     by a CHECK in `049` â€” a caller that skips this function still cannot write a
 *     value past the ceiling.
 *   * `assessPositionCap` derives the **warning**. It is advisory by construction:
 *     it never changes the cap, because the honest minimums it can reach at
 *     configuration time are approximations (see below) and an approximation must
 *     not silently overrule what a user asked for.
 */

/**
 * The platform hard ceiling on one user's concurrent positions.
 *
 * **The shape of the argument is real; the exact number is a judgement.** Stated
 * plainly so nobody reads 50 as a measured limit.
 *
 * Every open position is a *future forced exit* the platform is obliged to act on.
 * Stop-loss evaluation rides the mark-to-market cadence, which is **every 5
 * minutes** (`apps/scorer/src/index.ts` â€” "Mark-to-market every 5 minutes"), and
 * exits are submitted through the per-chain trade queues, each served by **exactly
 * one concurrency-1 worker** (`TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN`, `apps/trade-executor`). A
 * market-wide drawdown fires stop-losses on many of a user's positions at once, and
 * those exits then serialise behind that single worker. If the queue cannot drain
 * inside the 5-minute window, the next evaluation re-fires on positions whose exit
 * is still queued.
 *
 * So the ceiling is a *blast-radius bound on one user's share of a serialised exit
 * queue*. At a conservative 6 seconds per exit â€” a fresh book read (Polymarket
 * refuses a book older than `POLYMARKET_MAX_BOOK_AGE_MS=15000`), a signature and a
 * submission â€” one worker drains about 300/6 = 50 orders per window. 50 is that
 * number.
 *
 * **What this ceiling does NOT promise.** The queue is shared across all users, so
 * ten users at the ceiling put 500 exits behind one worker and the window is blown
 * regardless. A per-user ceiling cannot bound an aggregate; only per-chain
 * admission control can, and that does not exist. The 6-seconds-per-exit figure is
 * an estimate, not a measurement â€” nothing in this repo records observed exit
 * latency. Treat 50 as "small enough that one user alone is not the problem", and
 * revisit it against real latency once exits run in production.
 */
export const PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS = 50;

/**
 * The floor is 1, not 0.
 *
 * A cap of 0 would mean "never open a position", which the settings row already
 * expresses twice and more legibly â€” `killed` (the per-user kill switch) and a
 * per-chain `mode` of `off`. Admitting 0 here would create a third way to say stop,
 * one that reads to a skimming operator as "unlimited" rather than as "halted".
 */
export const MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS = 1;

/**
 * The default for a user who has never touched the control.
 *
 * Derived from the other defaults in `049` rather than picked: `max_position_pct`
 * defaults to 5 and `max_daily_exposure_pct` to 25, so five positions at the
 * default per-position size is exactly the point where the default daily exposure
 * cap is used up. A default above that would ship a cap that the daily limit makes
 * unreachable, which is a control that appears to do something and does not.
 */
export const DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS = 5;

/**
 * Why a chain's minimum order size either is or is not knowable when a user moves
 * a slider.
 *
 * This distinction is the whole point of the module. A warning that is wrong is
 * worse than absent â€” it teaches users to ignore warnings â€” so the basis travels
 * with the number and the caller can render it.
 */
export type VenueMinimumBasis =
  /**
   * The venue enforces a minimum order size, but its value is **per market** and is
   * only readable from the order book at submission time. Any figure used at
   * configuration time is a typical value, i.e. an approximation.
   */
  | 'venue-enforced-per-market'
  /**
   * The venue enforces no minimum order size at all. An AMM will quote any size.
   * There is nothing to warn about, and inventing a threshold here would be
   * fabricating a venue rule.
   */
  | 'no-venue-minimum';

export interface VenueMinimumOrderNotional {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  /** USD notional one order must reach. Meaningless unless `basis` is per-market. */
  readonly minOrderNotionalUsd: number;
  readonly basis: VenueMinimumBasis;
  /**
   * True when `minOrderNotionalUsd` is a typical value standing in for a
   * per-market one. Callers rendering the warning **must** surface this; the number
   * is not the venue's truth for the market the trade will land in.
   */
  readonly approximate: boolean;
  /** Where the figure came from, for the operator reading a warning they doubt. */
  readonly note: string;
}

/**
 * Per-chain minimum order notional, as far as it is honestly knowable at
 * configuration time.
 *
 * Typed `Record<Chain, ...>` so adding a chain to the union fails to compile until
 * somebody decides what its minimum is. A silent `undefined` would read as
 * "no minimum" and quietly stop warning.
 *
 * **Polymarket (polygon) is the only venue here with a minimum at all.** Solana
 * routes through the Jupiter aggregator and Robinhood Chain through a Uniswap V3
 * router (`apps/trade-executor/src/robinhood.ts` â€” `uniswap-v3-swap-router-01/02`);
 * both are AMMs and will quote any size. They have *economic* floors â€” Solana ATA
 * rent, priority fees, gas â€” but those are costs, not a venue rule that rejects an
 * order, and a trade under them is not "skipped", it is merely bad value. Modelling
 * them as a minimum order size would be inventing a rule the venue does not have,
 * so this warning does not cover them and says so.
 */
export const VENUE_MINIMUM_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD: Readonly<
  Record<Chain, VenueMinimumOrderNotional>
> = Object.freeze({
  polygon: Object.freeze({
    chain: 'polygon' as Chain,
    // 5 is the value Polymarket's own docs use in every worked example of a
    // market's trading constraints (`market-data/market-details`, whose Gamma
    // mapping shows `orderMinSize: 5`, and `trading/place-orders`, whose order-book
    // sample shows `min_order_size: "5"`). It is NOT a platform-wide constant: the
    // real value is per market and this executor already reads it per order from
    // the book (`book.minOrderSize` in `apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket.ts`,
    // enforced in `polymarket-mirror-bound.ts`). Hence `approximate: true`.
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 5,
    basis: 'venue-enforced-per-market',
    approximate: true,
    note:
      'Typical Polymarket per-market minimum. The binding value is read from the '
      + 'order book at submission and may be higher or lower for the market a copy '
      + 'lands in. Polymarket documents the units inconsistently: '
      + 'market-data/market-details calls minimumOrderSize a USDC notional while '
      + 'trading/place-orders calls min_order_size a share count. This executor '
      + 'treats it as a share count. Since an outcome share costs under $1, a share '
      + 'count of 5 needs at most $5 of notional, so comparing against $5 warns at '
      + 'or before the real boundary under either reading.'
  }),
  solana: Object.freeze({
    chain: 'solana' as Chain,
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 0,
    basis: 'no-venue-minimum',
    approximate: false,
    note:
      'Jupiter is an AMM aggregator and quotes any size. Rent, priority fees and '
      + 'slippage make a tiny swap poor value, but no venue rule rejects it, so '
      + 'there is no minimum order size to warn about.'
  }),
  'robinhood-chain': Object.freeze({
    chain: 'robinhood-chain' as Chain,
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 0,
    basis: 'no-venue-minimum',
    approximate: false,
    note:
      'A Uniswap V3 router quotes any size. Gas makes a tiny swap poor value, but '
      + 'no venue rule rejects it, so there is no minimum order size to warn about.'
  }),
  base: Object.freeze({
    chain: 'base' as Chain,
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 0,
    basis: 'no-venue-minimum',
    approximate: false,
    note: 'Uniswap v3 quotes any size.'
  }),
  ethereum: Object.freeze({
    chain: 'ethereum' as Chain,
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 0,
    basis: 'no-venue-minimum',
    approximate: false,
    note: 'Uniswap v3 quotes any size.'
  }),
  bsc: Object.freeze({
    chain: 'bsc' as Chain,
    minOrderNotionalUsd: 0,
    basis: 'no-venue-minimum',
    approximate: false,
    note: 'PancakeSwap v3 quotes any size.'
  })
});

export interface ClampedPositionCap {
  /** The value that may be stored: the request, clamped into range. */
  readonly cap: number;
  /** True when the platform ceiling, not the user, decided the stored value. */
  readonly clampedByCeiling: boolean;
  /** True when the floor decided it. */
  readonly clampedByFloor: boolean;
  readonly ceiling: number;
}

/**
 * A requested cap is not an integer in range.
 *
 * Separate from clamping on purpose. A request of 500 is a *coherent* wish the
 * platform declines, and clamping it to 50 is a defensible answer. A request of
 * `2.5` or `NaN` is not a wish about position counts at all, and clamping it would
 * be guessing which number the caller meant.
 */
export class InvalidPositionCapError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'InvalidPositionCapError';
  }
}

/**
 * Brings a requested cap inside `[MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS, ceiling]`.
 *
 * Clamps rather than rejects an out-of-range integer so the UI can show the user
 * what they will actually get, and reports *which* bound moved it so the UI can say
 * so instead of silently displaying a different number than was typed.
 */
export function clampConcurrentPositionCap(
  requested: number,
  ceiling: number = PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS
): ClampedPositionCap {
  if (!Number.isInteger(requested)) {
    throw new InvalidPositionCapError(
      `maxConcurrentPositions must be an integer, got ${requested}`
    );
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(ceiling) || ceiling < MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS) {
    throw new InvalidPositionCapError(
      `position cap ceiling must be an integer >= ${MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS}, got ${ceiling}`
    );
  }

  if (requested > ceiling) {
    return { cap: ceiling, clampedByCeiling: true, clampedByFloor: false, ceiling };
  }
  if (requested < MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS) {
    return {
      cap: MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS,
      clampedByCeiling: false,
      clampedByFloor: true,
      ceiling
    };
  }
  return { cap: requested, clampedByCeiling: false, clampedByFloor: false, ceiling };
}

export type PositionCapWarningCode =
  /**
   * The cap is what breaks it: spread over this many positions the balance no
   * longer funds one order to the venue minimum. Lowering the cap fixes it, and
   * `maxCapClearingMinimum` says to what.
   */
  | 'cap-spreads-balance-below-venue-minimum'
  /**
   * The per-position percentage alone is already under the minimum, at any cap.
   * A *different fix* â€” raise `maxPositionPct`, or fund the account â€” so it is a
   * different code rather than the same warning with different prose.
   */
  | 'position-pct-below-venue-minimum';

export interface PositionCapWarning {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly code: PositionCapWarningCode;
  /** What one copy comes to at the assessed cap. */
  readonly perPositionUsd: number;
  readonly minOrderNotionalUsd: number;
  readonly approximate: boolean;
  /**
   * The highest cap at which each copy still clears the minimum. `0` means no cap
   * does â€” the balance cannot fund even one order.
   */
  readonly maxCapClearingMinimum: number;
  /** One sentence for the slider. Always names the approximation when there is one. */
  readonly message: string;
}

/** Why a chain could not be assessed. Never conflated with "assessed, no warning". */
export type PositionCapUnassessedReason =
  /** The venue has no minimum order size, so there is nothing to check. */
  | 'no-venue-minimum'
  /** No USD balance is known for this chain, so no per-copy notional can be derived. */
  | 'balance-unknown';

export interface PositionCapUnassessedChain {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly reason: PositionCapUnassessedReason;
}

export interface PositionCapAssessment {
  readonly requestedCap: number;
  /** What would actually be stored. */
  readonly effectiveCap: number;
  readonly clampedByCeiling: boolean;
  readonly clampedByFloor: boolean;
  readonly ceiling: number;
  readonly warnings: readonly PositionCapWarning[];
  /**
   * Chains this assessment says **nothing** about, with the reason.
   *
   * Present so a caller cannot read an empty `warnings` array as "checked
   * everywhere and fine". Two of the three chains are permanently in here because
   * their venues have no minimum, and any chain whose balance is unknown joins
   * them â€” a missing balance must not read as a passing check.
   */
  readonly unassessed: readonly PositionCapUnassessedChain[];
}

export interface PositionCapAssessmentInput {
  readonly requestedCap: number;
  /**
   * Per-chain USD balance available to trade. A chain absent from the map, or
   * mapped to `null`, is *unknown* and lands in `unassessed` rather than being
   * treated as zero â€” the balance poller can be behind, and "we have not priced
   * your balance yet" is not "your copies will be skipped".
   */
  readonly balancesUsd: Partial<Readonly<Record<Chain, number | null>>>;
  /** `user_execution_settings.max_position_pct`. */
  readonly maxPositionPct: number;
  readonly ceiling?: number;
  /** Overridable so a test, or a later live-minimum feed, can supply its own. */
  readonly minimums?: Readonly<Record<Chain, VenueMinimumOrderNotional>>;
}

/**
 * What one copy is worth when the user is holding `cap` positions at once.
 *
 * Two limits, and the tighter one binds:
 *
 *   * `maxPositionPct` caps a single position as a share of the balance. It does
 *     not shrink as the cap rises.
 *   * Holding `cap` positions simultaneously out of one balance means each gets at
 *     most `balance / cap`. This is the term the slider moves, and it is why the
 *     warning exists at all: past `balance / minimum` positions, every copy is
 *     under the venue minimum no matter what `maxPositionPct` says.
 *
 * Exported because the UI needs the same number the warning was computed from, and
 * a second implementation in the frontend would drift.
 */
export function perPositionNotionalUsd(
  balanceUsd: number,
  cap: number,
  maxPositionPct: number
): number {
  if (!Number.isFinite(balanceUsd) || balanceUsd < 0) {
    throw new InvalidPositionCapError(
      `balanceUsd must be a non-negative finite number, got ${balanceUsd}`
    );
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(cap) || cap < 1) {
    throw new InvalidPositionCapError(`cap must be an integer >= 1, got ${cap}`);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(maxPositionPct) || maxPositionPct <= 0 || maxPositionPct > 100) {
    throw new InvalidPositionCapError(
      `maxPositionPct must be in (0, 100], got ${maxPositionPct}`
    );
  }
  return balanceUsd * Math.min(maxPositionPct / 100, 1 / cap);
}

/**
 * Comparison tolerance, so a balance that divides to exactly the minimum in exact
 * arithmetic is not warned about because float division landed a hair under.
 *
 * A cent is far below any venue minimum, so this cannot mask a real breach.
 */
const NOTIONAL_EPSILON = 1e-9;

/**
 * The derived warning, for a proposed cap.
 *
 * **Advisory only.** It returns the clamped cap so the caller can display it, but
 * the warnings never alter it: the minimums available at configuration time are
 * approximations, and an approximation must not override what a user asked for.
 *
 * Fails *loud* on an incoherent input (`InvalidPositionCapError`) and *closed* on a
 * missing one â€” an unknown balance produces an `unassessed` entry, never a silent
 * pass. Pure: no database, no clock.
 */
export function assessPositionCap(input: PositionCapAssessmentInput): PositionCapAssessment {
  const clamped = clampConcurrentPositionCap(input.requestedCap, input.ceiling);
  const minimums = input.minimums ?? VENUE_MINIMUM_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD;

  const warnings: PositionCapWarning[] = [];
  const unassessed: PositionCapUnassessedChain[] = [];

  for (const chain of Object.keys(minimums) as Chain[]) {
    const minimum = minimums[chain];
    if (minimum.basis === 'no-venue-minimum') {
      unassessed.push({ chain, reason: 'no-venue-minimum' });
      continue;
    }

    const balanceUsd = input.balancesUsd[chain];
    if (balanceUsd === null || balanceUsd === undefined || !Number.isFinite(balanceUsd)) {
      unassessed.push({ chain, reason: 'balance-unknown' });
      continue;
    }

    const perPositionUsd = perPositionNotionalUsd(
      balanceUsd,
      clamped.cap,
      input.maxPositionPct
    );
    if (perPositionUsd + NOTIONAL_EPSILON >= minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd) continue;

    // The highest cap at which balance/cap still clears the minimum. Floor, because
    // a fractional cap is not a cap. Zero when the balance cannot fund one order.
    const maxCapClearingMinimum = Math.floor(
      (balanceUsd + NOTIONAL_EPSILON) / minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd
    );

    // Which of the two terms in `perPositionNotionalUsd` is actually under the
    // minimum decides the code, because the two have different fixes. Checked on
    // the percentage term alone: if THAT is short, no cap value rescues it.
    const pctTermUsd = balanceUsd * (input.maxPositionPct / 100);
    const pctTermShort = pctTermUsd + NOTIONAL_EPSILON < minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd;

    const approximateSuffix = minimum.approximate
      ? ' This uses a typical minimum, not the one for the specific market; the '
        + 'binding value is read from the order book when the order is placed.'
      : '';

    warnings.push({
      chain,
      code: pctTermShort
        ? 'position-pct-below-venue-minimum'
        : 'cap-spreads-balance-below-venue-minimum',
      perPositionUsd,
      minOrderNotionalUsd: minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd,
      approximate: minimum.approximate,
      maxCapClearingMinimum,
      message: pctTermShort
        ? `At $${balanceUsd} on ${chain}, ${input.maxPositionPct}% per position is `
          + `$${pctTermUsd}, below the ~$${minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd} minimum order `
          + 'size â€” every copy would be skipped at any position cap. Raise the '
          + 'per-position size or add funds.'
          + approximateSuffix
        : `At $${balanceUsd} on ${chain}, ${clamped.cap} concurrent positions leaves `
          + `$${perPositionUsd} per copy, below the ~$${minimum.minOrderNotionalUsd} `
          + 'minimum order size, so every copy would be skipped. '
          + (maxCapClearingMinimum >= MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS
            ? `At most ${maxCapClearingMinimum} position`
              + `${maxCapClearingMinimum === 1 ? '' : 's'} clears it at this balance.`
            : 'This balance cannot fund even one order.')
          + approximateSuffix
    });
  }

  return {
    requestedCap: input.requestedCap,
    effectiveCap: clamped.cap,
    clampedByCeiling: clamped.clampedByCeiling,
    clampedByFloor: clamped.clampedByFloor,
    ceiling: clamped.ceiling,
    warnings,
    unassessed
  };
}

==> packages/db/src/quote-valuation.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  deriveFillPriceUsd,
  divideDecimalText,
  multiplyDecimalText,
  nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain,
  summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal,
  valuateChainNativeQuoteLeg,
  valuateQuoteLeg
} from './quote-valuation.js';

describe('nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain', () => {
  it('maps each chain to the unit its native size is denominated in', () => {
    expect(nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain('solana')).toBe('SOL');
    expect(nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain('robinhood-chain')).toBe('ETH');
    expect(nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain('polygon')).toBe('USD');
  });
});

describe('multiplyDecimalText', () => {
  it('multiplies exactly where binary floating point does not', () => {
    // 0.1 * 3 is 0.30000000000000004 in IEEE-754 doubles.
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('0.1', '3')).toBe('0.3');
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('1.1', '1.1')).toBe('1.21');
  });

  it('keeps full precision on lamport-scale amounts at realistic prices', () => {
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('0.123456789', '187.42')).toBe('23.13827139438');
  });

  it('handles zero and integers without dangling separators', () => {
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('0', '187.42')).toBe('0');
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('2', '3')).toBe('6');
    expect(multiplyDecimalText('2.50', '4')).toBe('10');
  });
});

describe('valuateQuoteLeg', () => {
  it('passes a USD leg straight through at a rate of 1', () => {
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: '4.5', currency: 'USD' })).toMatchObject({
      code: 'valued',
      currency: 'USD',
      nativeAmount: '4.5',
      nativeUsdPrice: '1',
      usdAmount: '4.5'
    });
  });

  it('converts a SOL leg and keeps the native amount and the rate used', () => {
    const valuation = valuateQuoteLeg({
      amount: '1.25',
      currency: 'SOL',
      nativeUsdPrice: 150
    });
    expect(valuation).toMatchObject({
      code: 'valued',
      currency: 'SOL',
      nativeAmount: '1.25',
      nativeUsdPrice: '150',
      usdAmount: '187.5'
    });
  });

  it('converts an ETH leg', () => {
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: '0.02', currency: 'ETH', nativeUsdPrice: '3200' }))
      .toMatchObject({ code: 'valued', currency: 'ETH', usdAmount: '64' });
  });

  it('never puts a native token amount in the USD field', () => {
    // The whole bug in one assertion: 1.25 SOL must not become 1.25 USD.
    const valuation = valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 150 });
    expect(valuation.usdAmount).not.toBe('1.25');
    expect(valuation.usdAmount).toBe('187.5');
  });

  it('reports an unknown USD value rather than zero when no rate is available', () => {
    for (const rate of [null, undefined, 0, Number.NaN, -5, '']) {
      const valuation = valuateQuoteLeg({
        amount: '1.25',
        currency: 'SOL',
        nativeUsdPrice: rate as number | string | null | undefined
      });
      expect(valuation.code, `rate ${String(rate)}`).toBe('native-price-unknown');
      expect(valuation.usdAmount, `rate ${String(rate)}`).toBeNull();
      // The observed half survives even when the derived half cannot.
      expect(valuation.nativeAmount).toBe('1.25');
      expect(valuation.currency).toBe('SOL');
      expect(valuation.nativeUsdPrice).toBeNull();
    }
  });

  it('distinguishes an absent quote leg from a zero one', () => {
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg(null)).toMatchObject({
      code: 'no-quote-leg',
      currency: null,
      nativeAmount: null,
      usdAmount: null
    });
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg(undefined).code).toBe('no-quote-leg');
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: 0, currency: 'USD' })).toMatchObject({
      code: 'valued',
      nativeAmount: '0',
      usdAmount: '0'
    });
  });

  it('expands exponent notation instead of refusing it', () => {
    // Number(1e-9).toString() is '1e-9'; a lamport-scale amount must survive.
    expect(valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: 1e-9, currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 200 }))
      .toMatchObject({ nativeAmount: '0.000000001', usdAmount: '0.0000002' });
  });

  it('throws on an amount that is not a non-negative decimal', () => {
    expect(() => valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: -1, currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 1 }))
      .toThrow(/non-negative decimal/);
    expect(() => valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: 'abc', currency: 'USD' }))
      .toThrow(/non-negative decimal/);
    expect(() => valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: Number.NaN, currency: 'USD' }))
      .toThrow(/non-negative decimal/);
  });

  it('throws on an unknown currency rather than guessing USD', () => {
    expect(() => valuateQuoteLeg({ amount: '1', currency: 'USDC' as never }))
      .toThrow(/currency must be one of/);
  });
});

describe('divideDecimalText', () => {
  it('divides exactly when the quotient terminates', () => {
    expect(divideDecimalText('187.5', '1000')).toBe('0.1875');
    expect(divideDecimalText('64', '2')).toBe('32');
  });

  it('truncates a repeating quotient at the configured scale', () => {
    expect(divideDecimalText('1', '3')).toBe('0.333333333333333333');
    expect(divideDecimalText('1', '3', 4)).toBe('0.3333');
  });

  it('returns null rather than Infinity on a zero denominator', () => {

describe('deriveFillPriceUsd', () => {
  it('derives the realised price from USD paid over units received', () => {
    // 1.25 SOL at 150 USD/SOL buys 1000 tokens => 0.1875 USD per token.
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd('187.5', '1000')).toBe('0.1875');
  });

  it('stays unknown when the USD amount is unknown', () => {
    // The Solana-live and robinhood-live paths reach this when the native price
    // feed is down. A NULL price_usd is correct there; a 0 would be a free fill.
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd(null, '1000')).toBeNull();
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd(undefined, '1000')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('stays unknown when the base quantity cannot support a ratio', () => {
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd('187.5', '0')).toBeNull();
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd('187.5', null)).toBeNull();
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd('187.5', 'abc')).toBeNull();
    expect(deriveFillPriceUsd('187.5', -1)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('never returns zero for a positive fill', () => {
    const price = deriveFillPriceUsd('4.5', '10');
    expect(price).not.toBeNull();
    expect(Number(price)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});

    expect(() => summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal({
      valuedFillCount: 1,
      unvaluedFillCount: 0,
      valuedUsdSum: null
    })).toThrow(/valuedUsdSum/);
  });

  it('refuses non-integer or negative counts', () => {
    expect(() => summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal({
      valuedFillCount: 1.5,
      unvaluedFillCount: 0,
      valuedUsdSum: '1'
    })).toThrow(/valuedFillCount/);
    expect(() => summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal({
      valuedFillCount: 0,
      unvaluedFillCount: -1,
      valuedUsdSum: null
    })).toThrow(/unvaluedFillCount/);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/quote-valuation.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';

/**
 * The quote leg of a copy fill: what was paid, in which token, and what that
 * came to in USD.
 *
 * ## Why this module exists (S4-M35)
 *
 * `copy_execution_evidence.quote_quantity` used to be a mixed-unit column. Each
 * executor path wrote whatever its venue settled in and nothing recorded the
 * unit:
 *
 *   * Polymarket live wrote `spendAmountUsd` â€” USD.
 *   * Paper simulation wrote `simAmountUsd` â€” USD.
 *   * Solana live wrote `nativeLamportsDelta / 1e9` â€” **SOL**.
 *   * robinhood-chain live wrote `result.amountEth` â€” **ETH**.
 *
 * `rebuildCopyPosition` then summed that column into `copy_positions.cost_basis_usd`,
 * *preferring* it over the `base_quantity * price_usd` fallback, so a column named
 * `_usd` accumulated SOL and ETH.
 *
 * The unit is a property of the executor path, not of the chain â€” the Solana paper
 * path settles in USD while the Solana live path settles in SOL â€” so it cannot be
 * inferred at read time and has to be declared at write time. That is what
 * {@link QuoteLegInput} forces: there is no way to hand the write path an amount
 * without also handing it the currency.
 *
 * ## Both halves are kept, deliberately
 *
 * A USD figure alone is lossy: it cannot be re-derived if the conversion rate was
 * wrong, it cannot be audited, and it cannot answer "how much SOL did this position
 * actually cost". So every valued fill persists three things â€” the native amount,
 * its currency, and the rate used â€” and the USD figure is the *derived* one.
 *
 * ## One conversion rule
 *
 * {@link nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain} and {@link valuateQuoteLeg} are the single
 * conversion rule in the codebase. `persistTrade` in `apps/trade-executor` used to
 * carry its own per-chain `if` chain (Solana x SOL price, robinhood x ETH price,
 * polygon already USD) and now calls these instead, so the two write paths cannot
 * drift apart.
 *
 * Everything here is pure: no database, no clock, no network, no price fetching.
 * The caller supplies the rate; this module decides what it means.
 */

/** Currencies a venue can settle a copy fill's quote leg in. */
export type QuoteCurrency = 'USD' | 'SOL' | 'ETH' | 'BNB';

export const QUOTE_CURRENCIES: readonly QuoteCurrency[] = ['USD', 'SOL', 'ETH', 'BNB'];

export function isQuoteCurrency(value: unknown): value is QuoteCurrency {
  return typeof value === 'string' && (QUOTE_CURRENCIES as readonly string[]).includes(value);
}

/**
 * The currency a chain's *native* quote leg is denominated in.
 *
 * This is the map `persistTrade` encoded inline. It answers "if a caller hands me
 * a raw size for this chain, what unit is that size in" â€” it does NOT answer "what
 * unit did this stored row use", because a paper fill on Solana is sized in USD.
 * Callers that already know they hold USD must say so rather than ask this.
 */
export function nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain(chain: Chain): QuoteCurrency {
  switch (chain) {
    case 'solana':
      return 'SOL';
    case 'robinhood-chain':
    case 'base':
    case 'ethereum':
      return 'ETH';
    case 'bsc':
      return 'BNB';
    case 'polygon':
      // Polymarket sizes and settles in USDC, which the whole codebase treats as
      // USD 1:1 (see `persistTrade`: polygon needs no conversion).
      return 'USD';
    default: {
      const exhaustive: never = chain;
      throw new Error(`Unsupported chain for quote valuation: ${String(exhaustive)}`);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * What the caller observed: an amount, the token it is denominated in, and the USD
 * price of one unit of that token at fill time.
 *
 * `nativeUsdPrice` is meaningless for `USD` and required for everything else. It is
 * accepted as `null` rather than made mandatory because "we could not get a SOL
 * price" is a real outcome the caller must be able to express â€” and one that must
 * produce an *unknown* USD value, never a zero.
 */
export interface QuoteLegInput {
  readonly amount: string | number;
  readonly currency: QuoteCurrency;
  readonly nativeUsdPrice?: string | number | null;
}

/**
 * Why a quote leg does or does not have a USD value. Mirrors the
 * `TrackingDifferenceCode` discipline in `tracking-difference.ts`: unknown is a
 * named code, never a number.
 */
export type QuoteValuationCode =
  /** Native amount, currency and rate all present; `usdAmount` is trustworthy. */
  | 'valued'
  /** The venue reported no quote amount at all. Nothing is known, not even zero. */
  | 'no-quote-leg'
  /**
   * The native amount is known but no usable USD rate was supplied, so the USD
   * value is unknown. The native amount is still persisted â€” it is the part that
   * was actually observed.
   */
  | 'native-price-unknown';

export interface QuoteLegValuation {
  readonly code: QuoteValuationCode;
  /** `null` only when there was no quote leg. */
  readonly currency: QuoteCurrency | null;
  /** Amount as settled, in `currency`. `null` only when there was no quote leg. */
  readonly nativeAmount: string | null;
  /** USD price of one unit of `currency`. `'1'` for USD. `null` when unknown. */
  readonly nativeUsdPrice: string | null;
  /** `nativeAmount * nativeUsdPrice`, exact. `null` when unknown â€” never `0`. */
  readonly usdAmount: string | null;
  /** One sentence, safe to log or surface. */
  readonly reason: string;
}

const UNSIGNED_DECIMAL = /^(?:\d+\.?\d*|\d*\.\d+)$/;

/**
 * Normalise a decimal to canonical unsigned text, or return `null` if it is not a
 * usable non-negative finite decimal.
 *
 * Exponent notation is expanded rather than rejected because `Number.toString()`
 * produces it for small numbers (`1e-7`), and a lamport-scale amount landing here
 * as `1e-9` must not be read as unparseable.
 */
function normalizeUnsignedDecimal(value: string | number | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
  if (typeof value === 'number') {
    if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) return null;
    return normalizeUnsignedDecimal(expandExponent(value.toString()));
  }
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  if (trimmed === '') return null;
  const expanded = expandExponent(trimmed);
  if (expanded === null) return null;
  if (!UNSIGNED_DECIMAL.test(expanded)) return null;
  return expanded;
}

/** Rewrite `1.5e-7` as `0.00000015`. Returns the input unchanged when there is no exponent. */
function expandExponent(text: string): string | null {
  const match = /^(\d*)(?:\.(\d*))?[eE]([+-]?\d+)$/.exec(text);
  if (!match) return text;
  const [, integerPart = '', fractionalPart = '', exponentText = '0'] = match;
  const digits = `${integerPart}${fractionalPart}`;
  if (digits === '') return null;
  const exponent = Number(exponentText);
  if (!Number.isFinite(exponent)) return null;
  const pointIndex = integerPart.length + exponent;
  if (pointIndex <= 0) return `0.${'0'.repeat(-pointIndex)}${digits}`;
  if (pointIndex >= digits.length) return `${digits}${'0'.repeat(pointIndex - digits.length)}`;
  return `${digits.slice(0, pointIndex)}.${digits.slice(pointIndex)}`;
}

function splitDecimal(text: string): { digits: bigint; scale: number } {
  const [integerPart = '0', fractionalPart = ''] = text.split('.');
  const combined = `${integerPart}${fractionalPart}`;
  return { digits: BigInt(combined === '' ? '0' : combined), scale: fractionalPart.length };
}

function trimDecimal(text: string): string {
  if (!text.includes('.')) return text.replace(/^0+(?=\d)/, '');
  const trimmed = text.replace(/0+$/, '').replace(/\.$/, '');
  const normalized = trimmed === '' ? '0' : trimmed;
  return normalized.replace(/^0+(?=\d)/, '');
}

/**
 * Exact decimal multiply on text, via BigInt.
 *
 * Money is not multiplied in binary floating point here. `0.1 * 3` in JS is
 * `0.30000000000000004`, and a cost basis assembled from thousands of those drifts
 * visibly. Both inputs must already be canonical unsigned decimals.
 */
export function multiplyDecimalText(left: string, right: string): string {
  const a = splitDecimal(left);
  const b = splitDecimal(right);
  const product = (a.digits * b.digits).toString();
  const scale = a.scale + b.scale;
  if (scale === 0) return trimDecimal(product);
  const padded = product.padStart(scale + 1, '0');
  const pointIndex = padded.length - scale;
  return trimDecimal(`${padded.slice(0, pointIndex)}.${padded.slice(pointIndex)}`);
}

/**
 * Turn an observed quote leg into a USD value plus the native record that makes it
 * checkable.
 *
 * Throws on an amount that is not a non-negative decimal â€” that is a caller bug,
 * not an unknown, and silently mapping it to `null` would hide a broken executor
 * path behind the same code that means "the price feed was down". A missing or
 * unusable *rate*, by contrast, is an expected outcome and yields
 * `native-price-unknown`.
 */
export function valuateQuoteLeg(leg: QuoteLegInput | null | undefined): QuoteLegValuation {
  if (leg === null || leg === undefined) {
    return {
      code: 'no-quote-leg',
      currency: null,
      nativeAmount: null,
      nativeUsdPrice: null,
      usdAmount: null,
      reason: 'The venue reported no quote amount for this fill.'
    };
  }

  if (!isQuoteCurrency(leg.currency)) {
    throw new Error(
      `quote leg currency must be one of ${QUOTE_CURRENCIES.join(', ')}, received ${JSON.stringify(leg.currency)}`
    );
  }

  const nativeAmount = normalizeUnsignedDecimal(leg.amount);
  if (nativeAmount === null) {
    throw new Error(
      `quote leg amount must be a non-negative decimal, received ${JSON.stringify(leg.amount)}`
    );
  }

  if (leg.currency === 'USD') {
    return {
      code: 'valued',
      currency: 'USD',
      nativeAmount,
      nativeUsdPrice: '1',
      usdAmount: nativeAmount,
      reason: 'Settled in USD; no conversion applied.'
    };
  }

  const rate = normalizeUnsignedDecimal(leg.nativeUsdPrice);
  if (rate === null || Number(rate) <= 0) {
    return {
      code: 'native-price-unknown',
      currency: leg.currency,
      nativeAmount,
      nativeUsdPrice: null,
      usdAmount: null,
      reason:
        `Settled ${nativeAmount} ${leg.currency} but no usable USD rate was available, `
        + 'so the USD value is unknown rather than zero.'
    };
  }

  return {
    code: 'valued',
    currency: leg.currency,
    nativeAmount,
    nativeUsdPrice: rate,
    usdAmount: multiplyDecimalText(nativeAmount, rate),
    reason: `Converted ${nativeAmount} ${leg.currency} at ${rate} USD per ${leg.currency}.`
  };
}

/**
 * Exact decimal divide on text, truncated to `scale` fractional digits.
 *
 * Truncated rather than rounded, and truncated at a scale far beyond any venue's
 * tick, because the result is a derived diagnostic price rather than a settlement
 * figure. Both inputs must already be canonical unsigned decimals.
 */
export function divideDecimalText(
  numerator: string,
  denominator: string,
  scale = 18
): string | null {
  const a = splitDecimal(numerator);
  const b = splitDecimal(denominator);
  if (b.digits === 0n) return null;
  const scaled = a.digits * 10n ** BigInt(b.scale) * 10n ** BigInt(scale);
  const quotient = (scaled / (b.digits * 10n ** BigInt(a.scale))).toString();
  if (scale === 0) return trimDecimal(quotient);
  const padded = quotient.padStart(scale + 1, '0');
  const pointIndex = padded.length - scale;
  return trimDecimal(`${padded.slice(0, pointIndex)}.${padded.slice(pointIndex)}`);
}

/**
 * The realised USD price of one base unit in a fill: USD paid over units received.
 *
 * This exists because the Solana-live and robinhood-live fill recorders passed no
 * `priceUsd` at all, leaving `copy_execution_evidence.price_usd` NULL on both --
 * which is why `S4-M23`'s tracking difference could only be computed on Polymarket
 * and in paper mode. The two numbers needed are already in hand at that point, so
 * the price is derived rather than fetched, and a derived *fill* price is strictly
 * better for that comparison than a spot quote taken moments later.
 *
 * Returns `null` -- never `0` -- when either input is unusable, which is the whole
 * point: a missing price must stay missing rather than become a free trade.
 */
export function deriveFillPriceUsd(
  usdAmount: string | null | undefined,
  baseQuantity: string | number | null | undefined
): string | null {
  const usd = normalizeUnsignedDecimal(usdAmount);
  const base = normalizeUnsignedDecimal(baseQuantity);
  if (usd === null || base === null) return null;
  if (Number(base) <= 0) return null;
  return divideDecimalText(usd, base);
}

/**
 * Build a quote leg from a chain-native size, for callers that hold a raw size and
 * know it is denominated in the chain's native unit.
 *
 * This is the `persistTrade` shape. It is deliberately *not* the shape the copy
 * write path uses, because a paper fill on Solana is sized in USD and would be
 * mislabelled `SOL` by a chain lookup.
 */
export function valuateChainNativeQuoteLeg(input: {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly amount: string | number;
  readonly nativeUsdPrice?: string | number | null;
}): QuoteLegValuation {
  return valuateQuoteLeg({
    amount: input.amount,
    currency: nativeQuoteCurrencyForChain(input.chain),
    nativeUsdPrice: input.nativeUsdPrice
  });
}

/**
 * Why a summed USD quote total is or is not the whole truth.
 *
 * `SUM` skips NULLs, so `COALESCE(SUM(quote_quantity), 0)` reported a complete
 * number whether every fill was valued, some were, or none were. These codes make
 * the three cases distinguishable, which is the point: a partial sum is a floor and
 * must not be rendered as a settled figure.
 */
export type ConfirmedQuoteTotalCode =
  /** No confirmed fills at all. The total is a genuine, known zero. */
  | 'no-fills'
  /** Every confirmed fill carries a USD value. The total is complete. */
  | 'complete'
  /** Some fills carry a USD value and some do not. The total is a lower bound. */
  | 'partially-valued'
  /** At least one confirmed fill exists and none carries a USD value. */
  | 'unvalued';

export interface ConfirmedQuoteTotalInput {
  /** Confirmed fills whose USD quote value is known. */
  readonly valuedFillCount: number;
  /** Confirmed fills whose USD quote value is unknown. */
  readonly unvaluedFillCount: number;
  /** `SUM` over the valued fills only, as Postgres text. `null` when there were none. */
  readonly valuedUsdSum: string | null;
}

export interface ConfirmedQuoteTotal {
  readonly code: ConfirmedQuoteTotalCode;
  /**
   * USD total over the fills that have a value. `null` when nothing is known â€”
   * never `0` standing in for unknown.
   */
  readonly usdAmount: string | null;
  /** Number of confirmed fills the total omits. `0` means it omits nothing. */
  readonly unvaluedFillCount: number;
  /** `true` only when the total accounts for every confirmed fill. */
  readonly complete: boolean;
  readonly reason: string;
}

export function summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal(
  input: ConfirmedQuoteTotalInput
): ConfirmedQuoteTotal {
  const valued = assertCount('valuedFillCount', input.valuedFillCount);
  const unvalued = assertCount('unvaluedFillCount', input.unvaluedFillCount);

  if (valued === 0 && unvalued === 0) {
    return {
      code: 'no-fills',
      usdAmount: '0',
      unvaluedFillCount: 0,
      complete: true,
      reason: 'No confirmed fills yet, so the quote total is a known zero.'
    };
  }

  if (valued === 0) {
    return {
      code: 'unvalued',
      usdAmount: null,
      unvaluedFillCount: unvalued,
      complete: false,
      reason:
        `${unvalued} confirmed fill(s) carry no USD quote value, so the total is unknown `
        + 'rather than zero.'
    };
  }

  const sum = normalizeUnsignedDecimal(input.valuedUsdSum);
  if (sum === null) {
    throw new Error(
      `valuedUsdSum must be a non-negative decimal when valuedFillCount > 0, received ${JSON.stringify(input.valuedUsdSum)}`
    );
  }

  if (unvalued === 0) {
    return {
      code: 'complete',
      usdAmount: sum,
      unvaluedFillCount: 0,
      complete: true,
      reason: `All ${valued} confirmed fill(s) are valued in USD.`
    };
  }

  return {
    code: 'partially-valued',
    usdAmount: sum,
    unvaluedFillCount: unvalued,
    complete: false,
    reason:
      `${valued} confirmed fill(s) are valued and ${unvalued} are not, so ${sum} USD is a `
      + 'lower bound rather than the settled total.'
  };
}

function assertCount(name: string, value: number): number {
  const numeric = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value);
  if (!Number.isInteger(numeric) || numeric < 0) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be a non-negative integer, received ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
  }
  return numeric;
}

==> packages/db/src/relationships.ts <==
import { query } from './client.js';
import { resolveChainAddress } from '@swat/shared';
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';

/**
 * Record (or reinforce) a funding relationship: `funder` sent SOL to `funded`.
 *
 * Confidence scales with transfer size (a one-off dust transfer is weak
 * evidence; a multi-SOL transfer is strong). Repeated transfers accumulate
 * total lamports and transfer count in `evidence`.
 */
export async function recordFundingEdge(
  funder: string,
  funded: string,
  lamports: number,
  chain: Chain = 'solana'
) {
  const prefixedFunder = resolveChainAddress(funder, chain).prefixed;
  const prefixedFunded = resolveChainAddress(funded, chain).prefixed;
  if (prefixedFunder === prefixedFunded) return;
  if (!Number.isFinite(lamports) || lamports <= 0) return;

  // Map 0â€“10 SOL onto roughly 0.5â€“0.95 confidence; clamp.
  const sol = lamports / 1e9;
  const confidence = Math.min(0.95, 0.5 + sol * 0.045);

  await query(
    `INSERT INTO wallet_relationships (wallet_a, wallet_b, relationship_type, confidence, evidence)
     VALUES ($1, $2, 'funding', $3, jsonb_build_object('total_lamports', $4::bigint, 'transfers', 1))
     ON CONFLICT (wallet_a, wallet_b, relationship_type) DO UPDATE SET
       confidence = GREATEST(wallet_relationships.confidence, EXCLUDED.confidence),
       evidence = jsonb_build_object(
         'total_lamports',
         COALESCE((wallet_relationships.evidence->>'total_lamports')::bigint, 0) + $4::bigint,
         'transfers',
         COALESCE((wallet_relationships.evidence->>'transfers')::int, 0) + 1
       ),
       updated_at = NOW()`,
    [prefixedFunder, prefixedFunded, confidence, Math.round(lamports)]
  );
}

==> packages/db/src/risk-policy-cache.test.ts <==
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  query: vi.fn()
}));

vi.mock('./client.js', () => ({
  query: mocks.query
}));

import {
  RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES,
  RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS,
  clearRiskPolicyCache,
  resolveRiskPolicy,
  riskPolicyCacheSize
} from './risk-policy.js';

/**
 * The policy cache is bounded (`S4-P3`).
 *
 * It was a module-level `Map` keyed `${account}:${chain}`, TTL-checked on read but
 * **never swept**. With one operator that is three entries and invisible. Under
 * fan-out the key carries a user id, so it grows one entry per active user per
 * chain and retains every user who has ever traded â€” including churned ones.
 *
 * That is unbounded growth keyed by user id inside the process that also holds the
 * custody master key, which is the last process in the system that should leak
 * memory. These tests exist because nothing else would notice: a cache that grows
 * forever passes every functional test it has.
 */

describe('risk policy cache bounds', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    vi.useRealTimers();
    clearRiskPolicyCache();
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
    clearRiskPolicyCache();
  });

  it('caches one entry per (account, chain) pair', async () => {
    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-a', 'solana');
    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-a', 'polygon');
    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-b', 'solana');

    // Distinct keys, because a shared slot would let one chain serve another
    // chain's limits, and one user serve another user's.
    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBe(3);
  });

  it('serves a repeat lookup from cache without a second query', async () => {
    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-a', 'solana');
    const callsAfterFirst = mocks.query.mock.calls.length;

    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-a', 'solana');

    expect(mocks.query.mock.calls.length).toBe(callsAfterFirst);
    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBe(1);
  });

  it('sweeps expired entries instead of retaining them forever', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    await resolveRiskPolicy('churned-user', 'solana');
    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBe(1);

    // A user who never returns. Before the fix this entry lived for the life of
    // the process, because expiry was only ever checked on a read that never came.
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS + 1);

    // The sweep runs on write, so one unrelated resolve collects the dead entry.
    await resolveRiskPolicy('active-user', 'solana');

    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBe(1);
  });

  it('never exceeds the hard entry cap, however many users appear', async () => {
    // The backstop: a fan-out burst can outrun TTL expiry entirely, so expiry
    // alone is not a bound.
    const overflow = RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + 250;
    for (let i = 0; i < overflow; i++) {
      await resolveRiskPolicy(`user-${i}`, 'solana');
    }

    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBeLessThanOrEqual(RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES);
  });

  it('evicts oldest-first, so the newest entries survive the cap', async () => {
    const overflow = RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + 10;
    for (let i = 0; i < overflow; i++) {
      await resolveRiskPolicy(`user-${i}`, 'solana');
    }

    const callsBefore = mocks.query.mock.calls.length;
    // The most recent user should still be cached â€” evicting newest-first would
    // make the cache useless precisely when it is under load.
    await resolveRiskPolicy(`user-${overflow - 1}`, 'solana');

    expect(mocks.query.mock.calls.length).toBe(callsBefore);
  });

  it('clearRiskPolicyCache empties it', async () => {
    await resolveRiskPolicy('user-a', 'solana');
    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    clearRiskPolicyCache();

    expect(riskPolicyCacheSize()).toBe(0);
  });
});

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({

import { clearRiskPolicyCache, resolveRiskPolicy } from './risk-policy.js';

const ENV_KEYS = [
  'PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT',
  'USDC_BALANCE_RISK_PCT',
  'ETH_BALANCE_RISK_PCT',
  'DAILY_EXPOSURE_PCT',

] as const;

describe('resolveRiskPolicy', () => {
  const savedEnv: Record<string, string | undefined> = {};

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    clearRiskPolicyCache();
    for (const key of ENV_KEYS) {
      savedEnv[key] = process.env[key];
      delete process.env[key];
    }

  });

  afterEach(() => {
    for (const key of ENV_KEYS) {
      if (savedEnv[key] === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = savedEnv[key];
    }
    clearRiskPolicyCache();
  });

  it('prefers DB config over env and defaults', async () => {
    process.env.STOP_LOSS_PCT = '10';
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([
      { key: 'trading', value: { max_position_pct: 3, max_daily_exposure_pct: 12, min_liquidity_usd: 25000 } },
      { key: 'risk', value: { stop_loss_pct: 18, circuit_breaker_failures: 5 } }
    ]);

    await expect(resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana')).resolves.toEqual({
      maxPositionPct: 3,
      maxDailyExposurePct: 12,
      stopLossPct: 18,
      maxConsecutiveFailures: 5,
      minLiquidityUsd: 25000
    });
  });

  it('falls back to env when the DB has no config row', async () => {
    process.env.STOP_LOSS_PCT = '12.5';
    process.env.PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT = '4';

    const policy = await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana');
    expect(policy.stopLossPct).toBe(12.5);
    expect(policy.maxPositionPct).toBe(4);
  });

  it('does not serve one chain the other chain policy from cache', async () => {
    // The chain-specific env fallbacks are the reason the cache must be keyed
    // by chain: a shared slot returned polygon's sizing for robinhood-chain.
    process.env.USDC_BALANCE_RISK_PCT = '2';
    process.env.ETH_BALANCE_RISK_PCT = '9';

    const polygon = await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'polygon');
    const robinhood = await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'robinhood-chain');

    expect(polygon.maxPositionPct).toBe(2);
    expect(robinhood.maxPositionPct).toBe(9);
    expect(mocks.query).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('serves a repeat lookup for the same chain from cache', async () => {
    await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana');
    await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana');
    expect(mocks.query).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('coalesces concurrent lookups for the same chain into one query', async () => {
    const [a, b] = await Promise.all([
      resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana'),
      resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana')
    ]);
    expect(a).toEqual(b);
    expect(mocks.query).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('clamps the breaker threshold to at least one failure', async () => {
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([{ key: 'risk', value: { circuit_breaker_failures: 0 } }]);
    const policy = await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana');
    expect(policy.maxConsecutiveFailures).toBe(1);
  });

  it('ignores non-numeric config values', async () => {
    process.env.STOP_LOSS_PCT = 'not-a-number';
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([{ key: 'risk', value: { stop_loss_pct: '' } }]);

    const policy = await resolveRiskPolicy('operator', 'solana');
    expect(Number.isFinite(policy.stopLossPct)).toBe(true);
    expect(policy.stopLossPct).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/risk-policy.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';

const RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS = 30_000;

export interface RiskPolicy {
  maxPositionPct: number;
  maxDailyExposurePct: number;
  stopLossPct: number;
  maxConsecutiveFailures: number;
  minLiquidityUsd: number;
}

interface CachedRiskPolicy {
  policy: RiskPolicy;
  timestamp: number;
}

// Keyed by account:chain. The resolved policy is chain-specific (the env
// fallbacks below differ per chain), so a single shared slot would let one
// chain serve another chain's limits for the whole TTL.
//
// Bounded on purpose (`S4-P3`). With one operator this map holds three entries;
// under fan-out the key includes a user id, so it grows one entry per active user
// per chain and â€” because entries were only ever TTL-checked on *read*, never
// swept â€” retained every user who had ever traded, including churned ones. That
// is unbounded growth keyed by user id inside the process that also holds the
// custody master key, which is the last place to leak memory.
const cachedPolicies = new Map<string, CachedRiskPolicy>();
const policyLoads = new Map<string, { generation: number; promise: Promise<RiskPolicy> }>();
let cacheGeneration = 0;

/**
 * Hard entry cap. Sized for a few thousand active (user, chain) pairs; well past
 * that the DB round trip is cheaper than the resident memory.
 */
const RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 5_000;

/**
 * Drops expired entries, then evicts oldest-first if still over the cap.
 *
 * Eviction is by insertion order, which `Map` preserves â€” an approximation of LRU
 * that costs nothing, and is adequate because every entry expires within the TTL
 * anyway. The cap is the backstop for a burst that outruns expiry, not the primary
 * mechanism.
 */
function pruneRiskPolicyCache(now: number): void {
  for (const [key, entry] of cachedPolicies) {
    if (now - entry.timestamp >= RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS) cachedPolicies.delete(key);
  }
  if (cachedPolicies.size <= RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES) return;
  const excess = cachedPolicies.size - RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES;
  let removed = 0;
  for (const key of cachedPolicies.keys()) {
    if (removed >= excess) break;
    cachedPolicies.delete(key);
    removed += 1;
  }
}

function policyCacheKey(account: string, chain: Chain): string {
  return `${account}:${chain}`;
}

function numberOrUndefined(v: unknown): number | undefined {
  if (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v)) return v;
  if (typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length > 0) {
    const n = Number(v);
    if (Number.isFinite(n)) return n;
  }
  return undefined;
}

async function loadRiskPolicyFromDb(chain: Chain): Promise<RiskPolicy> {
  const rows = await query<{ key: string; value: unknown }>(
    `SELECT key, value FROM config WHERE key IN ('trading', 'risk')`
  );

  const trading = rows.find((r) => r.key === 'trading')?.value as any | undefined;
  const risk = rows.find((r) => r.key === 'risk')?.value as any | undefined;

  // DB values
  const dbMaxPosition = trading ? numberOrUndefined(trading.max_position_pct) : undefined;
  const dbMaxDaily = trading ? numberOrUndefined(trading.max_daily_exposure_pct) : undefined;
  const dbMinLiquidity = trading ? numberOrUndefined(trading.min_liquidity_usd) : undefined;
  const dbStopLoss = risk ? numberOrUndefined(risk.stop_loss_pct) : undefined;
  const dbBreakerFailures = risk ? numberOrUndefined(risk.circuit_breaker_failures) : undefined;

  // Env fallbacks
  const envPaper = numberOrUndefined(process.env.PAPER_MAX_POSITION_PCT);
  const envChainFallback = chain === 'polygon'
    ? numberOrUndefined(process.env.USDC_BALANCE_RISK_PCT)
    : chain === 'robinhood-chain'
      ? numberOrUndefined(process.env.ETH_BALANCE_RISK_PCT)
      : undefined;

  const maxPositionPct = dbMaxPosition ?? envPaper ?? envChainFallback ?? DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.maxPositionPct;
  const maxDailyExposurePct = dbMaxDaily ?? numberOrUndefined(process.env.DAILY_EXPOSURE_PCT) ?? DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.maxDailyExposurePct;
  const stopLossPct = dbStopLoss ?? numberOrUndefined(process.env.STOP_LOSS_PCT) ?? DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.stopLossPct;
  const maxConsecutiveFailures = Math.max(1, Math.floor(dbBreakerFailures ?? DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.maxConsecutiveFailures));
  const minLiquidityUsd = dbMinLiquidity ?? DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.minLiquidityUsd;

  return {
    maxPositionPct,
    maxDailyExposurePct,
    stopLossPct,
    maxConsecutiveFailures,
    minLiquidityUsd
  };
}

export async function resolveRiskPolicy(account: string, chain: Chain): Promise<RiskPolicy> {
  // account is part of the cache key so per-account policies (Standing Rule 2)
  // can be added here without a cache redesign; the lookup itself is not yet
  // account-scoped.
  const key = policyCacheKey(account, chain);
  const cached = cachedPolicies.get(key);
  if (cached && Date.now() - cached.timestamp < RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS) {
    return cached.policy;
  }

  const inFlight = policyLoads.get(key);
  if (inFlight?.generation === cacheGeneration) return inFlight.promise;

  const generation = cacheGeneration;
  const promise = loadRiskPolicyFromDb(chain).then((policy) => {
    if (generation === cacheGeneration) {
      const now = Date.now();
      cachedPolicies.set(key, { policy, timestamp: now });
      // Swept on write rather than on a timer: a timer would keep the process
      // alive and would run when nothing is being cached, whereas growth only
      // ever happens here.
      pruneRiskPolicyCache(now);
    }
    return policy;
  });
  policyLoads.set(key, { generation, promise });

  try {
    return await promise;
  } finally {
    if (policyLoads.get(key)?.promise === promise) policyLoads.delete(key);
  }
}

export function clearRiskPolicyCache(): void {
  cacheGeneration += 1;
  cachedPolicies.clear();
  policyLoads.clear();
}

/** Entry count. Test-only â€” lets a test assert the cache is actually bounded. */
export function riskPolicyCacheSize(): number {
  return cachedPolicies.size;
}

export { RISK_POLICY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES, RISK_POLICY_CACHE_TTL_MS };

describe('subscriber probes ignore ended subscriptions (051 / S4-M3)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.resetAllMocks();
    vi.mocked(client.query).mockResolvedValue([]);
  });

  // `051` retains an ended subscription rather than deleting the row. A bare
  // existence check therefore reads a wallet nobody tracks as still subscribed and
  // pins it to `active` forever â€” indexing cost stops being sublinear in user
  // count and grows with user churn instead, which is the D9 bound both of these
  // sweeps exist to enforce.
  it.each([
    ['pauseUnderperformingWallets', pauseUnderperformingWallets],
    ['pauseUnsubscribedWallets', pauseUnsubscribedWallets]
  ])('%s excludes ended rows from its subscriber check', async (_name, run) => {
    await run();
    const sql = vi.mocked(client.query).mock.calls[0]?.[0] as string;
    expect(sql).toContain('user_wallet_subscriptions');
    expect(sql).toMatch(/uws\.state\s*<>\s*'ended'/);
  });

  it.each([
    ['pauseUnderperformingWallets', pauseUnderperformingWallets],
    ['pauseUnsubscribedWallets', pauseUnsubscribedWallets]
  ])('%s still counts a winding_down row as a subscriber', async (_name, run) => {
    // A winding-down subscriber holds positions whose exits arrive as this
    // wallet's sell mirror. Pausing it would strand them with no exit signal â€”
    // strictly worse than keeping one wallet indexed.
    await run();
    const sql = vi.mocked(client.query).mock.calls[0]?.[0] as string;
    expect(sql).not.toContain("'winding_down'");
    expect(sql).not.toMatch(/uws\.state\s*=\s*'active'/);
  });
