describe('subscribeToWallet re-subscribe path', () => {
  const input = {
    walletAddress: WALLET,
    chain: 'solana' as const,
    tier: 'free' as const,
    tierExpiresAt: null
  };

  it('revives an ended subscription forward-only, and charges quota for it', async () => {
    routeClient([
      { match: /FOR UPDATE/, rows: [{ id: scope.userId }] },
      { match: /COUNT\(\*\)/, rows: [{ count: '1' }] },
      { match: /SELECT wallet_address/, rows: [row('ended')] },
      // Migration 056: re-entering `active` allocates a membership ordinal
      // under a per-master advisory lock. See master-membership.test.ts.
      { match: /pg_advisory_xact_lock/, rows: [] },
      { match: /SELECT membership_slot/, rows: [] },
      { match: /^\s*UPDATE/, rows: [row('active', { wound_down_at: null, ended_at: null })] }
    ]);

    const result = await subscribeToWallet(scope, input);

    // A new lifecycle, so the API's 201 is honest.
    expect(result.subscriptionCreated).toBe(true);
    expect(result.subscription.state).toBe('active');
    // `active_since` is the forward-only boundary (S4-M2). Resetting it is what
    // stops a revived subscriber catching up on the master's trades from before
    // the revival â€” `created_at` still points at the first lifecycle.
    expect(updates()[0]).toContain('active_since = NOW()');
    expect(updates()[0]).toContain('wound_down_at = NULL');
    expect(updates()[0]).toContain('ended_at = NULL');
    expect(updates()[0]).toContain('close_all_requested_at = NULL');
  });

  it('excludes ended rows from the tracked-wallet quota', async () => {
    routeClient([
      { match: /FOR UPDATE/, rows: [{ id: scope.userId }] },
      { match: /COUNT\(\*\)/, rows: [{ count: '0' }] },
      { match: /SELECT wallet_address/, rows: [row('ended')] },
      { match: /pg_advisory_xact_lock/, rows: [] },
      { match: /SELECT membership_slot/, rows: [] },
      { match: /^\s*UPDATE/, rows: [row('active', { wound_down_at: null, ended_at: null })] }
    ]);

    await subscribeToWallet(scope, input);

    // Counting them would mean a free-tier user who ends three subscriptions
    // can never start another one.
    const counted = statements().find((text) => /COUNT\(\*\)/.test(text));
    expect(counted).toContain("state <> 'ended'");
  });

  it('refuses to revive an ended subscription when the user is at quota', async () => {
    routeClient([
      { match: /FOR UPDATE/, rows: [{ id: scope.userId }] },
      // Free tier tracks 3.
      { match: /COUNT\(\*\)/, rows: [{ count: '3' }] },
      { match: /SELECT wallet_address/, rows: [row('ended')] }
    ]);

    await expect(subscribeToWallet(scope, input)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(QuotaExceededError);
    expect(updates()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('resumes a winding-down subscription without charging quota again', async () => {
    routeClient([
      { match: /FOR UPDATE/, rows: [{ id: scope.userId }] },
      { match: /SELECT wallet_address/, rows: [row('winding_down')] },
      { match: /pg_advisory_xact_lock/, rows: [] },
      // No COUNT(*) stub, deliberately: the membership read is a plain SELECT of
      // the ordinals, so an accidental quota re-check would still be caught.
      { match: /SELECT membership_slot/, rows: [] },
      { match: /^\s*UPDATE/, rows: [row('active', { wound_down_at: null })] }
    ]);

    const result = await subscribeToWallet(scope, input);

    // The row was never released, so it still occupies its slot. Charging
    // again would refuse a user their own wallet back at the quota boundary;
    // the unstubbed COUNT below is what proves no charge happened.
    expect(statements().some((text) => /COUNT\(\*\)/.test(text))).toBe(false);
    // Resuming a wind-down is not a creation, so the API answers 200, not 201.
    expect(result.subscriptionCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(result.subscription.state).toBe('active');
  });

  it('is a no-op for an already-active subscription', async () => {
    routeClient([
      { match: /FOR UPDATE/, rows: [{ id: scope.userId }] },
      { match: /SELECT wallet_address/, rows: [row('active')] }
    ]);

    const result = await subscribeToWallet(scope, input);

    expect(result.subscriptionCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(result.walletCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(updates()).toEqual([]);
  });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Read scoping
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe('live-subscription reads', () => {
  it('hides ended subscriptions from the user without deleting them', async () => {
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);
    await listWalletSubscriptions(scope);
    await isSubscribed(scope, WALLET);

    // The filter is the behaviour here â€” PostgreSQL applies it â€” so the SQL is
    // what there is to assert. `winding_down` must survive both filters: those
    // users still have open positions being mirrored out and marked to market.
    for (const call of mocks.query.mock.calls) {
      expect(String(call[0])).toContain("state <> 'ended'");
    }
  });

  it('exposes the ended row to the lifecycle reader', async () => {
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([row('ended')]);
    const record = await getSubscriptionState(scope, WALLET);

    expect(record?.state).toBe('ended');
    // Retained for attribution, so this reader must NOT filter it out.
    expect(String(mocks.query.mock.calls[0]?.[0])).not.toContain("state <> 'ended'");
  });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Migration 051
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe('migration 051', () => {
  const sqlPath = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../sql/051_subscription_states.sql');

  /** Comments talk about CREATE and ADD; only executable text is interesting. */
  async function executableSql(): Promise<string> {
    const raw = await readFile(sqlPath, 'utf8');
    return raw
      .split('\n')
      .filter((line) => !line.trimStart().startsWith('--'))
      .join('\n');
  }

  it('constrains the column to exactly the states this module knows', async () => {
    const sql = await executableSql();
    const check = /CHECK \(state IN \(([^)]*)\)\)/.exec(sql);
    expect(check).not.toBeNull();
    const states = check![1]!.split(',').map((value) => value.trim().replace(/'/g, ''));
    // Drift between the TS union and the SQL CHECK is silent in both
    // directions: a state TS can emit but the database rejects fails a write at
    // runtime, and a state the database accepts but TS cannot read falls
    // through `mirrorEligibilityForState` to 'none' and stops mirroring.
    expect(states).toEqual([...SUBSCRIPTION_STATES]);
  });

  it('defaults existing rows to active', async () => {
    const sql = await executableSql();
    // Exact, not a fallback: every row that exists was written by
    // `subscribeToWallet` and no fan-out has run, so none can be mid-wind-down.
    expect(sql).toMatch(/state VARCHAR\(16\) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'/);
  });

  it('makes an incoherent state/timestamp row unrepresentable, and fails closed', async () => {
    const sql = await executableSql();
    expect(sql).toContain('chk_subscription_state_stamps');
    // A fourth state added to the enum without a branch here is rejected
    // loudly rather than escaping the invariant.
    expect(sql).toContain('ELSE FALSE');
  });

  it('replays safely: every constraint add is guarded', async () => {
    const sql = await executableSql();
    // `migrate.ts` has no applied-migrations table, so a bare ADD CONSTRAINT
    // would break `pnpm db:migrate` for every developer on the second run.
    const guards = sql.match(/IF NOT EXISTS \(\s*SELECT 1\s+FROM pg_constraint/g) ?? [];
    const adds = sql.match(/ADD CONSTRAINT/g) ?? [];
    expect(adds.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(guards.length).toBe(adds.length);
  });

  it('adds the forward-only boundary column and backfills it from created_at', async () => {
    const sql = await executableSql();
    expect(sql).toContain('ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS active_since');
    // Stamping NOW() instead would erase every existing subscription's real
    // start time, and it is the boundary S4-M2 filters on.
    expect(sql).toMatch(/SET active_since = created_at\s+WHERE active_since IS NULL/);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/subscriptions.ts <==
import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';
import { capabilitiesFor, quotaExceeded, type Chain, type UserTier } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { claimMasterMembershipSlot, requireGrantedSlot } from './master-membership.js';
import { withTransaction } from './transaction.js';
import type { UserScope } from './tenancy.js';

/**
 * Per-user wallet subscriptions and token watches (Stage 2).
 *
 * Every read here is scoped by `UserScope`. Every write that consumes a quota
 * checks and inserts **inside one transaction** â€” see `QuotaExceededError`.
 */

/**
 * Over quota. Mapped to HTTP **402**, not 403.
 *
 * 403 means "you may never do this"; 402 means "upgrade and you may". The
 * frontend needs that distinction to show an upgrade prompt rather than an
 * error, and conflating them makes every paywall look like a bug.
 */
export class QuotaExceededError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly quota: string,
    readonly limit: number,
    readonly used: number
  ) {
    super(`Quota exceeded: ${quota} (${used}/${limit})`);
    this.name = 'QuotaExceededError';
  }
}

export class WalletNotSubscribedError extends Error {
  constructor() {
    super('Wallet not subscribed');
    this.name = 'WalletNotSubscribedError';
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Subscription lifecycle (S4-M3, ADR-0005 Â§3.7)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Mirroring lifecycle of one subscription. Persisted as
 * `user_wallet_subscriptions.state` by migration `051`.
 *
 * - `active` â€” mirror the master's buys **and** sells.
 * - `winding_down` â€” mirror the master's **sells only**. Unsubscribe lands
 *   here: entries stop immediately, but a position opened while active keeps
 *   the exit path it was always going to use, which is the master's sell
 *   mirror. Auto-selling instead would be a market action the user never
 *   requested, and dropping the link would orphan the position.
 * - `ended` â€” mirror nothing. The last position opened under this
 *   subscription has closed, or unsubscribe found nothing open.
 */
export type SubscriptionState = 'active' | 'winding_down' | 'ended';

/**
 * Frozen rather than a `ReadonlySet`, following the `S4-M0` precedent in
 * `apps/signal-engine/src/trade-eligibility.ts`: `readonly` is a compile-time
 * claim only, and one stray `.add()` would widen the state machine
 * process-wide with no diff to review.
 */
export const SUBSCRIPTION_STATES: readonly SubscriptionState[] = Object.freeze([
  'active',
  'winding_down',
  'ended'
] as const);

export function isSubscriptionState(value: unknown): value is SubscriptionState {
  return typeof value === 'string' && (SUBSCRIPTION_STATES as readonly string[]).includes(value);
}

/** What the fan-out is allowed to mirror for a subscription in a given state. */
export type MirrorEligibility = 'buys-and-sells' | 'sells-only' | 'none';

/**
 * The single definition of what each state permits â€” the term `S4-13` consumes
 * when enumerating eligible users for a signal.
 *
 * **Fails closed.** The argument is `unknown` rather than `SubscriptionState`
 * on purpose: the value arrives from a database column, so a row written by a
 * future migration, a manual UPDATE, or a service running a different release
 * can carry a state this build has never heard of. An unrecognised state
 * mirrors nothing, because the alternative â€” treating it as `active` â€” opens
 * positions on behalf of a user whose intent we cannot read.
 */
export function mirrorEligibilityForState(state: unknown): MirrorEligibility {
  switch (state) {
    case 'active':
      return 'buys-and-sells';
    case 'winding_down':
      return 'sells-only';
    default:
      return 'none';
  }
}

export type SubscriptionTransitionVerdict =
  | { readonly kind: 'apply'; readonly from: SubscriptionState; readonly to: SubscriptionState }
  | { readonly kind: 'noop'; readonly state: SubscriptionState }
  | { readonly kind: 'illegal'; readonly from: unknown; readonly to: unknown; readonly reason: string };

/**
 * Legal transitions, as data. `undefined` entries are the illegal ones and
 * carry the reason, so the refusal is explainable rather than a bare boolean.
 */
const TRANSITION_REFUSALS: Readonly<
  Record<SubscriptionState, Partial<Record<SubscriptionState, string>>>
> = Object.freeze({
  active: {},
  winding_down: {},
  // An `ended` subscription holds nothing to wind down â€” that is what `ended`
  // means. Allowing it would create a row claiming sells-only eligibility over
  // positions that are already closed, and the sell mirror would then look for
  // holdings that do not exist.
  ended: { winding_down: 'an ended subscription has no open position to wind down' }
});

/**
 * Pure state machine. **This is the only place that decides transition
 * legality**; the database helpers below call it rather than embedding their
 * own rules, so the rules are unit-testable without infrastructure â€” the same
 * split `stop-loss.ts` uses between its decision math and its DB claim.
 *
 * The legal graph, and why:
 *
 * - `active â†’ winding_down` â€” unsubscribe. The main path.
 * - `active â†’ ended` â€” unsubscribe with nothing open. A subscription that
 *   never opened a position must not be forced through a fictitious wind-down
 *   it would then sit in forever, since nothing would ever close to end it.
 * - `winding_down â†’ ended` â€” the last open position closed. The normal exit.
 * - `winding_down â†’ active` â€” **legal, deliberately.** The user changed their
 *   mind while positions are still open. Refusing would be worse product for
 *   no correctness gain: the primary key `(user_id, wallet_address)` forbids a
 *   second row, so a refusal would mean the user cannot re-subscribe until
 *   every position happens to close. The positions in question came from this
 *   very subscription, so their cost basis is known and nothing is being
 *   entered blind. Forward-only (S4-M2) is preserved because entering `active`
 *   resets `active_since` â€” the wind-down window is never caught up on.
 * - `ended â†’ active` â€” an ordinary re-subscribe, forward-only from now.
 * - `ended â†’ winding_down` â€” refused, see `TRANSITION_REFUSALS`.
 *
 * Same-state requests are `noop`, not `illegal`: a double-clicked unsubscribe
 * or a redelivered job must be idempotent, not an error.
 */
export function evaluateSubscriptionTransition(
  from: unknown,
  to: unknown
): SubscriptionTransitionVerdict {
  if (!isSubscriptionState(from)) {
    return { kind: 'illegal', from, to, reason: 'unrecognised current state' };
  }
  if (!isSubscriptionState(to)) {
    return { kind: 'illegal', from, to, reason: 'unrecognised target state' };
  }
  if (from === to) {
    return { kind: 'noop', state: from };
  }
  const refusal = TRANSITION_REFUSALS[from][to];
  if (refusal) {
    return { kind: 'illegal', from, to, reason: refusal };
  }
  return { kind: 'apply', from, to };
}

export class IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly from: unknown,
    readonly to: unknown,
    readonly reason: string
  ) {
    super(`Illegal subscription transition ${String(from)} -> ${String(to)}: ${reason}`);
    this.name = 'IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError';
  }
}

export type SubscriptionSource = 'manual' | 'platform-signal' | 'discovered';

/**
 * One subscription as a user is allowed to see it.
 *
 * **There is deliberately no `membershipSlot` field** (`S4-M9`). The ordinal
 * migration `056` stores is a rank, and a rank is a headcount signal: "you are
 * member #37" tells a user roughly how many people are ahead of them in the
 * queue behind one worker, and tells a master when farming their own followers
 * pays. Adding it here would ship it straight to `GET /v1/me/wallets`.
 */
export interface WalletSubscription {
  readonly walletAddress: string;
  readonly label: string | null;
  readonly source: SubscriptionSource;
  readonly createdAt: Date;
  readonly state: SubscriptionState;
  /**
   * Start of the CURRENT active period, reset on every entry into `active`.
   * The forward-only mirror boundary (S4-M2) â€” not `createdAt`, which a
   * revived subscription keeps from its first lifecycle.
   */
  readonly activeSince: Date;
  readonly woundDownAt: Date | null;
  readonly endedAt: Date | null;
  readonly closeAllRequestedAt: Date | null;
}

interface SubscriptionRow {
  wallet_address: string;
  label: string | null;
  source: SubscriptionSource;
  created_at: Date;
  state: SubscriptionState;
  active_since: Date;
  wound_down_at: Date | null;
  ended_at: Date | null;
  close_all_requested_at: Date | null;
  /**
   * Present only on reads that use `SUBSCRIPTION_INTERNAL_COLUMNS`. Optional so
   * the user-facing reads cannot accidentally be typed as if they had it.
   */
  membership_slot?: number | null;
  membership_grandfathered?: boolean;
}

/** Every column `toSubscription` needs, in one place so the reads cannot drift. */
const SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS = `wallet_address, label, source, created_at,
          state, active_since, wound_down_at, ended_at, close_all_requested_at`;

/**
 * The above plus the membership-slot columns (migration `056`).
 *
 * Kept separate rather than folded into `SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS` because a slot
 * ordinal is a **rank**, and a rank discloses the follower count `S4-M9`
 * forbids showing â€” "you are member #37" tells a user roughly how many people
 * are ahead of them and tells a master when farming their own followers pays.
 * `toSubscription` therefore has no field for it, and only the writers that
 * must allocate or release an ordinal select it.
 */
const SUBSCRIPTION_INTERNAL_COLUMNS =
  `${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS},
          membership_slot, membership_grandfathered`;

function toSubscription(row: SubscriptionRow): WalletSubscription {
  return {
    walletAddress: row.wallet_address,
    label: row.label,
    source: row.source,
    createdAt: row.created_at,
    state: row.state,
    activeSince: row.active_since,
    woundDownAt: row.wound_down_at,
    endedAt: row.ended_at,
    closeAllRequestedAt: row.close_all_requested_at
  };
}

/**
 * The user's live subscriptions â€” `active` and `winding_down`.
 *
 * `ended` rows are excluded rather than deleted. They are retained so a closed
 * position stays attributable to the subscription that opened it, but they are
 * not something the user is tracking any more, so listing them would put dead
 * wallets in the dashboard and in `GET /v1/me/wallets`.
 */
export async function listWalletSubscriptions(scope: UserScope): Promise<WalletSubscription[]> {
  const rows = await query<SubscriptionRow>(
    `SELECT ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND state <> 'ended'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC`,
    [scope.userId]
  );
  return rows.map(toSubscription);
}

/**
 * Whether the user still holds a live subscription to this wallet.
 *
 * `winding_down` counts: those users still have open positions being mirrored
 * out and marked to market, so the per-wallet endpoints this gates must keep
 * working for them. `ended` does not.
 */
export async function isSubscribed(scope: UserScope, walletAddress: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ one: number }>(
    `SELECT 1 AS one FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2 AND state <> 'ended'`,
    [scope.userId, walletAddress]
  );
  return rows.length > 0;
}

export interface SubscribeResult {
  readonly subscription: WalletSubscription;
  /** True when this call created the global wallet row, i.e. a backfill is needed. */
  readonly walletCreated: boolean;
  /** False when the user was already subscribed â€” the call was a no-op. */
  readonly subscriptionCreated: boolean;
}

/**
 * Serialises quota-consuming writes for one user.
 *
 * **A transaction alone does not enforce a quota.** `withTransaction` runs at
 * READ COMMITTED, so N concurrent `COUNT(*)` reads all observe the state before
 * any of them commits â€” every one sees `0 < 3` and every one inserts. A test
 * firing five concurrent subscribes against a 3-wallet tier granted all five.
 *
 * Locking the user's own row first serialises that user's quota writes without
 * touching anyone else's: different users take different locks and never contend.
 * `FOR UPDATE` on `users` is preferred over `SERIALIZABLE` because it needs no
 * retry loop, and over an advisory lock because the row already exists and the
 * lock is released by the transaction automatically.
 */
async function lockUserForQuota(
  client: { query: (text: string, values: unknown[]) => Promise<unknown> },
  userId: string
): Promise<void> {
  await client.query('SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE', [userId]);
}

/**
 * Throws `QuotaExceededError` when the user is at their tracked-wallet limit.
 *
 * **`ended` rows do not count.** A subscription the user has finished with must
 * not occupy a tracked-wallet slot forever â€” those rows are retained for
 * attribution, and counting them would mean a free-tier user who ends three
 * subscriptions can never start another one.
 *
 * **`winding_down` rows DO count.** The platform is still indexing that wallet
 * and still mirroring exits against it, so the resource the quota bounds is
 * still being consumed. Excluding them would also make the quota trivially
 * bypassable: unsubscribe from each wallet in turn and track an unlimited
 * number of masters, all of them still receiving sell mirrors.
 *
 * Must be called with the user's row already locked (`lockUserForQuota`), or
 * concurrent callers all read the pre-insert count. See that function.
 */
async function assertTrackedWalletQuota(
  client: PoolClient,
  userId: string,
  limit: number | null
): Promise<void> {
  const counted = await client.query<{ count: string }>(
    `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND state <> 'ended'`,
    [userId]
  );
  const used = Number(counted.rows[0]?.count ?? '0');
  if (quotaExceeded(limit, used)) {
    throw new QuotaExceededError('trackedWallets', limit ?? 0, used);
  }
}

/**
 * Subscribes a user to a wallet, creating the global wallet row if absent.
 *
 * `walletCreated` is returned rather than inferred by the caller, so the backfill
 * is enqueued exactly when the wallet is genuinely new. Enqueuing on every
 * subscribe would re-backfill a wallet each time another user tracks it.
 *
 * Also the **re-subscribe** path (S4-M3): a `winding_down` or `ended` row is
 * transitioned back to `active` here rather than in a separate helper, so the
 * tracked-wallet quota is resolved in exactly one place.
 *
 * **Two independent caps bind here and they are not interchangeable.** The
 * tracked-wallet quota is the *user's* limit â€” how many masters this account may
 * follow â€” and over it means 402, upgrade and you may. The membership cap
 * (`S4-M43`, migration `056`) is the *master's* limit â€” how many users it may
 * serve â€” and over it means a refusal no upgrade can lift. The quota is checked
 * first because it is the more specific answer to the caller, and because
 * telling a user "the master is not accepting copiers" when they could not have
 * subscribed anyway discloses the master's state for nothing (`S4-M9`).
 */
export async function subscribeToWallet(
  scope: UserScope,
  input: {
    walletAddress: string;
    chain: Chain;
    tier: UserTier;
    tierExpiresAt: Date | null;
    label?: string | null;
    source?: SubscriptionSource;
  }
): Promise<SubscribeResult> {
  const capabilities = capabilitiesFor(input.tier, input.tierExpiresAt);

  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    await lockUserForQuota(client, scope.userId);

    const existing = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
      `SELECT ${SUBSCRIPTION_INTERNAL_COLUMNS}
         FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
      [scope.userId, input.walletAddress]
    );
    const current = existing.rows[0];

    // Already active: idempotent success, and it must not consume quota. Nor a
    // membership slot â€” the row already holds one (or is grandfathered), and
    // running the allocator here would refuse an existing member their own
    // wallet the moment the master filled up.
    if (current && current.state === 'active') {
      return {
        subscription: toSubscription(current),
        walletCreated: false,
        subscriptionCreated: false
      };
    }

    // A `winding_down` or `ended` row is a RE-SUBSCRIBE, not a duplicate. The
    // primary key `(user_id, wallet_address)` forbids a second row, so this
    // transition is the only representation a re-subscribe can have â€” and
    // returning "already subscribed" here instead would leave the user
    // permanently unable to restart a subscription they had ended.
    //
    // `active_since = NOW()` is what keeps this forward-only (S4-M2): the
    // master's trades during the wind-down or ended window are never caught up
    // on, no matter how long ago `created_at` was.
    if (current) {
      const verdict = evaluateSubscriptionTransition(current.state, 'active');
      if (verdict.kind === 'illegal') {
        throw new IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError(verdict.from, verdict.to, verdict.reason);
      }
      // Reviving an `ended` row consumes a slot, because `ended` rows are not
      // counted. Resuming a `winding_down` row does not â€” it is already counted.
      if (current.state === 'ended') {
        await assertTrackedWalletQuota(client, scope.userId, capabilities.trackedWallets);
      }

      // S4-M43 / S4-M44. Neither a `winding_down` nor an `ended` row holds a
      // membership ordinal â€” migration `056`'s CHECK makes that unrepresentable
      // â€” so re-entering `active` is an ordinary allocation and is refused when
      // the master is full. The slot the user used to hold is not reserved for
      // them: a reservation is a queue, and a queue holding a slot for an absent
      // user makes the cap dishonest.
      //
      // Note this also applies to `winding_down â†’ active`, the "changed my mind"
      // path. It has to: the row released its ordinal when it wound down, and
      // exempting it would let a user hold a slot indefinitely by cycling.
      const membership = await claimMasterMembershipSlot(client, {
        masterWalletAddress: input.walletAddress,
        requester: {
          priorState: current.state,
          heldSlot: current.membership_slot ?? null
        }
      });

      const revived = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
            SET state = 'active',
                active_since = NOW(),
                wound_down_at = NULL,
                ended_at = NULL,
                close_all_requested_at = NULL,
                membership_slot = $5,
                membership_grandfathered = FALSE,
                label = COALESCE($3, label),
                source = COALESCE($4, source)
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
        RETURNING ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}`,
        [
          scope.userId,
          input.walletAddress,
          input.label ?? null,
          input.source ?? null,
          requireGrantedSlot(membership)
        ]
      );
      return {
        subscription: toSubscription(revived.rows[0]!),
        walletCreated: false,
        // Reviving an ended subscription starts a new lifecycle, so the
        // caller's 201 is honest. Resuming a wind-down is not a creation.
        subscriptionCreated: current.state === 'ended'
      };
    }

    await assertTrackedWalletQuota(client, scope.userId, capabilities.trackedWallets);

    const inserted = await client.query<{ address: string }>(
      `INSERT INTO wallets (address, chain, source, status)
       VALUES ($1, $2, 'manual', 'active')
       ON CONFLICT (address) DO NOTHING
       RETURNING address`,
      [input.walletAddress, input.chain]
    );
    const walletCreated = inserted.rows.length > 0;

    // S4-M43: a first-time join takes an ordinal or is refused. Placed after the
    // `wallets` upsert so the global wallet row exists for the foreign key, and
    // inside the same transaction as the INSERT below so the advisory lock the
    // allocator takes is still held when the ordinal is consumed.
    const membership = await claimMasterMembershipSlot(client, {
      masterWalletAddress: input.walletAddress,
      requester: { priorState: null, heldSlot: null }
    });

    const subscription = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
      `INSERT INTO user_wallet_subscriptions
              (user_id, wallet_address, label, source, membership_slot)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, COALESCE($4, 'manual'), $5)
       RETURNING ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}`,
      [
        scope.userId,
        input.walletAddress,
        input.label ?? null,
        input.source ?? null,
        requireGrantedSlot(membership)
      ]
    );

    return {
      subscription: toSubscription(subscription.rows[0]!),
      walletCreated,
      subscriptionCreated: true
    };
  });
}

/**
 * Removes one user's subscription **row**, permanently.
 *
 * **Never touches the global wallet row.** Another tenant may be subscribed to
 * it, and the platform may be scoring it â€” deleting it here would be a
 * cross-tenant data loss triggered by an ordinary unsubscribe.
 *
 * **This is the pre-fan-out unsubscribe and it is not the ADR-0005 one.** Once
 * a subscription can have opened a copy position, deleting the row is exactly
 * the abandonment Â§3.7 rejects: the position's exit was going to arrive as the
 * master's sell mirror, and the row is what says so. The ADR-0005 operations
 * are `beginWindDown` (stop entries, keep honouring sells) and
 * `endSubscription` (nothing left open).
 *
 * It is deliberately left in place rather than redirected to `beginWindDown`,
 * because choosing between `winding_down` and `ended` requires knowing whether
 * the subscription has an open position, and **nothing in the schema can answer
 * that yet**: `copy_positions` is keyed `(target_account, chain, token_mint)`
 * plus `user_id` (028, 050) and carries no master-wallet column, so a position
 * cannot be attributed to the subscription that opened it. Defaulting to
 * `winding_down` would strand every unsubscribe in a state nothing can clear,
 * which is worse than the current behaviour. Redirect this at the moment
 * fan-out lands that attribution (S4-13/S4-15), not before.
 */
export async function unsubscribeFromWallet(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ wallet_address: string }>(
    `DELETE FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
      RETURNING wallet_address`,
    [scope.userId, walletAddress]
  );
  return rows.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Lifecycle transitions (S4-M3)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface SubscriptionStateChange {
  readonly subscription: WalletSubscription;
  /** False when the subscription was already in the requested state. */
  readonly changed: boolean;
}

/** The full lifecycle row, including `ended` â€” unlike `listWalletSubscriptions`. */
export async function getSubscriptionState(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<WalletSubscription | null> {
  const rows = await query<SubscriptionRow>(
    `SELECT ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
    [scope.userId, walletAddress]
  );
  return rows[0] ? toSubscription(rows[0]) : null;
}

/**
 * Applies one lifecycle transition, refusing anything
 * `evaluateSubscriptionTransition` calls illegal.
 *
 * `FOR UPDATE` on the subscription row, not on the user row: this consumes no
 * quota, and two concurrent transitions of the *same* subscription are the race
 * that matters â€” an unsubscribe and a "last position closed" sweep arriving
 * together must not both read `active` and produce a row whose timestamps
 * disagree with its state. Locking the subscription rather than the user also
 * keeps a wind-down from serialising behind that user's unrelated subscribes.
 *
 * Entry into `active` is deliberately NOT reachable here â€” it consumes
 * tracked-wallet quota, so it lives in `subscribeToWallet`.
 */
async function applyTransition(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string,
  to: 'winding_down' | 'ended'
): Promise<SubscriptionStateChange> {
  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    const locked = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
      `SELECT ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}
         FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
        FOR UPDATE`,
      [scope.userId, walletAddress]
    );
    const current = locked.rows[0];
    if (!current) throw new WalletNotSubscribedError();

    const verdict = evaluateSubscriptionTransition(current.state, to);
    if (verdict.kind === 'illegal') {
      throw new IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError(verdict.from, verdict.to, verdict.reason);
    }
    if (verdict.kind === 'noop') {
      return { subscription: toSubscription(current), changed: false };
    }

    // One statement per target rather than a single clever one, so each write
    // visibly satisfies `chk_subscription_state_stamps` from migration 051.
    //
    // `wound_down_at` is COALESCEd rather than overwritten on the way into
    // `winding_down` so that a subscription which was wound down, revived and
    // wound down again... cannot in fact reach that branch â€” entry into
    // `active` NULLs it. The COALESCE is defence against a future writer that
    // forgets, not dead code: silently resetting the clock would hide a
    // wind-down that has been stuck for weeks (S4-M17).
    //
    // Entering `ended` deliberately preserves `wound_down_at`, because
    // "how long did this take to close" is the operational question, and
    // leaves it NULL on the direct `active â†’ ended` path, which is why the
    // migration's CHECK does not require it for `ended`.
    //
    // Both branches release the membership ordinal (S4-M43/S4-M44, migration
    // `056`). A leaver must not hold a slot: they are no longer receiving
    // entries, so holding one would make the cap under-serve the master by
    // exactly the number of people on their way out. They **do** keep receiving
    // sell mirrors, because that is derived from `state` alone â€” nothing on the
    // fan-out path reads `membership_slot`, so releasing the slot cannot strand
    // their open positions. `membership_grandfathered` is cleared for the same
    // reason: `056`'s CHECK forbids a non-active row carrying the exemption, and
    // clearing it here is what makes re-subscribe take a real ordinal or be
    // refused.
    const updated =
      to === 'winding_down'
        ? await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
            `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
                SET state = 'winding_down',
                    wound_down_at = COALESCE(wound_down_at, NOW()),
                    membership_slot = NULL,
                    membership_grandfathered = FALSE
              WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
            RETURNING ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}`,
            [scope.userId, walletAddress]
          )
        : await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
            `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
                SET state = 'ended',
                    ended_at = NOW(),
                    membership_slot = NULL,
                    membership_grandfathered = FALSE
              WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
            RETURNING ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}`,
            [scope.userId, walletAddress]
          );

    return { subscription: toSubscription(updated.rows[0]!), changed: true };
  });
}

/**
 * Unsubscribe, ADR-0005 Â§3.7 semantics: **stop entries immediately, keep
 * honouring the master's sells** until each open position closes.
 *
 * Idempotent â€” a double-clicked unsubscribe returns `changed: false` rather
 * than throwing, and does not move `wound_down_at`.
 */
export async function beginWindDown(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<SubscriptionStateChange> {
  return applyTransition(scope, walletAddress, 'winding_down');
}

/**
 * Mirroring is over: the last position opened under this subscription has
 * closed, or the unsubscribe found nothing open at all.
 *
 * Reachable from `winding_down` (the normal path) and directly from `active`
 * (nothing was ever opened). The row is retained, not deleted, so a closed
 * position stays attributable to the subscription that opened it.
 */
export async function endSubscription(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<SubscriptionStateChange> {
  return applyTransition(scope, walletAddress, 'ended');
}

/**
 * The explicit **"close all now"** (S4-M3): exit every open position rather
 * than waiting for the master to sell.
 *
 * Winds the subscription down first when it is still `active`, because a user
 * asking to exit everything has certainly asked to stop entering. Both halves
 * land in one statement so there is no window in which entries are still
 * eligible while exits are being requested.
 *
 * Records the request; it does not place orders. It must be durable rather than
 * an in-flight command so the request survives an executor restart, and
 * `COALESCE` makes a second click a no-op instead of a second round of sells.
 *
 * Refused on an `ended` subscription: there is nothing open to close, and
 * accepting it would imply otherwise.
 */
export async function requestCloseAll(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<SubscriptionStateChange> {
  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    const locked = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
      `SELECT ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}
         FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
        FOR UPDATE`,
      [scope.userId, walletAddress]
    );
    const current = locked.rows[0];
    if (!current) throw new WalletNotSubscribedError();

    // Routed through the same state machine so "close all" can never reach a
    // state ordinary wind-down could not. From `active` this is `apply`; from
    // `winding_down` it is `noop` and only the stamp changes; from `ended` â€”
    // or any state this build does not recognise â€” it is illegal.
    const verdict = evaluateSubscriptionTransition(current.state, 'winding_down');
    if (verdict.kind === 'illegal') {
      throw new IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError(verdict.from, verdict.to, verdict.reason);
    }

    // Already winding down AND already requested: nothing to write. Keeps the
    // invariant that a no-op transition issues no UPDATE, and avoids a pointless
    // row version on every repeated click.
    if (verdict.kind === 'noop' && current.close_all_requested_at !== null) {
      return { subscription: toSubscription(current), changed: false };
    }

    const updated = await client.query<SubscriptionRow>(
      `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
          SET state = 'winding_down',
              wound_down_at = COALESCE(wound_down_at, NOW()),
              close_all_requested_at = COALESCE(close_all_requested_at, NOW()),
              membership_slot = NULL,
              membership_grandfathered = FALSE
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2
      RETURNING ${SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS}`,
      [scope.userId, walletAddress]
    );

    return { subscription: toSubscription(updated.rows[0]!), changed: true };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Token watches
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type TokenWatchStatus = 'pending' | 'running' | 'complete' | 'failed';

export interface TokenWatch {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly tokenMint: string;
  readonly status: TokenWatchStatus;
  readonly createdAt: Date;
}

interface TokenWatchRow {
  id: string;
  chain: Chain;
  token_mint: string;
  status: TokenWatchStatus;
  created_at: Date;
}

function toWatch(row: TokenWatchRow): TokenWatch {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    chain: row.chain,
    tokenMint: row.token_mint,
    status: row.status,
    createdAt: row.created_at
  };
}

export async function listTokenWatches(scope: UserScope): Promise<TokenWatch[]> {
  const rows = await query<TokenWatchRow>(
    `SELECT id, chain, token_mint, status, created_at
       FROM user_token_watches
      WHERE user_id = $1
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 100`,
    [scope.userId]
  );
  return rows.map(toWatch);
}

export interface RequestTokenWatchResult {
  readonly watch: TokenWatch;
  /** False when this token was already being watched â€” no quota was consumed. */
  readonly created: boolean;
}

/**
 * Starts a token backfill, subject to the rolling-24h quota.
 *
 * Re-requesting a token already watched returns the existing row and consumes no
 * quota â€” otherwise a user could exhaust their day by double-clicking.
 */
export async function requestTokenWatch(
  scope: UserScope,
  input: {
    chain: Chain;
    tokenMint: string;
    tier: UserTier;
    tierExpiresAt: Date | null;
  }
): Promise<RequestTokenWatchResult> {
  const capabilities = capabilitiesFor(input.tier, input.tierExpiresAt);

  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    // Same serialisation as the wallet quota â€” see `lockUserForQuota`.
    await lockUserForQuota(client, scope.userId);

    const existing = await client.query<TokenWatchRow>(
      `SELECT id, chain, token_mint, status, created_at
         FROM user_token_watches
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND chain = $2 AND token_mint = $3`,
      [scope.userId, input.chain, input.tokenMint]
    );
    if (existing.rows[0]) {
      return { watch: toWatch(existing.rows[0]), created: false };
    }

    // Rolling 24h, not calendar-day: a calendar reset lets a user spend two days'
    // quota in a few minutes across midnight.
    const counted = await client.query<{ count: string }>(
      `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM user_token_watches
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'`,
      [scope.userId]
    );
    const used = Number(counted.rows[0]?.count ?? '0');
    if (quotaExceeded(capabilities.tokenBackfillsPerDay, used)) {
      throw new QuotaExceededError('tokenBackfillsPerDay', capabilities.tokenBackfillsPerDay ?? 0, used);
    }

    const inserted = await client.query<TokenWatchRow>(
      `INSERT INTO user_token_watches (user_id, chain, token_mint)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
       RETURNING id, chain, token_mint, status, created_at`,
      [scope.userId, input.chain, input.tokenMint]
    );
    return { watch: toWatch(inserted.rows[0]!), created: true };
  });
}

==> packages/db/src/tenancy.ts <==
import type { PoolClient, QueryResultRow } from 'pg';
import { withTransaction, type TransactionOptions } from './transaction.js';

/**
 * Tenant scoping (D12 & Migration 064).
 *
 * Dual-layer defense-in-depth security model:
 *
 * 1. Application Layer (TypeScript Nominal Typing):
 *    `user_id` comes from the verified session, never from an untrusted request payload.
 *    Per-user query functions take a `UserScope` as their first parameter. The only
 *    constructor is `forUser(userId)`, which ensures raw string bodies cannot be passed.
 *
 * 2. Database Layer (PostgreSQL Row-Level Security):
 *    PostgreSQL RLS is enabled and forced (`FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`) across all 17
 *    user-scoped tables (`users`, `user_sessions`, `user_auth_wallets`, `user_api_keys`,
 *    `user_balances`, `user_wallet_subscriptions`, `user_token_watches`,
 *    `user_execution_grants`, `user_execution_settings`, `user_chain_execution_settings`,
 *    `user_payment_intents`, `crypto_payments`, `copy_positions`, `copy_executions`,
 *    `copy_position_master_lots`, `copy_position_applications`, `copy_position_close_all_claims`).
 *    When executing queries within `withTenantTransaction(scope, ...)` or `scopedQuery(scope, ...)`,
 *    Postgres sets `app.bypass_rls = 'off'` and `app.current_user_id = scope.userId`,
 *    enforcing kernel-level database isolation.
 */

declare const scopeBrand: unique symbol;

export interface UserScope {
  readonly userId: string;
  /** Prevents a bare `{ userId }` object literal from satisfying the type. */
  readonly [scopeBrand]: true;
}

/**
 * The only constructor for a `UserScope`.
 *
 * Call this with a session-derived id and nothing else. It is intentionally the
 * single grep target for "where does tenant scope enter the system?".
 */
export function forUser(userId: string): UserScope {
  if (!userId) {
    // An empty scope would silently widen every query built from it.
    throw new Error('forUser() requires a user id');
  }
  return { userId } as UserScope;
}

/**
 * Escape hatch for routes that legitimately cross tenants (admin listings,
 * platform-wide reports, background jobs).
 *
 * Deliberately verbose and separately named so that crossing tenants is
 * greppable rather than implicit â€” `grep -rn crossTenant` should return a short,
 * reviewable list. Any new occurrence is a security review item.
 */
export function crossTenantScope(reason: string): UserScope {
  if (!reason) throw new Error('crossTenantScope() requires a stated reason');
  return { userId: '*' } as UserScope;
}

export function isCrossTenant(scope: UserScope): boolean {
  return scope.userId === '*';
}

/**
 * Sets the PostgreSQL session variables for Row-Level Security on a checked-out client.
 *
 * Scopes queries to `scope.userId`, enabling Postgres RLS enforcement on all 17 user tables.
 * Setting `is_rls_bypassed = 'off'` activates kernel RLS filtering for specific users.
 * When `scope.userId === '*'`, sets `app.bypass_rls = 'on'` for cross-tenant administration.
 */
export async function setTenantScope(client: PoolClient, scope: UserScope): Promise<void> {
  if (isCrossTenant(scope)) {
    await client.query("SET LOCAL app.bypass_rls = 'on'");
    await client.query("SET LOCAL app.current_user_id = '*'");
  } else {
    await client.query("SET LOCAL app.bypass_rls = 'off'");
    await client.query("SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)", [scope.userId]);
  }
}

/**
 * Executes an operation inside a PostgreSQL transaction with active Row-Level Security (RLS).
 *
 * Enforces database-level isolation so that queries cannot read or mutate another tenant's rows,
 * even in the event of an application-level SQL logic error.
 */
export async function withTenantTransaction<T>(
  scope: UserScope,
  operation: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>,
  options: TransactionOptions = {}
): Promise<T> {
  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    await setTenantScope(client, scope);
    return operation(client);
  }, options);
}

/**
 * Runs a single query under tenant Row-Level Security within an isolated transaction.
 */
export async function scopedQuery<T extends QueryResultRow = QueryResultRow>(
  scope: UserScope,
  text: string,
  values?: unknown[]
): Promise<T[]> {
  return withTenantTransaction(scope, async (client) => {
    const result = await client.query<T>(text, values);
    return result.rows;
  });
}

==> packages/db/src/tracking-difference.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { QueryResultRow } from 'pg';
import {
  ADVERSE_SIGN,
  BPS_PER_UNIT,
  InvalidTrackingDifferenceError,
  TRACKING_DIFFERENCE_FEE_BASIS,
  computeTrackingDifference,
  entryLagMs,
  isTradeableSide,
  loadTrackingDifferenceSummary,
  loadTrackingDifferences,
  mapTrackingDifferenceRow,
  resolveMasterPriceUsd,
  resolveUserPriceUsd,
  summarizeTrackingDifferences,
  toTrackingDifferenceRecord
} from './tracking-difference.js';
import type {
  MasterFill,
  TrackingDifference,
  TrackingDifferenceCode,
  TrackingDifferenceDbRow,
  TrackingDifferenceInput,
  TrackingDifferenceQuery,
  UserFill
} from './tracking-difference.js';

// No `vi.hoisted` DATABASE_URL block is needed here, unlike `stop-loss.test.ts`:
// `tracking-difference.ts` never imports `./client.js`, so collecting this file does
// not construct a connection pool. The DB half takes its executor as a parameter.

const MASTER_EVENT_AT = new Date('2026-08-22T12:00:00.000Z');
const USER_FILL_AT = new Date('2026-08-22T12:00:04.250Z');

function master(overrides: Partial<MasterFill> = {}): MasterFill {
  return {
    side: 'buy',
    priceUsd: 0.4,
    amountUsd: 40,
    quantity: 100,
    eventAt: MASTER_EVENT_AT,
    ...overrides
  };
}

function user(overrides: Partial<UserFill> = {}): UserFill {
  return {
    side: 'buy',
    filledQuantity: 100,
    pricedQuantity: 100,
    pricedNotionalUsd: 42,
    firstFillAt: USER_FILL_AT,
    ...overrides
  };
}

function input(
  masterOverrides: Partial<MasterFill> = {},
  userOverrides: Partial<UserFill> = {}
): TrackingDifferenceInput {
  return { master: master(masterOverrides), user: user(userOverrides) };
}

describe('the master price is the master price (S4-M23 orientation)', () => {
  it('treats the source trade as the benchmark and our fill as the thing measured', () => {
    // If these two were ever swapped, this assertion inverts: the user paid 0.42 on
    // a buy where the master paid 0.40, so the user is WORSE, and the sign must say
    // so. `source_trades.price_usd` is the master's (per the comment on
    // `getCanonicalSourceTradeById`); `copy_execution_evidence.price_usd` is ours.
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input());
    expect(result.masterPriceUsd).toBe(0.4);
    expect(result.userPriceUsd).toBeCloseTo(0.42, 12);
    expect(result.worseForUser).toBe(true);
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});

describe('unknown is never zero â€” the core distinction', () => {
  const uncomparable: ReadonlyArray<[Exclude<TrackingDifferenceCode, 'computed'>, TrackingDifference]> = [
    [
      'master-price-unknown',
      // The common case: NULL on robinhood-chain and non-stablecoin Solana routes.
      computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: null }))
    ],
    [
      'user-price-unknown',
      // Our fill landed but no evidence row carried a `price_usd` (Solana and
      // robinhood-chain live paths pass none).
      computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { pricedQuantity: 0, pricedNotionalUsd: 0 }))
    ],
    [
      'both-prices-unknown',
      computeTrackingDifference(
        input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: null }, { pricedQuantity: 0, pricedNotionalUsd: 0 })
      )
    ],
    [
      'no-user-fill',
      computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { filledQuantity: 0, pricedQuantity: 0, pricedNotionalUsd: 0 }))
    ],
    ['side-mismatch', computeTrackingDifference(input({ side: 'sell' }, { side: 'buy' }))],
    ['master-side-not-tradeable', computeTrackingDifference(input({ side: 'transfer_in' }))],
    [
      'master-price-not-positive',
      computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0, amountUsd: 0, quantity: 100 }))
    ],
    ['user-price-not-positive', computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { pricedNotionalUsd: 0 }))]
  ];

  it('produces the expected code for each uncomparable situation', () => {
    for (const [code, result] of uncomparable) {
      expect(result.code).toBe(code);
    }
  });

  it.each(uncomparable)(
    'reports %s as null, never as a zero difference',
    (_code, result) => {
      // Reporting an unmeasured gap as 0 would tell the user they matched the
      // master's price when nothing was compared. `null` is the only honest answer,
      // and `toBeNull` plus `not.toBe(0)` states both halves.
      expect(result.adverseBps).toBeNull();
      expect(result.adverseBps).not.toBe(0);
      expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeNull();
      expect(result.adverseUsd).not.toBe(0);
      expect(result.worseForUser).toBeNull();
      expect(result.worseForUser).not.toBe(false);
      expect(result.adverseUsdPartial).toBe(false);
      expect(result.comparable).toBe(false);
      expect(result.explanation).toContain('Not compared');
    }
  );

  it('reserves a zero difference for two prices that were actually compared', () => {
    const matched = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 40 }));
    expect(matched.code).toBe('computed');
    expect(matched.comparable).toBe(true);
    expect(matched.adverseBps).toBe(0);
    expect(matched.adverseUsd).toBe(0);
    expect(matched.worseForUser).toBe(false);
    expect(matched.explanation).toContain('Matched');
  });

  it('keeps `comparable` in lockstep with the code, for every code', () => {
    for (const [, result] of uncomparable) expect(result.comparable).toBe(false);
    expect(computeTrackingDifference(input()).comparable).toBe(true);
  });

  it('still reports the entry lag when the difference itself is unknown', () => {
    // On the chains with no price, the lag is often the only honest number we have.
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: null }));
    expect(result.code).toBe('master-price-unknown');
    expect(result.entryLagMs).toBe(4250);
  });
});

describe('worse for the user is one sign on both sides', () => {
  it('calls paying above the master worse on a buy', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 42 }));
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(500, 9);
    expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(2, 9);
    expect(result.worseForUser).toBe(true);
  });

  it('calls receiving below the master worse on a sell, by the same number', () => {
    // The whole point of `ADVERSE_SIGN`: the same 2-cent adverse move gives the same
    // +500 bps and the same +$2 on a sell as on a buy. A raw signed
    // `userPrice - masterPrice` would be -0.02 here and +0.02 above, and a UI
    // colouring on the raw sign would render one of the two backwards.
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(
      input({ side: 'sell', priceUsd: 0.4 }, { side: 'sell', pricedNotionalUsd: 38 })
    );
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(500, 9);
    expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(2, 9);
    expect(result.worseForUser).toBe(true);
  });

  it('calls paying below the master better on a buy', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 38 }));
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(-500, 9);
    expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(-2, 9);
    expect(result.worseForUser).toBe(false);
    expect(result.explanation).toContain('in your favour');
  });

  it('calls receiving above the master better on a sell, by the same number', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(
      input({ side: 'sell', priceUsd: 0.4 }, { side: 'sell', pricedNotionalUsd: 42 })
    );
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(-500, 9);
    expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(-2, 9);
    expect(result.worseForUser).toBe(false);
  });

  it('exposes the sign map as +1 buy / -1 sell and nothing else', () => {
    expect(ADVERSE_SIGN).toEqual({ buy: 1, sell: -1 });
    expect(Object.isFrozen(ADVERSE_SIGN)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('never admits a transfer into the sign map', () => {
    expect(isTradeableSide('buy')).toBe(true);
    expect(isTradeableSide('sell')).toBe(true);
    expect(isTradeableSide('transfer_in')).toBe(false);
    expect(isTradeableSide('transfer_out')).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('basis points and dollars answer different questions', () => {
  it('makes a 2-cent gap on a cheap outcome and an expensive token comparable in bps', () => {
    // 2 cents on a $0.40 Polymarket outcome is 500 bps; the same 2 cents on a
    // $4,000 token is 0.05 bps. The bps figure is what makes those the same kind of
    // number, which is why bps is reported and not only dollars.
    const polymarket = computeTrackingDifference(
      input({ priceUsd: 0.4, amountUsd: null, quantity: null }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 42 })
    );
    const token = computeTrackingDifference(
      input(
        { priceUsd: 4_000, amountUsd: null, quantity: null },
        { filledQuantity: 1, pricedQuantity: 1, pricedNotionalUsd: 4_000.02 }
      )
    );
    expect(polymarket.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(500, 6);
    expect(token.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo(0.05, 6);

    // And the dollars are what makes them differently important: $2 lost against
    // 2 cents. Neither number alone tells the user both things.
    expect(polymarket.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(2, 9);
    expect(token.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(0.02, 9);
  });

  it('uses the master price as the ratio denominator', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 50 }));
    // (0.50 - 0.40) / 0.40, not / 0.50 and not / 0.45.
    expect(result.adverseBps).toBeCloseTo((0.1 / 0.4) * BPS_PER_UNIT, 6);
  });

  it('scales the dollar figure by the priced quantity, not by the whole fill', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(
      input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { filledQuantity: 100, pricedQuantity: 60, pricedNotionalUsd: 25.2 })
    );
    expect(result.userPriceUsd).toBeCloseTo(0.42, 12);
    expect(result.pricedQuantityFraction).toBeCloseTo(0.6, 12);
    expect(result.adverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(1.2, 9);
    expect(result.adverseUsdPartial).toBe(true);
    expect(result.explanation).toContain('priced part of the fill');
  });

  it('does not flag a fully priced fill as partial', () => {
    const result = computeTrackingDifference(input());
    expect(result.pricedQuantityFraction).toBe(1);
    expect(result.adverseUsdPartial).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('fees are excluded and the result says so', () => {
  it('stamps the fee basis on every result, comparable or not', () => {
    expect(computeTrackingDifference(input()).feeBasis).toBe(TRACKING_DIFFERENCE_FEE_BASIS);
    expect(computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: null })).feeBasis)
      .toBe(TRACKING_DIFFERENCE_FEE_BASIS);
    expect(TRACKING_DIFFERENCE_FEE_BASIS).toBe('gross-excludes-fees');
  });

  it('says gross of fees in the computed explanation', () => {
    expect(computeTrackingDifference(input()).explanation).toContain('Gross of fees');
  });
});

describe('resolveMasterPriceUsd', () => {
  it('prefers source_trades.price_usd and names that basis', () => {
    expect(resolveMasterPriceUsd(master())).toEqual({ priceUsd: 0.4, basis: 'source-price-usd' });
  });

  it('falls back to amount_usd / token_amount when the price column is null', () => {
    const resolved = resolveMasterPriceUsd(master({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: 45, quantity: 100 }));
    expect(resolved.basis).toBe('source-amount-over-quantity');
    expect(resolved.priceUsd).toBeCloseTo(0.45, 12);
    expect(computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: 45, quantity: 100 })).masterPriceBasis)
      .toBe('source-amount-over-quantity');
  });

  it('reports no basis when neither column pair yields a price', () => {
    expect(resolveMasterPriceUsd(master({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: 100 })))
      .toEqual({ priceUsd: null, basis: 'unavailable' });
    expect(resolveMasterPriceUsd(master({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: 40, quantity: 0 })))
      .toEqual({ priceUsd: null, basis: 'unavailable' });
    expect(resolveMasterPriceUsd(master({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: 0, quantity: 100 })))
      .toEqual({ priceUsd: null, basis: 'unavailable' });
  });
});

describe('resolveUserPriceUsd', () => {
  it('is the quantity-weighted average over the priced part', () => {
    expect(resolveUserPriceUsd(user({ pricedQuantity: 60, pricedNotionalUsd: 25.2 })))
      .toBeCloseTo(0.42, 12);
  });

  it('is null, not zero, when nothing was priced', () => {
    const price = resolveUserPriceUsd(user({ pricedQuantity: 0, pricedNotionalUsd: 0 }));
    expect(price).toBeNull();
    expect(price).not.toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('entryLagMs', () => {
  it('measures our first fill against the master event', () => {
    expect(entryLagMs(MASTER_EVENT_AT, USER_FILL_AT)).toBe(4250);
  });

  it('is null when either instant is unknown', () => {
    expect(entryLagMs(null, USER_FILL_AT)).toBeNull();
    expect(entryLagMs(MASTER_EVENT_AT, null)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('passes a negative lag through rather than clamping a clock defect to zero', () => {
    expect(entryLagMs(USER_FILL_AT, MASTER_EVENT_AT)).toBe(-4250);
  });
});

describe('incoherent input fails loud rather than becoming unknown', () => {
  it('rejects a non-finite or negative price', () => {
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: Number.NaN })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: -0.4 })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
  });

  it('rejects a negative or non-finite quantity', () => {
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { filledQuantity: -1 })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { pricedQuantity: Number.NaN })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
  });

  it('rejects a priced quantity larger than the fill it is part of', () => {
    expect(() => computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { filledQuantity: 10, pricedQuantity: 11 })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
  });
});

describe('summarizeTrackingDifferences keeps the uncompared visible', () => {
  const worse = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 42 }));
  const worseHarder = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 76 }));
  const better = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 38 }));
  const matched = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { pricedNotionalUsd: 40 }));
  const masterUnknown = computeTrackingDifference(input({ priceUsd: null, amountUsd: null, quantity: null }));
  const userUnknown = computeTrackingDifference(input({}, { pricedQuantity: 0, pricedNotionalUsd: 0 }));

  it('returns nulls, not zeros, for an empty set', () => {
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([]);
    expect(summary).toMatchObject({
      total: 0,
      comparedCount: 0,
      uncomparedCount: 0,
      matchedCount: 0,
      medianAdverseBps: null,
      meanAdverseBps: null,
      totalAdverseUsd: null
    });
    expect(summary.medianAdverseBps).not.toBe(0);
    expect(summary.totalAdverseUsd).not.toBe(0);
  });

  it('returns nulls when nothing in a non-empty set could be compared', () => {
    // The robinhood-chain reality: rows exist, none of them is a number. A zero
    // median here would read as "you track the master perfectly".
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([masterUnknown, masterUnknown, userUnknown]);
    expect(summary.total).toBe(3);
    expect(summary.comparedCount).toBe(0);
    expect(summary.uncomparedCount).toBe(3);
    expect(summary.medianAdverseBps).toBeNull();
    expect(summary.meanAdverseBps).toBeNull();
    expect(summary.totalAdverseUsd).toBeNull();
    expect(summary.uncomparedByCode).toEqual({
      'master-price-unknown': 2,
      'user-price-unknown': 1
    });
  });

  it('attributes every refusal to a code so an empty comparison is explainable', () => {
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([worse, masterUnknown, userUnknown]);
    expect(summary.comparedCount).toBe(1);
    expect(summary.uncomparedCount).toBe(2);
    expect(Object.values(summary.uncomparedByCode).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0))
      .toBe(summary.uncomparedCount);
  });

  it('counts a genuine match separately from a refusal to compare', () => {
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([matched, masterUnknown]);
    expect(summary.matchedCount).toBe(1);
    expect(summary.worseForUserCount).toBe(0);
    expect(summary.betterForUserCount).toBe(0);
    expect(summary.uncomparedCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('reports median and mean, which disagree on a skewed set', () => {
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([better, worse, worseHarder]);
    // bps are -500, +500, +9000: the median is the typical experience, the mean is
    // dragged by the one bad fill.
    expect(summary.medianAdverseBps).toBeCloseTo(500, 6);
    expect(summary.meanAdverseBps).toBeCloseTo(3_000, 6);
    expect(summary.worseForUserCount).toBe(2);
    expect(summary.betterForUserCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('sums the dollar figures and says how much of the set they cover', () => {
    const partial = computeTrackingDifference(
      input({ priceUsd: 0.4 }, { filledQuantity: 100, pricedQuantity: 60, pricedNotionalUsd: 25.2 })
    );
    const summary = summarizeTrackingDifferences([worse, partial, masterUnknown]);
    expect(summary.totalAdverseUsd).toBeCloseTo(3.2, 9);
    expect(summary.adverseUsdPartialCount).toBe(1);
    expect(summary.adverseUsdMissingCount).toBe(0);
    expect(summary.uncomparedCount).toBe(1);
    expect(summary.feeBasis).toBe(TRACKING_DIFFERENCE_FEE_BASIS);
  });
});

function dbRow(overrides: Partial<TrackingDifferenceDbRow> = {}): TrackingDifferenceDbRow {
  return {
    execution_id: 'execution-1',
    signal_id: 'signal-1',
    source_trade_id: 'source-1',
    chain: 'polygon',
    target_account: 'operator',
    user_id: null,
    token_mint: 'polygon:0xabc',
    execution_mode: 'live',
    state: 'confirmed',
    user_side: 'buy',
    master_side: 'buy',
    master_price_usd: '0.40000000',
    master_amount_usd: '40.00',
    master_quantity: '100',
    master_event_at: MASTER_EVENT_AT,
    user_filled_quantity: '100',
    user_priced_quantity: '100',
    user_priced_notional_usd: '42.00',
    user_first_fill_at: USER_FILL_AT,
    ...overrides
  };
}

function stubExecutor(rows: TrackingDifferenceDbRow[]): {
  execute: TrackingDifferenceQuery;
  calls: Array<{ sql: string; params: unknown[] }>;
} {
  const calls: Array<{ sql: string; params: unknown[] }> = [];
  const execute = (async <R extends QueryResultRow>(
    sql: string,
    params?: unknown[]
  ): Promise<R[]> => {
    calls.push({ sql, params: params ?? [] });
    return rows as unknown as R[];
  }) as TrackingDifferenceQuery;
  return { execute, calls };
}

describe('mapTrackingDifferenceRow', () => {
  it('parses NUMERIC-as-text into the pure input', () => {
    const mapped = mapTrackingDifferenceRow(dbRow());
    expect(mapped.master.priceUsd).toBeCloseTo(0.4, 12);
    expect(mapped.master.amountUsd).toBe(40);
    expect(mapped.master.quantity).toBe(100);
    expect(mapped.user.filledQuantity).toBe(100);
    expect(mapped.user.pricedNotionalUsd).toBe(42);
    expect(mapped.master.eventAt).toBe(MASTER_EVENT_AT);
    expect(mapped.user.firstFillAt).toBe(USER_FILL_AT);
  });

  it('keeps a NULL price as null rather than parsing it to zero', () => {
    const mapped = mapTrackingDifferenceRow(dbRow({ master_price_usd: null, master_amount_usd: null }));
    expect(mapped.master.priceUsd).toBeNull();
    expect(mapped.master.amountUsd).toBeNull();
  });

  it('throws on unparseable numeric text instead of calling it unknown', () => {
    expect(() => mapTrackingDifferenceRow(dbRow({ master_price_usd: 'NaN' })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
    expect(() => mapTrackingDifferenceRow(dbRow({ user_filled_quantity: 'oops' })))
      .toThrow(InvalidTrackingDifferenceError);
  });

  it('throws when our own execution direction violates the migration-028 CHECK', () => {
    expect(() => mapTrackingDifferenceRow(dbRow({ user_side: 'transfer_in' })))
      .toThrow(/copy_executions.direction must be buy or sell/);
  });

  it('accepts a transfer on the master side, which the schema does allow', () => {
    const record = toTrackingDifferenceRecord(dbRow({ master_side: 'transfer_out' }));
    expect(record.difference.code).toBe('master-side-not-tradeable');
    expect(record.difference.adverseBps).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('toTrackingDifferenceRecord', () => {

    expect(record).toMatchObject({

  });
