==> packages/shared/src/address.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';
import { isValidAddressForChain } from './validation.js';

const CHAINS: readonly Chain[] = ['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'base', 'ethereum', 'bsc'];
const EVM_ADDRESS = /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/;

export type ResolvedChainValue = {
  chain: Chain;
  raw: string;
  prefixed: string;
};

export function isChain(value: unknown): value is Chain {
  return typeof value === 'string' && CHAINS.includes(value as Chain);
}

export function getChainPrefix(value: string): Chain | null {
  for (const chain of CHAINS) {
    if (value.startsWith(`${chain}:`)) return chain;
  }
  return null;
}

export function normalizeChainValue(value: string, chain: Chain): string {
  if (!value || value.trim() !== value) {
    throw new Error('Chain value must be non-empty and contain no surrounding whitespace');
  }
  if (value.includes(':')) {
    throw new Error(`Nested or unsupported chain prefix in ${value}`);
  }
  return chain === 'solana' ? value : value.toLowerCase();
}

export function resolveChainValue(value: string, requestedChain?: Chain): ResolvedChainValue {
  if (!value || value.trim() !== value) {
    throw new Error('Chain value must be non-empty and contain no surrounding whitespace');
  }

  const existingChain = getChainPrefix(value);
  let chain: Chain;
  let raw: string;

  if (existingChain) {
    if (requestedChain && requestedChain !== existingChain) {
      throw new Error(
        `Chain prefix ${existingChain} does not match requested chain ${requestedChain}`
      );
    }
    chain = existingChain;
    raw = value.slice(existingChain.length + 1);
  } else {
    if (value.includes(':')) {
      throw new Error(`Unsupported chain prefix in ${value}`);
    }
    if (!requestedChain && EVM_ADDRESS.test(value)) {
      throw new Error('Raw EVM values require an explicit chain');
    }
    chain = requestedChain ?? 'solana';
    raw = value;
  }

  const normalized = normalizeChainValue(raw, chain);
  if (chain === 'solana' && EVM_ADDRESS.test(normalized)) {
    throw new Error('EVM-shaped values cannot be classified as Solana');
  }
  return {
    chain,
    raw: normalized,
    prefixed: `${chain}:${normalized}`
  };
}

export function resolveChainAddress(value: string, requestedChain?: Chain): ResolvedChainValue {
  const resolved = resolveChainValue(value, requestedChain);
  if (!isValidAddressForChain(resolved.raw, resolved.chain)) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid ${resolved.chain} address`);
  }
  return resolved;
}

export function prefixChainValue(value: string, chain: Chain): string {
  return resolveChainValue(value, chain).prefixed;
}

export function stripChainPrefix(value: string): string {
  const chain = getChainPrefix(value);
  if (chain) return resolveChainValue(value, chain).raw;
  if (EVM_ADDRESS.test(value)) return value.toLowerCase();
  return value;
}

==> packages/shared/src/authority/entrypoint.ts <==
/**
 * Pinned EntryPoint configuration for ERC-4337 on Robinhood Chain (S4-P11).
 *
 * Robinhood Chain (chain ID 4663) has three deployed EntryPoint versions:
 * - v0.6.0: 0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789
 * - v0.7.0: 0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032
 * - v0.8.0: 0x4337084D9E255Ff0702461CF8895CE9E3b5Ff108
 *
 * Paymaster interfaces, UserOperation packing, and gas accounting differ across
 * versions. An implicit or unpinned default creates silent-mismatch defects at
 * bundle submission. We pin v0.7.0 and assert it at runtime.
 */

export const ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ENTRYPOINTS = {
  v0_6: '0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789',
  v0_7: '0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032',
  v0_8: '0x4337084D9E255Ff0702461CF8895CE9E3b5Ff108'
} as const;

export type EntryPointVersion = keyof typeof ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ENTRYPOINTS;

export const PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_VERSION: EntryPointVersion = 'v0_7';
export const PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_ADDRESS = ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ENTRYPOINTS[PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_VERSION];

/**
 * Validates that an EntryPoint address matches the pinned v0.7.0 address.
 * Throws a descriptive error on mismatch.
 */
export function assertPinnedEntryPoint(address?: string): string {
  const target = address ?? process.env.ENTRYPOINT_ADDRESS ?? PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_ADDRESS;
  if (target.toLowerCase() !== PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_ADDRESS.toLowerCase()) {
    throw new Error(
      `[authority] Invalid EntryPoint address: expected ${PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_ADDRESS} (${PINNED_ENTRYPOINT_VERSION}), got ${target}`
    );
  }
  return target;
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  EnvMasterKeyWrapper,
  NullWrapper,
  type WrapContext
} from './key-wrapper.js';
import {
  sealSecret,
  openSealedSecret,
  EnvelopeAuthenticationError,
  EnvelopeEncryptionError
} from './envelope.js';

describe('Envelope Encryption and KeyWrapper (S4-3, S4-4)', () => {
  const masterKey = randomBytes(32);
  const wrapper = new EnvMasterKeyWrapper({ masterKey, version: 1 });
  const context: WrapContext = {
    userId: 'user-uuid-1234',
    chainKind: 'evm',
    keyVersion: 1
  };

  it('seals and opens secrets round-trip', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('my-super-secret-session-key', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);

    expect(envelope).toMatch(/^v1\.env:v1\.[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+\.[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+\.[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+\.[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/);

    const opened = await openSealedSecret(envelope, context, wrapper);
    expect(opened.toString('utf8')).toBe('my-super-secret-session-key');
  });

  it('binds envelope to user context (AAD): swapping userId fails authentication', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('user-a-secret', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);

    const attackerContext: WrapContext = {
      userId: 'attacker-uuid-9999',
      chainKind: 'evm',
      keyVersion: 1
    };

    await expect(openSealedSecret(envelope, attackerContext, wrapper)).rejects.toThrow(
      EnvelopeAuthenticationError
    );
  });

  it('binds envelope to chainKind (AAD): swapping evm to solana fails authentication', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('chain-bound-secret', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);

    const wrongChainContext: WrapContext = {
      ...context,
      chainKind: 'solana'
    };

    await expect(openSealedSecret(envelope, wrongChainContext, wrapper)).rejects.toThrow(
      EnvelopeAuthenticationError
    );
  });

  it('binds envelope to keyVersion (AAD): swapping version fails authentication', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('version-bound-secret', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);

    const wrongVersionContext: WrapContext = {
      ...context,
      keyVersion: 2
    };

    await expect(openSealedSecret(envelope, wrongVersionContext, wrapper)).rejects.toThrow(
      EnvelopeAuthenticationError
    );
  });

  it('detects tampered ciphertext', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('tamper-test-secret', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);
    const parts = envelope.split('.');
    // Tamper with the ciphertext component (last part)
    const ctBuffer = Buffer.from(parts[5], 'base64');
    ctBuffer[0] ^= 0xff;
    parts[5] = ctBuffer.toString('base64');
    const tampered = parts.join('.');

    await expect(openSealedSecret(tampered, context, wrapper)).rejects.toThrow(
      EnvelopeAuthenticationError
    );
  });

  it('detects wrapper id mismatch', async () => {
    const secret = Buffer.from('wrapper-mismatch-secret', 'utf8');
    const envelope = await sealSecret(secret, context, wrapper);

    const wrapperV2 = new EnvMasterKeyWrapper({ masterKey, version: 2 });
    await expect(openSealedSecret(envelope, context, wrapperV2)).rejects.toThrow(
      /envelope wrapper mismatch: expected env:v2, got env:v1/
    );

    const nullWrapper = new NullWrapper();
    expect(nullWrapper.id).toBe('null:v1');

    await expect(
      nullWrapper.wrap(randomBytes(32), context)
    ).rejects.toThrow(/NullWrapper refuses to wrap/);

    await expect(
      nullWrapper.unwrap(randomBytes(60), context)
    ).rejects.toThrow(/NullWrapper refuses to unwrap/);
  });

  it('refuses master key of invalid length', () => {
    expect(() => new EnvMasterKeyWrapper({ masterKey: randomBytes(16) })).toThrow(
      /must be exactly 32 bytes/
    );
    expect(() => new EnvMasterKeyWrapper({ masterKey: randomBytes(64) })).toThrow(
      /must be exactly 32 bytes/
    );
  });

  it('refuses to seal an empty secret', async () => {
    await expect(sealSecret(Buffer.alloc(0), context, wrapper)).rejects.toThrow(
      EnvelopeEncryptionError
    );
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/authority/envelope.ts <==
import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
import { type KeyWrapper, type WrapContext, buildWrapAad } from './key-wrapper.js';

export class EnvelopeEncryptionError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'EnvelopeEncryptionError';
  }
}

export class EnvelopeAuthenticationError extends EnvelopeEncryptionError {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'EnvelopeAuthenticationError';
  }
}

/**
 * Seals a plaintext secret under envelope encryption (`S4-3`, ADR-0003 Â§5).
 *
 * 1. Generates a fresh 32-byte AES-256-GCM data key.
 * 2. Encrypts the secret with the data key, a fresh 12-byte IV, and AAD bound to the user/chain/version.
 * 3. Wraps the data key using the provided KeyWrapper.
 * 4. Assembles the self-describing versioned envelope:
 *    `v1.<wrapperId>.<b64(wrappedDataKey)>.<b64(iv)>.<b64(authTag)>.<b64(ciphertext)>`
 */
export async function sealSecret(
  plaintext: Buffer | string,
  context: WrapContext,
  wrapper: KeyWrapper
): Promise<string> {
  const secretBytes = Buffer.isBuffer(plaintext) ? plaintext : Buffer.from(plaintext, 'utf8');
  if (secretBytes.length === 0) {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError('cannot seal an empty secret');
  }

  // 1. Fresh 32-byte data key
  const dataKey = randomBytes(32);

  // 2. Encrypt secret under dataKey
  const iv = randomBytes(12);
  const cipher = createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', dataKey, iv);
  cipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));

  const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(secretBytes), cipher.final()]);
  const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag();

  // 3. Wrap data key
  const wrappedDataKey = await wrapper.wrap(dataKey, context);

  // 4. Assemble envelope
  return [
    'v1',
    wrapper.id,
    wrappedDataKey.toString('base64'),
    iv.toString('base64'),
    authTag.toString('base64'),
    ciphertext.toString('base64')
  ].join('.');
}

/**
 * Opens a sealed secret envelope (`S4-3`, ADR-0003 Â§5).
 *
 * Validates the envelope format, checks wrapper ID, unwraps the data key with
 * the wrapper, and decrypts the ciphertext with GCM authentication.
 * If the ciphertext or context has been tampered with or swapped, throws an
 * EnvelopeAuthenticationError.
 */
export async function openSealedSecret(
  envelope: string,
  context: WrapContext,
  wrapper: KeyWrapper
): Promise<Buffer> {
  if (typeof envelope !== 'string') {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError('envelope must be a string');
  }

  const parts = envelope.split('.');
  if (parts.length !== 6) {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError(
      `invalid envelope format: expected 6 dot-separated components, got ${parts.length}`
    );
  }

  const [version, wrapperId, b64WrappedDataKey, b64Iv, b64AuthTag, b64Ciphertext] = parts;

  if (version !== 'v1') {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError(`unsupported envelope version: ${version}`);
  }

  if (wrapperId !== wrapper.id) {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError(
      `envelope wrapper mismatch: expected ${wrapper.id}, got ${wrapperId}`
    );
  }

  const wrappedDataKey = Buffer.from(b64WrappedDataKey, 'base64');
  const iv = Buffer.from(b64Iv, 'base64');
  const authTag = Buffer.from(b64AuthTag, 'base64');
  const ciphertext = Buffer.from(b64Ciphertext, 'base64');

  if (iv.length !== 12) {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError(`invalid IV length: expected 12 bytes, got ${iv.length}`);
  }
  if (authTag.length !== 16) {
    throw new EnvelopeEncryptionError(
      `invalid auth tag length: expected 16 bytes, got ${authTag.length}`
    );
  }

  // 1. Unwrap data key
  let dataKey: Buffer;
  try {
    dataKey = await wrapper.unwrap(wrappedDataKey, context);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new EnvelopeAuthenticationError(
      `data key unwrap failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`
    );
  }

  // 2. Decrypt secret
  try {
    const decipher = createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', dataKey, iv);
    decipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));
    decipher.setAuthTag(authTag);

    const plaintext = Buffer.concat([decipher.update(ciphertext), decipher.final()]);
    return plaintext;
  } catch (error) {
    throw new EnvelopeAuthenticationError(
      'secret decryption failed: ciphertext tampered or AAD mismatch (user/chain/version mismatch)'
    );
  }
}

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  ACCOUNT_EXECUTE,
  ERC20_APPROVE,
  ERC20_TRANSFER,
  decodeEvmCalldata,
  describeUserOperationCall,
  type EvmFunctionDescriptor
} from './evm-calldata.js';

const DESCRIPTORS: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[] = [
  ERC20_APPROVE,
  ERC20_TRANSFER,
  ACCOUNT_EXECUTE
];

const TOKEN = '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111';
const ACCOUNT = '0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555';

function addressWord(address: string): string {
  return address.replace(/^0x/, '').toLowerCase().padStart(64, '0');
}

function uintWord(value: bigint): string {
  return value.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');
}

function encodeApprove(spender: string, amount: bigint): string {
  return `${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(spender)}${uintWord(amount)}`;
}

function encodeExecute(dest: string, value: bigint, inner: string): string {
  const body = inner.replace(/^0x/, '');
  const byteLength = body.length / 2;
  const padded = body.padEnd(Math.ceil(byteLength / 32) * 64, '0');
  return `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(dest)}${uintWord(value)}${uintWord(96n)}${uintWord(
    BigInt(byteLength)
  )}${padded}`;
}

describe('decodeEvmCalldata (S4-P10)', () => {
  it('decodes a hand-written approve calldata literal', () => {
    // Written out by hand rather than produced by the helper above, so this test
    // is not just asserting that the encoder and decoder are inverses.
    const calldata =
      '0x095ea7b3' +
      '000000000000000000000000' +
      '1111111111111111111111111111111111111111' +
      '00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000003e8';

    const decoded = decodeEvmCalldata(calldata, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(decoded.kind).toBe('decoded');
    if (decoded.kind !== 'decoded') return;
    expect(decoded.functionName).toBe('approve');
    expect(decoded.selector).toBe('0x095ea7b3');
    expect(decoded.args.spender).toBe(TOKEN);
    expect(decoded.args.amount).toBe(1000n);
  });

  it('refuses an unknown selector under its own code rather than guessing', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(`0xdeadbeef${uintWord(1n)}`, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-unknown-selector' });
  });

  it('refuses calldata shorter than its declared head', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(`${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(TOKEN)}`, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

    const dirty = `ff${'0'.repeat(22)}${TOKEN.slice(2)}`;
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(

      DESCRIPTORS

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

    const forged = `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(TOKEN)}${uintWord(0n)}${uintWord(
      128n
    )}${uintWord(0n)}${uintWord(4n)}`;
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(forged, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

  it('refuses hex that is not whole bytes', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata('0x095ea7b', DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/authority/evm-calldata.ts <==
/**
 * Minimal EVM calldata decoding for the permission policy engine (`S4-P10`).
 *
 * **Moves to `packages/authority` with the rest of this directory** (checklist
 * Â§7.1).
 *
 * ## Why this exists rather than `viem`
 *
 * `viem@^2.55.1` is a dependency of `apps/api`, `apps/indexer`,
 * `apps/signal-engine` and `apps/trade-executor` â€” but **not** of
 * `packages/shared`, and pnpm's isolated `node_modules` means it is not
 * resolvable from here. Adding it would need a `pnpm install`. So the decoder
 * here is deliberately the *smallest correct* thing rather than a general ABI
 * decoder:
 *
 *   * argument types are `address`, `uint256`, `bool` (one static word each) and
 *     `bytes` (allowed **only** as the final argument, one dynamic tail);
 *   * anything else â€” arrays, structs, multiple dynamic arguments, `executeBatch`
 *     â€” has no descriptor and is refused, not partially decoded.
 *
 * That covers exactly what Â§2.1 needs to check: `approve(address,uint256)` on a
 * token, and the 4337 `execute(address,uint256,bytes)` wrapper it arrives inside.
 * Callers that already have `viem` (the trade executor) should decode richer
 * shapes there and hand `evaluateAuthorityAction` an `AuthorityContractCall`
 * directly â€” the engine does not require this module.
 *
 * ## Strictness is the feature
 *
 * Dirty high-order bits in an `address` word and non-0/1 `bool` words are
 * rejected rather than masked. A decoder that silently truncates disagrees with
 * whatever the EVM will actually do, and a policy that checks a value the chain
 * will not use is decoration.
 *
 * ## Selectors are constants, not computed
 *
 * There is no keccak256 in `packages/shared`, so selectors cannot be derived from
 * signatures here â€” they are written out as the published values below. A
 * consumer that has `viem` should assert them at startup with
 * `toFunctionSelector` rather than trust this file; the constants are marked so
 * that assertion is greppable.
 */

import type { AuthorityContractCall, AuthorityFieldValue } from './permission-policy.js';

export type EvmArgType = 'address' | 'uint256' | 'bool' | 'bytes';

export interface EvmArgDescriptor {
  /** The name a policy condition reaches this argument by. */
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: EvmArgType;
}

export interface EvmFunctionDescriptor {
  readonly name: string;
  /** `0x` + 8 hex. */
  readonly selector: string;
  readonly args: readonly EvmArgDescriptor[];
}

export type EvmDecodeFailureCode =
  /** No descriptor for this 4-byte selector. We cannot say what the call does. */
  | 'authority-action-unknown-selector'
  /** A descriptor matched but the bytes do not decode against it. */
  | 'authority-action-undecodable'
  /** `execute(dest, value, "")`. A definite refusal, not an integration fault. */
  | 'authority-deny-bare-value-transfer';

export interface EvmDecodeFailure {
  readonly kind: 'failed';
  readonly code: EvmDecodeFailureCode;
  readonly reason: string;
}

export interface EvmDecodedCall {
  readonly kind: 'decoded';
  readonly selector: string;
  readonly functionName: string;
  readonly args: Readonly<Record<string, AuthorityFieldValue>>;
}

/**
 * `approve(address,uint256)` â€” published selector. *Not computed here* (no
 * keccak in this package); assert with `viem`'s `toFunctionSelector` in a
 * consumer that has it.
 */
export const ERC20_APPROVE: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'approve',
  selector: '0x095ea7b3',
  args: [
    { name: 'spender', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
};

/** `transfer(address,uint256)` â€” published selector, same caveat. */
export const ERC20_TRANSFER: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'transfer',
  selector: '0xa9059cbb',
  args: [
    { name: 'to', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
};

/**
 * `execute(address,uint256,bytes)` â€” the ERC-4337 account wrapper a
 * UserOperation's `callData` normally is. Published selector, same caveat.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_EXECUTE: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'execute',
  selector: '0xb61d27f6',
  args: [
    { name: 'dest', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'value', type: 'uint256' },
    { name: 'func', type: 'bytes' }
  ]
};

/**
 * Selectors treated as an account-level execute wrapper, to be unwrapped to the
 * inner call before the policy sees it.
 *
 * Batch wrappers are absent on purpose. They are not listed as unsupported â€”
 * they are simply not decodable here, so they land on
 * `authority-action-unknown-selector`, which is the honest answer: an
 * `executeBatch` is an arbitrary `(target, value, data)` list and we cannot say
 * what it does without array-index paths, which `DG-3` records as unavailable.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_EXECUTE_SELECTORS: readonly string[] = [ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector];

const WORD_HEX = 64;

function failed(code: EvmDecodeFailureCode, reason: string): EvmDecodeFailure {
  return { kind: 'failed', code, reason };
}

/** Strips `0x`, lowercases, and rejects anything that is not whole bytes of hex. */
function normalizeHex(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return null;
  const body = value.startsWith('0x') || value.startsWith('0X') ? value.slice(2) : value;
  if (body.length % 2 !== 0) return null;
  if (body.length > 0 && !/^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/.test(body)) return null;
  return body.toLowerCase();
}

function readWord(body: string, wordIndex: number): string | null {
  const start = wordIndex * WORD_HEX;
  if (start + WORD_HEX > body.length) return null;
  return body.slice(start, start + WORD_HEX);
}

function validateDescriptor(descriptor: EvmFunctionDescriptor): string | null {
  for (let i = 0; i < descriptor.args.length; i += 1) {
    const arg = descriptor.args[i]!;
    if (arg.type === 'bytes' && i !== descriptor.args.length - 1) {
      return `descriptor ${descriptor.name} declares a bytes argument that is not last; this decoder supports one dynamic tail only`;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Decodes one call against a descriptor table.
 *
 * The descriptor table *is* the allowlist of shapes we are willing to reason
 * about â€” an unlisted selector is refused rather than guessed at, which is the
 * same allowlist discipline the policy itself uses.
 */
export function decodeEvmCalldata(
  calldata: string,
  descriptors: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[]
): EvmDecodedCall | EvmDecodeFailure {
  const body = normalizeHex(calldata);
  if (body === null) {
    return failed('authority-action-undecodable', 'calldata is not an even-length hex string');
  }
  if (body.length < 8) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      `calldata is ${body.length / 2} bytes, too short to carry a 4-byte selector`
    );
  }

  const selector = `0x${body.slice(0, 8)}`;
  const descriptor = descriptors.find((d) => d.selector.toLowerCase() === selector);
  if (descriptor === undefined) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-unknown-selector',
      `no descriptor for selector ${selector}; this engine will not authorise a call it cannot decode`
    );
  }

  const descriptorProblem = validateDescriptor(descriptor);
  if (descriptorProblem !== null) {
    return failed('authority-action-undecodable', descriptorProblem);
  }

  const argsBody = body.slice(8);
  const headWords = descriptor.args.length;
  if (argsBody.length < headWords * WORD_HEX) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      `call to ${descriptor.name} carries ${argsBody.length / 2} argument bytes, fewer than the ${headWords * 32} its head requires`
    );
  }

  const args: Record<string, AuthorityFieldValue> = {};

  for (let i = 0; i < descriptor.args.length; i += 1) {
    const arg = descriptor.args[i]!;
    const word = readWord(argsBody, i);
    if (word === null) {
      return failed('authority-action-undecodable', `argument ${arg.name} is truncated`);
    }

    if (arg.type === 'address') {
      // Reject dirty high-order bits rather than masking them: masking makes the
      // policy check a value the EVM will not necessarily use.
      if (word.slice(0, 24) !== '0'.repeat(24)) {
        return failed(
          'authority-action-undecodable',
          `argument ${arg.name} is not a clean address word (non-zero high-order bytes)`
        );
      }
      args[arg.name] = `0x${word.slice(24)}`;
      continue;
    }

    if (arg.type === 'uint256') {
      args[arg.name] = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
      continue;
    }

    if (arg.type === 'bool') {
      const asInt = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
      if (asInt !== 0n && asInt !== 1n) {
        return failed(
          'authority-action-undecodable',
          `argument ${arg.name} is not a canonical bool word (${asInt})`
        );
      }
      args[arg.name] = asInt === 1n;
      continue;
    }

    // `bytes`, the single dynamic tail.
    const offset = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
    const expectedOffset = BigInt(headWords * 32);
    if (offset !== expectedOffset) {
      // A non-canonical offset is how the same bytes decode two different ways in
      // two different decoders. Refuse rather than follow it.
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} has a non-canonical tail offset ${offset}, expected ${expectedOffset}`
      );
    }
    const lengthWord = readWord(argsBody, headWords);
    if (lengthWord === null) {
      return failed('authority-action-undecodable', `argument ${arg.name} has no length word`);
    }
    const byteLength = BigInt(`0x${lengthWord}`);
    if (byteLength > BigInt(argsBody.length)) {
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} declares ${byteLength} bytes, more than the calldata holds`
      );
    }
    const dataStart = (headWords + 1) * WORD_HEX;
    const dataHexLength = Number(byteLength) * 2;
    if (dataStart + dataHexLength > argsBody.length) {
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} declares ${byteLength} bytes but only ${(argsBody.length - dataStart) / 2} remain`
      );
    }
    args[arg.name] = `0x${argsBody.slice(dataStart, dataStart + dataHexLength)}`;
  }

  return { kind: 'decoded', selector, functionName: descriptor.name, args };
}

export interface EvmUserOperationCallInput {
  readonly chainId: number;
  /** The smart account. Target of record when `callData` is not an execute wrapper. */
  readonly sender: string;
  /** `UserOperation.callData`, verbatim. */
  readonly callData: string;
}

export type EvmUserOperationDescription =
  | { readonly kind: 'action'; readonly action: AuthorityContractCall }
  | EvmDecodeFailure;

/**
 * Turns a UserOperation's `callData` into the single `AuthorityContractCall` the
 * policy judges.
 *
 * One level of `execute` unwrapping, never recursive. A nested
 * `execute(execute(...))` therefore surfaces as a call to `execute` *on the
 * account itself*, which no sane scope permits, so it lands on
 * `authority-deny-no-matching-rule` â€” obfuscation gets no special case, it gets
 * the default.
 */
export function describeUserOperationCall(
  input: EvmUserOperationCallInput,
  descriptors: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[]
): EvmUserOperationDescription {
  const outer = decodeEvmCalldata(input.callData, descriptors);
  if (outer.kind === 'failed') return outer;

  if (!ACCOUNT_EXECUTE_SELECTORS.includes(outer.selector)) {
    // Not a wrapper: the UserOperation calls a function on the account itself.
    return {
      kind: 'action',
      action: {
        kind: 'contract-call',
        chainId: input.chainId,
        target: input.sender,
        selector: outer.selector,
        functionName: outer.functionName,
        value: 0n,
        args: outer.args
      }
    };
  }

  const dest = outer.args.dest;
  const value = outer.args.value;
  const func = outer.args.func;
  if (typeof dest !== 'string' || typeof value !== 'bigint' || typeof func !== 'string') {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      'execute wrapper did not decode to (address dest, uint256 value, bytes func)'
    );
  }

  const innerBody = normalizeHex(func);
  if (innerBody === null || innerBody.length === 0) {
    return failed(
      'authority-deny-bare-value-transfer',
      `execute(${dest}, ${value}, "") is a bare native transfer; this engine never authorises one`
    );
  }

  const inner = decodeEvmCalldata(func, descriptors);
  if (inner.kind === 'failed') return inner;

  return {
    kind: 'action',
    action: {
      kind: 'contract-call',
      chainId: input.chainId,
      target: dest,
      selector: inner.selector,
      functionName: inner.functionName,
      value,
      args: inner.args
    }
  };
}

import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

/**
 * Context passed to KeyWrapper wrap/unwrap operations (`S4-4`).
 * Both AWS KMS, Vault Transit, and AES-GCM require this context for AAD binding.
 */
export interface WrapContext {
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly chainKind: 'evm' | 'solana';
  readonly keyVersion: number;
}

/**
 * KeyWrapper interface for envelope encryption (`S4-4`, D11).
 *
 * Provides the abstraction seam separating data-key encryption from key-storage
 * backends. Allows transitioning from environment master keys (EnvMasterKeyWrapper)
 * to Vault Transit (VaultTransitWrapper) or AWS KMS with zero business-logic refactoring.
 */
export interface KeyWrapper {
  /** Stable id embedded in every SealedKey this wrapper produces (e.g. 'env:v1', 'null:v1'). */
  readonly id: string;
  wrap(dataKey: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer>;
  unwrap(wrapped: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer>;
}

export function buildWrapAad(context: WrapContext): Buffer {
  return Buffer.from(`${context.userId}|${context.chainKind}|${context.keyVersion}`, 'utf8');
}

/**
 * EnvMasterKeyWrapper (`env:v<n>`)
 *
 * Implements envelope encryption using a master key loaded from environment variables
 * (e.g. `CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY`). Data keys are wrapped using AES-256-GCM with a fresh
 * 12-byte IV and AAD bound to the WrapContext.
 */
export class EnvMasterKeyWrapper implements KeyWrapper {
  readonly id: string;
  private readonly masterKey: Buffer;

  constructor(options?: { masterKey?: Buffer | string; version?: number }) {
    const version = options?.version ?? 1;
    this.id = `env:v${version}`;

    let rawKey = options?.masterKey ?? process.env.CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY;
    if (!rawKey) {
      // If neither is provided, check if CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY_HEX or default is set
      rawKey = process.env.CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY_HEX;
    }

    if (!rawKey) {
      throw new Error('[custody] EnvMasterKeyWrapper requires CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY to be configured');
    }

    if (Buffer.isBuffer(rawKey)) {
      this.masterKey = rawKey;
    } else if (rawKey.length === 64 && /^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/.test(rawKey)) {
      this.masterKey = Buffer.from(rawKey, 'hex');
    } else {
      this.masterKey = Buffer.from(rawKey, 'utf8');
    }

    if (this.masterKey.length !== 32) {
      throw new Error(
        `[custody] EnvMasterKeyWrapper master key must be exactly 32 bytes (got ${this.masterKey.length})`
      );
    }
  }

  async wrap(dataKey: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    if (dataKey.length !== 32) {
      throw new Error(`[custody] data key to wrap must be 32 bytes, got ${dataKey.length}`);
    }

    const iv = randomBytes(12);
    const cipher = createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', this.masterKey, iv);
    cipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));

    const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(dataKey), cipher.final()]);
    const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();

    // Packed wire format for wrapped dataKey: IV (12) + Tag (16) + Ciphertext (32) = 60 bytes
    return Buffer.concat([iv, tag, ciphertext]);
  }

  async unwrap(wrapped: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    if (wrapped.length !== 60) {
      throw new Error(
        `[custody] invalid wrapped data key length: expected 60 bytes, got ${wrapped.length}`
      );
    }

    const iv = wrapped.subarray(0, 12);
    const tag = wrapped.subarray(12, 28);
    const ciphertext = wrapped.subarray(28);

    const decipher = createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', this.masterKey, iv);
    decipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));
    decipher.setAuthTag(tag);

    try {
      const plaintext = Buffer.concat([decipher.update(ciphertext), decipher.final()]);
      return plaintext;
    } catch (error) {
      throw new Error('[custody] failed to unwrap data key: authentication tag mismatch or tampered context');
    }
  }
}

/**
 * NullWrapper (`null:v1`)
 *
 * Refuses wrap and unwrap operations. Used by staging and tests to guarantee that
 * simulated execution environments cannot accidentally access or store real custody secrets.
 */
export class NullWrapper implements KeyWrapper {
  readonly id = 'null:v1';

  async wrap(_dataKey: Buffer, _context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    throw new Error('[custody] NullWrapper refuses to wrap secrets');
  }

  async unwrap(_wrapped: Buffer, _context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    throw new Error('[custody] NullWrapper refuses to unwrap secrets');
  }
}

  nowSeconds: NOW,

function addressWord(address: string): string {
  return address.replace(/^0x/, '').toLowerCase().padStart(64, '0');
}

function uintWord(value: bigint): string {
  return value.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');
}

function encodeApprove(spender: string, amount: bigint): string {
  return `${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(spender)}${uintWord(amount)}`;
}

function encodeExecute(dest: string, value: bigint, inner: string): string {
  const body = inner.replace(/^0x/, '');
  const byteLength = body.length / 2;
  const padded = body.padEnd(Math.ceil(byteLength / 32) * 64, '0');
  return `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(dest)}${uintWord(value)}${uintWord(96n)}${uintWord(
    BigInt(byteLength)
  )}${padded}`;
}

/** The approve rule Â§2.1 demands: allowlisted spender, bounded amount. */
const APPROVE_RULE = {
  id: 'approve-router',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    targets: [TOKEN],
    selector: ERC20_APPROVE.selector,
    functionName: 'approve'
  },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'approve.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
    { field: 'approve.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: APPROVE_CAP.toString() }
  ]
};

/** The swap rule Â§2.1 demands: recipient pinned to the user's own account. */
const SWAP_RULE = {
  id: 'swap-on-router',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    targets: [ROUTER],
    selector: SWAP_SELECTOR,
    functionName: 'swapTokens'
  },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'swapTokens.recipient', op: 'address_is_owner' },
    { field: 'swapTokens.amountIn', op: 'uint_lte', max: APPROVE_CAP.toString() }
  ]
};

function policy(rules: unknown[] = [APPROVE_RULE, SWAP_RULE]) {
  return compileAuthorityPolicy({ version: 1, chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID, rules });
}

function swapAction(overrides: Partial<AuthorityContractCall> = {}): AuthorityContractCall {
  return {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
    target: ROUTER,
    selector: SWAP_SELECTOR,
    functionName: 'swapTokens',
    value: 0n,
    args: { recipient: OWNER, amountIn: 500n },
    ...overrides
  };
}

describe('S4-P10 â€” footgun 1: overlapping ALLOW rules let the looser one win (DG-3)', () => {
  it('rejects overlapping ALLOW rules on the same (target, selector) at construction time', () => {
    // Without this, the second rule's wider allowlist unions with the first's and
    // the tight rule is silently defeated â€” the exact DG-3 finding.
    const loose = {
      id: 'approve-anything',
      effect: 'allow',
      scope: {
        kind: 'contract-call',
        targets: [TOKEN],
        selector: ERC20_APPROVE.selector,
        functionName: 'approve'
      },
      conditions: [
        { field: 'approve.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER, ATTACKER] },
        { field: 'approve.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '999999999' }
      ]
    };

    let thrown: unknown;
    try {
      policy([APPROVE_RULE, loose]);
    } catch (error) {
      thrown = error;
    }
    expect(thrown).toBeInstanceOf(AuthorityPolicyError);
    expect(thrown).toMatchObject({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-overlapping-allow' });
    expect((thrown as Error).message).toContain('approve-router');
    expect((thrown as Error).message).toContain('approve-anything');
  });

  it('rejects overlapping signed-struct ALLOW rules on the same (verifyingContract, primaryType)', () => {
    const permitRule = (id: string, spender: string) => ({
      id,
      effect: 'allow',
      scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
      conditions: [
        { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [spender] },
        { field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }
      ]
    });
    expect(() => policy([permitRule('tight', ROUTER), permitRule('loose', ATTACKER)])).toThrow(
      expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-overlapping-allow' })
    );
  });

  it('permits non-overlapping rules that differ only by target', () => {
    const otherToken = '0x7777777777777777777777777777777777777777';
    const compiled = policy([
      APPROVE_RULE,
      {
        ...APPROVE_RULE,
        id: 'approve-router-other-token',
        scope: { ...APPROVE_RULE.scope, targets: [otherToken] }
      }
    ]);
    expect(compiled.rules).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('rejects duplicate rule ids, because verdict codes name the rule', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        APPROVE_RULE,
        { ...SWAP_RULE, id: 'approve-router' }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-duplicate-rule-id' }));
  });

  it('reports a hand-built ambiguous policy as unresolved rather than picking a rule', () => {
    // compileAuthorityPolicy cannot produce this. A caller constructing a
    // CompiledAuthorityPolicy by hand can, and must not get union semantics.
    const compiled = policy([SWAP_RULE]);
    const handBuilt = {
      ...compiled,
      rules: [compiled.rules[0]!, { ...compiled.rules[0]!, id: 'shadow' }]
    };
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(handBuilt, swapAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-policy-ambiguous-match'
    });
  });
});

describe('S4-P10 â€” footgun 2: a mis-pathed condition fails closed (DG-3)', () => {
  it('reports a mis-pathed condition as a distinct unresolved diagnostic, not a denial', () => {
    // `recipent` is a typo for `recipient`. Every request through this rule is
    // refused â€” the right direction â€” but an operator must be told the *path* did
    // not resolve, or they will go and debug a trade that was fine.
    const typoPolicy = policy([
      {
        ...SWAP_RULE,
        conditions: [{ field: 'swapTokens.recipent', op: 'address_is_owner' }]
      }
    ]);

    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(typoPolicy, swapAction(), CONTEXT);

    expect(verdict.kind).toBe('unresolved');
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-path-unresolved',
      ruleId: 'swap-on-router',
      field: 'swapTokens.recipent'
    });
    // It must not present as a generic denial...
    expect(verdict.kind).not.toBe('deny');
    // ...and it must still refuse.
    expect(isPermitted(verdict)).toBe(false);
    if (verdict.kind !== 'unresolved') return;
    // The diagnostic names what was actually available, so the fix is one read.
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('recipient');
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('amountIn');
  });

  it('reports a mis-pathed nested struct field with the keys that were available', () => {
    const permitPolicy = policy([
      {
        id: 'permit2-single',
        effect: 'allow',
        scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
        conditions: [
          { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
          { field: 'message.details.amounts', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }
        ]
      }
    ]);
    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(permitPolicy, permitAction(), CONTEXT);
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-path-unresolved',
      field: 'message.details.amounts'
    });
    if (verdict.kind !== 'unresolved') return;
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('amount');
  });

  it('reports a type-mismatched path distinctly from a mis-pathed one', () => {
    const wrongTypePolicy = policy([
      {
        ...SWAP_RULE,
        conditions: [{ field: 'swapTokens.amountIn', op: 'address_is_owner' }]
      }
    ]);
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(wrongTypePolicy, swapAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch',
      field: 'swapTokens.amountIn'
    });
  });

  it('reports a path that lands on a nested struct as a type mismatch, not a value', () => {
    const structPolicy = policy([
      {
        id: 'permit2-single',
        effect: 'allow',
        scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
        conditions: [
          { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
          { field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' },
          { field: 'message.details', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] }
        ]
      }
    ]);
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(structPolicy, permitAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch',
      field: 'message.details'
    });
  });

  it('catches the commonest mis-path at construction: a root the rule does not permit', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...SWAP_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'transfer.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-field-path' }));
  });

  it('rejects a call-metadata path that names no real field', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...SWAP_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'call.gasLimit', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-field-path' }));
  });

  it('reports an owner account that is not an address as a type mismatch, never a pass', () => {
    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(policy(), swapAction(), {
      ...CONTEXT,
      ownerAccount: 'not-an-address'
    });
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch'
    });
  });

  it('refuses a UserOperation whose selector has no descriptor, under its own code', () => {
    const verdict = authorizeUserOperationCall(
      policy(),
      {
        chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
        sender: ACCOUNT,
        callData: encodeExecute(TOKEN, 0n, `0xdeadbeef${uintWord(1n)}`)
      },
      DESCRIPTORS,
      CONTEXT
    );
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-action-unknown-selector'
    });
    expect(isPermitted(verdict)).toBe(false);
  });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Permit2 / signed structs (S4-M13 forward compatibility)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function permitAction(
  overrides: { spender?: string; amount?: bigint; token?: string; deadline?: bigint } = {}
): AuthoritySignedStruct {
  return {
    kind: 'signed-struct',
    chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
    primaryType: 'PermitSingle',
    verifyingContract: PERMIT2,
    message: {
      details: {
        token: overrides.token ?? TOKEN,
        amount: overrides.amount ?? 500n,
        expiration: BigInt(NOW + 600),
        nonce: 0n
      },
      spender: overrides.spender ?? ROUTER,
      sigDeadline: overrides.deadline ?? BigInt(NOW + 600)
    }
  };
}

const PERMIT_RULE = {
  id: 'permit2-single',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'message.details.token', op: 'address_in', addresses: [TOKEN] },

==> packages/shared/src/authority/permission-policy.ts <==
/**
 * Argument-scoped permission policy engine â€” checklist `S4-P10`, ADR-0003 Â§2.1.
 *
 * **This directory moves to `packages/authority` when that package is created
 * (checklist Â§7.1).** It lives under `packages/shared/src/authority/` only
 * because standing up a new workspace package needs a `pnpm install` to link it.
 * Nothing in here imports anything else from `@swat/shared`, and nothing here
 * imports a third-party package at all, so the move is a directory rename plus a
 * `package.json` â€” deliberately, to keep that later move a non-event.
 *
 * ## The hole this closes
 *
 * A session key scoped to "the router, swap selectors only" is still drainable.
 * Every ERC-20 swap needs `approve(spender, amount)` on the *token*, so the scope
 * must permit `approve`. An unconstrained `spender` then lets the key approve an
 * attacker, who drains the token directly and never calls the router. "No
 * `transfer`, no `withdraw`" is an *incomplete* specification of the scope, and a
 * `(target, selector)` policy cannot express the missing half.
 *
 * So the unit of permission here is `(target, selector, decoded argument)`:
 *
 *   * `approve` only where `spender` is allowlisted **and** `amount` is bounded
 *     (never `type(uint256).max`, and never Permit2's `type(uint160).max`),
 *   * swap selectors only where the recipient argument is the user's own account,
 *   * everything not explicitly listed is denied.
 *
 * ## Not only calldata
 *
 * Checklist `S4-M13` moves EVM approvals to Permit2, which removes the on-chain
 * `approve` entirely and relocates the argument-level check onto the *signature's*
 * `token` / `spender` / `amount` / `deadline` fields. The thing being authorised
 * is therefore not always calldata, so `AuthorityAction` has two shapes from the
 * start: a decoded `contract-call` and a `signed-struct` (an EIP-712 payload).
 * The condition vocabulary is shared between them; only the field paths differ.
 * `apps/trade-executor/src/permit2.ts` (built separately) supplies the concrete
 * field names â€” this module is not coupled to them.
 *
 * ## Three verdict kinds, not two
 *
 * `permit` / `deny` / `unresolved`, following the split that
 * `apps/trade-executor/src/solana-simulation.ts` documents at length. The third
 * kind exists because of a specific documented footgun (`DG-3`): **a mis-pathed
 * condition fails closed.** A rule written against `transfer.amount` when the
 * call is `approve` denies every request â€” which is the *right* direction, but it
 * presents to an operator as "the integration is broken", not "the policy is
 * wrong". Folding it into `deny` sends that operator to debug a trade that was
 * fine. So an unresolvable path returns `unresolved` with
 * `authority-field-path-unresolved` and names the path and the keys that *were*
 * available. It still refuses â€” `isPermitted` is true for `permit` and nothing
 * else â€” but it refuses under its own name.
 *
 * ## Overlapping ALLOW rules are rejected at construction
 *
 * The other `DG-3` footgun: when two ALLOW rules both constrain the same field,
 * the union is what you get, so an accidentally-broad second rule silently
 * defeats a tight first one. Two resolutions were available â€” reject the overlap
 * at construction, or evaluate so the tighter constraint wins. This engine
 * **rejects at construction**, for three reasons:
 *
 *   1. "Tighter wins" needs an intersection semantics over heterogeneous
 *      operators (address sets vs numeric bounds), which is not always
 *      well-defined and would have to be *simulated* to be audited.
 *   2. Rejecting keeps the document its own specification: the permission for any
 *      `(target, selector)` is readable from exactly one rule, by eye.
 *   3. Our layer is defence in depth *alongside* a vendor engine (Privy) whose
 *      semantics are a union. Inventing different merge semantics here would mean
 *      the same policy text means two different things in two places â€” which is a
 *      worse footgun than the one being fixed.
 *
 * The check is deliberately coarse: at most one ALLOW rule may be reachable for
 * any `(target, selector)` pair. The cost is real and is documented on
 * `compileAuthorityPolicy` â€” per-target variation must be expressed inside one
 * rule, and a policy needing *different bounds per spender* on the same token and
 * selector is not expressible today. Coarse and loud beats clever and quiet in a
 * funds path.
 *
 * ## Default-deny is structural
 *
 * There is no `deny` effect and no deny list, in the same spirit as
 * `USER_REACHABLE_PREFIXES` in `apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`: a blocklist leaves
 * every newly-deployed selector permitted until somebody remembers to add it.
 * Rules only ever *add* a narrow permission, so the fallthrough is not an `else`
 * â€” it is the absence of a match. Native value is denied the same way: a rule
 * that says nothing about value permits zero.
 *
 * ## Pure
 *
 * No I/O, no DB, no network, no clock â€” `nowSeconds` is injected. The compiled
 * policy is what `execution_grants.scope_policy` holds
 * (`packages/db/src/execution-grants.ts`); the owner account and the grant expiry
 * are passed in from the grant row rather than duplicated in the document, so a
 * templated policy cannot pin to the wrong user's address.
 */

import {
  describeUserOperationCall,
  type EvmFunctionDescriptor,
  type EvmUserOperationCallInput
} from './evm-calldata.js';

/** Robinhood Chain (ADR-0003 Â§2). Every EVM scope in Stage 4 targets this chain. */
export const ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID = 4663;

export const MAX_UINT256 = (1n << 256n) - 1n;
/**
 * Permit2 treats `type(uint160).max` in `details.amount` as an unlimited
 * allowance, so a "bound" of that value is not a bound. Listed alongside
 * `type(uint256).max` for that reason.
 *
 * *Unverified against Permit2 source from this workspace* â€” `permit2.ts` does not
 * exist yet. Re-check when `S4-M13` lands; if the sentinel differs, this constant
 * is the only place to change.
 */
export const MAX_UINT160 = (1n << 160n) - 1n;

/** Amounts that mean "unlimited" and must never be accepted as a bound. */
export const UNBOUNDED_AMOUNT_SENTINELS: readonly bigint[] = [MAX_UINT256, MAX_UINT160];

const MAX_REASON_LENGTH = 500;
const EVM_ADDRESS = /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$/;
const PATH_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/;

function truncate(value: string, limit = MAX_REASON_LENGTH): string {
  return value.length > limit ? `${value.slice(0, limit)}...` : value;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stable codes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A definite refusal. The action was understood and is not permitted.
 * An operator seeing one of these should look at the *policy*, not the plumbing.
 */
export type AuthorityDenyCode =
  /** Default-deny: no ALLOW rule's scope covers this target/selector. */
  | 'authority-deny-no-matching-rule'
  /** A rule matched by scope and one of its argument conditions rejected. */
  | 'authority-deny-condition-failed'
  /** The action is on a different chain than the scope was written for. */
  | 'authority-deny-chain-mismatch'
  /** The grant's expiry has passed. */
  | 'authority-deny-grant-expired'
  /** Native value attached above what the matched rule permits (default zero). */
  | 'authority-deny-value-not-permitted'
  /** `execute(dest, value, "")` â€” a bare value transfer is never authorised. */
  | 'authority-deny-bare-value-transfer';

/**
 * The engine could not answer. Says nothing about whether the action was
 * legitimate â€” it means the policy or the decoder does not line up with the
 * payload. Every one of these still refuses; the separate names exist so the
 * operator is sent to the right place.
 */
export type AuthorityUnresolvedCode =
  /** A condition's field path does not exist on this action. Footgun 2. */
  | 'authority-field-path-unresolved'
  /** The path resolved, but to a value of the wrong kind for the operator. */
  | 'authority-field-type-mismatch'
  /** No descriptor for the 4-byte selector: we cannot say what this call does. */
  | 'authority-action-unknown-selector'
  /** A descriptor matched but the bytes do not decode against it. */
  | 'authority-action-undecodable'
  /** Two ALLOW rules matched. `compileAuthorityPolicy` should have refused it. */
  | 'authority-policy-ambiguous-match';

/** Construction-time rejections. All are thrown as `AuthorityPolicyError`. */
export type AuthorityPolicyErrorCode =
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-document'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-address'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-amount'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-duplicate-rule-id'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-unscoped-rule'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-overlapping-allow'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-unbounded-amount'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-unbounded-approval'
  | 'authority-policy-invalid-field-path';

export class AuthorityPolicyError extends Error {
  readonly code: AuthorityPolicyErrorCode;

  constructor(code: AuthorityPolicyErrorCode, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AuthorityPolicyError';
    this.code = code;
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The thing being authorised
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A leaf value a condition can be written against. */
export type AuthorityFieldValue = string | bigint | boolean;

/**
 * A nested EIP-712 message.
 *
 * **Arrays are deliberately not representable.** `DG-3` records that the vendor
 * engine has no documented array-index condition path, so a rule over
 * `calls[0].target` is not expressible there either; permitting it here would
 * produce a policy our defence-in-depth partner cannot mirror. The practical
 * consequence is that Permit2 `PermitSingle` is expressible and `PermitBatch` is
 * not, and that a 4337 `executeBatch` is refused rather than partially checked.
 */
export interface AuthorityStructNode {
  readonly [key: string]: AuthorityFieldValue | AuthorityStructNode;
}

/** A decoded contract call â€” one `(target, selector, args)` triple. */
export interface AuthorityContractCall {
  readonly kind: 'contract-call';
  readonly chainId: number;
  /** Contract being called. Raw EVM address; case is normalised on evaluation. */
  readonly target: string;
  /** `0x` + 8 hex. The on-chain identity of the function. */
  readonly selector: string;
  /** Decoded name, for diagnostics. Rule matching is on `selector`. */
  readonly functionName: string;
  /** Native value attached to this call. */
  readonly value: bigint;
  /** Decoded arguments by name. Reached as `<functionName>.<argName>`. */
  readonly args: Readonly<Record<string, AuthorityFieldValue>>;
}

/** An EIP-712 payload awaiting a signature â€” Permit2 today (`S4-M13`). */
export interface AuthoritySignedStruct {
  readonly kind: 'signed-struct';
  readonly chainId: number;
  readonly primaryType: string;
  readonly verifyingContract: string;
  readonly message: AuthorityStructNode;
}

export type AuthorityAction = AuthorityContractCall | AuthoritySignedStruct;

export type AuthorityConditionOp =
  | 'address_in'
  | 'address_is_owner'
  | 'uint_lte'
  | 'uint_eq'
  | 'uint_lte_now_plus'
  | 'bool_eq';

/**
 * One argument constraint.
 *
 * `field` is a dotted path. The roots are deliberately the same shape the vendor
 * engine uses (`approve.spender`), so one rule reads the same in both places.
 */
export type AuthorityCondition =
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'address_in'; readonly addresses: readonly string[] }
  /** Pins to the grant's own account. The swap-recipient constraint of Â§2.1. */
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'address_is_owner' }
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'uint_lte'; readonly max: bigint }
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'uint_eq'; readonly value: bigint }
  /** For Permit2 `deadline`: bounded relative to the injected clock. */
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'uint_lte_now_plus'; readonly maxSecondsAhead: number }
  | { readonly field: string; readonly op: 'bool_eq'; readonly value: boolean };

/**
 * A rule permits exactly **one** function or primary type.
 *
 * Not an arbitrary restriction: it is what makes `<functionName>.<arg>` paths
 * unambiguous. A rule covering both `approve` and `transfer` would have to answer
 * "what does a condition on `approve.spender` mean when the call is `transfer`?",
 * and every answer to that is either a loosening or a surprise.
 */
export type AuthorityRuleScope =
  | {
      readonly kind: 'contract-call';
      /** Contracts this rule covers. Never empty â€” an empty list is unscoped. */
      readonly targets: readonly string[];
      readonly selector: string;
      /** The path root for argument conditions in this rule. */
      readonly functionName: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: 'signed-struct';
      readonly verifyingContracts: readonly string[];
      readonly primaryType: string;
    };

export interface AuthorityRule {
  readonly id: string;
  /** Only `allow` exists. Default-deny is structural, not a rule. */
  readonly effect: 'allow';
  readonly scope: AuthorityRuleScope;
  readonly conditions: readonly AuthorityCondition[];
  /** Native value ceiling. Absent means zero. */
  readonly maxNativeValue: bigint;
}

export interface CompiledAuthorityPolicy {
  readonly version: 1;
  /** The chain this scope was written for. Robinhood Chain is 4663. */
  readonly chainId: number;
  readonly rules: readonly AuthorityRule[];
}

export interface AuthorityEvaluationContext {
  /**
   * The user's own account â€” what `address_is_owner` pins to. Sourced from
   * `execution_grants.account_address`, which is stored unprefixed; a
   * `chain:`-prefixed value is accepted and stripped so a caller reading from a
   * prefixed column cannot silently pin to a literal that matches nothing.

  readonly ownerAccount: string;
  /** Injected clock, unix seconds. Nothing here reads `Date.now()`. */
  readonly nowSeconds: number;

  readonly grantExpiresAtSeconds?: number | null;
}

export type AuthorityVerdict =
  | {
      readonly kind: 'permit';
      readonly ruleId: string;
      /** Which function/primary type the rule matched, for the audit line. */
      readonly matched: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: 'deny';
