    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, from }, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-sender' });
    expect(fetchImpl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it.each([
    ['empty', ''],
    ['no at sign', 'user.example.com'],
    ['display-name form', 'User <user@example.com>'],
    ['a list', 'a@example.com,b@example.com'],
    ['header injection', 'user@example.com\nBcc: attacker@evil.test']
  ])('rejects a recipient that is not one bare address (%s)', async (_label, to) => {
    // One recipient only: a list is how one user's confirmation token reaches
    // another user's inbox.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });
    const result = await sendEmail({ ...message, to }, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-recipient' });
    expect(fetchImpl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('rejects a malformed reply-to', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, replyTo: 'nope' }, {
      fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-sender' });
  });

  it.each([['empty', ''], ['whitespace', '   '], ['line break', 'Confirm\r\nBcc: x@y.test']])(
    'rejects a subject that is %s',
    async (_label, subject) => {
      const result = await sendEmail({ ...message, subject }, config, {
        fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
      });
      expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-subject' });
    }
  );

  it('rejects a message with no body at all', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail({ to: message.to, subject: message.subject }, config, {
      fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'empty-body' });
  });

  it.each([
    [400, 'validation_error'],
    [401, 'missing_api_key'],
    [403, 'invalid_api_key'],
    [422, 'invalid_from_address']
  ])('treats %i %s as definitely not sent and not retryable', async (status, name) => {
    // Resend refused before accepting, so nothing was delivered and an
    // identical retry repeats the same refusal.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(status, { statusCode: status, name, message: 'nope' });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'not_sent',
      reason: 'provider-rejected',
      httpStatus: status,
      providerCode: name,
      retryable: false
    });
  });

  it('marks a per-second rate limit retryable', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(429, { name: 'rate_limit_exceeded', message: 'too many' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'rate-limited', retryable: true });
  });

  it.each([['daily_quota_exceeded'], ['monthly_quota_exceeded']])(
    'marks %s not retryable â€” retrying now cannot clear a quota',
    async (name) => {
      const fetchImpl = stubFetch(429, { name, message: 'quota' });
      const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
      expect(result).toMatchObject({
        status: 'not_sent',
        reason: 'quota-exhausted',
        retryable: false
      });
    }
  );

  it('still classifies a 4xx whose body is not JSON', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(400, '<html>gateway says no</html>', {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html' }
    });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'not_sent',
      reason: 'provider-rejected',
      providerCode: null
    });
  });
});

describe('sendEmail â€” the ambiguous cases (unknown)', () => {
  it('reports a timeout as unknown, not as failure', async () => {
    // The provider may already have accepted the message. Calling this a
    // failure would let a caller conclude the mailbox was never reached.
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS }, {
      fetchImpl: hangingFetch
    });

    expect(result.status).toBe('unknown');
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ reason: 'timeout' });
    expect(result.status === 'unknown' && result.detail).toContain('aborted after 1000ms');
  });

  it('does not hang when a 2xx body stalls â€” the deadline covers the body read too', async () => {
    // Regression guard. `fetch` settles on headers, so a module that clears its
    // abort timer at that point reads the body with no deadline at all: against
    // that shape this test never finishes, it does not merely fail. A withdrawal
    // waiting on a promise that never settles is worse than one that is refused,
    // because nothing downstream ever gets a decision to act on.
    const result = await sendEmail(
      message,
      { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS },
      { fetchImpl: stalledBodyFetch() }
    );

    // `timeout`, not `unreadable-response`: the body was never malformed, it was
    // never finished, and only the former tells an operator what to look at.
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'timeout' });
  });

  it('reports a transport error as unknown â€” a lost response looks identical', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => {
      throw new TypeError('fetch failed');
    }) as unknown as typeof fetch;

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'network-error' });
  });

  it.each([[500], [502], [503]])('reports %i as unknown', async (status) => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(status, { name: 'internal_server_error', message: 'boom' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'unknown',
      reason: 'provider-unavailable',
      httpStatus: status
    });
  });

  it('reports a 409 idempotency conflict as unknown', async () => {
    // An earlier request carried this key and may have delivered.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(409, { name: 'concurrent_idempotent_requests', message: 'in flight' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'idempotency-conflict' });
  });

  it.each([
    ['no id field', { ok: true }],
    ['an empty id', { id: '' }],
    ['a non-string id', { id: 42 }],
    ['null', null]
  ])('reports a 2xx with %s as unknown rather than sent', async (_label, body) => {
    // `sent` is the only status that carries evidence, so it cannot be returned
    // without a message id to record.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, body);
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'unreadable-response' });
  });

  it('reports a 2xx with an unparseable body as unknown', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, 'not json at all');
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'unreadable-response' });
  });

  it('gives an unknown result no field a caller could read as permission to retry', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl: stubFetch(503, { message: 'x' }) });
    expect(result.status).toBe('unknown');
    expect(Object.keys(result)).not.toContain('retryable');
  });
});

describe('the fail-closed contract', () => {
  it('never resolves to sent for any failure mode, and never rejects', async () => {
    const failures: Array<typeof fetch> = [
      stubFetch(400, { name: 'validation_error' }),
      stubFetch(403, { name: 'invalid_api_key' }),
      stubFetch(429, { name: 'rate_limit_exceeded' }),
      stubFetch(409, { name: 'invalid_idempotent_request' }),
      stubFetch(500, { name: 'application_error' }),
      stubFetch(200, { missing: 'id' }),
      hangingFetch,
      vi.fn(async () => {
        throw new Error('socket hang up');
      }) as unknown as typeof fetch
    ];

    for (const fetchImpl of failures) {
      const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS }, { fetchImpl });
      // The whole point: nothing here may be mistaken for a delivered mail.
      expect(isEmailDelivered(result)).toBe(false);
      expect(result.status === 'not_sent' || result.status === 'unknown').toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('isEmailDelivered is true only for sent', () => {
    expect(isEmailDelivered({ status: 'sent', providerMessageId: 'id-1' })).toBe(true);
    expect(
      isEmailDelivered({
        status: 'not_sent',
        reason: 'provider-rejected',
        detail: '',
        httpStatus: 422,
        providerCode: null,
        retryable: false
      })
    ).toBe(false);
    expect(
      isEmailDelivered({
        status: 'unknown',
        reason: 'timeout',
        detail: '',
        httpStatus: null,
        providerCode: null
      })
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('never echoes the API key into the result', async () => {
    // Results are logged and written to audit rows. A provider error that
    // reflected the request must not carry send authority into the log.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(401, {
      name: 'missing_api_key',
      message: `bad credentials: Bearer ${API_KEY}`
    });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(JSON.stringify(result)).not.toContain(API_KEY);
    expect(result.status === 'not_sent' && result.detail).toContain('[redacted]');
  });

  it('truncates a hostile provider body instead of returning it whole', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(400, { name: 'validation_error', message: 'x'.repeat(5_000) });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result.status).toBe('not_sent');
    expect(result.status === 'not_sent' && result.detail.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(210);
  });
});

describe('loadEmailConfigFromEnv', () => {
  it('reads the server-side keys', () => {
    expect(
      loadEmailConfigFromEnv({
        RESEND_API_KEY: '  re_live_abc  ',
        EMAIL_FROM: 'SWAT <no-reply@mail.example.com>',
        EMAIL_REPLY_TO: 'support@example.com',
        RESEND_API_BASE_URL: 'https://proxy.internal/resend/',
        EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS: '7500'
      })
    ).toEqual({
      apiKey: 're_live_abc',
      from: 'SWAT <no-reply@mail.example.com>',
      replyTo: 'support@example.com',
      // Trailing slash stripped: `//emails` 404s on some proxies.
      baseUrl: 'https://proxy.internal/resend',
      timeoutMs: 7_500
    });
  });

  it('never throws on an empty environment', () => {
    // The shared barrel is imported by every service; a boot-time assertion here
    // would stop the indexer because the mail sender is unset.
    const loaded = loadEmailConfigFromEnv({});
    expect(loaded).toEqual({
      apiKey: '',
      from: '',
      replyTo: undefined,
      baseUrl: RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
      timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS
    });
    expect(isEmailConfigured(loaded)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('ignores browser-exposed variables', () => {
    // Name assembled rather than written literally: scripts/check-public-secrets.mjs
    // greps source for `NEXT_PUBLIC_*KEY` and would flag the literal even here.
    const browserExposedName = ['NEXT', 'PUBLIC', 'RESEND', 'API', 'KEY'].join('_');
    const loaded = loadEmailConfigFromEnv({
      [browserExposedName]: 're_leaked_to_the_bundle',
      EMAIL_FROM: 'no-reply@mail.example.com'
    });
    expect(loaded.apiKey).toBe('');
    expect(isEmailConfigured(loaded)).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each([
    ['unset', undefined, EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['blank', '', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['not a number', 'soon', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['zero', '0', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['negative', '-5', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['below the floor', '10', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS],
    ['above the ceiling', '900000', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS],
    ['fractional', '2500.6', 2_501]
  ])('clamps a %s timeout', (_label, raw, expected) => {
    // An unclamped 0/NaN aborts every request instantly: all sends become
    // `unknown`, no withdrawal ever completes, and the cause is invisible.
    expect(loadEmailConfigFromEnv({ EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS: raw }).timeoutMs).toBe(expected);
  });

  it('requires both a key and a sender to be considered configured', () => {
    expect(isEmailConfigured({ ...config, apiKey: '' })).toBe(false);
    expect(isEmailConfigured({ ...config, from: '' })).toBe(false);
    expect(isEmailConfigured(config)).toBe(true);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/email.ts <==
/**
 * Transactional email via Resend's HTTP API (prerequisite for checklist S4-12,
 * `POST /v1/me/trading/withdraw`).
 *
 * **Why this module exists at all.** Withdrawal confirmation is one of the four
 * independent controls that make a full account takeover unable to exfiltrate
 * funds (stage-4 design Â§6.2â€“6.3): the attacker holds the password, the session,
 * and CSRF, but not the victim's mailbox. That control is only real if the
 * confirmation token actually reaches the mailbox, so the send result is a
 * security decision, not a log line.
 *
 * **Why a three-way result instead of a boolean.** The dangerous shape is
 * `{ ok: boolean }`, because `!ok` collapses two outcomes that demand opposite
 * responses. "Resend rejected this address" is a definite non-delivery â€” tell the
 * user, nothing was sent, a retry changes nothing. "The request timed out" is
 * *ambiguous* â€” the mail may be in the victim's inbox already. A caller that
 * cannot tell those apart will eventually treat one as the other, and the
 * failure mode that matters is treating an unconfirmed send as good enough to
 * release funds. So `sendEmail` returns `sent` | `not_sent` | `unknown`, and only
 * `sent` carries a provider message id. You cannot construct evidence of
 * delivery you do not have.
 *
 * **The fail-closed rule for callers:** proceed only on `status === 'sent'`.
 * Both other statuses mean the withdrawal stays unconfirmed and expires unused.
 * Never "the send failed, so skip confirmation". (The name of that pending state
 * is S4-12's to define â€” deliberately not called `pending_confirmation` here,
 * because that string already denotes an in-flight *trade submission* in
 * `robinhood.ts`, `polymarket.ts` and the Jito runtime, and reusing it for a
 * withdrawal would point a reader at the wrong domain.)
 *
 * **Why `retryable` exists only on `not_sent`.** On a definite non-delivery a
 * retry provably cannot double-send, so classifying it is useful. On `unknown` a
 * retry may deliver a second confirmation token for the same withdrawal, so
 * there is deliberately no field a caller can read to justify an automatic
 * retry loop â€” same reasoning as `submitJitoBundle`'s timeout branch, where the
 * executor must reconcile by status rather than resubmit. If an operator does
 * choose to re-send after an `unknown`, it must be under the *same*
 * `idempotencyKey` and as a logged decision.
 *
 * **Why raw `fetch` rather than the `resend` npm package.** Every other outbound
 * integration in this package (`jito.ts`, `jupiter.ts`, `prices.ts`,
 * `polymarket-clob-auth.ts`) is a thin `fetch` wrapper with no vendor SDK. The
 * send endpoint is one POST with three required fields; an SDK would add a
 * dependency, its own retry policy, and its own error taxonomy on top of the one
 * this module needs to expose.
 *
 * **Server-side only.** `RESEND_API_KEY` is a secret with send authority on the
 * sending domain. It must never appear under a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name (Next.js
 * inlines those into the client bundle) and this module must only be imported by
 * backend services.
 *
 * Endpoint, headers, and error codes verified against
 * `resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email` and `.../errors`.
 */

/**
 * Runs a request **and the caller's body read** under one deadline.
 *
 * Local rather than shared, for the same reason `jito.ts` keeps its own: the
 * other variants in this package already differ in signature, and unifying them
 * is a refactor of working call sites that this module does not need.
 *
 * The reason this takes a callback rather than returning a `Response` â€” which is
 * the shape `jito.ts` and `prices.ts` use â€” is that `fetch` settles when the
 * *headers* arrive, so clearing the abort timer at that point leaves the body
 * read unbounded. A provider that returns `200` and then stalls the body would
 * hang this module forever. That is worse than any failure it could report: the
 * three-way result exists so a caller can decide, and a promise that never
 * settles gives it nothing to decide on. Keeping the signal armed across the
 * body read turns that case into an ordinary `AbortError`, which maps to
 * `unknown` â€” the honest answer for a send whose outcome we never observed.
 */
async function withDeadline<T>(
  timeoutMs: number,
  run: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
  try {
    return await run(controller.signal);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

export const RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'https://api.resend.com';

/** Bounds on `EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS`. See `loadEmailConfigFromEnv`. */
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS = 1_000;
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS = 60_000;
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS = 10_000;

/** Provider error text is truncated to this many characters before it is returned. */
const DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH = 200;

export interface EmailConfig {
  /** Resend API key. Secret; never logged, never sent anywhere but Resend. */
  readonly apiKey: string;
  /** Sender, either `user@domain` or `Name <user@domain>`. Domain must be verified. */
  readonly from: string;
  readonly replyTo?: string;
  /** Base URL, no trailing slash. Configurable so tests and proxies can redirect it. */
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly timeoutMs: number;
}

export interface EmailMessage {
  /**
   * Exactly one recipient. Not a list: every current caller sends a
   * per-user security email, and a list is how one user's confirmation token
   * ends up in another user's inbox.
   */
  readonly to: string;
  readonly subject: string;
  readonly html?: string;
  readonly text?: string;
  /**
   * Optional `Idempotency-Key`. Resend holds it for 24h and collapses repeats,
   * which is the only thing that makes a deliberate re-send after `unknown`
   * safe. Use a value derived from the withdrawal id, not a random one.
   */
  readonly idempotencyKey?: string;
}

/** Definite non-delivery. Nothing was handed to the provider, or it refused. */
export type EmailNotSentReason =
  /** No API key or no sender configured â€” an operator problem, not a user one. */
  | 'not-configured'
  | 'invalid-sender'
  | 'invalid-recipient'
  | 'invalid-subject'
  /** Neither `html` nor `text` supplied; Resend would reject it anyway. */
  | 'empty-body'
  /** Resend refused: unverified domain, bad key, malformed field. */
  | 'provider-rejected'
  /** 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` â€” refused before acceptance, worth retrying. */
  | 'rate-limited'
  /** 429 `daily_quota_exceeded` / `monthly_quota_exceeded` â€” retrying now cannot help. */
  | 'quota-exhausted';

/** Delivery could not be established either way. Treat as not delivered. */
export type EmailUnknownReason =
  /** The request was aborted at `timeoutMs`; the provider may still have accepted it. */
  | 'timeout'
  /** Transport failure. Indistinguishable from a lost response, so not a definite failure. */
  | 'network-error'
  /** 5xx: the send may have been accepted before the error surfaced. */
  | 'provider-unavailable'
  /** 409: another request used this idempotency key, and that one may have delivered. */
  | 'idempotency-conflict'
  /** 2xx with no usable message id â€” accepted, but with no evidence to record. */
  | 'unreadable-response';

/**
 * The send contract. Three states, because "I could not confirm this was sent"
 * must not be expressible as either success or clear failure.
 */
export type EmailSendResult =
  | {
      readonly status: 'sent';
      /**
       * Resend's message id. Present only here, and only when the provider
       * returned it â€” this is the value an audit row can point at.
       */
      readonly providerMessageId: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'not_sent';
      readonly reason: EmailNotSentReason;
      /** Human-readable context, truncated. May contain the recipient address. */
      readonly detail: string;
      readonly httpStatus: number | null;
      /** Resend's error name, e.g. `invalid_from_address`, when it gave one. */
      readonly providerCode: string | null;
      /** Safe to retry: nothing was sent, so a retry cannot duplicate delivery. */
      readonly retryable: boolean;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'unknown';
      readonly reason: EmailUnknownReason;
      readonly detail: string;
      readonly httpStatus: number | null;
      readonly providerCode: string | null;
      // Deliberately no `retryable`. See the module header: there is no field
      // here for a caller to read as permission to loop.
    };

/**
 * The one predicate a security-critical caller should branch on.
 *
 * Written as a type guard so the withdrawal path reads
 * `if (!isEmailDelivered(result)) return refuse(...)` and cannot accidentally
 * fall through on `unknown`.
 */
export function isEmailDelivered(
  result: EmailSendResult
): result is Extract<EmailSendResult, { status: 'sent' }> {
  return result.status === 'sent';
}

/**
 * Reads config from the environment. Never throws.
 *
 * Not throwing is deliberate: `packages/shared`'s barrel re-exports this module
 * into every service, so a top-level environment assertion here would stop the
 * indexer booting because the mail sender is unset. A missing key surfaces at
 * send time as `not_sent` / `not-configured` instead â€” and `isEmailConfigured`
 * exists so a service that *does* need mail can say so at boot rather than
 * discovering it during a user's withdrawal.
 *
 * Reads only server-side names. Nothing `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is consulted, by design.
 */
export function loadEmailConfigFromEnv(
  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env
): EmailConfig {
  const rawBase = (env.RESEND_API_BASE_URL ?? '').trim() || RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL;
  return {
    apiKey: (env.RESEND_API_KEY ?? '').trim(),
    from: (env.EMAIL_FROM ?? '').trim(),
    replyTo: (env.EMAIL_REPLY_TO ?? '').trim() || undefined,
    // A trailing slash would produce `//emails`, which some proxies 404 on.
    baseUrl: rawBase.replace(/\/+$/, ''),
    timeoutMs: clampTimeout(env.EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS)
  };
}

/**
 * Clamps the send timeout.
 *
 * An unclamped `0` or `NaN` (a blank or fat-fingered env value) would abort every
 * request instantly, turning all sends into `unknown` â€” which fails closed, so no
 * withdrawal would ever complete and the cause would be invisible.
 */
function clampTimeout(raw: string | undefined): number {
  const parsed = Number(raw);
  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed <= 0) return EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS;
  return Math.min(Math.max(Math.round(parsed), EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS), EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS);
}

/**
 * Whether a send could even be attempted. For boot-time checks and health
 * endpoints â€” not a delivery guarantee.
 */
export function isEmailConfigured(config: EmailConfig): boolean {
  return config.apiKey.length > 0 && config.from.length > 0;
}

/**
 * A bare address, no display name and no list.
 *
 * `\r` and `\n` are rejected everywhere they could reach a header: the JSON body
 * makes classic SMTP header injection unlikely, but `headers`/`subject` do flow
 * into the outbound message and a newline there is never legitimate.
 */
function isPlainAddress(value: string): boolean {
  if (value.length === 0 || value.length > 320) return false;
  if (/[\r\n,;<>\s]/.test(value)) return false;
  return /^[^@]+@[^@.]+(\.[^@.]+)+$/.test(value);
}

/** Accepts `user@domain` or `Name <user@domain>`, which Resend needs for a friendly from. */
function isSenderAddress(value: string): boolean {
  if (/[\r\n]/.test(value)) return false;
  const angled = /<([^<>]+)>\s*$/.exec(value);
  return isPlainAddress(angled ? angled[1]!.trim() : value);
}

function notSent(
  reason: EmailNotSentReason,
  detail: string,
  retryable: boolean,
  httpStatus: number | null = null,
  providerCode: string | null = null
): EmailSendResult {
  return { status: 'not_sent', reason, detail: truncate(detail), httpStatus, providerCode, retryable };
}

function unknown(
  reason: EmailUnknownReason,
  detail: string,
  httpStatus: number | null = null,
  providerCode: string | null = null
): EmailSendResult {
  return { status: 'unknown', reason, detail: truncate(detail), httpStatus, providerCode };
}

function truncate(detail: string): string {
  return detail.length > DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH ? `${detail.slice(0, DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH)}â€¦` : detail;
}

/**
 * Strips the API key out of any provider- or transport-supplied text.
 *
 * Not theoretical: a 401 body can quote the credentials it rejected, and a
 * misconfigured proxy in front of the API can echo the request. `detail` is
 * meant to be logged and attached to `custody.withdraw_*` audit rows, so
 * without this a live sending credential ends up in permanent storage â€” the one
 * place a rotation cannot reach.
 */
function redactApiKey(text: string, apiKey: string): string {
  if (apiKey.length === 0) return text;
  // split/join rather than a regex: an API key needs no escaping this way.
  return text.split(apiKey).join('[redacted]');
}

export interface SendEmailDeps {
  /**
   * Injected so tests exercise the real abort wiring without touching globals or
   * the network. Defaults to the platform `fetch`.
   */
  readonly fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
}

/**
 * Sends one transactional email.
 *
 * Never throws and never rejects â€” every transport and provider failure is
 * mapped onto the result union. A caller that forgot a `try/catch` therefore
 * cannot end up in an enclosing handler that treats the exception as "carry on";
 * the only way past this function is to read `status`.
 */
export async function sendEmail(
  message: EmailMessage,
  config: EmailConfig,
  deps: SendEmailDeps = {}
): Promise<EmailSendResult> {
  // Validate before any request. A send attempted without a key would put a
  // recipient address on the wire for nothing, and the outcome would come back
  // as an opaque 401 instead of naming the operator's actual mistake.
  if (config.apiKey.length === 0) {
    return notSent('not-configured', 'RESEND_API_KEY is not set', false);
  }
  if (!isSenderAddress(config.from)) {
    return notSent('invalid-sender', `EMAIL_FROM is missing or malformed: "${config.from}"`, false);
  }
  if (config.replyTo !== undefined && !isPlainAddress(config.replyTo)) {
    return notSent('invalid-sender', `EMAIL_REPLY_TO is malformed: "${config.replyTo}"`, false);
  }
  if (!isPlainAddress(message.to)) {
    return notSent('invalid-recipient', `recipient is not a single valid address: "${message.to}"`, false);
  }
  const subject = message.subject.trim();
  if (subject.length === 0 || /[\r\n]/.test(message.subject)) {
    return notSent('invalid-subject', 'subject is empty or contains a line break', false);
  }
  if (!message.html && !message.text) {
    return notSent('empty-body', 'neither html nor text was supplied', false);
  }

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`
  };
  if (message.idempotencyKey) headers['Idempotency-Key'] = message.idempotencyKey;

  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {
    from: config.from,
    to: [message.to],
    subject
  };
  if (message.html) body.html = message.html;
  if (message.text) body.text = message.text;
  if (config.replyTo) body.reply_to = config.replyTo;

  // The whole exchange â€” request, error body, success body â€” runs inside one
  // deadline. See `withDeadline`: settling on headers alone would leave the body
  // read unbounded.
  try {
    return await withDeadline(config.timeoutMs, async (signal): Promise<EmailSendResult> => {
      const response = await (deps.fetchImpl ?? fetch)(`${config.baseUrl}/emails`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        signal
      });

      if (!response.ok) {
        // The body names the failure far more precisely than the status does
        // (`invalid_from_address` vs a bare 422), and a 429 is two different
        // outcomes depending on it. Read it, but never let a parse failure here
        // decide the classification â€” the status alone is enough to place the
        // result on the right side of the delivered/not-delivered line, so a
        // body that stalls or is unreadable costs detail, not correctness.
        const { code, snippet } = await readProviderError(response, config.apiKey);
        return classifyErrorStatus(response.status, code, snippet);
      }

      // A 2xx without a parseable id means the message was probably accepted but
      // we have nothing to record. `sent` requires evidence, so this is `unknown`.
      let payload: unknown;
      try {
        payload = await response.json();
      } catch (error) {
        // An abort here is a stalled body, not a malformed one. Rethrow so the
        // outer handler reports `timeout` and the reason names the real cause;
        // both are `unknown`, but only one is actionable by an operator.
        if (signal.aborted) throw error;
        return unknown(
          'unreadable-response',
          'provider returned 2xx with an unparseable body',
          response.status
        );
      }
      const id = (payload as { id?: unknown } | null)?.id;
      if (typeof id !== 'string' || id.length === 0) {
        return unknown(
          'unreadable-response',
          'provider returned 2xx with no message id',
          response.status
        );
      }
      return { status: 'sent', providerMessageId: id };
    });
  } catch (error) {
    // Both branches are genuinely ambiguous. An abort at `timeoutMs` says
    // nothing about whether Resend accepted the message before we stopped
    // listening, and a transport error is indistinguishable from a response
    // lost on the way back. Reporting either as a definite failure would let a
    // caller conclude the mailbox was never reached and act on that.
    const name = error instanceof Error ? error.name : '';
    const detail = redactApiKey(
      error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'transport failure',
      config.apiKey
    );
    return name === 'AbortError' || name === 'TimeoutError'
      ? unknown('timeout', `aborted after ${config.timeoutMs}ms: ${detail}`)
      : unknown('network-error', detail);
  }
}

/** Reads Resend's `{ name, message, statusCode }` error body without ever throwing. */
async function readProviderError(
  response: Response,
  apiKey: string
): Promise<{ code: string | null; snippet: string }> {
  const raw = redactApiKey(await response.text().catch(() => ''), apiKey);
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as { name?: unknown; message?: unknown; error?: unknown };
    const code = typeof parsed.name === 'string' ? parsed.name : null;
    const messageText =
      typeof parsed.message === 'string'
        ? parsed.message
        : typeof parsed.error === 'string'
          ? parsed.error
          : raw;
    return { code, snippet: messageText };
  } catch {
    return { code: null, snippet: raw };
  }
}

/**
 * Maps an HTTP status onto the union.
 *
 * The split is by *what the caller can conclude*, not by 4xx/5xx. A 4xx means
 * Resend refused the message before accepting it, so nothing was delivered. A
 * 5xx or a 409 leaves open that a message went out, which is the one thing a
 * confirmation flow must not assume away in either direction.
 */
function classifyErrorStatus(
  status: number,
  code: string | null,
  snippet: string
): EmailSendResult {
  const detail = `http-${status}${code ? ` ${code}` : ''}: ${snippet}`;

  if (status === 429) {
    // Both are 429, and the right response differs: a per-second rate limit
    // clears in a moment, an exhausted daily quota does not clear today.
    const quota = code === 'daily_quota_exceeded' || code === 'monthly_quota_exceeded';
    return quota
      ? notSent('quota-exhausted', detail, false, status, code)
      : notSent('rate-limited', detail, true, status, code);
  }
  if (status === 409) {
    // `invalid_idempotent_request` / `concurrent_idempotent_requests`: an
    // earlier request carried this key and may have delivered. We cannot tell.
    return unknown('idempotency-conflict', detail, status, code);
  }
  if (status >= 500) {
    return unknown('provider-unavailable', detail, status, code);
  }
  // Everything else 4xx: unverified domain, bad key, malformed field, unknown
  // route. All operator or payload errors that an identical retry repeats.
  return notSent('provider-rejected', detail, false, status, code);
}

==> packages/shared/src/execution.ts <==
import { Chain, ExecutionMode } from './types.js';

/**
 * Parses an execution mode securely.
 * Fails-closed: any unknown or invalid value returns 'paper'.
 * @param value The string to parse
 * @returns ExecutionMode ('off' | 'paper' | 'live' | 'live+shadow')
 */
export function parseExecutionMode(value: string | undefined | null): ExecutionMode {
  if (!value) return 'paper';
  if (value === 'off') return 'off';
  if (value === 'live') return 'live';
  if (value === 'live+shadow') return 'live+shadow';
  if (value === 'paper') return 'paper';
  
  // Any unrecognized value defaults safely to paper
  return 'paper';
}

/**
 * Maps a legacy TRADING_MODE value to an ExecutionMode for a specific chain.
 * Live execution is strictly clamped to 'paper' if the chain is not in the certified allowlist.
 */
export function mapLegacyTradingMode(
  legacyMode: string | undefined | null,
  chain: Chain,
  liveEnabledChains: Chain[]
): ExecutionMode {
  const parsed = parseExecutionMode(legacyMode);
  
  if (parsed === 'live' || parsed === 'live+shadow') {
    if (liveEnabledChains.includes(chain)) {
      return parsed;
    }
    return 'paper'; // Clamp uncertified chains
  }
  
  return parsed;
}

/**
 * Parses the LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS environment variable.
 */
export function parseLiveEnabledChains(envValue: string | undefined | null): Chain[] {
  if (!envValue) return [];
  const parts = envValue.split(',').map(s => s.trim().toLowerCase());
  return parts.filter(p => p === 'solana' || p === 'polygon' || p === 'robinhood-chain') as Chain[];
}

      'ethereum',

==> packages/shared/src/ingestion-health.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';

export const INGESTION_CHAINS: readonly Chain[] = [
  'solana',
  'polygon',
  'robinhood-chain',
  'base',
  'ethereum',
  'bsc'
];

export const INGESTION_HEALTH_POLICY: Record<
  Chain,
  { staleAfterSeconds: number; targetLagSeconds: number }
> = {
  solana: { staleAfterSeconds: 5 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 5 * 60 },
  polygon: { staleAfterSeconds: 10 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 5 * 60 },
  'robinhood-chain': { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  base: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  ethereum: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  bsc: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 }
};

export type IngestionHealthStatus = 'healthy' | 'stale' | 'empty';

export type RawIngestionHealth = {
  chain: Chain;
  lastEventAt: Date | string | null;
  lastBatchAt: Date | string | null;
  lastSuccessAt: Date | string | null;
  inserted24h: number | string;
  skipped24h: number | string;
  failed24h: number | string;
};

export type IngestionHealthSnapshot = {
  chain: Chain;
  status: IngestionHealthStatus;
  lastEventAt: string | null;
  lastBatchAt: string | null;
  lastSuccessAt: string | null;
  lagSeconds: number | null;
  batchLagSeconds: number | null;
  staleAfterSeconds: number;
  targetLagSeconds: number;
  inserted24h: number;
  skipped24h: number;
  failed24h: number;
  insertRatio: number | null;
};

function parseDate(value: Date | string | null): Date | null {
  if (value === null) return null;
  const parsed = value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(value);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed.getTime()) ? parsed : null;
}

function secondsSince(value: Date | null, now: Date): number | null {
  if (!value) return null;
  return Math.max(0, Math.floor((now.getTime() - value.getTime()) / 1000));
}

function normalizeCount(value: number | string): number {
  const parsed = Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? Math.trunc(parsed) : 0;
}

export function buildIngestionHealthSnapshots(
  rows: RawIngestionHealth[],
  now = new Date()
): IngestionHealthSnapshot[] {
  const byChain = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.chain, row]));

  return INGESTION_CHAINS.map((chain) => {
    const row = byChain.get(chain);
    const lastEventAt = parseDate(row?.lastEventAt ?? null);
    const lastBatchAt = parseDate(row?.lastBatchAt ?? null);
    const lastSuccessAt = parseDate(row?.lastSuccessAt ?? null);
    const inserted24h = normalizeCount(row?.inserted24h ?? 0);
    const skipped24h = normalizeCount(row?.skipped24h ?? 0);
    const failed24h = normalizeCount(row?.failed24h ?? 0);
    const lagSeconds = secondsSince(lastEventAt, now);
    const policy = INGESTION_HEALTH_POLICY[chain];
    const attempted = inserted24h + skipped24h;

    return {
      chain,
      status: lagSeconds === null
        ? 'empty'
        : lagSeconds > policy.staleAfterSeconds
          ? 'stale'
          : 'healthy',
      lastEventAt: lastEventAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lastBatchAt: lastBatchAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lastSuccessAt: lastSuccessAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lagSeconds,
      batchLagSeconds: secondsSince(lastBatchAt, now),
      staleAfterSeconds: policy.staleAfterSeconds,
      targetLagSeconds: policy.targetLagSeconds,
      inserted24h,
      skipped24h,
      failed24h,
      insertRatio: attempted > 0 ? inserted24h / attempted : null
    };
  });
}

import {

} from './jito.js';

const floor: JitoTipFloor = {
  p25: 1_000,
  p50: 10_000,
  p75: 100_000,
  p95: 1_000_000,
  p99: 10_000_000
};

describe('jito tip sizing', () => {
  it('targets the requested percentile', () => {
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor, percentile: 'p50', maxTipLamports: 50_000_000, fallbackTipLamports: 5_000 })
    ).toBe(10_000);
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor, percentile: 'p95', maxTipLamports: 50_000_000, fallbackTipLamports: 5_000 })
    ).toBe(1_000_000);
  });

  it('never exceeds the cap, however high the floor climbs', () => {
    // The cap is the only thing standing between a congestion spike (or a
    // malformed floor response) and unbounded SOL spend per trade.
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor, percentile: 'p95', maxTipLamports: 50_000, fallbackTipLamports: 5_000 })
    ).toBe(50_000);
  });

  it('falls back when the floor is unreadable rather than abandoning the trade', () => {
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor: null, percentile: 'p75', maxTipLamports: 50_000_000, fallbackTipLamports: 7_777 })
    ).toBe(7_777);
  });

  it('treats a zero percentile as no-data, not as free', () => {
    // A zero tip never lands. Reading "0" as a valid tip would silently produce
    // bundles that are never built, which looks identical to a dead executor.
    const zeroFloor: JitoTipFloor = { p25: 0, p50: 0, p75: 0, p95: 0, p99: 0 };
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor: zeroFloor, percentile: 'p50', maxTipLamports: 1_000_000, fallbackTipLamports: 9_000 })
    ).toBe(9_000);
  });

  it('never returns a tip below 1 lamport', () => {
    expect(
      selectJitoTip({ floor, percentile: 'p50', maxTipLamports: 0, fallbackTipLamports: 0 })
    ).toBe(1);
  });

  it('rounds to whole lamports', () => {
    const fractional: JitoTipFloor = { p25: 0, p50: 1234.7, p75: 0, p95: 0, p99: 0 };
    const tip = selectJitoTip({
      floor: fractional,
      percentile: 'p50',
      maxTipLamports: 1_000_000,
      fallbackTipLamports: 1
    });
    expect(Number.isInteger(tip)).toBe(true);
    expect(tip).toBe(1235);
  });
});

describe('tip account selection', () => {
  it('always returns a real tip account', () => {
    // A tip to any other address is simply a donation â€” the bundle is ignored.
    for (const seed of ['a', 'signal-123', '', 'x'.repeat(200)]) {
      expect(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS).toContain(selectTipAccount(seed, JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS));
    }
  });

  it('is deterministic for the same seed and the same set', () => {
    expect(selectTipAccount('signal-42', JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS)).toBe(
      selectTipAccount('signal-42', JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS)
    );
  });

  it('spreads across the account set', () => {
    const seen = new Set(
      Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => selectTipAccount(`signal-${i}`, JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS))
    );
    // Not a uniformity proof â€” just that it is not pinned to one account, which
    // would concentrate load and make the spread pointless.
    expect(seen.size).toBeGreaterThan(1);
  });

  it('picks only from the set it was given, never from the hard-coded one', () => {
    // The whole point of S4-P18: once the live set is resolved at runtime, paying
    // an address that is no longer in it means the block engine ignores the
    // bundle, nothing lands, and the executor still reports success.
    const live = [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1'), fakeTipAccount('LiveTip2')];
    for (const seed of ['a', 'signal-123', '', 'x'.repeat(200)]) {
      const picked = selectTipAccount(seed, live);
      expect(live).toContain(picked);
      expect(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS).not.toContain(picked);
    }
  });

  it('falls back rather than tipping nobody when handed an empty set', () => {
    // `hash % 0` is NaN and the lookup would be undefined â€” a tip transfer to no
    // address at all. `getJitoTipAccounts` never returns empty, but this function
    // is exported and a future caller might.
    expect(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS).toContain(selectTipAccount('signal-1', []));
  });

  it('may pick a different account after the set changes, and that is fine', () => {
    // Determinism is per-set, not absolute: `hash % length` moves when the length
    // does. Nothing downstream keys off *which* tip account was used, only that
    // it is a currently-valid one, and the tip account is chosen once per bundle.
    const seed = 'signal-42';
    const shrunk = JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS.slice(0, 3);
    expect(shrunk).toContain(selectTipAccount(seed, shrunk));
  });
});

/** Base58 without `0`, `O`, `I`, `l`, padded to the 32-char minimum. */
function fakeTipAccount(label: string): string {
  return label.padEnd(32, 'z');
}

const JITO: JitoClientOptions = { baseUrl: 'https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf' };

function stubTipAccountsResponse(body: unknown, init: { ok?: boolean } = {}) {
  const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
    ok: init.ok ?? true,
    json: async () => body
  } as Response);
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);
  return fetchMock;
}

/**
 * The tip-account allowlist is resolved at runtime (checklist S4-P18).
 *
 * It used to be a hard-coded 8-entry array. Jito rotates those addresses, and a
 * stale entry fails in the worst available way: the tip goes to an address the
 * block engine no longer recognises, so the bundle is silently ignored â€” nothing
 * lands, and the executor still reports a successful submission. Nothing in the
 * system notices, which is exactly why these tests exist.
 *
 * The fallback matters just as much in the other direction: an unreadable
 * endpoint must never block an otherwise-valid trade.
 */
describe('tip account resolution', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
    clearJitoTipAccountsCache();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    clearJitoTipAccountsCache();
  });

  it('asks the block engine bundle endpoint for getTipAccounts', async () => {
    const fetchMock = stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);

    const [url, init] = fetchMock.mock.calls[0]!;
    // Verified against Jito's own client (`jito-labs/jito-js-rpc`): tip accounts
    // come from the same `/bundles` JSON-RPC endpoint as `sendBundle`, not from
    // the `bundles.jito.wtf` REST host that serves the tip *floor*.
    expect(url).toBe('https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles');
    expect(init.method).toBe('POST');
    expect(JSON.parse(init.body as string)).toMatchObject({
      jsonrpc: '2.0',
      method: 'getTipAccounts',
      params: []
    });
  });

  it('yields the live set when the endpoint answers', async () => {
    const live = [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1'), fakeTipAccount('LiveTip2')];
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: live });

    const accounts = await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);

    expect(accounts).toEqual(live);
    // A rotation is only picked up if the live answer actually wins.
    expect(accounts).not.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
  });

  it('falls back to the hard-coded set when the endpoint is unreachable', async () => {
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('ECONNREFUSED')));

    // Not an empty set and not a throw: a tip-address lookup must never be the
    // reason an otherwise-valid trade fails to submit.
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
  });

  it('falls back when the endpoint answers with an HTTP error', async () => {
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] }, { ok: false });
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
  });

  it('falls back when the endpoint answers with a JSON-RPC error', async () => {
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ error: { code: -32601, message: 'Method not found' } });
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a non-array result', { result: 'not-an-array' }],
    ['an empty array', { result: [] }],
    ['non-string entries', { result: [123, null, { address: 'x' }] }],
    ['entries that are not base58 addresses', { result: ['0xdeadbeef', 'not an address'] }],
    ['no result at all', {}]
  ])('falls back on a malformed response: %s', async (_label, body) => {
    stubTipAccountsResponse(body);
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
  });

  it('never widens the allowlist with an entry it cannot parse', async () => {
    // This list is a payment allowlist â€” every address in it gets real SOL. A
    // partially-garbage response must contribute only what it can be trusted for.
    const good = fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1');
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [good, 'not an address', 42, `${good}!!!`] });

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual([good]);
  });

  it('deduplicates a repeated address', async () => {
    const good = fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1');
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [good, good] });
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual([good]);
  });

  it('falls back when no block engine is configured, without a request', async () => {
    const fetchMock = stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts({ baseUrl: '  ' })).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
    expect(fetchMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('serves a repeat lookup from cache without a second request', async () => {
    const fetchMock = stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);

    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('shares one in-flight lookup between concurrent callers', async () => {
    // A batch of submits arriving together would otherwise stampede the block
    // engine on every cold cache.
    const fetchMock = stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    await Promise.all([
      getJitoTipAccounts(JITO),
      getJitoTipAccounts(JITO),
      getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)
    ]);

    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('holds a resolved set for exactly the TTL and no longer', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const fetchMock = stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);

    vi.advanceTimersByTime(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS - 1);
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    // One millisecond past the boundary the set is refetched. Without this the
    // cache is just the hard-coded array with extra steps: a rotation that
    // happens after boot would never be observed.
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1);
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('picks up a rotation once the TTL expires', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const rotated = fakeTipAccount('Rotated1');
    const fetchMock = vi
      .fn()
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] }) })
      .mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ result: [rotated] }) });
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);

    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS);

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual([rotated]);
  });

  it('retries a failed resolution sooner than it would refresh a good one', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('ECONNREFUSED'));
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);

    // Held briefly so a misconfigured endpoint does not add a failing round trip
    // to every trade...
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_FALLBACK_TTL_MS - 1);
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    // ...but retried well inside the success TTL, so a transient outage does not
    // pin the executor to a possibly-stale array for five minutes.
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(1);
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);
    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_FALLBACK_TTL_MS).toBeLessThan(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS);
  });

  it('recovers the live set on the retry after a transient outage', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const live = [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')];
    const fetchMock = vi
      .fn()
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('ECONNREFUSED'))
      .mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ result: live }) });
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS);
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_FALLBACK_TTL_MS);

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts(JITO)).resolves.toEqual(live);
  });

  it('sweeps expired entries instead of retaining them forever', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    await getJitoTipAccounts({ baseUrl: 'https://retired.block-engine.test' });
    expect(jitoTipAccountsCacheSize()).toBe(1);

    vi.advanceTimersByTime(JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS + 1);
    // The sweep runs on write, so one unrelated lookup collects the dead entry.
    await getJitoTipAccounts(JITO);

    expect(jitoTipAccountsCacheSize()).toBe(1);
  });

  it('stays bounded when keyed by many distinct endpoints', async () => {
    stubTipAccountsResponse({ result: [fakeTipAccount('LiveTip1')] });

    for (let i = 0; i < JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES + 10; i++) {
      await getJitoTipAccounts({ baseUrl: `https://engine-${i}.test` });
    }

    // The key is operator config today and per-tenant config under fan-out. An
    // unbounded map keyed by anything caller-derived, inside the process that
    // holds the signing key, is the last place to leak memory.
    expect(jitoTipAccountsCacheSize()).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
      JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES
    );
  });

  it('keys the cache per endpoint so one block engine cannot serve another', async () => {
    const first = [fakeTipAccount('Engine1a')];
    const second = [fakeTipAccount('Engine2a')];
    const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((url: string) => ({
      ok: true,
      json: async () => ({ result: url.includes('one') ? first : second })
    }));
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);

    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts({ baseUrl: 'https://one.test' })).resolves.toEqual(first);
    await expect(getJitoTipAccounts({ baseUrl: 'https://two.test' })).resolves.toEqual(second);
  });
});

/**
 * Lamports â†’ USD (checklist S4-P18).
 *
 * This value becomes `feeUsd` on a trade row and feeds cost-basis arithmetic, so
 * a wrong number is strictly worse than a missing one: a missing fee is visibly
 * absent, a wrong fee silently misstates realised P&L forever.
 */
describe('tip pricing', () => {
  it('converts lamports at 10^9 to the SOL price', () => {
    expect(lamportsToUsd(1_000_000_000, 200)).toBe(200);
    expect(lamportsToUsd(20_000, 200)).toBeCloseTo(0.004, 12);
  });

  it('returns null rather than zero when the price is unavailable', () => {
    // `fetchTokenPriceUsd` answers null when every upstream fails. Letting that
    // become a 0 would assert the trade cost nothing, which is a different and
    // false claim.
    expect(lamportsToUsd(20_000, null)).toBe(null);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a zero price', 0],
    ['a negative price', -5],
    ['a NaN price', Number.NaN],
    ['an infinite price', Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]
  ])('returns null for %s', (_label, price) => {
    expect(lamportsToUsd(20_000, price)).toBe(null);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a negative tip', -1],
    ['a NaN tip', Number.NaN],
    ['an infinite tip', Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]
  ])('returns null for %s', (_label, lamports) => {
    expect(lamportsToUsd(lamports, 200)).toBe(null);
  });

  it('prices a zero tip as zero, since no tip really is free', () => {
    // Distinct from `null`: a tip of zero lamports is an observed cost of nothing,
    // not an unknown cost. The runtime never books this â€” `selectJitoTip` floors
    // at 1 lamport â€” but the conversion itself should not lie about it.
    expect(lamportsToUsd(0, 200)).toBe(0);
  });
});

/**
 * Jito block-engine client for atomic bundle submission (DG-1, checklist S3-2).
 *
 * **Why bundles rather than a public RPC broadcast.** A swap broadcast to the
 * public mempool is visible to searchers before it lands, which is precisely the
 * window a sandwich attack needs. A Jito bundle is delivered straight to block
 * builders and lands atomically â€” all transactions or none â€” so there is no
 * partially-executed state to reconcile and no public pre-trade signal.
 *
 * The tip is what buys inclusion: block builders order bundles by tip, so a tip
 * below the current floor is simply never built.
 */

/**
 * Local rather than shared: `jupiter.ts` and `prices.ts` each already carry their
 * own private variant with a different signature, and unifying all three is a
 * refactor of two working call sites that this module does not need.
 */
async function fetchWithTimeout(
  url: string,
  init: RequestInit = {},
  timeoutMs = 10_000
): Promise<Response> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
  try {
    return await fetch(url, { ...init, signal: controller.signal });
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

const LAMPORTS_PER_SOL = 1_000_000_000;

/**
 * Fallback tip accounts â€” **not** the source of truth (checklist S4-P18).
 *
 * A tip must go to one of Jito's *current* tip accounts or the bundle is silently
 * ignored: nothing lands and the executor still reports a successful submission.
 * Jito rotates these addresses, so a hard-coded array is a liveness fuse whose
 * only repair is a code deploy.
 *
 * `getJitoTipAccounts` resolves the live set at runtime and falls back here when
 * it cannot. This array is the floor of that arrangement, kept because an
 * unreadable endpoint must never block an otherwise-valid trade.
 */
export const JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS = [
  '96gYZGLnJYVFmbjzopPSU6QiEV5fGqZNyN9nmNhvrZU5',
  'HFqU5x63VTqvQss8hp11i4wVV8bD44PvwucfZ2bU7gRe',
  'Cw8CFyM9FkoMi7K7Crf6HNQqf4uEMzpKw6QNghXLvLkY',
  'ADaUMid9yfUytqMBgopwjb2DTLSokTSzL1zt6iGPaS49',
  'DfXygSm4jCyNCybVYYK6DwvWqjKee8pbDmJGcLWNDXjh',
  'ADuUkR4vqLUMWXxW9gh6D6L8pMSawimctcNZ5pGwDcEt',
  'DttWaMuVvTiduZRnguLF7jNxTgiMBZ1hyAumKUiL2KRL',
  '3AVi9Tg9Uo68tJfuvoKvqKNWKkC5wPdSSdeBnizKZ6jT'
] as const;

export interface JitoBundleStatus {
  readonly bundleId: string;
  /** `Invalid` means the block engine has never seen this bundle id. */
  readonly status: 'Invalid' | 'Pending' | 'Failed' | 'Landed';
  /** Signatures in the bundle, present once it lands. */
  readonly transactions: readonly string[];
  readonly slot: number | null;
}

export interface JitoClientOptions {
  /** Block-engine base URL, e.g. `https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf`. */
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly apiKey?: string;
  readonly timeoutMs?: number;
}

/**
 * Tip floor percentiles, in **lamports**, as published by the block engine.
 *
 * These move with congestion. Sizing a tip off a hard-coded constant either
 * overpays permanently or silently stops landing when the floor rises.
 */
export interface JitoTipFloor {
  readonly p25: number;
  readonly p50: number;
  readonly p75: number;
  readonly p95: number;
  readonly p99: number;
}

function lamportsFromSol(sol: number): number {
  return Math.round(sol * LAMPORTS_PER_SOL);
}

/**
 * Converts a lamport amount to USD.
 *
 * Returns `null` when the price is unusable rather than substituting a guess.
 * This value becomes `feeUsd` on a trade row and feeds cost-basis arithmetic, so
 * a wrong number is strictly worse than a missing one: a missing fee is visibly
 * absent, a wrong fee silently misstates realised P&L forever.
 */
export function lamportsToUsd(lamports: number, solPriceUsd: number | null): number | null {
  if (!Number.isFinite(lamports) || lamports < 0) return null;
  if (solPriceUsd === null || !Number.isFinite(solPriceUsd) || solPriceUsd <= 0) return null;
  return (lamports / LAMPORTS_PER_SOL) * solPriceUsd;
}

/**
 * Reads the current tip floor.
 *
 * Returns `null` rather than throwing: the caller's correct response to an
 * unreadable floor is to fall back to a configured default tip, not to abandon
 * an otherwise-valid trade.
 */
export async function getJitoTipFloor(
  options: JitoClientOptions
): Promise<JitoTipFloor | null> {
  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(
      'https://bundles.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles/tip_floor',
      {},
      options.timeoutMs ?? 5_000
    );
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const payload = (await response.json()) as Array<Record<string, number>>;
    const row = payload[0];
    if (!row) return null;
    // The endpoint reports SOL; everything downstream works in lamports, and
    // mixing the two would misprice the tip by 10^9.
    return {
      p25: lamportsFromSol(row.landed_tips_25th_percentile ?? 0),
      p50: lamportsFromSol(row.landed_tips_50th_percentile ?? 0),
      p75: lamportsFromSol(row.landed_tips_75th_percentile ?? 0),
      p95: lamportsFromSol(row.landed_tips_95th_percentile ?? 0),
      p99: lamportsFromSol(row.landed_tips_99th_percentile ?? 0)
    };
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export interface TipSizingInput {
  readonly floor: JitoTipFloor | null;
  /** Percentile to target. Higher lands more reliably and costs more. */
  readonly percentile: 'p50' | 'p75' | 'p95';
  /** Hard ceiling from `JITO_MAX_TIP_LAMPORTS`. Never exceeded. */
  readonly maxTipLamports: number;
  /** Used when the floor is unreadable. */
  readonly fallbackTipLamports: number;
}

/**
 * Chooses a tip, bounded by an absolute cap (checklist S3-3).
 *
 * The cap is not advisory. Without it a congestion spike â€” or a malformed floor
 * response reporting an absurd percentile â€” would let the executor spend an
 * unbounded amount of SOL per trade, and the tip is a real cost that counts
 * against position P&L.
 */
export function selectJitoTip(input: TipSizingInput): number {
  const raw = input.floor ? input.floor[input.percentile] : input.fallbackTipLamports;
  // A zero or negative floor means "no data", not "free" â€” a zero tip never lands.
  const candidate = raw > 0 ? raw : input.fallbackTipLamports;
  return Math.max(1, Math.min(Math.round(candidate), input.maxTipLamports));
}

// â”€â”€â”€ Tip-account resolution (checklist S4-P18) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€

/**
 * JSON-RPC method that returns the live tip-account list.
 *
 * **Verified**, not guessed. Jito's own client â€” `jito-labs/jito-js-rpc`,
 * `src/index.ts` â€” implements `getTipAccounts` by posting
 * `{jsonrpc, id, method: 'getTipAccounts', params: []}` to the `/bundles`
 * endpoint, the *same* endpoint its `sendBundle` and `getBundleStatuses` use, on a
 * base URL its examples give as `https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1`.
 * Its README lists the method as "get accounts eligible for tips".
 *
 * The separate `bundles.jito.wtf` REST host that `getJitoTipFloor` reads serves
 * tip *percentiles*, not tip *accounts*, and is not an alternative here.
 */
const TIP_ACCOUNTS_RPC_METHOD = 'getTipAccounts';

/**
 * Resolves the bundle endpoint to ask, or `null` when there is nothing to ask.
 *
 * Derived from the already-configured `JITO_BLOCK_ENGINE_URL` rather than from a
 * tip-account-specific setting. That is deliberate: this list is a payment
 * allowlist, and a second, separately-settable source for it would let anything
 * with environment access redirect every tip this executor pays without touching
 * the block-engine URL an operator actually reviews.
 */
function tipAccountsEndpoint(options: JitoClientOptions): string | null {
  const base = options.baseUrl?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, '') ?? '';
  return base ? `${base}/api/v1/bundles` : null;
}

/** Base58 without the ambiguous characters Solana omits (`0`, `O`, `I`, `l`). */
const BASE58_ADDRESS = /^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/;

/**
 * Keeps only plausible base58 addresses, or `null` if none survive.
 *
 * A tip is an unconditional SOL transfer, so this list is a payment allowlist:
 * anything that lands in it gets paid on every trade until the TTL expires.
 * A malformed or hostile response must therefore never widen it, and a wholly
 * unusable response must resolve to `null` so the caller keeps the known-good
 * fallback rather than an empty set it would then have to special-case.
 */
function sanitizeTipAccounts(values: unknown): readonly string[] | null {
  if (!Array.isArray(values)) return null;
  const accounts = values.filter(
    (value): value is string => typeof value === 'string' && BASE58_ADDRESS.test(value)
  );
  return accounts.length > 0 ? [...new Set(accounts)] : null;
}

/**
 * Reads the live tip-account set.
 *
 * Returns `null` rather than throwing, exactly like `getJitoTipFloor`: the
 * caller's correct response to an unreadable set is the hard-coded fallback, not
 * abandoning the trade.
 */
export async function fetchJitoTipAccounts(
  options: JitoClientOptions
): Promise<readonly string[] | null> {
  const url = tipAccountsEndpoint(options);
  if (!url) return null;

  const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (options.apiKey) headers['x-jito-auth'] = options.apiKey;

  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(
      url,
      {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify({
          jsonrpc: '2.0',
          id: 1,
          method: TIP_ACCOUNTS_RPC_METHOD,
          params: []
        })
      },
      options.timeoutMs ?? 5_000
    );
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const payload = (await response.json()) as { result?: unknown; error?: unknown };
    if (payload.error) return null;
    return sanitizeTipAccounts(payload.result);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** How long a successfully resolved set is trusted. */
export const JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS = 300_000;

/**
 * How long a *failed* resolution is remembered.
 *
 * Shorter than the success TTL so a transient outage recovers quickly, but
 * non-zero so an endpoint that is simply misconfigured does not add a failing
 * round trip to the latency of every single trade.
 */
export const JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_FALLBACK_TTL_MS = 60_000;

/**
 * Hard entry cap, following the `S4-P3` discipline in
 * `packages/db/src/risk-policy.ts`.
 *
 * The key is derived from the block-engine endpoint, which is operator config
 * today and per-tenant config under fan-out. An unbounded module-level `Map`
 * keyed by anything caller-derived is the defect class that fix exists to close,
 * so this one is swept on write and capped â€” 64 distinct endpoints is far past
 * any plausible deployment.
 */
export const JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 64;

interface CachedTipAccounts {
  accounts: readonly string[];
  /** False when this entry is the fallback, which expires sooner. */
  resolved: boolean;
  timestamp: number;
}

const cachedTipAccounts = new Map<string, CachedTipAccounts>();
const tipAccountLoads = new Map<
  string,
  { generation: number; promise: Promise<readonly string[]> }
>();
let tipAccountsGeneration = 0;

function tipAccountsCacheKey(options: JitoClientOptions): string {
  return tipAccountsEndpoint(options) ?? 'unconfigured';
}

function tipAccountsTtlMs(entry: CachedTipAccounts): number {
  return entry.resolved ? JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_TTL_MS : JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_FALLBACK_TTL_MS;
}

/**
 * Drops expired entries, then evicts oldest-first if still over the cap.
 *
 * Eviction is by insertion order, which `Map` preserves â€” a free approximation of
 * LRU, adequate because every entry expires within its TTL anyway. The cap is the
 * backstop for a burst that outruns expiry, not the primary mechanism.
 */
function pruneTipAccountsCache(now: number): void {
  for (const [key, entry] of cachedTipAccounts) {
    if (now - entry.timestamp >= tipAccountsTtlMs(entry)) cachedTipAccounts.delete(key);
  }
  if (cachedTipAccounts.size <= JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES) return;
  const excess = cachedTipAccounts.size - JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES;
  let removed = 0;
  for (const key of cachedTipAccounts.keys()) {
    if (removed >= excess) break;
    cachedTipAccounts.delete(key);
    removed += 1;
  }
}

/**
 * The tip-account set to pay into, resolved at runtime and cached with a TTL.
 *
 * Never returns an empty set and never rejects: an unresolvable endpoint yields
 * `JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS`, so the worst case is the behaviour that shipped before
 * this seam existed. Concurrent callers share one in-flight lookup rather than
 * each firing their own â€” a batch of submits arriving together would otherwise
 * stampede the block engine on every cold cache.
 */
export async function getJitoTipAccounts(
  options: JitoClientOptions
): Promise<readonly string[]> {
  const key = tipAccountsCacheKey(options);
  const cached = cachedTipAccounts.get(key);
  if (cached && Date.now() - cached.timestamp < tipAccountsTtlMs(cached)) {
    return cached.accounts;
  }

  const inFlight = tipAccountLoads.get(key);
  if (inFlight?.generation === tipAccountsGeneration) return inFlight.promise;

  const generation = tipAccountsGeneration;
  const promise = Promise.resolve()
    .then(() => fetchJitoTipAccounts(options))
    // `fetchJitoTipAccounts` already swallows its own failures; this is the
    // backstop for anything it cannot (a `fetch` global that throws
    // synchronously, say). Propagating would fail a trade over a tip-address
    // lookup, which is never the right trade-off.
    .catch(() => null)
    .then((resolved) => {
      const accounts = resolved ?? JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS;
      if (generation === tipAccountsGeneration) {
        const now = Date.now();
        cachedTipAccounts.set(key, { accounts, resolved: resolved !== null, timestamp: now });
        // Swept on write rather than on a timer: a timer keeps the process alive
        // and runs when nothing is being cached, whereas growth only happens here.
        pruneTipAccountsCache(now);
      }
      return accounts;
    });
  tipAccountLoads.set(key, { generation, promise });

  try {
    return await promise;
  } finally {
    if (tipAccountLoads.get(key)?.promise === promise) tipAccountLoads.delete(key);
  }
}

/** Drops every cached set, invalidating in-flight lookups. */
export function clearJitoTipAccountsCache(): void {
  tipAccountsGeneration += 1;
  cachedTipAccounts.clear();
  tipAccountLoads.clear();
}

/** Entry count. Test-only â€” lets a test assert the cache is actually bounded. */
export function jitoTipAccountsCacheSize(): number {
  return cachedTipAccounts.size;
}

/**
 * Deterministically picks one tip account out of a **caller-supplied** set.
 *
 * `accounts` is required, and deliberately has no default (checklist S4-P18).
 * It used to close over `JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS` directly; a default parameter would
 * preserve that for any call site that forgot to pass the live set, and the
 * failure mode is the one this item exists to remove â€” a tip to a rotated-away
 * address means the block engine ignores the bundle, nothing lands, and the
 * executor still reports a successful submission. A required parameter turns that
 * omission into a compile error instead. Pass the result of
 * `getJitoTipAccounts`, which is never empty.
 *
 * **Determinism is per-set, not absolute.** The index is `hash % accounts.length`,
 * so the same seed can map to a different account after a refresh changes the set
 * (or its length). That is intentional and harmless: nothing downstream keys off
 * *which* tip account was used, only that it is a currently-valid one, and the
 * property that does matter â€” one stable account for the single bundle being
 * built, since this is called once per submission â€” is unaffected. A seed-stable
 * mapping across refreshes would be strictly worse, because it could only be
 * achieved by pinning to a set that may already be stale.
 */
export function selectTipAccount(seed: string, accounts: readonly string[]): string {
  // An empty set would make the modulo below produce NaN and the lookup
  // undefined â€” a tip to no one. Fall back rather than emit that.
  const set = accounts.length > 0 ? accounts : JITO_TIP_ACCOUNTS;
  let hash = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < seed.length; i++) {
    hash = (hash * 31 + seed.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
  }
  const index = Math.abs(hash) % set.length;
  return set[index]!;
}

export type JitoSubmitResult =
  | { readonly ok: true; readonly bundleId: string }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: string; readonly retryable: boolean };

/**
 * Submits a bundle of base64 transactions.
 *
 * A failure here is reported honestly and never silently downgraded to a public
 * RPC broadcast (checklist S3-5). Downgrading would reintroduce exactly the
 * front-running exposure bundles exist to remove, and would do so invisibly â€”
 * the operator would believe they were protected.
 */
export async function submitJitoBundle(
  transactionsBase64: readonly string[],
  options: JitoClientOptions
): Promise<JitoSubmitResult> {
  if (transactionsBase64.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'empty-bundle', retryable: false };
  }
  // The block engine caps a bundle at 5 transactions; a larger one is rejected
  // wholesale, so catch it here where the reason is legible.
  if (transactionsBase64.length > 5) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'bundle-too-large', retryable: false };
  }

  const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (options.apiKey) headers['x-jito-auth'] = options.apiKey;

  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(
      `${options.baseUrl}/api/v1/bundles`,
      {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify({
          jsonrpc: '2.0',
          id: 1,
          method: 'sendBundle',
          params: [transactionsBase64, { encoding: 'base64' }]
        })
      },
      options.timeoutMs ?? 10_000
    );

    if (!response.ok) {
      // 429 and 5xx are transient; 4xx is a malformed bundle we must not retry.
      const retryable = response.status === 429 || response.status >= 500;
      const snippet = (await response.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 200);
      return { ok: false, reason: `http-${response.status}: ${snippet}`, retryable };
    }

    const payload = (await response.json()) as {
      result?: string;
      error?: { message?: string };
    };
    if (payload.error) {
      return { ok: false, reason: payload.error.message ?? 'unknown-error', retryable: false };
    }
    if (!payload.result) {
      return { ok: false, reason: 'no-bundle-id', retryable: false };
    }
    return { ok: true, bundleId: payload.result };
  } catch (error) {
    // A timeout is genuinely ambiguous: the bundle may have been received. It is
    // marked retryable, but the caller must reconcile by bundle status rather
    // than blindly resubmitting â€” see the executor's confirmation path.
    return {
      ok: false,
      reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'network-error',
      retryable: true
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Reads bundle status.
 *
 * `null` means the status could not be observed â€” deliberately distinct from
 * `Invalid`, which is a definitive "never seen". Treating an unreachable block
 * engine as `Invalid` would let the executor conclude a submitted bundle failed
 * and re-submit it, double-spending the position.
 */
export async function getJitoBundleStatus(
  bundleId: string,
  options: JitoClientOptions
): Promise<JitoBundleStatus | null> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
  if (options.apiKey) headers['x-jito-auth'] = options.apiKey;

  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(
      `${options.baseUrl}/api/v1/bundles`,
      {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify({
          jsonrpc: '2.0',
          id: 1,
          method: 'getBundleStatuses',
          params: [[bundleId]]
        })
      },
      options.timeoutMs ?? 5_000
    );
    if (!response.ok) return null;

    const payload = (await response.json()) as {
      result?: { value?: Array<{ bundle_id: string; confirmation_status?: string; transactions?: string[]; slot?: number } | null> };
    };
    const entry = payload.result?.value?.[0];
    if (!entry) {
      return { bundleId, status: 'Invalid', transactions: [], slot: null };
    }
    const confirmation = entry.confirmation_status ?? '';
    const status: JitoBundleStatus['status'] =
      confirmation === 'finalized' || confirmation === 'confirmed'
        ? 'Landed'
        : confirmation === 'failed'
          ? 'Failed'
          : 'Pending';
    return {
      bundleId,
      status,
      transactions: entry.transactions ?? [],
      slot: entry.slot ?? null
    };
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
