==> pattern-ml/README.md <==
# Pattern ML

Trade-pattern discovery over KOL (Key Opinion Leader) wallet history on Solana
and Polymarket. Self-contained: it never reads or writes the main SWAT
Postgres.

## Status

| Stage | Command | State |
|---|---|---|
| Check Bitquery schema | `pattern-ml solana-probe` | ready |
| Find unmapped venues | `pattern-ml venue-audit` | ready |
| Source trade history | `pattern-ml pull` | ready |
| Normalize both venues | `pattern-ml index` | ready |
| Reconstruct positions | `pattern-ml positions` | ready |
| Build choice sets | `pattern-ml choice-sets` | ready |
| Train the ranker | `pattern-ml rank` | ready |
| Score live candidates | `pattern-ml score` | ready |
| Backtest with frictions | `pattern-ml validate` | ready |
| Archive a run | `pattern-ml archive` | ready |

Nothing here has run against real data. Syntax and imports are verified; first
contact will surface runtime issues.

## The question this asks

Not *"was this trade good?"* â€” that is answerable only after the KOL has already
acted, which makes you a follower who arrives late. Instead:

> Of the assets competing for this trader's attention at time *t*, why did they
> pick **this** one?

That is a **discrete choice** problem. Each KOL buy becomes a group: the token
they chose, plus the alternatives that were on screen at the same instant. A
learning-to-rank model (LightGBM `lambdarank`) learns to put the chosen one on
top. At serve time you rank today's candidates and act on the leader â€” before
anyone has traded.

Labels are graded, not binary: **2** for the asset bought at *t*, **1** for one
bought within 24h (attractive, just not first), **0** for a genuine rejection.
Assets the KOL traded within Â±5 minutes are dropped entirely â€” three buys in
ninety seconds is one decision about three assets, and scoring two as rejections
would teach the model to reject exactly what this trader likes.

### Where the negatives come from is the whole ballgame

A KOL buying one Solana token did not evaluate 100,000 alternatives. They looked
at a screen holding maybe 10â€“30 names. Draw negatives uniformly from all tokens
and the model learns "is this a real token with volume" â€” trivially true of
every KOL buy, and worth nothing. The `Screen` object *is* the modelling
assumption, and `screen_coverage` measures whether it is the right one.

**Read screen coverage before reading any NDCG number.** It reports what
fraction of real KOL buys the screen would have surfaced. Above ~0.7 the screen
describes the trader; below ~0.4 it does not, and no amount of model tuning
fixes a mis-specified choice set â€” that KOL is sourcing from somewhere
unobservable and should be excluded.

## Setup

Requires Python â‰¥ 3.11, a Helius API key (Solana sourcing) and a Bitquery OAuth
token (Solana opportunity-set reconstruction). Polymarket's Data API is public.
Designed to run on a server â€” at 1â€“2M trades the pull is long and rate-limited.

```bash
cd pattern-ml
./scripts/setup-server.sh
```

That creates an isolated `.venv`, installs everything, seeds `.env` and
`config/kols.yaml` from the examples, and runs the tests. It pulls no data.

Then add your keys to `.env` (the repo-root `../.env` is read as a fallback, so
an existing key need not be duplicated) and list the traders you care about in
`config/kols.yaml`:

```yaml
solana:
  - address: 5Q544fKrFoe6tsEbD7S8EmxGTJYAKtTVhAW5Q5pge4j1
    handle: some-kol
    tags: [memecoin]

polymarket:
  - address: "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
    handle: some-predictor
```

Addresses are bare â€” no `solana:` / `polygon:` prefix, though a prefix pasted
from the main SWAT database is stripped rather than rejected. The Polymarket
address is the trader's proxy wallet, from `polymarket.com/profile/<address>`.

## Running it

```bash
pattern-ml solana-probe          # FIRST: check every Bitquery query is accepted
pattern-ml pull                  # network; long; resumable
pattern-ml index                 # normalize raw dumps into the trade table
pattern-ml venue-audit           # which execution venues aren't recognised yet
pattern-ml positions             # pair entries with exits, produce win/loss labels

pattern-ml choice-sets --chain polymarket --max-decisions 50   # trial run
pattern-ml choice-sets --chain solana --max-decisions 50
pattern-ml rank
pattern-ml rank --drop-kol-features
pattern-ml score --chain solana --venue pump-bonding-curve --top 10

pattern-ml validate              # backtest copying the roster, after frictions
pattern-ml stats                 # what's in the warehouse
```

Start every `choice-sets` run with `--max-decisions 50` and read the screen
coverage table before committing to a full run.

`--drop-kol-features` on `rank` excludes `prior_kol_entries` and
`seconds_since_first_kol_entry`. Those columns are strongest precisely when you
are *latest*. If the model only beats its baselines with them, it learned to
follow, not to anticipate â€” which is the exact failure this project exists to
avoid. Run it both ways and compare.

## What the pipeline actually does

**Sourcing.** Solana goes through Helius's Enhanced Transactions API â€” up to
100 pre-parsed swaps per request, roughly 100Ã— fewer calls than the
per-signature RPC walk the main indexer uses. Polymarket uses `/activity`
rather than `/trades`, which matters: a *winning* Polymarket position usually
closes by redeeming shares at resolution, which emits no trade. Sourcing fills
alone would leave every winner permanently open and bias the labels toward
losers. (`/trades` also defaults to `takerOnly=true`, silently dropping maker
fills.)

**Normalization.** Both venues map onto one trade schema. `price` means
different things per venue â€” USD per token on Solana, implied probability on
Polymarket â€” so anything comparing them must rank-transform rather than use the
raw number. Raw API responses stay immutable in Parquet, so re-running a
normalization rule over 2M trades is free rather than another multi-hour crawl.

**Venue resolution.** Every Solana swap is resolved to the program that held the
market, from the outer and inner instructions. Helius's own `source` label is
not enough: it says "JUPITER" for every routed swap, and cannot distinguish a
Pump.fun bonding curve from PumpSwap. That distinction decides which board gets
reconstructed, so the program id wins and the aggregator is recorded separately
as `router`. `venue-audit` counts program ids in your own data that
`venues.py` does not recognise â€” that is how the registry gets extended, by
observation rather than guesswork.

**Positions.** Trades are folded into round trips using average-cost,
flat-to-flat matching: a position opens on the first buy from zero inventory
and closes when inventory returns to ~zero. This is what produces `is_win` â€”
a single trade has no outcome. Positions still holding inventory are labelled
null and excluded, because the bags a KOL still holds are disproportionately
losers and counting them would inflate every win rate.

**Choice sets.** The core stage. For each KOL buy, the provider reconstructs the
opportunity set as of that instant â€” never later. The two venues have opposite
cost shapes:

| | Polymarket | Solana |
|---|---|---|
| Method | enumerate a catalogue | aggregate a time window |
| Source | Gamma + CLOB + Data API | Bitquery Solana GraphQL |
| Cost | 2 requests **per candidate** per decision | 2 queries **per decision** |
| Routing | one order book | per venue: curve board vs AMM board |

On Solana the venue picks the question. A bonding-curve buy queries curves live
in the window ranked by completion; an AMM buy queries tokens by volume on that
protocol. A Jupiter route into an unrecognised pool widens to all AMMs â€” losing
precision beats dropping the decision.

**Validation.** The backtest models *you copying them*, not them trading: 150
bps slippage per leg, 30 bps fees per side, and positions held under 60 seconds
dropped as un-copyable. It also runs a random-selection null â€” if picking
trades at random from the same roster returns nearly the same, the edge is your
list of traders, not any pattern.

## Lookahead bias

The failure mode this codebase is built against. A leak does not crash anything
â€” it produces an excellent NDCG, a confident model, and losses in production,
with nothing upstream to indicate why. Three defences:

1. **Every query is bounded at the decision instant.** `endTs` on Polymarket
   price history, `end` on its trades, `till` on every Bitquery query. Tests
   intercept every outbound request and assert none ever asks past *t*.
2. **Returned rows are re-filtered anyway.** Never trust a boundary you did not
   enforce yourself.
3. **Unfillable fields are `None`, never zero.** A zero liquidity is a claim; a
   null is an admission. Screens reject nulls, so an unfillable field shrinks
   the opportunity set rather than poisoning it.

The subtlest case is `age_seconds` on Solana. A token that first traded before
the discovery window has a *censored* age, and clamping it to the window length
would manufacture novelty out of an old token â€” the most damaging error
available here, since novelty is exactly what a launchpad trader selects on. It
is recorded as null instead.

Consequently `SolanaScreen`'s age and liquidity gates, and `PolymarketScreen`'s
spread gate, all default to **off**. Gating on a field the reconstruction cannot
fill would reject every candidate; worse, gating on one that live scoring *can*
fill while historical assembly cannot would train and serve from two different
universes.

## Reading the output

Artefacts land in `artifacts/` and are overwritten each run. `pattern-ml
archive` snapshots them to `reports/<UTC-timestamp>/` with a readable
`REPORT.md`, so a past run's claims survive to be checked against what happened
next. `pattern-ml runs` lists archives.

`rank` prints per-fold NDCG@5 and hit@1 against two mandatory baselines: random
ordering and rank-by-volume. Absolute NDCG is unreadable in isolation â€” with 8
candidates per group, random ordering already scores ~0.6. Only the margin
matters, and the verdict requires clearing **both** baselines on **every** fold.
A model that cannot beat "pick the highest-volume candidate" has learned an
expensive sort.

Parquet is compressed binary â€” `cat` gives you nothing useful:

```python
import polars as pl
pl.read_parquet("artifacts/choice_candidates.parquet")
```

```bash
duckdb data/warehouse.duckdb "SELECT * FROM positions WHERE is_win LIMIT 10"
```

## Layout

```
pattern-ml/
```

## Testing

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest
```

Nothing here has been executed against real data yet. The likeliest first
failures:

- **Bitquery query shape.** The GraphQL field names in `sources/bitquery.py`
  were written without network access and Bitquery's Solana schema has moved
  between versions. A renamed field returns an *empty result*, not an error â€”
  which at scale reads as "these KOLs had no alternatives". `solana-probe`
  exists to catch exactly this; run it first.
- DuckDB Arrow registration in `storage.py`.
- The Polymarket window-advance loop.
- Gamma's `clobTokenIds` shape (both string and list are handled).

## On multiple testing

Any pattern claim must correct for how many hypotheses it tested. `stats.py`
provides Benjaminiâ€“Hochberg FDR control and Wilson confidence bounds for that
reason. Testing thousands of candidate patterns at p < 0.05 and keeping the
winners manufactures roughly 100 "significant" findings from 2,000 candidates
with no real edge anywhere. A pattern is only reportable when its whole
confidence interval clears the baseline, not just its point estimate.

# Intentionally does NOT pull data â€” sourcing 1-2M trades is a long,

if ! command -v "$PYTHON" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: $PYTHON not found. Install Python 3.11+ first." >&2
  exit 1
fi

version="$("$PYTHON" -c 'import sys; print("%d.%d" % sys.version_info[:2])')"
major="${version%%.*}"
minor="${version##*.}"
if (( major < 3 || (major == 3 && minor < 11) )); then
  echo "ERROR: Python 3.11+ required, found ${version}." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "    Python ${version}"

# --- Virtualenv ---------------------------------------------------------------

# shellcheck disable=SC1091

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/__init__.py <==
"""Discrete-choice modelling of KOL entries.

The question this package asks
-----------------------------
Not *"was this trade good?"* â€” that is a follower's question, answerable only
after the KOL has already acted. Instead:

    Of the assets competing for this trader's attention at time t,
    why did they pick THIS one?

Framing it as a choice among simultaneously-available alternatives is what
makes the model usable *before* anyone trades: score today's candidates, act on
the top of the ranking.

Why the opportunity set matters more than the model
---------------------------------------------------
A KOL buying one Solana token did not evaluate 100,000 alternatives. They
looked at a screen â€” DexScreener trending, a Pump.fun bonding-curve board, a
Telegram feed â€” holding maybe 10-30 names. The negatives must come from *that*
set. Draw them uniformly from all tokens and the model learns "is this a real
token with volume", which is trivially true of every KOL buy and worth nothing.
Hard negatives from the same screen force it to learn the actual differential.

This makes ``Screen`` the highest-leverage object here: it *is* the modelling
assumption. ``screen_coverage`` measures whether it is the right one, by
checking what fraction of real KOL buys the screen would even have surfaced. A
trader whose buys mostly fail the screen is sourcing elsewhere, and no amount
of model tuning fixes a mis-specified choice set.

Modules
-------
``schema``    choice-set tables, graded relevance levels, the ``Screen`` contract
``assemble``  turn KOL buys + market snapshots into training groups
``snapshot``  the provider protocol, and a forward collector for clean ground truth
``rank``      LightGBM ``lambdarank`` with group-aware temporal validation
"""

from .schema import (
    CANDIDATE_SCHEMA,
    CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA,
    REL_CHOSEN,
    REL_IGNORED,
    REL_LATER,
    PolymarketScreen,
    PumpFunScreen,
    Screen,
    SolanaScreen,
    screen_coverage,
)

__all__ = [
    "CANDIDATE_SCHEMA",
    "CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA",
    "REL_CHOSEN",
    "REL_IGNORED",
    "REL_LATER",
    "PolymarketScreen",
    "PumpFunScreen",
    "Screen",
    "SolanaScreen",
    "screen_coverage",
]

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/assemble.py <==
"""Assemble choice sets: one KOL decision, its alternatives, graded labels.

This is where lookahead bias gets in if it gets in anywhere, so the ordering
of operations matters and is stated explicitly:

1. Take a KOL buy at ``t``. That asset is the positive.
2. Ask the provider for the universe **as of** ``t``. Never later.
3. Apply the screen; keep the top ``max_candidates`` by attention order.
4. Label: chosen = 2, bought-within-24h = 1, everything else = 0.
5. Drop candidates the KOL also traded inside Â±5 minutes â€” those were part of
   the same decision, not rejections of it.
6. If the chosen asset failed the screen, re-insert it and flag the group. A
   group with no positive teaches nothing, and the flag is what
   ``screen_coverage`` counts.

Step 5 is subtle and worth stating plainly: a KOL who buys three tokens in
ninety seconds made one decision about three assets. Scoring two of them as
rejections of the third would teach the model to reject exactly the things this
trader likes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from collections.abc import Mapping
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import polars as pl

from ..schema import SIDE_BUY
from .schema import (
    CANDIDATE_SCHEMA,
    CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA,
    DEFAULT_LATER_WINDOW,
    DEFAULT_SIMULTANEITY_WINDOW,
    REL_CHOSEN,
    REL_IGNORED,
    REL_LATER,
    Screen,
)
from .snapshot import MarketSnapshotProvider

# A group with too few alternatives teaches nothing â€” ranking one item against
# zero others is not a ranking problem.
MIN_CANDIDATES = 3

# A screen per venue, or one screen for everything. The per-venue form exists
# because a launchpad board and an AMM trending list are ranked by different
# things, and forcing one screen across both would describe neither.
ScreenSpec = Screen | Mapping[str, Screen]


def _screen_for(spec: ScreenSpec, venue: str | None) -> Screen | None:
    """Resolve the screen governing one decision.

    A mapping without a match returns ``None``, which drops the decision. That
    is intentional: assembling a launchpad buy against an AMM screen would
    manufacture alternatives the trader never saw, and a silently mis-screened
    group is worse than a missing one.
    """
    if not isinstance(spec, Mapping):
        return spec
    if venue and venue in spec:
        return spec[venue]
    from ..venues import venue_kind

    kind = venue_kind(venue) if venue else None
    if kind and kind in spec:
        return spec[kind]
    return spec.get("*")


def _group_id(kol_address: str, market_id: str, at: datetime) -> str:
    payload = f"{kol_address}|{market_id}|{at.isoformat()}"
    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:24]


def kol_entries(trades: pl.DataFrame, *, chain: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The buys that count as decisions.

    Only *opening* buys: a scale-in on a position already held is not a fresh
    choice among alternatives, it is a follow-through on one already made.
    First-buy-per-(kol, market) approximates that without needing the position
    table, and errs toward fewer, cleaner decisions.
    """
    if trades.is_empty():
        return trades

    buys = trades.filter((pl.col("chain") == chain) & (pl.col("side") == SIDE_BUY))
    if buys.is_empty():
        return buys

    return (
        buys.sort("ts")
        .group_by(["kol_address", "market_id"], maintain_order=True)
        .first()
        .sort("ts")
    )


def _traded_within(
    trades: pl.DataFrame, kol_address: str, at: datetime, window: timedelta
) -> set[str]:
    """Markets this KOL traded inside Â±window of ``at``."""
    if trades.is_empty():
        return set()
    lower, upper = at - window, at + window
    rows = trades.filter(
        (pl.col("kol_address") == kol_address)
        & (pl.col("ts") >= lower)
        & (pl.col("ts") <= upper)
    )
    return set(rows["market_id"].to_list())


def _bought_later(
    trades: pl.DataFrame, kol_address: str, at: datetime, window: timedelta
) -> set[str]:
    """Markets this KOL bought strictly after ``at``, within ``window``."""
    if trades.is_empty():
        return set()
    rows = trades.filter(
        (pl.col("kol_address") == kol_address)
        & (pl.col("side") == SIDE_BUY)
        & (pl.col("ts") > at)
        & (pl.col("ts") <= at + window)
    )
    return set(rows["market_id"].to_list())


def _prior_kol_context(
    trades: pl.DataFrame, market_id: str, at: datetime
) -> tuple[float, float | None]:
    """How much tracked-KOL interest this asset had accumulated *before* ``at``.

    Strictly ``< at``: a trade at exactly ``at`` is simultaneous, not prior, and
    including it would let the model see the very decision it is predicting.

    Note this feature cuts against early entry â€” it is strongest precisely when
    you are latest. Kept because measuring that tradeoff is more useful than
    assuming it, but a model that ranks well *only* with these two columns has
    learned to follow, not to anticipate.
    """
    if trades.is_empty():
        return 0.0, None
    prior = trades.filter(
        (pl.col("market_id") == market_id)
        & (pl.col("side") == SIDE_BUY)
        & (pl.col("ts") < at)
    )
    if prior.is_empty():
        return 0.0, None
    first = prior.select(pl.col("ts").min()).item()
    return float(prior.height), float((at - first).total_seconds())


def build_choice_sets(
    trades: pl.DataFrame,
    provider: MarketSnapshotProvider,
    screen: ScreenSpec,
    *,
    chain: str,
    later_window: timedelta = DEFAULT_LATER_WINDOW,
    simultaneity_window: timedelta = DEFAULT_SIMULTANEITY_WINDOW,
    min_candidates: int = MIN_CANDIDATES,
    max_decisions: int | None = None,
) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame, pl.DataFrame]:
    """Turn KOL buys into ranked training groups.

    ``screen`` is either one ``Screen`` or a mapping keyed by venue name or
    venue kind (``"bonding-curve"``, ``"amm"``), with ``"*"`` as the fallback.

    Returns ``(candidates, choice_sets)`` â€” the per-candidate training matrix
    and one metadata row per decision.
    """
    entries = kol_entries(trades, chain=chain)
    if entries.is_empty():
        return (
            pl.DataFrame(schema=CANDIDATE_SCHEMA),
            pl.DataFrame(schema=CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA),
        )

    if max_decisions:
        entries = entries.head(max_decisions)

    candidate_rows: list[dict] = []
    group_rows: list[dict] = []

    for entry in entries.iter_rows(named=True):
        kol = entry["kol_address"]
        chosen_id = entry["market_id"]
        at = entry["ts"]
        # The venue the KOL actually traded on decides which board gets
        # reconstructed. On Solana this is the whole question; on Polymarket
        # there is one order book and the provider ignores it.
        venue = entry.get("venue")

        active_screen = _screen_for(screen, venue)
        if active_screen is None:
            continue

        universe = provider.candidates_at(at, venue=venue)
        if not universe:
            continue

        # Category gating, when the screen asks for it. A politics specialist
        # was not choosing between an election and a football game, so markets
        # from unrelated categories are phantom alternatives. Enforced here
        # rather than in `Screen.passes`, which sees one candidate at a time and
        # cannot know the chosen market's category.
        if getattr(active_screen, "same_category_only", False):
            chosen_row = next(
                (c for c in universe if c.get("market_id") == chosen_id), None
            )
            chosen_category = chosen_row.get("category") if chosen_row else None
            if chosen_category:
                universe = [
                    c
                    for c in universe
                    if c.get("category") == chosen_category
                    or c.get("market_id") == chosen_id
                ]

        # Screen, then take the top slice by attention order.
        passing = [c for c in universe if active_screen.passes(c)]
        passing.sort(key=active_screen.rank_key, reverse=True)
        passing = passing[: active_screen.max_candidates]

        chosen_passed = any(c.get("market_id") == chosen_id for c in passing)
        if not chosen_passed:
            # The chosen asset was invisible to our screen. Re-insert it so the
            # group has a positive, and flag it â€” a KOL with many such groups is
            # telling you the screen does not describe how they find trades.
            features = provider.features_at(chosen_id, at, venue=venue)
            if features is None:
                continue
            features["market_id"] = chosen_id
            passing.append(features)

        # Simultaneous trades are part of this decision, not rejections of it.
        simultaneous = _traded_within(trades, kol, at, simultaneity_window)
        later = _bought_later(trades, kol, at, later_window)

        kept: list[dict] = []
        for candidate in passing:
            market_id = candidate.get("market_id")
            if not market_id:
                continue
            if market_id != chosen_id and market_id in simultaneous:
                continue
            kept.append(candidate)

        if len(kept) < min_candidates:
            continue

        group_id = _group_id(kol, chosen_id, at)
        n_positive = 0

        for candidate in kept:
            market_id = candidate["market_id"]
            if market_id == chosen_id:
                relevance = REL_CHOSEN
                n_positive += 1
            elif market_id in later:
                relevance = REL_LATER
            else:
                relevance = REL_IGNORED

            prior_entries, since_first = _prior_kol_context(trades, market_id, at)

            row = {
                "group_id": group_id,
                "chain": chain,
                "kol_address": kol,
                "decided_at": at,
                "market_id": market_id,
                "market_label": candidate.get("market_label"),
                "outcome": candidate.get("outcome"),
                "venue": venue,
                "category": candidate.get("category"),
                "relevance": relevance,
                "chosen": market_id == chosen_id,
                "snapshot_source": candidate.get("snapshot_source", provider.source),
                "snapshot_at": candidate.get("snapshot_at", at),
                "prior_kol_entries": prior_entries,
                "seconds_since_first_kol_entry": since_first,
            }
            # Copy only declared feature columns â€” an unexpected key from a
            # provider must never silently become a model input.
            for column in CANDIDATE_SCHEMA:
                if column not in row and column in candidate:
                    row[column] = candidate[column]
            candidate_rows.append(row)

        group_rows.append(
            {
                "group_id": group_id,
                "chain": chain,
                "kol_address": kol,
                "kol_handle": entry.get("kol_handle"),
                "decided_at": at,
                "chosen_market_id": chosen_id,
                "venue": venue,
                "n_candidates": len(kept),
                "n_positive": n_positive,
                "screen_name": active_screen.name,
                "snapshot_source": provider.source,
                "chosen_passed_screen": chosen_passed,
            }
        )

    if not candidate_rows:
        return (
            pl.DataFrame(schema=CANDIDATE_SCHEMA),
            pl.DataFrame(schema=CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA),
        )

    from ..schema import conform

    return (
        conform(pl.DataFrame(candidate_rows, infer_schema_length=None, strict=False),
                CANDIDATE_SCHEMA),
        conform(pl.DataFrame(group_rows, infer_schema_length=None, strict=False),
                CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA),
    )

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/providers/__init__.py <==
"""Snapshot providers, one per venue.

Each implements ``choice.snapshot.MarketSnapshotProvider``: given an instant,
return the assets that were plausibly on screen, with every feature computed
strictly as-of that instant.

The two differ in shape, not just in vendor:

* **Polymarket** enumerates. The live universe is hundreds of markets, so the
  provider walks a catalogue and prices each candidate individually â€” two
  requests per candidate per decision.
* **Solana** aggregates. There is no enumerable universe, so the provider asks
  Bitquery a question about a time window and gets back both the candidate set
  and its features â€” two queries per *decision*, whatever the candidate count.

The Solana path is venue-routed: a Pump.fun bonding-curve buy and a Raydium buy
at the same instant were made in front of different boards, so
``candidates_at`` takes the venue resolved from the trade's program ids.
"""

from .polymarket import PolymarketMarket, PolymarketSnapshotProvider
from .solana import SolanaSnapshotProvider, curve_completion

__all__ = [
    "PolymarketMarket",
    "PolymarketSnapshotProvider",
    "SolanaSnapshotProvider",
    "curve_completion",
]

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/providers/polymarket.py <==
"""Point-in-time market snapshots for Polymarket.

Why this venue is tractable and Solana is not
---------------------------------------------
Two properties make historical reconstruction genuinely possible here:

1. The live universe is hundreds of markets, not a hundred thousand tokens, so
   the opportunity set is close to enumerable rather than approximated.
2. The CLOB price-history endpoint accepts absolute ``startTs``/``endTs`` with
   minute ``fidelity``, so a candidate's state at any past minute can be read
   directly. Solana has no free equivalent.

The one hazard, and how it is handled
-------------------------------------
Gamma's ``/markets`` returns **current** state: today's volume, today's
liquidity, whether it has since resolved. Using those fields as-of a past
timestamp would be textbook lookahead bias â€” the model would learn which
markets ended up busy, which is unknowable at decision time.

So Gamma is used only for facts that cannot change after creation:

* ``condition_id``, ``question``, ``slug``
* category / tags
* ``created_at``, ``end_date``

Everything dynamic â€” price, volume, spread, momentum â€” is derived from price
history windows that **end at the decision instant**. A market that had not
been created by ``at``, or that had already resolved, is excluded outright: it
could not have been on screen.

Cost note
---------
One price-history call per candidate per decision. With ~50 candidates and a
few thousand decisions that is six figures of requests, which is why
``SnapshotCache`` keys by minute and why ``max_candidates`` on the screen is
enforced *before* features are fetched, not after.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any

import httpx

from ..snapshot import SOURCE_RECONSTRUCTED

GAMMA_API = "https://gamma-api.polymarket.com"
CLOB_API = "https://clob.polymarket.com"
DATA_API = "https://data-api.polymarket.com"

# Gamma pages at 100; the active universe is small enough to walk fully.
MARKETS_PAGE_LIMIT = 100

# Minute resolution. Finer would multiply cost for detail the screen cannot
# resolve, and matches what the endpoint reliably serves over long windows.
PRICE_FIDELITY_MINUTES = 1

# Lookback windows for momentum features, all ending at the decision instant.
WINDOW_5M = timedelta(minutes=5)
WINDOW_1H = timedelta(hours=1)
WINDOW_24H = timedelta(hours=24)


def _epoch(ts: datetime) -> int:
    return int(ts.astimezone(timezone.utc).timestamp())


def _parse_iso(value: Any) -> datetime | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _f(value: Any) -> float | None:
    """Coerce API numerics, which arrive as both strings and numbers."""
    if value is None or value == "":
        return None
    try:
        out = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return out if out == out else None  # drop NaN


def _first_token_id(market: dict) -> str | None:
    """The YES token id, which is what price history is keyed by.

    ``clobTokenIds`` arrives as either a JSON-encoded string or a real list
    depending on endpoint and era, so both are handled.
    """
    raw = market.get("clobTokenIds")
    if isinstance(raw, str):
        import json

        try:
            raw = json.loads(raw)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if isinstance(raw, list) and raw:
        return str(raw[0])
    return None


@dataclass
class PolymarketMarket:
    """Immutable facts about a market â€” safe to read from current Gamma state."""

    condition_id: str
    token_id: str | None
    question: str | None
    slug: str | None
    category: str | None
    created_at: datetime | None
    end_date: datetime | None

    def existed_at(self, at: datetime) -> bool:
        """Was this market tradeable at ``at``?

        Excludes markets created later (could not be on screen) and markets
        already resolved (no longer on screen). Both would be phantom
        alternatives the trader never actually faced.
        """
        if self.created_at and self.created_at > at:
            return False
        if self.end_date and self.end_date <= at:
            return False
        return True


@dataclass
class PolymarketSnapshotProvider:
    """Reconstructs the Polymarket opportunity set at a past instant."""

    chain: str = "polymarket"
    source: str = SOURCE_RECONSTRUCTED
    timeout: float = 30.0
    max_rps: float = 15.0
    # Filled lazily on first use and reused across decisions â€” the market
    # catalogue is stable, and re-walking it per decision would dominate cost.
    _catalogue: dict[str, PolymarketMarket] = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    _client: httpx.Client | None = field(default=None, repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = httpx.Client(
                timeout=httpx.Timeout(self.timeout), follow_redirects=True
            )

    # -- lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------------

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._client is not None:
            self._client.close()
            self._client = None

    def __enter__(self) -> "PolymarketSnapshotProvider":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()

    @property
    def client(self) -> httpx.Client:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = httpx.Client(
                timeout=httpx.Timeout(self.timeout), follow_redirects=True
            )
        return self._client

    # -- catalogue ----------------------------------------------------------

    def load_catalogue(self, *, max_markets: int = 5_000) -> dict[str, PolymarketMarket]:
        """Walk Gamma once for the immutable facts about every market.

        Deliberately reads *closed* markets too: a market that has resolved
        since was still a live alternative back at the decision instant, and
        omitting those would shrink historical choice sets to only the markets
        that happen to still be open today â€” a subtle survivorship bias in the
        universe itself.
        """
        if self._catalogue:
            return self._catalogue

        catalogue: dict[str, PolymarketMarket] = {}
        offset = 0
        while offset < max_markets:
            params = {
                "limit": MARKETS_PAGE_LIMIT,
                "offset": offset,
                # No `active`/`closed` filter, for the reason above.
                "order": "startDate",
                "ascending": "false",
            }
            try:
                response = self.client.get(f"{GAMMA_API}/markets", params=params)
                response.raise_for_status()
                page = response.json()
            except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
                break

            rows = page if isinstance(page, list) else page.get("data") or []
            if not rows:
                break

            for row in rows:
                if not isinstance(row, dict):
                    continue
                condition_id = row.get("conditionId")
                if not condition_id:
                    continue
                catalogue[condition_id] = PolymarketMarket(
                    condition_id=condition_id,
                    token_id=_first_token_id(row),
                    question=row.get("question"),
                    slug=row.get("slug"),
                    category=row.get("category"),
                    created_at=_parse_iso(row.get("startDate"))
                    or _parse_iso(row.get("createdAt")),
                    end_date=_parse_iso(row.get("endDate")),
                )

            if len(rows) < MARKETS_PAGE_LIMIT:
                break
            offset += MARKETS_PAGE_LIMIT

        self._catalogue = catalogue
        return catalogue

    # -- price history ------------------------------------------------------

    def _price_history(
        self, token_id: str, start: datetime, end: datetime
    ) -> list[dict[str, float]]:
        """Price points in ``[start, end]``.

        ``endTs`` is the leakage boundary for this entire module. It must never
        exceed the decision instant, and every caller passes ``at`` directly.
        """
        params = {
            "market": token_id,
            "startTs": _epoch(start),
            "endTs": _epoch(end),
            "fidelity": PRICE_FIDELITY_MINUTES,
        }
        try:
            response = self.client.get(f"{CLOB_API}/prices-history", params=params)
            response.raise_for_status()
            payload = response.json()
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
            return []

        history = payload.get("history") if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload
        if not isinstance(history, list):
            return []

        points: list[dict[str, float]] = []
        for entry in history:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            ts = _f(entry.get("t"))
            price = _f(entry.get("p"))
            if ts is None or price is None:
                continue
            # Defence in depth: drop anything at or after the boundary even if
            # the API returns it. A single leaked point is a leaked feature.
            if ts >= _epoch(end):
                continue
            points.append({"t": ts, "p": price})
        return sorted(points, key=lambda p: p["t"])

    # -- feature derivation -------------------------------------------------

    def _features_from_history(
        self, points: list[dict[str, float]], at: datetime
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        """Momentum and activity features from a price series ending at ``at``.

        Polymarket's public history gives price, not size, so true traded
        volume is not derivable here. ``trades_5m`` counts *price observations*,
        which is a proxy for activity â€” a market printing many distinct prices
        is being traded. It is explicitly not a dollar volume, and the volume
        fields stay ``None`` rather than being filled with a fabrication.
        """
        if not points:
            return {
                "price": None,
                "price_change_5m": None,
                "price_change_1h": None,
                "trades_5m": None,
                "volume_5m_usd": None,
                "volume_1h_usd": None,
                "volume_24h_usd": None,
            }

        latest = points[-1]["p"]
        cutoff_5m = _epoch(at - WINDOW_5M)
        cutoff_1h = _epoch(at - WINDOW_1H)

        def price_at_or_before(cutoff: int) -> float | None:
            earlier = [p["p"] for p in points if p["t"] <= cutoff]
            return earlier[-1] if earlier else None

        price_5m_ago = price_at_or_before(cutoff_5m)
        price_1h_ago = price_at_or_before(cutoff_1h)

        return {
            "price": latest,
            # Absolute probability change, not percentage: a move from 0.02 to
            # 0.04 is +100% but only two points of probability, and the point
            # difference is what a trader reads.
            "price_change_5m": (latest - price_5m_ago) if price_5m_ago is not None else None,
            "price_change_1h": (latest - price_1h_ago) if price_1h_ago is not None else None,
            "trades_5m": float(sum(1 for p in points if p["t"] > cutoff_5m)),
            "volume_5m_usd": None,
            "volume_1h_usd": None,
            "volume_24h_usd": None,
        }

    # -- traded volume ------------------------------------------------------

    def _volume_windows(
        self, condition_id: str, at: datetime
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        """Real traded volume in the 5m / 1h / 24h windows ending at ``at``.

        Derived from the public Data API's ``/trades``, filtered to the market
        and bounded by ``end=at``. This is the honest source: Gamma's ``volume``
        field is *current* cumulative volume, and using it as-of a past instant
        would tell the model which markets ended up busy â€” unknowable at
        decision time and a guaranteed leak.

        One request covers all three windows: fetch 24h of fills once and
        bucket locally, rather than three calls per candidate.

        ``limit`` is 10000 â€” the documented maximum for ``/trades``, which is
        20x the ``/activity`` cap. At that size a single request covers the full
        24h of fills for all but the very busiest markets, so the volume figure
        is accurate rather than the floor a 500-row page would have produced.
        """
        params = {
            "market": condition_id,
            "limit": 10_000,
            "takerOnly": "false",  # spec default is true; maker fills are volume too
            # Spec: "rows newer than `end` are excluded". This is the leakage
            # boundary. Market-scoped requests keep a ~3-year floor, so `start`
            # can only narrow the window here â€” never widen it past `end`.
            "start": _epoch(at - WINDOW_24H),
            "end": _epoch(at),
        }
        try:
            response = self.client.get(f"{DATA_API}/trades", params=params)
            response.raise_for_status()
            payload = response.json()
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError):
            return {"volume_5m_usd": None, "volume_1h_usd": None, "volume_24h_usd": None}

        rows = payload if isinstance(payload, list) else payload.get("items") or []
        if not isinstance(rows, list):
            return {"volume_5m_usd": None, "volume_1h_usd": None, "volume_24h_usd": None}

        boundary = _epoch(at)
        cutoff_5m = _epoch(at - WINDOW_5M)
        cutoff_1h = _epoch(at - WINDOW_1H)
        totals = {"volume_5m_usd": 0.0, "volume_1h_usd": 0.0, "volume_24h_usd": 0.0}
        buyers: set[str] = set()
        buys = sells = 0

        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, dict):
                continue
            ts = _f(row.get("timestamp"))
            size = _f(row.get("size"))
            price = _f(row.get("price"))
            if ts is None or size is None or price is None:
                continue
            # The API is asked for end=at, but never trust a boundary you did
            # not enforce yourself.
            if ts >= boundary:
                continue

            notional = size * price
            totals["volume_24h_usd"] += notional
            if ts > cutoff_1h:
                totals["volume_1h_usd"] += notional
            if ts > cutoff_5m:
                totals["volume_5m_usd"] += notional
                wallet = row.get("proxyWallet")
                side = (row.get("side") or "").upper()
                if side == "BUY":
                    buys += 1
                    if wallet:
                        buyers.add(str(wallet))
                elif side == "SELL":
                    sells += 1

        # At limit=10000 a truncated 24h window is possible only for the very
        # busiest markets. Recorded as-is: it preserves the ordering the screen
        # uses, and paging every candidate would multiply cost several fold for
        # a number used only to rank attention.
        result: dict[str, float | None] = dict(totals)
        result["unique_buyers_5m"] = float(len(buyers)) if buyers else 0.0
        result["buy_sell_ratio_5m"] = (buys / sells) if sells else (float(buys) if buys else None)
        return result

    # -- provider protocol --------------------------------------------------

    def candidates_at(
        self, at: datetime, *, limit: int = 200, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict]:
        """The opportunity set at ``at``.

        ``venue`` is accepted for protocol compatibility and ignored: Polymarket
        has one order book, so there is no second board a trader could have been
        looking at instead.

        Note the cost shape: this fetches price history per candidate, so
        ``limit`` should stay close to the screen's ``max_candidates`` rather
        than being set generously.
        """
        catalogue = self.load_catalogue()
        live = [m for m in catalogue.values() if m.existed_at(at) and m.token_id]

        candidates: list[dict] = []
        for market in live[:limit]:
            row = self._candidate_row(market, at)
            if row is not None:
                candidates.append(row)
        return candidates

    def features_at(
        self, market_id: str, at: datetime, *, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> dict | None:
        """Point-in-time features for one market, by condition id."""
        catalogue = self.load_catalogue()
        market = catalogue.get(market_id)
        if market is None or not market.token_id:
            return None
        return self._candidate_row(market, at)

    def _candidate_row(self, market: PolymarketMarket, at: datetime) -> dict | None:
        assert market.token_id is not None
        points = self._price_history(market.token_id, at - WINDOW_24H, at)
        if not points:
            # No observable price means it was not visibly trading. Returning a
            # row of nulls would add a candidate the screen then rejects anyway.
            return None

        features = self._features_from_history(points, at)
        volumes = self._volume_windows(market.condition_id, at)
        age = (at - market.created_at).total_seconds() if market.created_at else None

        # Spread needs an order-book snapshot, which has no historical endpoint.
        # Left null: PolymarketScreen rejects nulls, so a spread-gated screen is
        # only usable live. Use `max_spread_pct=None`-equivalent screens for
        # historical assembly, or supply a provider that fills it.
        return {
            "market_id": market.condition_id,
            "market_label": market.question,
            "outcome": "Yes",  # history is keyed on the YES token
            "category": market.category,
            "age_seconds": age,
            "liquidity_usd": None,
            "spread_pct": None,
            "holder_count": None,
            "top10_holder_pct": None,
            "snapshot_source": self.source,
            "snapshot_at": at.isoformat(),
            **features,
            # Volume windows overwrite the null placeholders in `features`.
            **volumes,
        }

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/providers/solana.py <==
"""Point-in-time market snapshots for Solana, reconstructed via Bitquery.

The reconstruction, in one paragraph
------------------------------------
A KOL's swap is first resolved to the program that held the market (see
``pattern_ml.venues``). That program decides which question to ask about the
ten minutes before the trade:

* **Bonding curve** (Pump.fun, Moonshot, LaunchLab) â€” which curves were live and
  how far along were they? A trader watching a launchpad board is choosing among
  curves by completion, not by dollar volume.
* **AMM / CLMM** (Raydium, Meteora, Orca, PumpSwap) â€” which tokens had real
  volume on that protocol in the window? A trader on a trending board is
  choosing among names that were moving.
* **Aggregator only** (a Jupiter route into a pool the registry does not know) â€”
  fall back to the union of all AMM programs. Losing venue precision is better
  than dropping the decision.

Cost, versus the Polymarket path
--------------------------------
Polymarket costs two HTTP requests *per candidate per decision*. Here the
aggregation happens server-side: two queries per **decision** return fifty
candidates with volume, trade count, unique buyers and price already computed.
That is the difference between a run that is merely expensive and one that is
not worth starting.

What is *not* filled, and why that is deliberate
------------------------------------------------
``age_seconds`` is real only when a token's first trade falls *inside* the
query window. Outside it the value is censored â€” "older than ten minutes" â€”
and censored is recorded as ``None``, never as the window length. A censored
age silently clamped to the window would be a feature that means one thing in
training and another at serve time.

``liquidity_usd`` needs pool-state rows, which cost an extra query per program
per decision. Off by default (``fetch_liquidity=True`` enables it). Bonding
curves get it for free, because curve state *is* the pool state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any

from ...schema import SOLANA_QUOTE_MINTS
from ...sources.bitquery import BitqueryClient, BitqueryError
from ...venues import (
    BY_VENUE,
    KIND_AMM,
    KIND_BONDING_CURVE,
    KIND_CLMM,
    PROGRAMS,
    venue_kind,
)
from ..snapshot import SOURCE_RECONSTRUCTED

# The spec's window: what was active on this protocol in the ten minutes before
# the trade. Long enough that a quiet minute does not empty the board, short
# enough that it still describes the screen at that moment.
DISCOVERY_WINDOW = timedelta(minutes=10)

# Feature windows. Both end at the decision instant.
WINDOW_5M = timedelta(minutes=5)
WINDOW_1H = timedelta(hours=1)

# Pump.fun curve arithmetic. A curve starts full and drains as people buy, so a
# *lower* remaining balance means a *more* complete curve. These two constants
# are the documented Bitquery values for launch and graduation; everything else
# (completion percentage, filter bands) is derived from them so a correction
# only has to be made once.
PUMP_CURVE_INITIAL_TOKENS = 793_100_000.0
PUMP_CURVE_GRADUATION_REMAINING = 206_900_000.0

# Every program that holds a market itself, as opposed to routing to one.
AMM_PROGRAM_ADDRESSES: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(
    p.address for p in PROGRAMS if p.kind in (KIND_AMM, KIND_CLMM)
)


def _f(value: Any) -> float | None:
    if value is None or value == "":
        return None
    try:
        out = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return out if out == out else None  # drop NaN


def _parse_time(value: Any) -> datetime | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        return None
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def curve_completion(remaining: float | None) -> float | None:
    """How far a bonding curve has progressed, as a fraction in [0, 1].

    0.0 is a fresh launch, 1.0 is graduation to an AMM. This is the bonding-curve
    analogue of "how hot is this" â€” a board watcher reads completion, not volume,
    because a curve at 90% is minutes from migrating.
    """
    if remaining is None:
        return None
    span = PUMP_CURVE_INITIAL_TOKENS - PUMP_CURVE_GRADUATION_REMAINING
    if span <= 0:
        return None
    progressed = (PUMP_CURVE_INITIAL_TOKENS - remaining) / span
    return max(0.0, min(1.0, progressed))


def remaining_for_completion(completion: float) -> float:
    """Inverse of :func:`curve_completion` â€” the balance at a given progress."""
    span = PUMP_CURVE_INITIAL_TOKENS - PUMP_CURVE_GRADUATION_REMAINING
    return PUMP_CURVE_INITIAL_TOKENS - (completion * span)


def _age_seconds(
    first_seen: datetime | None, window_start: datetime, at: datetime
) -> float | None:
    """Token age, or ``None`` when the window censored it.

    If the earliest trade Bitquery reports sits at (or before) the window edge,
    the token was already trading before we started looking and its true age is
    unknown. Returning the window length instead would invent a young token out
    of an old one â€” the single most damaging thing this module could do, since
    novelty is exactly what a launchpad trader selects on.
    """
    if first_seen is None:
        return None
    if first_seen <= window_start:
        return None
    return max(0.0, (at - first_seen).total_seconds())


@dataclass
class SolanaSnapshotProvider:
    """Reconstructs the Solana opportunity set at a past instant.

    ``venue`` is passed per call rather than fixed on the provider: one KOL's
    history spans launchpads and AMMs, and each decision must be scored against
    the board the trader was actually on.
    """

    chain: str = "solana"
    source: str = SOURCE_RECONSTRUCTED
    discovery_window: timedelta = DISCOVERY_WINDOW
    # Minimum curve progress to count as "on the board". A curve at 3% is not
    # competing for attention with one about to migrate.
    min_curve_completion: float = 0.70
    # Pool-state rows for liquidity cost one extra query per program per
    # decision. Off by default; see the module docstring.
    fetch_liquidity: bool = False
    candidate_limit: int = 50
    _client: BitqueryClient | None = field(default=None, repr=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self._client is None:
            from ...config import get_settings

            self._client = BitqueryClient(max_rps=get_settings().bitquery_max_rps)

    # -- lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------------

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._client is not None:
            self._client.close()
            self._client = None

    def __enter__(self) -> "SolanaSnapshotProvider":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()

    @property
    def client(self) -> BitqueryClient:
        if self._client is None:
            from ...config import get_settings

            self._client = BitqueryClient(max_rps=get_settings().bitquery_max_rps)
        return self._client

    # -- provider protocol --------------------------------------------------

    def candidates_at(
        self, at: datetime, *, limit: int = 200, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict]:
        """The opportunity set at ``at``, routed by venue.

        Never queries past ``at``: every window below is ``[at - w, at]``.
        """
        kind = venue_kind(venue) if venue else None
        cap = min(limit, self.candidate_limit)

        try:
            if kind == KIND_BONDING_CURVE:
                rows = self._bonding_curve_candidates(at, venue, cap)
            else:
                rows = self._amm_candidates(at, venue, cap)
        except BitqueryError:
            # One failed snapshot drops one decision. Raising would abandon a
            # run that may already have assembled thousands of usable groups.
            return []
        return rows[:cap]

    def features_at(
        self, market_id: str, at: datetime, *, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> dict | None:
        """Point-in-time features for one mint â€” the re-insertion path.

        Called when a KOL's chosen token failed the screen, so the group still
        gets its positive. Uses the 1h window rather than the discovery window:
        a token that failed the screen is by definition thin, and the shorter
        window would often return nothing at all.
        """
        try:
            row = self.client.token_window(
                since=at - WINDOW_1H, till=at, mint=market_id
            )
        except BitqueryError:
            return None
        if not row:
            return None
        return self._trade_row_to_candidate(row, at, window_start=at - WINDOW_1H)

    # -- AMM path -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _programs_for(self, venue: str | None) -> list[str]:
        """Which program addresses to query for a venue.

        An unknown or aggregator-only venue widens to every AMM: the trade was
        routed somewhere we could not name, and a broad universe is a better
        approximation of the board than no universe at all.
        """
        if venue:
            program = BY_VENUE.get(venue)
            if program is not None and not program.is_aggregator:
                return [program.address]
        return list(AMM_PROGRAM_ADDRESSES)

    def _amm_candidates(
        self, at: datetime, venue: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[dict]:
        programs = self._programs_for(venue)
        window_start = at - self.discovery_window

        # Query 1 â€” the board itself, ranked by volume over the discovery window.
        discovery = self.client.top_by_volume(
            since=window_start, till=at, programs=programs, limit=limit
        )
        if not discovery:
            return []

        # Query 2 â€” the same programs over an hour, for slower-moving context.
        # Deliberately a wider limit so tokens ranked highly over 10 minutes are
        # still present in the hourly ranking; anything that misses stays null.
        try:
            hourly = self.client.top_by_volume(
                since=at - WINDOW_1H, till=at, programs=programs, limit=limit * 4
            )
        except BitqueryError:
            hourly = []
        hourly_volume = {
            mint: _f(row.get("volume_usd"))
            for row in hourly
            if (mint := _mint_of_trade(row))
        }

        liquidity = self._liquidity_by_mint(at, programs) if self.fetch_liquidity else {}

        candidates: list[dict] = []
        for row in discovery:
            candidate = self._trade_row_to_candidate(row, at, window_start=window_start)
            if candidate is None:
                continue
            mint = candidate["market_id"]
            candidate["volume_1h_usd"] = hourly_volume.get(mint)
            if liquidity:
                candidate["liquidity_usd"] = liquidity.get(mint)
            candidates.append(candidate)
        return candidates

    def _trade_row_to_candidate(
        self, row: dict, at: datetime, *, window_start: datetime
    ) -> dict | None:
        """One ``DEXTradeByTokens`` row â†’ one candidate."""
        trade = row.get("Trade")
        if not isinstance(trade, dict):
            return None
        currency = trade.get("Currency")
        if not isinstance(currency, dict):
            return None
        mint = currency.get("MintAddress")
        if not mint:
            return None
        # Both sides of every swap appear in this aggregation, so SOL and the
        # stablecoins come back as "tokens". They are the unit of account, not
        # opportunities, and would otherwise top every board by volume.
        if mint in SOLANA_QUOTE_MINTS:
            return None

        dex = trade.get("Dex") if isinstance(trade.get("Dex"), dict) else {}
        price_last = _f(row.get("price_last"))
        price_first = _f(row.get("price_first"))
        first_seen = _parse_time(row.get("first_seen"))

        return {
            "market_id": str(mint),
            "market_label": currency.get("Symbol") or currency.get("Name"),
            "outcome": None,
            "venue": dex.get("ProtocolName"),
            "category": None,
            "age_seconds": _age_seconds(first_seen, window_start, at),
            "price": price_last,
            # Percentage move: unlike a Polymarket probability, a token price
            # has no natural scale, so only the relative change is comparable
            # across candidates.
            "price_change_5m": (
                (price_last - price_first) / price_first
                if price_last is not None and price_first
                else None
            ),
            "price_change_1h": None,
            "volume_5m_usd": _f(row.get("volume_usd")),
            "volume_1h_usd": None,
            "volume_24h_usd": None,
            "trades_5m": _f(row.get("trades")),
            "unique_buyers_5m": _f(row.get("buyers")),
            "buy_sell_ratio_5m": None,
            "liquidity_usd": None,
            "curve_completion": None,
            "holder_count": None,
            "top10_holder_pct": None,
            "spread_pct": None,
            "snapshot_source": self.source,
            "snapshot_at": at.isoformat(),
        }

    def _liquidity_by_mint(
        self, at: datetime, programs: list[str]
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Pool-side liquidity, one query per program. Opt-in; see the docstring."""
        out: dict[str, float] = {}
        for program in programs:
            try:
                pools = self.client.pool_creations(
                    since=at - self.discovery_window,
                    till=at,
                    program=program,
                    limit=self.candidate_limit * 2,
                )
            except BitqueryError:
                continue
            for row in pools:
                pool = row.get("Pool")
                if not isinstance(pool, dict):
                    continue
                mint = _mint_of_pool(pool)
                quote = pool.get("Quote") if isinstance(pool.get("Quote"), dict) else {}
                value = _f(quote.get("PostAmountInUSD"))
                if mint and value is not None:
                    # Latest state in the window wins.
                    out[mint] = value
        return out

    # -- bonding-curve path -------------------------------------------------

    def _bonding_curve_candidates(
        self, at: datetime, venue: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[dict]:
        program = BY_VENUE.get(venue or "pump-bonding-curve")
        if program is None:
            return []

        window_start = at - self.discovery_window
        rows = self.client.bonding_curves(
            since=window_start,
            till=at,
            program=program.address,
            # A *more* complete curve has a *lower* remaining balance, so the
            # completion floor becomes the upper bound on remaining tokens.
            min_remaining=PUMP_CURVE_GRADUATION_REMAINING,
            max_remaining=remaining_for_completion(self.min_curve_completion),
            limit=limit * 2,  # deduped below, so over-fetch a little
        )

        # A curve emits a row per state change; keep only the last one before
        # `at`, which is what the board would have shown.
        latest: dict[str, tuple[datetime, dict]] = {}
        for row in rows:
            observed = _parse_time((row.get("Block") or {}).get("Time"))
            if observed is None or observed > at:
                continue
            pool = row.get("Pool")
            if not isinstance(pool, dict):
                continue
            mint = _mint_of_pool(pool)
            if not mint:
                continue
            existing = latest.get(mint)
            if existing is None or observed > existing[0]:
                latest[mint] = (observed, pool)

        candidates: list[dict] = []
        for mint, (observed, pool) in latest.items():
            base = pool.get("Base") if isinstance(pool.get("Base"), dict) else {}
            quote = pool.get("Quote") if isinstance(pool.get("Quote"), dict) else {}
            market = pool.get("Market") if isinstance(pool.get("Market"), dict) else {}
            currency = (
                market.get("BaseCurrency")
                if isinstance(market.get("BaseCurrency"), dict)
                else {}
            )
            completion = curve_completion(_f(base.get("PostAmount")))

            candidates.append(
                {
                    "market_id": mint,
                    "market_label": currency.get("Symbol") or currency.get("Name"),
                    "outcome": None,
                    "venue": program.venue,
                    "category": None,
                    # Curve state is a snapshot, not a window, so there is no
                    # first-trade timestamp to age it from.
                    "age_seconds": None,
                    "price": _f(quote.get("PriceInUSD")),
                    "price_change_5m": None,
                    "price_change_1h": None,
                    "volume_5m_usd": None,
                    "volume_1h_usd": None,
                    "volume_24h_usd": None,
                    "trades_5m": None,
                    "unique_buyers_5m": None,
                    "buy_sell_ratio_5m": None,
                    # SOL sitting in the curve: the closest thing to liquidity
                    # a pre-migration token has, and free with this query.
                    "liquidity_usd": _f(quote.get("PostAmountInUSD")),
                    "curve_completion": completion,
                    "holder_count": None,
                    "top10_holder_pct": None,
                    "spread_pct": None,
                    "snapshot_source": self.source,
                    "snapshot_at": at.isoformat(),
                }
            )

        candidates.sort(key=lambda c: c.get("curve_completion") or 0.0, reverse=True)
        return candidates


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Row helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _mint_of_trade(row: dict) -> str | None:
    trade = row.get("Trade")
    if not isinstance(trade, dict):
        return None
    currency = trade.get("Currency")
    if not isinstance(currency, dict):
        return None
    mint = currency.get("MintAddress")
    return str(mint) if mint else None


def _mint_of_pool(pool: dict) -> str | None:
    market = pool.get("Market")
    if not isinstance(market, dict):
        return None
    base = market.get("BaseCurrency")
    if not isinstance(base, dict):
        return None
    mint = base.get("MintAddress")
    return str(mint) if mint else None

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/rank.py <==
"""Learning to rank: which candidate does this KOL pick?

``LGBMRanker`` with ``lambdarank``, which optimizes NDCG directly and consumes
the graded relevance labels natively. LightGBM rather than XGBoost only because
it is already a dependency here; the formulation is identical.

Two things make this evaluation trustworthy rather than decorative.

**Groups never split across a fold.** A choice set is one decision. Put some of
its candidates in train and the rest in test and the model has seen the
alternatives it is being asked to rank against â€” the single easiest way to
manufacture a spectacular NDCG that means nothing. Splits are therefore by
*group*, in time order.

**Two baselines are mandatory.** NDCG in isolation is unreadable: with 8
candidates per group, random ranking already scores ~0.6 by construction. The
numbers that matter are the margins over (a) random and (b) ranking by raw
volume. A model that cannot beat "pick the highest-volume candidate" has
learned nothing, however good its absolute score looks â€” that is the
learning-to-rank analogue of the random-pick null in the backtest.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

from .schema import FEATURE_COLUMNS, REL_CHOSEN

try:
    from lightgbm import LGBMRanker

    _HAS_LGBM = True
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - depends on install
    _HAS_LGBM = False


@dataclass
class FoldMetrics:
    fold: int
    train_groups: int
    test_groups: int
    ndcg_at_5: float
    hit_at_1: float
    mrr: float
    # Baselines on the identical test groups.
    random_hit_at_1: float
    volume_hit_at_1: float
    random_mrr: float
    volume_mrr: float

    @property
    def lift_over_random(self) -> float:
        return self.hit_at_1 - self.random_hit_at_1

    @property
    def lift_over_volume(self) -> float:
        return self.hit_at_1 - self.volume_hit_at_1


@dataclass
class RankerResult:
    model: object
    features_used: list[str]
    folds: list[FoldMetrics]
    importance: pl.DataFrame
    n_groups: int
    mean_candidates: float
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def mean_hit_at_1(self) -> float:
        return float(np.mean([f.hit_at_1 for f in self.folds])) if self.folds else 0.0

    @property
    def mean_lift_over_volume(self) -> float:
        return (
            float(np.mean([f.lift_over_volume for f in self.folds]))
            if self.folds
            else 0.0
        )

    @property
    def beats_baselines(self) -> bool:
        """The only verdict worth reading.

        Absolute NDCG says little; beating *both* naive orderings on every fold
        is what distinguishes a model from an expensive sort.
        """
        return bool(
            self.folds
            and all(f.lift_over_random > 0 for f in self.folds)
            and all(f.lift_over_volume > 0 for f in self.folds)
        )


def _hit_at_1(scores: np.ndarray, relevance: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Did the top-scored candidate turn out to be the chosen one?

    The most operationally honest metric here: if you act on one pick per
    decision, this is how often you were right.
    """
    return float(relevance[int(np.argmax(scores))] == REL_CHOSEN)


def _reciprocal_rank(scores: np.ndarray, relevance: np.ndarray) -> float:
    order = np.argsort(-scores)
    ranked = relevance[order]
    hits = np.where(ranked == REL_CHOSEN)[0]
    return float(1.0 / (hits[0] + 1)) if hits.size else 0.0


def _ndcg(scores: np.ndarray, relevance: np.ndarray, k: int = 5) -> float:
    order = np.argsort(-scores)[:k]
    gains = (2.0 ** relevance[order] - 1) / np.log2(np.arange(2, order.size + 2))
    ideal_order = np.argsort(-relevance)[:k]
    ideal = (2.0 ** relevance[ideal_order] - 1) / np.log2(
        np.arange(2, ideal_order.size + 2)
    )
    denominator = ideal.sum()
    return float(gains.sum() / denominator) if denominator > 0 else 0.0


def _evaluate(
    frame: pl.DataFrame, scores: np.ndarray, k: int = 5
) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Average NDCG@k, hit@1 and MRR across the groups in ``frame``."""
    working = frame.with_columns(_score=pl.Series("_score", scores))
    ndcgs, hits, rrs = [], [], []
    for _, group in working.group_by("group_id", maintain_order=True):
        relevance = group["relevance"].to_numpy().astype(float)
        group_scores = group["_score"].to_numpy()
        if relevance.max() < REL_CHOSEN:
            continue  # no positive to find
        ndcgs.append(_ndcg(group_scores, relevance, k))
        hits.append(_hit_at_1(group_scores, relevance))
        rrs.append(_reciprocal_rank(group_scores, relevance))
    if not hits:
        return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    return float(np.mean(ndcgs)), float(np.mean(hits)), float(np.mean(rrs))


def _baseline_scores(frame: pl.DataFrame, kind: str, seed: int) -> np.ndarray:
    if kind == "random":
        return np.random.default_rng(seed).random(frame.height)
    if kind == "volume":
        # Rank by the screen's own attention key â€” the coarsest sensible
        # heuristic, and the thing a human scanning the board actually does.
        #
        # `curve_completion` is in the list because on a launchpad every volume
        # column is null: the curve-state query returns progress, not dollars.
        # Falling through to zeros there would make the baseline a constant,
        # beatable by any ordering at all, and `beats_baselines` would read as
        # a pass on a model that had learned nothing.
        for column in (
            "volume_5m_usd",
            "volume_24h_usd",
            "volume_1h_usd",
            "curve_completion",
        ):
            if column in frame.columns and frame[column].null_count() < frame.height:
                return np.nan_to_num(frame[column].to_numpy().astype(float), nan=-1.0)
        return np.zeros(frame.height)
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown baseline: {kind}")


def _usable_features(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
    """Declared features that are present and not entirely null."""
    present = [c for c in FEATURE_COLUMNS if c in frame.columns]
    return [c for c in present if frame[c].null_count() < frame.height]


def _split_groups(group_order: list[str], n_splits: int) -> list[tuple[list[str], list[str]]]:
    """Expanding-window splits over groups in time order.

    Train always precedes test. Never a random split: these decisions are
    ordered in time and a model trained on August must not be tested on July.
    """
    total = len(group_order)
    folds: list[tuple[list[str], list[str]]] = []
    step = total // (n_splits + 1)
    if step < 1:
        return folds
    for i in range(1, n_splits + 1):
        cut = step * i
        train, test = group_order[:cut], group_order[cut : cut + step]
        if train and test:
            folds.append((train, test))
    return folds


def train_ranker(
    candidates: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    n_splits: int = 4,
    seed: int = 0,
    min_groups: int = 200,
) -> RankerResult:
    """Fit and time-validate a candidate ranker."""
    if not _HAS_LGBM:  # pragma: no cover
        raise ImportError("lightgbm is required for ranking; pip install lightgbm")
    if candidates.is_empty():
        raise ValueError("No choice sets. Build them with `pattern-ml choice-sets`.")

    features = _usable_features(candidates)
    if not features:
        raise ValueError(
            "No usable feature columns â€” every candidate feature was all-null. "
            "The snapshot provider is not filling them."
        )

    notes: list[str] = []
    # Chronological, and grouped: every row of a group stays together.
    frame = candidates.sort(["decided_at", "group_id"])
    group_order = frame.select("group_id").unique(maintain_order=True)["group_id"].to_list()

    if len(group_order) < min_groups:
        notes.append(
            f"Only {len(group_order)} choice sets â€” below the {min_groups} needed "
            "for a trustworthy ranking. Treat these numbers as directional."
        )

    dropped = [c for c in FEATURE_COLUMNS if c not in features]
    if dropped:
        notes.append(f"Unavailable features dropped: {', '.join(dropped)}")

    folds: list[FoldMetrics] = []
    for index, (train_ids, test_ids) in enumerate(_split_groups(group_order, n_splits)):
        train = frame.filter(pl.col("group_id").is_in(train_ids))
        test = frame.filter(pl.col("group_id").is_in(test_ids))
        if train.is_empty() or test.is_empty():
            continue

        model = _make_ranker(seed)
        model.fit(
            train.select(features).to_numpy(),
            train["relevance"].to_numpy(),
            group=_group_sizes(train),
        )

        scores = model.predict(test.select(features).to_numpy())
        ndcg, hit, mrr = _evaluate(test, scores)
        _, random_hit, random_mrr = _evaluate(
            test, _baseline_scores(test, "random", seed + index)
        )
        _, volume_hit, volume_mrr = _evaluate(
            test, _baseline_scores(test, "volume", seed)
        )

        folds.append(
            FoldMetrics(
                fold=index,
                train_groups=len(train_ids),
                test_groups=len(test_ids),
                ndcg_at_5=ndcg,
                hit_at_1=hit,
                mrr=mrr,
                random_hit_at_1=random_hit,
                volume_hit_at_1=volume_hit,
                random_mrr=random_mrr,
                volume_mrr=volume_mrr,
            )
        )

    if not folds:
        notes.append("Too few groups to form a single train/test split.")

    final = _make_ranker(seed)
    final.fit(
        frame.select(features).to_numpy(),
        frame["relevance"].to_numpy(),
        group=_group_sizes(frame),
    )

    importance = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "feature": features,
            "gain": final.booster_.feature_importance(importance_type="gain").tolist(),
        }
    ).sort("gain", descending=True)

    mean_candidates = float(
        frame.group_by("group_id").len()["len"].mean() or 0.0
    )

    return RankerResult(
        model=final,
        features_used=features,
        folds=folds,
        importance=importance,
        n_groups=len(group_order),
        mean_candidates=mean_candidates,
        notes=notes,
    )


def _make_ranker(seed: int):
    return LGBMRanker(
        objective="lambdarank",
        metric="ndcg",
        ndcg_eval_at=[1, 3, 5],
        n_estimators=300,
        learning_rate=0.05,
        num_leaves=31,
        # Choice sets are small and noisy; these constrain the fit.
        min_child_samples=20,
        subsample=0.8,
        subsample_freq=1,
        colsample_bytree=0.8,
        reg_lambda=1.0,
        random_state=seed,
        verbose=-1,
    )


def _group_sizes(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> list[int]:
    """Row counts per group, in the frame's current order.

    LightGBM's ranking API takes group *sizes*, not ids, and assumes rows are
    already contiguous by group. A frame sorted differently would silently
    mis-associate candidates with decisions.
    """
    return (
        frame.group_by("group_id", maintain_order=True)
        .len()["len"]
        .to_list()
    )


def score_candidates(
    result: RankerResult, candidates: pl.DataFrame
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Score a live candidate set. Highest score = most KOL-like.

    The scores are ordinal, not probabilities: only their order within one
    choice set is meaningful, and comparing scores across different decisions
    is not valid.
    """
    if candidates.is_empty():
        return candidates
    matrix = candidates.select(result.features_used).to_numpy()
    scores = result.model.predict(matrix)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    return candidates.with_columns(score=pl.Series("score", scores)).sort(
        "score", descending=True
    )

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/schema.py <==
"""Choice-set schema, relevance grades, and the screening contract.

The tables here are *group-structured*: rows belong to a ``group_id``, one
group per KOL decision, and a model consumes whole groups rather than
independent rows. Getting that structure wrong â€” splitting a group across a
train/test boundary, say â€” leaks the answer, because the other candidates in a
group tell you a great deal about which one was chosen.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Protocol

import polars as pl

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Relevance grades
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graded rather than binary. A token the KOL bought 40 minutes later was not a
# negative â€” it was attractive, just not *first*. Labelling it 0 teaches the
# model the opposite of the truth, and NDCG consumes grades natively, so there
# is no reason to throw the distinction away.
REL_CHOSEN = 2   # bought at t: chosen over everything else on screen
REL_LATER = 1    # bought within the lookahead window: liked, but not first
REL_IGNORED = 0  # never bought: a genuine rejection

# How far ahead to look when assigning REL_LATER. Beyond this the connection to
# the decision at t is too weak to be evidence of anything.
DEFAULT_LATER_WINDOW = timedelta(hours=24)

# Candidates traded inside this window around t are treated as simultaneous â€”
# a KOL clicking three tokens in ninety seconds made one decision, not three,
# so the others must not be scored as rejections.
DEFAULT_SIMULTANEITY_WINDOW = timedelta(minutes=5)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tables
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# One row per (decision, candidate). This is the model's training matrix.
CANDIDATE_SCHEMA: dict[str, pl.DataType] = {
    # grouping â€” a model must never see rows from one group split across folds
    "group_id": pl.Utf8,
    "chain": pl.Utf8,
    "kol_address": pl.Utf8,
    "decided_at": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone="UTC"),
    # the candidate
    "market_id": pl.Utf8,
    "market_label": pl.Utf8,
    "outcome": pl.Utf8,
    # which board this decision was made on â€” the universe the alternatives
