    # were drawn from, kept so a model is never trained across mixed venues
    # without that being visible
    "venue": pl.Utf8,
    "category": pl.Utf8,
    # label
    "relevance": pl.Int32,
    "chosen": pl.Boolean,
    # provenance of the alternatives: how U_t was produced, so a model trained
    # on a reconstructed universe is never silently mixed with a live one
    "snapshot_source": pl.Utf8,   # "live" | "reconstructed" | "synthetic"
    "snapshot_at": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone="UTC"),
    # --- point-in-time features, all strictly as-of `decided_at` ------------
    "age_seconds": pl.Float64,
    "price": pl.Float64,
    "liquidity_usd": pl.Float64,
    "volume_5m_usd": pl.Float64,
    "volume_1h_usd": pl.Float64,
    "volume_24h_usd": pl.Float64,
    "trades_5m": pl.Float64,
    "unique_buyers_5m": pl.Float64,
    "buy_sell_ratio_5m": pl.Float64,
    "price_change_5m": pl.Float64,
    "price_change_1h": pl.Float64,
    "holder_count": pl.Float64,
    "top10_holder_pct": pl.Float64,
    "spread_pct": pl.Float64,
    # Bonding-curve progress in [0, 1]: 0 is a fresh launch, 1 is migration to
    # an AMM. Null off launchpads, which is correct â€” an AMM token has no curve.
    "curve_completion": pl.Float64,
    # roster-relative: how many tracked KOLs were already in, before t
    "prior_kol_entries": pl.Float64,
    "seconds_since_first_kol_entry": pl.Float64,
}

# One row per decision. Metadata about the group as a whole.
CHOICE_SET_SCHEMA: dict[str, pl.DataType] = {
    "group_id": pl.Utf8,
    "chain": pl.Utf8,
    "kol_address": pl.Utf8,
    "kol_handle": pl.Utf8,
    "decided_at": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone="UTC"),
    "chosen_market_id": pl.Utf8,
    "venue": pl.Utf8,
    "n_candidates": pl.Int32,
    "n_positive": pl.Int32,
    "screen_name": pl.Utf8,
    "snapshot_source": pl.Utf8,
    # False when the chosen asset failed the screen and had to be re-inserted.
    # These groups are the screen telling you it does not describe this trader.
    "chosen_passed_screen": pl.Boolean,
}

# Columns a ranker may learn from. Everything else is an identifier, a label,
# or provenance. Keeping this explicit is what stops `relevance` or `chosen`
# from being handed to the model by an careless `select`.
FEATURE_COLUMNS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "age_seconds",
    "price",
    "liquidity_usd",
    "volume_5m_usd",
    "volume_1h_usd",
    "volume_24h_usd",
    "trades_5m",
    "unique_buyers_5m",
    "buy_sell_ratio_5m",
    "price_change_5m",
    "price_change_1h",
    "holder_count",
    "top10_holder_pct",
    "spread_pct",
    "curve_completion",
    "prior_kol_entries",
    "seconds_since_first_kol_entry",
)

LABEL_COLUMNS: tuple[str, ...] = ("relevance", "chosen")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Screens
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Screen(Protocol):
    """What the trader could plausibly have been looking at.

    A screen is the modelling assumption made explicit. It should approximate
    the tool the KOL actually uses â€” a DexScreener filter, a Pump.fun board â€”
    because the negatives it admits are what the model learns to reject.
    """

    name: str
    max_candidates: int

    def passes(self, candidate: dict) -> bool:
        """Whether one candidate belongs in U_t."""
        ...

    def rank_key(self, candidate: dict) -> float:
        """Attention ordering. The top ``max_candidates`` are kept.

        Screens surface far more than a human reads. This is the proxy for
        which ones actually got looked at â€” usually recent volume, since that
        is what trending boards sort by.
        """
        ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SolanaScreen:
    """Approximates a DEX trending board â€” Raydium, Meteora, Orca, PumpSwap.

    Only ``min_volume_5m_usd`` is on by default, because it is the only field
    the Bitquery reconstruction fills for every candidate.

    ``max_age_seconds`` and ``min_liquidity_usd`` default to ``None`` â€” off â€”
    and that is a correctness requirement, not laziness. Age is censored
    whenever a token first traded before the discovery window, and liquidity
    costs an extra query per program per decision (``fetch_liquidity=True`` on
    the provider). Gating on a field the reconstruction usually cannot fill
    would reject every candidate and produce zero choice sets. Worse, gating on
    one that live scoring *can* fill while historical assembly cannot would
    train and serve from two different universes.

    Turn either on only once the provider demonstrably fills it â€” check the null
    rate in ``artifacts/choice_candidates.parquet`` before doing so.
    """

    name: str = "solana-trending"
    min_volume_5m_usd: float = 10_000.0
    max_age_seconds: float | None = None
    min_liquidity_usd: float | None = None
    max_candidates: int = 20

    def passes(self, candidate: dict) -> bool:
        volume = candidate.get("volume_5m_usd")
        # A missing value is not a pass. Admitting unknowns would fill U_t with
        # candidates whose features are all null, and the model would learn to
        # rank on missingness â€” which does not exist at serve time.
        if volume is None or volume < self.min_volume_5m_usd:
            return False
        if self.max_age_seconds is not None:
            age = candidate.get("age_seconds")
            if age is None or age > self.max_age_seconds:
                return False
        if self.min_liquidity_usd is not None:
            liquidity = candidate.get("liquidity_usd")
            if liquidity is None or liquidity < self.min_liquidity_usd:
                return False
        return True

    def rank_key(self, candidate: dict) -> float:
        return float(candidate.get("volume_5m_usd") or 0.0)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PumpFunScreen:
    """Approximates a launchpad board â€” Pump.fun, Moonshot, LaunchLab.

    A different question from the AMM screen, deliberately. Nobody watching a
    bonding-curve board sorts by dollar volume; they sort by how close a curve
    is to migrating, because migration is the event being front-run. So the gate
    and the attention ordering are both curve completion.

    Both fields come free with the curve-state query, so unlike ``SolanaScreen``
    this screen gates on values the provider actually fills.
    """

    name: str = "pump-launchpad"
    min_completion: float = 0.70
    min_liquidity_usd: float = 0.0
    max_candidates: int = 20

    def passes(self, candidate: dict) -> bool:
        completion = candidate.get("curve_completion")
        if completion is None or completion < self.min_completion:
            return False
        if self.min_liquidity_usd > 0:
            liquidity = candidate.get("liquidity_usd")
            if liquidity is None or liquidity < self.min_liquidity_usd:
                return False
        return True

    def rank_key(self, candidate: dict) -> float:
        return float(candidate.get("curve_completion") or 0.0)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PolymarketScreen:
    """Approximates the active-markets board.

    Far more tractable than Solana: the live universe is hundreds of markets,
    not a hundred thousand, so U_t is close to genuinely enumerable rather than
    approximated.

    ``max_spread_pct`` defaults to ``None`` â€” off. Spread requires an order-book
    snapshot, and there is no historical endpoint for one, so a spread-gated
    screen can be applied live but never reconstructed. Enabling it would make
    historical and live choice sets come from *different* universes, which is
    worse than not filtering on it at all. Turn it on only if you have a
    provider that fills the field historically.
    """

    name: str = "polymarket-active"
    min_volume_24h_usd: float = 50_000.0
    max_spread_pct: float | None = None
    max_candidates: int = 20
    # When set, only markets sharing the chosen market's category compete. A
    # politics specialist was not choosing between an election and a football
    # game, and pretending otherwise adds noise, not signal.
    same_category_only: bool = True

    def passes(self, candidate: dict) -> bool:
        volume = candidate.get("volume_24h_usd")
        if volume is None or volume < self.min_volume_24h_usd:
            return False
        if self.max_spread_pct is not None:
            spread = candidate.get("spread_pct")
            if spread is None or spread > self.max_spread_pct:
                return False
        return True

    def rank_key(self, candidate: dict) -> float:
        return float(candidate.get("volume_24h_usd") or 0.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The diagnostic that decides whether any of this is valid
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def screen_coverage(
    choice_sets: pl.DataFrame, *, by_kol: bool = True
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """What fraction of real KOL buys the screen would have surfaced.

    **Read this before reading any NDCG number.** If a KOL's buys mostly fail
    the screen, the negatives are drawn from a universe they never looked at,
    and the model is learning to discriminate within the wrong set. No amount
    of tuning fixes that; the screen has to change, or that KOL has to be
    excluded as sourcing from somewhere unobservable (a private group, a
    launch they were told about directly).

    Rough reading: above ~0.7 the screen describes the trader well; below ~0.4
    it does not describe them at all.
    """
    if choice_sets.is_empty():
        return pl.DataFrame(
            schema={
                "kol_address": pl.Utf8,
                "decisions": pl.Int32,
                "passed": pl.Int32,
                "coverage": pl.Float64,
            }
        )

    keys = ["kol_address"] if by_kol else []
    grouped = (
        choice_sets.group_by(keys) if keys else choice_sets.group_by(pl.lit(1).alias("_all"))
    )
    out = grouped.agg(
        decisions=pl.len().cast(pl.Int32),
        passed=pl.col("chosen_passed_screen").sum().cast(pl.Int32),
        median_candidates=pl.col("n_candidates").median(),
    ).with_columns(coverage=pl.col("passed") / pl.col("decisions"))

    if not keys:
        out = out.drop("_all")
    return out.sort("coverage")

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/choice/snapshot.py <==
"""Market snapshots: what was on screen at a given instant.

This module is the hard part of the whole design, and the honest place to say
why.

The reconstruction problem
--------------------------
Scoring live candidates is easy â€” DexScreener and Pump.fun will tell you what
is trending *right now*. Training is the problem: neither will tell you what was
trending at 14:02 UTC on some past Tuesday. "Query the indexer at ``t_event``"
works in production and quietly does not work for building the training set.

Three ways out, and they trade off badly:

1. **Reconstruct from raw swaps** (Bitquery / Dune / Flipside). Aggregate every
   DEX swap into per-token, per-minute bars yourself, then apply the screen at
   any past minute. Faithful and vendor-independent; by far the most work.
2. **Per-candidate OHLCV** (Birdeye / GeckoTerminal). Cheaper, but you need the
   candidate universe *before* you can query it, and the liquidity/holder
   fields often have no historical endpoint at all.
3. **Forward collection.** Snapshot U_t on a schedule starting now. Zero
   leakage risk by construction, zero reconstruction work â€” and useless for
   months, because positives accrue only as fast as the KOLs trade.

The binding constraint is positives, not candidates. Twenty KOLs making ~50
buys a month is ~1,000 decisions a month, and learning-to-rank wants thousands
of groups. So reconstruction is not optional if you want results this quarter.

Forward collection should nonetheless run from day one. It is the only
ground truth that is provably leakage-free, which makes it the yardstick for
whether the reconstructed universe is trustworthy: train on reconstructed,
then check the ranking still holds on forward-collected groups.

Fields a provider cannot fill must be ``None``, never zero. A zero liquidity is
a claim; a null is an admission. ``SolanaScreen.passes`` rejects nulls, so an
unfillable field shrinks U_t rather than poisoning it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from ..config import get_settings

# Provenance values for `snapshot_source`. Mixing these in one training set
# silently mixes two different universes, so every row carries its origin.
SOURCE_LIVE = "live"
SOURCE_RECONSTRUCTED = "reconstructed"
SOURCE_SYNTHETIC = "synthetic"


@runtime_checkable
class MarketSnapshotProvider(Protocol):
    """Returns the candidate universe as it stood at a point in time.

    Implementations must honour one rule absolutely: **no field may incorporate
    data from at or after ``at``**. Not the 24h volume measured at end of day,
    not the liquidity as it is now. If a value cannot be obtained as-of ``at``,
    return ``None`` for it.

    A provider that leaks even ten seconds of the future produces a model that
    looks excellent in validation and fails in production, with nothing
    upstream to indicate why.
    """

    chain: str
    source: str

    def candidates_at(
        self, at: datetime, *, limit: int = 200, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict]:
        """Every plausibly-visible asset at ``at``, pre-screen.

        Returns dicts keyed by the feature names in
        ``choice.schema.CANDIDATE_SCHEMA`` (``market_id`` required).

        ``venue`` is the protocol the trade being reconstructed executed on. On
        Solana it decides the whole question asked â€” a launchpad board and a
        Raydium trending list are different universes at the same instant.
        Providers for venues where it is meaningless (Polymarket has one order
        book) accept and ignore it.
        """
        ...

    def features_at(
        self, market_id: str, at: datetime, *, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> dict | None:
        """Point-in-time features for one asset.

        Needed when the chosen asset failed the screen and must be re-inserted
        into its own choice set â€” a group with no positive is untrainable.
        """
        ...


class SnapshotCache:
    """On-disk cache of snapshots, keyed by (chain, venue, minute).

    Reconstruction is expensive and rate-limited, and several KOLs trading in
    the same minute must all see the *same* U_t â€” otherwise the model can learn
    which provider call produced a row. Caching to the minute enforces that and
    makes re-runs free.

    Venue is part of the key, not a detail. Two KOLs trading at 14:02 â€” one on a
    Pump.fun curve, one on Raydium â€” were looking at different boards, and
    serving one the other's universe would fabricate alternatives neither faced.

    Minute granularity is a deliberate rounding: it is the resolution most
    OHLCV sources offer anyway, and sub-minute precision would multiply cost
    for detail the screen cannot resolve.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: Path | None = None) -> None:
        settings = get_settings()
        self._root = root or (settings.data_dir / "snapshots")
        self._root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def _path(self, chain: str, at: datetime, venue: str | None = None) -> Path:
        minute = at.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M")
        # Shard by day so a directory never holds a million files.
        day = minute[:8]
        scope = _safe_scope(venue) if venue else "_all"
        directory = self._root / chain / scope / day
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return directory / f"{minute}.json"

    def get(self, chain: str, at: datetime, venue: str | None = None) -> list[dict] | None:
        path = self._path(chain, at, venue)
        if not path.exists():
            return None
        try:
            payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            # A half-written cache entry should be refetched, not crash a run.
            return None
        return payload if isinstance(payload, list) else None

    def put(
        self,
        chain: str,
        at: datetime,
        candidates: list[dict],
        venue: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        path = self._path(chain, at, venue)
        # Write-then-rename so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file
        # that a later run would read as authoritative.
        tmp = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(candidates, default=str))
        tmp.replace(path)

    def stats(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        for chain_dir in self._root.iterdir() if self._root.exists() else []:
            if chain_dir.is_dir():
                counts[chain_dir.name] = sum(1 for _ in chain_dir.rglob("*.json"))
        return counts


def _safe_scope(venue: str) -> str:
    """Venue names come from an API field, so they cannot be trusted as paths."""
    return "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_" else "_" for c in venue)[:48] or "_all"


class CachingProvider:
    """Wraps a provider so repeated calls for the same minute hit disk.

    Also the enforcement point for same-minute consistency: two KOLs trading at
    14:02:07 and 14:02:41 on the same venue get an identical U_t, because they
    were looking at the same board.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: MarketSnapshotProvider, cache: SnapshotCache | None = None):
        self._inner = inner
        self._cache = cache or SnapshotCache()
        self.chain = inner.chain
        self.source = inner.source

    def candidates_at(
        self, at: datetime, *, limit: int = 200, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> list[dict]:
        cached = self._cache.get(self.chain, at, venue)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached[:limit]
        fetched = self._inner.candidates_at(at, limit=limit, venue=venue)
        self._cache.put(self.chain, at, fetched, venue)
        return fetched

    def features_at(
        self, market_id: str, at: datetime, *, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> dict | None:
        return self._inner.features_at(market_id, at, venue=venue)


class ForwardCollector:
    """Snapshots U_t on a schedule, building leakage-proof ground truth.

    Runs as a cron job. Every snapshot is taken *before* anyone knows which
    asset a KOL will pick, so a choice set assembled from these files cannot
    contain lookahead bias by construction â€” the future had not happened yet.

    Slow to accumulate and worth starting immediately: it is the only dataset
    that can adjudicate whether a reconstructed universe was faithful.
    """

    def __init__(self, provider: MarketSnapshotProvider, cache: SnapshotCache | None = None):
        self._provider = provider
        self._cache = cache or SnapshotCache()

    def collect(
        self, *, limit: int = 200, venue: str | None = None
    ) -> tuple[datetime, int]:
        """Take one snapshot of the current universe. Returns (when, how many)."""
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        candidates = self._provider.candidates_at(now, limit=limit, venue=venue)
        for candidate in candidates:
            candidate["snapshot_source"] = SOURCE_LIVE
            candidate["snapshot_at"] = now.isoformat()
        self._cache.put(self._provider.chain, now, candidates, venue)
        return now, len(candidates)

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/cli.py <==
"""Pattern-ML command line.

    pull â†’ index â†’ positions â†’ choice-sets â†’ rank â†’ score

Each stage persists its output, so stages can be re-run independently. Only
``pull``, ``choice-sets``, ``score`` and the probes touch the network.

The modelling question is a *discrete choice*: of the assets competing for a
trader's attention at time t, why this one? That framing is what makes the
output usable before anyone trades â€” score today's candidates and act on the
top of the ranking, rather than waiting to copy a fill you will always be late
to.

Two diagnostics run before the pipeline rather than inside it:
``solana-probe`` checks the Bitquery queries against the live schema, and
``venue-audit`` reports execution venues the program registry cannot name. Both
fail loudly for problems that would otherwise show up as an empty result.

``validate`` is separate and answers a different question: what would copying
the whole roster have returned, after slippage and fees. It needs no model and
is the baseline any ranking must beat to be worth having.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import typer
from rich.console import Console
from rich.table import Table

from .config import KolRosterError, get_settings, load_kols
from .storage import get_storage

app = typer.Typer(
    name="pattern-ml",
    help="Find and test trading patterns in KOL trade history.",
    no_args_is_help=True,
    add_completion=False,
)
console = Console()


def _fail(message: str) -> None:
    console.print(f"[bold red]âœ—[/bold red] {message}")
    raise typer.Exit(1)


def _roster(path: Path | None):
    try:
        return load_kols(path)
    except KolRosterError as exc:
        _fail(str(exc))
        raise  # unreachable; keeps type checkers happy


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 0 â€” diagnostics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@app.command("solana-probe")
def solana_probe() -> None:
    """Check every Bitquery query against the live schema. Run this first.

    The GraphQL field names in `sources/bitquery.py` were written without
    network access and Bitquery's Solana schema has moved between versions. A
    renamed field returns an empty result rather than an error, which at scale
    looks like "these KOLs had no alternatives" rather than "the query is
    wrong". This surfaces the difference in one command.
    """
    from .sources.bitquery import BitqueryClient, BitqueryError

    settings = get_settings()
    if not settings.bitquery_token:
        _fail(
            "BITQUERY_TOKEN is not set. Add it to pattern-ml/.env.\n"
            "It must be an OAuth access token, not the legacy X-API-KEY."
        )

    console.print("[bold]Probing Bitquery Solana schema[/bold]")
    console.print("[dim]Each query runs once with a one-row limit.[/dim]\n")

    try:
        with BitqueryClient(max_rps=settings.bitquery_max_rps) as client:
            results = client.probe()
    except BitqueryError as exc:
        _fail(str(exc))
        return

    table = Table("Query", "Status", "Rows", "Detail")
    for result in results:
        status = "[green]ok[/green]" if result["ok"] else "[red]failed[/red]"
        table.add_row(
            result["query"], status, str(result["rows"]), result["detail"][:80]
        )
    console.print(table)

    failed = [r["query"] for r in results if not r["ok"]]
    if failed:
        console.print(
            f"\n[bold red]âœ—[/bold red] {len(failed)} quer(y/ies) rejected: "
            f"{', '.join(failed)}.\n"
            "Fix the query constants in `sources/bitquery.py` before running "
            "`choice-sets --chain solana` â€” a rejected query produces empty "
            "choice sets, not an error."
        )
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    empty = [r["query"] for r in results if r["ok"] and r["rows"] == 0]
    if empty:
        console.print(
            f"\n[yellow]![/yellow] Accepted but empty: {', '.join(empty)}. "
            "The schema is right; the window may just have been quiet. Re-run, "
            "and if it stays empty for long-past windows only, add "
            "`(dataset: archive)` to the queries."
        )
    console.print("\n[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Schema accepted.")


@app.command("venue-audit")
def venue_audit(
    top: int = typer.Option(25, "--top", help="How many unmapped programs to show"),
) -> None:
    """Find execution venues the program registry does not recognise.

    Counts program ids appearing in the KOLs' own pulled transactions that
    `venues.py` has no entry for. A program near the top of this list is a board
    the choice-set builder is currently blind to â€” those decisions fall back to
    the broad AMM universe, which is a weaker approximation of what the trader
    was looking at.
    """
    from .venues import unmapped_programs

    settings = get_settings()
    raw_files = sorted((settings.raw_dir / "solana").glob("*.parquet"))
    if not raw_files:
        _fail("No raw Solana data. Run `pattern-ml pull --chains solana` first.")

    frames = []
    for path in raw_files:
        frame = pl.read_parquet(path)
        if "instructions_json" in frame.columns:
            frames.append(frame.select("instructions_json"))
    if not frames:
        _fail(
            "No `instructions_json` column in the raw files â€” they predate venue "
            "resolution. Re-run `pattern-ml pull --chains solana` to capture it."
        )

    unmapped = unmapped_programs(pl.concat(frames), top=top)
    if unmapped.is_empty():
        console.print(
            "[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Every program in the pulled data is "
            "recognised."
        )
        return

    console.print("[bold]Unmapped programs[/bold]")
    console.print(
        "[dim]Present in KOL transactions, absent from the registry. Look each "
        "up on Solscan and add it to `venues.py` if it is a DEX.[/dim]"
    )
    table = Table("Program ID", "Transactions")
    for row in unmapped.iter_rows(named=True):
        table.add_row(row["program_id"], f"{row['transactions']:,}")
    console.print(table)

# Stage 1 â€” pull
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@app.command()
def pull(
    kols: Path = typer.Option(
        None, "--kols", help="Roster YAML (default config/kols.yaml)"
    ),
    chains: str = typer.Option("solana,polymarket", "--chains", help="Comma-separated"),
) -> None:
    """Fetch raw trade history for every KOL into data/raw/."""
    from .sources import polymarket, solana

    settings = get_settings()
    storage = get_storage()
    wanted = {c.strip() for c in chains.split(",") if c.strip()}
    roster = [k for k in _roster(kols) if k.chain in wanted]
    if not roster:
        _fail(f"No KOLs in the roster match chains: {sorted(wanted)}")

    if any(k.chain == "solana" for k in roster) and not settings.helius_api_key:
        _fail("HELIUS_API_KEY is not set â€” required for Solana. See .env.example.")

    console.print(f"[bold]Pulling {len(roster)} KOL(s)[/bold]")

    async def run() -> dict:
        results: dict = {}
        results.update(await polymarket.pull_all(roster))
        results.update(await solana.pull_all(roster))
        return results

    results = asyncio.run(run())

    table = Table("KOL", "Chain", "Rows", "Requests", "File")
    total = 0
    problems: list[str] = []
    for kol in roster:
        frame, stats = results.get(kol.key, (None, None))
        if frame is None or frame.is_empty():
            table.add_row(
                kol.label, kol.chain, "0", str(stats.requests if stats else 0), "â€”"
            )
            if stats:
                problems.extend(stats.errors)
            continue
        path = storage.write_raw_parquet(kol.chain, kol.address, frame)
        total += frame.height
        table.add_row(
            kol.label, kol.chain, f"{frame.height:,}", f"{stats.requests:,}", path.name
        )
        problems.extend(stats.errors)

    console.print(table)
    for problem in problems:
        console.print(f"[yellow]![/yellow] {problem}")
    console.print(f"[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Pulled {total:,} raw rows")

@app.command()
def index() -> None:
    """Normalize raw dumps into the canonical trade table."""
    from .index.normalize import normalize_file
    from .prices import coverage, load_sol_usd

    storage = get_storage()
    files = storage.list_raw_parquet()
    if not files:
        _fail("No raw files. Run `pattern-ml pull` first.")

    console.print(f"[bold]Indexing {len(files)} raw file(s)[/bold]")

    # Without SOL/USD, every SOL-quoted swap gets a null size_usd, which nulls
    # most sizing signal on the Solana half.
    sol_usd = load_sol_usd()
    if sol_usd:
        console.print(f"[dim]Loaded {len(sol_usd)} days of SOL/USD rates[/dim]")
    else:
        console.print(
            "[yellow]![/yellow] Could not fetch SOL/USD rates. "
            "Solana trades quoted in SOL will have a null size_usd."
        )

    settings = get_settings()
    inserted = 0
    for path in files:
        try:
            chain = path.relative_to(settings.raw_dir).parts[0]
        except (ValueError, IndexError):
            console.print(f"[yellow]![/yellow] Skipping unrecognised path {path}")
            continue
        frame = normalize_file(path, chain, sol_usd=sol_usd)
        if frame.is_empty():
            continue
        inserted += storage.insert_trades(frame)

    console.print(
        f"[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] {inserted:,} new trades "
        f"({storage.count_trades():,} total)"
    )

    if sol_usd:
        sol_trades = storage.get_trades(chain="solana")
        if not sol_trades.is_empty():
            first = sol_trades.select(pl.col("ts").min()).item()
            last = sol_trades.select(pl.col("ts").max()).item()
            if first and last:
                console.print(
                    f"[dim]SOL/USD coverage: {coverage(sol_usd, first, last):.1%} "
                    "of Solana trade days[/dim]"
                )

@app.command()
def positions() -> None:
    """Reconstruct round-trip positions from the trade table."""
    from .index.positions import label_coverage

    storage = get_storage()
    if storage.count_trades() == 0:
        _fail("No trades. Run `pattern-ml index` first.")

    count = storage.rebuild_positions()
    stats = label_coverage(storage.get_positions())

    table = Table("Metric", "Value")
    table.add_row("Positions", f"{stats['positions']:,}")
    table.add_row("Closed", f"{stats['closed']:,}")
    table.add_row("Labelled (win/loss)", f"{stats['labelled']:,}")
    table.add_row("Closed rate", f"{stats['closed_rate']:.1%}")
    console.print(table)

    if stats["closed_rate"] < 0.3:
        console.print(
            "[yellow]![/yellow] Under 30% of positions are closed. The labelled "
            "set skews toward trades the KOLs chose to exit, so treat win rates "
            "as optimistic."
        )
    console.print(f"[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Built {count:,} positions")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4 â€” discrete choice: what would this KOL have bought?
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@app.command("choice-sets")
def choice_sets(
    chain: str = typer.Option("polymarket", "--chain", help="polymarket | solana"),
    min_volume: float = typer.Option(
        50_000.0,
        "--min-volume",
        help="Screen floor: 24h volume (polymarket) or 5m volume (solana)",
    ),
    min_completion: float = typer.Option(
        0.70,
        "--min-curve-completion",
        help="Solana launchpads: minimum bonding-curve progress, 0-1",
    ),
    max_candidates: int = typer.Option(20, "--max-candidates"),
    max_decisions: int = typer.Option(
        None, "--max-decisions", help="Cap decisions processed (useful for a trial run)"
    ),
    same_category: bool = typer.Option(
        True, "--same-category/--any-category",
        help="Polymarket: only markets in the chosen market's category compete",
    ),
    fetch_liquidity: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--fetch-liquidity",
        help="Solana: extra query per program per decision to fill liquidity_usd",
    ),
) -> None:
    """Assemble ranked choice sets: each KOL entry against its alternatives.

    Every candidate's features are computed strictly as-of the decision instant.
    Start with `--max-decisions 50` to sanity-check the screen before committing
    to a full run â€” and on Solana, run `pattern-ml solana-probe` first.
    """
    from .choice.assemble import build_choice_sets
    from .choice.schema import screen_coverage
    from .choice.snapshot import CachingProvider

    if chain not in ("polymarket", "solana"):
        _fail(f"No snapshot provider for {chain!r}.")

    settings = get_settings()
    storage = get_storage()
    trades = storage.get_trades(chain=chain)
    if trades.is_empty():
        _fail(f"No {chain} trades. Run `pattern-ml pull` and `index` first.")

    console.print(f"[bold]Assembling choice sets for {chain}[/bold]")

    if chain == "polymarket":
        from .choice.providers.polymarket import PolymarketSnapshotProvider
        from .choice.schema import PolymarketScreen

        screen = PolymarketScreen(
            min_volume_24h_usd=min_volume,
            max_candidates=max_candidates,
            same_category_only=same_category,
        )
        console.print(
            f"[dim]Screen: {screen.name} Â· 24h volume â‰¥ ${min_volume:,.0f} Â· "
            f"top {max_candidates}[/dim]"
        )
        provider_ctx = PolymarketSnapshotProvider()
    else:
        from .choice.providers.solana import SolanaSnapshotProvider
        from .choice.schema import PumpFunScreen, SolanaScreen
        from .venues import KIND_AMM, KIND_BONDING_CURVE, KIND_CLMM

        if not settings.bitquery_token:
            _fail(
                "BITQUERY_TOKEN is not set â€” Solana reconstruction cannot run.\n"
                "Add it to pattern-ml/.env, then verify the schema with "
                "`pattern-ml solana-probe`."
            )

        # One screen per kind of board. A launchpad watcher ranks by how close a
        # curve is to migrating; an AMM watcher ranks by volume. Forcing one
        # screen across both would describe neither.
        amm_screen = SolanaScreen(
            min_volume_5m_usd=min_volume, max_candidates=max_candidates
        )
        curve_screen = PumpFunScreen(
            min_completion=min_completion, max_candidates=max_candidates
        )
        screen = {
            KIND_BONDING_CURVE: curve_screen,
            KIND_AMM: amm_screen,
            KIND_CLMM: amm_screen,
            "*": amm_screen,  # unresolved venue: widen rather than drop
        }
        console.print(
            f"[dim]Screens: {curve_screen.name} (completion â‰¥ "
            f"{min_completion:.0%}) Â· {amm_screen.name} (5m volume â‰¥ "
            f"${min_volume:,.0f}) Â· top {max_candidates}[/dim]"
        )
        provider_ctx = SolanaSnapshotProvider(
            min_curve_completion=min_completion,
            fetch_liquidity=fetch_liquidity,
            candidate_limit=max(max_candidates * 3, 50),
        )

    with provider_ctx as raw_provider:
        provider = CachingProvider(raw_provider)
        candidates, groups = build_choice_sets(
            trades,
            provider,
            screen,
            chain=chain,
            max_decisions=max_decisions,
        )

    if groups.is_empty():
        _fail(
            "No choice sets could be built. Either no KOL entries fell inside "
            "the snapshot coverage, or every group had too few candidates."
            + (
                "\n\nOn Solana the usual cause is a schema mismatch â€” run "
                "`pattern-ml solana-probe` to check every query is accepted."
                if chain == "solana"
                else ""
            )
        )

    settings.artifacts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    candidates.write_parquet(settings.artifacts_dir / "choice_candidates.parquet")
    groups.write_parquet(settings.artifacts_dir / "choice_sets.parquet")

    table = Table("Metric", "Value")
    table.add_row("Decisions", f"{groups.height:,}")
    table.add_row("Candidate rows", f"{candidates.height:,}")
    table.add_row(
        "Median candidates/decision",
        f"{groups['n_candidates'].median():.0f}",
    )
    console.print(table)

    # Which boards the decisions came from â€” a run that is 95% one venue is a
    # single-venue model wearing a multi-venue label.
    if "venue" in groups.columns and groups["venue"].null_count() < groups.height:
        venues = (
            groups.group_by("venue")
            .agg(decisions=pl.len())
            .sort("decisions", descending=True)
        )
        venue_table = Table("Venue", "Decisions")
        for row in venues.iter_rows(named=True):
            venue_table.add_row(str(row["venue"] or "â€”"), f"{row['decisions']:,}")
        console.print(venue_table)

    # The diagnostic that decides whether any of this is valid.
    coverage = screen_coverage(groups)
    console.print("\n[bold]Screen coverage[/bold]")
    console.print(
        "[dim]What fraction of real KOL buys the screen would have surfaced. "
        "Low coverage means the negatives come from a universe the trader "
        "never looked at.[/dim]"
    )
    cov_table = Table("KOL", "Decisions", "Passed", "Coverage")
    for row in coverage.iter_rows(named=True):
        value = row["coverage"]
        colour = "green" if value >= 0.7 else "yellow" if value >= 0.4 else "red"
        cov_table.add_row(
            row["kol_address"][:16],
            f"{row['decisions']:,}",
            f"{row['passed']:,}",
            f"[{colour}]{value:.1%}[/{colour}]",
        )
    console.print(cov_table)

    worst = coverage.head(1)
    if not worst.is_empty() and worst.row(0, named=True)["coverage"] < 0.4:
        console.print(
            "[yellow]![/yellow] At least one KOL is under 40% coverage â€” they "
            "are sourcing trades the screen cannot see (a private group, a "
            "direct tip). Loosen the screen or exclude them; no amount of model "
            "tuning fixes a mis-specified choice set."
        )

    console.print(f"\n[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Wrote {settings.artifacts_dir}")


@app.command()
def rank(
    n_splits: int = typer.Option(4, "--splits"),
    drop_kol_features: bool = typer.Option(
        False,
        "--drop-kol-features",
        help="Exclude prior-KOL-entry columns to measure true early-entry skill",
    ),
) -> None:
    """Train the candidate ranker and check it against the naive baselines."""
    import pickle

    from .choice.rank import train_ranker

    settings = get_settings()
    path = settings.artifacts_dir / "choice_candidates.parquet"
    if not path.exists():
        _fail("No choice sets. Run `pattern-ml choice-sets` first.")

    candidates = pl.read_parquet(path)
    if drop_kol_features:
        # These are strongest precisely when you are latest. Dropping them
        # measures whether the model can find candidates on market state alone.
        candidates = candidates.drop(
            [c for c in ("prior_kol_entries", "seconds_since_first_kol_entry")
             if c in candidates.columns]
        )
        console.print("[dim]Roster-presence features excluded[/dim]")

    try:
        result = train_ranker(candidates, n_splits=n_splits)
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as exc:
        _fail(str(exc))
        return

    for note in result.notes:
        console.print(f"[yellow]![/yellow] {note}")

    console.print(
        f"\n[bold]{result.n_groups:,} choice sets[/bold] Â· "
        f"{result.mean_candidates:.1f} candidates each"
    )

    table = Table("Fold", "Test groups", "NDCG@5", "Hit@1", "vs random", "vs volume")
    for fold in result.folds:
        table.add_row(
            str(fold.fold),
            f"{fold.test_groups:,}",
            f"{fold.ndcg_at_5:.3f}",
            f"{fold.hit_at_1:.1%}",
            f"{fold.lift_over_random:+.1%}",
            f"{fold.lift_over_volume:+.1%}",
        )
    console.print(table)

    if result.beats_baselines:
        console.print(
            f"[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Beats both baselines on every fold "
            f"(mean hit@1 {result.mean_hit_at_1:.1%}, "
            f"{result.mean_lift_over_volume:+.1%} over rank-by-volume)."
        )
    else:
        console.print(
            "[bold red]âœ—[/bold red] Does not beat both naive baselines on every "
            "fold. Absolute NDCG is not evidence â€” random ordering already "
            "scores highly with few candidates. This model has learned nothing "
            "beyond an expensive sort."
        )

    if not result.importance.is_empty():
        imp = Table("Feature", "Gain")
        for row in result.importance.head(10).iter_rows(named=True):
            imp.add_row(row["feature"], f"{row['gain']:,.0f}")
        console.print(imp)
        result.importance.write_parquet(
            settings.artifacts_dir / "rank_importance.parquet"
        )

    with (settings.artifacts_dir / "ranker.pkl").open("wb") as handle:
        pickle.dump(
            {"model": result.model, "features": result.features_used},
            handle,
            protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL,
        )
    console.print(f"[dim]Model â†’ {settings.artifacts_dir / 'ranker.pkl'}[/dim]")


@app.command()
def score(
    chain: str = typer.Option("polymarket", "--chain"),
    venue: str = typer.Option(
        None, "--venue",
        help="Solana: which board to score (e.g. pump-bonding-curve, raydium-amm-v4)",
    ),
    top: int = typer.Option(10, "--top", help="How many to show"),
) -> None:
    """Rank today's candidates by how KOL-like they look.

    Scores are ordinal within one snapshot â€” only their order is meaningful,
    and comparing across snapshots is not valid.
    """
    import pickle
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    from .choice.rank import RankerResult, score_candidates

    settings = get_settings()
    model_path = settings.artifacts_dir / "ranker.pkl"
    if not model_path.exists():
        _fail("No trained ranker. Run `pattern-ml rank` first.")

    if chain not in ("polymarket", "solana"):
        _fail(f"No snapshot provider for {chain!r}.")

    with model_path.open("rb") as handle:
        bundle = pickle.load(handle)

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    if chain == "polymarket":
        from .choice.providers.polymarket import PolymarketSnapshotProvider
        from .choice.schema import PolymarketScreen

        screen = PolymarketScreen()
        with PolymarketSnapshotProvider() as provider:
            universe = provider.candidates_at(now, limit=100)
    else:
        from .choice.providers.solana import SolanaSnapshotProvider
        from .choice.schema import PumpFunScreen, SolanaScreen
        from .venues import KIND_BONDING_CURVE, venue_kind

        if not settings.bitquery_token:
            _fail("BITQUERY_TOKEN is not set.")
        # The screen must match the board being scored, exactly as in training:
        # scoring a launchpad universe through the AMM screen would filter on a
        # field the curve query never fills.
        screen = (
            PumpFunScreen()
            if venue_kind(venue or "") == KIND_BONDING_CURVE
            else SolanaScreen()
        )
        with SolanaSnapshotProvider() as provider:
            universe = provider.candidates_at(now, limit=100, venue=venue)

    passing = [c for c in universe if screen.passes(c)]
    if not passing:
        _fail(
            "No candidates passed the screen right now."
            + (
                f" (venue={venue or 'all AMMs'})"
                if chain == "solana"
                else ""
            )
        )

    frame = pl.DataFrame(passing, infer_schema_length=None, strict=False)
    for column in bundle["features"]:
        if column not in frame.columns:
            frame = frame.with_columns(pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Float64).alias(column))

    result = RankerResult(
        model=bundle["model"],
        features_used=bundle["features"],
        folds=[],
        importance=pl.DataFrame(),
        n_groups=0,
        mean_candidates=0.0,
    )
    ranked = score_candidates(result, frame)

    console.print(f"[bold]Top {top} candidates â€” {now:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC}[/bold]")
    table = Table("Rank", "Market", "Price", "24h vol", "Score")
    for i, row in enumerate(ranked.head(top).iter_rows(named=True), start=1):
        label = (row.get("market_label") or row["market_id"])[:52]
        price = row.get("price")
        volume = row.get("volume_24h_usd")
        table.add_row(
            str(i),
            label,
            f"{price:.3f}" if price is not None else "â€”",
            f"${volume:,.0f}" if volume is not None else "â€”",
            f"{row['score']:.3f}",
        )
    console.print(table)
    console.print(
        "\n[dim]A ranking, not a recommendation. Nothing here has been tested "
        "forward on decisions that had not yet happened.[/dim]"
    )

@app.command()
def validate(
    entry_slippage: float = typer.Option(150.0, "--entry-slippage-bps"),
    exit_slippage: float = typer.Option(150.0, "--exit-slippage-bps"),
    fee: float = typer.Option(30.0, "--fee-bps"),
    kol: str = typer.Option(None, "--kol", help="Restrict to one KOL address"),
) -> None:
    """Backtest as a follower, with frictions, against a random-pick null.

    Runs directly against the position table, so it works without a model: this
    measures what copying the roster itself would have returned.
    """
    from .validate import backtest as bt

    settings = get_settings()
    storage = get_storage()

    everything = storage.get_positions(labelled_only=True)
    if everything.is_empty():
        _fail("No labelled positions. Run `pattern-ml positions` first.")

    selection = everything
    if kol:
        selection = everything.filter(pl.col("kol_address") == kol)
        if selection.is_empty():
            _fail(f"No labelled positions for {kol}.")
        console.print(f"[bold]Backtesting {kol}[/bold]")
    else:
        console.print("[bold]Backtesting every labelled position[/bold]")

    frictions = bt.Frictions(
        entry_slippage_bps=entry_slippage,
        exit_slippage_bps=exit_slippage,
        fee_bps_per_side=fee,
    )
    console.print(
        f"[dim]Frictions: {entry_slippage:.0f}/{exit_slippage:.0f} bps slippage, "
        f"{fee:.0f} bps fee per side "
        f"({frictions.round_trip_cost:.2%} round trip)[/dim]"
    )

    result = bt.backtest(selection, frictions=frictions)
    for note in result.notes:
        console.print(f"[yellow]![/yellow] {note}")

    if result.n_positions == 0:
        _fail("Nothing left to backtest after filtering.")

    null = bt.null_baseline(everything, result.n_positions, frictions=frictions)
    verdict = bt.significance_vs_null(result, null)

    table = Table("Metric", "Value")
    table.add_row("Positions", f"{result.n_positions:,}")
    table.add_row("Win rate (after costs)", f"{result.win_rate:.1%}")
    table.add_row("Mean ROI", f"{result.mean_roi:+.2%}")
    table.add_row("Median ROI", f"{result.median_roi:+.2%}")
    table.add_row("ROI 95% CI", f"{result.roi_ci[0]:+.2%} â€¦ {result.roi_ci[1]:+.2%}")
    table.add_row("Total return", f"{result.total_return:+.1%}")
    table.add_row("Max drawdown", f"{result.max_drawdown:.1%}")
    if result.sharpe is not None:
        table.add_row("Sharpe (per position)", f"{result.sharpe:.2f}")
    if kol:
        table.add_row("Random-pick mean ROI", f"{null['mean_roi']:+.2%}")
        table.add_row("Edge over random", f"{verdict['edge']:+.2%}")
    console.print(table)

    if result.is_profitable:
        console.print(
            "[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Profitable after follower frictions."
        )
    else:
        console.print(
            "[bold red]âœ—[/bold red] Not profitable once follower frictions are "
            "applied. Copying this roster as-is loses money."
        )

    settings.artifacts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result.equity_curve.write_parquet(settings.artifacts_dir / "equity_curve.parquet")

@app.command()
def archive(
    include_model: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--include-model", help="Also snapshot model.pkl (megabytes per run)"
    ),
) -> None:
    """Snapshot the current artefacts and write a readable report.

    Runs overwrite `artifacts/`, so without this a previous run's claims are
    gone â€” and comparing what a pattern claimed last month against what it did
    this month is the only test that isn't purely retrospective.
    """
    from .report import new_run_id, snapshot_run, write_report

    run_id = new_run_id()
    destination = snapshot_run(run_id, include_model=include_model)
    if destination is None:
        _fail("Nothing to archive yet.")

    report = write_report(destination, run_id=run_id)
    write_report(get_settings().artifacts_dir, run_id=f"{run_id} (latest)")

    console.print(f"[bold green]âœ“[/bold green] Archived run [bold]{run_id}[/bold]")
    console.print(f"[dim]{destination}[/dim]")
    console.print(f"[dim]Report: {report}[/dim]")


@app.command()
def runs() -> None:
    """List archived runs."""
    from .report import list_runs

    archived = list_runs()
    if not archived:
        console.print("[yellow]No archived runs.[/yellow] Run `pattern-ml archive`.")
        return

    table = Table("Run", "Patterns", "Survivors", "Report")
    for directory in archived:
        patterns = directory / "sequence_patterns.parquet"
        tested = survivors = "â€”"
        if patterns.exists():
            frame = pl.read_parquet(patterns)
            tested = f"{frame.height:,}"
            survivors = f"{frame.filter(pl.col('survives_fdr')).height:,}"
        table.add_row(
            directory.name,
            tested,
            survivors,
            "yes" if (directory / "REPORT.md").exists() else "no",
        )
    console.print(table)


@app.command("run-all")
def run_all(
    kols: Path = typer.Option(None, "--kols"),
    skip_pull: bool = typer.Option(False, "--skip-pull", help="Reuse data/raw/"),
    with_choice_sets: str = typer.Option(
        None,
        "--with-choice-sets",
        help="Also assemble + train for these chains, e.g. 'polymarket,solana'.",
    ),
    max_decisions: int = typer.Option(
        None, "--max-decisions", help="Cap decisions per chain. Strongly advised."
    ),
) -> None:
    """Run the deterministic stages end to end.

    Choice-set assembly is **opt-in** rather than part of the default chain. It
    is the one stage whose cost scales with your data rather than being bounded
    by the roster: Bitquery bills points per query on Solana, and Polymarket
    costs two requests per candidate per decision. A `run-all` that silently
    burned a quota would be a bad default, so it is requested explicitly.
    """
    if not skip_pull:
        pull(kols=kols, chains="solana,polymarket")
        console.print()
    index()
    console.print()
    positions()
    console.print()

    chains = [c.strip() for c in (with_choice_sets or "").split(",") if c.strip()]
    for chain in chains:
        # Every parameter is passed explicitly. Calling a Typer-decorated
        # function directly leaves any omitted argument as an `OptionInfo`
        # sentinel rather than its default value, which fails deep inside the
        # stage instead of here.
        choice_sets(
            chain=chain,
            min_volume=50_000.0,
            min_completion=0.70,
            max_candidates=20,
            max_decisions=max_decisions,
            same_category=True,
            fetch_liquidity=False,
        )
        console.print()
    if chains:
        rank(n_splits=4, drop_kol_features=False)
        console.print()
    else:
        # Say what was skipped. A stage missing from a run reads as "covered
        # everything" unless the omission is stated.
        console.print(
            "[dim]choice-sets/rank skipped â€” pass --with-choice-sets "
            "polymarket,solana to include them.[/dim]\n"
        )

    validate(entry_slippage=150.0, exit_slippage=150.0, fee=30.0, kol=None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

==> pattern-ml/src/pattern_ml/config.py <==
"""Configuration and KOL roster loading.

Everything pattern_ml reads or writes lives under this package's own directory.
The one exception is *reading* the repo-root ``.env`` as a fallback for API
keys, so a Helius key doesn't have to be duplicated. Nothing is ever written
outside the project directory.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from dotenv import load_dotenv

# src/pattern_ml/config.py -> pattern-ml/
PACKAGE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PROJECT_ROOT = PACKAGE_ROOT.parent.parent
REPO_ROOT = PROJECT_ROOT.parent

Chain = str  # "solana" | "polymarket"
CHAINS: tuple[str, ...] = ("solana", "polymarket")


def _load_env() -> None:
    """Load the local .env first, then fall back to the repo-root .env.

    ``load_dotenv`` does not override already-set keys, so the local file wins
    and the repo-root file only fills gaps.
    """
    load_dotenv(PROJECT_ROOT / ".env")
    load_dotenv(REPO_ROOT / ".env")


def _env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    raw = os.getenv(name)
    if raw is None or raw.strip() == "":
        return default
    try:
        return float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return default


def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
    return int(_env_float(name, default))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Kol:
    """One tracked trader on one chain."""

    address: str
    chain: Chain
    handle: str | None = None
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    note: str | None = None
    since: datetime | None = None

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable identity for reports."""
        if self.handle:
            return self.handle
        return f"{self.address[:6]}â€¦{self.address[-4:]}"

    @property
    def key(self) -> str:
        """Stable unique id across chains."""
        return f"{self.chain}:{self.address}"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    helius_api_key: str | None
    bitquery_token: str | None
    polymarket_data_api: str
    data_dir: Path
    db_path: Path
    solana_max_rps: float
    polymarket_max_rps: float
    bitquery_max_rps: float
    source_concurrency: int

    @property
    def raw_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.data_dir / "raw"

    @property
    def checkpoint_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.data_dir / "checkpoints"

    @property
    def artifacts_dir(self) -> Path:
        return PROJECT_ROOT / "artifacts"

    @property
    def reports_dir(self) -> Path:
        return PROJECT_ROOT / "reports"

    def ensure_dirs(self) -> None:
        for path in (
            self.data_dir,
            self.raw_dir,
            self.checkpoint_dir,
            self.artifacts_dir,
            self.reports_dir,
        ):
            path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def _resolve(path_str: str) -> Path:
    path = Path(path_str)
    return path if path.is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / path


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)

    _load_env()
    return Settings(

        source_concurrency=_env_int("SOURCE_CONCURRENCY", 4),
    )


class KolRosterError(RuntimeError):
    """The KOL roster is missing or malformed."""


def _coerce_since(value: object) -> datetime | None:
    if value is None or value == "":
        return None
    if isinstance(value, datetime):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    raise KolRosterError(f"Unparseable `since` value: {value!r}")


def _normalize_address(address: object, chain: Chain) -> str:
    if not isinstance(address, str) or not address.strip():
        raise KolRosterError(f"A {chain} entry is missing a non-empty `address`")
    addr = address.strip()
    # Tolerate chain-prefixed addresses pasted over from the main SWAT DB.
    for prefix in ("solana:", "polygon:", "polymarket:", "robinhood-chain:"):
        if addr.lower().startswith(prefix):
            addr = addr[len(prefix) :]
            break
    if chain == "polymarket":
        # EVM addresses are case-insensitive; lowercase so joins can't miss.
        if not addr.lower().startswith("0x") or len(addr) != 42:
            raise KolRosterError(
                f"Polymarket address must be a 42-char 0xâ€¦ EVM address, got {addr!r}"
            )
        return addr.lower()
    # Solana base58 is case-SENSITIVE â€” never fold case here.
    if addr.lower().startswith("0x"):
        raise KolRosterError(
            f"{addr!r} looks like an EVM address but is listed under `solana:`"
        )
    return addr


def load_kols(path: Path | None = None) -> list[Kol]:
    """Read the curated KOL roster.

    Returns every tracked trader across all chains, in file order.
    """
    roster_path = path or (PROJECT_ROOT / "config" / "kols.yaml")
    if not roster_path.exists():
        example = PROJECT_ROOT / "config" / "kols.example.yaml"
        raise KolRosterError(
            f"No KOL roster at {roster_path}.\n"
            f"Create one with:  cp {example} {roster_path}\n"
            "then add the wallet addresses you want to track."
        )

    data = yaml.safe_load(roster_path.read_text()) or {}
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise KolRosterError(f"{roster_path} must be a YAML mapping")

    defaults = data.get("defaults") or {}
    default_since = _coerce_since(defaults.get("since"))

    kols: list[Kol] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for chain in CHAINS:
        entries = data.get(chain) or []
        if not isinstance(entries, list):
            raise KolRosterError(f"`{chain}` in {roster_path} must be a list")
        for entry in entries:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                raise KolRosterError(
                    f"Each `{chain}` entry must be a mapping with an `address`"
                )
            address = _normalize_address(entry.get("address"), chain)
            kol = Kol(
                address=address,
                chain=chain,
                handle=(entry.get("handle") or None),
                tags=tuple(entry.get("tags") or ()),
                note=(entry.get("note") or None),
                since=_coerce_since(entry.get("since")) or default_since,
            )
            if kol.key in seen:
                raise KolRosterError(f"Duplicate address in roster: {kol.key}")
            seen.add(kol.key)
            kols.append(kol)

    if not kols:
        raise KolRosterError(
            f"{roster_path} has no KOLs yet. Add at least one address under "
            "`solana:` or `polymarket:`."
        )
    return kols
