==> tests/integration/copy-position-tenancy.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { describe, it, expect, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { Keypair } from '@swat/shared';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { createUser } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';
import {
  recordSourceTradeEvent,
  requestCopyExecution,
  recordCopyExecutionEvidence
} from '../../packages/db/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.js';

/**
 * Tenancy key on `copy_positions` (checklist S4-10, migration 050).
 *
 * **The bug this locks down.** `copy_positions` used to be keyed
 * `PRIMARY KEY (target_account, chain, token_mint)`. In live mode each user
 * trades from a distinct address, so that key separated users by accident. In
 * paper mode `resolvePaperCopyTargetAccount(chain)` returns ONE synthetic
 * address per chain with no user dimension, so every paper user on a chain
 * collapsed onto a single row: user A's buy inflated user B's
 * `confirmed_quantity`, and B's exit computed P&L against A's cost basis. Paper
 * is the default mode for every free-tier user, so this was the common path.
 *
 * **These assertions fail against the old key**, which is the point of writing
 * them â€” the first test's second INSERT raises `23505 unique_violation` under a
 * three-column primary key, and the migration is what makes it pass.
 *
 * **Why this suite is at the schema level.** The property under test is a
 * property of the DDL, not of any one query helper, and it has to hold for every
 * writer including ones not yet written. Testing it here means a future migration
 * that drops `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` or narrows the index fails immediately rather
 * than at whichever call site happens to notice first.
 *
 * **Still owed:** an end-to-end assertion driving two paper users through
 * `requestCopyExecution` / `recordCopyExecutionEvidence` and comparing the
 * resulting ledgers. That needs tenancy threaded through
 * `tests/integration/helpers/lifecycle-fixture.ts`, which does not carry a user
 * dimension yet. The schema guarantees below are necessary for that test to pass
 * but are not a substitute for it.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const userIds: string[] = [];
const targetAccounts: string[] = [];

/** The shared synthetic address paper mode settles from â€” deliberately not per-user. */
function paperTarget(suffix: string): string {
  const account = `solana:${Keypair.generate().publicKey.toBase58()}`;
  targetAccounts.push(account);
  return account;
}

async function makeUser() {
  const user = await createUser({
    email: `s4-10-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
    password: 'a-very-long-password',
    tier: 'free'
  });
  userIds.push(user.id);
  return user;
}

afterAll(async () => {
  // Order matters: `copy_positions.user_id` is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so positions
  // must go before the users they belong to. That ordering is itself asserted
  // below â€” deleting a user out from under financial history must not be
  // possible.
  if (targetAccounts.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lot_reductions WHERE lot_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_position_master_lots WHERE position_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = ANY($1)))', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lots WHERE position_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = ANY($1))', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_applications WHERE execution_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_executions WHERE target_account = ANY($1))', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_execution_evidence WHERE execution_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_executions WHERE target_account = ANY($1))', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_execution_state_history WHERE execution_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_executions WHERE target_account = ANY($1))', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_executions WHERE target_account = ANY($1)', [targetAccounts]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = ANY($1)', [targetAccounts]);
  }
  await pool.query("DELETE FROM source_position_applications WHERE source_trade_id IN (SELECT id FROM source_trades WHERE source_event_id LIKE 'tx:' || $1 || ':%')", [runId]);
  await pool.query("DELETE FROM source_trade_confirmation_history WHERE source_trade_id IN (SELECT id FROM source_trades WHERE source_event_id LIKE 'tx:' || $1 || ':%')", [runId]);
  await pool.query("DELETE FROM source_trades WHERE source_event_id LIKE 'tx:' || $1 || ':%'", [runId]);
  if (userIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
  }
  // Deliberately no `pool.end()`. The pool is shared across integration files
  // (globalSetup closes its own separate one for exactly this reason), so
  // closing it here would break whichever file vitest runs next.
});

describe('copy_positions tenancy (S4-10)', () => {
  it('gives two paper users independent positions behind one shared target account', async () => {
    const [alice, bob] = [await makeUser(), await makeUser()];
    const target = paperTarget('A');
    const token = `TOKEN${runId}`;

    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,$3)`,
      [target, token, alice.id]
    );
    // Against the old three-column primary key this raises 23505. It is the
    // whole regression: same target, same chain, same token, different tenant.
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,$3)`,
      [target, token, bob.id]
    );

    const { rows } = await pool.query<{ user_id: string; id: string }>(
      `SELECT id, user_id FROM copy_positions
        WHERE target_account = $1 AND chain = 'solana' AND token_mint = $2
        ORDER BY user_id`,
      [target, token]
    );

    expect(rows).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(new Set(rows.map((r) => r.id)).size).toBe(2);
    expect(new Set(rows.map((r) => r.user_id))).toEqual(new Set([alice.id, bob.id]));
  });

  it('keeps quantities and cost bases from bleeding between tenants', async () => {
    const [alice, bob] = [await makeUser(), await makeUser()];
    const target = paperTarget('B');
    const token = `TOKEN${runId}`;

    for (const userId of [alice.id, bob.id]) {
      await pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,$3)`,
        [target, token, userId]
      );
    }

    // Alice buys. Under the old key this write landed on the row Bob also read.
    await pool.query(
      `UPDATE copy_positions
          SET confirmed_quantity = 500, cost_basis_usd = 1000
        WHERE target_account = $1 AND chain = 'solana' AND token_mint = $2 AND user_id = $3`,
      [target, token, alice.id]
    );

    const read = async (userId: string) => {
      const { rows } = await pool.query<{ confirmed_quantity: number; cost_basis_usd: number }>(
        `SELECT confirmed_quantity, cost_basis_usd FROM copy_positions
          WHERE target_account = $1 AND chain = 'solana' AND token_mint = $2 AND user_id = $3`,
        [target, token, userId]
      );
      return rows[0]!;
    };

    expect(await read(alice.id)).toMatchObject({ confirmed_quantity: 500, cost_basis_usd: 1000 });
    // Bob's exit would otherwise compute P&L against Alice's basis.
    expect(await read(bob.id)).toMatchObject({ confirmed_quantity: 0, cost_basis_usd: 0 });
  });

  it('still collapses legacy operator rows, because NULLS NOT DISTINCT is load-bearing', async () => {
    const target = paperTarget('C');
    const token = `TOKEN${runId}`;

    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,NULL)`,
      [target, token]
    );

    // Under PostgreSQL's default NULLS DISTINCT, two NULL-tenant rows would NOT
    // collide â€” so migration 050 would have *removed* the uniqueness that
    // existed before it while appearing to add a dimension, and every
    // `ensureCopyPosition` call for the operator would insert a fresh duplicate
    // until the ledger fragmented silently. This assertion is what stops a
    // future migration quietly dropping that clause.
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,NULL)`,
        [target, token]
      )
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23505' });
  });

  it('refuses to delete a user who still owns financial history', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const target = paperTarget('D');

    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) VALUES ($1,'solana',$2,$3)`,
      [target, `TOKEN${runId}`, user.id]
    );

    // ON DELETE RESTRICT, not CASCADE. `copy_positions` is the ledger `trades`
    // is derived from; a DELETE FROM users must not destroy the evidence chain
    // behind a retained trade. Users with financial rows are soft-deleted.
    await expect(
      pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1', [user.id])
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23503' });
  });

  it('is keyed on a single surrogate column, so the migration can replay', async () => {
    // Migration 050 guards its constraint drops on `cardinality(conkey)` rather
    // than on name, because the replacement primary key reuses the name
    // `copy_positions_pkey`. If the key were ever three columns again, that
    // guard would drop the live key on the next `pnpm db:migrate` â€” and
    // migrate.ts replays every file on every invocation.
    const { rows } = await pool.query<{ n: number }>(
      `SELECT cardinality(conkey)::int AS n
         FROM pg_constraint
        WHERE conrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass AND contype = 'p'`
    );
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[0]!.n).toBe(1);
  });

  it('drives two paper users through execution and evidence with completely disjoint ledgers', async () => {
    const [alice, bob] = [await makeUser(), await makeUser()];
    const target = paperTarget('E');
    const master = `solana:${Keypair.generate().publicKey.toBase58()}`;
    const token = `solana:${Keypair.generate().publicKey.toBase58()}`;
    const occurredAt = new Date('2026-10-01T00:00:00Z');

    const sourceEventId = `tx:${runId}:1`;
    const source = await recordSourceTradeEvent({
      chain: 'solana',
      sourceEventType: 'transaction',
      sourceEventId,
      transactionHash: sourceEventId,
      walletAddress: master,
      tokenMint: token,
      side: 'buy',
      quantity: '100',
      amountUsd: 1000,
      eventAt: occurredAt,
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      confirmationEvidenceId: randomUUID()
    });

    const aliceExec = await requestCopyExecution({
      sourceTradeId: source.event.id,
      targetAccount: target,
      executionMode: 'paper',
      userId: alice.id,
      requestedBaseQuantity: '10'
    });

    const bobExec = await requestCopyExecution({
      sourceTradeId: source.event.id,
      targetAccount: target,
      executionMode: 'paper',
      userId: bob.id,
      requestedBaseQuantity: '20'
    });

    expect(aliceExec.execution.id).not.toBe(bobExec.execution.id);
    expect(aliceExec.execution.userId).toBe(alice.id);
    expect(bobExec.execution.userId).toBe(bob.id);

    await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
      executionId: aliceExec.execution.id,
      evidenceType: 'paper_simulation',
      evidenceId: aliceExec.execution.clientOrderId,
      baseQuantity: '10',
      quoteLeg: { currency: 'USD', amount: 100 },
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      completesExecution: true,
      occurredAt
    });

    await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
      executionId: bobExec.execution.id,
      evidenceType: 'paper_simulation',
      evidenceId: bobExec.execution.clientOrderId,
      baseQuantity: '20',
      quoteLeg: { currency: 'USD', amount: 200 },
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      completesExecution: true,
      occurredAt
    });

    const { rows: positions } = await pool.query<{
      user_id: string;
      confirmed_quantity: string;
      cost_basis_usd: string;
    }>(
      `SELECT user_id, confirmed_quantity::text, cost_basis_usd::text
         FROM copy_positions
        WHERE target_account = $1 AND token_mint = $2
        ORDER BY user_id`,
      [target, token]
    );

    expect(positions).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(positions.find(p => p.user_id === alice.id)).toMatchObject({
      confirmed_quantity: '10',
      cost_basis_usd: '100'
    });
    expect(positions.find(p => p.user_id === bob.id)).toMatchObject({
      confirmed_quantity: '20',
      cost_basis_usd: '200'
    });

    const { rows: lots } = await pool.query<{
      user_id: string;
      remaining_quantity: string;
    }>(
      `SELECT user_id, remaining_quantity::text
         FROM copy_position_master_lots
        WHERE token_mint = $1
        ORDER BY user_id`,
      [token]
    );

    expect(lots).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(lots.find(l => l.user_id === alice.id)?.remaining_quantity).toBe('10');
    expect(lots.find(l => l.user_id === bob.id)?.remaining_quantity).toBe('20');
  });
});

async function ensureSignalToken(tokenMint: string, chain: string): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO tokens (mint, chain) VALUES ($1, $2)

      expect(simulatedRetry).toMatchObject({

        nextState: 'reconciliation_required',
        reason: 'fixture requires reconciliation',
        nextReconciliationAt: new Date(Date.now() + 1_000)
      });

      expect(reconciliationRetry).toMatchObject({
        created: false,
        execution: { id: claimed.execution?.id, state: 'reconciliation_required' }
      });

        completesExecution: false,
        occurredAt: now
      };

      const replay = await recordCopyExecutionEvidence(evidence);

        `SELECT
           COUNT(evidence.id)::int AS evidence_count,
           execution.confirmed_base_quantity::text AS confirmed_quantity
         FROM copy_executions execution
         LEFT JOIN copy_execution_evidence evidence ON evidence.execution_id = execution.id

        [claimed.execution!.id]
      );

      expect(first.execution.state).toBe('partially_filled');
      expect(replay.execution.confirmedBaseQuantity).toBe('2');
      expect(stored).toEqual({ evidence_count: 1, confirmed_quantity: '2' });
    }, 'polygon');

==> tests/integration/cross-tenant.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID, createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import Fastify, { type FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import cookie from '@fastify/cookie';
import { Redis } from 'ioredis';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { forUser, listAuthWallets, linkAuthWallet } from '../../packages/db/src/index.js';
import { registerAuth, requireUser, requireRole } from '../../apps/api/src/auth/plugin.js';
import { registerAuthRoutes } from '../../apps/api/src/auth/routes.js';

/**
 * Cross-tenant isolation suite (D12, checklist S1-16).
 *
 * This exists to run **before** Stage 2 adds `/v1/me/*` routes, not after. Its
 * job is to make tenant leakage a test failure rather than a code review
 * question, and to keep doing so as routes are added.
 *
 * It builds a minimal Fastify app around the *real* auth plugin and routes
 * rather than importing `apps/api/src/index.ts`, which opens Redis connections
 * and BullMQ queues at module scope â€” importing it would start a second API
 * against the test database. Same constraint the pipeline suite documents for
 * `signal-engine`.
 */

const DOMAIN = 'app.swat.test';
const URI = 'https://app.swat.test';
const LEGACY_KEY = 'cross-tenant-suite-legacy-key';

interface Actor {
  readonly email: string;
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly cookies: string;
  readonly csrf: string;
}

let app: FastifyInstance;
let redis: Redis;
const createdUserIds: string[] = [];

async function buildApp(): Promise<FastifyInstance> {
  const instance = Fastify({ logger: false });
  await instance.register(cookie);

  await registerAuth(instance, {
    legacyKeyHash: createHash('sha256').update(LEGACY_KEY).digest(),
    isProduction: false,
    consumeSseTicket: async () => false
  });

  await registerAuthRoutes(instance, {
    redis,
    isProduction: false,
    domain: DOMAIN,
    uri: URI
  });

  /**
   * Stand-in for a Stage 2 `/v1/me/*` route: reads user-owned rows through the
   * scope that `requireUser` derives from the session. If scoping regresses,
   * this route starts returning another tenant's wallets.
   */
  instance.get('/v1/me/wallets', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const wallets = await listAuthWallets(scope);
    return reply.send({ wallets: wallets.map((w) => w.address) });
  });

  /** Stand-in for an admin-only route. */
  instance.get('/v1/admin/ping', async (request, reply) => {
    const user = requireRole(request, reply, 'admin');
    if (!user) return;
    return reply.send({ ok: true });
  });

  await instance.ready();
  return instance;
}

async function signup(email: string): Promise<Actor> {
  const response = await app.inject({
    method: 'POST',
    url: '/v1/auth/signup',
    payload: { email, password: 'a-very-long-password' }
  });
  if (response.statusCode !== 201) {
    throw new Error(`signup failed for ${email}: ${response.statusCode} ${response.body}`);
  }
  const setCookies = response.headers['set-cookie'];
  const raw = Array.isArray(setCookies) ? setCookies : [String(setCookies)];
  const cookies = raw.map((c) => c.split(';')[0]).join('; ');
  const csrf = /swat_csrf=([^;]+)/.exec(cookies)?.[1] ?? '';
  const userId = (JSON.parse(response.body) as { user: { id: string } }).user.id;
  createdUserIds.push(userId);
  return { email, userId, cookies, csrf };
}

beforeAll(async () => {
  redis = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL ?? 'redis://localhost:6379', {
    maxRetriesPerRequest: null
  });
  app = await buildApp();
});

afterAll(async () => {
  await app?.close();
  await redis?.quit();
  if (createdUserIds.length > 0) {
    // user_auth_wallets and user_sessions cascade from users.
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [createdUserIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [createdUserIds]);
  }
});

describe('cross-tenant isolation', () => {
  it("does not leak one tenant's wallets to another", async () => {
    const alice = await signup(`alice-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const bob = await signup(`bob-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);

    // Give each a distinct linked wallet, written through the scoped helper.
    await linkAuthWallet(forUser(alice.userId), {
      chainKind: 'evm',
      address: `0xa${alice.userId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 39)}`
    });
    await linkAuthWallet(forUser(bob.userId), {
      chainKind: 'evm',
      address: `0xb${bob.userId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 39)}`
    });

    const aliceView = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/me/wallets',
      headers: { cookie: alice.cookies }
    });
    const bobView = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/me/wallets',
      headers: { cookie: bob.cookies }
    });

    expect(aliceView.statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(bobView.statusCode).toBe(200);
    const aliceWallets = (JSON.parse(aliceView.body) as { wallets: string[] }).wallets;
    const bobWallets = (JSON.parse(bobView.body) as { wallets: string[] }).wallets;

    expect(aliceWallets).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(bobWallets).toHaveLength(1);
    // The actual isolation assertion: disjoint, and neither contains the other's.
    expect(aliceWallets).not.toEqual(bobWallets);
    expect(aliceWallets[0]).not.toBe(bobWallets[0]);
  });

  it('rejects a request with no credential', async () => {
    const response = await app.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/v1/me/wallets' });
    expect(response.statusCode).toBe(401);
  });

  it('rejects the tenant-less service key on a per-user route', async () => {
    // The legacy shared key predates tenancy. If it satisfied a `/v1/me/*` route
    // there would be no tenant to scope by, so `requireUser` must refuse it â€”
    // this is a cross-tenant hole by construction, not a policy choice.
    const response = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/me/wallets',
      headers: { 'x-api-key': LEGACY_KEY }
    });
    expect(response.statusCode).toBe(401);
  });

  it('does not let a normal user reach an admin route', async () => {
    const user = await signup(`user-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const response = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/admin/ping',
      headers: { cookie: user.cookies }
    });
    expect(response.statusCode).toBe(403);
  });

  it("rejects one tenant's CSRF token paired with another's session", async () => {
    const alice = await signup(`csrfa-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const bob = await signup(`csrfb-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);

    // Alice's session cookie, Bob's CSRF token. Double-submit must compare the
    // header against *this request's* cookie, so a token lifted from another
    // session is useless.
    const aliceSessionOnly = alice.cookies
      .split('; ')
      .filter((c) => c.startsWith('swat_session='))
      .join('; ');

    const response = await app.inject({
      method: 'POST',
      url: '/v1/auth/logout',
      headers: { cookie: aliceSessionOnly, 'x-csrf-token': bob.csrf }
    });
    expect(response.statusCode).toBe(403);
  });

  it('revokes only the logging-out tenantâ€™s session', async () => {
    const alice = await signup(`revoke-a-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const bob = await signup(`revoke-b-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);

    const logout = await app.inject({
      method: 'POST',
      url: '/v1/auth/logout',
      headers: { cookie: alice.cookies, 'x-csrf-token': alice.csrf }
    });
    expect(logout.statusCode).toBe(200);

    const aliceAfter = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/auth/me',
      headers: { cookie: alice.cookies }
    });
    const bobAfter = await app.inject({
      method: 'GET',
      url: '/v1/auth/me',
      headers: { cookie: bob.cookies }
    });

    expect(aliceAfter.statusCode).toBe(401);
    // Bob must be untouched: a revoke-all bug would show up here and nowhere else.
    expect(bobAfter.statusCode).toBe(200);
  });

  it('will not link a wallet already owned by another tenant', async () => {
    const alice = await signup(`link-a-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const bob = await signup(`link-b-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const shared = `0xc${alice.userId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 39)}`;

    await linkAuthWallet(forUser(alice.userId), { chainKind: 'evm', address: shared });

    // Silently re-pointing a verified wallet would hand over its role as a
    // Stage 4 withdrawal destination.
    await expect(
      linkAuthWallet(forUser(bob.userId), { chainKind: 'evm', address: shared })
    ).rejects.toThrow(/already linked/i);
  });

  it('treats re-linking a tenantâ€™s own wallet as idempotent', async () => {
    const alice = await signup(`idem-${randomUUID()}@example.com`);
    const address = `0xd${alice.userId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 39)}`;
    const scope = forUser(alice.userId);

    const first = await linkAuthWallet(scope, { chainKind: 'evm', address });
    const second = await linkAuthWallet(scope, { chainKind: 'evm', address });

    expect(second.id).toBe(first.id);
    expect(await listAuthWallets(scope)).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});

import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { listFanoutCandidates } from '../../packages/db/src/fanout-candidates.js';
import { planFanout } from '../../packages/db/src/fanout-eligibility.js';
import {
  beginWindDown,
  endSubscription,
  subscribeToWallet
} from '../../packages/db/src/subscriptions.js';
import { crossTenantScope, forUser } from '../../packages/db/src/tenancy.js';
import { upsertUserBalance } from '../../packages/db/src/user-balances.js';
import { upsertUserExecutionSettings } from '../../packages/db/src/user-execution-settings.js';
import { createUser, type UserRecord } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';

/**
 * The fetch half of fan-out enumeration (`S4-13`), against a real database.
 *
 * âš ï¸ **WRITTEN AND NEVER RUN.** There is no database on the branch this landed
 * on, so every assertion below is a claim about PostgreSQL's behaviour and not an
 * observation of it. `packages/db/src/fanout-candidates.test.ts` covers the
 * mapping and the statement text with a mocked `query`; what only PostgreSQL can
 * prove is here, and it is exactly the set of things a mocked test silently
 * passes:
 *
 *   1. **The statement parses and every column exists.** A mocked `query` never
 *      touches the grammar. In particular `copy_positions position` uses
 *      `position` as a table alias â€” a `col_name_keyword` â€” and the correlated
 *      scalar subquery reaches out to `subscription.user_id` from inside it.
 *   2. **`ended` is genuinely not enumerated** and `winding_down` genuinely is.
 *      The unit test can only assert that the predicate appears in the text.
 *   3. **A user with no `user_execution_settings` row survives the join.** The
 *      unit test asserts `LEFT JOIN` is written; only the database proves the row
 *      comes back.
 *   4. **A suspended account is excluded**, which is the one filter here with no
 *      double cover in `planFanout`.
 *   5. **The open-position count is what `copy_positions` actually holds** â€”
 *      `confirmed_quantity > 0`, every chain, this tenant only. `NULLS NOT
 *      DISTINCT` on `uq_copy_positions_account_chain_token_user` (migration
 *      `050`) means a legacy operator row shares the natural key space, so a
 *      count that leaked across tenants would be invisible in a unit test.
 *
 * Deliberately **not** asserted: that the planner chooses
 * `idx_uws_wallet_live`. On a table holding a handful of fixture rows it will
 * choose a sequential scan whatever the index says, so an `EXPLAIN` assertion
 * here would either be vacuous or would fail for the wrong reason.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const userIds: string[] = [];
const walletAddresses: string[] = [];
const targetAccounts: string[] = [];

const sweep = () => crossTenantScope('fan-out enumeration integration test');

function walletFor(suffix: string): string {
  const address = `solana:SWATfo${runId}${suffix}`.slice(0, 100);
  walletAddresses.push(address);
  return address;
}

async function makeUser(tier: 'free' | 'operator' | 'ultra' = 'ultra'): Promise<UserRecord> {
  const user = await createUser({
    email: `s414-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
    password: 'a-very-long-password',
    tier
  });
  userIds.push(user.id);
  return user;
}

async function subscribe(user: UserRecord, address: string) {
  return subscribeToWallet(forUser(user.id), {
    walletAddress: address,
    chain: 'solana',
    tier: user.tier,
    tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
  });
}

/** A funded, freshly priced balance, so the balance gate is not what excludes. */
async function fund(user: UserRecord, usd: number, chain: 'solana' | 'polygon' = 'solana') {
  await upsertUserBalance(forUser(user.id), {
    chain,
    asset: chain === 'solana' ? 'SOL' : 'USDC',
    amount: 1,
    decimals: chain === 'solana' ? 9 : 6,
    usd,
    usdPricedAt: new Date()
  });
}

async function openPosition(
  user: UserRecord,
  chain: 'solana' | 'polygon',
  tokenMint: string,
  confirmedQuantity: number
) {
  const targetAccount = `paper:${chain}:${runId}`;
  targetAccounts.push(targetAccount);
  await pool.query(
    `INSERT INTO copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id, confirmed_quantity)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
     ON CONFLICT (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id)
       DO UPDATE SET confirmed_quantity = EXCLUDED.confirmed_quantity`,
    [targetAccount, chain, tokenMint, user.id, confirmedQuantity]
  );
}

afterAll(async () => {
  if (targetAccounts.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = ANY($1)', [targetAccounts]);
  }
  if (walletAddresses.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_wallet_subscriptions WHERE wallet_address = ANY($1)', [
      walletAddresses
    ]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = ANY($1)', [walletAddresses]);
  }
  if (userIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_balances WHERE user_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_execution_settings WHERE user_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
  }
});

describe('listFanoutCandidates against PostgreSQL', () => {
  it('executes and returns the subscriber of a master wallet', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('exec');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 500);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });

    expect(candidates.map((candidate) => candidate.userId)).toEqual([user.id]);
    expect(candidates[0]).toMatchObject({
      subscriptionState: 'active',
      tier: 'ultra',
      openPositionCount: 0,
      knownBalanceUsd: 500
    });
  });

  it('returns nothing for a master nobody is subscribed to', async () => {
    const master = walletFor('lonely');
    // No `subscribeToWallet`, so no `wallets` row either â€” the query must simply
    // return zero rows rather than error.
    walletAddresses.pop();
    await expect(
      listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), { masterWalletAddress: master, chain: 'solana' })
    ).resolves.toEqual([]);
  });

  it('omits an ended subscription and keeps a winding-down one', async () => {
    const leaver = await makeUser();
    const winder = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('states');
    await subscribe(leaver, master);
    await subscribe(winder, master);
    await fund(leaver, 500);
    await fund(winder, 500);

    await endSubscription(forUser(leaver.id), master);
    await beginWindDown(forUser(winder.id), master);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });

    expect(candidates.map((candidate) => candidate.userId)).toEqual([winder.id]);
    expect(candidates[0]!.subscriptionState).toBe('winding_down');
  });

  it('lets a winding-down subscriber mirror a sell but not a buy', async () => {
    // The end-to-end version of the distinction `S4-13` exists to keep: dropping
    // these users strands the positions whose only exit is the master's sell.
    const winder = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('sells');
    await subscribe(winder, master);
    await fund(winder, 500);
    await upsertUserExecutionSettings(forUser(winder.id), { autoExecute: true });
    await beginWindDown(forUser(winder.id), master);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    const platform = {
      chainMode: { effectiveMode: 'paper' as const },
      minimumBalanceUsd: 0,
      capacity: { outcome: 'admit' as const }
    };
    const signal = {
      chain: 'solana' as const,
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      tokenMint: 'solana:SomeMint',
      score: 90,
      eventAt: new Date('2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z')
    };

    expect(planFanout(candidates, { ...signal, direction: 'sell' }, platform).eligible)
      .toHaveLength(1);
    expect(planFanout(candidates, { ...signal, direction: 'buy' }, platform).exclusionCounts)
      .toEqual({ 'winding-down-buy-refused': 1 });
  });

  it('returns a user who has no execution settings row, filled with the defaults', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('nosett');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 500);

    const rows = await pool.query('SELECT 1 FROM user_execution_settings WHERE user_id = $1', [
      user.id
    ]);
    expect(rows.rowCount).toBe(0);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    expect(candidates).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(candidates[0]).toMatchObject({
      autoExecute: false,
      killed: false,
      minSignalScore: 80,
      maxConcurrentPositions: 5
    });
  });

  it('reads a persisted settings row rather than the defaults', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('sett');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 500);
    await upsertUserExecutionSettings(forUser(user.id), {
      autoExecute: true,
      minSignalScore: 95,
      maxConcurrentPositions: 2
    });

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    expect(candidates[0]).toMatchObject({
      autoExecute: true,
      minSignalScore: 95,
      maxConcurrentPositions: 2
    });
  });

  it('omits a suspended account, the one filter planFanout cannot report', async () => {
    const suspended = await makeUser();
    const active = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('susp');
    await subscribe(suspended, master);
    await subscribe(active, master);
    await pool.query(`UPDATE users SET status = 'suspended' WHERE id = $1`, [suspended.id]);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    expect(candidates.map((candidate) => candidate.userId)).toEqual([active.id]);
  });

  it('counts open positions across chains and only for the asking tenant', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const other = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('poscnt');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 500);

    await openPosition(user, 'solana', 'solana:MintA', 5);
    await openPosition(user, 'polygon', 'polygon:0xaaa', 3);
    // Closed: must not count.
    await openPosition(user, 'solana', 'solana:MintClosed', 0);
    // Another tenant's position: must not count.
    await openPosition(other, 'solana', 'solana:MintB', 9);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    expect(candidates[0]!.openPositionCount).toBe(2);
  });

  it('reports an unpriced balance as unknown rather than as zero', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('unpr');

    await upsertUserBalance(forUser(user.id), {
      chain: 'solana',
      asset: 'BONK',
      amount: 1000,
      decimals: 5,
      usd: null
    });

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });
    expect(candidates[0]!.knownBalanceUsd).toBeNull();
  });

  it('reports a stale balance as unknown', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('stale');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 500);

    const candidates = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana',
      // The row was written with `fetched_at = NOW()`, so a one-millisecond
      // window makes it stale without touching the clock.
      balanceMaxAgeMs: 1,
      now: new Date(Date.now() + 60_000)
    });
    expect(candidates[0]!.knownBalanceUsd).toBeNull();
  });

  it('does not let one chain balance feed poison another chain fan-out', async () => {
    // The reason the balance read is chain-scoped: `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`
    // returns null on any unpriced row it is given, so a cross-chain sum would
    // stop Polymarket copying because a Solana token could not be priced.
    const user = await makeUser();
    const master = walletFor('chsc');
    await subscribe(user, master);
    await fund(user, 250, 'polygon');
    await upsertUserBalance(forUser(user.id), {
      chain: 'solana',
      asset: 'BONK',
      amount: 1000,
      decimals: 5,
      usd: null
    });

    const polygon = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'polygon'
    });
    const solana = await listFanoutCandidates(sweep(), {
      masterWalletAddress: master,
      chain: 'solana'
    });

    expect(polygon[0]!.knownBalanceUsd).toBe(250);
    expect(solana[0]!.knownBalanceUsd).toBeNull();
  });

  it('refuses a per-user scope against a real connection too', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    await expect(
      listFanoutCandidates(forUser(user.id), {
        masterWalletAddress: walletFor('scope'),
        chain: 'solana'
      })
    ).rejects.toThrow(/crossTenantScope/);
    walletAddresses.pop();
  });
});

==> tests/integration/funder-degree-cap.integration.test.ts <==
import { afterAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  closePool,
  generateFundingClusters,
  MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE,
  MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS,
  pool,
  query
} from '../../packages/db/src/index.js';

/**
 * S4-M11: the funder degree cap and hub exclusion, against real SQL.
 *
 * WRITTEN BUT NEVER RUN. No database was available in the session that produced
 * it, so treat every assertion here as unverified. It exists because two things
 * in S4-M11 cannot live in the pure predicate and therefore cannot be tested
 * without Postgres:
 *
 *  1. `BETWEEN ... AND ...` over `COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b)` -- the degree is
 *     an aggregate over a table. Pulling it into TypeScript would mean loading
 *     every funding edge into the scorer, so the band is evaluated in SQL and
 *     `assessFunderIndependence` is the testable statement of the same rule.
 *  2. Cluster teardown on demotion. That a funder crossing the ceiling loses its
 *     cluster is an emergent consequence of four statements running in order
 *     (membership DELETE -> membership INSERT -> recount -> empty-cluster
 *     DELETE). The unit test can only assert the statements and their order; only
 *     a database shows the row is gone.
 *
 * Requires `INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL`) on a `_integration` /
 * `_test` database -- `vitest.integration.config.ts` refuses otherwise.
 */

const CHAIN = 'solana';
const PREFIX = 's4m11';

function addr(name: string): string {
  return `${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-${name}`;
}

async function seedWallet(address: string, status = 'active'): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO wallets (address, chain, source, status)
     VALUES ($1, $2, 'manual', $3)
     ON CONFLICT (address) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status`,
    [address, CHAIN, status]
  );
}

/** Give `funder` `degree` distinct funded wallets, all seeded. */
async function seedFunding(funder: string, degree: number): Promise<void> {
  await seedWallet(funder);
  for (let i = 0; i < degree; i += 1) {
    const funded = addr(`${funder.split('-').pop()}-recipient-${i}`);
    await seedWallet(funded);
    await query(
      `INSERT INTO wallet_relationships (wallet_a, wallet_b, relationship_type, confidence)
       VALUES ($1, $2, 'funding', 0.60)
       ON CONFLICT (wallet_a, wallet_b, relationship_type) DO NOTHING`,
      [funder, funded]
    );
  }
}

async function fundingCluster(funder: string) {
  const rows = await query<{ id: string; wallet_count: number }>(
    `SELECT id, wallet_count FROM wallet_clusters
     WHERE cluster_type = 'funding' AND name = $1`,
    [`Funding Group ${funder}`]
  );
  return rows[0] ?? null;
}

async function cleanup(): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `DELETE FROM cluster_memberships
     WHERE wallet_address LIKE $1
        OR cluster_id IN (SELECT id FROM wallet_clusters WHERE name LIKE $2)`,
    [`${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-%`, `Funding Group ${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-%`]
  );
  await query(`DELETE FROM wallet_clusters WHERE name LIKE $1`, [
    `Funding Group ${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-%`
  ]);
  await query(`DELETE FROM wallet_relationships WHERE wallet_a LIKE $1 OR wallet_b LIKE $1`, [
    `${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-%`
  ]);
  await query(`DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address LIKE $1`, [`${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-%`]);
}

describe('funder degree cap', () => {
  beforeEach(cleanup);
  afterAll(async () => {
    await cleanup();
    await closePool();
  });

  it('clusters a person-scale funder', async () => {
    const funder = addr('friends');
    await seedFunding(funder, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS + 1);

    await generateFundingClusters();

    const cluster = await fundingCluster(funder);
    expect(cluster).not.toBeNull();
    // Funder plus each recipient.
    expect(Number(cluster?.wallet_count)).toBe(MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS + 2);
  });

  it('forms no cluster for a funder one wallet over the ceiling', async () => {
    const funder = addr('hotwallet');
    await seedFunding(funder, MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE + 1);

    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).toBeNull();
    const memberships = await query<{ n: string }>(
      `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM cluster_memberships WHERE wallet_address LIKE $1`,
      [`${CHAIN}:${PREFIX}-hotwallet%`]
    );
    expect(Number(memberships[0]?.n)).toBe(0);
  });

  it('clusters a funder sitting exactly on the ceiling', async () => {
    const funder = addr('edge');
    await seedFunding(funder, MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE);

    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it('tears down the cluster of a funder that grows past the ceiling', async () => {
    // The regression that matters: the ceiling must apply to funders already
    // clustered, not only to new ones.
    const funder = addr('grower');
    await seedFunding(funder, MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE);
    await generateFundingClusters();
    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).not.toBeNull();

    await seedFunding(funder, MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE + 5);
    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('excludes a blacklisted funder whose degree is inside the band', async () => {
    // The hub exclusion, doing what the band cannot: an exchange only a handful
    // of whose recipients we index has a small OBSERVED degree.
    const funder = addr('quietcex');
    await seedFunding(funder, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS + 1);
    await seedWallet(funder, 'blacklisted');

    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('tears down the cluster of a funder blacklisted after the fact', async () => {
    const funder = addr('lateflag');
    await seedFunding(funder, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS + 1);
    await generateFundingClusters();
    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).not.toBeNull();

    await seedWallet(funder, 'blacklisted');
    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(funder)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('leaves other funders untouched when one is excluded', async () => {
    const good = addr('good');
    const hub = addr('hub');
    await seedFunding(good, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS);
    await seedFunding(hub, MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE + 1);

    await generateFundingClusters();

    expect(await fundingCluster(good)).not.toBeNull();
    expect(await fundingCluster(hub)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('holds the pool open for the suite', () => {
    expect(pool).toBeDefined();
  });
});

==> tests/integration/global-setup.ts <==
import { assertIntegrationSchemaCurrent } from './helpers/schema-guard.js';
import { closePool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';

/**
 * Runs once before any integration file. Guards the schema so a stale database
 * fails with one actionable message instead of N per-test failures.
 */
export async function setup(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await assertIntegrationSchemaCurrent();
  } finally {
    // globalSetup runs in its own module context from the test files, so the
    // pool opened here is not the one they use and must be closed or vitest
    // hangs on an open handle.
    await closePool();
  }
}

==> tests/integration/helpers/lifecycle-fixture.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { resolveChainAddress, resolveChainValue, type Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { pool } from '../../../packages/db/src/client.js';

const SOLANA_SOURCE_WALLET = '11111111111111111111111111111111';
const SOLANA_TARGET_ACCOUNT = 'So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112';
const SOLANA_TOKEN_MINT = 'TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA';

export interface LifecycleFixture {
  runId: string;
  chain: Chain;
  sourceEventPrefix: string;
  sourceWallet: string;
  targetAccount: string;
  tokenMint: string;
}

export function createLifecycleFixture(chain: Chain = 'solana'): LifecycleFixture {
  const runId = randomUUID();
  const runHex = runId.replaceAll('-', '');
  const sourceWallet = chain === 'solana'
    ? SOLANA_SOURCE_WALLET
    : `0x${runHex}00000001`;
  const targetAccount = chain === 'solana'
    ? SOLANA_TARGET_ACCOUNT
    : `0x${runHex}00000002`;
  const tokenMint = chain === 'solana'
    ? SOLANA_TOKEN_MINT
    : `0x${runHex}00000003`;
  return {
    runId,
    chain,
    sourceEventPrefix: `it:${runId}:`,
    sourceWallet,
    targetAccount,
    tokenMint
  };
}

function asError(reason: unknown): Error {
  return reason instanceof Error ? reason : new Error(String(reason));
}

async function cleanupLifecycleFixture(fixture: LifecycleFixture): Promise<void> {
  const sourcePattern = `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}%`;
  const sourceWallet = resolveChainAddress(fixture.sourceWallet, fixture.chain).prefixed;
  const targetAccount = resolveChainAddress(fixture.targetAccount, fixture.chain).prefixed;
  const tokenMint = resolveChainValue(fixture.tokenMint, fixture.chain).prefixed;

  /**
   * How a `source_trades` row is recognised as this fixture's.
   *
   * A test that stages a row directly controls `source_event_id` and gets the
   * fixture prefix. A test that drives the *real* ingestion path does not: the
   * EVM builders set `sourceEventId` to the transaction hash, so a prefix-only
   * selector silently matches nothing and leaves the run's rows behind.
   *
   * The wallet/token fallback is limited to the EVM chains because their
   * fixture addresses are derived from `runId` and so cannot collide with
   * another run. The Solana fixture reuses three constant addresses, where the
   * same fallback would delete a concurrent run's rows.
   */
  const scopedByAddress = fixture.chain !== 'solana';
  const isFixtureSource = (alias: string): string =>
    scopedByAddress
      ? `(${alias}.source_event_id LIKE $1
           OR (${alias}.wallet_address = $2 AND ${alias}.chain = $3 AND ${alias}.token_mint = $4))`
      : `${alias}.source_event_id LIKE $1`;
  /** Parameters `$1..$4` for any statement built with `isFixtureSource`. */
  const sourceValues = scopedByAddress
    ? [sourcePattern, sourceWallet, fixture.chain, tokenMint]
    : [sourcePattern];

  const cleanupStatements: Array<[string, string, unknown[]]> = [
    [
      'linked trades',
      `DELETE FROM trades trade
       USING source_trades source
       WHERE trade.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      // An exit trade â€” a stop-loss, or anything else the scorer queues off the
      // position rather than off a source event â€” carries the signal but no
      // `source_trade_id`, so the delete above cannot see it. Left behind, it
      // holds a foreign key on the signal and blocks the rest of the teardown.
      'signal-attributed trades',
      `DELETE FROM trades trade
       USING signals signal, source_trades source
       WHERE trade.signal_id = signal.id
         AND signal.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'copy position lot reductions',
      `DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lot_reductions reduction
       USING copy_position_master_lots lot, copy_positions position
       WHERE reduction.lot_id = lot.id
         AND lot.position_id = position.id
         AND position.target_account = $1
         AND position.chain = $2
         AND position.token_mint = $3`,
      [targetAccount, fixture.chain, tokenMint]
    ],
    [
      'copy position master lots',
      `DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lots lot
       USING copy_positions position
       WHERE lot.position_id = position.id
         AND position.target_account = $1
         AND position.chain = $2
         AND position.token_mint = $3`,
      [targetAccount, fixture.chain, tokenMint]
    ],
    [
      'copy position applications',
      `DELETE FROM copy_position_applications application
       USING copy_executions execution, source_trades source
       WHERE application.execution_id = execution.id
         AND execution.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'copy execution evidence',
      `DELETE FROM copy_execution_evidence evidence
       USING copy_executions execution, source_trades source
       WHERE evidence.execution_id = execution.id
         AND execution.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'copy execution history',
      `DELETE FROM copy_execution_state_history history
       USING copy_executions execution, source_trades source
       WHERE history.execution_id = execution.id
         AND execution.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'copy executions',
      `DELETE FROM copy_executions execution
       USING source_trades source
       WHERE execution.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'copy positions',
      'DELETE FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = $1 AND chain = $2 AND token_mint = $3',
      [targetAccount, fixture.chain, tokenMint]
    ],
    [
      // Must precede the signals delete: the rejection row references signals(id).
      'copy eligibility rejections',
      `DELETE FROM copy_eligibility_rejections rejection
       USING signals signal, source_trades source
       WHERE rejection.signal_id = signal.id
         AND signal.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'source signals',
      `DELETE FROM signals signal
       USING source_trades source
       WHERE signal.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'source position applications',
      `DELETE FROM source_position_applications application
       USING source_trades source
       WHERE application.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'source confirmation history',
      `DELETE FROM source_trade_confirmation_history history
       USING source_trades source
       WHERE history.source_trade_id = source.id
         AND ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'source trades',
      `DELETE FROM source_trades source WHERE ${isFixtureSource('source')}`,
      sourceValues
    ],
    [
      'source positions',
      'DELETE FROM wallet_positions WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND chain = $2 AND token_mint = $3',
      [sourceWallet, fixture.chain, tokenMint]
    ],
    [
      // Only tests that exercise wallet-selection policy create this row, and
      // the address is fixture-scoped. Guarded so a wallet another table still
      // points at is left alone rather than failing the delete on its FK.
      'fixture source wallet',
      `DELETE FROM wallets wallet
       WHERE wallet.address = $1 AND wallet.chain = $2
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cluster_memberships WHERE wallet_address = wallet.address)
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transactions WHERE wallet_address = wallet.address)
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM trades WHERE wallet_address = wallet.address)`,
      [sourceWallet, fixture.chain]
    ],
    [
      'fixture token',
      `DELETE FROM tokens token
       WHERE token.mint = $1 AND token.chain = $2
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_trades WHERE token_mint = token.mint)
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM signals WHERE token_mint = token.mint)
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM trades WHERE token_mint = token.mint)
         AND NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM transactions
           WHERE target_token = token.mint OR token_in = token.mint OR token_out = token.mint
         )`,
      [tokenMint, fixture.chain]
    ]
  ];
  const failures: Error[] = [];

  for (const [label, statement, values] of cleanupStatements) {
    try {
      await pool.query(statement, values);
    } catch (error) {
      failures.push(new Error(`Failed to clean ${label}: ${asError(error).message}`, { cause: asError(error) }));
    }
  }

  try {
    // `$1..$4` are the `isFixtureSource` parameters; the address-scoped ones are
    // reused for the position counts, and `$5` is the copy side's account.
    const verifyValues = scopedByAddress
      ? [...sourceValues, targetAccount]
      : [sourcePattern, sourceWallet, fixture.chain, tokenMint, targetAccount];
    const result = await pool.query<{
      source_trades: number;
      copy_executions: number;
      source_positions: number;
      copy_positions: number;
      trades: number;
    }>(
      `SELECT
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM source_trades source
           WHERE ${isFixtureSource('source')}) AS source_trades,
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM copy_executions execution
           JOIN source_trades source ON source.id = execution.source_trade_id
          WHERE ${isFixtureSource('source')}) AS copy_executions,
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM wallet_positions
           WHERE wallet_address = $2 AND chain = $3 AND token_mint = $4) AS source_positions,
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM copy_positions
           WHERE target_account = $5 AND chain = $3 AND token_mint = $4) AS copy_positions,
         -- Counted on the token rather than through a join: a trade that has lost
         -- every link is precisely the one that blocks migration 030, and a join
         -- through source_trades would be blind to it in exactly that case.
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::int FROM trades
           WHERE token_mint = $4 AND chain = $3) AS trades`,
      verifyValues
    );
    const leftovers = Object.entries(result.rows[0] ?? {})
      .filter(([, count]) => Number(count) !== 0)
      .map(([table, count]) => `${table}=${count}`);
    if (leftovers.length > 0) {
      failures.push(new Error(`Lifecycle fixture cleanup left rows: ${leftovers.join(', ')}`));
    }
  } catch (error) {
    failures.push(new Error('Failed to verify lifecycle fixture cleanup', { cause: asError(error) }));
  }

  if (failures.length > 0) {
    throw new AggregateError(
      failures,
      `Lifecycle fixture ${fixture.runId} cleanup failed: ${failures.map((error) => error.message).join('; ')}`
    );
  }
}

export async function withLifecycleFixture(
  operation: (fixture: LifecycleFixture) => Promise<void>,
  chain: Chain = 'solana'
): Promise<void> {
  const fixture = createLifecycleFixture(chain);
  const failures: Error[] = [];
  try {
    await operation(fixture);
  } catch (error) {
    failures.push(asError(error));
  }

  try {
    await cleanupLifecycleFixture(fixture);
  } catch (error) {
    failures.push(asError(error));
  }

  if (failures.length > 0) {
    throw new AggregateError(
      failures,
      `Lifecycle fixture ${fixture.runId} failed: ${failures.map((error) => error.message).join('; ')}`
    );
  }
}

==> tests/integration/helpers/schema-guard.ts <==
import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { pool } from '../../../packages/db/src/client.js';

/**
 * Fails the suite fast when the integration database is behind the migration
 * set, rather than letting every test fail on its own missing table.
 *
 * This exists because of a real incident: `swat_integration` sat at migration
 * `029` while the tree was at `038`. The suite reported 20 failures across all
 * five files â€” the loudest of which was a *cleanup* error â€” which reads like a
 * teardown bug and sent the investigation to the wrong place entirely. The
 * schema was the only thing wrong.
 *
 * It checks the newest migration's table rather than counting applied files
 * because there is no applied-migrations table: `migrate.ts` deliberately
 * replays every file on every run (D16). The schema itself is the only record.
 */

const MIGRATIONS_DIR = new URL('../../../packages/db/sql/', import.meta.url).pathname;

/**
 * Tables that must exist, each introduced by a late migration. Extend this when
 * adding a migration whose absence would be confusing to debug from a test
 * failure â€” the newest entry is what actually catches staleness.
 */
const REQUIRED_TABLES = [
  'copy_executions',             // 028
  'signal_stop_losses',          // 034
  'copy_eligibility_rejections', // 035
  'users',                       // 039
  'user_sessions',               // 040
  'user_auth_wallets',           // 041
  'user_api_keys',               // 042
  'audit_log',                   // 043
  'user_wallet_subscriptions',   // 044
  'user_token_watches',          // 045
  'user_execution_grants',       // 047
  'user_balances',               // 048
  'user_execution_settings',     // 049
  'user_chain_execution_settings', // 049
  'copy_position_master_lots',   // 058 core lot accounting
  'lp_pools',                    // 059
  'lp_positions',                // 059
  'lp_guardrail_configs',        // 059
  'lp_tracked_wallets'           // 059
] as const;

/** Columns whose absence would otherwise surface as an opaque SQL error. */
const REQUIRED_COLUMNS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [table: string, column: string]> = [
  ['trades', 'venue_settlement_status'], // 038
  // 050. The newest entry is what actually catches staleness, and this one is
  // load-bearing twice over: `copy-position-tenancy.integration.test.ts` asserts
  // the tenancy key directly, so without this guard a database sitting at 046
  // fails that suite with an opaque "column user_id does not exist" â€” exactly
  // the misdirected investigation this file was written after.
  ['copy_positions', 'user_id'],
  ['copy_position_applications', 'position_id'],
  ['copy_executions', 'user_id'],
  ['trades', 'user_id'],
  // 051. Same reasoning as the 050 entries above: `subscription-states.integration.test.ts`
  // asserts the state CHECK constraints directly, so a database sitting at 050
  // would fail it with an opaque "column state does not exist" rather than the
  // actionable "schema is stale, run migrations" this guard exists to produce.
  ['user_wallet_subscriptions', 'state'],
  // 053. Without this a database at 051 fails the capacity suite with an opaque
  // "relation master_capacity_ledger does not exist".
  ['master_capacity_ledger', 'notional_basis'],
  ['user_wallet_subscriptions', 'active_since'],
  ['copy_position_master_lots', 'master_wallet_address'],
  ['lp_positions', 'auto_rebalance']
];

export async function assertIntegrationSchemaCurrent(): Promise<void> {
  const highestMigration = readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
    .sort()
    .at(-1);

  const missing: string[] = [];

  const tables = await pool.query<{ table_name: string }>(
    `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables
      WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = ANY($1)`,
    [[...REQUIRED_TABLES]]
  );
  const present = new Set(tables.rows.map((row) => row.table_name));
  for (const table of REQUIRED_TABLES) {
    if (!present.has(table)) missing.push(`table ${table}`);
  }

  for (const [table, column] of REQUIRED_COLUMNS) {
    const result = await pool.query(
      `SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
        WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = $1 AND column_name = $2`,
      [table, column]
    );
    if (result.rowCount === 0) missing.push(`column ${table}.${column}`);
  }

  if (missing.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `Integration database schema is stale â€” missing ${missing.join(', ')}.\n`
        + `Latest migration on disk is ${highestMigration}.\n`
        + 'Run migrations against the integration database first:\n'
        + '  DATABASE_URL=$INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL pnpm db:migrate\n'
        + 'Note: migrations can be blocked by leftover fixture rows from a crashed '
        + 'run; if so the migrate output names the violated constraint.'
    );
  }
}

import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const runId = randomUUID();

const master = `robinhood-chain:0x${hex}00000002`;
const token = `robinhood-chain:0x${hex}00000003`;
const executionIds: string[] = [];
const sourceIds: string[] = [];
const occurredAt = new Date('2026-10-01T00:00:00Z');

async function acquire(quantity = '10') {
  const sourceEventId = `${runId}:${randomUUID()}`;
  const source = await recordSourceTradeEvent({
    chain: 'robinhood-chain', sourceEventType: 'transaction',
    sourceEventId, transactionHash: sourceEventId, walletAddress: master,
    tokenMint: token, side: 'buy', quantity, amountUsd: Number(quantity) * 10,
    eventAt: occurredAt, confirmationState: 'confirmed', confirmationEvidenceId: randomUUID()
  });
  sourceIds.push(source.event.id);
  const { execution } = await requestCopyExecution({
    sourceTradeId: source.event.id, targetAccount: target,
    executionMode: 'paper', requestedBaseQuantity: quantity
  });
  executionIds.push(execution.id);
  await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
    executionId: execution.id, evidenceType: 'paper_simulation', evidenceId: execution.clientOrderId,
    baseQuantity: quantity, quoteLeg: { currency: 'USD', amount: Number(quantity) * 10 },
    confirmationState: 'confirmed', completesExecution: true, occurredAt
  });
  const lot = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
    'SELECT id FROM copy_position_master_lots WHERE acquisition_execution_id = $1', [execution.id]
  );
  return lot.rows[0].id;
}

async function claim(lotId: string, requestId = randomUUID(), quantity?: string) {
  const result = await claimLotExitExecution({
    lotId, userId: null, requestId, trigger: 'manual', requestedBaseQuantity: quantity
  });
  if (!executionIds.includes(result.execution.id)) executionIds.push(result.execution.id);
  return result;
}

async function fill(executionId: string, quantity: string, evidenceId = randomUUID(), completes = true) {
  const input = {
    executionId, evidenceId, evidenceType: 'paper_simulation' as const,
    baseQuantity: quantity, quoteLeg: { currency: 'USD' as const, amount: Number(quantity) * 12 },
    confirmationState: 'confirmed' as const, completesExecution: completes,
    occurredAt: new Date('2026-10-01T00:01:00Z')
  };
  return { input, result: await recordCopyExecutionEvidence(input) };
}

async function remaining(lotId: string) {
  const result = await pool.query<{ quantity: string }>(
    'SELECT remaining_quantity::text AS quantity FROM copy_position_master_lots WHERE id = $1', [lotId]
  );
  return Number(result.rows[0].quantity);
}

afterAll(async () => {
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lot_reductions WHERE sell_execution_id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_applications WHERE execution_id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_execution_evidence WHERE execution_id = ANY($1) AND execution_id IN (SELECT id FROM copy_executions WHERE exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_execution_state_history WHERE execution_id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_executions WHERE id = ANY($1) AND exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_position_master_lots WHERE acquisition_execution_id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_execution_evidence WHERE execution_id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_executions WHERE id = ANY($1)', [executionIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM copy_positions WHERE target_account = $1', [target]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM source_position_applications WHERE source_trade_id = ANY($1)', [sourceIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM source_trade_confirmation_history WHERE source_trade_id = ANY($1)', [sourceIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM source_trades WHERE id = ANY($1)', [sourceIds]);
  await pool.query('DELETE FROM wallet_positions WHERE wallet_address = $1', [master]);
});

describe('canonical lot exits', () => {
  it('claims exactly one execution concurrently and reserves the original paper inventory', async () => {
    const lotId = await acquire('10');
    const requestId = randomUUID();
    const results = await Promise.all([claim(lotId, requestId), claim(lotId, requestId)]);
    expect(results.filter((result) => result.created)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(results[0].execution.id).toBe(results[1].execution.id);
    expect(results[0].execution).toMatchObject({
      sourceTradeId: null, exitLotId: lotId, exitTrigger: 'manual',
      executionMode: 'paper', targetAccount: target, requestedBaseQuantity: '10', reservedBaseQuantity: '10'
    });
    await expect(claim(lotId)).rejects.toThrow();
    await fill(results[0].execution.id, '10');
    expect(await remaining(lotId)).toBe(0);
  });

  it('reduces only the specified lot and is unchanged by partial-fill evidence replay', async () => {
    const lotA = await acquire('5');
    const lotB = await acquire('7');
    const exit = await claim(lotB);
    const { input } = await fill(exit.execution.id, '3', randomUUID(), false);
    await recordCopyExecutionEvidence(input);
    expect(await remaining(lotA)).toBe(5);
    expect(await remaining(lotB)).toBe(4);
    await expect(fill(exit.execution.id, '5')).rejects.toThrow('reserved lot inventory');
    expect(await remaining(lotB)).toBe(4);
    await fill(exit.execution.id, '4');
    expect(await remaining(lotB)).toBe(0);
    expect(await remaining(lotA)).toBe(5);
    await expect(claimLotExitExecution({ lotId: lotA, userId: randomUUID(), requestId: randomUUID(), trigger: 'manual' }))
      .rejects.toThrow('owning tenant');
    await fill((await claim(lotA)).execution.id, '5');
  });
});

==> tests/integration/master-attributed-inventory.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import {
  recordCopyExecutionEvidence,
  recordSourceTradeEvent,
  requestCopyExecution
} from '../../packages/db/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.js';
import { createUser } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';

/**
 * S4-M3 / ADR-0007.
 *
 * This is intentionally database-backed: the invariant is not just that a
 * query mentions a master column. It is that two source masters can share one
 * fungible tenant position, one master's sell is capped by its own lot, and
 * the aggregate venue row remains the sum that can actually be sold.
 *
 * The integration runner requires a database name ending in `_integration` or
 * `_test`; it is written here but must remain unrun on this environment.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);

function encodeBase58(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  const alphabet = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz';
  const digits = [0];
  for (const byte of bytes) {
    let carry = byte;
    for (let index = 0; index < digits.length; index += 1) {
      carry += digits[index]! << 8;
      digits[index] = carry % 58;
      carry = Math.floor(carry / 58);
    }
    while (carry > 0) {
      digits.push(carry % 58);
      carry = Math.floor(carry / 58);
    }
  }
  let result = '';
  for (const byte of bytes) {
    if (byte !== 0) break;
    result += alphabet[0];
  }
  for (let index = digits.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
    result += alphabet[digits[index]!];
  }
  return result;
}

function fixtureAddress(role: number): string {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(32);
  bytes.set(Buffer.from(runId, 'hex'), 0);
  bytes[31] = role;
  return `solana:${encodeBase58(bytes)}`;
}

const targetAccount = fixtureAddress(1);
const tokenMint = fixtureAddress(2);
const masterA = fixtureAddress(3);
const masterB = fixtureAddress(4);
const createdSourceTradeIds: string[] = [];
const createdExecutionIds: string[] = [];
let userId: string | null = null;

async function sourceTrade(input: {
  walletAddress: string;
  side: 'buy' | 'sell';
  quantity: string;
  suffix: string;
}) {
  const result = await recordSourceTradeEvent({
    chain: 'solana',
    sourceEventType: 'transaction',
    sourceEventId: `${runId}-${input.suffix}`,
    transactionHash: `${runId}-${input.suffix}`,
    walletAddress: input.walletAddress,
    tokenMint,
    side: input.side,
    quantity: input.quantity,
    amountUsd: input.quantity,
    priceUsd: '1',
    eventAt: new Date('2026-10-03T00:00:00.000Z'),
    confirmationState: 'confirmed',
    confirmationEvidenceId: `${runId}-${input.suffix}-confirmed`
  });
  createdSourceTradeIds.push(result.event.id);
  return result.event;
}

async function mirror(sourceTradeId: string, quantity: string, evidenceId: string) {
  const requested = await requestCopyExecution({
    sourceTradeId,
    targetAccount,
    userId,
    executionMode: 'paper',
    requestedBaseQuantity: quantity,
    requestedQuoteQuantity: quantity
  });
  createdExecutionIds.push(requested.execution.id);
  const filled = await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
    executionId: requested.execution.id,
    evidenceType: 'paper_simulation',
    evidenceId,
    baseQuantity: requested.execution.requestedBaseQuantity ?? quantity,
    quoteLeg: { amount: requested.execution.requestedQuoteQuantity ?? quantity, currency: 'USD' },
    priceUsd: '1',
    confirmationState: 'confirmed',
    completesExecution: true,
    occurredAt: new Date('2026-10-03T00:00:01.000Z')
  });
  return { requested: requested.execution, filled };
}
