describe('master-attributed copy inventory', () => {
  it('keeps one master sell from consuming another master lot', async () => {
    const user = await createUser({
      email: `s4-m3-${runId}@example.com`,
      password: 'a-very-long-password',
      tier: 'free'
    });
    userId = user.id;

    const [buyA, buyB] = await Promise.all([
      sourceTrade({ walletAddress: masterA, side: 'buy', quantity: '100', suffix: 'buy-a' }),
      sourceTrade({ walletAddress: masterB, side: 'buy', quantity: '200', suffix: 'buy-b' })
    ]);
    await mirror(buyA.id, '100', `${runId}-copy-buy-a`);
    await mirror(buyB.id, '200', `${runId}-copy-buy-b`);

    const sourceSellA = await sourceTrade({
      walletAddress: masterA,
      side: 'sell',
      quantity: '100',
      suffix: 'sell-a'
    });
    const sell = await requestCopyExecution({
      sourceTradeId: sourceSellA.id,
      targetAccount,
      userId,
      executionMode: 'paper',
      requestedBaseQuantity: '150'
    });
    createdExecutionIds.push(sell.execution.id);

    // The request exceeds master A's 100-token lot, even though the aggregate
    // venue position contains 300 tokens. Sizing must cap at A's lot.
    expect(sell.execution.requestedBaseQuantity).toBe('100');
    await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
      executionId: sell.execution.id,
      evidenceType: 'paper_simulation',
      evidenceId: `${runId}-copy-sell-a`,
      baseQuantity: '100',
      quoteLeg: { amount: '100', currency: 'USD' },
      priceUsd: '1',
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      completesExecution: true,
      occurredAt: new Date('2026-10-03T00:00:02.000Z')
    });

    const { rows: lots } = await pool.query<{
      master_wallet_address: string;
      confirmed_quantity: string;
    }>(
      `SELECT lot.master_wallet_address, lot.remaining_quantity::text AS confirmed_quantity
         FROM copy_position_master_lots lot
         JOIN copy_positions position ON position.id = lot.position_id
        WHERE position.target_account = $1 AND lot.user_id = $2 AND lot.chain = 'solana' AND lot.token_mint = $3
        ORDER BY lot.master_wallet_address`,
      [targetAccount, userId, tokenMint]
    );
    expect(lots).toEqual([
      { master_wallet_address: masterA, confirmed_quantity: '0' },
      { master_wallet_address: masterB, confirmed_quantity: '200' }
    ]);

    const { rows: aggregate } = await pool.query<{ confirmed_quantity: string }>(
      `SELECT confirmed_quantity::text AS confirmed_quantity
         FROM copy_positions
        WHERE target_account = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND chain = 'solana' AND token_mint = $3`,
      [targetAccount, userId, tokenMint]
    );
    expect(aggregate[0]?.confirmed_quantity).toBe('200');
  });
});

==> tests/integration/master-capacity.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import {
  MASTER_CAPACITY_WINDOWS,
  assessMasterCapacity,
  fetchMasterCapacityPolicy,
  fetchMasterWindowNotional,
  recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry,
  usableLiquidityFromPoolTvlUsd
} from '../../packages/db/src/master-capacity.js';

/**
 * Per-master capacity accounting (`S4-M6`, migration `053`).
 *
 * `packages/db/src/master-capacity.test.ts` covers the decision with no
 * database â€” that is where the arithmetic, the uniform-skip guard and the two
 * messages are tested. What only PostgreSQL can prove is here:
 *
 *  1. The CHECK constraints genuinely make an incoherent ledger row
 *     unrepresentable. The one that matters most is
 *     `chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis`: it is what stops an unpriceable leg
 *     from being recorded as `$0` with a priced basis, which would make real
 *     copy flow read as no flow and turn the cap into a control that passes
 *     everything.
 *  2. `unq_master_capacity_ledger_event` makes the writer idempotent, so a
 *     retried fan-out cannot double-count itself into its own cap.
 *  3. The window aggregate really does exclude rows outside the window, other
 *     tokens and other masters â€” a leak there would either free capacity that
 *     was consumed or charge a master for someone else's flow.
 *  4. **Neither table has a `user_id` column, now or ever.** That is the
 *     structural half of "capacity binds uniformly on every user" (`S4-M7`) and
 *     of "follower counts are never displayed" (`S4-M9`): a table that cannot
 *     see users cannot prioritise between them, and a cohort-level ledger makes
 *     a headcount undrivable from capacity data.
 *  5. `053` is replay-safe. `migrate.ts` has no applied-migrations table and
 *     re-runs every file on every invocation, so this is a correctness property
 *     of the file, not a nicety.
 *
 * **This file has never been executed.** No database was available when `S4-M6`
 * landed and `053` has not been applied anywhere.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const ADDRESS_PREFIX = `solana:SWATcap${runId}`;
const MASTER = `${ADDRESS_PREFIX}A`;
const OTHER_MASTER = `${ADDRESS_PREFIX}B`;
const TOKEN = `solana:SWATtok${runId}A`;
const OTHER_TOKEN = `solana:SWATtok${runId}B`;

const sourceTradeIds: string[] = [];

/** A source trade to hang a ledger row off. The FK is RESTRICT, so it is real. */
async function makeSourceTrade(walletAddress = MASTER, tokenMint = TOKEN): Promise<string> {
  const eventId = `s4m6-${randomUUID()}`;
  const result = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(
    `INSERT INTO source_trades (
       chain, transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint, direction,
       amount_usd, token_amount, source_event_type, source_event_id, event_at
     ) VALUES ('solana', $1, $2, $3, 'buy', 1000, 1000, 'transaction', $1, NOW())
     RETURNING id`,
    [eventId, walletAddress, tokenMint]
  );
  const id = result.rows[0]!.id;
  sourceTradeIds.push(id);
  return id;
}

async function ledgerRowCount(): Promise<number> {
  const result = await pool.query<{ count: string }>(
    `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM master_capacity_ledger
      WHERE master_wallet_address = ANY($1)`,
    [[MASTER, OTHER_MASTER]]
  );
  return Number(result.rows[0]!.count);
}

afterAll(async () => {
  await pool.query(`DELETE FROM master_capacity_ledger WHERE master_wallet_address = ANY($1)`, [
    [MASTER, OTHER_MASTER]
  ]);
  await pool.query(
    `DELETE FROM master_capacity_policy WHERE master_wallet_address LIKE $1 || '%'`,
    [ADDRESS_PREFIX]
  );
  if (sourceTradeIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query(`DELETE FROM source_trades WHERE id = ANY($1)`, [sourceTradeIds]);
  }
});

describe('master_capacity_ledger constraints', () => {
  it('rejects a bare address in the chain-prefixed column', async () => {
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ('BareAddressNoPrefix', 'solana', $1, $2, 'live', 100, 'quote-stablecoin')`,
        [TOKEN, sourceTradeId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_prefix/);
  });

  it('refuses to record an unpriced leg as a zero-dollar priced leg', async () => {
    // The whole point of the basis CHECK. A leg that could not be priced,
    // written as 0 with a priced basis, would make real flow read as no flow.
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ($1, 'solana', $2, $3, 'live', 0, 'unpriced')`,
        [MASTER, TOKEN, sourceTradeId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis/);
  });

  it('refuses a NULL notional under a priced basis', async () => {
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ($1, 'solana', $2, $3, 'live', NULL, 'quote-stablecoin')`,
        [MASTER, TOKEN, sourceTradeId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis/);
  });

  it('refuses a negative notional and an unknown basis', async () => {
    const negativeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ($1, 'solana', $2, $3, 'live', -1, 'quote-stablecoin')`,
        [MASTER, TOKEN, negativeId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis/);

    const basisId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ($1, 'solana', $2, $3, 'live', 10, 'vibes')`,
        [MASTER, TOKEN, basisId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis/);
  });

  it('accepts an unpriced leg with a NULL notional', async () => {
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry({
      masterWalletAddress: MASTER,
      chain: 'solana',
      tokenMint: TOKEN,
      sourceTradeId,
      executionMode: 'live',
      notionalUsd: null,
      notionalBasis: 'unpriced',
      committedAt: new Date()
    });
    const observation = await fetchMasterWindowNotional({
      masterWalletAddress: MASTER,
      chain: 'solana',
      tokenMint: TOKEN,
      windowStartsAt: new Date(Date.now() - 60_000),
      windowEndsAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60_000),
      executionModes: ['live']
    });
    expect(observation.coverage).toBe('partial-unpriced-legs');
    expect(observation.unpricedLegCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
  });

  it('rejects an unknown chain and an unknown execution mode', async () => {
    const chainId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ('ethereum:0xmaster', 'ethereum', $1, $2, 'live', 10, 'quote-stablecoin')`,
        [TOKEN, chainId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_chain/);

    const modeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO master_capacity_ledger (
           master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, source_trade_id,
           execution_mode, notional_usd, notional_basis
         ) VALUES ($1, 'solana', $2, $3, 'dry-run', 10, 'quote-stablecoin')`,
        [MASTER, TOKEN, modeId]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_master_capacity_ledger_mode/);
  });
});

describe('the writer is idempotent per fan-out event', () => {
  it('does not let a retried fan-out double-count itself into its own cap', async () => {
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    const before = await ledgerRowCount();
    const entry = {
      masterWalletAddress: MASTER,
      chain: 'solana' as const,
      tokenMint: TOKEN,
      sourceTradeId,
      executionMode: 'live' as const,
      notionalUsd: 2_500,
      notionalBasis: 'quote-stablecoin' as const,
      committedAt: new Date()
    };
    await recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry(entry);
    await recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry(entry);
    await recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry({ ...entry, notionalUsd: 999_999 });
    expect(await ledgerRowCount()).toBe(before + 1);

    const stored = await pool.query<{ notional_usd: string }>(
      `SELECT notional_usd FROM master_capacity_ledger
        WHERE source_trade_id = $1 AND execution_mode = 'live'`,
      [sourceTradeId]
    );
    // DO NOTHING, not DO UPDATE: the first record of a committed cohort stands.
    expect(Number(stored.rows[0]!.notional_usd)).toBe(2_500);
  });

  it('keeps paper and live flow as separate rows for the same source trade', async () => {
    const sourceTradeId = await makeSourceTrade();
    for (const executionMode of ['paper', 'live', 'shadow'] as const) {
      await recordMasterCapacityLedgerEntry({
        masterWalletAddress: MASTER,
        chain: 'solana',
        tokenMint: TOKEN,
        sourceTradeId,
        executionMode,
        notionalUsd: 100,
        notionalBasis: 'quote-stablecoin',
        committedAt: new Date()
      });
    }
    const rows = await pool.query(

==> tests/integration/master-membership.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { forUser } from '../../packages/db/src/tenancy.js';
import { createUser } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';
import {
  MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP,
  MEMBERSHIP_USER_MESSAGE,
  MasterMembershipFullError
} from '../../packages/db/src/master-membership.js';
import {
  beginWindDown,
  endSubscription,
  subscribeToWallet
} from '../../packages/db/src/subscriptions.js';

/**
 * Master membership cap (`S4-M43`) and slot release (`S4-M44`), migration `056`.
 *
 * **NEVER EXECUTED.** There is no database in the environment this was written
 * in, so every assertion below is an unverified claim about SQL. That is stated
 * rather than implied: the unit suite in
 * `packages/db/src/master-membership.test.ts` proves the decision function and
 * the statement text, and nothing outside this file proves that PostgreSQL
 * accepts these statements or that the constraints bind.
 *
 * These cases exist here because they are **only** answerable with a real
 * database:
 *
 *   1. **Concurrency.** A `COUNT(*) < 50` guard is exceeded by exactly the
 *      number of concurrent racers. Only firing real concurrent transactions at
 *      a real Postgres shows whether the cap holds. A mocked client cannot fail
 *      this test, so it cannot pass it either.
 *   2. **The constraints actually exist and bind.** A unit test can assert the
 *      migration's *text*; only Postgres can assert that the partial unique
 *      index rejects a duplicate ordinal and that the coherence CHECK rejects a
 *      leaver holding one.
 *   3. **Slot release round-trips.** That winding down frees an ordinal and a
 *      new joiner immediately gets it is a claim about three statements agreeing
 *      with one CHECK constraint.
 *
 * Run with `pnpm test:integration` against a database whose name ends in
 * `_integration` or `_test`.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const userIds: string[] = [];
const walletAddresses: string[] = [];

function walletFor(suffix: string): string {
  const address = `solana:SWATmem${runId}${suffix}`.slice(0, 100);
  walletAddresses.push(address);
  return address;
}

async function makeUser() {
  const user = await createUser({
    email: `s4m43-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
    password: 'a-very-long-password',
    // `operator` tracks 25 wallets; the tracked-wallet quota is a per-USER
    // limit and must not be what refuses anyone in these cases, so each case
    // uses one wallet per user.
    tier: 'operator'
  });
  userIds.push(user.id);
  return user;
}

async function subscribe(userId: string, tier: 'operator', address: string) {
  return subscribeToWallet(forUser(userId), {
    walletAddress: address,
    chain: 'solana',
    tier,
    tierExpiresAt: null
  });
}

async function slotsHeld(address: string): Promise<number> {
  const result = await pool.query<{ count: string }>(
    `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND membership_slot IS NOT NULL`,
    [address]
  );
  return Number(result.rows[0]?.count ?? '0');
}

afterAll(async () => {
  if (walletAddresses.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_wallet_subscriptions WHERE wallet_address = ANY($1)', [
      walletAddresses
    ]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = ANY($1)', [walletAddresses]);
  }
  if (userIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
  }
});

describe('membership cap under concurrency (S4-M43)', () => {
  it('admits at most the cap when every subscribe arrives at once', async () => {
    // The whole reason the cap is a constraint rather than a count. With
    // check-then-insert, all cap+10 of these observe a pre-insert occupancy
    // below the cap and all cap+10 insert.
    const address = walletFor('race');
    const users = [];
    for (let index = 0; index < MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP + 10; index += 1) {
      users.push(await makeUser());
    }

    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
      users.map((user) => subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address))
    );

    const granted = results.filter((entry) => entry.status === 'fulfilled').length;
    expect(granted).toBe(MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP);
    expect(await slotsHeld(address)).toBe(MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP);

    // Every refusal is the membership refusal, not a stray unique violation
    // leaking out as a 500.
    for (const entry of results) {
      if (entry.status === 'rejected') {
        expect(entry.reason).toBeInstanceOf(MasterMembershipFullError);
        expect((entry.reason as Error).message).toBe(MEMBERSHIP_USER_MESSAGE);
        expect((entry.reason as Error).message).not.toMatch(/\d/);
      }
    }
  });

  it('refuses the next joiner once the cap is reached', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('full');
    const users = [];
    for (let index = 0; index < MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP; index += 1) {
      users.push(await makeUser());
    }
    for (const user of users) await subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address);

    const outsider = await makeUser();
    await expect(subscribe(outsider.id, 'operator', address)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      MasterMembershipFullError
    );
  });
});

describe('the database, not the code, is what enforces the cap', () => {
  it('rejects a second row claiming the same ordinal', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('dupe');
    const [first, second] = await Promise.all([makeUser(), makeUser()]);
    await subscribe(first!.id, 'operator', address);
    await subscribe(second!.id, 'operator', address);

    // Hand-written, bypassing every application guard. The partial unique index
    // is what has to refuse this, or the cap is only as good as the code above.
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET membership_slot = 1
          WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
        [address, second!.id]
      )
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23505' });
  });

  it('rejects an ordinal above the cap', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('range');
    const user = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address);

    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET membership_slot = $3
          WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
        [address, user.id, MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP + 1]
      )
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23514' });
  });

  it('rejects a winding-down row that still holds an ordinal', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('leaver');
    const user = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address);

    // The coherence CHECK is what makes "a leaver holds no slot" an invariant
    // rather than a convention that one forgetful UPDATE can break.
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
            SET state = 'winding_down', wound_down_at = NOW()
          WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
        [address, user.id]
      )
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23514' });
  });

  it('rejects an active row with no ordinal and no grandfathering flag', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('nullslot');
    const user = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address);

    // This is the hole the grandfathering flag closes: without it, an active row
    // with a NULL ordinal would have to be permitted forever and the cap would
    // silently stop being a cap.
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET membership_slot = NULL
          WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
        [address, user.id]
      )
    ).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23514' });
  });
});

describe('a dropped copier does not get their slot back (S4-M44)', () => {
  it('frees the ordinal on wind-down and hands it to the next joiner', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('release');
    const leaver = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(leaver.id, 'operator', address);
    expect(await slotsHeld(address)).toBe(1);

    await beginWindDown(forUser(leaver.id), address);
    // Winding down releases the ordinal. It does NOT stop the sell mirror â€”
    // that is derived from `state`, and the row is still `winding_down`.
    expect(await slotsHeld(address)).toBe(0);
    const stillEnumerated = await pool.query<{ state: string }>(
      `SELECT state FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
        WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
      [address, leaver.id]
    );
    expect(stillEnumerated.rows[0]?.state).toBe('winding_down');

    const newcomer = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(newcomer.id, 'operator', address);
    expect(await slotsHeld(address)).toBe(1);
  });

  it('refuses a returning copier whose slot was taken while they were away', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('noreclaim');
    const leaver = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(leaver.id, 'operator', address);
    await endSubscription(forUser(leaver.id), address);

    // Fill every ordinal with other people.
    const others = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP }, () => makeUser())
    );
    for (const other of others) await subscribe(other.id, 'operator', address);

    // No grandfathering, no waitlist priority: the slot was not theirs once
    // released, and the refusal reads exactly the same as for a stranger.
    await expect(subscribe(leaver.id, 'operator', address)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      MasterMembershipFullError
    );
  });

  it('does not let a winding-down member occupy a slot they can then reclaim', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('cycle');
    const cycler = await makeUser();
    await subscribe(cycler.id, 'operator', address);
    await beginWindDown(forUser(cycler.id), address);

    const others = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP }, () => makeUser())
    );
    for (const other of others) await subscribe(other.id, 'operator', address);

    // Their ordinal went back into the pool when they wound down, so changing
    // their mind now competes for a free one and loses. Exempting this path
    // would let a user hold a slot indefinitely by cycling.
    await expect(subscribe(cycler.id, 'operator', address)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      MasterMembershipFullError
    );
  });

  it('is idempotent for an existing member of a full master', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('idem');
    const users = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP }, () => makeUser())
    );
    for (const user of users) await subscribe(user.id, 'operator', address);

    // An existing member must not be refused their own wallet, and must not
    // burn a second ordinal.
    const again = await subscribe(users[0]!.id, 'operator', address);
    expect(again.subscriptionCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(await slotsHeld(address)).toBe(MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP);
  });
});

==> tests/integration/pipeline.integration.test.ts <==
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { resolveChainAddress, resolveChainValue, type Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import {
  claimSourceSignalForCopyExecution,
  closePool,
  insertSourceTradeSignal,
  listSourceTradeSignalCandidates,
  markSourceTradeSignalDispatched,
  markToMarketOpenPositions,
  pool,
  recordCopyExecutionEvidence,
  transitionCopyExecution,
  upsertWallet,
  type SourceTradeSignalCandidate
} from '../../packages/db/src/index.js';
import { parseCanonicalSolanaSwapEvent, type HeliusParsedTransaction } from '../../apps/indexer/src/parse.js';
import {
  persistPolymarketSourceTrade,
  persistRobinhoodSourceTrade,
  persistSolanaSourceTrade
} from '../../apps/indexer/src/source-trade-lifecycle.js';
import { persistTrade } from '../../apps/trade-executor/src/index.js';
import { withLifecycleFixture, type LifecycleFixture } from './helpers/lifecycle-fixture.js';

/**
 * E2 acceptance (`G7-T2`): the production pipeline, per chain, end to end â€”
 * seed wallet -> backfill -> transactions -> signal -> paper trade ->
 * attribution.
 *
 * Every stage calls the function the running service calls. The one service
 * module that cannot be imported is `apps/signal-engine/src/index.ts`: it opens
 * BullMQ queues and arms `setInterval(tick, 15_000)` at module scope, so
 * importing it starts a second signal engine against the test database. The
 * signal stage therefore drives `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates` ->
 * `insertSourceTradeSignal` -> `markSourceTradeSignalDispatched`, which is
 * exactly what its `enqueueSignal` does either side of the Telegram/BullMQ
 * fan-out. What is skipped is the fan-out and the token-metadata lookup, both
 * of which are network calls that would make this suite flaky in CI.
 *
 * The pipeline runs a **round trip** â€” canonical entry, then exit â€” for two
 * reasons: it is the only way attribution can be asserted without a live price
 * feed (a closed position needs no mark), and a buy-only ledger would never
 * exercise the realized-PnL path that the scorer actually reports on.
 *
 * The exit is modelled as the executor's stop-loss exit rather than as a second
 * source trade, because that is the only production shape that closes a
 * *signal's* ledger. A source sell is its own signal with its own canonical
 * execution, and `fk_trades_copy_execution_identity` will not let a trade be
 * attributed to a signal its execution does not belong to â€” so a source-sell
 * round trip leaves two open one-sided ledgers, not one closed one. A stop-loss
 * exit carries the entry's `signalId` with no `sourceTradeId` and no canonical
 * execution, which is exactly what `apps/trade-executor/src/index.ts` persists
 * when the scorer queues one.
 */

const MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS = 10 * 60_000;
const EVIDENCE_AGE_MS = 10 * 60_000;

/** Buy 100 units at $2, sell them at $3. Realized PnL is therefore $100. */
const BUY_QUANTITY = 100;
const BUY_PRICE_USD = 2;
const SELL_PRICE_USD = 3;
const EXPECTED_REALIZED_PNL_USD = BUY_QUANTITY * (SELL_PRICE_USD - BUY_PRICE_USD);

afterAll(async () => {
  await closePool();
});

/** 32-byte hex derived from the fixture run, so no two runs collide. */
function fixtureHash(fixture: LifecycleFixture, salt: string): string {
  const runHex = fixture.runId.replaceAll('-', '');
  const saltHex = Buffer.from(salt).toString('hex');
  return `0x${(runHex + saltHex).padEnd(64, '0').slice(0, 64)}`;
}

/**
 * Stage 1 â€” seed. The same call the indexer makes for a `WALLET_ADDRESSES`
 * entry or an API-submitted wallet.
 *
 * The score and `active` status are written separately because `upsertWallet`
 * deliberately does not touch them: scoring is the scorer's job, and the
 * pipeline needs a wallet the candidate query will actually select.
 */
async function seedWallet(fixture: LifecycleFixture): Promise<string> {
  await upsertWallet({
    address: fixture.sourceWallet,
    chain: fixture.chain,
    source: 'manual',
    nickname: `pipeline-${fixture.runId.slice(0, 8)}`
  });
  const address = resolveChainAddress(fixture.sourceWallet, fixture.chain).prefixed;
  await pool.query(
    `UPDATE wallets
        SET status = 'active', composite_score = 92, tier = 'elite',
            total_trades = 40, last_active = NOW()
      WHERE address = $1`,
    [address]
  );
  return address;
}

/**
 * Stage 2 â€” backfill into canonical source trades, through each chain's real
 * ingestion path. The three differ in more than naming: Solana parses a raw
 * Helius transaction into a swap event, Polymarket takes a confirmed Data API
 * fill, and Robinhood Chain takes a decoded log.
 */
async function ingestSourceTrade(fixture: LifecycleFixture, eventAt: Date): Promise<string> {
  const label = `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}buy`;

  if (fixture.chain === 'solana') {
    const wallet = fixture.sourceWallet;
    const usdc = 'EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v';
    const quote = String(BUY_QUANTITY * BUY_PRICE_USD * 1_000_000);
    const base = String(BUY_QUANTITY);
    // A buy moves USDC out of the wallet and the target token in.
    const transaction: HeliusParsedTransaction = {
      slot: 1,
      blockTime: Math.floor(eventAt.getTime() / 1000),
      transaction: { signatures: [label] },
      meta: {
        preTokenBalances: [
          { owner: wallet, mint: usdc, uiTokenAmount: { amount: quote } },
          { owner: wallet, mint: fixture.tokenMint, uiTokenAmount: { amount: '0' } }
        ],
        postTokenBalances: [
          { owner: wallet, mint: usdc, uiTokenAmount: { amount: '0' } },
          { owner: wallet, mint: fixture.tokenMint, uiTokenAmount: { amount: base } }
        ]
      }
    };

    const event = parseCanonicalSolanaSwapEvent(transaction, wallet);
    if (!event) throw new Error('indexer refused to parse the staged Solana swap');
    expect(event.direction).toBe('buy');
    const persisted = await persistSolanaSourceTrade({ event, source: 'solana-backfill' });
    return persisted.event.id;
  }

  if (fixture.chain === 'polygon') {
    const persisted = await persistPolymarketSourceTrade({
      trade: {
        proxyWallet: fixture.sourceWallet,
        timestamp: eventAt,
        conditionId: fixtureHash(fixture, 'condition-buy'),
        asset: fixture.tokenMint,
        size: BUY_QUANTITY,
        // Polymarket prices are probabilities, so the entry is 20c rather than
        // the $2 the other chains use.
        price: 0.2,
        side: 'BUY',
        transactionHash: fixtureHash(fixture, 'tx-buy'),
        outcome: 'Yes',
        title: 'pipeline integration market'
      },
      quantity: String(BUY_QUANTITY),
      amountUsd: BUY_QUANTITY * 0.2
    });
    return persisted.event.id;
  }

  const persisted = await persistRobinhoodSourceTrade({
    transactionHash: fixtureHash(fixture, 'tx-buy'),
    walletAddress: fixture.sourceWallet,
    tokenMint: fixture.tokenMint,
    side: 'buy',
    quantity: String(BUY_QUANTITY),
    eventAt,
    blockNumber: 1_000n
  });
  return persisted.event.id;
}

/**
 * Stage 3 â€” signal. `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates` is the gate the signal
 * engine polls on; a source trade that does not surface here never becomes a
 * signal, so the candidate is asserted rather than assumed.
 */
async function deriveSignal(
  fixture: LifecycleFixture,
  sourceTradeId: string
): Promise<{ signalId: string; candidate: SourceTradeSignalCandidate }> {
  await pool.query(
    'INSERT INTO tokens (mint, chain) VALUES ($1, $2) ON CONFLICT (mint) DO NOTHING',
    [resolveChainValue(fixture.tokenMint, fixture.chain).prefixed, fixture.chain]
  );

  const candidates = await listSourceTradeSignalCandidates({
    sourceTradeId,
    maxEventAgeMs: MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS,
    limit: 1
  });
  expect(candidates).toHaveLength(1);
  const candidate = candidates[0]!;
  expect(candidate.chain).toBe(fixture.chain);

  const signal = await insertSourceTradeSignal({
    sourceTradeId: candidate.sourceTradeId,
    clusterId: candidate.clusterId,
    confidence: candidate.clusterConfidence,
    signalScore: candidate.walletScore,
    triggerData: {
      sourceWallet: candidate.walletAddress,
      sourceQuantity: candidate.quantity,
      sourceEventAt: candidate.eventAt.toISOString()
    },
    maxEventAgeMs: MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS,
    maxPositionEvidenceAgeMs: EVIDENCE_AGE_MS
  });
  expect(await markSourceTradeSignalDispatched(signal.id)).toBe(true);

  // The engine hands off exactly once; a second poll must not re-emit it.
  const afterDispatch = await listSourceTradeSignalCandidates({
    sourceTradeId,
    maxEventAgeMs: MAX_EVENT_AGE_MS,
    limit: 1
  });
  expect(afterDispatch).toHaveLength(0);

  return { signalId: signal.id, candidate };
}

/**
 * Stage 4 â€” paper trade. The canonical claim, the simulate/submit transitions,
 * the venue evidence that moves the copy position, and the `trades` row the
 * dashboard and the scorer read from.
 */
async function executePaperEntry(
  fixture: LifecycleFixture,
  input: { signalId: string; sourceTradeId: string }
): Promise<string> {
  const claimed = await claimSourceSignalForCopyExecution({
    signalId: input.signalId,
    targetAccount: fixture.targetAccount,
    executionMode: 'paper',
    requestedBaseQuantity: String(BUY_QUANTITY),
    maxPositionEvidenceAgeMs: EVIDENCE_AGE_MS
  });
  expect(claimed.execution, claimed.reason).not.toBeNull();
  const executionId = claimed.execution!.id;
  expect(claimed.execution!.direction).toBe('buy');

  await transitionCopyExecution({
    executionId,
    nextState: 'simulated',
    simulationId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}sim-buy`
  });
  await transitionCopyExecution({
    executionId,
    nextState: 'submitted',
    submissionType: 'order',
    submissionId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}submit-buy`,
    nextReconciliationAt: new Date(Date.now() + 30_000)
  });

  const amountUsd = BUY_QUANTITY * BUY_PRICE_USD;
  const settled = await recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
    executionId,
    evidenceType: 'paper_simulation',
    evidenceId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}fill-buy`,
    baseQuantity: String(BUY_QUANTITY),
    quoteLeg: { amount: String(amountUsd), currency: 'USD' as const },
    priceUsd: String(BUY_PRICE_USD),
    confirmationState: 'finalized',
    completesExecution: true,
    occurredAt: new Date()
  });
  expect(settled.execution.state).toBe('confirmed');

  // Prices and USD amounts are passed explicitly: left out, `persistTrade`
  // reaches for a live price feed, which has no place in an integration run.
  await persistTrade({
    signalId: input.signalId,
    sourceTradeId: input.sourceTradeId,
    copyExecutionId: executionId,
    tokenMint: resolveChainValue(fixture.tokenMint, fixture.chain).prefixed,
    size: amountUsd,
    chain: fixture.chain,
    executionMode: 'paper',
    direction: 'buy',
    executor: 'pipeline-entry',
    amountUsd,
    tokenAmount: BUY_QUANTITY,
    priceUsd: BUY_PRICE_USD,
    feeUsd: 0
  });

  return executionId;
}

/**
 * Stage 5 â€” exit, shaped exactly as the executor's stop-loss job persists one:
 * the entry's `signalId`, no `sourceTradeId`, and no canonical execution, since
 * the scorer queues it off the position ledger rather than off a source trade.
 */
async function exitPosition(fixture: LifecycleFixture, signalId: string): Promise<void> {
  const amountUsd = BUY_QUANTITY * SELL_PRICE_USD;
  await persistTrade({
    signalId,
    sourceTradeId: null,
    copyExecutionId: null,
    tokenMint: resolveChainValue(fixture.tokenMint, fixture.chain).prefixed,
    size: amountUsd,
    chain: fixture.chain,
    executionMode: 'paper',
    direction: 'sell',
    executor: 'pipeline-exit',
    amountUsd,
    tokenAmount: BUY_QUANTITY,
    priceUsd: SELL_PRICE_USD,
    feeUsd: 0
  });
}

==> tests/integration/polymarket-redemption.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { describe, it, expect, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import {
  claimPolymarketRedemption,
  confirmPolymarketRedemption,
  failPolymarketRedemption,
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims
} from '../../packages/db/src/polymarket-redemptions.js';

/**
 * Exactly-once redemption of resolved Polymarket positions (checklist S3-18).
 *
 * A resolved market stops accepting orders, so a winning position cannot be
 * sold â€” redemption is the only exit. `redeemPositions()` takes no amount and
 * redeems the wallet's whole balance for both outcomes, so a second call after a
 * successful first is an on-chain no-op that still burns gas and still returns a
 * transaction hash a reconciler would read as a fresh fill.
 *
 * These tests exist because the first version of the guard was **inert**. The
 * partial unique index was on `(user_id, condition_id)`, but `user_id` is NULL
 * for the whole of Stage 3, and by default NULL never conflicts with NULL â€” so
 * two concurrent sweeps both claimed the same market. A direct SQL probe caught
 * it; nothing in the type system or the test suite would have.
 */

const conditionIds: string[] = [];

function conditionId(label: string): string {
  const id = `it-redeem-${label}-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
  conditionIds.push(id);
  return id;
}

afterAll(async () => {
  if (conditionIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM polymarket_redemptions WHERE condition_id = ANY($1)', [
      conditionIds
    ]);
  }
});

describe('polymarket redemption claims', () => {
  it('grants a claim to exactly one of two concurrent sweeps', async () => {
    const condition = conditionId('concurrent');

    // Fired together rather than sequentially: sequential calls would pass even
    // with a broken guard, because the second would see the first's committed row.
    const [first, second] = await Promise.all([
      claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition }),
      claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })
    ]);

    const granted = [first, second].filter(Boolean);
    expect(granted).toHaveLength(1);

    const live = await pool.query(
      `SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM polymarket_redemptions
        WHERE condition_id = $1 AND status IN ('claimed','confirmed')`,
      [condition]
    );
    expect(live.rows[0].n).toBe(1);
  });

  it('refuses a re-claim while a claim is still open', async () => {
    const condition = conditionId('open');
    expect(await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })).not.toBe(null);
    expect(await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })).toBe(null);
  });

  it('refuses a re-claim after the redemption is confirmed', async () => {
    // The important one: a confirmed redemption already moved the money. A
    // second claim would redeem again for zero gain and non-zero gas.
    const condition = conditionId('confirmed');
    const claim = await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition });
    expect(claim).not.toBe(null);

    await confirmPolymarketRedemption({
      id: claim!.id,
      transactionHash: '0xdeadbeef',
      redeemedCollateral: '100.000000',
      winningTokenId: 'token-yes'
    });

    expect(await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })).toBe(null);
  });

  it('allows a retry after a failed attempt', async () => {
    // A venue error must not poison the market forever â€” the position is still
    // redeemable and the collateral is still owed.
    const condition = conditionId('retry');
    const claim = await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition });
    await failPolymarketRedemption({ id: claim!.id, reason: 'venue 500' });

    expect(await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })).not.toBe(null);
  });

  it('rejects a confirmed row that carries no evidence', async () => {
    // Enforced by a CHECK constraint, not by convention: a confirmed row with no
    // transaction hash reads as settled money that cannot be verified on chain.
    const condition = conditionId('no-evidence');
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `INSERT INTO polymarket_redemptions (condition_id, status) VALUES ($1, 'confirmed')`,
        [condition]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_polymarket_redemption_confirmed_evidence/);
  });

  it('releases a stale claim so a crashed sweep cannot block the market forever', async () => {
    const condition = conditionId('stale');
    const claim = await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition });
    expect(claim).not.toBe(null);

    // Backdate the claim past the recovery window.
    await pool.query(
      `UPDATE polymarket_redemptions SET claimed_at = now() - interval '2 hours' WHERE id = $1`,
      [claim!.id]
    );

    const released = await releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims(60 * 60 * 1000);
    expect(released).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

    // Marked failed rather than retried silently: the on-chain call may or may
    // not have landed, and only a fresh claim should decide to try again.
    const row = await pool.query(
      'SELECT status, failure_reason FROM polymarket_redemptions WHERE id = $1',
      [claim!.id]
    );
    expect(row.rows[0].status).toBe('failed');
    expect(await claimPolymarketRedemption({ conditionId: condition })).not.toBe(null);
  });
});

==> tests/integration/reconciliation-coordinator.integration.test.ts <==
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import {
  claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation,
  closePool,
  getCopyExecutionByClientOrderId,
  recordSourceTradeEvent,
  releaseCopyExecutionReconciliationClaim,
  requestCopyExecution,
  transitionCopyExecution,
  type CopyExecutionRecord
} from '../../packages/db/src/index.js';
import {
  RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT,
  runReconciliationCoordinator
} from '../../apps/trade-executor/src/reconciliation-coordinator.js';
import { withLifecycleFixture } from './helpers/lifecycle-fixture.js';

/**
 * C1 acceptance: an execution left in `reconciliation_required` must be picked
 * up on a later sweep, which is what happens after a process restart.
 *
 * The scenario this covers is the one the per-venue sweeps structurally cannot:
 * the venue-side pending record is gone (Redis expiry, flush, or a process that
 * died before writing it), so nothing but a sweep over `copy_executions` itself
 * will ever look at the row again.
 */

const eventAt = new Date('2026-01-01T12:00:00.000Z');
const observedAt = new Date('2026-01-01T12:00:01.000Z');

afterAll(async () => {
  await closePool();
});

async function stageAmbiguousExecution(fixture: {
  chain: Chain;
  sourceEventPrefix: string;
  sourceWallet: string;
  targetAccount: string;
  tokenMint: string;
}): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord> {
  const source = await recordSourceTradeEvent({
    chain: fixture.chain,
    sourceEventType: 'transaction',
    sourceEventId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}stuck-buy`,
    transactionHash: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}stuck-buy`,
    walletAddress: fixture.sourceWallet,
    tokenMint: fixture.tokenMint,
    side: 'buy',
    quantity: '10',
    amountUsd: '100',
    priceUsd: '10',
    eventAt,
    observedAt,
    confirmationState: 'finalized',
    confirmationEvidenceId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}stuck-finalized`
  });
  const requested = await requestCopyExecution({
    sourceTradeId: source.event.id,
    targetAccount: fixture.targetAccount,
    executionMode: 'paper',
    requestedBaseQuantity: '5',
    maxReconciliationAttempts: 3
  });
  await transitionCopyExecution({
    executionId: requested.execution.id,
    nextState: 'simulated',
    simulationId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}simulation`
  });
  await transitionCopyExecution({
    executionId: requested.execution.id,
    nextState: 'submitted',
    submissionType: 'transaction',
    submissionId: `${fixture.sourceEventPrefix}submission`,
    nextReconciliationAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1_000)
  });
  // Whatever submitted this execution then died, leaving it ambiguous with its
  // venue-side pending record gone.
  const stuck = await transitionCopyExecution({
    executionId: requested.execution.id,
    nextState: 'reconciliation_required',
    reason: 'venue pending record was lost',
    nextReconciliationAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1_000)
  });
  expect(stuck.state).toBe('reconciliation_required');
  return stuck;
}

describe('canonical reconciliation coordinator', () => {
  it('picks up an execution left in reconciliation_required and releases its claim', async () => {
    await withLifecycleFixture(async (fixture) => {
      const stuck = await stageAmbiguousExecution(fixture);

      const seen: string[] = [];
      const escalated: string[] = [];
      const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator({
        account: RECONCILIATION_ACCOUNT,
        limit: 100,
        claim: ({ limit }) => claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation({
          chain: fixture.chain,
          limit
        }),
        release: (input) => releaseCopyExecutionReconciliationClaim(input),
        reconcilers: {
          [fixture.chain]: async (execution: CopyExecutionRecord) => {
            seen.push(execution.id);
            // The venue still has no answer, which is the realistic first pass.
            return { status: 'pending' };
          }
        },
        escalate: async (execution) => {
          escalated.push(execution.id);
        }
      });

      expect(seen).toContain(stuck.id);
      expect(result.pending).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
      expect(escalated).toHaveLength(0);

      // The claim must be handed back, otherwise the row stays locked for the
      // full stale-claim window â€” the exact stuck state this prevents.
      const afterSweep = await getCopyExecutionByClientOrderId({
        chain: fixture.chain,
        targetAccount: fixture.targetAccount,
        clientOrderId: stuck.clientOrderId
      });
      expect(afterSweep).toMatchObject({
        state: 'reconciliation_required',
        reconciliationClaimId: null,
        reconciliationAttempts: 1
      });
    });
  });

  it('resolves the execution when the venue proves the submission failed', async () => {
    await withLifecycleFixture(async (fixture) => {
      const stuck = await stageAmbiguousExecution(fixture);

      const result = await runReconciliationCoordinator({
        limit: 100,
        claim: ({ limit }) => claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation({
          chain: fixture.chain,
          limit
        }),
        release: (input) => releaseCopyExecutionReconciliationClaim(input),
        reconcilers: {
          [fixture.chain]: async (execution: CopyExecutionRecord) => {
            await transitionCopyExecution({
              executionId: execution.id,
              nextState: 'failed',
              reason: 'venue reported the transaction reverted'
            });
            return { status: 'resolved' };
          }
        },
        escalate: async () => undefined
      });

      expect(result.resolved).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

      const settled = await getCopyExecutionByClientOrderId({
        chain: fixture.chain,
        targetAccount: fixture.targetAccount,
        clientOrderId: stuck.clientOrderId
      });
      expect(settled).toMatchObject({ state: 'failed', reconciliationClaimId: null });

      // A terminal execution must not be claimable again.
      const reclaimed = await claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation({
        chain: fixture.chain,
        limit: 100
      });
      expect(reclaimed.some((candidate) => candidate.id === stuck.id)).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  // Attempts are consumed by the claim itself, so a repeatedly unobservable
  // execution eventually stops being claimed. It must reach a human first.
  it('escalates rather than abandoning an execution that exhausts its attempts', async () => {
    await withLifecycleFixture(async (fixture) => {
      const stuck = await stageAmbiguousExecution(fixture);
      const escalated: Array<{ id: string; reason: string }> = [];

      const sweep = () => runReconciliationCoordinator({
        limit: 100,
        claim: ({ limit }) => claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation({
          chain: fixture.chain,
          limit,
          // Ignore the claim cooldown so consecutive sweeps in one test see it.
          staleClaimBefore: new Date(Date.now() + 60_000)
        }),
        release: (input) => releaseCopyExecutionReconciliationClaim({
          ...input,
          retryAt: new Date(Date.now() - 1_000)
        }),
        reconcilers: {
          [fixture.chain]: async () => ({ status: 'unresolved', reason: 'venue unreachable' })
        },
        escalate: async (execution, reason) => {
          escalated.push({ id: execution.id, reason });
        }
      });

      // maxReconciliationAttempts is 3, so the third sweep is the last one that
      // can claim the row.
      await sweep();
      await sweep();
      const third = await sweep();

      expect(third.exhausted).toBe(1);
      expect(escalated).toEqual([
        { id: stuck.id, reason: expect.stringContaining('venue unreachable') }
      ]);

      const exhausted = await claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation({
        chain: fixture.chain,
        limit: 100,
        staleClaimBefore: new Date(Date.now() + 60_000)
      });
      expect(exhausted.some((candidate) => candidate.id === stuck.id)).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});

==> tests/integration/source-trade-legacy-key.integration.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it, beforeAll } from 'vitest';
// Relative deep import, matching every other suite in this directory. The repo
// root has no `@swat/db` dependency (only `@swat/shared`), so the bare specifier
// is unresolvable when vitest runs this file from the root â€” it would throw
// ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before a single assertion ran.
import { query } from '../../packages/db/src/index.js';
import { assertIntegrationSchemaCurrent } from './helpers/schema-guard.js';

/**
 * `028`'s drop of `023`'s UNIQUE key â€” the bug and the fix.
 *
 * WRITTEN BUT NEVER EXECUTED: no database was available in the session that wrote
 * it. Everything below is the assertion set that would prove the fix; treat the
 * behaviour as unverified until `pnpm test:integration` runs.
 *
 * The bug: `028` guarded the drop on
 * `conname = 'source_trades_chain_transaction_hash_wallet_address_token_mint_direction_key'`
 * â€” 76 characters, where PostgreSQL truncates identifiers at 63. The comparison
 * could never be true, so the guard did nothing and the DROP never ran. `023`'s
 * key therefore survived on every database that applied `023`, while `028` went on
 * to install the replacement identity as though it were gone.
 *
 * Why that matters: the surviving key forbids two rows sharing
 * `(chain, transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint, direction)`. One
 * transaction carrying two fills of the same token in the same direction is a
 * shape real ingestion produces â€” `source_event_index` exists in the replacement
 * key precisely to distinguish them â€” so those inserts were being rejected with a
 * `23505` rather than stored.
 */
describe('source_trades legacy uniqueness key (028 shape-matched drop)', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await assertIntegrationSchemaCurrent();
  });

  it('has no unique constraint on the legacy five-column shape', async () => {
    // Matched by shape, not name â€” the same reason the migration had to be.
    const rows = await query<{ conname: string }>(`
      SELECT c.conname
        FROM pg_constraint c
       WHERE c.conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
         AND c.contype = 'u'
         AND (
           SELECT array_agg(a.attname::text ORDER BY a.attname)
             FROM unnest(c.conkey) AS k(attnum)
             JOIN pg_attribute a
               ON a.attrelid = c.conrelid
              AND a.attnum = k.attnum
         ) = ARRAY['chain', 'direction', 'token_mint', 'transaction_hash', 'wallet_address']
    `);
    expect(rows).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('still has the replacement canonical-event identity', async () => {
    // The drop must not have taken the new key with it.
    const rows = await query<{ indexname: string }>(`
      SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes
       WHERE tablename = 'source_trades'
         AND indexname = 'unq_source_trades_canonical_event'
    `);
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('accepts two fills of the same token and direction in one transaction', async () => {
    // The exact insert the surviving key rejected. Distinguished only by
    // source_event_index, which is why the replacement key includes it.
    const wallet = 'solana:legacy-key-probe-wallet';
    const token = 'solana:legacy-key-probe-token';
    const txHash = 'legacy-key-probe-signature';

    await query(
      `INSERT INTO wallets (address, chain, status)
       VALUES ($1, 'solana', 'active')
       ON CONFLICT (address) DO NOTHING`,
      [wallet]
    );

    const insertFill = (index: string) => query(
      `INSERT INTO source_trades (
         chain, source_event_type, source_event_id, source_event_index,
         transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint, direction,
         token_amount, event_at, observed_at, confirmation_state
       ) VALUES (
         'solana', 'transaction', $1, $2,
         $1, $3, $4, 'buy',
         1, NOW(), NOW(), 'confirmed'
       )`,
      [txHash, index, wallet, token]
    );

    try {
      await insertFill('0');
      // Before the fix this second insert raised 23505 on the legacy key.
      await expect(insertFill('1')).resolves.not.toThrow();

      const stored = await query<{ count: string }>(
        `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM source_trades
          WHERE transaction_hash = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [txHash, wallet]
      );
      expect(stored[0]?.count).toBe('2');
    } finally {
      await query(`DELETE FROM source_trades WHERE transaction_hash = $1`, [txHash]);
      await query(`DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = $1`, [wallet]);
    }
  });

  it('still rejects a genuine duplicate of the canonical event identity', async () => {
    // Dropping the old key must not have made the table permissive: the same
    // (chain, event_type, event_id, event_index) is still one event.
    const wallet = 'solana:legacy-key-dupe-wallet';
    const token = 'solana:legacy-key-dupe-token';
    const txHash = 'legacy-key-dupe-signature';

    await query(
      `INSERT INTO wallets (address, chain, status)
       VALUES ($1, 'solana', 'active')
       ON CONFLICT (address) DO NOTHING`,
      [wallet]
    );

    const insertSame = () => query(
      `INSERT INTO source_trades (
         chain, source_event_type, source_event_id, source_event_index,
         transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint, direction,
         token_amount, event_at, observed_at, confirmation_state
       ) VALUES (
         'solana', 'transaction', $1, '0',
         $1, $2, $3, 'buy',
         1, NOW(), NOW(), 'confirmed'
       )`,
      [txHash, wallet, token]
    );

    try {
      await insertSame();
      await expect(insertSame()).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23505' });
    } finally {
      await query(`DELETE FROM source_trades WHERE transaction_hash = $1`, [txHash]);
      await query(`DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = $1`, [wallet]);
    }
  });

  it('replays cleanly â€” a second migrate leaves the same shape', async () => {
    // migrate.ts re-runs every file, so the shape-matched drop must be a no-op the
    // second time. Asserted by shape rather than by running migrate here.
    const rows = await query<{ contype: string; conname: string }>(`
      SELECT contype::text, conname FROM pg_constraint
       WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass AND contype = 'u'
    `);
    const shapes = rows.map((r) => r.conname);
    expect(new Set(shapes).size).toBe(shapes.length);
  });
});

==> tests/integration/subscription-states.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { forUser } from '../../packages/db/src/tenancy.js';
import { createUser, type UserRecord } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';
import {
  beginWindDown,
  endSubscription,
  getSubscriptionState,
  IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError,
  isSubscribed,
  listWalletSubscriptions,
  QuotaExceededError,
  requestCloseAll,
  subscribeToWallet
} from '../../packages/db/src/subscriptions.js';

/**
 * Subscription lifecycle states (`S4-M3`, ADR-0005 Â§3.7, migration `051`).
 *
 * `packages/db/src/subscriptions.test.ts` covers the state machine with no
 * database. What only PostgreSQL can prove is here:
 *
 *  1. The CHECK constraints genuinely reject an incoherent row. A state column
 *     whose invariant lives only in TypeScript is one manual UPDATE away from a
 *     `winding_down` row with no `wound_down_at`, and then "how long has this
 *     been winding down?" has no answer for exactly the rows that need it.
 *  2. A re-subscribe after `ended` is representable under the primary key
 *     `(user_id, wallet_address)`. If it were not, a user who ended a
 *     subscription could never restart it, and the failure would arrive as a
 *     duplicate-key error at the worst possible moment.
 *  3. `active_since` moves forward on revival while `created_at` does not â€”
 *     the forward-only boundary S4-M2 filters on.
 *  4. The quota counts `winding_down` and ignores `ended`.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const userIds: string[] = [];
const walletAddresses: string[] = [];

function walletFor(suffix: string): string {
  const address = `solana:SWATm3${runId}${suffix}`.slice(0, 100);
  walletAddresses.push(address);
  return address;
}

async function makeUser(tier: 'free' | 'operator' | 'ultra' = 'free') {
  const user = await createUser({
    email: `s4m3-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
    password: 'a-very-long-password',
    tier
  });
  userIds.push(user.id);
  return user;
}

async function subscribe(user: UserRecord, address: string) {
  return subscribeToWallet(forUser(user.id), {
    walletAddress: address,
    chain: 'solana',
    tier: user.tier,
    tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
  });
}

async function readRow(userId: string, address: string) {
  const result = await pool.query<{
    state: string;
    created_at: Date;
    active_since: Date;
    wound_down_at: Date | null;
    ended_at: Date | null;
    close_all_requested_at: Date | null;
  }>(
    `SELECT state, created_at, active_since, wound_down_at, ended_at, close_all_requested_at
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
    [userId, address]
  );
  return result.rows[0];
}

afterAll(async () => {
  if (walletAddresses.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_wallet_subscriptions WHERE wallet_address = ANY($1)', [
      walletAddresses
    ]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = ANY($1)', [walletAddresses]);
  }
  if (userIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
  }
});

describe('migration 051 schema', () => {
  it('defaults an existing-shape insert to active with active_since set', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('def');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    const row = await readRow(user.id, address);
    expect(row?.state).toBe('active');
    expect(row?.active_since).toBeInstanceOf(Date);
    expect(row?.wound_down_at).toBeNull();
    expect(row?.ended_at).toBeNull();
  });

  it('rejects a state the CHECK does not know', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('badst');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET state = 'paused'
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [user.id, address]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_subscription_state/);
  });

  it('rejects winding_down with no wound_down_at', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('nostamp');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET state = 'winding_down'
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [user.id, address]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_subscription_state_stamps/);
  });

  it('rejects ended with no ended_at', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('noend');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET state = 'ended'
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [user.id, address]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_subscription_state_stamps/);
  });

  it('rejects an active row carrying wind-down or close-all stamps', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('activest');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    // An active subscription with a wind-down stamp would read as sells-only to
    // an operator and buys-and-sells to the fan-out.
    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET wound_down_at = NOW()
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [user.id, address]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_subscription_state_stamps/);

    await expect(
      pool.query(
        `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions SET close_all_requested_at = NOW()
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
        [user.id, address]
      )
    ).rejects.toThrow(/chk_subscription_state_stamps/);
  });

  it('keeps the partial index the fan-out path depends on', async () => {
    // Without it every mirror scans the accumulated history of everyone who
    // ever left this master, because `ended` rows are retained forever.
    const indexes = await pool.query<{ indexname: string }>(
      `SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes
        WHERE tablename = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'`
    );
    const names = indexes.rows.map((row) => row.indexname);
    expect(names).toContain('idx_uws_wallet_live');
    expect(names).toContain('idx_uws_winding_down');
  });
});

describe('wind-down lifecycle', () => {
  it('walks active -> winding_down -> ended and keeps both stamps', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('walk');
    await subscribe(user, address);
    const scope = forUser(user.id);

    const wound = await beginWindDown(scope, address);
    expect(wound.changed).toBe(true);
    expect(wound.subscription.state).toBe('winding_down');
    expect(wound.subscription.woundDownAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date);

    // Still listed and still gated-in: the user has open positions being
    // mirrored out, so their per-wallet endpoints must keep working.
    expect(await isSubscribed(scope, address)).toBe(true);
    expect((await listWalletSubscriptions(scope)).map((s) => s.state)).toEqual(['winding_down']);

    const ended = await endSubscription(scope, address);
    expect(ended.subscription.state).toBe('ended');
    expect(ended.subscription.endedAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date);
    // Preserved: "how long did this take to close" is the operational question.
    expect(ended.subscription.woundDownAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date);

    // Hidden from the user, but retained for attribution.
    expect(await isSubscribed(scope, address)).toBe(false);
    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(scope)).toHaveLength(0);
    expect((await getSubscriptionState(scope, address))?.state).toBe('ended');
    expect(await readRow(user.id, address)).toBeDefined();
  });

  it('ends directly from active when nothing was ever opened', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('direct');
    await subscribe(user, address);

    const ended = await endSubscription(forUser(user.id), address);
    expect(ended.subscription.state).toBe('ended');
    // No fictitious wind-down it would then sit in forever.
    expect(ended.subscription.woundDownAt).toBeNull();
  });

  it('refuses to wind down an ended subscription', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('reended');
    await subscribe(user, address);
    const scope = forUser(user.id);
    await endSubscription(scope, address);

    await expect(beginWindDown(scope, address)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      IllegalSubscriptionTransitionError
    );
    expect((await getSubscriptionState(scope, address))?.state).toBe('ended');
  });

  it('records close-all once and winds down in the same step', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('closeall');
    await subscribe(user, address);
    const scope = forUser(user.id);

    const first = await requestCloseAll(scope, address);
    expect(first.subscription.state).toBe('winding_down');
    expect(first.subscription.closeAllRequestedAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date);

    const second = await requestCloseAll(scope, address);
    // A second click is a no-op, not a second round of sells.
    expect(second.changed).toBe(false);
    expect(second.subscription.closeAllRequestedAt).toEqual(first.subscription.closeAllRequestedAt);
  });
});

describe('re-subscribe', () => {
  it('revives an ended subscription in place and moves the forward-only boundary', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('revive');
    await subscribe(user, address);
    const scope = forUser(user.id);

    const before = await readRow(user.id, address);
    await endSubscription(scope, address);

    // The primary key forbids a second row, so this must not raise a duplicate
    // key â€” the transition IS the re-subscribe.
    const revived = await subscribe(user, address);
    expect(revived.subscriptionCreated).toBe(true);
    expect(revived.subscription.state).toBe('active');

    const after = await readRow(user.id, address);
    expect(after?.created_at).toEqual(before?.created_at);
    // Forward-only (S4-M2): the boundary moves even though created_at does not.
    expect(after!.active_since.getTime()).toBeGreaterThan(before!.active_since.getTime());
    expect(after?.wound_down_at).toBeNull();
    expect(after?.ended_at).toBeNull();

    const rows = await pool.query<{ count: string }>(
      `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
        WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
      [user.id, address]
    );
    expect(rows.rows[0]?.count).toBe('1');
  });

  it('resumes a winding-down subscription without a second quota charge', async () => {
    // Free tier tracks 3, so a wrongly-charged resume at the boundary would
    // refuse the user their own wallet back.
    const user = await makeUser('free');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);
    const addresses = [walletFor('q1'), walletFor('q2'), walletFor('q3')];
    for (const address of addresses) await subscribe(user, address);

    await beginWindDown(scope, addresses[0]!);
    const resumed = await subscribe(user, addresses[0]!);
    expect(resumed.subscription.state).toBe('active');
    expect(resumed.subscriptionCreated).toBe(false);
  });

  it('counts winding_down against the quota and ignores ended', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser('free');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);
    const addresses = [walletFor('c1'), walletFor('c2'), walletFor('c3')];
    for (const address of addresses) await subscribe(user, address);

    // Winding down still consumes the resource: the wallet is still indexed and
    // its sells are still mirrored. Otherwise the quota is bypassable by
    // unsubscribing from each wallet in turn.
    await beginWindDown(scope, addresses[0]!);
    await expect(subscribe(user, walletFor('c4'))).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(QuotaExceededError);

    // Ended does not: a finished subscription must not occupy a slot forever.
    await endSubscription(scope, addresses[0]!);
    const fifth = await subscribe(user, walletFor('c5'));
    expect(fifth.subscriptionCreated).toBe(true);
  });
});

==> tests/integration/subscriptions.integration.test.ts <==
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { describe, it, expect, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { capabilitiesFor } from '@swat/shared';
import { pool } from '../../packages/db/src/client.js';
import { forUser } from '../../packages/db/src/tenancy.js';
import { createUser } from '../../packages/db/src/users.js';
import {
  listWalletSubscriptions,
  QuotaExceededError,
  requestTokenWatch,
  subscribeToWallet,
  unsubscribeFromWallet
} from '../../packages/db/src/subscriptions.js';
import {
  pauseUnderperformingWallets,
  pauseUnsubscribedWallets
} from '../../packages/db/src/scoring-queries.js';

/**
 * Stage 2 subscription model (checklist S2-1 â€¦ S2-6).
 *
 * The assertions that matter here are the *negative* ones â€” that a subscribed
 * wallet survives the nightly pause sweep, and that unsubscribing one user does
 * not delete a wallet another user still tracks. Both are silent data-loss bugs
 * if they regress, invisible until a user reports missing data days later.
 */

const runId = randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12);
const userIds: string[] = [];
const walletAddresses: string[] = [];

function walletFor(suffix: string): string {
  const address = `solana:SWATtest${runId}${suffix}`.slice(0, 100);
  walletAddresses.push(address);
  return address;
}

async function makeUser(tier: 'free' | 'operator' | 'ultra' = 'free') {
  const user = await createUser({
    email: `s2-${randomUUID()}@example.com`,
    password: 'a-very-long-password',
    tier
  });
  userIds.push(user.id);
  return user;
}

afterAll(async () => {
  if (walletAddresses.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM user_wallet_subscriptions WHERE wallet_address = ANY($1)', [
      walletAddresses
    ]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM wallets WHERE address = ANY($1)', [walletAddresses]);
  }
  if (userIds.length > 0) {
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE actor_id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
    await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1)', [userIds]);
  }
});

describe('stage 2 subscriptions', () => {
  it('indexes a wallet once and links many subscribers (global dedup)', async () => {
    const alice = await makeUser();
    const bob = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('dedup');

    const first = await subscribeToWallet(forUser(alice.id), {
      walletAddress: address,
      chain: 'solana',
      tier: alice.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: alice.tierExpiresAt
    });
    const second = await subscribeToWallet(forUser(bob.id), {
      walletAddress: address,
      chain: 'solana',
      tier: bob.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: bob.tierExpiresAt
    });

    // Only the first subscriber creates the global wallet, so only that call
    // should trigger a backfill. Enqueuing on every subscribe is the cost the
    // dedup model exists to avoid.
    expect(first.walletCreated).toBe(true);
    expect(second.walletCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(second.subscriptionCreated).toBe(true);

    const wallets = await pool.query('SELECT address FROM wallets WHERE address = $1', [address]);
    expect(wallets.rowCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('is idempotent and consumes no quota when re-subscribing', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('idem');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);

    const first = await subscribeToWallet(scope, {
      walletAddress: address,
      chain: 'solana',
      tier: user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
    });
    const again = await subscribeToWallet(scope, {
      walletAddress: address,
      chain: 'solana',
      tier: user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
    });

    expect(first.subscriptionCreated).toBe(true);
    expect(again.subscriptionCreated).toBe(false);
    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(scope)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('enforces the free-tier wallet quota at the limit', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser('free');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);

    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      await subscribeToWallet(scope, {
        walletAddress: walletFor(`q${i}`),
        chain: 'solana',
        tier: user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
      });
    }

    await expect(
      subscribeToWallet(scope, {
        walletAddress: walletFor('q3'),
        chain: 'solana',
        tier: user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
      })
    ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(QuotaExceededError);

    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(scope)).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  it('does not let concurrent subscribes exceed the quota', async () => {
    // The TOCTOU this guards: check-then-insert lets two requests both observe
    // `2 < 3` and both insert, landing a free user on 4 wallets.
    const user = await makeUser('free');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);
    const addresses = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((i) => walletFor(`c${i}`));

    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
      addresses.map((walletAddress) =>
        subscribeToWallet(scope, {
          walletAddress,
          chain: 'solana',
          tier: user.tier,
          tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
        })
      )
    );

    const granted = results.filter((r) => r.status === 'fulfilled').length;
    expect(granted).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(scope)).toHaveLength(granted);
  });

  it('unsubscribing one user leaves the other subscriber and the wallet intact', async () => {
    const alice = await makeUser();
    const bob = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('unsub');

    for (const user of [alice, bob]) {
      await subscribeToWallet(forUser(user.id), {
        walletAddress: address,
        chain: 'solana',
        tier: user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
      });
    }

    expect(await unsubscribeFromWallet(forUser(alice.id), address)).toBe(true);

    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(forUser(alice.id))).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(await listWalletSubscriptions(forUser(bob.id))).toHaveLength(1);
    // The global wallet must survive â€” deleting it here would be cross-tenant
    // data loss triggered by an ordinary unsubscribe.
    const wallets = await pool.query('SELECT address FROM wallets WHERE address = $1', [address]);
    expect(wallets.rowCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('never pauses a subscribed wallet, however badly it scores', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser();
    const address = walletFor('pinned');
    await subscribeToWallet(forUser(user.id), {
      walletAddress: address,
      chain: 'solana',
      tier: user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
    });
    // Squarely inside the underperformance rule.
    await pool.query(
      `UPDATE wallets SET total_trades = 100, composite_score = 5,
              last_active = NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
        WHERE address = $1`,
      [address]
    );

    await pauseUnderperformingWallets();
    await pauseUnsubscribedWallets();

    const rows = await pool.query<{ status: string }>(
      'SELECT status FROM wallets WHERE address = $1',
      [address]
    );
    // A user chose this wallet. Pausing it would silently stop their data.
    expect(rows.rows[0]?.status).toBe('active');
  });

  it('pauses an unsubscribed wallet with no platform interest', async () => {
    const address = walletFor('orphan');
    await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO wallets (address, chain, source, status, total_trades, composite_score, last_active)
       VALUES ($1, 'solana', 'discovered', 'active', 100, 5, NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days')
       ON CONFLICT (address) DO NOTHING`,
      [address]
    );

    await pauseUnsubscribedWallets();

    const rows = await pool.query<{ status: string }>(
      'SELECT status FROM wallets WHERE address = $1',
      [address]
    );
    expect(rows.rows[0]?.status).toBe('paused');
  });

  it('enforces the rolling-24h token backfill quota, and re-requests are free', async () => {
    const user = await makeUser('free');
    const scope = forUser(user.id);
    const mint = `solana:MINT${runId}a`;

    const first = await requestTokenWatch(scope, {
      chain: 'solana',
      tokenMint: mint,
      tier: user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
    });
    expect(first.created).toBe(true);

    // Same token again: idempotent, and must not spend any quota.
    const repeat = await requestTokenWatch(scope, {
      chain: 'solana',
      tokenMint: mint,
      tier: user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
    });
    expect(repeat.created).toBe(false);

    const quota = capabilitiesFor(user.tier, user.tierExpiresAt).tokenBackfillsPerDay ?? 1;
    for (let i = 1; i < quota; i++) {
      await requestTokenWatch(scope, {
        chain: 'solana',
        tokenMint: `solana:MINT${runId}${i}`,
        tier: user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
      });
    }

    await expect(
      requestTokenWatch(scope, {
        chain: 'solana',
        tokenMint: `solana:MINT${runId}exhausted`,
        tier: user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: user.tierExpiresAt
      })
    ).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(QuotaExceededError);
  });
});
